item.description: So the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the chamber, "Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word1 from Allah and (who will be) honorable, abstaining (from women), and a prophet from among the righteous." See 3:38

item.description: Before, as guidance for the people. And He revealed the Criterion (i.e., the Qur’ān). Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah will have a severe punishment, and Allah is Exalted in Might, the Owner of Retribution.1 See 3:1

item.description: He said, "My Lord, how will I have a boy when I have reached old age and my wife is barren?" He (the angel) said, "Such is Allah; He does what He wills." See 3:38

item.description: He said, "My Lord, make for me a sign." He said, "Your sign is that you will not (be able to) speak to the people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord much and exalt (Him with praise) in the evening and the morning." See 3:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) when the angels said, "O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds. And (remember) when the angels said: "O Maryam! Verily, Allah has chosen you, purified you, and chosen you above the women of the nations (3:42). "O Maryam! Submit yourself with obedience (Aqnuti) to your Lord and prostrate yourself, and bow down along with Ar-Raki'in (3:43). This is a part of the news of the Ghayb (Unseen) which We reveal to you. You were not with them, when they cast lots with their pens as to which of them should be charged with the care of Maryam; nor were you with them when they disputed (3:44).The Virtue of Maryam Over the Women of Her TimeAllah states that the angels spoke to Maryam by His command and…

item.description: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, (O Muḥammad). And you were not with them when they cast their pens1 as to which of them should be responsible for Maryam. Nor were you with them when they disputed. See 3:42

"He will speak to the people, in the cradle and in manhood, and he will be one of the righteous (3:46). She said: "O my Lord! How shall I have a son when no man has touched me." And I inform you of what you eat, and what you store in your houses. Surely, therein is a sign for you, if you believe (3:49). "(And I have come) confirming that which was before me of the Tawrah, and to make…

item.description: And (make him) a messenger to the Children of Israel, (who will say), 'Indeed I have come to you with a sign from your Lord in that I design for you from clay (that which is) like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by permission of Allah. And I cure the blind (from birth) and the leper, and I give life to the dead - by permission of Allah. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers. See 3:48

item.description: Indeed, from Allah nothing is hidden in the earth nor in the heaven. Truly, nothing is hidden from Allah, in the earth or in the heaven (3:5). He it is Who shapes you in the wombs as He wills. None has the right to be worshipped but He, the Almighty, the All-Wise (3:6).Allah states that He has perfect knowledge in the heavens and earth and that nothing in them is hidden from His watch.هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الْأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُHe it is Who shapes you in the wombs as He wills.Meaning: He creates you in the wombs as He wills, whether male or female, handsome or otherwise, happy or miserable.لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُLa ilaha illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He), the Almighty, the All-Wise.Meaning: He is the Creator and thus is the only…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (I have come) confirming what was before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me. See 3:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is the straight path.'" See 3:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But when Isa felt (persistence in) disbelief from them, he said, "Who are my supporters for (the cause of) Allah?" The disciples said, "We are supporters for Allah. We have believed in Allah and testify that we are Muslims (submitting to Him). Then when Isa came to know of their disbelief, he said: "Who will be my helpers in Allah's cause?" Al-Hawariyyun said: "We are the helpers of Allah; we believe in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims (3:52). "Our Lord! We believe in what You have sent down, and we follow the Messenger (Isa); so write us down among those who bear witness (3:53). And they (disbelievers) plotted and Allah planned too. item.description: Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed and have followed the messenger (i.e., Isa), so register us among the witnesses (to truth)." See 3:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they (i.e., the disbelievers) planned, but Allah planned. And Allah is the best of planners. See 3:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Mention) when Allah said, "O Isa, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify (i.e., free) you from those who disbelieve and make those who follow you (in submission to Allah alone) superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that in which you used to differ. And (remember) when Allah said: "O Isa! I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify (save) you from those who disbelieve, and I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve till the Day of Resurrection. Then you will return to Me and I will judge between you in the matters in which you used to dispute (3:55). "As to those who disbelieve, I will punish them with…

item.description: And as for those who disbelieved, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers." See 3:55

item.description: But as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them in full their rewards, and Allah does not like the wrongdoers. See 3:55

item.description: This is what We recite to you, (O Muḥammad), of (Our) verses and the precise (and wise) message (i.e., the Qur’ān). See 3:55

item.description: Indeed, the example of Isa to Allah1 is like that of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was. Verily, the likeness of Isa before Allah is the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him: Be!" and he was (3:59). (This is) the truth from your Lord, so be not of those who doubt (3:60). Then whoever disputes with you concerning him after the knowledge that has come to you, say: "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then we pray and we invoke Allah's curse upon the liars (3:61). Verily, this is the true narrative, and there is no god except Allah. And indeed, Allah is the Almighty, the All-Wise (3:62). And if they turn away, then…

item.description: It is He who forms you in the wombs however He wills. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. See 3:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters. See 3:59

item.description: Then whoever argues with you about it after (this) knowledge has come to you - say, "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then supplicate earnestly (together) and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars (among us)." See 3:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, this is the true narration. And there is no deity except Allah. And indeed, Allah is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. See 3:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But if they turn away, then indeed - Allah is Knowing of the corrupters. See 3:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you - that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allah."1 But if they turn away, then say, "Bear witness that we are Muslims (submitting to Him)." Say: O people of the Scripture: Come to a word that is just between us and you, that we worship none but Allah the same, and that we associate no partners with Him, and that none of us shall take others as lords besides Allah." Then, if they turn away, say: "Bear witness that we are Muslims (3:64).Every Person Knows about TawhidThis Ayah includes the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, and those who follow their ways.قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ تَعَالَوْا…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Ibrahim while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Then will you not reason? O people of the Scripture! Why do you dispute about Ibrahim, while the Tawrah and the Injil were not revealed till after him? Have you then no sense (3:65). Verily, you are those who have disputed about that of which you have knowledge. Why do you then dispute concerning that of which you have no knowledge? It is Allah Who knows, and you know not (3:66). Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a true Muslim Hanifa and he was not of the Mushrikin (3:67). Verily, among mankind who have the best claim to Ibrahim are those who followed him, and this Prophet and those who have believed.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Here you are - those who have argued about that of which you have (some) knowledge, but why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge? And Allah knows, while you know not. See 3:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was one inclining toward truth, a Muslim (submitting to Allah). And he was not of the polytheists.1 See 3:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the most worthy of Ibrahim among the people are those who followed him (in submission to Allah) and this prophet (i.e., Muḥammad SAW) and those who believe (in his message). And Allah is the Ally1 of the believers. See 3:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: A faction of the People of the Scripture wish they could mislead you. But they do not mislead except themselves, and they perceive (it) not. A party of the People of the Scripture wish to lead you astray. But they shall not lead astray anyone except themselves, and they perceive not (3:69). O People of the Scripture! Why do you disbelieve in the Ayat of Allah, while you bear witness (3:70). "O People of the Scripture! Why do you mix truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know? (3:71). And a party of the People of the Scripture say: "Believe in the morning in that which is revealed to the believers, and reject it at the end of the day, so that they may turn back (3:72). And believe no one except the one who follows your religion."…

And no one knows its (true) interpretation except Allah. But those firm in knowledge say, "We believe in it. All (of it) is from our Lord." And no one will be reminded except those of understanding. So as for those in whose hearts there is a deviation (from the…

item.description: O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah1 while you witness (to their truth)? See 3:69

item.description: O People of the Scripture, why do you mix (i.e., confuse) the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know (it)? See 3:69

item.description: And a faction of the People of the Scripture say (to each other), "Believe in that which was revealed to the believers at the beginning of the day and reject it at its end that perhaps they will return (i.e., abandon their religion). See 3:69

That is because they say, "There is no blame upon us concerning the unlearned."1 And they speak untruth about Allah while they know (it). item.description: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their (own) oaths for a small price will have no share in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them or look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them; and they will have a painful punishment. Verily, those who purchase a small gain at the cost of Allah's covenant and their oaths, they shall have no portion in the Hereafter (Paradise). Neither will Allah speak to them nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and they shall have a painful torment (3:77).There is No Share in the Hereafter for Those Who Break Allah's CovenantAllah states that whoever prefers the small things of this short, soon to end life, instead of fulfilling what they have promised Allah by following…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:78 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, there is among them a party who alter the Scripture with their tongues so you may think it is from the Scripture, but it is not from the Scripture. And they say, "This is from Allah," but it is not from Allah. And they speak untruth about Allah while they know. And verily, among them is a party who distort the Book with their tongues, so that you may think it is from the Book, but it is not from the Book, and they say: This is from Allah, but it is not from Allah; and they speak a lie against Allah while they know it (3:78).The Jews Alter Allah's WordsAllah states that some Jews, may Allah's curses descend on them, distort Allah's Words with their tongues, change them from their appropriate places, and alter their intended meanings.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:79 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is not for a human (prophet)1 that Allah should give him the Scripture2 and authority and prophethood and then he would say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than Allah," but (instead, he would say), "Be pious scholars of the Lord because of what you have taught of the Scripture and because of what you have studied." It is not (possible) for any human being to whom Allah has given the Book and Al-Hukm and prophethood to say to the people: Be my worshippers rather than Allah's." On the contrary (he would say): "Be you Rabbaniyyun, because you are teaching the Book, and you are studying it (3:79). Nor would he order you to take angels and Prophets for lords. Would he order you to disbelieve after you have submitted to Allah's will (3:80).No Prophet Ever Called…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Who say), "Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.1 See 3:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:80 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Nor could he order you to take the angels and prophets as lords. Would he order you to disbelief after you had been Muslims? See 3:79

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:81 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (recall, O People of the Scripture), when Allah took the covenant of the prophets, (saying), "Whatever I give you of the Scripture and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you (must) believe in him and support him." (Allah) said, "Have you acknowledged and taken upon that My commitment?"1 They said, "We have acknowledged it." He said, "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses." And (remember) when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets, saying: Take whatever I gave you from the Book and Hikmah, and afterwards there will come to you a Messenger confirming what is with you; you must, then, believe in him and help him." Allah said: "Do you agree (to it) and will you take up Isri?" They said: "We agree." He said: "Then…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:82 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever turned away after that - they were the defiantly disobedient. See 3:81

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:83 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So is it other than the religion of Allah they desire, while to Him have submitted (all) those within the heavens and earth, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him they will be returned? Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him submitted all creatures in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly. And to Him shall they all be returned (3:83). Say: We believe in Allah and in what has been sent down to us, and what was sent down to Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Ya'qub and Al-Asbat, and what was given to Musa, Isa and the Prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between one another among them and to Him (Allah) we have submitted (3:84). And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted of him, and in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:84 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "We have believed in Allah and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Ya'qub, and the Descendants (al-Asbāṭ), and in what was given to Musa and Isa and to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims (submitting) to Him." See 3:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:85 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever desires other than Islām as religion - never will it be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers. See 3:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:86 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: How shall Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and had witnessed that the Messenger is true and clear signs had come to them? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. How shall Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and after they bore witness that the Messenger is true and after clear proofs came to them? And Allah guides not the people who are wrongdoer (3:86). They are those whose recompense is that on them (rests) the curse of Allah, of the angels and of all mankind (3:87). They will abide therein. Neither will their torment be lightened nor will it be delayed or postponed (3:88). Except for those who repent after that and do righteous deeds. Verily, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful (3:89).Allah Does Not Guide People Who Disbelieve After they Believed, Unless…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:87 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those - their recompense will be that upon them is the curse of Allah and the angels and the people, all together. See 3:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:88 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Abiding eternally therein. The punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved. See 3:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:89 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except for those who repent after that1 and correct themselves. For indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. See 3:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Our Lord, surely You will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise." See 3:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:90 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who disbelieve (i.e., reject the message) after their belief and then increase in disbelief - never will their (claimed) repentance be accepted, and they are the ones astray. Verily, those who disbelieved after their belief and then went on increasing in their disbelief never will their repentance be accepted. And they are those who are astray (3:90). Verily, those who disbelieved, and died while they were disbelievers, the (whole) earth full of gold will not be accepted from anyone of them if they offered it as a ransom. For them is a painful torment and they will have no helpers (3:91).Neither Repentance of the Disbeliever Upon Death, Nor His Ransoming Himself on the Day of Resurrection Shall be AcceptedAllah threatens and warns those who revert to disbelief after they believed and who thereafter insist on disbelief until death.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:91 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - never would the (whole) capacity of the earth in gold be accepted from one of them if he would (seek to) ransom himself with it. For those there will be a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers. See 3:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:92 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Never will you attain the good (reward)1 until you spend (in the way of Allah) from that which you love. And whatever you spend - indeed, Allah is Knowing of it. By no means shall you attain Al-Birr, unless you spend of that which you love; and whatever of good you spend, Allah knows it well (3:92).Al-Birr is Spending from the Best of One's WealthIn his Tafsir, Waki' reported, that 'Amr bin Maymun said that:لَن تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّBy no means shall you attain Al-Birris in reference to attaining Paradise.Imam Ahmad reported that Anas bin Malik said, Abu Talhah had more property than any other among the Ansar in Al-Madinah, and the most beloved of his property to him was Bayruha' garden, which was in front of the (Messenger's) Masjid. Sometimes, Allah's Messenger SAW used to go to the garden and drink…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:93 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel (i.e., Ya'qub) had made unlawful to himself before the Torah was revealed. Say, (O Muḥammad), "So bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful." All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Isra'il made unlawful for himself before the Tawrah was revealed. Say: "Bring here the Tawrah and recite it, if you are truthful (3:93). Then after that, whosoever shall invent a lie against Allah, then it is these that are the wrongdoers (3:94). Say:"Allah has spoken the truth; follow the religion of Ibrahim the Hanif (monotheist), and he was not of the Mushrikin (idolators) (3:95).The Questions that the Jews Asked Our Prophet SAWImam Ahmad recorded that Ibn 'Abbas said, A group of Jews came to Allah's Prophet SAW and said, 'Talk…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:94 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever invents about Allah untruth after that - then those are (truly) the wrongdoers. See 3:93

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:95 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Allah has told the truth. So follow the religion of Ibrahim, inclining toward truth; and he was not of the polytheists."1 See 3:93

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:96 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the first House (of worship) established for mankind was that at Bakkah (i.e., Makkah) - blessed and a guidance for the worlds. Verily, the first House (of worship) appointed for mankind was that at Bakkah (Makkah), full of blessing, and a guidance for Al-'Alamin (mankind and Jinn (96)In it are manifest signs (for example), the Maqam (station) of Ibrahim; whosoever enters it, he attains security. And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to Allah, for those who are able to undertake the journey; and whoever disbelieves, then Allah stands not in need of any of the 'Alamin (97)The Ka'bah is the First House of WorshipAllah said:إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِVerily, the first House appointed for mankindfor all people, for their acts of worship and religious rituals. They go around the House (in Tawaf), pray in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:97 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: In it are clear signs (such as) the standing place of Ibrahim. And whoever enters it (i.e., the Ḥaram) shall be safe. And (due) to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House - for whoever is able to find thereto a way. But whoever disbelieves (i.e., refuses) - then indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.1 See 3:96

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:98 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah while Allah is Witness over what you do?" Say: "O People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians)! Why do you reject the Ayat of Allah, while Allah is Witness to what you do? (3:98). Say: "O People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians)! Why do you stop those who have believed, from the path of Allah, seeking to make it seem crooked, while you (yourselves) are witnesses? And Allah is not unaware of what you do (3:99).Chastising the People of the Book for Their Disbelief and Blocking the Path of AllahIn this Ayah Allah criticizes the disbelieving People of the Book for refusing the truth, rejecting Allah's Ayat and hindering those who seek to believe from His path, although they know that what the Messenger…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:99 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it (seem) deviant, while you are witnesses (to the truth)? And Allah is not unaware of what you do." See 3:98

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He (i.e., the Prophet SAW ) frowned and turned away. كِرَامٍ بَرَرَةٍHonorable and obedient.Meaning: they are noble, handsome, and honorable in their creation. Their character and their deeds are righteous, pure and perfect. Here it should be noted that it is necessary for one who carries the Qur'an (i.e., the angel) to be following righteousness and guidance.Imam Ahmad recorded from Aisha that the Messenger of Allah SAW said:الَّذِي يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ وَهُوَ مَاهِرٌ بِهِ، مَعَ السَّفَرَةِ الْكِرَامِ الْبَرَرَةِ، وَالَّذِي يَقْرَؤُهُ وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِ شَاقٌّ، لَهُ أَجْرَانِHe who recites the Qur'an proficiently, will be with the noble, righteous, ambassador angels, and the one who recites it with difficulty will receive two rewards.This Hadith was reported by the group.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: From him you are distracted. See 80:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No! Indeed, they (i.e., these verses) are a reminder. See 80:1

item.description: So whoever wills may remember it.1 See 80:1

item.description: Exalted and purified. See 80:1

item.description: (Carried) by the hands of messenger-angels. See 80:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Noble and dutiful. See 80:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Destroyed (i.e., cursed) is man;1 how disbelieving is he. Qutila mankind! How ungrateful he is (80:17). From what thing did He create him (80:18). From a Nutfah He created him and then set him in due proportion (80:19). Then He made the path easy for him (80:20). Then He causes him to die and puts him in his grave (80:21). Then when it is His will, He will resurrect him (80:22). Nay, but he has not done what He commanded him (80:23). Then let man look at his food (80:24). We pour forth water in abundance (80:25). And We split the earth in clefts (80:26). And We cause therein Habb to grow (80:27). And grapes and Qadb (80:28). And olives and date palms (80:29). And Ghulb Hada'iq (80:30). And fruits (Fakihah) and herbage (Abb) (80:31). A provision and benefit for…

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: From what thing (i.e., substance) did He create him? See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: From a sperm-drop He created him and destined for him.1 See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Because there came to him the blind man,1 (interrupting). See 80:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then He eased the way for him.1 See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then He causes his death and provides a grave for him.1 See 80:17

item.description: Then when He wills, He will resurrect him. See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No! He (i.e., man) has not yet accomplished what He commanded him. See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then let mankind look at his food. See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: How We poured down water in torrents. See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then We broke open the earth, splitting (it with sprouts). See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And caused to grow within it grain. See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And grapes and herbage. See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And olive and palm trees. See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But what would make you perceive, (O Muḥammad), that perhaps he might be purified.1 See 80:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And gardens of dense shrubbery. See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And fruit and grass. See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (As) enjoyment (i.e., provision) for you and your grazing livestock. See 80:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But when there comes the Deafening Blast.1 Then when there comes As-Sakhkha (33)That Day shall a man flee from his brother (34)And from his mother and his father (35)And from his wife and his children (36)Every man that Day will have enough to make him careless of others (37)Some faces that Day will be bright (38)Laughing, rejoicing at good news (39)And other faces that Day will be dust-stained (40)Darkness will cover them (41)Such will be the disbelieving, the wicked evil doers (42)The Day of Judgement and the Fleeing of the People from Their Relatives during itIbn 'Abbas said, "As-Sakhkhah is one of the names of the Day of Judgement that Allah has magnified and warned His servants of." Ibn Jarir said, "Perhaps it is a name for the blowing into Trumpet." Al-Baghawi said, "As-Sakhkhah means the thunderous shout of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: On the Day a man will flee from his brother. See 80:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And his mother and his father. See 80:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And his wife and his children. See 80:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For every man, that Day, will be a matter adequate for him.1 See 80:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Some) faces, that Day, will be bright. See 80:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Laughing, rejoicing at good news. See 80:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or be reminded and the remembrance would benefit him? See 80:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (other) faces, that Day, will have upon them dust. See 80:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Blackness will cover them. See 80:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those are the disbelievers, the wicked ones. See 80:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: As for he who thinks himself without need.1 See 80:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: To him you give attention. See 80:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And not upon you (is any blame) if he will not be purified.1 See 80:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But as for he who came to you striving (for knowledge). See 80:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: While he fears (Allah). See 80:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By the morning brightness. وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْAnd procalim the grace of your Lord.Meaning: 'just as you were poor and needy, and Allah made you wealthy, then tell about Allah's favor upon you.'Abu Dawud recorded from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet SAW said:لَا يَشْكُرُ اللهَ مَنْ لَا يَشْكُرُ النَّاسَWhoever is not thankful to the people, then he is not thankful to Allah.At-Tirmidhi also recorded this Hadith and he said, "Sahih".Abu Dawud recorded from Jabir that the Prophet SAW said:مَنْ أُبْلِيَ بَلَاءً فَذَكَرَهُ فَقَدْ شَكَرَهُ، وَمَنْ كَتَمَهُ فَقَدْ كَفَرَهُWhoever overcomes some test (i.e., calamity) and mentions it (to others), then he is indeed thankful. And whoever conceals it, then indeed he was ungrateful.Abu Dawud was alone in recording this Hadith.This is the end of the Tafsir of Surat Ad-Duha, and unto Allah is due all praise and thanks.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And as for the petitioner,1 do not repel (him). See 93:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But as for the favor of your Lord, report (it). See 93:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (by) the night when it covers with darkness.1 See 93:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Your Lord has not taken leave of you, (O Muḥammad), nor has He detested (you). See 93:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the Hereafter is better for you than the first (life). See 93:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied. See 93:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Did He not find you an orphan and give (you) refuge? See 93:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And He found you lost and guided (you). See 93:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And He found you poor and made (you) self-sufficient. See 93:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So as for the orphan, do not oppress (him). See 93:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Ḥā, Meem.1 لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ ۖ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبَائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَLa ilaha illa Huwa. He gives life and causes death – your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.This is like the Ayah:قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ جَمِيعًا الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ ۖSay: "O mankind! Verily, I am sent to you all as the Messenger of Allah – to Whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. La ilaha illa Huwa. He gives life and causes death... (7:158)

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke. See 44:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Covering the people; this is a painful torment. See 44:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (They will say), "Our Lord, remove from us the torment; indeed, we are believers." See 44:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: How will there be for them a reminder (at that time)? And there had come to them a clear Messenger. See 44:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then they turned away from him and said, "(He was) taught (and is) a madman." See 44:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We will remove the torment for a little. Indeed, you (disbelievers) will return (to disbelief). See 44:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Day We will strike with the greatest assault, indeed, We will take retribution. See 44:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We had already tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger (i.e., Musa). And indeed We tried before them Fir'awn's people, when there came to them a noble Messenger (44:17). Saying: Deliver to me the servants of Allah. Verily, I am to you a Messenger worthy of all trust (44:18). "And exalt not yourselves against Allah. Truly, I have come to you with a manifest authority (44:19). "And truly, I seek refuge with my Lord and your Lord, lest you should stone me (44:20). "But if you believe me not, then keep away from me and leave me alone (44:21). So he (Musa) called upon his Lord (saying): "These are indeed the people who are criminals (44:22). (Allah said): "Depart you with My servants by night. Surely, you will be pursued (44:23).…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Saying), "Render to me the servants of Allah.1 Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger." See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (saying), "Be not haughty with Allah. Indeed, I have come to you with clear evidence. See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By the clear Book. See 44:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me.1 See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But if you do not believe me, then leave me alone." See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (finally) he called to his Lord that these were a criminal people. See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Allah said), "Then set out with My servants by night. Indeed, you are to be pursued. See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And leave the sea in stillness.1 Indeed, they are an army to be drowned." See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: How much they left behind of gardens and springs. See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And crops and noble sites. See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And comfort wherein they were amused. See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Thus. And We caused to inherit it another people. See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the heaven and earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved. See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night.1 Indeed, We were to warn (mankind). See 44:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment. See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: From Pharaoh. Indeed, he was a haughty one among the transgressors. See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We certainly chose them by knowledge over (all) the worlds. See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We gave them of signs that in which there was a clear trial. See 44:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, these (disbelievers) are saying. Verily, these people are saying (44:34). "There is nothing but our first death, and we shall not be resurrected (44:35). "Then bring back our forefathers, if you speak the truth! (44:36). Are they better or the people of Tubba' and those before them We destroyed them because they were indeed criminals (44:37).Refutation of Those Who Deny the ResurrectionHere Allah denounces the idolators for their denial of the Resurrection and their belief that there is nothing after this life and no life or resurrection after death, which they based on the fact that their forefathers had died and had not returned. They said, If the resurrection is true:فَأْتُوا بِآبَائِنَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَThen bring back our forefathers, if you speak the truth!This is false evidence and a specious argument, for the resurrection will happen on the Day…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: "There is not but our first death, and we will not be resurrected. See 44:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then bring (back) our forefathers, if you should be truthful." See 44:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Are they better or the people of Tubbaʿ1 and those before them? We destroyed them, (for) indeed, they were criminals. See 44:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We did not create the heavens and earth and that between them in play. This World was Created for a WisdomHere Allah tells us of His justice, and that He is far above mere play, folly and falsehood. This is like the Ayah:وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَآءَ وَالاٌّرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا بَـطِلاً ذَلِكَ ظَنُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنَ النَّارِAnd We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them without purpose! That is the consideration of those who disbelieve! Then woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire! (38:27)أَفَحَسِبْتُمْ أَنَّمَا خَلَقْنَـكُمْ عَبَثاً وَأَنَّكُمْ إِلَيْنَا لاَ تُرْجَعُونَ - فَتَعَـلَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ لاَ إِلَـهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِDid you think that We had created you in play, and that you would not be brought back to Us So Exalted be Allah, the True King: La ilaha…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: We did not create them except in truth, but most of them do not know. See 44:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Therein (i.e., on that night) is made distinct1 every precise matter. See 44:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the Day of Judgement is the appointed time for them all. See 44:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Day when no relation1 will avail a relation at all, nor will they be helped. See 44:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except those (believers) on whom Allah has mercy. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. See 44:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the tree of zaqqūm. Verily, the tree of Zaqqu (44:43). Will be the food of the sinners (44:44). Like boiling oil, it will boil in the bellies (44:45). Like the boiling of scalding water (44:46). (It will be said:) "Seize him and drag him into the midst of blazing Fire, (44:47). "Then pour over his head the torment of boiling water (44:48). "Taste you (this)! Verily, you were (pretending to be) the mighty, the generous (44:49). "Verily, this is that whereof you used to doubt! (44:50).The Condition of the Idolators and Their Punishment on the Day of ResurrectionAllah tells us how He will punish the disbelievers who deny the meeting with Him:إِنَّ شَجَرَتَ الزَّقُّومِ - طَعَامُ الْأَثِيمِVerily, the tree of Zaqqum will be the food of the sinners.Those who sinned by their words and in deeds. These are the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Is food for the sinful. See 44:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Like murky oil, it boils within bellies. See 44:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Like the boiling of scalding water. See 44:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (It will be commanded), "Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Hellfire. See 44:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then pour over his head from the torment of scalding water." See 44:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (It will be said), "Taste! Indeed, you are the honored, the noble!1 See 44:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Every) matter (proceeding) from Us. Indeed, We were to send (a messenger). See 44:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, this is what you used to dispute." See 44:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place. Verily, those who have Taqwa, will be in place of security (44:51). Among Gardens and Springs (44:52). Dressed in Sundus and Istabraq, facing each other (44:53). So (it will be). And We shall marry them to Hur (fair females) with wide lovely eyes (44:54). They will call therein for every kind of fruit in peace and security (44:55). They will never taste death therein except the first death, and He will save them from the torment of the blazing Fire (44:56). As a bounty from your Lord! That will be the supreme success (44:57). Certainly, We have made this easy in your tongue, in order that they may remember (44:58). Wait then; verily, they (too) are waiting (44:59).The State of Those Who have Taqwa and the Delights.They will Enjoy in ParadiseWhen…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Within gardens and springs. See 44:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Wearing (garments of) fine silk and brocade, facing each other. See 44:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Thus. And We will marry them to fair women with large, (beautiful) eyes. See 44:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will call therein for every (kind of) fruit - safe and secure. See 44:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will not taste death therein except the first death, and He will have protected them from the punishment of Hellfire. See 44:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: As bounty from your Lord. That is what is the great attainment. See 44:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, We have eased it (i.e., the Qur’ān) in your tongue that they might be reminded. See 44:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So watch, (O Muḥammad); indeed, they are watching (for your end). See 44:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: As mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing. See 44:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Lord of the heavens and the earth and that between them, if you would be certain. See 44:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death. (He is) your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers. See 44:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But they are in doubt, amusing themselves. Nay! They play about in doubt (44:9). Then wait you for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke (44:10). Covering mankind, this is a painful torment (44:11). (They will say): "Our Lord! Remove the torment from us, really we shall become believers! (44:12). How can there be for them an admonition, when a Messenger explaining things clearly has already come to them (44:13). Then they had turned away from him and said: "(He is) one taught, a madman! (44:14). Verily, We shall remove the torment for a while. Verily, you will revert (44:15). On the Day when We shall strike you with the great Batshah. Verily, We will exact retribution (44:16).Alarming the Idolators with News of the Day When the Sky will Bring forth a Visible SmokeAllah says, these…

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By the (winds) scattering (dust), dispersing (it). يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ(It will be) a Day when they will be Yuftanun in the Fire!Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan and several others said that Yuftanun means punished. Mujahid said: "Just as gold is forged in the fire." A group of others also including Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Ibrahim An-Nakha'i, Zayd bin Aslam, and Sufyan Ath-Thawri said, "They will be burnt."ذُوقُوا فِتْنَتَكُمْTaste you your trial!Mujahid said, "Your burning" while others said, "Your punishment."هَٰذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَThis is what you used to ask to be hastened!This will be said admonishing, chastising, humiliating and belittling them. Allah knows best.

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Destroyed are the misinformers.1 See 51:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Who are within a flood (of confusion) and heedless. See 51:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They ask, "When is the Day of Recompense?" See 51:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (It is) the Day they will be tormented over the Fire. See 51:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (And will be told), "Taste your torment. This is that for which you were impatient." See 51:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs. Verily, those who have Taqwa will be in the midst of Gardens and Springs (51:15). Taking joy in the things which their Lord has given them. Verily, they were before this doers of good (51:16). They used to sleep but little by night (51:17). And in the hours before dawn, they were asking for forgiveness (51:18). And in their wealth there was the right of the Sa'il and the Mahrum (51:19). And on the earth are signs for those who have faith with certainty (51:20). And also in yourselves. Will you not then see (51:21). And in the heaven is your provision, and that which you are promised (51:22). Then by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is the truth, just as you can speak (51:23).Qualities of Those…

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Accepting what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good. See 51:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They used to sleep but little of the night.1 See 51:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness. See 51:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And from their properties was (given) the right of the (needy) petitioner and the deprived. See 51:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the (clouds) carrying a load (of water). See 51:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And on the earth are signs for the certain (in faith). See 51:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And in yourselves. Then will you not see? See 51:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And in the heaven is your provision and whatever you are promised. See 51:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then by the Lord of the heaven and earth, indeed, it is truth - just as (sure as) it is that you are speaking. See 51:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Has there reached you the story of the honored guests of Ibrahim?1. Has the story reached you, of the honored guests of Ibrahim (51:24). When they came in to him and said: "Salaman!" He answered: "Salamun" and said: "You are a people unknown to me (51:25). Then he turned to his household, and brought out a roasted calf (51:26). And placed it before them (saying): "Will you not eat? (51:27). Then he conceived fear of them (when they ate not). They said: "Fear not." And they gave him glad tidings of a son having knowledge (51:28). Then his wife came forward with a loud voice; she smote her face, and said: "A barren old woman! (51:29). They said: "Even so says your Lord. Verily, He is the All-Wise, the All-Knower (51:30).The Guests of the Prophet IbrahimWe mentioned this story before…

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When they entered upon him and said, "(We greet you with) peace." He answered, "(And upon you) peace; (you are) a people unknown." See 51:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then he went to his family and came with a fat (roasted) calf. See 51:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And placed it near them; he said, "Will you not eat?" See 51:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he felt from them apprehension.1 They said, "Fear not," and gave him good tidings of a learned boy. See 51:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And his wife approached with a cry (of alarm) and struck her face and said, "(I am) a barren old woman!" See 51:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the ships sailing with ease. See 51:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Thus has said your Lord; indeed, He is the Wise, the Knowing." See 51:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Ibrahim) said, "Then what is your business (here), O messengers?" (Ibrahim) said: "Then for what purpose you have come, O messengers? (51:31). They said: "We have been sent to a people who are criminals (51:32). "To send down upon them stones of clay (51:33). "Marked by your Lord for transgressors (51:34). So We brought out from therein the believers (51:35). But We found not there any household of the Muslims except one (51:36). And We have left there a sign for those who fear the painful torment (51:37).The Angels were Sent to Destroy the People of the Prophet LutAllah the Exalted said about Ibrahim (AS):فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الرَّوْعُ وَجَاءَتْهُ الْبُشْرَىٰ يُجَادِلُنَا فِي قَوْمِ لُوطٍ - إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لَحَلِيمٌ أَوَّاهٌ مُنِيبٌ - يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَٰذَا ۖ إِنَّهُ قَدْ جَاءَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ ۖ وَإِنَّهُمْ آتِيهِمْ عَذَابٌ غَيْرُ مَرْدُودٍThen when…

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a people of criminals.1 See 51:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: To send down upon them stones of clay. See 51:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Marked in the presence of your Lord for the transgressors." See 51:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So We brought out whoever was in them (i.e., the cities) of the believers. See 51:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We found not within them other than a (single) house of Muslims.1 See 51:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment. See 51:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And in Musa (was a sign), when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority.1 And in Musa, when We sent him to Fir'awn with a manifest authority (51:38). But (he) turned away along with his hosts, and said: "A sorcerer or a madman (51:39). So We took him and his armies, and dumped them into the sea (Yamm), for he was blameworthy (51:40). And in 'Ad when We sent against them the barren wind (51:41). It spared nothing that it reached, but blew it into broken spreads of rotten ruins (51:42). And in Thamud, when they were told: "Enjoy yourselves for a while! (51:43). But they insolently defied the command of their Lord, so the Sa'iqah overtook them while they were looking (51:44). Then they were unable to rise up, nor could they help themselves (51:45). (So were) the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But he turned away with his supporters and said, "A magician or a madman." See 51:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the (angels) apportioning (each) matter. See 51:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So We took him and his soldiers and cast them into the sea, and he was blameworthy. See 51:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And in ʿAad (was a sign), when We sent against them the barren wind.1 See 51:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It left nothing of what it came upon but that it made it like disintegrated ruins. See 51:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And in Thamūd, when it was said to them, "Enjoy yourselves for a time." See 51:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But they were insolent toward the command of their Lord, so the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on. See 51:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they were unable to arise, nor could they defend themselves. See 51:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (We destroyed) the people of Nuh before; indeed, they were a people defiantly disobedient. See 51:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the heaven We constructed with strength,1 and indeed, We are (its) expander. With Hands We constructed the heaven. Verily, We are able to expand the vastness of space thereof (51:47). And We have made the earth a Firash; how excellent spreader (thereof) are We (51:48). And of everything We have created pairs, that you may remember (51:49). So, flee to Allah. Verily, I am a plain warner to you from Him (51:50). And set not up any other god along with Allah. Verily, I am a plain warner to you from Him (51:51).Proofs of Allah's Oneness Abound in the Creation of the Heavens and the EarthAllah reminds us of the creating of the higher and lower worlds:وَالسَّمَاءَ بَنَيْنَاهَاWe constructed the heaven.Meaning: 'We made it as a high roof, protected from falling,'بِأَيْدٍwith HandsWhich is meaning, with strength, according to 'Abdullah…

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the earth We have spread out, and excellent is the preparer. See 51:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And of all things We created two mates (i.e., counterparts); perhaps you will remember. See 51:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, what you are promised is true. See 51:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So flee to Allah.1 Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner. See 51:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And do not make (as equal) with Allah another deity. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner. See 51:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Similarly, there came not to those before them any messenger except that they said, "A magician or a madman." Likewise, no Messenger came to those before them but they said: A sorcerer or a madman! (51:52). Have they transmitted this saying to these? Nay, they are themselves a people transgressing beyond bounds (51:53). So turn away from them, you are not blameworthy (51:54). And remind, for verily, the reminding profits the believers (51:55). And I created not the Jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me (51:56). I seek not any provision from them nor do I ask that they should feed Me (51:57). Verily, Allah is the All-Provider, Owner of power, the Most Strong (51:58). And verily, for those who do wrong, there is a portion of torment like to the evil portion of torment (which came for)…

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Did they suggest it to them?1 Rather, they (themselves) are a transgressing people. See 51:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So leave them, (O Muḥammad), for you are not to be blamed. See 51:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And remind, for indeed, the reminder benefits the believers. See 51:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. See 51:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me. See 51:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, it is Allah who is the (continual) Provider,1 the firm possessor of strength. See 51:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, for those who have wronged is a portion (of punishment) like the portion of their companions (i.e., predecessors), so let them not impatiently urge Me. See 51:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, the recompense is to occur. See 51:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And woe to those who have disbelieved from their Day which they are promised. See 51:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By the heaven containing pathways.1 See 51:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, you are in differing speech.1 See 51:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Deluded away from it (i.e., the Qur’ān) is he who is deluded. See 51:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By the racers, panting.1 إِنَّ رَبَّهُم بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّخَبِيرٌVerily, that Day their Lord will be Well-Acquainted with them.Meaning: He knows all of that they used to do, and He will compensate them for it with the most deserving reward. He does not do even the slightest amount of injustice.This is the end of the Tafsir of Surat Al-'Adiyat, and all praise and thanks are due to Allah.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that within the breasts is obtained.1 See 100:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, their Lord with them, that Day, is (fully) Aware.1 See 100:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the producers of sparks (when) striking.1 See 100:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the chargers at dawn.1 See 100:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Stirring up thereby (clouds of) dust. See 100:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Arriving thereby in the center1 collectively. See 100:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed mankind, to his Lord, is ungrateful. See 100:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, he is to that a witness.1 See 100:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed he is, in love of wealth, intense. See 100:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But does he not know that when the contents of the graves are scattered. See 100:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Ḥā, Meem.1 وَإِذَا حُشِرَ النَّاسُ كَانُوا لَهُمْ أَعْدَاءً وَكَانُوا بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ كَافِرِينَAnd when mankind are gathered, they will become their enemies and will deny their worship.This is similar to Allah's saying:وَاتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ آلِهَةً لِيَكُونُوا لَهُمْ عِزًّا - كَلَّا ۚ سَيَكْفُرُونَ بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدًّاThey have taken gods beside Allah, that they might give them dignity. No! They will deny their worship of them, and will be opponents to them. (19:81-82)Meaning: they will betray them when they need them the most. (Ibrahim) Al-Khalil (AS), said:إِنَّمَا اتَّخَذْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْثَانًا مَوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ۖ ثُمَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يَكْفُرُ بَعْضُكُمْ بِبَعْضٍ وَيَلْعَنُ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضًا وَمَأْوَاكُمُ النَّارُ وَمَا لَكُمْ مِنْ نَاصِرِينَYou have taken only idols besides Allah! The love between you is only in the life of this world. On the Day of Resurrection, you shall disown each other and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Have you considered: if it (i.e., the Qur’ān) was from Allah, and you disbelieved in it while a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something similar1 and believed while you were arrogant...?"2 Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. Say: Tell me! If it was from Allah and you disbelieved it, (at the same time), a witness from among the Children of Israel has testified to something similar and believed while you rejected (the truth)!" Verily, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people (46:10). And those who disbelieve say of those who believe: "Had it been a good thing, they (the poor believers) would not have preceded us to it!" And when they have not been guided by it, they say: "This is ancient falsehood! (46:11). And before this was the Scripture of Musa as…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who disbelieve say of those who believe, "If it had (truly) been good, they would not have preceded us to it." And when they are not guided by it, they will say, "This is an ancient falsehood." See 46:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And before it was the scripture of Musa to lead and as a mercy. And this is a confirming Book in an Arabic tongue to warn those who have wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good. See 46:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained on a right course - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. See 46:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein as reward for what they used to do. See 46:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his gestation and weaning (period) is thirty months. (He grows) until, when he reaches maturity and reaches (the age of) forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me1 to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to work righteousness of which You will approve and make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims." And We have enjoined on man to be dutiful and kind to his parents. His mother bears him with hardship. And she delivers him with hardship. And (the period of) his gestation and the weaning of him is thirty months, till when…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those are the ones from whom We will accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds, (their being) among the companions of Paradise. (That is) the promise of truth which they had been promised. See 46:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But one who says to his parents, "Uff1 to you; do you promise me that I will be brought forth (from the earth) when generations before me have already passed on (into oblivion)?" while they call to Allah for help (and to their son), "Woe to you! Believe! Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth." But he says, "This is not but legends of the former peoples". But he who says to his parents: "Uff to you! Do you promise me that I will be raised up when generations before me have passed?" While they invoke Allah for help: "Woe to you! Believe! Verily, the promise of Allah is true." But he says: "This is nothing but the legends of the ancient (46:17). They are those against whom the Word (of torment) has justified among the previous generations of Jinn…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those are the ones upon whom the word (i.e., decree) has come into effect, (who will be) among nations which had passed on before them of jinn and men. Indeed, they (all) were losers. See 46:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And for all there are degrees (of reward and punishment) for what they have done, and (it is) so that He may fully compensate them for their deeds, and they will not be wronged. See 46:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. See 46:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the Day those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire (it will be said), "You exhausted your pleasures during your worldly life and enjoyed them, so this Day you will be awarded the punishment of (extreme) humiliation because you were arrogant upon the earth without right and because you were defiantly disobedient." See 46:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And mention, (O Muḥammad), the brother of ʿAad,1 when he warned his people in (the region of) al-Aḥqāf - and warners had already passed on before him and after him - (saying), "Do not worship except Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible day."2 And remember the brother of 'Ad, when he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf. And surely, warners had already passed on before him and after him (saying): Worship none but Allah; truly, I fear for you the torment of a mighty Day (46:21). They said: "Have you come to delude us from our gods? Then bring us that with which you threaten us, if you are one of the truthful! (46:22). He said: "The knowledge (of that) is only with Allah. And I convey to you that wherewith I have been sent, but…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Have you come to delude us away from our gods? Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful." See 46:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Knowledge (of its time) is only with Allah, and I convey to you that with which I was sent; but I see you (to be) a people behaving ignorantly." See 46:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain!" Rather, it is that for which you were impatient:1 a wind, within it a painful punishment. See 46:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Destroying everything by command of its Lord. And they became so that nothing was seen (of them) except their dwellings. Thus do We recompense the criminal people. See 46:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We had certainly established them in such as We have not established you, and We made for them hearing and vision and hearts (i.e., intellect). But their hearing and vision and hearts availed them not from anything (of the punishment) when they were (continually) rejecting the signs of Allah; and they were enveloped by what they used to ridicule. And indeed We had firmly established them with that wherewith We have not established you! We also gave them hearing, vision, and hearts. But their hearing, vision, and hearts availed them nothing since they used to deny the Ayat of Allah, and they were completely encircled by that which they used to ridicule (46:26). And indeed We have destroyed towns round about you, and We have shown (them) the signs in various ways so that they might return (46:27). As…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have already destroyed what surrounds you of (those) cities, and We have diversified the signs (or verses) that perhaps they might return (from disbelief). See 46:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then why did those they took besides Allah as deities by which to approach (Him)1 not aid them? But they had strayed (i.e., departed) from them. And that was their falsehood and what they were inventing. See 46:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention, O Muḥammad), when We directed to you a few of the jinn, listening to the Qur’ān. And when they attended it, they said, "Listen attentively." And when it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners. And (remember) when We sent toward you a group of the Jinn, to listen to the Qur'an. When they attended it, they said: Listen quietly!" And when it was concluded, they returned to their people, as warners (46:29). They said: "O our people! Verily, we have heard a Book sent down after Musa, confirming what came before it, it guides to the truth and to the straight path (46:30). "O our people! Respond to Allah's Caller, and believe in him. He (Allah) will forgive you some of your sins, and protect you from a painful torment (46:31). "And whosoever does…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: We did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them except in truth and (for) a specified term. But those who disbelieve, from that of which they are warned, are turning away. See 46:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "O our people, indeed we have heard a (recited) Book revealed after Musa confirming what was before it which guides to the truth and to a straight path. See 46:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O our people, respond to the Caller (i.e., Messenger) of Allah1 and believe in him; He (i.e., Allah) will forgive for you your sins and protect you from a painful punishment. See 46:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But he who does not respond to the Caller of Allah will not cause failure (to Him) upon earth, and he will not have besides Him any protectors. Those are in manifest error." See 46:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and earth and did not fail in their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes. Indeed, He is over all things competent. Do they not see that Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth, and was not wearied by their creation, is Able to give life to the dead Yes, He surely is Able to do all things (46:33). And on the Day when those who disbelieve will be exposed to the Fire (it will be said to them): Is this not the truth?" They will say: "Yes, by our Lord!" He will say: "Then taste the torment, because you used to disbelieve! (46:34). Therefore be patient as did those of determination among the Messengers and be in no hurry for them. On the Day when…
