See they not that We gradually reduce the land from its outlying borders Is it then they who will overcome (21:44). Say: I warn you only by the revelation. "But the deaf will not hear the call, (even) when they are warned (21:45). And if a breath of the torment of your Lord touches them, they will surely cry: "Woe unto us! Indeed we have been wrongdoers (21:46). And We shall set up Balances of justice…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "I only warn you by revelation." But the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned. See 21:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if (as much as) a whiff of the punishment of your Lord should touch them, they would surely say, "O woe to us! Indeed, we have been wrongdoers." See 21:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We place the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be treated unjustly at all. And if there is (even) the weight of a mustard seed,1 We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountant. See 21:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We had already given Musa and Harun the criterion and a light and a reminder1 for the righteous. And indeed We granted to Musa and Harun the criterion, and a shining light and a Reminder for those who have Taqwa (21:48). Those who fear their Lord in the unseen, and they are afraid of the Hour (21:49). And this is a blessed Reminder which We have sent down; will you then deny it (21:50).The Revelation of the Tawrah and the Qur'anWe have already noted that Allah often mentions Musa and Muhammad together – may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon them both – and He often mentions their Books together as well. He says:وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَهَارُونَ الْفُرْقَانَAnd indeed We granted to Musa and Harun the criterionMujahid said, "This means the Scripture." Abu Salih said: "The Tawrah."…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Who fear their Lord unseen,1 while they are of the Hour apprehensive. See 21:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But they say, "(The revelation is but) a mixture of false dreams; rather, he has invented it; rather, he is a poet. So let him bring us a sign just as the previous (messengers) were sent (with miracles)." See 21:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And this (Qur’ān) is a blessed message which We have sent down. Then are you with it unacquainted?1 See 21:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We had certainly given Ibrahim his sound judgement before,1 and We were of him well-Knowing. And indeed We bestowed aforetime on Ibrahim his guidance, and We were Well-Acquainted with him (21:51). When he said to his father and his people: What are these images to which you are devoted? (21:52). They said: "We found our fathers worshipping them (21:53). He said: "Indeed you and your fathers have been in manifest error (21:54). They said: "Have you brought us the Truth, or are you one of those who play about?? (21:55). He said: "Nay, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who created them and to that I am one of the witnesses (21:56).The Story of Ibrahim and his PeopleAllah tells us about His close Friend Ibrahim (AS), and how He bestowed upon him guidance aforetime,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?" See 21:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "We found our fathers worshippers of them." See 21:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "You were certainly, you and your fathers, in manifest error." See 21:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Have you come to us with truth, or are you of those who jest?" See 21:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "(No), rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth who created them, and I, to that, am of those who testify. See 21:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (I swear) by Allah, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned and gone away." "And by Allah, I shall plot a plan for your idols after you have gone away and turned your backs (21:57). So he broke them to pieces, except the biggest of them, that they might turn to it (21:58). They said: "Who has done this to our gods He must indeed be one of the wrongdoers (21:59). They said: "We heard a young man talking against them, who is called Ibrahim (21:60). They said: "Then bring him before the eyes of the people, that they may testify (21:61). They said: "Are you the one who has done this to our gods, O Ibrahim? (21:62). He said: "Nay, this one, the biggest of them did it. Ask them, if they can speak!…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So he made them into fragments, except a large one among them, that they might return to it (and question). See 21:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers." See 21:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Not a (single) city which We destroyed believed before them,1 so will they believe? See 21:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "We heard a young man mention them who is called Ibrahim." See 21:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people that they may testify."1 See 21:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Have you done this to our gods, O Ibrahim?" See 21:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Rather, this - the largest of them - did it, so ask them, if they should (be able to) speak." See 21:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So they returned to (blaming) themselves and said (to each other), "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers." So they turned to themselves and said: "Verily, you are the wrongdoers (21:64). Then they turned to themselves: "Indeed you know well that these speak not! (21:65). He said: "Do you then worship besides Allah, things that can neither profit you nor harm you? (21:66). "Fie upon you, and upon that which you worship besides Allah! Have you then no sense? (21:67).The People's Admission of their Gods' Incapability, and Ibrahim's PreachingAllah tells us that when Ibrahim said what he said, his people:فَرَجَعُوا إِلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْturned to themselvesMeaning: they blamed themselves for not taking precautions and protecting their gods. They said:إِنَّكُمْ أَنتُمُ الظَّالِمُونَVerily, you are the wrongdoersi.e., because you neglected them and did not guard them.ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمْThen they turned to themselvesmeans, they looked at…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then they reversed themselves,1 (saying), "You have already known that these do not speak!" See 21:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Then do you worship instead of Allah that which does not benefit you at all or harm you? See 21:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Uff1 to you and to what you worship instead of Allah. Then will you not use reason?" See 21:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Burn him and support your gods - if you are to act." They said: "Burn him and help your gods, if you will be doing (21:68). We said: "O fire! Be you cool and safety for Ibrahim! (21:69). And they wanted to harm him, but We made them the worst losers (21:70).How Ibrahim was Thrown into the Fire and How Allah Controlled itWhen their arguments were refuted and their incapability became clear, when truth was made manifest and falsehood was defeated, they resorted to using their power and strength, and said:حَرِّقُوهُ وَانصُرُوا آلِهَتَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ فَاعِلِينَ"Burn him and help your gods, if you will be doing."So they gathered together a huge amount of wood.As-Suddi said, "I if a woman was sick, she would make a vow that if she recovered she would bring wood to burn Ibrahim. Then…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: We (i.e., Allah) said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim." See 21:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We sent not before you, (O Muḥammad), except men to whom We revealed (the message), so ask the people of the message (i.e., former scriptures) if you do not know. And We sent not before you but men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know (21:7). And We did not place them in bodies that did not eat food, nor were they immortals (21:8). Then We fulfilled to them the promise. So We saved them and those whom We willed, but We destroyed Al-Musrifin (21:9).The Messengers are No More than Human BeingsHere Allah refutes those who denied that human Messengers could be sent:وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُّوحِي إِلَيْهِمْAnd We sent not before you but men to whom We revealed.Meaning: all the Messengers who came before you were men, human…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:70 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they intended for him a plan (i.e., harm), but We made them the greatest losers. See 21:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We delivered him and Lut to the land which We had blessed for the worlds (i.e., peoples). And We rescued him and Lut to the land which We have blessed for the nations (21:71). And We bestowed upon him Ishaq, and Ya'qub Nafilatan. Each one We made righteous (21:72). And We made them leaders, guiding by Our command, and We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, performing Salah, and the giving of Zakah, and of Us (Alone) they were the worshippers (21:73). And (remember) Lut, We gave him wisdom and knowledge, and We saved him from the town who practised Al-Khaba'ith. Verily, they were a people given to evil, and were rebellious (21:74). And We admitted him to Our mercy; truly, he was of the righteous (21:75).The Migration of Ibrahim to Ash-Sham (Greater Syria), Accompanied by LutAllah…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:72 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub in addition, and all (of them) We made righteous. See 21:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:73 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We made them leaders guiding by Our command. And We inspired to them the doing of good deeds, establishment of prayer, and giving of zakāh; and they were worshippers of Us. See 21:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to Lut We gave judgement and knowledge, and We saved him from the city that was committing wicked deeds. Indeed, they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient. See 21:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was of the righteous. See 21:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:76 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) Nuh, when he called (to Allah)1 before (that time), so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great affliction (i.e., the flood). And (remember) Nuh, when he cried (to Us) aforetime. We answered to his invocation and saved him and his family from the great distress (21:76). We helped him against the people who denied Our Ayat. Verily, they were a people given to evil. So We drowned them all (21:77).Nuh and His PeopleAllah tells us how He responded to His servant and Messenger Nuh (AS), when he prayed to Him against his people for their disbelief in him:فَدَعَا رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ فَانتَصِرْThen he invoked his Lord (saying): "I have been overcome, so help (me)!" (54:10)وَقَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ دَيَّارًا - إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوا…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:77 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We aided (i.e., saved) him from the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them, all together. See 21:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:78 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) Dawud and Sulayman, when they judged concerning the field - when the sheep of a people overran it (at night),1 and We were witness to their judgement. And (remember) Dawud and Sulayman, when they gave judgement in the case of the field in which the sheep of certain people had Nafashat; and We were witness to their judgement (21:78). And We made Sulayman to understand (the case); and to each of them We gave wisdom (Hukm) and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains and the birds to glorify Our praises along with Dawud. And it was We Who were the doer (of all these things) (21:79). And We taught him the making of metal coats of mail (for battles), to protect you in your fighting. Are you then grateful (21:80). And to Sulayman (We subjected) the wind strongly…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:79 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We gave understanding of it (i.e., the case) to Sulayman, and to each (of them) We gave judgement and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to exalt (Us), along with Dawud and (also) the birds. And We were doing (that).1 See 21:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We did not make them (i.e., the prophets) forms not eating food,1 nor were they immortal (on earth). See 21:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:80 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We taught him the fashioning of coats of armor to protect you from your (enemy in) battle. So will you then be grateful? See 21:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:81 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to Sulayman (We subjected) the wind, blowing forcefully, proceeding by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever, of all things, Knowing. See 21:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:82 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And of the devils (i.e., jinn) were those who dived for him and did work other than that. And We were of them a guardian.1 See 21:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:83 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) Ayyub, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful." And (remember) Ayyub, when he cried to his Lord: Verily, distress has seized me, and You are the Most Merciful of all those who show mercy (21:83). So We answered his call, and We removed the distress that was on him, and We restored his family to him, and the like thereof along with them as a mercy from Ourselves and a Reminder for all those who worship Us (21:84).The Prophet AyyubAllah tells us about Ayyub, and the trials that struck him, affecting his wealth, children and physical health. He had plenty of livestock, cattle and crops, many children and beautiful houses, and he was tested in these things, losing everything he had. Then he was tested…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:84 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity. And We gave him (back) his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers (of Allah). See 21:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:85 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) Ismail and Idrees and Dhul-Kifli; all were of the patient. And (remember) Ismail, Idris and Dhul-Kifli: All were from among the patient (21:85). And We admitted them to Our mercy. Verily, they were of the righteous (21:86).Ismail, Idris and Dhul-KifliIsmail was the son of Ibrahim Al-Khalil (AS). He has already been mentioned in Surah Maryam, where mention was also made of Idris. From the context and the fact that Dhul-Kifli is mentioned alongside Prophets, it appears that he was also a Prophet. Others say that he was a righteous man, a just king and a fair judge. Ibn Jarir refrained from making any decisive comment. And Allah knows best.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:86 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were of the righteous. See 21:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:87 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) the man of the fish (i.e., Yunus), when he went off in anger1 and thought that We would not decree (anything) upon him.2 And he called out within the darknesses,3 "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers." And (remember) Dhun-Nun, when he went off in anger, and imagined that We shall not punish him! But he cried through the darknesses (Zulumat) (saying): There is no God but You, Glorified be You! Truly, I have been of the Zalimin wrongdoers (21:87). So We answered his call, and delivered him from the distress. And thus We do deliver the believers (21:88).YunusThis story is mentioned here, and in Surat As-Saffat and Surah Nun. Yunus bin Matta, upon him be peace, was sent by Allah to the people of Nineveh, which was a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:88 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers. See 21:87

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:89 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) Zakariyya, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone (with no heir), while You are the best of inheritors." And (remember) Zakariyya, when he cried to his Lord: O My Lord! Leave me not single (childless), though You are the Best of the inheritors (21:89). So We answered his call, and We bestowed upon him Yahya, and cured his wife for him. Verily, they used to hasten on to do good deeds, and they used to call on Us with hope and fear, and they were Khashi'in before Us (21:90).Zakariyya and YahyaAllah tells us of His servant Zakariyya, who asked Allah to grant him a son who would be a Prophet after him. The story has already been given in detail at the beginning of Surah Maryam and also in Surah 'Imran. Here…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then1 We fulfilled for them the promise, and We saved them and whom We willed and destroyed the transgressors. See 21:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:90 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So We responded to him, and We gave to him Yahya, and amended for him his wife. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate1 Us in hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive. See 21:89

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:91 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) the one who guarded her chastity (i.e., Maryam), so We blew into her (garment) through Our angel (i.e., Jibril), and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds. And she who guarded her chastity, We breathed into her through Our Ruh, and We made her and her son a sign for nations (21:91).Isa and Maryam the True BelieverHere Allah mentions the story of Maryam and her son Isa, just after mentioning Zakariyya and his son Yahya (AS). He mentions the story of Zakariyya first, followed by the story of Maryam because the one is connected to the other. The former is the story of a child being born to an old man of advanced years, from an old woman who had been barren and had never given birth when she was younger. Then Allah mentions…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:92 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed this, your religion, is one religion,1 and I am your Lord, so worship Me. Truly, this, your Ummah is one, and I am your Lord, therefore worship Me (21:92). But they have broken up and differed in their religion among themselves. (And) they all shall return to Us (21:93). So whoever does righteous good deeds while he is a believer, his efforts will not be rejected. Verily, We record it for him (in his Book of deeds) (21:94).Mankind is One Ummahإِنَّ هَٰذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةًTruly, this, your Ummah is one,Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Qatadah and 'Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd bin Aslam said, "Your religion is one religion." Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: "In this Ayah, Allah explains to them what they should avoid and what they should do." Then He said:إِنَّ هَٰذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةًTruly, this, your Ummah is one…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:93 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (yet) they divided their affair (i.e., that of their religion) among themselves,1 (but) all to Us will return. See 21:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:94 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer - no denial will there be for his effort,1 and indeed We (i.e., Our angels), of it, are recorders. See 21:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:95 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it is prohibited to (the people of) a city which We have destroyed that they will (ever) return.1 And a ban is laid on every town which We have destroyed that they shall not return (21:95). Until, when Ya'juj and Ma'juj (Gog and Magog people) are let loose, and they swoop down from every Hadab (21:96). And the true promise shall draw near. Then, you shall see the eyes of the disbelievers fixedly staring in horror. (They will say:) Woe to us! We were indeed heedless of this – nay, but we were wrongdoers (21:97). Those who have been destroyed, will never return to this World.وَحَرَامٌ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍAnd a ban is laid on every townIbn 'Abbas said, "it is enforced", i.e., it has been decreed that the people of each township that has been destroyed will never return to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:96 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Until when (the dam of) Gog and Magog has been opened and they, from every elevation, descend. See 21:95

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:97 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (when) the true promise (i.e., the resurrection) has approached; then suddenly the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring (in horror, while they say), "O woe to us; we had been unmindful of this; rather, we were wrongdoers." See 21:95

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:98 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, you (disbelievers) and what you worship other than Allah are the firewood of Hell. You will be coming to (enter) it. Certainly you and that which you are worshipping now besides Allah, are (but) fuel (Hasab) for Hell! (Surely) you will enter it (21:98). Had these been gods, they would not have entered there (Hell), and all of them will abide therein forever (21:99). Therein they will be breathing out with deep sighs and roaring and therein they will hear not (21:100). Verily, those for whom the good has preceded from Us, they will be removed far therefrom (Hell) (21:101). They shall not hear the slightest sound of it (Hell), while they abide in that which their own selves desire (21:102). The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will meet them, (with the greeting:) This is…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:99 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Had these (false deities) been (actual) gods, they would not have come to it, but all are eternal therein. See 21:98

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They ask you, (O Muḥammad), about the bounties (of war). Say, "The (decision concerning) bounties is for Allah and the Messenger." So fear Allah and amend that which is between you and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you should be believers.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah made it not but good tidings and so that your hearts would be assured thereby. And victory is not but from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise. See 8:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Remember) when He overwhelmed you with drowsiness (giving) security from Him and sent down upon you from the sky, rain by which to purify you and remove from you the evil (suggestions) of Satan and to make steadfast your hearts and plant firmly thereby your feet. (Remember) when He covered you with a slumber as a security from Him, and He caused water (rain) to descend on you from the sky, to clean you thereby and to remove from you the Rijz (whispering or dirt) of Shaytan, and to strengthen your hearts, and make your feet firm thereby (8:11). (Remember) when your Lord revealed to the angels, Verily, I am with you, so keep firm those who have believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who have disbelieved, so strike them over the necks, and smite over…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Remember) when your Lord inspired to the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike (them) upon the necks and strike from them every fingertip."1 See 8:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger - indeed, Allah is severe in penalty. See 8:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: "That (is yours), so taste it." And indeed for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire. See 8:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing (in battle), do not turn to them your backs (in flight). O you who believe! When you meet those who disbelieve, in a battlefield, never turn your backs to them (8:15). And whoever turns his back to them on such a day – unless it be a stratagem of war, or to retreat to a troop (of his own) – he indeed has drawn upon himself wrath from Allah. And his abode is Hell, and worst indeed is that destination (8:16).Fleeing from Battle is Prohibited, and its PunishmentAllah said, while warning against fleeing from the battlefield and threatening those who do it with the Fire:يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا لَقِيتُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا زَحْفًاO you who believe! When you meet those who disbelieve, in a battlefield,when you get near…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever turns his back to them on such a day, unless swerving (as a strategy) for war or joining (another) company, has certainly returned with anger (upon him) from Allah, and his refuge is Hell - and wretched is the destination. See 8:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you did not kill them, but it was Allah who killed them.1 And you threw not, (O Muḥammad), when you threw, but it was Allah who threw2 that He might test the believers with a good test.3 Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing. You killed them not, but Allah killed them. And you threw not when you did throw, but Allah threw, that He might test the believers by a fair trial from Him. Verily, Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower (8:17). This (is the fact) and surely Allah weakens the deceitful plots of the disbelievers (8:18).Allah's Signs Displayed during Badr, And Throwing Sand in the Eyes of the DisbelieversAllah states that He creates the actions that the servants perform and that whatever good actions they take, it is He Who should be praised for them, for He directed and helped…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That (is so), and (also) that Allah will weaken the plot of the disbelievers. See 8:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: If you (disbelievers) seek the decision (i.e., victory) - the decision (i.e., defeat) has come to you. And if you desist (from hostilities), it is best for you; but if you return (to war), We will return, and never will you be availed by your (large) company at all, even if it should increase; and (that is) because Allah is with the believers. (O disbelievers) if you ask for a judgement, now has the judgement come unto you; and if you cease (to do wrong), it will be better for you, and if you return (to the attack), so shall We return, and your forces will be of no avail to you, however numerous they be; and verily, Allah is with the believers (8:19).The Response to the Disbelievers Who Ask for a JudgementAllah says to the disbeliever:إِن تَسْتَفْتِحُواIf you ask…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith; and upon their Lord they rely. The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, feel a fear in their hearts and when His Ayat are recited unto them, they increase their faith; and they put their trust in their Lord (8:2). Who perform the Salah and spend out of what We have provided them (8:3). It is they who are the believers in truth. For them are grades of dignity with their Lord, and forgiveness and a generous provision (Paradise) (8:4).Qualities of the Faithful and Truthful BelieversAli bin Abi Talhah reported that Ibn 'Abbas said about the Ayah:إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْThe believers are only those who, when…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger and do not turn from him while you hear (his order). O you who believe! Obey Allah and His Messenger, and turn not away from him while you are hearing (8:20). And be not like those who say: "We have heard," but they hear not (8:21). Verily, the worst of living creatures with Allah are the deaf and the dumb (the disbelievers), who understand not (8:22). Had Allah known of any good in them, He would indeed have made them listen; and even if He had made them listen, they would but have turned away with aversion (8:23).The Command to Obey Allah and His Messenger SAWAllah commands His believing servants to obey Him and His Messenger SAW and warns them against defying him and imitating the disbelievers who reject him.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And do not be like those who say, "We have heard," while they do not hear. See 8:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not use reason (i.e., the disbelievers). See 8:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would (still) have turned away, while they were refusing. See 8:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart and that to Him you will be gathered. O you who believe! Answer Allah and (His) Messenger when he (the Messenger) calls you to that which will give you life, and know that Allah comes between a person and his heart. And verily to Him you shall (all) be gathered (8:24).The Command to Answer and Obey Allah and His Messenger SAWAl-Bukhari said:اسْتَجِيبُواAnswerWhich is obey:لِمَا يُحْيِيكُمْthat which will give you lifethat which will make your affairs good." Al-Bukhari went on to narrate that Abu Sa'id bin Al-Mu'alla said, "I was praying when the Prophet SAW passed by and called me, but I did not answer him until I…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And fear a trial1 which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively, and know that Allah is severe in penalty. And fear the Fitnah (affliction and trial) which affects not in particular (only) those of you who do wrong, and know that Allah is severe in punishment (8:25).Warning against an Encompassing FitnahAllah warns His believing servants of a Fitnah, trial and test, that encompasses the wicked and those around them. Therefore, such Fitnah will not be restricted to the sinners and evildoers. Rather, it will reach the others if the sins are not stopped and prevented. Imam Ahmad recorded that Mutarrif said, We asked Az-Zubayr, 'O Abu 'Abdullah! What brought you here (for the battle of Al-Jamal)? You abandoned the Khalifah who was assassinated (Uthman (RA)) and then came asking for revenge for his blood' He said,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people might abduct you, but He sheltered you, supported you with His victory, and provided you with good things - that you might be grateful. And remember when you were few and were reckoned weak in the land, and were afraid that men might kidnap you, but He provided a safe place for you, strengthened you with His help, and provided you with good things (for livelihood) so that you might be grateful (8:26).Reminding Muslims of Their Previous State of Weakness and Subjugation which Changed into Might and TriumphAllah, the Exalted, reminds His believing servants of His blessings and favors on them. They were few and He made them many, weak and fearful and He provided them with strength and victory. They were meek and poor, and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know (the consequence). O you who believe! Betray not Allah and His Messenger, nor betray knowingly your Amanat (things entrusted to you) (8:27). And know that your possessions and your children are but a trial and that surely, with Allah is a mighty reward (8:28).Reason behind Revealing This Ayah, and the Prohibition of BetrayalThe Two Sahihs mention the story of Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah. In the year of the victory of Makkah he wrote to the Quraysh alerting them that the Messenger of Allah SAW intended to march towards them. Allah informed His Messenger SAW of this, and he sent a Companion to retrieve the letter that Hatib sent, and then he summoned him. He admitted to what he did. Umar bin…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And know that your properties and your children are but a trial and that Allah has with Him a great reward. See 8:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion1 and will remove from you your misdeeds and forgive you. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty. O you who believe! If you obey and fear Allah, He will grant you Furqan, and will expiate for you your sins, and forgive you; and Allah is the Owner of the great bounty (8:29).Ibn 'Abbas, As-Suddi, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Muqatil bin Hayyan and several others said that:فُرْقَانًاFurqanMeans, 'a way out'; Mujahid added, "In this life and the Hereafter." In another narration, Ibn 'Abbas is reported to have said, 'Furqan' means 'salvation' or – according to another narration – 'aid'. Muhammad bin Ishaq said that 'Furqan' means 'criterion between truth and falsehood'. This last explanation from Ibn Ishaq is more general than the rest that we…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The ones who establish prayer, and from what We have provided them, they spend. See 8:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (remember, O Muḥammad), when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you or kill you or evict you (from Makkah). But they plan, and Allah plans. And Allah is the best of planners. And (remember) when the disbelievers plotted against you to imprison you, or to kill you, or to expel you (from your home, Makkah); they were plotting and Allah too was plotting; and Allah is the best of plotters (8:30).The Makkans Plot to Kill the Prophet SAW, Imprison Him or Expel Him from MakkahIbn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said:لِيُثْبِتُوكَ'Liyuthbitūka'means "to imprison you." As-Suddi said, "Ithbāt is to confine or to shackle."Imam Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar, the author of Al-Maghazi, reported from 'Abdullah bin Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, Some of the chiefs of the various tribes of Quraysh gathered in Dar An-Nadwah (their…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we willed, we could say (something) like this. This is not but legends of the former peoples." And when Our Ayat are recited to them, they say: "We have heard (the Qur'an); if we wish we can say the like of this. This is nothing but the tales of the ancients (8:31). And (remember) when they said: "O Allah! If this (the Qur'an) is indeed the truth (revealed) from You, then rain down stones on us from the sky or bring on us a painful torment (8:32). And Allah would not punish them while you (Muhammad SAW) are among them, nor will He punish them while they seek (Allah's) forgiveness (8:33).The Quraysh Claimed They can Produce Something Similar to the Qur'anAllah describes the disbelief, transgression, rebellion,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (remember) when they said, "O Allah, if this should be the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment." See 8:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But Allah would not punish them while you, (O Muḥammad), are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness. See 8:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But why should Allah not punish them while they obstruct (people) from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām and they were not (fit to be) its guardians? Its (true) guardians are not but the righteous, but most of them do not know. And why should not Allah punish them while they hinder (men) from Al-Masjid Al-Haram, and they are not its guardians? None can be its guardians except those who have Taqwa, but most of them know not (8:34). Their Salah at the House was nothing but Muka' and Tasdiyah. Therefore taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve (8:35).The Idolators Deserved Allah's Torment after Their AtrocitiesAllah states that the idolators deserved the torment, but He did not torment them in honor of the Prophet SAW residing among them. After Allah allowed the Prophet SAW to migrate away from them, He sent His torment…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And their prayer at the House (i.e., the Kaʿbah) was not except whistling and handclapping. So taste the punishment for what you disbelieved (i.e., practiced of deviations). See 8:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert (people) from the way of Allah. So they will spend it; then it will be for them a (source of) regret; then they will be overcome. And those who have disbelieved - unto Hell they will be gathered. Verily, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to hinder (men) from the path of Allah, and so will they continue to spend it; but in the end it will become an anguish for them. Then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve will be gathered unto Hell (8:36). In order that Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good, and put the wicked one over another, heap them together and cast them into Hell. Those! it is they who are the losers (8:37).The Disbelievers Spend Their Wealth to Hinder Others from Allah's…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (It is) so that Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good and place the wicked some of them upon others and heap them all together and put them into Hell. It is those who are the losers. See 8:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say to those who have disbelieved (that) if they cease, what has previously occurred will be forgiven for them. But if they return (to hostility) - then the precedent of the former (rebellious) peoples has already taken place.1 Say to those who have disbelieved, if they cease, their past will be forgiven. But if they return (thereto), then the examples of those (punished) before them have already preceded (as a warning) (8:38). And fight them until there is no more Fitnah, and the religion (worship) will all be for Allah alone. But if they cease, then certainly, Allah is All-Seer of what they do (8:39). And if they turn away, then know that Allah is your protector – (what) an excellent protector and (what) an excellent helper (8:40).Encouraging the Disbelievers to Seek Allah's Forgiveness, Warning Them against DisbeliefAllah commands His…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And fight against them until there is no fitnah1 and (until) the religion (i.e., worship), all of it, is for Allah.2 And if they cease - then indeed, Allah is Seeing of what they do. See 8:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those are the believers, truly. For them are degrees (of high position) with their Lord and forgiveness and noble provision. See 8:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But if they turn away - then know that Allah is your protector. Excellent is the protector, and excellent is the helper. See 8:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And know that anything you obtain of war booty - then indeed, for Allah is one fifth of it and for the Messenger1 and for (his) near relatives2 and the orphans, the needy, and the (stranded) traveler,3 if you have believed in Allah and in that which We sent down to Our Servant4 on the day of criterion (i.e., decisive encounter) - the day when the two armies met (at Badr). And Allah, over all things, is competent. And know that whatever of war booty that you may gain, verily, one-fifth of it is assigned to Allah, and to the Messenger, and to the near relatives (of the Messenger), the orphans, the poor, and the wayfarer, if you have believed in Allah and in that which We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the Day when…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Remember) when you were on the near side of the valley, and they were on the farther side, and the caravan was lower (in position) than you. If you had made an appointment (to meet), you would have missed the appointment. But (it was) so that Allah might accomplish a matter already destined - that those who perished (through disbelief) would perish upon evidence and those who lived (in faith) would live upon evidence; and indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing. (And remember) when you (the Muslim army) were on the near side of the valley, and they on the farther side, and the caravan on the ground lower than you. Even if you had made a mutual appointment to meet, you would certainly have failed in the appointment, but (you met) that Allah might accomplish a matter already ordained…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Remember, O Muḥammad), when Allah showed them to you in your dream as few; and if He had shown them to you as many, you (believers) would have lost courage and would have disputed in the matter (of whether to fight), but Allah saved (you from that). Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts. (And remember) when Allah showed them to you as few in your dream; if He had shown them to you as many, you would surely have been discouraged, and you would surely have disputed in making a decision. But Allah saved (you). Certainly, He is the All-Knower of that is in the breasts (8:43). And (remember) when you met, He showed them to you as few in your eyes and He made you appear as few in their eyes, so that Allah might accomplish…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (remember) when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes, and He made you (appear) as few in their eyes so that Allah might accomplish a matter already destined. And to Allah are (all) matters returned. See 8:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, when you encounter a company (from the enemy forces), stand firm and remember Allah much that you may be successful. O you who believe! When you meet (an enemy) force, take a firm stand against them and remember Allah much, so that you may be successful (8:45). And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute (with one another) lest you lose courage and your strength departs, and be patient. Surely, Allah is with the patients (8:46).Manners of WarAllah instructs His faithful servants in the manners of fighting and methods of courage when meeting the enemy in battle:يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا لَقِيتُمْ فِئَةً فَاثْبُتُواO you who believe! When you meet (an enemy) force, take a firm stand against themIn the Two Sahihs, it is recorded that 'Abdullah bin Abi Awfa said that during…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute and (thus) lose courage and (then) your strength would depart; and be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient. See 8:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And do not be like those who came forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people and avert (them) from the way of Allah. And Allah is encompassing1 of what they do. And be not like those who come out of their homes boastfully and to be seen of men, and hinder (men) from the path of Allah; and Allah is 'Muhīt' (eneompassing and thoroughly comprehending) all that they do (8:47). And (remember) when Shaytan made their (evil) deeds seem fair to them and said, No one of mankind can overcome you this day (of the battle of Badr) and verily, I am your neighbor (for each and every help)." But when the two forces came in sight of each other, he ran away and said "Verily, I have nothing to do with you. Verily, I see…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (remember) when Satan made their deeds pleasing to them and said, "No one can overcome you today from among the people, and indeed, I am your protector." But when the two armies sighted each other, he turned on his heels and said, "Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I see what you do not see; indeed, I fear Allah. And Allah is severe in penalty." See 8:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Remember) when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts was disease (i.e., arrogance and disbelief) said, "Their religion has deluded those (Muslims)." But whoever relies upon Allah - then indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise. See 8:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: [It1 is] just as when your Lord brought you out of your home (for the battle of Badr) in truth, while indeed, a party among the believers were unwilling. As your Lord caused you to go out from your home with the truth; and verily, a party among the believers disliked it (8:5). Disputing with you concerning the truth after it was made manifest, as if they were being driven to death, while they were looking (at it) (8:6). And (remember) when Allah promised you (Muslims) one of the two parties, that it should be yours; you wished that the one not armed should be yours, but Allah willed to justify the truth by His Words and to cut off the roots of the disbelievers (8:7). That He might cause the truth to triumph and bring falsehood to nothing, even…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if you could but see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved...1 They are striking their faces and their backs and (saying), "Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire. And if you could see when the angels take away the souls of those who disbelieve (at death); they smite their faces and their backs, (saying): "Taste the punishment of the blazing Fire (8:50). "This is because of that which your hands forwarded. And verily, Allah is not unjust to His servants (8:51).The Angels Smite the Disbelievers upon Capturing Their SoulsAllah says, if you witnessed the angels capturing the souls of the disbelievers, you would witness a tremendous, terrible, momentous and awful matter:يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبَارَهُمْthey smite their faces and their backsWhich is saying to them:وَذُوقُوا عَذَابَ الْحَرِيقِ"Taste the punishment of the blazing Fire."Ibn Jurayj said that Mujahid…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is for what your hands have put forth (of evil) and because Allah is not ever unjust to (His) servants." See 8:50

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Theirs is) like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and of those before them. They disbelieved in the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and severe in penalty. Similar to the behavior of the people of Fir'awn, and of those before them – they rejected the Ayat of Allah, so Allah punished them for their sins. Verily, Allah is All-Strong, severe in punishment (8:52).Allah says, 'The behavior of these rebellious disbelievers against what I sent you with, O Muhammad, is similar to the behavior of earlier disbelieving nations. So We behaved with them according to Our Da'b, that is, Our behavior (or custom) and way, as We did with them with what We often do and decide concerning their likes, the denying people of Fir'awn and the earlier nations who rejected…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is because Allah would not change a favor which He had bestowed upon a people until they change what is within themselves. And indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing. That is so because Allah will never change a grace which He has bestowed on a people until they change what is in themselves. And verily, Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower (8:53). Similar to the behavior of the people of Fir'awn, and those before them. They belied the Ayat of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins, and We drowned the people of Fir'awn for they were all wrongdoers (8:54).Allah affirms His perfect justice and fairness in His decisions, for He decided that He will not change a bounty that He has granted someone, except on account of an evil that they committed. Allah said in another Ayah:إِنَّ اللَّهَ…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Theirs is) like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and of those before them. They denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins, and We drowned the people of Pharaoh. And all (of them) were wrongdoers. See 8:53

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who have disbelieved, and they will not (ever) believe. Verily, the worst of living creatures before Allah are those who disbelieve, – so they shall not believe (8:55). They are those with whom you made a covenant, but they break their covenant every time and they do not have Taqwa (8:56). So if you gain the mastery over them in war, then disperse those who are behind them, so that they may learn a lesson (8:57).Striking Hard against Those Who Disbelieve and Break the CovenantsAllah states here that the worst moving creatures on the face of the earth are those who disbelieve, who do not embrace the faith, and break promises whenever they make a covenant, even when they vow to keep them:وَهُمْ لَا يَتَّقُونَand they do…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The ones with whom you made a treaty but then they break their pledge every time, and they do not fear Allah. See 8:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So if you, (O Muḥammad), gain dominance over them in war, disperse by (means of) them those behind them that perhaps they will be reminded.1 See 8:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: If you (have reason to) fear from a people betrayal, throw (their treaty) back to them, (putting you) on equal terms.1 Indeed, Allah does not like traitors. If you fear treachery from any people, throw back (their covenant) to them (so as to be) on equal terms. Certainly Allah likes not the treacherous.) make a heading, Allah says to His Prophet (SAW (58)وَإِمَّا تَخَافَنَّ مِن قَوْمٍIf you fear from any peopleWhich is with whom you have a treaty of peace:خِيَانَةًtreacheryAnd betrayal of peace treaties and agreements that you have conducted with them:فَانبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْthen throw back (their covenant) to themWhich is meaning their treaty of peace.عَلَىٰ سَوَاءٍon equal termsInforming them that you are severing the treaty. This way, you will be on equal terms, in that, you and they will be aware that a state of war exists between you and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And let not those who disbelieve think they will escape. Indeed, they will not cause failure (to Allah). And let not those who disbelieve think that they can outstrip (escape from the punishment). Verily, they will never be able to save themselves (from Allah's punishment) (8:59). And make ready against them all you can of power, including steeds of war to threaten the enemy of Allah and your enemy, and others besides them, whom you may not know but whom Allah does know. And whatever you shall spend in the cause of Allah shall be repaid unto you, and you shall not be treated unjustly (8:60).Making Preparations for War to Strike Fear in the Hearts of the Enemies of AllahAllah says to His Prophet SAW, in this Ayah:الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَبَقُواthose who disbelieve think that they can outstripWhich is Do not…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Arguing with you concerning the truth after it had become clear, as if they were being driven toward death while they were looking on. See 8:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war1 by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know (but) whom Allah knows. And whatever you spend in the cause of Allah will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged. See 8:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if they incline to peace, then incline to it (also) and rely upon Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing. But if they incline to peace, you also incline to it, and trust in Allah. Verily, He is the All-Hearer, the All-Knower (8:61). And if they intend to deceive you, then verily, Allah is All-Sufficient for you. He it is Who has supported you with His help and with the believers (8:62). And He has united their (believers') hearts. If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have united their hearts, but Allah has united them. Certainly He is All-Mighty, All-Wise (8:63).The Command to Facilitate Peace When the Enemy Seeks a Peaceful ResolutionAllah says, if you fear betrayal from a clan of people, then sever the peace treaty with them,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But if they intend to deceive you - then sufficient for you is Allah. It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers. See 8:61

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And brought together their hearts. If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together; but Allah brought them together. Indeed, He is Exalted in Might and Wise. See 8:61

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O Prophet, sufficient for you is Allah and for whoever follows you of the believers. O Prophet! Allah is sufficient for you and for the believers who follow you (8:64). O Prophet! Urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty steadfast persons among you, they will overcome two hundred, and if there be a hundred steadfast persons they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they (the disbelievers) are people who do not understand (8:65). Now Allah has lightened your (task), for He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are of you a hundred steadfast persons, they shall overcome two hundred, and if there are a thousand of you, they shall overcome two thousand by the leave of Allah. And Allah is with the patient (8:66).Encouraging Believers to Fight in Jihad; the Good…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O Prophet, urge the believers to battle. If there are among you twenty (who are) steadfast, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are among you one hundred (who are steadfast), they will overcome a thousand of those who have disbelieved because they are a people who do not understand. See 8:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Now, Allah has lightened (the hardship) for you, and He knows that among you is weakness. So if there are from you one hundred (who are) steadfast, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two thousand by permission of Allah. And Allah is with the steadfast. See 8:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is not for a prophet to have captives (of war) until he inflicts a massacre (upon Allah's enemies) in the land. You (i.e., some Muslims) desire the commodities of this world,1 but Allah desires (for you) the Hereafter. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise. It is not (fitting) for a Prophet that he should have prisoners of war until he has fought (his enemies thoroughly) in the land. You desire the goods of this world, but Allah desires (for you) the Hereafter. And Allah is All-Mighty, All-Wise (8:67). Were it not a previous ordainment from Allah, a severe torment would have touched you for what you took (8:68). So enjoy what you have gotten of booty in war, lawful and good, and have Taqwa of Allah. Certainly, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful (8:69).Imam Ahmad recorded that Anas…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: If not for a decree from Allah that preceded,1 you would have been touched for what you took by a great punishment. See 8:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So consume what you have taken of war booty (as being) lawful and good, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. See 8:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Remember, O believers), when Allah promised you one of the two groups1 - that it would be yours - and you wished that the unarmed one would be yours. But Allah intended to establish the truth by His words and to eliminate the disbelievers. See 8:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:70 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O Prophet, say to whoever is in your hands of the captives, "If Allah knows (any) good in your hearts, He will give you (something) better than what was taken from you, and He will forgive you; and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." O Prophet! Say to the captives that are in your hands: If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you something better than what has been taken from you, and He will forgive you, and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful (8:70). But if they intend to betray you, they indeed betrayed Allah before. So He gave (you) power over them. And Allah is All-Knower, All-Wise (8:71).Pagan Prisoners at Badr were Promised Better than what They Lost, If They Become Righteous in the FutureMuhammad bin Ishaq reported that 'Abdullah bin 'Abbas said that before the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But if they intend to betray you - then they have already betrayed Allah before, and He empowered (you) over them. And Allah is Knowing and Wise. See 8:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:72 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who have believed and emigrated and fought with their wealth and lives in the cause of Allah and those who gave shelter and aided - they are allies of one another. But those who believed and did not emigrate - for you there is no support of them until they emigrate. And if they seek help of you for the religion, then you must help, except against a people between yourselves and whom is a treaty. And Allah is Seeing of what you do. Verily, those who believed, and emigrated and strove hard and fought with their property and their lives in the cause of Allah as well as those who gave (them) asylum and help, – these are (all) allies to one another. And as to those who believed but did not emigrate, you owe no duty…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:73 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who disbelieved are allies of one another. If you do not do so (i.e., ally yourselves with other believers), there will be fitnah (i.e., disbelief and oppression) on earth and great corruption. And those who disbelieve are allies of one another, (and) if you (Muslims) do not do so (protect one another), there will be Fitnah on the earth, and great corruption (8:73).The Disbelievers are Allies of Each Other; the Muslims are Not their AlliesAfter Allah mentioned that the believers are the supporters of one another, He severed all ties of support between them and the disbelievers. In his Mustadrak, Al-Hakim recorded that Usamah said that the Prophet SAW said:لَا يَتَوَارَثُ أَهْلُ مِلَّتَيْنِ، وَلَا يَرِثُ مُسْلِمٌ كَافِرًا، وَلَا كَافِرٌ مُسْلِمًاNo followers of two religions inherit from each other. Therefore, neither a Muslim inherits from a disbeliever nor a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But those who have believed and emigrated and fought in the cause of Allah and those who gave shelter and aided - it is they who are the believers, truly. For them is forgiveness and noble provision. And those who believed, and emigrated and strove hard in the cause of Allah (Al-Jihad), as well as those who gave (them) asylum and aid – these are the believers in truth, for them is forgiveness and a generous provision (8:74). And those who believed afterwards, and emigrated and strove hard along with you, they are of you. But kindred by blood are nearer to one another (regarding inheritance) in the decree ordained by Allah. Verily, Allah is the All-Knower of everything (8:75).Believers in TruthAfter Allah affirmed the ruling of loyalty and protection between the believers in this life, He then mentioned their…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who believed after (the initial emigration) and emigrated and fought with you - they are of you. But those of (blood) relationship are more entitled (to inheritance) in the decree of Allah.1 Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things. See 8:74

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That He should establish the truth and abolish falsehood, even if the criminals disliked it. See 8:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Remember) when you were asking help of your Lord, and He answered you, "Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand from the angels, following one another." (Remember) when you sought help of your Lord and He answered you (saying): I will help you with a thousand of the angels Murdifin (8:9). Allah made it only as glad tidings, and that your hearts be at rest therewith. And there is no victory except from Allah. Verily, Allah is Almighty, All-Wise (8:10).Muslims Invoke Allah for Help, Allah Sends the Angels to Help ThemAl-Bukhari wrote in the book of battles (in his Sahih) under Chapter; Allah's statement:إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ فَاسْتَجَابَ لَكُمْ(Remember) when you sought help of your Lord and He answered youuntil:فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِthen verily, Allah is severe in punishment" that Ibn Mas'ud said, "I was a witness to something that…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Alif, Lām, Meem.1 أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئَاتِ أَنْ يَسْبِقُونَا ۚOr think those who do evil deeds that they can outstrip UsMeaning: "escape" from Us.سَاءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَEvil is that which they judge!what they think is evil.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And of the people are some who say, "We believe in Allah," but when one (of them) is harmed for (the cause of) Allah, he considers the trial (i.e., harm) of the people as (if it were) the punishment of Allah. But if victory comes from your Lord, they say, "Indeed, We were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds (i.e., all creatures)? Of mankind are some who say: "We believe in Allah." But if they are made to suffer for Allah, they consider the trial of mankind as Allah's punishment; and if victory comes from your Lord, they will say: "Verily, we were with you." Is not Allah Best Aware of what is in the breasts of the creatures (29:10). And indeed Allah knows those who believe, and verily, He…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites. See 29:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will carry your sins."1 But they will not carry anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars. And those who disbelieve say to those who believe: "Follow our way and let us bear your sins." Never will they bear anything of their sins. Surely, they are liars (29:12). And verily, they shall bear their own loads, and other loads besides their own; and verily, they shall be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about that which they used to fabricate (29:13).The Arrogant Claim of the Disbelievers that They would Carry the Sins of Others If They would Return to DisbeliefAllah tells us that the disbelievers of Quraysh said to those who believed and followed the truth: leave your religion, come back to our religion, and follow…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But they will surely carry their (own) burdens and (other) burdens along with their burdens,1 and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent. See 29:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We certainly sent Nuh to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers. And indeed We sent Nuh to his people, and he stayed among them a thousand years less fifty years; so the Deluge overtook them while they were wrongdoers (29:14). Then We saved him and the Companions of the Boat, and made it an Ayah for all people (29:15).Nuh and His PeopleHere Allah consoles His servant and Messenger Muhammad SAW by telling him that Nuh (AS), stayed among his people for this long period of time, calling them night and day, in secret and openly, but in spite of all that they still persisted in their aversion to the truth, turning away from it and disbelieving in him. Only a few of them…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But We saved him and the companions of the ship, and We made it1 a sign for the worlds. See 29:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (We sent) Ibrahim, when he said to his people, "Worship Allah and fear Him. That is best for you, if you should know. And (remember) Ibrahim when he said to his people: Worship Allah, and have Taqwa of Him, that is better for you if you know (29:16). You worship besides Allah only idols, and you only invent falsehood. Verily, those whom you worship besides Allah have no power to give you provision, so seek from Allah your provision, and worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be brought back (29:17). And if you deny, then nations before you have denied. And the duty of the Messenger is only to convey plainly (29:18).Ibrahim's Preaching to His PeopleAllah tells us how His servant, Messenger and close friend Ibrahim, the Imam of the monotheists, called his people…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: You only worship, besides Allah, idols, and you produce a falsehood. Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you (the power of) provision. So seek from Allah provision and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned." See 29:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if you (people) deny (the message) - already nations before you have denied. And there is not upon the Messenger except (the duty of) clear notification.1 See 29:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have they not considered how Allah begins creation and then repeats it? Indeed that, for Allah, is easy. See they not how Allah originates the creation, then repeats it. Verily, that is easy for Allah (29:19). Say: Travel in the land and see how He originated the creation, and then Allah will bring forth the creation of the Hereafter. Verily, Allah is able to do all things (29:20). He punishes whom He wills, and shows mercy to whom He wills; and to Him you will be returned (29:21). And you cannot escape in the earth or in the heaven. And besides Allah you have neither any protector nor any helper (29:22). And those who disbelieve in the Ayat of Allah and meeting with Him, such have no hope of My mercy: and for such there is a painful torment (29:23).The…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Do the people think that they will be left to say, "We believe" and they will not be tried? See 29:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, (O Muḥammad), "Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allah will produce the final creation (i.e., development). Indeed Allah, over all things, is competent." See 29:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He punishes whom He wills and has mercy upon whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned. See 29:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you will not cause failure (to Allah) upon the earth or in the heaven. And you have not other than Allah any protector or any helper. See 29:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the ones who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and the meeting with Him - those have despaired of My mercy, and they will have a painful punishment. See 29:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the answer of his (i.e., Ibrahim's) people was not but that they said, "Kill him or burn him," but Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe. So nothing was the answer of people except that they said: Kill him or burn him." Then Allah saved him from the fire. Verily, in this are indeed signs for a people who believe (29:24). And (Ibrahim) said: "You have taken idols instead of Allah. The love between you is only in the life of this world, but on the Day of Resurrection, you shall deny each other, and curse each other, and your abode will be the Fire, and you shall have no helper (29:25).The Response of Ibrahim's People – and How Allah Controlled the FireAllah tells us how Ibrahim's people stubbornly and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (Ibrahim) said, "You have only taken, other than Allah, idols as (a bond of) affection among you in worldly life. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will deny one another and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will not have any helpers." See 29:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Lut believed him. (Ibrahim) said, "Indeed, I will emigrate to (the service of) my Lord. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise." So, Lut believed in him. He said: I will emigrate for the sake of my Lord. Verily, He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise (29:26). And We bestowed on him, Ishaq and Ya'qub, and We ordained among his offspring prophethood and the Book, and We granted him his reward in this world; and verily, in the Hereafter he is indeed among the righteous (29:27).The Faith of Lut and His Emigration with IbrahimAllah tells us that Lut believed in Ibrahim. It was said that he was the son of Ibrahim's brother, and that his name was Lut bin Haran bin Azar. None of Ibrahim's people believed in Ibrahim besides Lut and Sarah the wife of Ibrahim. But…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We gave to him Ishaq and Ya'qub and placed in his descendants prophethood and scripture. And We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, he is in the Hereafter among the righteous. See 29:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) Lut, when he said to his people, "Indeed, you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds. And (remember) Lut, when he said to his people: You commit immoral sins which none has preceded you in (committing) it in all creatures (29:28). "Verily, you practice sodomy with men, and rob the wayfarer! And practice Al-Munkar in your meetings." But his people gave no answer except that they said: "Bring Allah's torment upon us if you are one of the truthful (29:29). He said: "My Lord! Give me victory over the people who are corrupt (29:30).The Preaching of Lut and what Happened between Him and His PeopleAllah tells us that His Prophet Lut (AS), denounced his people for their evil deed and their immoral actions in having intercourse with males, a deed which…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, you approach men and obstruct the road1 and commit in your meetings (every) evil." And the answer of his people was not but that they said, "Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you should be of the truthful." See 29:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But We have certainly tried those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars. See 29:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "My Lord, support me against the corrupting people." See 29:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when Our messengers (i.e., angels) came to Ibrahim with the good tidings,1 they said, "Indeed, we will destroy the people of that (i.e., Lut's) city. Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers." And when Our messengers came to Ibrahim with the glad tidings they said: "Verily, we are going to destroy the people of this town; truly, its people have been wrongdoers (29:31). Ibrahim said: "But there is Lut in it." They said: "We know better who is there. We will verily, save him and his family – except his wife, she will be of those who remain behind (29:32). And when Our messengers came to Lut, he was grieved because of them, and felt straitened on their account. They said: "Have no fear, and do not grieve! Truly, we shall save you and your family except your wife: she…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Ibrahim) said, "Indeed, within it is Lut." They said, "We are more knowing of who is within it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife. She is to be of those who remain behind." See 29:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when Our messengers (i.e., angels) came to Lut, he was distressed for them and felt for them great discomfort.1 They said, "Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is to be of those who remain behind. See 29:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, we will bring down on the people of this city punishment from the sky because they have been defiantly disobedient." See 29:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have certainly left of it a sign as clear evidence for a people who use reason. See 29:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
