item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Bayyina:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, they who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. Those are the worst of creatures. Verily, those who disbelieve from among the People of the Scripture and idolators, will abide in the fire of Hell. They are the worst of creatures (98:6). Verily, those who believe and do righteous good deeds, they are the best of creatures (98:7). Their reward with their Lord is Eternal Gardens, underneath which rivers flow. They will abide therein forever, Allah will be pleased with them, and they well-pleased with Him. That is for him who fears his Lord (98:8).Mentioning the Worse and Best of Creation and Their RecompenseAllah informs of what will happen to the wicked disbelievers among the People of the Scripture and the idolators who oppose the Allah's…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Bayyina:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, they who have believed and done righteous deeds - those are the best of creatures. See 98:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Bayyina:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Their reward with their Lord will be gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, Allah being pleased with them and they with Him. That is for whoever has feared his Lord. See 98:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Burooj:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By the sky containing great stars. إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِVerily, those who put into trial the believing men and believing women,Meaning: they burned (them). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and Ibn Abza.ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُواand then do not turn in repentance,Meaning: 'they do not cease from what they are doing, and do not regret what they had done before.'فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ الْحَرِيقِthen they will have the torment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the burning Fire.This is because the recompense is based upon the type of deed performed. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, "Look at this generosity and kindness. These people killed Allah's Awliya' and He still invites them to make repentance and seek forgiveness."

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Burooj:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who have tortured1 the believing men and believing women and then have not repented will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the Burning Fire. See 85:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Burooj:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great attainment. Verily, those who believe and do righteous good deeds, for them will be Gardens under which rivers flow. That is the supreme success (85:11). Verily, the punishment of your Lord is severe and painful (85:12). Verily, He it is Who begins and repeats (85:13). And He is Oft-Forgiving, Al-Wadud (85:14). Owner of the Throne, Al-Majid (the Glorious) (85:15). Doer of what He intends (85:16). Has the story reached you of the hosts (85:17). Of Fir'awn and Thamud (85:18). Nay! The disbelievers (persisted) in denying (85:19). And Allah encompasses them from behind (85:20). Nay! This is a Glorious Qur'an (85:21). item.description: To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah, over all things, is Witness.1 See 85:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Faatiha:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: In the name of Allah,1 the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.2 بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَـنِ الرَّحِيمِIn the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Mercifulwhether in the beginning or the end of the recitation. Similar is recorded in the Sunan books from 'Abdullah bin Mughaffal (RA).These are the opinions held by the respected Imams, and their statements are similar in that they agree that the prayer of those who recite Al-Fatihah aloud or in secret is correct. All the favor is from Allah.The Virtue of Al-FatihahImam Ahmad recorded in his Musnad, that a person who was riding behind the Prophet SAW said, The Prophet's animal tripped, so I said, 'Cursed Shaytan.' The Prophet said:لَا تَقُلْ: تَعِسَ الشَّيْطَانُ، فَإِنَّكَ إِذَا قُلْتَ: تَعِسَ الشَّيْطَانُ، تَعَاظَمَ وَقَالَ: بِقُوَّتِي صَرَعْتُهُ، وَإِذَا قُلْتَ: بِاسْمِ اللهِ تَصَاغَرَ حَتى يَصِيرَ مِثْلَ الذُبَابِDo not say, 'Cursed Shaytan,' for…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Faatiha:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (All) praise is (due) to Allah, Lord1 of the worlds. The Meaning of Al-HamdAbu Ja'far bin Jarir said, "The meaning of الْحَمْدُ للَّهِ (Al-Hamdu Lillah) (all praise and thanks be to Allah) is: all thanks are due purely to Allah, alone, not any of the objects that are being worshipped instead of Him, nor any of His creation. These thanks are due to Allah's innumerable favors and bounties, that only He knows the amount of. Allah's bounties include creating the tools that help the creation worship Him, the physical bodies with which they are able to implement His commands, the sustenance that He provides them in this life, and the comfortable life He has granted them, without anything or anyone compelling Him to do so. Allah also warned His creation and alerted them about the means and methods with which…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Faatiha:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Allah said next:الرَّحْمَـنِ الرَّحِيمِAr-Rahman (the Most Gracious), Ar-Rahim (the Most Merciful)We explained these Names in the Basmalah. Al-Qurtubi said, Allah has described Himself by 'Ar-Rahman, Ar-Rahim' after saying 'the Lord of the Alamin', so His statement here includes a warning, and then an encouragement. Similarly, Allah said:نَبِّىءْ عِبَادِى أَنِّى أَنَا الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ - وَأَنَّ عَذَابِى هُوَ ٱلْعَذَابُ ٱلْأَلِيمُDeclare (O Muhammad SAW) unto My servants, that truly, I am the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful. And that My torment is indeed the most painful torment. (15:49-50)Allah said:إِنَّ رَبَّكَ سَرِيعُ الْعِقَابِ وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌSurely, your Lord is swift in retribution, and certainly He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. (6:165)Hence, Rabb contains a warning while Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim encourages. Further, Muslim recorded in his Sahih that the Messenger of Allah SAW said:لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الْمُؤْمِنُ مَا عِنْدَ اللهِ مِنَ الْعُقُوبَةِ مَا…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Faatiha:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Sovereign of the Day of Recompense.1 Indicating Sovereignty on the Day of JudgmentAllah mentioned His sovereignty of the Day of Resurrection, but this does not negate His sovereignty over all other things. For Allah mentioned that He is the Lord of existence, including this earthly life and the Hereafter. Allah only mentioned the Day of Recompense here because on that Day, no one except Him will be able to claim ownership of anything whatsoever. On that Day, no one will be allowed to speak without His permission. Similarly, Allah said:يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ وَالْمَلَـئِكَةُ صَفّاً لاَّ يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلاَّ مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَـنُ وَقَالَ صَوَاباًThe Day that Ar-Ruh (Jibril or another angel) and the angels will stand forth in rows, they will not speak except him whom the Most Gracious (Allah) allows, and he will speak what is right. (78:38)وَخَشَعَتِ الأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَـنِ…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Faatiha:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is You we worship and You we ask for help. The Linguistic and Religious Meaning of 'IbadahLinguistically, 'Ibadah means subdued. For instance, a road is described as Mu'abbadah, meaning, 'paved'. In religious terminology, 'Ibadah implies the utmost love, humility and fear.The Merit of Stating the Object of the Action before the Doer of the Act, and the Merit of these Negations"You...", means, we worship You alone and none else, and rely on You alone and none else. This is the perfect form of obedience and the entire religion is implied by these two ideas. Some of the Salaf said, Al-Fatihah is the secret of the Qur'an, while these words are the secret of Al-Fatihah:إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ5 You we worship, and You we ask for help from.The first part is a declaration of innocence from Shirk (polytheism), while the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Faatiha:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Guide us to the straight path. The Meaning of Guidance Mentioned in the SurahThe guidance mentioned in the Surah implies being directed and guided to success. Allah said:اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَGuide us to the straight pathmeaning guide, direct, lead and grant us the correct guidance. Also:وَهَدَيْنَـهُ النَّجْدَينِAnd shown him the two ways (good and evil) (90:10)Means, 'We explained to him the paths of good and evil.' Also, Allah said:اجْتَبَـهُ وَهَدَاهُ إِلَى صِرَطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍHe (Allah) chose him (as an intimate friend) and guided him to a straight path (16:121)And:فَاهْدُوهُمْ إِلَى صِرَطِ الْجَحِيمِAnd lead them on to the way of flaming Fire (Hell) (37:23)Similarly, Allah said:وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِى إِلَى صِرَطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍAnd verily, you (O Muhammad ) are indeed guiding (mankind) to the straight path (42:52)And:الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِى هَدَانَا لِهَـذَاAll praise and thanks be to Allah, Who has guided us to this (7:43)Which is meaning,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Faatiha:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have earned (Your) anger or of those who are astray. We mentioned the Hadith in which the servant proclaims:اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَGuide us to the straight wayand Allah says, "This is for My servant, and My servant shall acquire what he asks for." Allah's statement.صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْThe way of those upon whom You have bestowed Your gracedefines the path. 'Those upon whom Allah has bestowed His grace' are those mentioned in Surat An-Nisa' (chapter 4), when Allah said:وَمَن يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ فَأُوْلَـئِكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ وَالشُّهَدَآءِ وَالصَّـلِحِينَ وَحَسُنَ أُولَـئِكَ رَفِيقاً - ذلِكَ الْفَضْلُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ عَلِيماًAnd whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger (Muhammad SAW ), then they will be in the company of those on whom Allah has bestowed…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By the dawn. إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصَادِVerily, your Lord is Ever Watchful.Ibn 'Abbas said, "He hears and He sees." This means that He watches over His creation in that which they do, and He will reward them in this life and in the Hereafter based upon what each of them strove for. He will bring all of the creation before Him and He will judge them with justice. He will requit each of them with that which he deserves, for He is far removed from injustice and tyranny.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (with) Pharaoh, owner of the stakes?1 See 89:1

item.description: (All of) whom oppressed within the lands. See 89:1

item.description: And increased therein the corruption. See 89:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, your Lord is in observation. See 89:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And as for man, when his Lord tries him and (thus) is generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me."1 As for man, when his Lord tries him by giving him honor and bounties, then he says: "My Lord has honored me (89:15). But when He tries him by straitening his means of life, he says: "My Lord has humiliated me! (89:16). But no! But you treat not the orphans with kindness and generosity (89:17). And urge not one another on the feeding of the Miskin (89:18). And you devour the Turath – devouring with greed (89:19). And you love wealth with love Jamma (89:20).Wealth and Poverty are Both a Test and Honor or Disgrace for the ServantAllah refutes man in his belief that if Allah gives Him abundant provisions to test him with it,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me." See 89:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No!1 But you do not honor the orphan. See 89:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor. See 89:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you consume inheritance, devouring (it) altogether.1 See 89:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (by) ten nights.1 See 89:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you love wealth with immense love. See 89:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No! When the earth has been leveled - pounded and crushed. Nay! When the earth is flatened, Dakkan Dakka (89:21). And your Lord comes with the angels in rows (89:22). And Hell will be brought near that Day. On that Day will man remember, but how will that remembrance avail him (89:23). He will say: Alas! Would that I had sent forth for my life! (89:24). So on that Day none will punish as He will punish (89:25). And none will bind as He will bind (89:26). "O tranquil soul! (89:27). "Come back to your Lord, – well-pleased and well-pleasing! (89:28). "Enter then among My servants, (89:29). "And enter My Paradise! (89:30). On the Day of Judgement Everyone will be recompensed according to what He did of Good or Evil Allah informs of what will happen on the Day of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And your Lord has come1 and the angels, rank upon rank. See 89:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And brought (within view), that Day, is Hell - that Day, man will remember, but how (i.e., what good) to him will be the remembrance? See 89:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent ahead (some good) for my life."1 See 89:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So on that Day, none will punish (as severely) as His punishment. See 89:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And none will bind (as severely) as His binding (of the evildoers). See 89:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (To the righteous it will be said), "O reassured soul. See 89:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing (to Him). See 89:21

item.description: And enter among My (righteous) servants. See 89:21

item.description: And (by) the even (number) and the odd. See 89:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And enter My Paradise." See 89:21

item.description: And (by) the night when it passes. See 89:1

item.description: Is there (not) in (all) that an oath (sufficient) for one of perception?1 See 89:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fajr:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿAad. See 89:1

item.description: (With) Iram1 - who had lofty pillars.2 See 89:1

item.description: The likes of whom had never been created in the land? See 89:1

item.description: And (with) Thamūd, who carved out the rocks in the valley? See 89:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Falaq:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak. وَمِن شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِAnd from the evil of the blowers in knots,Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak all said, "This means the witches." Mujahid said, "When they perform their spells and blow into the knots."In another Hadith it has been reported that Jibril came to the Prophet SAW and said, "Are you suffering from any ailment, O Muhammad?" The Prophet SAW replied:نَعَمْYes.So Jibril said, "In the Name of Allah, I recite prayer (Ruqyah) over you, from every illness that harms you, from the evil of every envious person and evil eye. May Allah cure you."Discussion of the Bewitchment of the Prophet SAWIn the Book of Medicine of his Sahih, Al-Bukhari recorded that Aisha said, "The Messenger of Allah SAW was bewitched until he thought that he had relations with his…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Falaq:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: From the evil of that which He created. See 113:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Falaq:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And from the evil of darkness when it settles. See 113:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Falaq:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And from the evil of the blowers in knots.1 See 113:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Falaq:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And from the evil of an envier when he envies." See 113:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We have given you, (O Muḥammad), a clear conquest.1 وَيَنْصُرَكَ اللَّهُ نَصْرًا عَزِيزًاAnd that Allah may help you with strong help.due to your obedience of the orders of Allah, the Exalted and Most Honored; Allah will elevate your status and give you victory above your enemies. An authentic Hadith states:وَمَا زَادَ اللهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلَّا عِزًّا. وَمَا تَوَاضَعَ أَحَدٌ للهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِلَّا رَفَعَهُ اللهُ تَعَالَىٰNo servant pardons but Allah grants him honor, and none humbles himself for Allah except that Allah the exalted and sublime raises him (in rank).Umar bin Al-Khattab said, "You will never punish someone who disobeyed Allah with you better than obeying Allah the Exalted and Most Honored with him."

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, (O Muḥammad) - they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand1 of Allah is over their hands.2 So he who breaks his word only breaks it to the detriment of himself. And he who fulfills that which he has promised Allah - He will give him a great reward. See 48:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those who remained behind1 of the bedouins will say to you, "Our properties and our families occupied us, so ask forgiveness for us." They say with their tongues what is not within their hearts. Say, "Then who could prevent Allah at all if He intended for you harm or intended for you benefit? Rather, ever is Allah, of what you do, Aware. Those of the bedouins who lagged behind will say to you: Our possessions and our families occupied us, so ask forgiveness for us." They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say: "Who then has any power at all (to intervene) on your behalf with Allah, if He intends you hurt or intends you benefit? Nay, but Allah is Aware of what you do (48:11). Nay, but you thought that the Messenger and the believers…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, ever, and that was made pleasing in your hearts. And you assumed an assumption of evil and became a people ruined." See 48:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever has not believed in Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze. See 48:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful. See 48:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those who remained1 behind will say when you set out toward the war booty to take it, "Let us follow you." They wish to change the words of Allah. Say, "Never will you follow us. Thus did Allah say before." So they will say, "Rather, you envy us." But (in fact) they were not understanding except a little.2 Those who lagged behind will say, when you set forth to take the spoils, "Allow us to follow you." They want to change Allah's Words. Say: "You shall not follow us; thus Allah has said beforehand." Then they will say: "Nay, you envy us." Nay, but they understand not except a little (48:15).Allah characterizes the bedouins who lagged behind the Messenger of Allah SAW during the 'Umrah of Hudaybiyyah, saying that when the Prophet SAW and his Companions later went on to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say to those who remained behind of the bedouins, "You will be called to (face) a people of great military might; you may fight them, or they will submit.1 So if you obey, Allah will give you a good reward; but if you turn away as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment." Say to the bedouins who lagged behind: You shall be called to fight against a people given to great warfare, then you shall fight them, or they shall surrender. Then if you obey, Allah will give you a fair reward; but if you turn away as you did turn away before, He will punish you with a painful torment (48:16). No blame or sin is there upon the blind, nor is there sin upon the lame, nor is there sin upon the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: There is not upon the blind any guilt or upon the lame any guilt or upon the ill any guilt (for remaining behind). And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow; but whoever turns away - He will punish him with a painful punishment. See 48:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Certainly was Allah pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you, (O Muḥammad), under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest.1 Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they gave the pledge to you under the tree, He knew what was in their hearts, and He sent down As-Sakinah upon them, and He rewarded them with a near victory (48:18). And abundant spoils that they will capture. And Allah is Ever All-Mighty, All-Wise (48:19).Good News to the Participants of the Ridwan Pledge of Allah's Pleasure and Earning Spoils of WarAllah declares that He is pleased with the believers who gave the pledge to the Messenger of Allah SAW under the tree. We mentioned the number of these believers as being…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And much war booty which they will take. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise. See 48:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That Allah may forgive for you what preceded of your sin (i.e., errors) and what will follow and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path. See 48:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah has promised you much booty that you will take (in the future) and has hastened for you this (victory) and withheld the hands of people from you - that it may be a sign for the believers and (that) He may guide you to a straight path. Allah has promised you abundant spoils that you will capture, and He has hastened for you this, and He has restrained the hands of men from you, that it may be a sign for the believers, and that He may guide you to the straight path (48:20). And other (victories) which are not yet within your power; indeed Allah encompasses them. And Allah is Ever Able to do all things (48:21). And if those who disbelieve fight against you, they certainly would have turned their backs; then they would have found neither…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (He promises) other (victories) that you were (so far) unable to (realize) which Allah has already encompassed.1 And ever is Allah, over all things, competent. See 48:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if those (Makkans) who disbelieve had fought you, they would have turned their backs (in flight). Then they would not find a protector or a helper. See 48:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (This is) the established way of Allah which has occurred before. And never will you find in the way of Allah any change. See 48:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them within (the area of) Makkah after He caused you to overcome them. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing. See 48:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They are the ones who disbelieved and obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām while the offering1 was prevented from reaching its place of sacrifice. And if not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know - that you might trample (i.e., kill) them and there would befall you because of them dishonor without (your) knowledge - (you would have been permitted to enter Makkah). (This was so) that Allah might admit to His mercy whom He willed. If they had been apart (from them), We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with painful punishment. They are those who disbelieved and hindered you from Al-Masjid Al-Haram and detained the sacrificial animals, from reaching their place of sacrifice. Had there not been believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you may kill and on…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When those who disbelieved had put into their hearts chauvinism - the chauvinism of the time of ignorance. But Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and imposed upon them the word of righteousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it. And ever is Allah, of all things, Knowing. See 48:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Certainly has Allah showed to His Messenger the vision (i.e., dream) in truth. You will surely enter al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, if Allah wills, in safety, with your heads shaved and (hair) shortened,1 not fearing (anyone). He knew what you did not know and has arranged before that a conquest near (at hand). Indeed Allah shall fulfill the true vision which He showed to His Messenger in very truth. Certainly, you shall enter Al-Masjid Al-Haram, if Allah wills, secure, (some) having your heads shaved, and (some) having your hair cut short, having no fear. He knew what you knew not, and He granted besides that a near victor (48:27). He it is Who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it superior to all religions. And All-Sufficient is Allah as a Witness (48:28).Allah has…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion. And sufficient is Allah as Witness. See 48:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah; and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating (in prayer), seeking bounty from Allah and (His) pleasure. Their sign is in their faces from the effect of prostration (i.e., prayer). That is their description in the Torah. And their description in the Gospel is as a plant which produces its offshoots and strengthens them so they grow firm and stand upon their stalks, delighting the sowers - so that He (i.e., Allah) may enrage by them1 the disbelievers. Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward. Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. And those who are with him are severe against disbelievers, and merciful among themselves. You see them bowing falling down prostrate, seeking reward…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (that) Allah may aid you with a mighty victory. See 48:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers that they would increase in faith along with their (present) faith. And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and ever is Allah Knowing and Wise. He it is Who sent down As-Sakinah into the hearts of the believers, that they may grow more in faith along with their faith. And to Allah belong the armies of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Ever All-Knower, All-Wise (48:4). That He may admit the believing men and the believing women to Gardens under which rivers flow to abide therein forever, and He may expiate from them their sins; and that is with Allah supreme success (48:5). And that He may punish the hypocrites men and women, and also the idolators men and women,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (And) that He may admit the believing men and the believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow to abide therein eternally and remove from them their misdeeds - and ever is that, in the sight of Allah, a great attainment. See 48:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (that) He may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women - those who assume about Allah an assumption of evil nature. Upon them is a misfortune of evil nature; and Allah has become angry with them and has cursed them and prepared for them Hell, and evil it is as a destination. See 48:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise. See 48:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner. Verily, We have sent you as a witness, as a bearer of glad tidings, and as a warner (48:8). In order that you (O mankind) may believe in Allah and His Messenger and that you Tu'azziruh and Tuwaqqiruh, and Tusabbihuh Bukrah and Asila (48:9). Verily, those who give pledge to you, they are giving pledge to Allah. The Hand of Allah is over their hands. Then whosoever breaks his pledge, breaks it only to his own harm; and whosoever fulfills what he has the covenants he makes with Allah, He will bestow on him a great reward (48:10).Qualities of the Messenger of Allah SAWAllah the Exalted says to His Prophet, Muhammad SAW:إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِدًاVerily, We have sent you as a witness,of the creation:وَمُبَشِّرًاas…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fath:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That you (people) may believe in Allah and His Messenger and honor him and respect him (i.e., the Prophet SAW) and exalt Him (i.e., Allah) morning and afternoon. See 48:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fil:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have you not considered, (O Muḥammad), how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?1 فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَّأْكُولٍAnd He made them like 'Asf, Ma'kul.Sa'id bin Jubayr said, "This means straw, which the common people call Habbur." In a report from Sa'id he said, "The leaves of wheat." He also said, "Al-'Asf is straw, and Al-Ma'kul refers to the fodder that is cut for animals." Al-Hasan Al-Basri said the same thing. Ibn 'Abbas said, "Al-'Asf is the shell of the grain, just like the covering of wheat." Ibn Zayd said, "Al-'Asf are the leaves of vegetation and produce. When the cattle eat it they defecate it out and it becomes dung."The meaning of this is that Allah destroyed them, annihilated them and repelled them in their plan and their anger. They did not achieve any good. He made a mass…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fil:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Did He not make their plan into misguidance?1 See 105:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fil:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And He sent against them birds in flocks. See 105:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fil:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Striking them with stones of hard clay. See 105:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Fil:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And He made them like eaten straw.1 See 105:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner. الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَدًا وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ شَرِيكٌ فِي الْمُلْكِHe to Whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Who has begotten no son and for Whom there is no partner in the dominion.Allah states that He is above having any offspring or partner. Then He tells us:خَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًاHe has created everything, and has measured it exactly according to its due measurements.Meaning: everything apart from Him is created and subject to Him. He is the Creator, Lord, Master and God of all things, and everything is subject to His dominion, control and power.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Blessed is He who, if He willed, could have made for you (something) better than that - gardens beneath which rivers flow - and could make for you palaces. See 25:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But they have denied the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a Blaze. See 25:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When it (i.e., the Hellfire) sees them from a distant place, they will hear its fury and roaring. See 25:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when they are thrown into a narrow place therein bound in chains, they will cry out thereupon for destruction. See 25:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (They will be told), "Do not cry this Day for one destruction but cry for much destruction." See 25:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Is that better or the Garden of Eternity which is promised to the righteous? It will be for them a reward and destination. Say: "Is that better or the Paradise of Eternity which is promised to those who have Taqwa" It will be theirs as a reward and final destination (25:15). For them there will be therein all that they desire, and they will abide (therein forever). It is upon your Lord a Wa'dan Mas'ula (25:16).Is the Fire Better, or Paradise?Here Allah says: 'O Muhammad, this that We have described to you about the state of those who are doomed, who will be dragged on their faces to Hell, which will receive them with a scowling face, with hatred and moans. There they will be thrown into their constricted spaces, tied up to their shoulders, unable to move or…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For them therein is whatever they wish, (while) abiding eternally. It is ever upon your Lord a promise (worthy to be) requested.1 See 25:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) the Day He will gather them and that which they worship besides Allah and will say, "Did you mislead these, My servants, or did they (themselves) stray from the way?" And on the Day when He will gather them together and that which they worship besides Allah. He will say: "Was it you who misled these My servants or did they stray from the path (25:17). They will say: "Glorified be You! It was not for us to take any Awliya' besides You, but You gave them and their fathers comfort till they forgot the warning, and became a lost people (25:18). Thus they will deny you in what you say; then you can neither avert nor find help. And whoever among you does wrong, We shall make him taste a great torment (25:19).The Gods of the Idolators…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for us to take besides You any allies (i.e., protectors). But You provided comforts for them and their fathers until they forgot the message and became a people ruined." See 25:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So they will deny you, (disbelievers), in what you say,1 and you cannot avert (punishment) or (find) help. And whoever commits injustice2 among you - We will make him taste a great punishment. See 25:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in dominion and has created each thing and determined it with (precise) determination. See 25:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We did not send before you, (O Muḥammad), any of the messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. And We have made some of you (people) as trial for others - will you have patience? And ever is your Lord, Seeing. And We never sent before you any of the Messengers but verily, they ate food and walked in the markets. And We have made some of you as a trial for others; will you have patience And your Lord is Ever All-Seer (25:20).All of the Previous Messengers Were HumanAllah tells us about the previous Messengers He sent: they all used to eat food needing the nourishment in it. They used to go around in the marketplaces seeking to engage in trade and earn a livelihood. This should not, however, affect their status as Messengers,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, "Why were not angels sent down to us, or (why) do we (not) see our Lord?" They have certainly become arrogant within themselves1 and (become) insolent with great insolence. And those who expect not a meeting with Us said: Why are not the angels sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord" Indeed they think too highly of themselves, and are scornful with great pride (25:21). On the Day they will see the angels – no good news will there be for the criminals that day. And they will say: "Hijran Mahjura (25:22). And We shall turn to whatever deeds they did, and We shall make such deeds as scattered floating particles of dust (25:23). The dwellers of Paradise will, on that Day, have the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The day they see the angels1 - no good tidings will there be that day for the criminals, and (the angels) will say, "Prevented and inaccessible."2 See 25:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We will approach (i.e., regard)1 what they have done of deeds and make them as dust dispersed. See 25:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The companions of Paradise, that Day, are (in) a better settlement and better resting place. See 25:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) the Day when the heaven will split open with (emerging) clouds,1 and the angels will be sent down in successive descent. And (remember) the Day when the heaven shall be rent asunder with clouds, and the angels will be sent down, with a grand descending (25:25). The sovereignty on that Day will be the true (sovereignty) of the Most Gracious, and it will be a hard Day for the disbelievers (25:26). And (remember) the Day when the wrongdoer will bite at his hands, he will say: Oh! Would that I had taken a path with the Messenger (25:27). "Ah! Woe to me! Would that I had never taken so-and-so as an intimate friend! (25:28). "He indeed led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me. And Shaytan is to man ever a deserter (25:29).The Terrors…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: True sovereignty, that Day, is for the Most Merciful. And it will be upon the disbelievers a difficult Day. See 25:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands (in regret) he will say, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way.1 See 25:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Oh, woe to me! I wish I had not taken that one1 as a friend. See 25:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He led me away from the remembrance1 after it had come to me. And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter."2 See 25:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But they have taken besides Him gods which create nothing, while they are created, and possess not for themselves any harm or benefit and possess not (power to cause) death or life or resurrection. Yet they have taken besides Him other gods who created nothing but are themselves created, and possess neither harm nor benefit for themselves, and possess no power (of causing) death, nor (of giving) life, nor of raising the dead (25:3).The Foolishness of the IdolatorsAllah tells us of the ignorance of the idolators in taking other gods instead of Allah, the Creator of all things, the One Who controls the affairs of all things; whatever He wills happens and whatever He does not will does not happen. In spite of that, they still worshipped others besides Him, idols who could not even create the wing of a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the Messenger has said, "O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur’ān as (a thing) abandoned."1 And the Messenger will say: O my Lord! Verily, my people deserted this Qur'an (25:30). Thus have We made for every Prophet an enemy among the criminals. But sufficient is your Lord as a Guide and Helper (25:31).The Messenger SAW will Complain against His OpponentsAllah tells how His Messenger and Prophet Muhammad will say: "O my Lord! Verily, my people deserted this Qur'an." The idolators would not listen to the Qur'an, as Allah says:وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَٰذَا الْقُرْآنِ وَالْغَوْا فِيهِAnd those who disbelieve say: "Listen not to this Qur'an, and make noise in the midst of it." (41:26)When he would recite Qur'an to them, they would talk nonsense or speak about something else, so that they would not hear…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And thus have We made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. But sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper. See 25:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur’ān not revealed to him all at once?" Thus (it is) that We may strengthen thereby your heart. And We have spaced it distinctly.1 And those who disbelieve say: "Why is not the Qur'an revealed to him all at once" Thus, that We may strengthen your heart thereby. And We have revealed it to you gradually, in stages (25:32). And no example or parable do they bring, but We reveal to you the truth, and the better explanation thereof (25:33). Those who will be gathered to Hell on their faces, such will be in an evil state, and most astray from the path (25:34).The Reason Why the Qur'an Was Revealed in Stages, the Refutation of the Disbelievers, and Their Evil EndAllah tells us about the many objections raised by the disbelievers, their…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they do not come to you with an example (i.e., argument) except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation. See 25:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The ones who are gathered on their faces to Hell - those are the worst in position and farthest astray in (their) way. See 25:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We had certainly given Musa the Scripture and appointed with him his brother Harun as an assistant. And indeed We gave Musa the Scripture, and placed his brother Harun with him as a helper (25:35). And We said: "Go you both to the people who have denied Our Ayat." Then We destroyed them with utter destruction (25:36). And Nuh's people, when they denied the Messengers, We drowned them, and We made them as a sign for mankind. And We have prepared a painful torment for the wrongdoers (25:37). And (also) 'Ad and Thamud, and the Dwellers of Ar-Rass, and many generations in between (25:38). And for each We put forward examples, and each We brought to utter ruin (25:39). And indeed they have passed by the town on which was rained the evil rain. Did they not then see…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We said, "Go both of you to the people who have denied Our signs." Then We destroyed them with (complete) destruction. See 25:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the people of Nuh - when they denied the messengers,1 We drowned them, and We made them for mankind a sign. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment. See 25:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (We destroyed) ʿAad and Thamūd and the companions of the well1 and many generations between them. See 25:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And for each We presented examples (as warnings), and each We destroyed with (total) destruction. See 25:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who disbelieve say, "This (Qur’ān) is not except a falsehood he invented, and another people assisted him in it." But they have committed an injustice and a lie. Those who disbelieve say: "This is nothing but a lie that he has invented, and others have helped him in it." In fact, they have produced an unjust wrong and a lie (25:4). And they say: "Tales of the ancients which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and afternoon (25:5). Say: "It has been sent down by Him Who knows the secret of the heavens and the earth. Truly, He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful (25:6).What the Disbelievers Said About the Qur'anAllah tells us about the foolishness of the disbelievers' ignorant minds, when they said about the Qur'an:إِنْ هَٰذَا إِلَّا إِفْكٌThis is nothing but a lieWhich…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they have already come upon the town which was showered with a rain of evil (i.e., stones). So have they not seen it? But they are not expecting resurrection.1 See 25:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when they see you, (O Muḥammad), they take you not except in ridicule, (saying), "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger? And when they see you, they treat you only in mockery (saying): Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a Messenger (25:41). "He would have nearly misled us from our gods, had it not been that we were patient and constant in their worship!" And they will know, when they see the torment, who it is that is most astray from the path (25:42). Have you seen him who has taken as his god his own vain desire Would you then be a guardian over hi (25:43). Or do you think that most of them hear or understand They are only like cattle – nay, they are even farther astray from the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He almost would have misled us from our gods had we not been steadfast in (worship of) them." But they are going to know, when they see the punishment, who is farthest astray in (his) way. See 25:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire? Then would you be responsible for him? See 25:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or do you think that most of them hear or reason? They are not except like livestock.1 Rather, they are (even) more astray in (their) way. See 25:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have you not considered your Lord - how He extends the shadow, and if He willed, He could have made it stationary? Then We made the sun for it an indication.1 Have you not seen how your Lord spread the shadow. If He willed, He could have made it still – but We have made the sun its guide (25:45). Then We withdraw it towards Ourselves – a gradual withdrawal (25:46). And it is He Who makes the night a covering for you, and the sleep (as) a repose, and makes the day Nushur (25:47).Evidence of the Existence of the Creator and the Extent of His PowerHere Allah begins explaining the evidence for His existence and His perfect power to create various things and pairs of opposites. Allah says:أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّHave you not seen how your…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then We (retract and) hold it with Us for a brief grasp.1 See 25:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it is He who has made the night for you as clothing1 and sleep (a means for) rest and has made the day a resurrection.2 See 25:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy (i.e., rainfall), and We send down from the sky pure water. And it is He Who sends the winds as heralds of glad tidings, going before His mercy; and We send down pure water from the sky (25:48). That We may give life thereby to a dead land, and We give to drink thereof many of the cattle and men that We have created (25:49). And indeed We have distributed it among them in order that they may remember the grace of Allah, but most men refuse (out of) gratitude (25:50).This is Also Part of His Complete Power and Supreme Authority:Allah sends the winds as heralds of glad tidings, i.e., they bring the clouds behind them. The winds are of many different types, depending on the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That We may bring to life thereby a dead land and give it as drink to those We created of numerous livestock and men. See 25:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they say, "Legends of the former peoples which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and afternoon." See 25:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have certainly distributed it among them that they might be reminded,1 but most of the people refuse except disbelief. See 25:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if We had willed, We could have sent into every city a warner.1 And had We willed, We would have raised a warner in every town (25:51). So obey not the disbelievers, but strive against them with the utmost endeavor with it (25:52). And it is He Who has let free the two seas, this is palatable and sweet, and that is salty and bitter; and He has set a barrier and a complete partition between them (25:53). And it is He Who has created man from water, and has appointed for him kindred by blood, and kindred by marriage. And your Lord is Ever All-Powerful to do what He wills (25:54).The Universality of the Prophet's Message, How He Was Supported in His Mission and Allah's Blessings to MankindAllah says:وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَبَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ نَّذِيرًاAnd had We willed,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it (i.e., the Qur’ān) a great striving. See 25:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it is He who has released (simultaneously) the two seas (i.e., bodies of water), one fresh and sweet and one salty and bitter, and He placed between them a barrier and prohibiting partition. See 25:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it is He who has created from water (i.e., semen) a human being and made him (a relative by) lineage and marriage. And ever is your Lord competent (concerning creation). See 25:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But they worship rather than Allah that which does not benefit them or harm them, and the disbeliever is ever, against his Lord, an assistant (to Satan). And they worship besides Allah, that which can neither profit them nor harm them; and the disbeliever is ever a helper against his Lord (25:55). And We have sent you only as a bearer of good news and a warner (25:56). Say: No reward do I ask of you for this, save that whosoever wills may take a path to his Lord (25:57). And put your trust in the Ever Living One Who dies not, and glorify His praises, and sufficient is He as the All-Knower of the sins of His servants (25:58). Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six Days. Then He rose over…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have not sent you, (O Muḥammad), except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. See 25:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "I do not ask of you for it any payment - only that whoever wills might take to his Lord a way." See 25:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt (Allah) with His praise. And sufficient is He to be, with the sins of His servants, (fully) Aware. See 25:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days and then established Himself above the Throne1 - the Most Merciful, so ask about Him one well informed (i.e., the Prophet SAW). See 25:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, (O Muḥammad), "It has been revealed by He who knows (every) secret within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful." See 25:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Should we prostrate to that which you order us?" And it increases them in aversion. See 25:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Blessed is He who has placed in the sky great stars and placed therein a (burning) lamp and luminous moon. Blessed be He Who has placed in the heaven Al-Buruj, and has placed therein a great lamp, and a moon giving light (25:61). And He it is Who has put the night and the day in succession (Khilfatan), for such who desires to remember or desires to show his gratitude (25:62).Mentioning the Might and Power of AllahHere Allah glorifies Himself and praises the beauty He created in the heavens of Al-Buruj, the giant stars, according to the view of Mujahid, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Abu Salih, Al-Hasan and Qatadah. This is like the Ayah:وَلَقَدْ زَيَّنَّا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا بِمَصَابِيحَAnd indeed We have adorned the nearest heaven with lamps (67:5)Allah says:تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ فِي السَّمَاءِ بُرُوجًا وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَاجًاBlessed be He Who has…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it is He who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude. See 25:61

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth easily,1 and when the ignorant address them (harshly), they say (words of) peace.2 And the servants of the Most Gracious are those who walk on the earth Hawna, and when the foolish address them they say; "Salama (25:63). And those who spend the night in worship of their Lord, prostrate and standing (25:64). And those who say: "Our Lord! Avert from us the torment of Hell. Verily, its torment is ever an inseparable, permanent punishment (25:65). Evil indeed it is as an abode and as a place to rest in (25:66). And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are in a just balance between them (25:67).Attributes of the Servants of the Most GraciousThese are the attributes of the believing servants of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who spend (part of) the night to their Lord prostrating and standing (in prayer). See 25:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell. Indeed, its punishment is ever adhering. See 25:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, it is evil as a settlement and residence." See 25:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (they are) those who, when they spend, do so not excessively or sparingly but are ever, between that, (justly) moderate. See 25:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who do not invoke1 with Allah another deity or kill the soul which Allah has forbidden (to be killed), except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever should do that will meet a penalty. And those who invoke not any other god along with Allah, nor kill such person as Allah has forbidden, except for just cause, nor commit illegal sexual intercourse – and whoever does this shall receive Athama (25:68). The torment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in disgrace (25:69). Except those who repent and believe, and do righteous deeds; for those, Allah will change their sins into good deeds, and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful (25:70). And whosoever repents and does righteous good deeds; then indeed he has repented to Allah Mataba…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Multiplied for him is the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated. See 25:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they say, "What is this messenger that eats food and walks in the markets? Why was there not sent down to him an angel so he would be with him a warner? And they say: "Why does this Messenger eat food, and walk about in the markets. Why is not an angel sent down to him to be a warner with him (25:7). "Or (why) has not a treasure been granted to him, or why has he not a garden whereof he may eat" And the wrongdoers say: "You follow none but a man bewitched (25:8). See how they coin similitudes for you, so they have gone astray, and they cannot find a path (25:9). Blessed be He Who, if He wills, will assign you better than (all) that – Gardens under which rivers flow and will assign you…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:70 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work. For them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful. See 25:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he who repents and does righteousness does indeed turn to Allah with (accepted) repentance. See 25:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:72 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (they are) those who do not testify to falsehood, and when they pass near ill speech, they pass by with dignity. And those who do not bear witness to falsehood, and if they pass by some evil play or evil talk, they pass by it with dignity (25:72). And those who, when they are reminded of the Ayat of their Lord, fall not deaf and blind thereat (25:73). And those who say: Our Lord! Bestow on us from our wives and our offspring the comfort of our eyes, and make us leaders of those who have Taqwa (25:74).More Attributes of the Servants of the Most GraciousThese are further attributes of the servants of the Most Gracious. They do not bear witness to falsehood, including lies, immorality, disbelief, foul speech and false words. 'Amr bin Qays said, this refers to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:73 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who, when reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind. See 25:72

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes1 and make us a leader (i.e., example) for the righteous." See 25:72

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those will be awarded the Chamber1 for what they patiently endured, and they will be received therein with greetings and (words of) peace. Those will be rewarded with the highest place because of their patience. Therein they shall be met with greetings and the word of peace and respect (25:75). Abiding therein – excellent it is as an abode, and as a place to rest in (25:76). Say: My Lord pays attention to you only because of your invocation to Him. But now you have indeed denied. So the torment will be yours forever (25:77).The Reward of the Servants of the Most Gracious, and a Warning to the People of MakkahAfter mentioning the beautiful attributes of His believing servants, and their fine words and deeds, Allah then says:أُولَٰئِكَThoseMeaning: the people who are described in this manner:يُجْزَوْنَwill be rewardedon the Day…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:76 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Abiding eternally therein. Good is the settlement and residence. See 25:75

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:77 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "What would my Lord care for you if not for your supplication?"1 For you (disbelievers) have denied, so it (i.e., your denial) is going to be adherent.2 See 25:75

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or (why is not) a treasure presented to him (from heaven), or does he (not) have a garden from which he eats?" And the wrongdoers say, "You follow not but a man affected by magic." See 25:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Furqaan:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Look how they strike for you comparisons;1 but they have strayed, so they cannot (find) a way. See 25:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Ḥā, Meem.1 غَافِرِ الذَّنْبِ وَقَابِلِ التَّوْبِThe Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance,means, He forgives sins that have been committed in the past, and He accepts repentance for sins that may be committed in the future, from the one who repents and submits to Him.شَدِيدِ الْعِقَابِthe Severe in punishment,means, to the one who persists in transgression and prefers the life of this world, who stubbornly turns away from the commands of Allah and commits sin. This is like the Ayah:نَبِّئْ عِبَادِي أَنِّي أَنَا الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ - وَأَنَّ عَذَابِي هُوَ الْعَذَابُ الْأَلِيمُDeclare unto My servants that truly I am the Oft-Forgiving, the Most-Merciful. And that My torment is indeed the most painful torment. (15:49-50)These two attributes (mercy and punishment) are often mentioned together in the Qur'an, so that people will remain in a state of both hope and fear.ذِي الطَّوْلِthe Bestower.Ibn…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who disbelieve will be addressed, "The hatred of Allah for you was (even) greater than your hatred of yourselves (this Day in Hell) when you were invited to faith, but you disbelieved (i.e., refused)." Those who disbelieve will be addressed: Indeed, Allah's aversion was greater towards you than your aversion toward yourselves, when you were called to the Faith but you used to refuse (40:10). They will say: "Our Lord! You have made us to die twice, and You have given us life twice! Now we confess our sins, then is there any way to get out? (40:11). (It will be said): "This is because, when Allah Alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but when partners were joined to Him, you believed! So the judgement is only with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great! (40:12). It is He…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will say, "Our Lord, You made us lifeless twice and gave us life twice, and we have confessed our sins. So is there to an exit any way?" See 40:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (They will be told), "That is because, when Allah was called upon alone, you disbelieved; but if others were associated with Him, you believed. So the judgement is with Allah, the Most High, the Grand." See 40:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is He who shows you His signs and sends down to you from the sky, provision. But none will remember except he who turns back (in repentance). See 40:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So invoke Allah, (being) sincere to Him in religion, although the disbelievers dislike it. See 40:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (He is) the Exalted above (all) degrees, Owner of the Throne; He places the inspiration of His command (i.e., revelation) upon whom He wills of His servants to warn of the Day of Meeting. (He is Allah) Owner of high ranks and degrees, the Owner of the Throne. He sends the revelation by His command to any of His servants He wills, that he may warn of the Day of Mutual Meeting (40:15). The Day when they will come out, nothing of them will be hidden from Allah. Whose is the kingdom this Day? It is Allah's, the One, the Irresistible (40:16). This Day shall every person be recompensed for what he earned. This Day no injustice. Truly, Allah is swift in reckoning (40:17).Allah Sends the Revelation to Warn His Servants of the Day of Mutual MeetingAllah tells us of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Day they come forth nothing concerning them will be concealed from Allah. To whom belongs (all) sovereignty this Day? To Allah, the One, the Prevailing.1 See 40:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: This Day every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. No injustice today! Indeed, Allah is swift in account. See 40:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And warn them, (O Muḥammad), of the Approaching Day, when hearts are at the throats, filled (with distress). For the wrongdoers there will be no devoted friend and no intercessor (who is) obeyed. And warn them of the Day that is drawing near, when the hearts will be at the throats Kazimin. There will be no friend, nor an intercessor for the wrongdoers, who could be given heed to (40:18). Allah knows the fraud of the eyes, and all that the breasts conceal (40:19). And Allah judges with truth, while those to whom they invoke besides Him, cannot judge anything. Certainly, Allah! He is the All-Hearer, the All-Seer (40:20).Warning of the Day of Resurrection and Allah's Judgement on that DayThe Day that is drawing near' is one of the names of the Day of Judgement. It is so called because…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He knows that which deceives the eyes and what the breasts conceal. See 40:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The revelation of the Book (i.e., the Qur’ān) is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. See 40:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke1 besides Him judge not with anything. Indeed, Allah - He is the Hearing, the Seeing. See 40:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those who were before them? They were greater than them in strength and in impression on the land, but Allah seized them for their sins. And they had not from Allah any protector. Have they not traveled in the land and seen what was the end of those who were before them? They were superior to them in strength, and in the traces in the land. But Allah seized them with punishment for their sins. And none had they to protect them from Allah (40:21). That was because there came to them their Messengers with clear evidences but they disbelieved (in them). So Allah seized them. Verily, He is All-Strong, Severe in punishment (40:22).The Severe Punishment for the Disbelieversأَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُواHave they not traveledMeaning, 'these people who…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That was because their messengers were coming to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Powerful and severe in punishment. See 40:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We did certainly send Musa with Our signs and a clear authority.1 And indeed We sent Musa with Our Ayat, and a manifest authority (40:23). To Fir'awn, Haman and Qarun, but they called (him): A sorcerer, a liar! (40:24). Then, when he brought them the Truth from Us, they said: "Kill with him the sons of those who believe and let their women live;" but the plots of disbelievers are nothing but in vain (40:25). Fir'awn said: "Leave me to kill Musa, and let him call his Lord! I fear that he may change your religion, or that he may cause mischief to appear in the land! (40:26). Musa said: "Verily, I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant who believes not in the Day of Reckoning! (40:27). The Story of Musa and Fir'awn Allah…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: To Pharaoh, Hāmān and Qārūn, but they said, "(He is) a magician and a liar." See 40:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, "Kill the sons of those who have believed with him and keep their women alive." But the plan of the disbelievers is not except in error. See 40:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Pharaoh said, "Let me kill Musa and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption1 in the land." See 40:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But Musa said, "Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account." See 40:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh who concealed his faith said, "Do you kill a man (merely) because he says, 'My Lord is Allah' while he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? And if he should be lying, then upon him is (the consequence of) his lie; but if he should be truthful, there will strike you some of what he promises you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar. And a believing man of Fir'awn's family, who hid his Faith said: "Would you kill a man because he says: 'My Lord is Allah,' and he has come to you with clear signs from your Lord? And if he is a liar, upon him will be (the sin of) his lie; but if he is telling the truth, then…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O my people, sovereignty is yours today, (your being) dominant in the land. But who would protect us from the punishment of Allah if it came to us?" Pharaoh said, "I do not show you except what I see, and I do not guide you except to the way of right conduct." See 40:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The forgiver of sin, acceptor of repentance, severe in punishment, owner of abundance. There is no deity except Him; to Him is the destination. See 40:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he who believed said, "O my people, indeed I fear for you (a fate) like the day of the companies1. And he who believed said: O my people! Verily, I fear for you an end like that day (of disaster) of the groups (of old)! (40:30). "Like the end of the people of Nuh, and 'Ad, and Thamud and those who came after them. And Allah wills no injustice for (His) servants (40:31). "And, O my people! Verily, I fear for you the Day when there will be mutual calling (40:32). A Day when you will turn your backs and flee having no protector from Allah. And whomsoever Allah sends astray, for him there is no guide (40:33). And indeed Yusuf did come to you, in times gone by, with clear signs, but you ceased not to doubt in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Like the custom of the people of Nuh and of ʿAad and Thamūd and those after them. And Allah wants no injustice for (His) servants. See 40:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling1. See 40:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Day you will turn your backs fleeing; there is not for you from Allah any protector. And whoever Allah sends astray - there is not for him any guide. See 40:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Yusuf had already come to you before with clear proofs, but you remained in doubt of that which he brought to you, until when he died, you said, 'Never will Allah send a messenger after him.' Thus does Allah leave astray he who is a transgressor and skeptic." See 40:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without an authority1 having come to them - great is hatred (of them) in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who have believed. Thus does Allah seal over every heart (belonging to) an arrogant tyrant. See 40:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Pharaoh said, "O Hāmān, construct for me a tower that I might reach the ways1. How Fir'awn Mocked the Lord of MusaAllah tells us of the arrogant and hostile defiance of Fir'awn and his rejection of Musa, when he commanded his minister Haman to build him a tower, i.e., a tall, high, strong fortress. He built it of bricks made from baked clay, as Allah says:فَأَوْقِدْ لِى يَهَـمَـنُ عَلَى الطِّينِ فَاجْعَل لِّى صَرْحاًSo kindle for me (a fire), O Haman, to bake (bricks out of) clay, and set up for me a lofty tower (28:38)لَّعَـلِّى أَبْلُغُ الاٌّسْبَـبَ - أَسْبَـبَ السَّمَـوَتِthat I may arrive at the ways -- the ways of the heavens,Sa'id bin Jubayr and Abu Salih said, "The gates of the heavens." Or it was said, the ways of the heavens.فَأَطَّلِعَ إِلَى إِلَـهِ مُوسَى وَإِنِّى لاّظُنُّهُ كَـذِباًand I…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The ways into the heavens - so that I may look at the deity of Musa; but indeed, I think he is a liar." And thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed, and he was averted from the (right) way. And the plan of Pharaoh was not except in ruin. See 40:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he who believed said, "O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the way of right conduct. And the man who believed said: O my people! Follow me, I will guide you to the way of right conduct (40:38). "O my people! Truly, this life of the world is nothing but an enjoyment, and verily, the Hereafter that is the home that will remain forever (40:39). "Whoever does an evil deed, will not be requited except the like thereof; and whosoever does a righteous deed, whether male or female and is a true believer, such will enter Paradise, where they will be provided therein without limit (40:40). More of what the Believer from Fir'awn's Family said This believer said to his people who persisted in their rebellion and transgression, and preferred the life of this world:يَا قَوْمِ…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O my people, this worldly life is only (temporary) enjoyment, and indeed, the Hereafter - that is the home of (permanent) settlement. See 40:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No one disputes concerning the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so be not deceived by their (uninhibited) movement throughout the land. None disputes in the Ayat of Allah but those who disbelieve. So let not their ability of going about here and there through the land (for their purposes) deceive you (40:4). The people of Nuh and the groups after them denied before these; and every nation plotted against their Messenger to seize him, and disputed by means of falsehood to refute therewith the truth. So I seized them, and how was My punishment (40:5).
