item.description: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke (or recited), Satan threw into it (some misunderstanding). But Allah abolishes that which Satan throws in; then Allah makes precise His verses.1 And Allah is Knowing and Wise. Never did We send a Messenger or a Prophet before you but when he did recite (the revelation or narrated or spoke), Shaytan threw (some falsehood) in his recitation (of the revelation). But Yansakh Allah that which Shaytan throws in. Then Allah establishes His revelations. And Allah is All-Knower, All-Wise (22:52). That He (Allah) may make what is thrown in by Shaytan a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and whose hearts are hardened. And certainly, the wrongdoers are in an opposition far-off (from the truth) (22:53). And that those who have been…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (That is) so He may make what Satan throws in (i.e., asserts) a trial for those within whose hearts is disease1 and those hard of heart. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension. See 22:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And so those who were given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord and (therefore) believe in it, and their hearts humbly submit to it. And indeed is Allah the Guide of those who have believed to a straight path. See 22:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt of it until the Hour comes upon them unexpectedly or there comes to them the punishment of a barren Day.1 And those who disbelieved, will not cease to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes suddenly upon them, or there comes to them the torment of Yawm 'Aqim (22:55). The sovereignty on that Day will be that of Allah. He will judge between them. So those who believed and did righteous good deeds will be in Gardens of Delight (22:56). And those who disbelieved and denied Our Ayat, for them will be a humiliating torment (in Hell) (22:57).The Disbelievers will Remain in Doubt and ConfusionAllah tells us that the disbelievers will remain in doubt concerning this Qur'an. This was the view of Ibn Jurayj and was the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (All) sovereignty that Day is for Allah;1 He will judge between them. So they who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the Gardens of Pleasure. See 22:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they who disbelieved and denied Our signs - for those there will be a humiliating punishment. See 22:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who emigrated for the cause of Allah and then were killed or died - Allah will surely provide for them a good provision. And indeed, it is Allah who is the best of providers. Those who emigrated in the cause of Allah and after that were killed or died, surely, Allah will provide a good provision for them. And verily, it is Allah Who indeed is the Best of those who make provision (22:58). Truly, He will make them enter an entrance with which they shall be well-pleased, and verily, Allah indeed is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing (22:59). That is so. And whoever has retaliated with the like of that which he was made to suffer, and then has again been wronged, Allah will surely help him. Verily, Allah indeed is Oft-Pardoning, Oft-Forgiving (22:60).The Great Reward for Those Who…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He will surely cause them to enter an entrance with which they will be pleased, and indeed, Allah is Knowing and Forbearing. See 22:58

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is because Allah is the True Reality and because He gives life to the dead and because He is over all things competent. See 22:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That (is so). And whoever responds (to injustice) with the equivalent of that with which he was harmed and then is tyrannized - Allah will surely aid him. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.1 See 22:58

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That1 is because Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night and because Allah is Hearing and Seeing. That is because Allah merges the night into the day, and He merges the day into the night. And verily, Allah is All-Hearer, All-Seer (22:61). That is because Allah – He is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him, it is false. And verily, Allah – He is the Most High, the Most Great (22:62).The Creator and Controller of this World is AllahAllah tells us that He is the Creator Who directs the affairs of His creation as He wills. He tells us:قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَن تَشَاءُ وَتَنزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّن تَشَاءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَن تَشَاءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَن تَشَاءُ ۖ بِيَدِكَ الْخَيْرُ ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ - تُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is because Allah is the True Reality, and that which they call upon other than Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Grand. See 22:61

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Do you not see that Allah has sent down rain from the sky and the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allah is Subtle1 and Aware.2 See you not that Allah sends down water from the sky, and then the earth becomes green? Verily, Allah is the Most Kind and Courteous, Well-Acquainted with all things (22:63). To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth. And verily, Allah – He is Rich, Worthy of all praise (22:64). See you not that Allah has subjected to you all that is on the earth, and the ships that sail through the sea by His command He withholds the heaven from falling on the earth except by His leave. Verily, Allah is for mankind, full of kindness, Most Merciful (22:65). It is He, Who gave you life, and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. And indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy. See 22:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is on the earth and the ships which run through the sea by His command? And He restrains the sky from falling upon the earth, unless by His permission. Indeed Allah, to the people, is Kind and Merciful. See 22:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And He is the one who gave you life; then He causes you to die and then will (again) give you life. Indeed, mankind is ungrateful. See 22:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For every (religious) community We have appointed rites which they perform. So, (O Muḥammad), let them (i.e., the disbelievers) not contend with you over the matter but invite (them) to your Lord. Indeed, you are upon straight guidance. For every nation We have made Mansak which they must follow; so let them not dispute with you on the matter, but invite them to your Lord. Verily, you indeed are on the straight guidance (22:67). And if they argue with you, say: "Allah knows best of what you do (22:68). "Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection about that wherein you used to differ (22:69).Every Nation has its Religious CeremoniesAllah tells us that He has made Mansak for every nation. Ibn Jarir said, "This means that there are Mansak for every Prophet's nation." He said, "The origin of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if they dispute with you, then say, "Allah is most knowing of what you do. See 22:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ." See 22:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (that they may know) that the Hour is coming - no doubt about it - and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves. See 22:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:70 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and earth? Indeed, that is in a Record.1 Indeed that, for Allah, is easy. Know you not that Allah knows all that is in the heaven and on the earth? Verily, it is (all) in the Book. Verily, that is easy for Allah (22:70).Allah tells us how perfect is His knowledge of His creation, and that He encompasses all that is in the heavens and on earth.Not even the weight of a speck of dust, or less than that or greater escapes His knowledge in the heavens or in the earth. He knows all things even before they happen, and He has written that in His Book, Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz, as was reported in Sahih Muslim from 'Abdullah bin 'Amr, who said, The Messenger of Allah SAW said:إِنَّ اللهَ…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they worship besides Allah that for which He has not sent down authority and that of which they have no knowledge. And there will not be for the wrongdoers any helper. And they worship besides Allah others for which He has sent down no authority, and of which they have no knowledge; and for the wrongdoers there is no helper (22:71). And when Our clear Ayat are recited to them, you will notice a denial on the faces of the disbelievers! They are nearly ready to attack with violence those who recite Our Ayat to them. Say: Shall I tell you of something worse than that The Fire which Allah has promised to those who disbelieved, and worst indeed is that destination! (22:72).The Idolators' Worship of Others Besides Allah and Their Vehement Rejection of the Ayat of AllahAllah tells…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:72 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, you recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve disapproval. They are almost on the verge of assaulting those who recite to them Our verses. Say, "Then shall I inform you of (what is) worse than that?1 (It is) the Fire which Allah has promised those who disbelieve, and wretched is the destination." See 22:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:73 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O people, an example is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create (as much as) a fly, even if they gathered together for it (i.e., that purpose). And if the fly should steal from them a (tiny) thing, they could not recover it from him. Weak are the pursuer and pursued.1 O mankind! A parable has been made, so listen to it: Verily, those on whom you call besides Allah, cannot create a fly, even though they combine together for the purpose. And if the fly snatches away a thing from them, they will have no power to release it from the fly. So weak are the seeker and the sought (22:73). They have not regarded Allah with His rightful esteem. Verily, Allah is All-Strong, All-Mighty (22:74).The Insignificance of the Idols and the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They have not appraised Allah with true appraisal.1 Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might. See 22:73

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah chooses from the angels messengers and from the people. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing. Allah chooses Messengers from angels and from men. Verily, Allah is All-Hearer, All-Seer (22:75). He knows what is before them, and what is behind them. And to Allah return all matters (22:76).Allah Chooses Messengers from the Angels and Messengers from MankindAllah tells us that He chooses Messengers from His angels as He wills by His law and decree, and He chooses Messengers from mankind to convey His Message.إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌVerily, Allah is All-Hearer, All-Seer.means, He hears all that His servants say, and He sees them and knows who among them is deserving of that, as He says:اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ رِسَالَتَهُAllah knows best with whom to place His Message (6:124)يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۗ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُHe knows what is…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:76 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He knows what is (presently) before them and what will be after them.1 And to Allah will be returned (all) matters. See 22:75

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:77 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good - that you may succeed. O you who believe! Bow down, and prostrate yourselves, and worship your Lord and do good that you may be successful (22:77). And strive hard in Allah's cause as you ought to strive. He has chosen you, and has not laid upon you in religion any hardship: it is the religion of your father Ibrahim. He has named you Muslims both before and in this (Qur'an), that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you be witnesses over mankind! So, perform the Salah, give the Zakah and hold fast to Allah. He is your Mawla, what an Excellent Mawla and what an Excellent Helper (22:78).The Command to Worship Allah and Engage in JihadIt was reported from 'Uqbah bin…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:78 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. (It is) the religion of your father, Ibrahim. He (i.e., Allah) named you "Muslims" before (in former scriptures) and in this (revelation) that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer and give zakāh and hold fast to Allah. He is your protector; and excellent is the protector, and excellent is the helper. See 22:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And of the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening book (from Him). And among men is he who disputes about Allah, without knowledge or guidance, or a Book giving light (from Allah) (22:8). Bending his neck in pride, and leading (others) too (far) astray from the path of Allah. For him there is disgrace in this worldly life, and on the Day of Resurrection We shall make him taste the torment of burning (22:9). That is because of what your hands have sent forth, and verily, Allah is not unjust to servants (22:10).Clarifying the State of the Leaders of the Innovators and Those Who Lead People AstrayAllah has already told us about the ignorant imitators who are led astray:وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجَادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَيَتَّبِعُ كُلَّ شَيْطَانٍ مَرِيدٍAnd among mankind…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Twisting his neck (in arrogance) to mislead (people) from the way of Allah. For him in the world is disgrace, and We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the Burning Fire (while it is said). See 22:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah,1 and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. مَا قَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ لِينَةٍ أَوْ تَرَكْتُمُوهَا قَائِمَةً عَلَىٰ أُصُولِهَا فَبِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَلِيُخْزِيَ الْفَاسِقِينَWhat you cut down of the Linah, or you left them standing on their stems, it was by leave of Allah, and in order that He might disgrace the rebellious.Muhammad bin Ishaq reported that the battle of Bani An-Nadir occurred after the battles of Uhud and Bi'r Ma'unah.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (there is a share for) those who come after them, saying, "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts (any) resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful." See 59:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have you not considered those who practice hypocrisy, saying to their brothers (i.e., associates) who have disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, "If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you, and we will not obey, in regard to you, anyone - ever; and if you are fought, we will surely aid you." But Allah testifies that they are liars. Have you not observed the hypocrites who say to their disbelieving brethren among the People of the Scripture, If you are expelled, we indeed will go out with you, and we shall never obey anyone against you; and if you are attacked, we shall indeed help you." But Allah is Witness that they verily are liars (59:11). Surely, if they (the Jews) are expelled, never will they (hypocrites) go out with them; and if they are attacked, they…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: If they are expelled, they will not leave with them, and if they are fought, they will not aid them. And (even) if they should aid them, they will surely turn their backs; then (thereafter) they will not be aided. See 59:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: You (believers) are more fearful within their breasts than Allah. That is because they are a people who do not understand. See 59:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will not fight you all except within fortified cities or from behind walls. Their violence (i.e., enmity) among themselves is severe. You think they are together, but their hearts are diverse. That is because they are a people who do not reason. See 59:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Theirs is) like the example of those shortly before them: they tasted the bad consequence of their affair, and they will have a painful punishment. See 59:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (The hypocrites are) like the example of Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds." See 59:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So the outcome for both of them is that they will be in the Fire, abiding eternally therein. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers. See 59:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow - and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Aware of what you do. O you who believe! Have Taqwa of Allah and let every person look to what he has sent forth for tomorrow, and fear Allah. Verily, Allah is All-Aware of what you do (59:18). And be not like those who forgot Allah, and He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the rebellious (59:19). Not equal are the dwellers of the Fire and the dwellers of the Paradise. It is the dwellers of Paradise that will be successful (59:20).The Command to have Taqwa and to Prepare for the Day of ResurrectionImam Ahmad recorded that Al-Mundhir bin Jarir narrated that his father said, While we were in the company of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient. See 59:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is He who expelled the ones who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture1 from their homes at the first gathering.2 You did not think they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah; but (the decree of) Allah came upon them from where they had not expected, and He cast terror into their hearts (so) they destroyed their houses by their (own) hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O people of vision. See 59:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Not equal are the companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise. The companions of Paradise - they are the attainers (of success). See 59:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: If We had sent down this Qur’ān upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and splitting from fear of Allah. And these examples We present to the people that perhaps they will give thought. Had We sent down this Qur'an on a mountain, you would surely have seen it humbling itself and rent asunder by the fear of Allah. Such are the parables which We put forward to mankind that they may reflect (59:21). He is Allah, beside Whom La ilaha illa Huwa, the All-Knower of the unseen and the seen. He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful (59:22). He is Allah, beside Whom La ilaha illa Huwa, Al-Malik, Al-Quddus, As-Salam, Al-Mu'min, Al-Muhaymin, Al-'Aziz, Al-Jabbar, Al-Mutakabbir. Glory be to Allah! Above all that they associate as partners with Him (59:23). He is Allah, Al-Khaliq, Al-Bari, Al-Musawwir. To…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.1 He is the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. See 59:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign,1 the Pure,2 the Perfection,3 the Grantor of Security,4 the Overseer,5 the Exalted in Might,6 the Compeller,7 the Superior.8 Exalted is Allah above whatever they associate with Him. See 59:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He is Allah, the Creator,1 the Producer,2 the Fashioner;3 to Him belong the best names.4 Whatever is in the heavens and earth is exalting Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.5 See 59:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if not that Allah had decreed for them evacuation, He would have punished them in (this) world, and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire. See 59:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah - then indeed, Allah is severe in penalty. See 59:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Whatever you have cut down of (their) palm trees or left standing on their trunks - it was by permission of Allah and so He would disgrace the defiantly disobedient. See 59:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And what Allah restored (of property) to His Messenger from them - you did not spur for it (in an expedition) any horses or camels,1 but Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent. And what Allah gave as booty (Fai') to His Messenger from them – for this you made no expedition with either cavalry or camelry. But Allah gives power to His Messengers over whomsoever He wills. And Allah is Able to do all things (59:6). What Allah gave as booty (Fai') to His Messenger from the people of the townships – it is for Allah, His Messenger, the kindred, the orphans, the poor, and the wayfarer, in order that it may not become a fortune used by the rich among you. And whatsoever the Messenger gives you, take it;…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And what Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns - it is for Allah and for the Messenger and for (his) near relatives1 and orphans and the needy and the (stranded) traveler2 - so that it will not be a perpetual distribution among the rich from among you. And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty. See 59:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from Allah and (His) approval and supporting (the cause of) Allah and His Messenger, (there is also a share). Those are the truthful. (And there is also a share in this booty) for the poor emigrants, who were expelled from their homes and their property, seeking bounties from Allah and (His) good pleasure, and helping Allah and His Messenger. Such are indeed the truthful (59:8). And (it is also for) those who, before them, had homes and had adopted the faith, love those who emigrate to them, and have no jealousy in their breasts for that which they have been given, and give them preference over themselves even though they were in need of that. And whosoever is saved from his own greed, such are…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hashr:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (also for) those who were settled in the Home (i.e., al-Madīnah) and (adopted) the faith before them.1 They love those who emigrated to them and find not any want in their breasts of what they (i.e., the emigrants) were given but give (them) preference over themselves, even though they are in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful. See 59:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Alif, Lām, Rā.1 These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur’ān (i.e., recitation). رُّبَمَا يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواHow much would those who disbelieved wishHere Allah tells us that they will regret having lived in disbelief, and will wish that they had been Muslims in this world. Regarding Allah's saying:رُّبَمَا يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ كَانُوا مُسْلِمِينَHow much would those who disbelieved wish that they had been Muslims.Sufyan Ath-Thawri reported from Salamah bin Kuhayl, who reported from Abi Az-Za'ra', from 'Abdullah, who said: "This is about the Jahannamiyyun (the sinners among the believers who will stay in Hell for some time), when they (the disbelievers) see them being brought out of Hell."رُّبَمَا يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ كَانُوا مُسْلِمِينَHow much would those who disbelieved wish that they had been Muslims.Ibn Jarir reported that Ibn 'Abbas and Anas bin Malik explained that…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We had certainly sent (messengers) before you, (O Muḥammad), among the sects of the former peoples. Indeed, We sent (Messengers) before you (O Muhammad) amongst the earlier communities (15:10). And there never came a Messenger to them but that they mocked him (15:11). Thus We allow it to enter the hearts of the guilty (15:12). They would not believe in it (the Qur'an); and already the example of the ancients has gone forth (15:13).The Idolators of Every Nation Made a Mockery of their MessengersConsoling His Messenger SAW for the rejection of the disbelieving Quraysh, Allah says that He has sent Messengers before him to the nations of the past, and no Messenger came to a nation but they rejected him and mocked him. Then He tells him that He lets disbelief enter the hearts of those sinners who are…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And no messenger would come to them except that they ridiculed him. See 15:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Thus do We insert it (i.e., denial) into the hearts of the criminals. See 15:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will not believe in it, while there has already occurred the precedent of the former peoples. See 15:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (even) if We opened to them a gate from the heaven and they continued therein to ascend. And even if We opened to them a gate to the heavens and they were to continue ascending through it (all day long) (15:14). They would surely say (in the evening): Our eyes have been (as if) dazzled (we have not seen any angel or heaven). Nay, we are a people bewitched (15:15).The Stubborn Disbelievers will Never Believe, No Matter what Signs and Wonders They SeeAllah explains the extent of their disbelief and stubborn resistance to the truth by stating that even if a door to heaven were to be opened for them, and they were to be taken up through it, they would still not believe. Rather, they would say:إِنَّمَا سُكِّرَتْ أَبْصَارُنَاOur eyes have been (as if) dazzled.Mujahid, Ibn Kathir and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They would say, "Our eyes have only been dazzled. Rather, we are a people affected by magic." See 15:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have placed within the heaven great stars and have beautified it for the observers. And indeed, We have put the big stars in the heaven and We beautified it for the beholders (15:16). And We have guarded it (near heaven) from every outcast Shaytan (devil) (15:17). Except him (devil) who steals the hearing, then he is pursued by a clear flaming fire (15:18). And We have spread out the earth, and have placed firm mountains in it, and caused all kinds of things to grow in it, in due proportion (15:19). And in it We have provided means of living, for you and for those whom you provide not (15:20).The Power of Allah and His Signs in the Heavens and on EarthTo those who ponder, and look repeatedly at the dazzling signs and wonders that are to be…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have protected it from every devil expelled (from the mercy of Allah). See 15:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except one who steals a hearing and is pursued by a clear burning flame. See 15:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the earth - We have spread it and cast therein firmly set mountains and caused to grow therein (something) of every well-balanced thing. See 15:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish1 that they had been Muslims. See 15:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have made for you therein means of living and (for) those for whom you are not providers.1 See 15:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except according to a known (i.e., specified) measure. And there is not a thing, but the supplies for it are with Us, and We do not send it down but in a known measure (15:21). And We send the winds fertilizing, then We cause the water to descend from the sky, and We give it to you to drink, and it is not you who are the owners of its supply (15:22). And certainly We! It is We Who give life, and cause death, and We are the Inheritors (15:23). And indeed, We know the first generations of you who have passed away, and indeed, We know the present generations of you (mankind), and also those who will come afterwards…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have sent the fertilizing winds1 and sent down water from the sky and given you drink from it. And you are not its retainers. See 15:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritor.1 See 15:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have already known the preceding (generations) among you, and We have already known the later (ones to come). See 15:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, your Lord will gather them; indeed, He is Wise and Knowing. See 15:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We did certainly create man out of clay from an altered black mud. And indeed, We created man from dried (sounding) clay of altered mud (15:26). And the Jinn, We created earlier from the smokeless flame of fire (15:27).The Substances from which Mankind and Jinns were CreatedIbn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said that Salsal means dry mud. The apparent meaning is similar to the Ayah:خَلَقَ الْإِنسَانَ مِن صَلْصَالٍ كَالْفَخَّارِ - وَخَلَقَ الْجَانَّ مِن مَّارِجٍ مِّن نَّارٍHe created man (Adam) from sounding clay like the potter's clay, And He created the Jinns from a smokeless flame of fire. (55:14-15)It was also reported from Mujahid that:صَلْصَالٍdried (sounding) claymeans "putrid", but it is more appropriate to interpret an Ayah with another Ayah.مِّنْ حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍof altered mudmeans the dried clay that comes from mud, which is soil. "Altered" here means smooth.وَالْجَانَّ خَلَقْنَاهُ مِن…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the jinn We created before from scorching fire. See 15:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention, O Muḥammad), when your Lord said to the angels, "I will create a human being out of clay from an altered black mud. And (remember) when your Lord said to the angels: "I am going to create a man (Adam) from dried (sounding) clay of altered mud (15:28). "So, when I have fashioned him completely and breathed into him (Adam) of My spirit (the soul which I created for him,) then fall down, prostrating yourselves before him (15:29). So the angels prostrated themselves, all of them together (15:30). Except Iblis (Shaytan) - he refused to be among the prostrate (15:31). (Allah) said: "O Iblis! What is your reason for not being among the prostrate? (15:32). (Iblis) said: "I am not one to prostrate myself to a human, whom You created from dried (sounding) clay of altered mud (15:33).The…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My (created) soul,1 then fall down to him in prostration." See 15:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Let them eat and enjoy themselves and be diverted by (false) hope, for they are going to know. See 15:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So the angels prostrated - all of them entirely. See 15:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except Iblees;1 he refused to be with those who prostrated. See 15:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Allah) said, "O Iblees, what is (the matter) with you that you are not with those who prostrate?" See 15:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Never would I prostrate to a human whom You created out of clay from an altered black mud." See 15:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Allah) said, "Then depart from it,1 for indeed, you are expelled. (Allah) said: Then leave, for verily, you are an outcast (15:34). "And verily, the curse shall be upon you until the Day of Recompense (15:35). (Iblis) said: "O my Lord! Then give me respite until the Day they (the dead) will be resurrected (15:36). Allah said: "Then verily, you are of those reprieved, (15:37). "Until the Day of the time appointed (15:38).The Expulsion of Iblis from Jannah, and His Reprieve until the Day of ResurrectionAllah tells us how He issued an unconditional command to Iblis to leave the position he held among the highest of heights. He told him that he was an outcast, i.e., cursed, and that he would be followed by a curse that would hound him until the Day of Resurrection. It was reported that Sa'id…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense." See 15:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected." See 15:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Allah) said, "So indeed, you are of those reprieved. See 15:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Until the Day of the time well-known." See 15:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Iblees) said, "My Lord, because You have put me in error, I will surely make (disobedience) attractive to them (i.e., mankind) on earth, and I will mislead them all. (Iblis) said: "O my Lord! Because You misled me, I shall indeed adorn the path of error for them (mankind) on the earth, and I shall mislead them all (15:39). "Except Your chosen (guided) servants among them (15:40). (Allah) said: "This is the way which will lead straight to Me (15:41). "Certainly, you shall have no authority over My servants, except those of the astray who follow you (15:42). And surely, Hell is the place promised for them all (15:43). It has seven gates, for each of those gates is a class assigned (15:44).The Threat of Iblis to Tempt Mankind, and Allah's Promise of Hell for himAllah informed about the rebellion…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We did not destroy any city but that for it was a known decree. And never did We destroy a township but there was a known decree for it (15:4). No nation can advance its term, nor delay it (15:5).Every Township has its Allotted TimeAllah is informing us that He never destroys a township until He has established evidences for it and its allotted time has ended. When the time for a nation's destruction has come, He never delays it, and He never moves its appointed time forward. This was a message and a warning to the people of Makkah, telling them to give up their Shirk, their stubbornness and disbelief for which they deserved to be destroyed.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except, among them, Your chosen servants." See 15:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Allah) said, "This is a path (of return) to Me (that is) straight. See 15:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, My servants - no authority will you have over them, except those who follow you of the deviators. See 15:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all. See 15:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It has seven gates; for every gate is of them (i.e., Satan's followers) a portion designated." See 15:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the righteous will be within gardens and springs. Truly, those who have Taqwa, will dwell in Gardens and water springs (15:45). (It will be said to them): Enter it in peace and security (15:46). And We shall remove any deep feeling of bitterness from their breasts. (So they will be like) brothers facing each other on thrones (15:47). No sense of fatigue shall touch them, nor shall they be asked to leave i (15:48). Declare to My servants that I am truly the Forgiving, the Most Merciful (15:49). And that My torment is indeed the most painful torment (15:50).Description of the People of ParadiseSince Allah mentioned the condition of the people of Hell, He followed that by mentioning the people of Paradise. He tells us that they will dwell in Gardens and water springs.ادْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَامٍEnter it in peacemeaning free…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Having been told), "Enter it in peace, safe (and secure)." See 15:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment,1 (so they will be) brothers, on thrones facing each other. See 15:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No fatigue will touch them therein, nor from it will they (ever) be removed. See 15:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (O Muḥammad), inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Merciful. See 15:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No nation will precede its term, nor will they remain thereafter. See 15:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that it is My punishment which is the painful punishment. See 15:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And inform them about the guests of Ibrahim. And tell them about the guests (i. e., the angels) of Ibrahim (15:51). When they entered upon him, and said: Salaman (peace!)." He said: "Indeed we are frightened of you (15:52). They said: "Do not be afraid! We bring you the good news of a boy possessing much knowledge and wisdom (15:53). He said: "Do you give me this good news while old age has overtaken me? Of what then is your news about? (15:54). They said: "We give you good news in truth. So do not be of those who despair (15:55). He said: "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except those who are astray? (15:56).The Guests of Ibrahim and their Good News of a Son for HimAllah is saying: 'Tell them, O Muhammad, about the story of:ضَيْفِ…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When they entered upon him and said, "Peace." (Ibrahim) said, "Indeed, we are fearful (i.e., apprehensive) of you." See 15:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (The angels) said, "Fear not. Indeed, we give you good tidings of a learned boy." See 15:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Have you given me good tidings although old age has come upon me? Then of what (wonder) do you inform?" See 15:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "We have given you good tidings in truth, so do not be of the despairing." See 15:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except for those astray?" See 15:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Ibrahim) said, "Then what is your business (here), O messengers?" He said: "What then is the business for which you have come, O messengers? (15:57). They said: "We have been sent to a guilty people (15:58). "(All) except the family of Lut, all of whom we are to save (from the destruction) (15:59). "Except for his wife, of whom We have decreed that she shall be of those who remain behind (15:60).The Reason Why the Angels CameAllah tells us that after Ibrahim had calmed down from the excitement of this good news, he started to ask them why they had come to him. They said:إِنَّا أُرْسِلْنَا إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ مُّجْرِمِينَWe have been sent to a guilty people.meaning the people of Lut. They told him that they were going to save the family of Lut from among those people, except for his…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a people of criminals. See 15:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except the family of Lut; indeed, we will save them all. See 15:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they say, "O you upon whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad.1 And they say: "O you (Muhammad) to whom the Dhikr (the Qur'an) has been revealed! Verily, you are a madman (15:6). "Why do you not bring angels to us if you are of the truthful? (15:7). We do not send the angels down except with the truth, and in that case, they (the disbelievers) would have no respite (15:8). Verily, We, it is We Who revealed the Dhikr (i.e. the Qur'an) and surely We will guard it (from corruption) (15:9).The Accusation that the Prophet SAW was a Madman and Demands for Him to Bring down AngelsAllah tells us about the disbelief, arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers as reflected in their words:يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِي نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُO you (Muhammad) to whom the Dhikr…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except his wife." We (i.e., Allah) decreed that she is of those who remain behind.1 See 15:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when the messengers came to the family of Lut. Then when the messengers (the angels) came to the family of Lu (15:61). He (Lut) said: Verily, you are people unknown to me (15:62). They said: "Nay, we have come to you with that (torment) which they have been doubting (15:63). "And we have brought you the truth and certainly we tell the truth (15:64).The Angels Coming to LutAllah tells us about when the angels came to Lut in the form of young men with handsome faces. When they entered his home, he said:إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ - قَالُوا بَلْ جِئْنَاكَ بِمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ"Verily, you are people unknown to me." They said: "Nay, we have come to you with that (torment) which they have been doubting."meaning that they were bringing the punishment and destruction that the people doubted they would…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Indeed, you are people unknown." See 15:61

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "But we have come to you with that about which they were disputing. See 15:61

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And we have come to you with truth, and indeed, we are truthful. See 15:61

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So set out with your family during a portion of the night and follow behind them and let not anyone among you look back and continue on to where you are commanded." Then travel for a portion of the night with your family, and you go behind them in the rear, and let no one amongst you look back, but go on to where you are ordered (15:65). And We made this decree known to him that those (sinners) would be rooted out in the early morning (15:66).Lut is Ordered to Leave with His Family during the NightAllah tells us that His angels ordered Lut to set out after part of the night had passed. They told him to walk behind them, to protect them. Similarly, the Messenger of Allah SAW would walk in the rear of the army on…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We conveyed to him (the decree) of that matter: that those (sinners) would be eliminated by early morning. See 15:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the people of the city came rejoicing.1 And the inhabitants of the city came rejoicing (15:67). (Lut) said: "Verily, these are my guests, so do not shame me (15:68). "And have Taqwa of Allah, and do not disgrace me (15:69). They said: "Did we not forbid you from entertaining any of the 'Alamin? (15:70). Lut ]said: "These are my daughters, if you must act (so) (15:71). Verily, by your life, in their wild intoxication, they were wandering blindly (15:72).The People of the City Arrive upon the Angels, Thinking that they are MenAllah tells us about how Lut's people came to him when they found out about his handsome guests, and they came happily rejoicing about them.قَالَ إِنَّ هَٰؤُلَاءِ ضَيْفِي فَلَا تَفْضَحُونِ - وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلَا تُخْزُونِ(Lut) said: "Verily, these are my guests, so do not shame me. And have…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Lut) said, "Indeed, these are my guests, so do not shame me. See 15:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And fear Allah and do not disgrace me." See 15:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Why do you not bring us the angels, if you should be among the truthful?" See 15:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:70 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Have we not forbidden you from (protecting) people?" See 15:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Lut) said, "These are my daughters1 - if you would be doers (of lawful marriage)." See 15:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:72 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By your life, (O Muḥammad), indeed they were, in their intoxication, wandering blindly. See 15:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:73 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So the shriek1 seized them at sunrise. So the Sayhah overtook them at the time of sunrise (15:73). And We turned them upside down and rained stones of baked clay upon them (15:74). Surely, in this are signs for those who see (15:75). And verily, they were right on the highroad (15:76). Surely, there is indeed a sign in that for the believers (15:77).The Destruction of the People of LutAllah said;فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّيْحَةُSo the Sayhah overtook themThis is the piercing sound that came to them when the sun rose, which was accompanied by the city being flipped upside down, and stones of baked clay (As-Sijjil) raining down upon them. The discussion of As-Sijjil in Surah Hud is a sufficient explanation. Allah said:إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّلْمُتَوَسِّمِينَSurely, in this are signs for those who see.meaning that the traces of the destruction of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We made the highest part (of the city) its lowest and rained upon them stones of hard clay. See 15:73

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed in that are signs for those who discern. See 15:73

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:76 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, they (i.e., those cities) are (situated) on an established road. See 15:73

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:77 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed in that is a sign for the believers. See 15:73

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:78 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the companions of the thicket (i.e., the people of Madyan) were (also) wrongdoers. And the Dwellers of Al-Aykah, were also wrongdoers (15:78). So, We took vengeance on them. They are both on an open route, plain to see (15:79).The Destruction of the Dwellers of Al-Aykah, the People of Shu'aybThe Dwellers of Al-Aykah, were the people of Shu'ayb. Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah and others said that Al-Aykah refers to intertwined trees. Their evildoing included associating partners with Allah (Shirk), banditry and cheating in weights and measures. Allah punished them with the Sayhah (the awful cry or torment), the earthquake, and the torment of the Day of Shadow. They lived near the people of Lut, but at a later time, and the people of Lut were known to them, which is why Allah says:وَإِنَّهُمَا لَبِإِمَامٍ مُّبِينٍThey are both on an open route, plain…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:79 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So We took retribution from them, and indeed, both (cities) are on a clear highway. See 15:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: We do not send down the angels except with truth;1 and they (i.e., the disbelievers) would not then be reprieved. See 15:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:80 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And certainly did the companions of al-Ḥijr1 (i.e., the Thamūd) deny the messengers. And verily, the Dwellers of Al-Hijr denied the Messengers (15:80). And We gave them Our signs, but they were averse to them (15:81). And they used to hew out dwellings from the mountains, (feeling) secure (15:82). But the Sayhah (torment - awful cry) overtook them in the early morning (15:83). And all that they used to earn availed them not (15:84).The Destruction of the Dwellers of Al-Hijr, Who are the People Called ThamudThe Dwellers of the Al Hijr were the people of Thamud who rejected their Prophet, Salih. Whoever denies even one Messenger, then he has disbelieved in all of the Messengers, thus they are described as rejecting "the Messengers". Allah tells us that he (Salih) brought them signs to prove that what he was telling them…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:81 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We gave them Our signs, but from them they were turning away. See 15:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:82 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they used to carve from the mountains, houses, feeling secure. See 15:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:83 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But the shriek seized them at early morning. See 15:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:84 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So nothing availed them (from) what they used to earn. See 15:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:85 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have not created the heavens and earth and that between them except in truth. And indeed, the Hour is coming; so forgive with gracious forgiveness. And We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except with the truth, and the Hour is surely coming, so overlook their faults with gracious forgiveness (15:85). Verily, your Lord is the Knowing Creator (15:86).The World has been Created for Some Purpose, Then the Hour will ComeAllah says:وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ ۗ وَإِنَّ السَّاعَةَ لَآتِيَةٌAnd We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except with the truth, and the Hour is surely comingI.e., with justice to -لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوا بِمَا عَمِلُواrequite those who do evil with that which they have done (53:31)Allah says:وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاءَ…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:86 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, your Lord - He is the Knowing Creator. See 15:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:87 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have certainly given you, (O Muḥammad), seven of the often repeated (verses)1 and the great Qur’ān. And indeed, We have bestowed upon you seven of the Mathani, and the Grand Qur'an (15:87). Look not with your eyes ambitiously at what We have given to certain classes of them, nor grieve over them. And lower your wings to the believers (15:88).A Reminder of the Blessing of the Qur'an and the Command to Focus on its MessageAllah is saying to His Prophet SAW: Since We have given you the Grand Qur'an, then do not look at this world and its attractions, or the transient delights that we have given to its people in order to test them. Do not envy what they have in this world, and do not upset yourself with regret for their rejection of you and their…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:88 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to (certain) categories of them (i.e., the disbelievers), and do not grieve over them. And lower your wing (i.e., show kindness) to the believers. See 15:87

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:89 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And say, "Indeed, I am the clear warner". And say (O Muhammad): I am indeed a plain warner (15:89). As We have sent down on the Muqtasimin (conspiring confederates) (15:90). Who have made the Qur'an into parts (15:91). So, by your Lord, We shall certainly call all of them to account (15:92). For all that they used to do (15:93).The Messenger SAW is a Plain WarnerAllah commanded His Prophet SAW to tell the people:إِنِّي أَنَا النَّذِيرُ الْمُبِينُI am indeed a plain warnercoming to warn the people of a severe punishment that they will suffer if they reject him, as happened to those nations before them who disbelieved in their Messengers, upon whom Allah sent His punishment and vengeance. In the two Sahihs it is reported from Abu Musa that the Prophet SAW said:إِنَّمَا مَثَلِي وَمَثَلُ مَا بَعَثَنِي اللهُ بِهِ كَمَثَلِ…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, it is We who sent down the message (i.e., the Qur’ān), and indeed, We will be its guardian. See 15:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:90 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Just as We had revealed (scriptures) to the separators.1 See 15:89

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:91 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Who have made the Qur’ān into portions.1 See 15:89

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:92 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So by your Lord, We will surely question them all. See 15:89

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:93 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: About what they used to do. See 15:89

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:94 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then declare what you are commanded1 and turn away from the polytheists.2 Therefore openly proclaim what you have been commanded, and turn away from the idolators (15:94). Truly, We will suffice you against the mockers (15:95). Who make another god along with Allah; but they will come to know (15:96). Indeed, We know that your breast becomes tight because of what they say (15:97). So glorify the praises of your Lord and be of those who prostrate themselves (to Him) (15:98). And worship your Lord until the certainty (i.e. death) comes to you (15:99).The Command to Proclaim the Truth OpenlyAllah commanded His Messenger SAW to convey what He sent him with, to proclaim and spread the Message, which means confronting the idolators with it. Ibn 'Abbas said that the Ayah:فَاصْدَعْ بِمَا تُؤْمَرُTherefore openly proclaim that what you have been commanded,means,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:95 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We are sufficient for you against the mockers. See 15:94

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:96 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Who make (equal) with Allah another deity. But they are going to know. See 15:94

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:97 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We already know that your breast is constrained by what they say. See 15:94

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:98 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So exalt (Allah) with praise of your Lord and be of those who prostrate (to Him). See 15:94

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hijr:99 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty (i.e., death). See 15:94

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, do not put (yourselves) before Allah and His Messenger1 but fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The believers are but brothers, so make settlement between your brothers. And fear Allah that you may receive mercy. See 49:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule (another) people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule (other) women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not insult one another and do not call each other by (offensive) nicknames. Wretched is the name (i.e., mention) of disobedience after (one's) faith. And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers. O you who believe! Let not a group scoff at another group, it may be that the latter are better than the former. Nor let (some) women scoff at other women, it may be that the latter are better than the former. Nor defame yourselves, nor insult one another by nicknames. Evil is the name of wickedness after faith. And whosoever does not repent, then such are indeed…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, avoid much (negative) assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of Repentance and Merciful. O you who believe! Avoid much suspicion; indeed some suspicion is sin. And spy not, neither backbite one another. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would hate it. And have Taqwa of Allah. Verily, Allah is the One Who forgives and accepts repentance, Most Merciful (49:12).The Prohibition of Unfounded SuspicionAllah the Exalted forbids His faithful servants from being suspicious, which includes having doubts and suspicions about the conduct of one's family, relatives and other people in general. Therefore, Muslims are to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous1 of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Aware. O mankind! We have created you from a male and a female, and made you into nations and tribes that you may know one another. Verily, the most honorable of you with Allah is that (believer) who has At-Taqwa. Verily, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware (49:13).All of Mankind are the Children of 'Adam and Hawwa'Allah the Exalted declares to mankind that He has created them all from a single person, 'Adam, and from that person He created his mate, Hawwa'. From their offspring He made nations, comprised of tribe, which include subtribes of all sizes.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not (yet) believed; but say (instead), 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you from your deeds1 of anything. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." The bedouins say: "We believe." Say: "You do not believe. But say, 'We have submitted,' for Faith has not yet entered your hearts. But if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not decrease anything in reward for your deeds. Verily, Allah is Forgiving, Most Merciful (49:14). Only those are the believers who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and afterward doubt not but strive with their wealth and their lives for the cause of Allah. Those! They are the truthful (49:15). Say: "Will you inform Allah of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The believers are only the ones who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then doubt not but strive with their properties and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is those who are the truthful. See 49:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Would you acquaint Allah with your religion while Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things?" See 49:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They consider it a favor to you that they have accepted Islām. Say, "Do not consider your Islām a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred favor upon you that He has guided you to the faith, if you should be truthful." See 49:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, Allah knows the unseen (aspects) of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Seeing of what you do. See 49:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or be loud to him in speech like the loudness of some of you to others, lest your deeds become worthless while you perceive not. See 49:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who lower their voices before the Messenger of Allah - they are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for righteousness. For them is forgiveness and great reward. See 49:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who call you, (O Muḥammad), from behind the chambers - most of them do not use reason. Verily, those who call you from behind the dwellings, most of them have no sense (49:4). And if they had patience till you could come out to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving, Most Merciful (49:5).Admonishing Those Who Call the Prophet (ٰٰٰSAW) from behind DwellingsAllah the Exalted and Most Blessed admonished those, such as the uncivilized bedouins, who used to call to the Prophet SAW from behind the dwellings which belong to his wives:أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَmost of them have no sense.Allah the Exalted and Most Honored then ordains the better behavior in this regard:وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ صَبَرُوا حَتَّىٰ تَخْرُجَ إِلَيْهِمْ لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ ۚAnd if they had patience till you could come out to them, it…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if they had been patient until you (could) come out to them, it would have been better for them. But Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. See 49:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful. See 49:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty, but Allah has endeared to you the faith and has made it pleasing in your hearts and has made hateful to you disbelief, defiance and disobedience. Those are the (rightly) guided. النَّبِىُّ أَوْلَى بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْThe Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves (33:6)Then He clarifies that they fall short in overseeing their own benefit;لَوْ يُطِيعُكُمْ فِى كَثِيرٍ مِّنَ الاٌّمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ7 cont. - If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would surely be in trouble.'if he obeys all of your opinions and desires, you will earn trouble and hardship.' Allah the Exalted and Most Honored said:وَلَوِ اتَّبَعَ الْحَقُّ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ لَفَسَدَتِ السَّمَـوَتُ وَالاٌّرْضُ وَمَن فِيهِنَّ بَلْ أَتَيْنَـهُمْ بِذِكْرِهِمْ فَهُمْ…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (It is) as bounty from Allah and favor. And Allah is Knowing and Wise. See 49:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hujuraat:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if two factions among the believers should fight, then make settlement between the two. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the ordinance of Allah. And if it returns, then make settlement between them in justice and act justly. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly. And if two parties among the believers fall to fighting, then make peace between them both. But if one of them outrages against the other, then fight you (all) against the one that which outrages till it complies with the command of Allah. Then if it complies, then make reconciliation between them justly, and be equitable. Verily, Allah loves those who are the equitable (49:9). The believers are but a brotherhood. So make reconciliation between your brothers, and have Taqwa of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Humaza:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Woe to every scorner and mocker. فِي عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةٍIn pillars stretched forth.Atiyah Al-'Awfi said, "Pillars of Iron." As-Suddi said, "Made of fire." Al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas, "He will make them enter pillars stretched forth, meaning there will be columns over them, and they will have chains on their necks, and the gates (of Hell) will be shut upon them." This is the end of the Tafsir of Surat Al-Humazah, and all praise and thanks are due to Allah.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Humaza:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Who collects wealth and (continuously) counts it.1 See 104:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Humaza:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal. See 104:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Humaza:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No! He will surely be thrown into the Crusher.1 See 104:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Humaza:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And what can make you know what is the Crusher? See 104:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Humaza:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is the fire of Allah, (eternally) fueled. See 104:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Humaza:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Which mounts directed at the hearts.1 See 104:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Humaza:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, it (i.e., Hellfire) will be closed down upon them. See 104:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Humaza:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: In extended columns.1 See 104:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ikhlaas:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "He is Allah, (who is) One.1 وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌAnd there is none comparable to Him."This means He does not have a spouse." This is as Allah says:بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ تَكُن لَّهُ صَاحِبَةٌ ۖ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍHe is the Originator of the heavens and the earth. How can He have children when He has no wife He created all things. (6:101)Meaning: He owns everything and He created everything. So how can He have a peer among His creatures who can be equal to Him, or a relative who can resemble Him? Glorified, Exalted and far removed is Allah from such a thing.Allah says:وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ وَلَدًا - لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئًا إِدًّا - تَكَادُ السَّمَاوَاتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ وَتَنشَقُّ الْأَرْضُ وَتَخِرُّ الْجِبَالُ هَدًّا - أَن دَعَوْا لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ وَلَدًا - وَمَا يَنبَغِي لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ikhlaas:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah, the Eternal Refuge.1 See 112:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ikhlaas:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He neither begets nor is born. See 112:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ikhlaas:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Nor is there to Him any equivalent." See 112:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When the sky breaks apart. كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِNay! But you deny (the Day of) Ad-Din.Meaning: 'you are only compelled to oppose the Most Generous and meet Him with disobedience, by your rejection in your hearts of the Hereafter, the recompense and the reckoning.' Concerning Allah's statement:وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحَافِظِينَ - كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ - يَعْلَمُونَ مَا تَفْعَلُونَBut verily, over you to watch you (are) Kiraman Katibin, they know all that you do. (82:10-12)Meaning: 'indeed there are noble guardian angels over you, so do not meet them with evil deeds, because they write down all that you do.'

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, (appointed) over you are keepers.1 See 82:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Noble and recording. See 82:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They know whatever you do. See 82:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure. Verily, the Abrar (the righteous believers) will be in Delight (82:13). And verily, the wicked will be in the blazing Fire (Hell) (82:14). Therein they will enter, and taste its burning flame on the Day of Recompense (82:15). And they will not be absent therefrom (82:16). And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is (82:17). Again, what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is (82:18). (It will be) the Day when no person shall have power for another, and the Decision, that Day, will be with Allah (82:19).The Reward of the Righteous and the SinnersAllah informs of what the righteous will receive of delight. They are those who obeyed Allah and did not meet Him with disobedience (sins). Then He mentions that the evildoers will be…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire. See 82:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will (enter to) burn therein on the Day of Recompense. See 82:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And never therefrom will they be absent. See 82:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And what can make you know what is the Day of Recompense? See 82:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then, what can make you know what is the Day of Recompense? See 82:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is the Day when a soul will not possess for another soul (power to do) a thing; and the command, that Day, is (entirely) with Allah. See 82:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when the stars fall, scattering. See 82:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when the seas are erupted. See 82:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when the (contents of) graves are scattered (i.e., exposed). See 82:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: A soul will (then) know what it has put forth and kept back. See 82:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous. See 82:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you? See 82:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: In whatever form He willed has He assembled you. See 82:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No! But you deny the Recompense. See 82:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Has there (not) come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing (even) mentioned? إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَVerily, We guided to him the way,Meaning: 'We explained it to him, made it clear to him and showed it to him.' This is as Allah says:وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ فَاسْتَحَبُّوا الْعَمَىٰ عَلَى الْهُدَىٰAnd as for Thamud, We guided them but they preferred blindness to guidance. (41:17)Allah also said:وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِAnd We guided him to the two ways. (90:10)Meaning: 'We explained to him the path of good and the path of evil.' This is the statement of 'Ikrimah, 'Atiyah, Ibn Zayd and Mujahid from what is well-known from him and the majority. Allah then says:إِمَّا شَاكِرًا وَإِمَّا كَفُورًاWhether he be grateful or ungrateful.This is his decree. Thus, with this he is either wretched or happy. This is like what has been recorded…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We fear from our Lord a Day austere and distressful." See 76:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day and give them radiance and happiness. See 76:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And will reward them for what they patiently endured (with) a garden (in Paradise) and silk (garments). See 76:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (They will be) reclining therein on adorned couches. They will not see therein any (burning) sun or (freezing) cold. The Raised Couches and the Lack of Heat and ColdAllah tells us about the people of Paradise and the eternal delights they will experience, as well as the comprehensive favors that they will be given. Allah says:مُّتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا عَلَى الاٌّرَائِكِReclining therein on raised couches.This has already been discussed in Surat As-Saffat and the difference of opinion about the meaning of reclining. Is it lying down, reclining on the elbows, sitting down cross-legged, or being firmly seated We have also mentioned that the Al-Ara'ik are couches beneath curtained canopies. Concerning Allah's statement:لاَ يَرَوْنَ فِيهَا شَمْساً وَلاَ زَمْهَرِيراًthey will see there neither the excessive heat, nor the excessive bitter cold.Meaning: there will be no disturbing heat with them, nor any painful cold, rather…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And near above them are its shades, and its (fruit) to be picked will be lowered in compliance. See 76:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver and cups having been (created) clear (as glass). See 76:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Clear glasses (made) from silver of which they have determined the measure. See 76:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they will be given to drink a cup (of wine) whose mixture is of ginger. See 76:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (From) a fountain within it (i.e., Paradise) named Salsabeel. See 76:13
