Verily, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection about that wherein they used to differ (45:17). Then We have put you on a (legal) way of commandment. So follow you that, and follow not the desires of those who know not (45:18). Verily, they can avail you nothing against Allah. Verily,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We gave them clear proofs of the matter (of religion). And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ. See 45:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then We put you, (O Muḥammad), on an ordained way concerning the matter (of religion); so follow it and do not follow the inclinations of those who do not know. See 45:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, they will never avail you against Allah at all. And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another; but Allah is the protector of the righteous. See 45:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. See 45:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: This (Qur’ān) is enlightenment for mankind and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain (in faith). See 45:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or do those who commit evils think We will make them like those who have believed and done righteous deeds - (make them) equal in their life and their death?1 Evil is that which they judge (i.e., assume). Or do those who earn evil deeds think that We shall hold them equal with those who believe and do righteous good deeds, in their present life and after their death? Worst is the judgement that they make (45:21). And Allah has created the heavens and the earth with truth, in order that each person may be recompensed what he has earned, and they will not be wronged (45:22). Have you seen him who takes his own lust as his god? And Allah, left him astray with knowledge, and sealed his hearing and his heart, and put a cover on his sight.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah created the heavens and earth in truth and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged. See 45:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have you seen he who has taken as his god his (own) desire, and Allah has sent him astray due to knowledge1 and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put over his vision a veil? So who will guide him after Allah? Then will you not be reminded? See 45:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they say, "There is not but our worldly life; we die and live,1 and nothing destroys us except time." And they have of that no knowledge; they are only assuming. And they say: There is nothing but our life of this world, we die and we live and nothing destroys us except Ad-Dahr (time). And they have no knowledge of it, they only presume (45:24). And when Our Clear Ayat are recited to them, their argument is no other than that they say: "Bring back our (dead) fathers, if you are truthful! (45:25). Say (to them): "Allah gives you life, then causes you to die, then He will assemble you on the Day of Resurrection about which there is no doubt. But most of mankind know not (45:26). The Conviction of the Disbelievers, Their Argument and the Refutation of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, their argument is only that they say, "Bring (back) our forefathers, if you should be truthful." See 45:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Allah causes you to live, then causes you to die; then He will assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt, but most of the people do not know." See 45:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And the Day the Hour appears - that Day the falsifiers will lose. And to Allah belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. And on the Day that the Hour will be established – on that Day the followers of falsehood shall lose (45:27). And you will see each nation humbled to their knees (Jathiyah), each nation will be called to its Record (of deeds). This Day you shall be recompensed for what you used to do (45:28). This Our Record speaks about you with truth. Verily, We were recording what you used to do (45:29).Some of the Conditions of the Day of Resurrection and its HorrorsAllah mentions that He is the King and Owner of the heavens and earth, and the Only Ruler over them…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you will see every nation kneeling (from fear). Every nation will be called to its record (and told), "Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do. See 45:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: This, Our record, speaks about you in truth. Indeed, We were having transcribed1 whatever you used to do." See 45:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, within the heavens and earth are signs for the believers. See 45:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is what is the clear attainment. Then, as for those who believed and did good deeds, their Lord will admit them to His mercy. That will be the evident success (45:30). But as for those who disbelieved (it will be said to them): Were not Our Ayat recited to you? But you were proud, and you were a people who were criminals (45:31). And when it was said: "Verily, Allah's promise is the truth, and there is no doubt about the coming of the Hour," you said: "We know not what is the Hour: we do not think it but conjecture, and we have no firm convincing belief (therein) (45:32). And the evil of what they did will appear to them,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But as for those who disbelieved, (it will be said), "Were not Our verses recited to you, but you were arrogant and became a criminal people? See 45:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when it was said, 'Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth and the Hour (is coming) - no doubt about it,' you said, 'We know not what is the Hour. We assume only assumption, and we are not convinced.'" See 45:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the evil consequences of what they did will appear to them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to ridicule. See 45:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it will be said, "Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours, and your refuge is the Fire, and for you there are no helpers. See 45:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is because you took the verses of Allah in ridicule, and worldly life deluded you." So that Day they will not be removed from it, nor will they be asked to appease (Allah). See 45:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then, to Allah belongs (all) praise - Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds. See 45:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to Him belongs (all) grandeur within the heavens and the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. See 45:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And in the creation of yourselves and what He disperses of moving creatures are signs for people who are certain (in faith). See 45:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (in) the alternation of night and day and (in) what Allah sends down from the sky of provision (i.e., rain) and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness and (in His) directing of the winds are signs for a people who reason. See 45:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth. Then in what statement after Allah and His verses will they believe? These are the Ayat of Allah, which We recite to you with truth. Then in which speech after Allah and His Ayat will they believe (45:6). Woe to every sinful liar (45:7). Who hears the Ayat of Allah Tutla (recited) to him, yet persists with pride as if he heard them not. So announce to him a painful torment (45:8). And when he learns something of Our Ayat, he makes them a jest. For such there will be a humiliating torment (45:9). In front of them there is Hell. And that which they have earned will be of no profit to them, nor those whom they have taken as protective friends besides Allah. And theirs…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Woe to every sinful liar. See 45:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Who hears the verses of Allah recited to him, then persists arrogantly as if he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment. See 45:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jaathiya:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when he knows anything of Our verses, he takes them in ridicule. Those will have a humiliating punishment. See 45:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, (O Muḥammad), "It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened and said, 'Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur’ān (i.e., recitation). وَأَنَّهُمْ ظَنُّوا كَمَا ظَنَنْتُمْ أَنْ لَنْ يَبْعَثَ اللَّهُ أَحَدًاAnd they thought as you thought, that Allah will not send any Messenger.Meaning: Allah would never send a Messenger after this long period of time. This was said by Al-Kalbi and Ibn Jarir.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And we do not know (therefore) whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them a right course. See 72:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And among us are the righteous, and among us are (others) not so; we were (of) divided ways.1 'There are among us some that are righteous, and some the contrary; we are groups having different ways (72:11). 'And we think that we cannot escape Allah in the earth, nor can we escape Him by flight (72:12). 'And indeed when we heard the Guidance, we believed therein, and whosoever believes in his Lord shall have no fear, either of a decrease in the reward of his good deeds or an increase in the punishment for his sins (72:13). 'And of us some are Muslims, and of us some are Al-Qasitun. And whosoever has embraced Islam, then such have sought the right path.' (72:14). And as for the Qasitun, they shall be firewood for Hell (72:15). If they had believed in Allah,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And we have become certain that we will never cause failure to Allah upon earth, nor can we escape Him by flight. See 72:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when we heard the guidance (i.e., the Qur’ān), we believed in it. And whoever believes in his Lord will not fear deprivation or burden.1 See 72:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And among us are Muslims (in submission to Allah), and among us are the unjust.1 And whoever has become Muslim - those have sought out the right course. See 72:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But as for the unjust, they will be, for Hell, firewood.' See 72:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (Allah revealed) that if they had remained straight on the way, We would have given them abundant rain (i.e., provision). See 72:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So We might test them therein. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord1 He will put into arduous punishment. See 72:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (He revealed) that the masjids1 are for Allah, so do not invoke2 with Allah anyone. And the Masjids are for Allah, so invoke not anyone along with Allah (72:18). And when the servant of Allah stood up invoking Him in prayer they just made round him a dense crowd as if sticking one over the other (72:19). Say: "I invoke only my Lord, and I associate none as partners along with Him (72:20). Say: "It is not in my power to cause you harm, or to bring you to the right path (72:21). Say: "None can protect me from Allah's punishment, nor can I find refuge except in Him (72:22). "(Mine is) but conveyance from Allah and His Messages, and whosoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then verily, for him is the fire of Hell, he shall dwell therein…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that when the Servant (i.e., Prophet) of Allah stood up supplicating Him, they almost became about him a compacted mass."1 See 72:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It guides to the right course, and we have believed in it. And we will never associate with our Lord anyone. See 72:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, (O Muḥammad), "I only invoke my Lord and do not associate with Him anyone." See 72:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Indeed, I do not possess for you (the power of) harm or right direction." See 72:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Indeed, there will never protect me from Allah anyone (if I should disobey), nor will I find in other than Him a refuge. See 72:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But (I have for you) only notification from Allah, and His messages." And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, for him is the fire of Hell; they will abide therein forever. See 72:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (The disbelievers continue) until, when they see that which they are promised, then they will know who is weaker in helpers and less in number. See 72:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "I do not know if what you are promised is near or if my Lord will grant for it a (long) period." Say: "I know not whether that which you are promised is near or whether my Lord will appoint for it a distant term (72:25). "The All-Knower of the Unseen, and He reveals to none His Unseen (72:26). Except to a Messenger whom He has chosen, and then He makes a band of watching guards to march before him and behind him (72:27). Till he knows that they have conveyed the Messages of their Lord. And He surrounds all that which is with them, and He keeps count of all things (72:28).The Messenger of Allah SAW does not know when the Hour will beAllah commands His Messenger SAW to say to the people that he has no knowledge…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (He is) Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His (knowledge of the) unseen to anyone. See 72:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except whom He has approved of messengers, and indeed, He sends before him (i.e., each messenger) and behind him observers.1 See 72:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That he (i.e., Muḥammad SAW) may know1 that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord; and He has encompassed whatever is with them and has enumerated all things in number. See 72:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (it teaches) that exalted is the nobleness of our Lord; He has not taken a wife or a son. See 72:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that our foolish one (i.e., Iblees)1 has been saying about Allah an excessive transgression. See 72:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And we had thought that mankind and the jinn would never speak about Allah a lie. See 72:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And there were men from mankind who sought refuge in men from the jinn, so they (only) increased them in burden (i.e., sin). See 72:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they had thought, as you thought, that Allah would never send anyone (as a messenger). See 72:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And we have sought (to reach) the heaven but found it filled with powerful guards and burning flames. 'And we have sought to reach the heaven; but we found it filled with stern guards and flaming fires (72:8). 'And verily, we used to sit there in stations, to (steal) a hearing, but any who listens now will find a flaming fire watching him in ambush (72:9). 'And we know not whether evil is intended for those on the earth, or whether their Lord intends for them guidance (72:10).The Jinns Stealing Information from the Sky before the Messenger SAW was Sent and Striking Them with Flaming Fire after His ComingAllah informs about the Jinns when He sent His Messenger Muhammad SAW and revealed the Qur'an to him. Among the ways He protected it (the Qur'an) was by filling sky with stern…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jinn:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And we used to sit therein in positions for hearing,1 but whoever listens now will find a burning flame lying in wait for him. See 72:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jumu'a:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is exalting Allah,1 the Sovereign, the Pure, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.2 ذَٰلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ ۚ وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِThat is the grace of Allah, which He bestows on whom He wills. And Allah is the Owner of mighty grace.refers to the great prophethood that He granted Muhammad SAW and the qualities that He favored his Ummah with, by sending Muhammad SAW to them.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jumu'a:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often that you may succeed. See 62:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jumu'a:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But (on one occasion) when they saw a transaction or a diversion, (O Muḥammad), they rushed to it and left you standing. Say, "What is with Allah is better than diversion and than a transaction, and Allah is the best of providers." And when they see some merchandise or some amusement, they disperse headlong to it, and leave you standing. Say: That which Allah has is better than any amusement or merchandise! And Allah is the best of providers (62:11). The Prohibition of leaving the Masjid while the Imam is delivering the Friday Sermon Allah criticizes what happened during one Friday sermon, when a caravan arrived at Al-Madinah and the people rushed out to the merchandise. Allah said:وَإِذَا رَأَوْا تِجَارَةً أَوْ لَهْوًا انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْهَا وَتَرَكُوكَ قَائِمًا ۚAnd when they see some merchandise or some amusement, they disperse headlong to it,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jumu'a:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is He who has sent among the unlettered (Arabs) a Messenger from themselves reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book (i.e., the Qur’ān) and wisdom (i.e., the sunnah) - although they were before in clear error. See 62:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jumu'a:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (to) others of them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. See 62:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jumu'a:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty. See 62:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jumu'a:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not take it on1 is like that of a donkey who carries volumes (of books).2 Wretched is the example of the people who deny the signs of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Tawrah, but did not carry it, is as the likeness of a donkey which carries huge burdens of books. How bad is the example of people who deny the Ayat of Allah. And Allah does not guide the people who are wrongdoers (62:5). Say: "O you Jews! If you pretend that you are friends of Allah, to the exclusion of (all) other people, then long for death if you are truthful (62:6). But they will never long for it, because of what…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jumu'a:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah, excluding the (other) people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful." See 62:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jumu'a:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But they will not wish for it, ever, because of what their hands have put forth. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers. See 62:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jumu'a:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Indeed, the death from which you flee - indeed, it will meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you about what you used to do." See 62:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Jumu'a:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, when (the adhān) is called for the prayer on the day of Jumuʿah (Friday), then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew. O you who believe! When the call is proclaimed for the Salah on Al-Jumu'ah (Friday), then hasten (Fas'aw) to the remembrance of Allah and leave off business. That is better for you if you did but know (62:9). Then when the Salah is complete, you may disperse through the land, and seek the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah much, that you may be successful (62:10).Al-Jumu'ah (Friday), and the Orders and Etiquette for FridayFriday is called Al-Jumu'ah because it is derived from Al-Jam', literally, gathering. The people of Islam gather weekly, on every Friday in the major places of worship. It was…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kaafiroon:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "O disbelievers. لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْTo you be your religion.means disbelief.وَلِيَ دِينِand to me my religion.means, Islam.This is the end of the Tafsir of Surat Qul ya Ayyuhal-Kafirun.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kaafiroon:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: I do not worship what you worship. See 109:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kaafiroon:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. See 109:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kaafiroon:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Nor will I be a worshipper of what you worship. See 109:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kaafiroon:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Nor will you be worshippers of what I worship. See 109:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kaafiroon:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For you is your religion, and for me is my religion." See 109:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (All) praise is (due) to Allah, who has sent down upon His Servant (Muḥammad SAW) the Book and has not made therein any deviance.1 مَّا لَهُم بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍNo knowledge have they of such a thing,Meaning: this thing that they have fabricated and made up.وَلَا لِآبَائِهِمْnor had their fathers.Meaning: their predecessors.كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةًMighty is the wordThis highlights the seriousness and enormity of the lie they have made up. Allah says:كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْMighty is the word that comes out of their mouths.Meaning: it has no basis apart from what they say, and they have no evidence for it apart from their own lies and fabrications. Hence Allah says:إِن يَقُولُونَ إِلَّا كَذِبًاThey utter nothing but a lie.Reason Why this Surah was RevealedMuhammad bin Ishaq mentioned the reason why this Surah was revealed. He said that an old man from among the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Mention) when the youths retreated to the cave and said, "Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance." See 18:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:100 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We will present Hell that Day to the disbelievers, on display. And on that Day We shall present Hell to the disbelievers, plain to view (18:100). (To) those whose eyes had been under a covering from My Reminder, and they could not bear to hear (it) (18:101). Do then those who disbelieved think that they can take My servants as Awliya' (protectors) besides Me? Verily, We have prepared Hell as an entertainment for the disbelievers (18:102).Hell will be Displayed before the Disbelievers on the Day of ResurrectionAllah tells us what He will do to the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection. He will show Hell to them, meaning He will bring it forth for them to see its punishment and torment before they enter it. This will intensify their distress and grief. In Sahih Muslim it is recorded that…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:101 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those whose eyes had been within a cover (removed) from My remembrance,1 and they were not able to hear.2 See 18:100

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:102 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants instead of Me as allies? Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a lodging. See 18:100

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:103 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, (O Muḥammad), "Shall we (believers) inform you of the greatest losers as to (their) deeds? Say: "Shall We tell you the greatest losers in respect of (their) deeds? (18:103). "Those whose efforts have been wasted in this life while they thought that they were acquiring good by their deeds (18:104). "They are those who deny the Ayat of their Lord and the meeting with Him. So their works are in vain, and on the Day of Resurrection, We shall assign no weight for them (18:105). "That shall be their recompense, Hell; because they disbelieved and took My Ayat and My Messengers for jest (18:106).The Greatest Losers in Respect of (Their) DeedsAl-Bukhari recorded from 'Amr that Mus'ab who said: I asked my father – meaning Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas – about Allah's saying:قُلْ هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُم بِالْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَالًاSay: "Shall We tell…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:104 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (They are) those whose effort is lost in worldly life, while they think that they are doing well in work." See 18:103

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:105 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those are the ones who disbelieve in the verses of their Lord and in (their) meeting Him, so their deeds have become worthless; and We will not assign to them on the Day of Resurrection any weight (i.e., importance). See 18:103

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:106 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is their recompense - Hell - for what they denied and (because) they took My signs and My messengers in ridicule. See 18:103

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:107 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - they will have the Gardens of Paradise1 as a lodging. "Verily, those who believe and do righteous deeds, shall have the Gardens of Al-Firdaws for their entertainment (18:107). "Wherein they shall dwell (forever). No desire will they have for removal therefrom (18:108).The Reward of the Righteous BelieversAllah tells us about His blessed servants, those who believed in Allah and His Messengers and accepted as truth what the Messengers brought. He tells us that they will have the Gardens of Al-Firdaws (Paradise). Abu Umamah said, "Al-Firdaws is the center of Paradise." Qatadah said, "Al-Firdaws is a hill in Paradise, at its center, the best of it." This was also narrated from Samurah and attributed to the Prophet SAW:الْفِرْدَوْسُ رَبْوَةُ الْجَنَّةِ أَوْسَطُهَا وَأَحْسَنُهَاAl-Firdaws is a hill in Paradise, at its center, the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:108 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Wherein they abide eternally. They will not desire from it any transfer. See 18:107

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:109 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "If the sea were ink for (writing) the words1 of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it in (continual) supplement." Say: If the sea were ink for the Words of my Lord, surely, the sea would be exhausted before the Words of my Lord would be finished, even if We brought like it for its aid (18:109).The Words of the Lord Can Never be FinishedAllah says: 'Say, O Muhammad, if the water of the sea were ink for a pen to write down the words, wisdom and signs of Allah, the sea would run dry before it all could be written down.وَلَوْ جِئْنَا بِمِثْلِهِeven if We brought like itmeans, another sea, then another, and so on, additional seas to be used for writing.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So We cast (a cover of sleep) over their ears within the cave for a number of years. See 18:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:110 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "I am only a man like you, to whom has been revealed that your god is one God. So whoever would hope for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone." Say: I am only a man like you. It has been revealed to me that your God is One God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him work righteousness and associate none as a partner in the worship of his Lord (18:110).Muhammad SAW is a Human Being and a Messenger, and the God is OneAllah says to His Messenger Muhammad SAW:قُلْSayto these idolators who reject your message to them:إِنَّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ'I am only a man like you.Whoever claims that I am lying, let him bring something like this that I…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then We awakened them that We might show which of the two factions was most precise in calculating what (extent) they had remained in time. See 18:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is We who relate to you, (O Muḥammad), their story in truth. Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance. We narrate unto you their story with truth: Truly, they were young men who believed in their Lord (Allah), and We increased them in guidance (18:13). And We made their hearts firm and strong when they stood up and said: "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, never shall we call upon any god other than Him; if we did, we should indeed have uttered an enormity in disbelief (18:14). These our people have taken for worship gods other than Him. Why do they not bring for them a clear authority? And who does more wrong than he who invents a lie against Allah (18:15). (The young men…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We bound (i.e., made firm) their hearts when they stood up and said, "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. Never will we invoke besides Him any deity. We would have certainly spoken, then, an excessive transgression. See 18:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: These, our people, have taken besides Him deities. Why do they not bring for (worship of) them a clear evidence? And who is more unjust than one who invents about Allah a lie?" See 18:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (The youths said to one another), "And when you have withdrawn from them and that which they worship other than Allah, retreat to the cave. Your Lord will spread out for you of His mercy and will prepare for you from your affair facility." See 18:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (had you been present), you would see the sun when it rose, inclining away from their cave on the right, and when it set, passing away from them on the left, while they were (lying) within an open space thereof. That was from the signs of Allah. He whom Allah guides is the (rightly) guided, but he whom He sends astray - never will you find for him a protecting guide. And you might have seen the sun, when it rose, declining to the right from their cave, and when it set, turning away from them to the left, while they lay in the midst of the cave. That is from the Ayat of Allah. He whom Allah guides, he is the rightly-guided; but he whom He sends astray, for him you will find no guardian to lead him…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you would think them awake, while they were asleep. And We turned them to the right and to the left, while their dog stretched his forelegs at the entrance. If you had looked at them, you would have turned from them in flight and been filled by them with terror. And you would have thought them awake, whereas they were asleep. And We turned them on their right and on their left sides, and their dog stretching forth his two forelegs at the Wasid. Had you happened upon them, you would certainly have turned back from them in flight, and would certainly have been filled with awe of them (18:18).Their Sleep in the CaveSome of the scholars mentioned that when Allah caused them to sleep, their eyelids did not close, lest disintegration took hold of them. If their eyes…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And similarly,1 We awakened them that they might question one another. Said a speaker from among them, "How long have you remained (here)?" They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day." They said, "Your Lord is most knowing of how long you remained. So send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city and let him look to which is the best of food and bring you provision from it and let him be cautious. And let no one be aware of you. Likewise, We woke them that they might question one another. A speaker among them said: "How long have you stayed (here)?" They said: "We have stayed a day or part of a day." They said: "Your Lord knows best how long you have stayed (here). So send one of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (He has made it) straight, to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward (i.e., Paradise). See 18:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, if they come to know of you, they will stone you or return you to their religion. And never would you succeed, then - ever." See 18:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And similarly, We caused them to be found that they (who found them) would know that the promise of Allah is truth and that of the Hour there is no doubt. (That was) when they1 disputed among themselves about their affair and (then) said, "Construct over them a structure. Their Lord is most knowing about them." Said those who prevailed in the matter, "We will surely take (for ourselves) over them a masjid."2 And thus We made their case known, that they might know that the promise of Allah is true, and that there can be no doubt about the Hour. (Remember) when they (the people) disputed among themselves about their case, they said: Construct a building over them; their Lord knows best about them," (then) those who won their point said: "We verily, shall build a place of worship…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They (i.e., people) will say there were three, the fourth of them being their dog; and they will say there were five, the sixth of them being their dog - guessing at the unseen; and they will say there were seven, and the eighth of them was their dog. Say, (O Muḥammad), "My Lord is most knowing of their number. None knows them except a few. So do not argue about them except with an obvious argument1 and do not inquire about them among (the speculators) from anyone." They say they were three, the dog being the fourth among them; and they say they were five, the dog being the sixth, guessing at the unseen; and they say they were seven, and the dog being the eighth. Say: "My Lord knows best their number; none knows them but a few."…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow." And never say of anything, "I shall do such and such thing tomorrow (18:23). Except (with the saying), "If Allah wills!" And remember your Lord when you forget and say: "It may be that my Lord guides me to a nearer way of truth than this (18:24).Saying "If Allah Wills" When Determining to do Something in the FutureHere Allah, may He be glorified, shows His Messenger SAW the correct etiquette when determining to do something in the future; this should always be referred to the will of Allah, the Knower of the Unseen, Who knows what was and what is yet to be and what is not to be, and how it will be if it is to be. It was recorded in the Two Sahihs that Abu Hurayrah…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except (when adding), "If Allah wills." And remember your Lord when you forget (it) and say, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right conduct." See 18:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and exceeded by nine.1 And they stayed in their cave three hundred years, adding nine (18:25). Say: "Allah knows best how long they stayed. With Him is the unseen of the heavens and the earth." How clearly He sees, and hears (everything)! They have no protector other than Him, and He makes none to share in His decision and His rule (18:26).The Length of their Stay in the CaveHere Allah tells His Messenger SAW the length of time the people of the Cave spent in their cave, from the time when He caused them to sleep until the time when He resurrected them and caused the people of that era to find them. The length of time was three hundred plus nine years in lunar years, which is three hundred…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Allah is most knowing of how long they remained. He has (knowledge of) the unseen (aspects) of the heavens and the earth. How Seeing is He and how Hearing! They have not besides Him any protector, and He shares not His legislation with anyone." See 18:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And recite, (O Muḥammad), what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord. There is no changer of His words, and never will you find in other than Him a refuge. And recite what has been revealed to you (O Muhammad) of your Lord's Book. None can change His Words, and none will you find as refuge other than Him (18:27). And keep yourself (O Muhammad) patiently with those who call on their Lord morning and afternoon, seeking His Face; and let not your eyes overlook them, desiring the pomp and glitter of the life of the world; and obey not him whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, and who follows his own lusts, and whose affair has been lost (18:28).The Command to Recite the Qur'an and to Patiently Keep Company with the BelieversCommanding…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And keep yourself patient (by being) with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His face (i.e., acceptance). And let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring adornments of the worldly life, and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire and whose affair is ever (in) neglect.1 See 18:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve." Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a fire whose walls will surround them. And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like murky oil, which scalds (their) faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place. And say: "The truth is from your Lord." Then whosoever wills, let him believe; and whosoever wills, let him disbelieve. Verily, We have prepared for the wrongdoers, a Fire whose walls will be surrounding them. And if they ask for drink, they will be granted water like Al-Muhl, that will scald their faces. Terrible is the drink, and an evil Murtafaq (18:29).The Truth is from Allah, and the Punishment of Those Who do Not Believe…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: In which they will remain forever. See 18:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of any who did well in deeds. Verily, as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, certainly We shall not make the reward of anyone to be lost who does his (righteous) deeds in the most perfect manner (18:30). These! For them will be Jannatu 'Adn; wherein rivers flow beneath them; therein they will be adorned with bracelets of gold, and they will wear green garments of Sundus and Istabraq. They will be Muttaki'in therein on Ara'ik. How good is the reward, and what an excellent Murtafaq (18:31).The Reward of those Who Believe and do Righteous DeedsWhen Allah mentions the state of those who are doomed, He follows that by mentioning the blessed who believed in Allah and believed…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those will have gardens of perpetual residence; beneath them rivers will flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and will wear green garments of fine silk and brocade, reclining therein on adorned couches. Excellent is the reward, and good is the resting place. See 18:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And present to them an example of two men: We granted to one of them two gardens of grapevines, and We bordered them with palm trees and placed between them (fields of) crops. And put forward to them the example of two men: unto one of them We had given two gardens of grapes, and We had surrounded both with date palms; and had put between them green crops (cultivated fields) (18:32). Each of those two gardens brought forth its produce, and failed not in the least therein, and We caused a river to gush forth in the midst of both (18:33). And he had Thamar, and he said to his companion in the course of discussion: I am greater than you in wealth and have a mightier entourage (18:34). And he went into his garden while having been unjust…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Each of the two gardens produced its fruit and did not fall short thereof in anything. And We caused to gush forth within them a river. See 18:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he had fruit, so he said to his companion while he was conversing with him, "I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in (numbers of) men." See 18:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he entered his garden while he was unjust to himself.1 He said, "I do not think that this will perish - ever. See 18:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And I do not think the Hour will occur. And even if I should be brought back to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a return." See 18:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: His companion said to him while he was conversing with him, "Have you disbelieved in He who created you from dust and then from a sperm-drop and then proportioned you (as) a man? His companion said to him during his discussion: Do you disbelieve in Him Who created you out of dust, then out of Nutfah, then fashioned you into a man? (18:37). "But as for my part, (I believe) that He is Allah, my Lord, and none shall I associate as partner with my Lord (18:38). "It was better for you to say, when you entered your garden: 'That which Allah wills! There is no power but with Allah!' If you see me less than you in wealth, and children, (18:39). "It may be that my Lord will give me something better than your garden, and will send on…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But as for me, He is Allah, my Lord, and I do not associate with my Lord anyone. See 18:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And why did you, when you entered your garden, not say, 'What Allah willed (has occurred); there is no power except in Allah'? Although you see me less than you in wealth and children. See 18:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son." See 18:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It may be that my Lord will give me (something) better than your garden and will send upon it a (disastrous) penalty from the sky, and it will become a smooth, dusty ground. See 18:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or its water will become sunken (into the earth), so you would never be able to seek it." See 18:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And his fruits were encompassed (by ruin), so he began to turn his hands about (in dismay) over what he had spent on it, while it had collapsed upon its trellises, and said, "Oh, I wish I had not associated with my Lord anyone."1 So his fruits were encircled (with ruin). And began Yuqallibu his hands over what he had spent upon it, while it was all destroyed on its trellises, and he could only say: Would that I had ascribed no partners to my Lord! (18:42). And he had no group of men to help him against Allah, nor could he defend (or save) himself (18:43). There (on the Day of Resurrection), Al-Walayah will be for Allah (Alone), the True God. He (Allah) is the best for reward and the best for the final end (18:44).The Evil Results of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And there was for him no company to aid him other than Allah, nor could he defend himself. See 18:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: There1 the authority is (completely) for Allah, the Truth. He is best in reward and best in outcome. See 18:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And present to them the example of the life of this world, (its being) like rain which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it1 and (then) it becomes dry remnants, scattered by the winds. And Allah is ever, over all things, Perfect in Ability. And mention the parable of the worldly life: it is like the water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, and becomes fresh and green. But (later) it becomes dry and broken pieces, which the winds scatter. And Allah is able to do everything (18:45). Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world. But the good righteous deeds that last, are better with your Lord for reward and better for hope (18:46).The Parable of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Wealth and children are (but) adornment of the worldly life. But the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord1 for reward and better for (one's) hope. See 18:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (warn of) the Day when We will remove the mountains and you will see the earth exposed,1 and We will gather them and not leave behind from them anyone. And (remember) the Day We shall cause the mountains to pass away, and you will see the earth as a levelled plain, and We shall gather them so that We will leave not one of them behind (18:47). And they will be set before your Lord, aligned. (He will say:) Now indeed, you have come to Us as We created you the first time. Nay, but you thought that We had appointed no meeting for you (with Us) (18:48). And the Book will be produced, and you will see the criminals, fearful of that which is therein. They will say: "Woe to us! What sort of Book is this that…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they will be presented before your Lord in rows, (and He will say), "You have certainly come to Us just as We created you the first time. But you claimed that We would never make for you an appointment." See 18:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the record (of deeds) will be placed (open), and you will see the criminals fearful of that within it, and they will say, "Oh, woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present (before them). And your Lord does injustice to no one. See 18:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They have no knowledge of it,1 nor had their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak not except a lie. See 18:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except for Iblees. He was of the jinn and departed from (i.e., disobeyed) the command of his Lord. Then will you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me while they are enemies to you? Wretched it is for the wrongdoers as an exchange. And (remember) when We said to the angels: "Prostrate yourselves unto Adam." So they prostrated themselves, except Iblis. He was one of the Jinn; he disobeyed the command of his Lord. Will you then take him and his offspring as protectors and helpers rather than Me while they are enemies to you? What an evil is the exchange for the wrongdoers (18:50).The Story of Adam and IblisAllah points out to the Children of Adam the enmity of Iblis towards them…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: I did not make them witness to the creation of the heavens and the earth or to the creation of themselves, and I would not have taken the misguiders as assistants. They did not witness the creation of the heavens and the earth nor their own creation, nor did I take those who mislead as 'Adudan (18:51).The Gods of the Idolators did Not Witness the Creation of Anything, Not Even ThemselvesAllah says: 'These whom you take as helpers instead of Me are creatures just like you. They do not possess anything and did not witness the creation of heaven and earth, because they did not exist at that time.' Allah says, 'I am the One Who independently and exclusively creates and controls all things, and I have no partner, associate or advisor in that.' As Allah says:قُلِ ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُم…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (warn of) the Day when He will say, "Call My 'partners' whom you claimed," and they will invoke them, but they will not respond to them. And We will put between them (a valley of) destruction. And (remember) the Day He will say: "Call those (so-called) partners of Mine whom you claimed." Then they will cry unto them, but they will not answer them, and We shall put Mawbiq between them (18:52). And the criminals shall see the Fire and apprehend that they are to fall therein. And they will find no way of escape from it (18:53).Their Partners are Not Able to Respond and the Criminals are Brought to the FireAllah tells us how He will address the idolators on the Day of Resurrection before all of creation, rebuking and scolding them:نَادُوا شُرَكَائِيَ الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْCall those (so-called) partners…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are to fall therein. And they will not find from it a way elsewhere. See 18:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have certainly diversified in this Qur’ān for the people from every (kind of) example; but man has ever been, most of anything, (prone to) dispute. And indeed We have given every kind of example in this Qur'an for mankind. But, man is ever more quarrelsome than anything (18:54).Examples Put forth in the Qur'anAllah says, 'In this Qur'an, We have explained to mankind and given clear details of matters so that they will not stray from the truth or be misled from the path of guidance. Despite this explanation, man is very quarrelsome and opposes truth with falsehood,' except for those whom Allah guides to the path of salvation. Imam Ahmad recorded that Ali bin Abi Talib said that the Messenger of Allah SAW came to visit him and Fatimah, the daughter of Allah's Messenger at night, and said:أَلَا…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And nothing has prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them and from asking forgiveness of their Lord except that there (must) befall them the (accustomed) precedent of the former peoples1 or that the punishment should come (directly) before them. And nothing prevents men from believing, while the guidance has come to them, and from asking forgiveness of their Lord, except that the ways of the ancients be repeated with them, or the torment be brought to them face to face (18:55). And We send not the Messengers except as bearers of good news and warners. But those who disbelieve, argue with falsehood, in order to refute the truth thereby. And they take My Ayat and that which they are warned for jest (18:56).The Rebellion of the DisbelieversAllah tells us about the rebellion of the disbelievers in ancient…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We send not the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners. And those who disbelieve dispute by (using) falsehood to (attempt to) invalidate thereby the truth and have taken My verses, and that of which they are warned, in ridicule. See 18:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forth? Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if you invite them to guidance - they will never be guided, then - ever. And who does more wrong than he who is reminded of the Ayat (signs) of his Lord, but turns away from them, forgetting what his hands have sent forth. Truly, We have set over their hearts Akinnah, lest they should understand this (the Qur'an), and in their ears, deafness. And if you call them to guidance, even then they will never be guided (18:57). And your Lord is Most Forgiving, Owner of mercy. Were He to call them…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And your Lord is the Forgiving, the possessor of mercy. If He were to impose blame upon them for what they earned, He would have hastened for them the punishment. Rather, for them is an appointment from which they will never find an escape. See 18:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those cities - We destroyed them when they wronged, and We made for their destruction an appointed time. See 18:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then perhaps you would kill yourself through grief over them, (O Muḥammad), if they do not believe in this message, (and) out of sorrow. Perhaps, you would kill yourself in grief, over their footsteps, because they believe not in this narration (18:6). Verily, we have made that which is on earth an adornment for it, in order that We may test which of them are best in deeds (18:7). And verily, We shall make all that is on it bare, dry soil (18:8).Do Not Feel Sorry Because the Idolators do Not BelieveAllah consoles His Messenger SAW for his sorrow over the idoltors because they would not believe and keep away from him. He also said:فَلَا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسَرَاتٍSo destroy not yourself in sorrow for them. (35:8)وَلَا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْAnd grieve not over them. (16:127)لَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَIt may…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) when Musa said to his boy (i.e., servant), "I will not cease (traveling) until I reach the junction of the two seas or continue for a long period." And (remember) when Musa said to his boy-servant: I will not give up until I reach the junction of the two seas or a Huqub passes (18:60). But when they reached the junction of the two seas, they forgot their fish, and it took its way through the sea as in a tunnel (18:61). So when they passed further on, Musa said to his boy-servant: "Bring us our morning meal; truly, we have suffered Nasaban in this, our journey (18:62). He said: "Do you remember when we betook ourselves to the rock? I indeed forgot the fish; none but Shaytan made me forget to remember it. It took its course…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But when they reached the junction between them, they forgot their fish, and it took its course into the sea, slipping away. See 18:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So when they had passed beyond it, (Musa) said to his boy, "Bring us our morning meal. We have certainly suffered in this, our journey, (much) fatigue." See 18:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Did you see when we retired to the rock? Indeed, I forgot (there) the fish. And none made me forget it except Satan - that I should mention it. And it took its course into the sea amazingly." See 18:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "That is what we were seeking." So they returned, following their footprints. See 18:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they found a servant from among Our servants (i.e., al-Khiḍr) to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him from Us a (certain) knowledge. See 18:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Musa said to him, "May I follow you on (the condition) that you teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgement?" Musa said to him: May I follow you so that you teach me something of that knowledge which you have been taught (by Allah)? (18:66). He said: "Verily, you will not be able to have patience with me! (18:67). "And how can you have patience about a thing which you know not? (18:68). Musa said: "If Allah wills, you will find me patient, and I will not disobey you in aught (18:69). He said: "Then, if you follow me, ask me not about anything till I myself mention of it to you (18:70).Musa Meeting with Al-Khidr and Accompanying HimAllah tells us what Musa said to that learned man, who was Al-Khidr. He was one to whom…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Indeed, with me you will never be able to have patience. See 18:66

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And how can you have patience for what you do not encompass in knowledge?" See 18:66

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in (any) order." See 18:66

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them (as to) which of them is best in deed. See 18:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:70 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I make to you about it mention (i.e., explanation)." See 18:66

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So they set out, until when they had embarked on the ship, he (i.e., al-Khiḍr) tore it open. (Musa) said, "Have you torn it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing." So they both proceeded, till, when they boarded the boat, he (Khidr) damaged it. Musa said: Have you damaged it wherein its people will drown? Verily, you have committed a thing Imr (18:71). He said: "Did I not tell you, that you would not be able to have patience with me? (18:72). He said: "Call me not to account for what I forgot, and be not hard upon me for my affair (with you) (18:73).Damaging the BoatAllah tells us that Musa and his companion Al-Khidr set out having come to an agreement and reached an understanding. Al-Khidr had made the condition that Musa should…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:72 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Al-Khiḍr) said, "Did I not say that with me you would never be able to have patience?" See 18:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:73 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "Do not blame me for what I forgot and do not overwhelm me in my matter with difficulty." See 18:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So they set out, until when they met a boy, he (i.e., al-Khiḍr) killed him. (Musa) said, "Have you killed a pure soul for other than (having killed) a soul? You have certainly done a deplorable thing." Then they both proceeded till they met a boy, and he (Khidr) killed him. Musa said: Have you killed an innocent person without Nafs? Verily, you have committed a thing Nukr! (18:74). He said: "Did I not tell you that you can have no patience with me? (18:75). He said: "If I ask you anything after this, keep me not in your company, you have received an excuse from me (18:76).The Story of Killing the BoyفَانطَلَقَاThen they both proceeded,means, after the first incident:حَتَّىٰ إِذَا لَقِيَا غُلَامًا فَقَتَلَهُtill they met a boy, and he (Khidr) killed him.It has been stated previously that this boy…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Al-Khiḍr) said, "Did I not tell you that with me you would never be able to have patience?" See 18:74

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:76 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "If I should ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as a companion. You have obtained from me an excuse." See 18:74

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:77 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So they set out, until when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. And they found therein a wall about to collapse, so he (i.e., al-Khiḍr) restored it. (Musa) said, "If you wished, you could have taken for it a payment." Then they both proceeded till when they came to the people of a town, they asked them for food, but they refused to entertain them. Then they found therein a wall about to collapse and he set it up straight. (Musa) said: "If you had wished, surely you could have taken wages for it! (18:77). He said: "This is the parting between you and I, I will tell you the interpretation of (those) things over which you were not able to be patient (18:78).The Story…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:78 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Al-Khiḍr) said, "This is parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience. See 18:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:79 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea. So I intended to cause defect in it as there was after them a king who seized every (good) ship by force. As for the boat, it belonged to poor people working in the sea. So I wished to make a defective damage in it, as there was a king behind them who seized every boat by force (18:79).Interpretations of Why the Ship was DamagedThis is an explanation of what Musa found so hard to understand, and the appearence of which he condemed. Allah showed Al-Khidr the hidden reasons, so he said, I damaged the ship to make it faulty, because they used to pass by a king who was one of the oppressors, who يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ (seized every boat), i.e., every good, sound boat غَصْبًا (by…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, We will make that which is upon it (into) a barren ground. See 18:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:80 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them by transgression and disbelief. "And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared he would oppress them by rebellion and disbelief (18:80). "So we intended that their Lord should exchange him for them for one better in righteousness and nearer to mercy (18:81).Interpretation of Why the Boy was KilledIbn 'Abbas narrated from Ubayy bin Ka'b that the Prophet SAW said:الْغُلَامُ الَّذِي قَتَلَهُ الْخَضِرُ طُبِعَ يَوْمَ طُبِعَ كَافِرًاThe boy Al-Khidr killed was destined to be a disbeliever from the day he was created.It was recorded by Ibn Jarir from Ibn 'Abbas. He said:فَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤْمِنَيْنِ فَخَشِينَا أَن يُرْهِقَهُمَا طُغْيَانًا وَكُفْرًاhis parents were believers, and we feared he would oppress them by rebellion and disbeliefTheir love for him might make them follow…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:81 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer to mercy. See 18:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:82 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was beneath it a treasure for them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord intended that they reach maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did it not of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience." And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the town; and there was under it a treasure belonging to them; and their father was a righteous man, and your Lord intended that they should attain their age of full strength and take out their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did them not of my own accord. That is the interpretation of those (things)…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:83 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they ask you, (O Muḥammad), about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say, "I will recite to you about him a report." And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say: I shall recite to you something of his story (18:83). Verily, We established him in the earth, and We gave him the means of everything (18:84).The Story of Dhul-QarnaynAllah says to His Prophet SAW:وَيَسْأَلُونَكَAnd they ask youO Muhammad SAW:عَن ذِي الْقَرْنَيْنِabout Dhul-Qarnayn.i.e., about his story. We have already mentioned how the disbelievers of Makkah sent word to the People of the Book and asked them for some information with which they could test the Prophet SAW. They (the People of the Book) said, 'Ask him about a man who traveled extensively throughout the earth, and about some young men who nobody knows what they did, and about the Ruh (the soul),' then Surat Al-Kahf was…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:84 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We established him upon the earth, and We gave him from everything a way (i.e., means). See 18:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:85 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So he followed a way. So he followed a way (18:85). Until, when he reached the setting place of the sun, he found it setting in a spring of Hami'ah. And he found near it a people. We said: O Dhul-Qarnayn! Either you punish them or treat them with kindness (18:86). He said: "As for him who does wrong, we shall punish him, and then he will be brought back unto his Lord, Who will punish him with a terrible torment (Hell) (18:87). "But as for him who believes and works righteousness, he shall have the best reward, and we shall speak unto him mild words (18:88).His Traveling and Reaching the Place Where the Sun Sets (the West)فَأَتْبَعَ سَبَبًاSo he followed a way.Ibn 'Abbas said that he followed different routes to achieve what he wanted.فَأَتْبَعَ سَبَبًاSo he followed a way.Mujahid…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:86 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun (i.e., the west), he found it (as if) setting in a body of dark water,1 and he found near it a people. We (i.e., Allah) said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish (them) or else adopt among them (a way of) goodness." See 18:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:87 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "As for one who wrongs,1 we will punish him. Then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment (i.e., Hellfire). See 18:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:88 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But as for one who believes and does righteousness, he will have a reward of the best (i.e., Paradise), and we (i.e., Dhul-Qarnayn) will speak to him from our command with ease." See 18:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:89 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then he followed a way. Then he followed (another) way (18:89). Until, when he came to the rising place of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We (Allah) had provided no shelter against the sun (18:90). So (it was)! And We knew all about him (Dhul-Qarnayn) (18:91).His Journey EastAllah tells us that Dhul-Qarnayn then traveled from the west of the earth towards the east. Every time he passed a nation, he subjugated the people and called them to Allah. If they obeyed him, all well and good, otherwise he would humiliate them and take their wealth and possessions. From every nation he took what his armies needed to fight the next nation. When he reached the place where the sun rises, as Allah says:وَجَدَهَا تَطْلُعُ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍhe found it rising on a peoplemeaning a nation:لَّمْ…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or have you thought that the companions of the cave and the inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder?1 Do you think that the people of Al-Kahf and Ar-Raqim were a wonder among Our signs (18:9). When the young men fled for refuge to Al-Kahf. They said: Our Lord! Bestow on us mercy from Yourself, and facilitate for us our affair in the right way! (18:10). Therefore, We covered up their hearing in Al-Kahf for a number of years (18:11). Then We raised them up, that We might test which of the two parties was best at calculating the time period they tarried (18:12).The Story of the People of Al-KahfHere Allah tells us about the story of the people of Al-Kahf in brief and general terms, then He explains it in more detail. He Says:أَمْ حَسِبْتَDo you think– O Muhammad…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:90 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Until, when he came to the rising of the sun (i.e., the east), he found it rising on a people for whom We had not made against it any shield. See 18:89

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:91 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Thus.1 And We had encompassed (all) that he had in knowledge. See 18:89

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:92 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then he followed a way. Then he followed (another) way (92)Until, when he reached between two mountains, he found before them a people who scarcely understood a word (93)They said: O Dhul-Qarnayn! Verily, Ya'juj and Ma'juj are doing great mischief in the land. Shall we then pay you a tribute in order that you might erect a barrier between us and them? (94)He said: "That in which my Lord had established me is better. So help me with strength, I will erect between you and them a barrier. (95)"Give me Zubar of iron;" then, when he had filled up the gap between the two mountain-cliffs, he said: "Blow;" then when he had made them (red as) fire, he said: "Bring me Qitran to pour over them. (96)His Journey to the Land of Ya'juj and Ma'juj, and Building the BarrierAllah says…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:93 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Until, when he reached (a pass) between two mountains, he found beside them a people who could hardly understand (his) speech. See 18:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:94 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog1 are (great) corrupters in the land. So may we assign for you an expenditure that you might make between us and them a barrier?" See 18:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:95 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "That in which my Lord has established me is better (than what you offer), but assist me with strength (i.e., manpower); I will make between you and them a dam. See 18:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:96 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Bring me bars of iron" - until, when he had leveled (them) between the two mountain walls, he said, "Blow (with bellows)," until when he had made it (like) fire, he said, "Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper." See 18:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:97 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So they (i.e., Gog and Magog) were unable to pass over it, nor were they able (to effect) in it any penetration. So they could not scale it or dig through it (18:97). He said: This is a mercy from my Lord, but when the promise of my Lord comes, He shall Dakka' it down to the ground. And the promise of my Lord is ever true (18:98). And on that Day, We shall leave some of them to surge like waves on one another; and the Trumpet will be blown, and We shall collect them (the creatures) all together (18:99).The Barrier Restrains Them, but It will be Breached When the Hour Draws NighAllah tells us that Ya'juj and Ma'juj could not climb over the barrier or penetrate its lower portion. Varying forms of the verb are used here in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:98 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Dhul-Qarnayn) said, "This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord1 comes (i.e., approaches), He will make it level, and ever is the promise of my Lord true." See 18:97

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kahf:99 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We will leave them that day1 surging over each other, and (then) the Horn will be blown, and We will assemble them in (one) assembly. See 18:97

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kawthar:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We have granted you, (O Muḥammad), al-Kawthar. إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ الْأَبْتَرُFor he who hates you, he will be cut off.So they thought in their ignorance that if his sons died, his remembrance would be cut off. Allah forbid! To the contrary, Allah preserved his remembrance for all the world to see, and He obligated all the servants to follow his Law. This will continue for all of time until the Day of Gathering and the coming of the Hereafter. May the blessings of Allah and His peace be upon him forever until the Day of Assembling.This is the end of the Tafsir of Surat Al-Kawthar, and all praise and blessings are due to Allah.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kawthar:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So pray to your Lord and offer sacrifice (to Him alone). See 108:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Kawthar:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.1 See 108:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By the night when it covers.1 وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰAnd what will his wealth avail him when he goes down?Mujahid said, "This means when he dies." Abu Salih and Malik said – narrating from Zayd bin Aslam, "When he goes down into the Fire."

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: We will ease him toward difficulty. See 92:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And what will his wealth avail him when he falls?1 See 92:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
