item.description: Indeed, (incumbent) upon Us is guidance. Truly, on Us is (to give) guidance (92:12). And truly, unto Us (belong) the last (Hereafter) and the first (this world) (92:13). Therefore I have warned you of a Fire Talazza (92:14). None shall enter it save the most wretched (92:15). Who denies and turns away (92:16). And those with Taqwa will be far removed from it (92:17). He who gives of his wealth for self-purification (92:18). And who has (in mind) no favor from anyone to be paid back (92:19). Except to seek the Face of his Lord, the Most High (92:20). He, surely, will be pleased (92:21).The Matter of Guidance and Other than it is in the Hand of Allah, and Allah's Warning about the HellfireQatadah said:إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰTruly, on Us is (to give) guidance."This means, We will explain what is lawful…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, to us belongs the Hereafter and the first (life). See 92:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So I have warned you of a Fire which is blazing. See 92:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: None will (enter to) burn therein except the most wretched one. See 92:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Who had denied and turned away. See 92:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But the righteous one will avoid it. See 92:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (He) who gives (from) his wealth to purify himself. See 92:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And not (giving) for anyone who has (done him) a favor to be rewarded1. See 92:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (by) the day when it appears. See 92:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But only seeking the face (i.e., acceptance) of his Lord, Most High. See 92:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he is going to be satisfied. See 92:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (by) He who created the male and female. See 92:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, your efforts are diverse. See 92:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: As for he who gives and fears Allah. See 92:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And believes in the best (reward). See 92:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: We will ease him toward ease. See 92:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But as for he who withholds and considers himself free of need. See 92:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Lail:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And denies the best (reward). See 92:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: A supplicant asked for a punishment bound to happen.1 وَنَرَاهُ قَرِيبًاBut We see it (quite) near.Meaning: the believers believe that its occurrence is near, even though its time of occurrence is unknown and no one knows when it will be except Allah. All of what is approaching then it is near and it will definitely happen.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And no friend will ask (anything of) a friend. See 70:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will be shown each other. The criminal will wish that he could be ransomed from the punishment of that Day by his children. See 70:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And his wife and his brother. See 70:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And his nearest kindred who shelter him. See 70:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever is on earth entirely (so) then it could save him. See 70:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No!1 Indeed, it is the Flame (of Hell). See 70:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: A remover of exteriors.1 See 70:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It invites he who turned his back (on truth) and went away (from obedience). See 70:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And collected (wealth) and hoarded. See 70:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, mankind was created anxious. Verily, man was created very impatient (70:19). Apprehensive when evil touches him (70:20). And suppressive when good touches him (70:21). Except those who are devoted to Salah (70:22). Those who with their Salah are Da'imun (70:23). And those in whose wealth there is a recognized right (70:24). For the one who asks, and for the deprived (70:25). And those who believe in the Day of Recompense (70:26). And those who fear the torment of their Lord (70:27). Verily, the torment of their Lord is that before which none can feel secure (70:28). And those who guard their private part (chastity) (70:29). Except from their wives or their right hand possessions – for (then) they are not blameworthy (70:30). But whosoever seeks beyond that, then it is those who are trespassers (70:31). And those who keep…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: To the disbelievers; of it there is no preventer. See 70:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When evil touches him, impatient. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when good touches him, withholding (of it). See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except the observers of prayer. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those who are constant in their prayer. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those within whose wealth is a known right.1 See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For the petitioner and the deprived. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who believe in the Day of Recompense. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not that from which one is safe. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who guard their private parts. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (It is) from Allah, owner of the ways of ascent. See 70:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess,1 for indeed, they are not to be blamed. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But whoever seeks beyond that, then they are the transgressors. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who are to their trusts and promises attentive. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who are in their testimonies upright. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who (carefully) maintain their prayer. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will be in gardens,1 honored. See 70:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So what is (the matter) with those who disbelieve, hastening (from) before you, (O Muḥammad). So, what is the matter with those disbelievers, before you Muhti'i (70:36). On the right and on the left, 'Izin (70:37). Does every man of them hope to enter the Paradise of Delight (70:38). But no! Verily, We have created them out of that which they know (70:39). But no! I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests that surely We are Abl (70:40). To replace them by (others) better than them; and We are not to be outrun (70:41). So, leave them to plunge in vain talk and play about, until they meet their Day which they are promised (70:42). The Day when they will come out of the graves quickly as racing to a Nusub (70:43). With their eyes lowered…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (To sit) on (your) right and (your) left in separate groups?1 See 70:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Does every person among them aspire to enter a garden of pleasure? See 70:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No! Indeed, We have created them from that which they know.1 See 70:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The angels and the Spirit (i.e., Jibril) will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. See 70:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So I swear by the Lord of (all) risings and settings1 that indeed We are able. See 70:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: To replace them with better than them; and We are not to be outdone. See 70:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So leave them to converse vainly and amuse themselves until they meet their Day which they are promised. See 70:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Day they will emerge from the graves rapidly as if they were, toward an erected idol, hastening.1 See 70:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. That is the Day which they had been promised. See 70:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So be patient with gracious patience. See 70:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, they see it (as) distant. See 70:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But We see it (as) near. See 70:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: On the Day the sky will be like murky oil.1 The Day that the sky will be like the Al-Muhl (70:8). And the mountains will be like 'Ihn (70:9). And no friend will ask a friend (70:10). Though they shall be made to see one another, the criminal would desire to ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by his children (70:11). And his wife and his brother (70:12). And his Fasilah who sheltered him (70:13). And all that are in the earth, so that it might save him (70:14). By no means! Verily, it will be the fire of Hell (70:15). Naza'ah the Shawa (70:16). Calling (all) such as turn their backs and turn away their faces (70:17). And collect (wealth) and hide it (from spending it in the cause of Allah) (70:18).Terrors of the Day of JudgementAllah…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ma'aarij:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the mountains will be like wool.1 See 70:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, fulfill (all) contracts.1 Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock except for that which is recited to you (in this Qur’ān) - hunting not being permitted while you are in the state of iḥrām.2 Indeed, Allah ordains what He intends.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire. See 5:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:100 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Not equal are the evil and the good, although the abundance of evil might impress you." So fear Allah, O you of understanding, that you may be successful. Say: "Not equal are the bad things and the good things, even though the abundance of the bad may please you. " So have Taqwa of Allah, O men of understanding in order that you may be successful (5:100). O you who believe! Ask not about things which, if made plain to you, may cause you trouble. But if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made plain to you. Allah has forgiven that, and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Forbearing (5:101). Before you, a community asked such questions, then on that account they became disbelievers.) Allah says to His Messenger (SAW (102)قُلْSay,O Muhammad SAW:لَّا يَسْتَوِي…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:101 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you. But if you ask about them while the Qur’ān is being revealed, they will be shown to you. Allah has pardoned it (i.e., that which is past); and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing. See 5:100

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:102 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: A people asked such (questions) before you; then they became thereby disbelievers.1 See 5:100

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:103 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah has not appointed (such innovations as) baḥīrah or sā’ibah or waṣīlah or ḥām.1 But those who disbelieve invent falsehood about Allah, and most of them do not reason. Allah has not instituted things like Bahirah or a Sa'ibah or a Wasilah or a Ham. But those who disbelieve invent lies against Allah, and most of them have no understanding (5:103). And when it is said to them: "Come to what Allah has revealed and unto the Messenger." They say: "Enough for us is that which we found our fathers following," even though their fathers had no knowledge whatsoever and no guidance (5:104).The Meaning of Bahirah, Sa'ibah, Wasilah and HamAl-Bukhari recorded that Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib said, The Bahirah is a female camel whose milk was spared for the idols and no one was allowed to milk it. The Sa'ibah is…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:104 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers knew nothing, nor were they guided? See 5:103

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:105 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, upon you is (responsibility for) yourselves. Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided. To Allah is your return all together; then He will inform you of what you used to do. O you who believe! Take care of yourselves. If you follow the right guidance, no hurt can come to you from those who are in error. The return of you all is to Allah, then He will inform you about (all) that you used to do (5:105).One is Required to Reform Himself FirstAllah commands His believing servants to reform themselves and to do as many righteous deeds as possible. He also informs them that whoever reforms himself, he would not be affected by the wickedness of the wicked, whether they were his relatives or otherwise.Imam Ahmad recorded…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:106 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, testimony (should be taken) among you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest - (that of) two just men from among you or two others from outside if you are traveling through the land and the disaster of death should strike you. Detain them after the prayer and let them both swear by Allah if you doubt (their testimony, saying), "We will not exchange it (i.e., our oath) for a price (i.e., worldly gain), even if he should be a near relative, and we will not withhold the testimony of (i.e., ordained by) Allah. Indeed, we would then be of the sinful." O you who believe! When death approaches any of you, and you make a bequest, then take the testimony of two just men of your own folk or two…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:107 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But if it is found that those two were guilty of sin (i.e., perjury), let two others stand in their place (who are) foremost (in claim) from those who have a lawful right. And let them swear by Allah, "Our testimony is truer than their testimony, and we have not transgressed. Indeed, we would then be of the wrongdoers." See 5:106

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:108 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is more likely that they will give testimony according to its (true) objective, or (at least) they would fear that (other) oaths might be taken after their oaths. And fear Allah and listen (i.e., obey Him); and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people. See 5:106

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:109 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Be warned of) the Day when Allah will assemble the messengers and say, "What was the response you received?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, it is You who is Knower of the unseen". On the Day when Allah will gather the Messengers together and say to them: What was the response you received (from men to your teaching)?" They will say: "We have no knowledge, verily, only You are the Knower of all that is hidden (5:109).The Messengers Will be Asked About Their NationsAllah states that on the Day of Resurrection, He will ask the Messengers about how their nations, to whom He sent them, answered and responded to their teachings. Allah said in other Ayat:فَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ الَّذِينَ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ الْمُرْسَلِينَThen surely, We shall question those (people) to whom it (the Book) was sent and verily, We…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands (in aggression) against you, but He withheld their hands from you; and fear Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely. See 5:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:110 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (The Day) when Allah will say, "O Isa, Son of Maryam, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother when I supported you with the Pure Spirit (i.e., the angel Jibril) and you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity; and (remember) when I taught you writing and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel; and when you designed from clay (what was) like the form of a bird with My permission, then you breathed into it, and it became a bird with My permission; and you healed the blind (from birth) and the leper with My permission; and when you brought forth the dead with My permission; and when I restrained the Children of Israel from (killing) you when you came to them with clear proofs and those who disbelieved among them said, "This is…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:111 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (remember) when I inspired to the disciples, "Believe in Me and in My messenger (i.e., Isa)." They said, "We have believed, so bear witness that indeed we are Muslims (in submission to Allah)." See 5:110

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:112 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (And remember) when the disciples said, "O Isa, Son of Maryam, can your Lord1 send down to us a table (spread with food) from the heaven?" (Isa) said, "Fear Allah, if you should be believers." (Remember) when Al-Hawariyun said: "O Isa, son of Maryam! Can your Lord send down to us a Ma'idah from heaven?" Isa said: "Have Taqwa of Allah, if you are indeed believers (5:112). They said: "We wish to eat thereof and to be stronger in faith, and to know that you have indeed told us the truth and that we ourselves be its witnesses (5:113). Isa, son of Maryam, said: "O Allah, our Lord! Send us from heaven a table spread (with food) that there may be for us – for the first and the last of us – a festival and a sign from You;…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:113 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "We wish to eat from it and let our hearts be reassured and know that you have been truthful to us and be among its witnesses." See 5:112

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:114 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Said Isa, the son of Maryam, "O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table (spread with food) from the heaven to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You. And provide for us, and You are the best of providers." See 5:112

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:115 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah said, "Indeed, I will send it down to you, but whoever disbelieves afterwards from among you - then indeed will I punish him with a punishment by which I have not punished anyone among the worlds." See 5:112

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:116 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (beware the Day) when Allah will say, "O Isa, Son of Maryam, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?'" He will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, it is You who is Knower of the unseen. And (remember) when Allah will say (on the Day of Resurrection): O Isa, son of Maryam! Did you say unto men: 'Worship me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'" He will say: "Glory be to You! It was not for me to say what I had no right (to say). Had I said such a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:117 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: I said not to them except what You commanded me - to worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Observer over them, and You are, over all things, Witness. See 5:116

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:118 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: If You should punish them - indeed they are Your servants; but if You forgive them - indeed it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise." See 5:116

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:119 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah will say, "This is the Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness." For them are gardens (in Paradise) beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, Allah being pleased with them, and they with Him. That is the great attainment. Allah will say: This is a Day on which the truthful will profit from their truth: Theirs are Gardens under which rivers flow (in Paradise) – they shall abide therein forever. Allah is pleased with them and they with Him. That is the great success (5:119). To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all that is therein, and He is able to do all things (5:120).Only Truth will be of Benefit on the Day of ResurrectionAllah answers His servant and Messenger Isa, son of Maryam, after he disowns the disbelieving Christians…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah had already taken a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We delegated from among them twelve leaders. And Allah said, "I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakāh and believe in My messengers and support them and loan Allah a goodly loan,1 I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever of you disbelieves after that has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way." Indeed, Allah took the covenant from the Children of Israel (Jews), and We appointed twelve leaders among them. And Allah said: I am with you if you perform the Salah and give the Zakah and believe in My Messengers; honor and assist them, and lend to Allah a good loan, verily, I will remit your sins and admit you…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:120 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is within them. And He is over all things competent. See 5:119

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So for their breaking of the covenant We cursed them and made their hearts hardened. They distort words from their (proper) places (i.e., usages) and have forgotten a portion of that of which they were reminded.1 And you will still observe deceit among them, except a few of them. But pardon them and overlook (their misdeeds). Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good. See 5:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And from those who say, "We are Christians" We took their covenant; but they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded.1 So We caused among them2 animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah is going to inform them about what they used to do. See 5:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and overlooking much.1 There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book (i.e., the Qur’ān). O People of the Scripture! Now has come to you Our Messenger explaining to you much of that which you used to hide from the Scripture and passing over much. Indeed, there has come to you from Allah a light and a plain Book (5:15). Wherewith Allah guides all those who seek His Pleasure to ways of peace, and He brings them out of darkness by His permission unto light and guides them to a straight path (5:16).Explaining the Truth Through the Messenger and the Qur'anAllah states that He sent His Messenger Muhammad SAW with…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By which Allah guides those who pursue His pleasure to the ways of peace1 and brings them out from darknesses into the light, by His permission, and guides them to a straight path. See 5:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They have certainly disbelieved who say that Allah is Christ, the son of Maryam. Say, "Then who could prevent Allah at all if He had intended to destroy Christ, the son of Maryam, or his mother or everyone on the earth?" And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent. Surely, in disbelief are they who say that Allah is the Messiah, son of Maryam. Say: "Who then has the least power against Allah, if He were to destroy the Messiah, son of Maryam, his mother, and all those who are on the earth together?" And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them. He creates what He wills. And Allah…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But the Jews and the Christians say, "We are the children of Allah and His beloved." Say, "Then why does He punish you for your sins?" Rather, you are human beings from among those He has created. He forgives whom He wills, and He punishes whom He wills. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the (final) destination. See 5:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger to make clear to you (the religion) after a period (of suspension) of messengers, lest you say, "There came not to us any bringer of good tidings or a warner." But there has come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And Allah is over all things competent. O People of the Scripture! Now has come to you Our Messenger making (things) clear unto you, after a break in (the series of) Messengers, lest you say: "There came to us no bringer of glad tidings and no warner." But now has come unto you a bringer of glad tidings and a warner. And Allah is able to do all things (5:19).Allah is addressing the People of the Book – the Jews and the Christians, saying…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah or (the sanctity of) the sacred month or (neglect the marking of) the sacrificial animals and garlanding (them) or (violate the safety of) those coming to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and (His) approval. But when you come out of iḥrām, then (you may) hunt. And do not let the hatred of a people for having obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām lead you to transgress. And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty. See 5:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention, O Muḥammad), when Musa said to his people, "O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you when He appointed among you prophets and made you possessors1 and gave you that which He had not given anyone among the worlds. And (remember) when Musa said to his people: O my people! Remember the favor of Allah to you: when He made Prophets among you, made you kings and gave you what He had not given to any other among the nations (Al-'Alamin) (5:20). "O my people! Enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned to you and turn not back; for then you will be returned as losers (5:21). They said: "O Musa! In it are a people of great strength, and we shall never enter it, till they leave it; when they leave, then we will…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O my people, enter the blessed land (i.e., Palestine) which Allah has assigned to you and do not turn back (from fighting in Allah's cause) and (thus) become losers." See 5:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "O Musa, indeed within it is a people of tyrannical strength, and indeed, we will never enter it until they leave it; but if they leave it, then we will enter." See 5:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Said two men from those who feared (to disobey) upon whom Allah had bestowed favor, "Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, you will be predominant.1 And upon Allah rely, if you should be believers." See 5:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "O Musa, indeed we will not enter it, ever, as long as they are within it; so go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are remaining right here." See 5:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "My Lord, indeed I do not possess (i.e., control) except myself and my brother, so part us1 from the defiantly disobedient people." See 5:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Allah) said, "Then indeed, it is forbidden to them for forty years (in which) they will wander throughout the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people." See 5:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And recite to them the story of Adam's two sons, in truth, when they both made an offering (to Allah), and it was accepted from one of them but was not accepted from the other. Said (the latter), "I will surely kill you." Said (the former), "Indeed, Allah only accepts from the righteous (who fear Him). And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth; when each offered a sacrifice, it was accepted from the one but not from the other. The latter said to the former: I will surely, kill you." The former said: "Verily, Allah accepts only from those who have Taqwa (5:27). "If you do stretch your hand against me to kill me, I shall never stretch my hand against you to kill you, for I fear Allah; the Lord of all…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: If you should raise your hand toward me to kill me - I shall not raise my hand toward you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds. See 5:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, I want you to obtain (thereby) my sin and your sin so you will be among the companions of the Fire. And that is the recompense of wrongdoers." See 5:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Prohibited to you are dead animals,1 blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and (those animals) killed by strangling or by a violent blow or by a head-long fall or by the goring of horns, and those from which a wild animal has eaten, except what you (are able to) slaughter (before its death), and those which are sacrificed on stone altars,2 and (prohibited is) that you seek decision through divining arrows. That is grave disobedience. This day those who disbelieve have despaired of (defeating) your religion; so fear them not, but fear Me. This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islām as religion. But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin - then indeed,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And his soul permitted to him1 the murder of his brother, so he killed him and became among the losers. See 5:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then Allah sent a crow searching (i.e., scratching) in the ground to show him how to hide the disgrace1 of his brother. He said, "O woe to me! Have I failed to be like this crow and hide the disgrace (i.e., body) of my brother?" And he became of the regretful. See 5:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul1 or for corruption (done) in the land2 - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves one3 - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And Our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, (even) after that, throughout the land, were transgressors.4 Because of that, We ordained for the Children of Israel that if anyone killed a person not in retaliation of murder, or (and) to spread mischief in the land - it would be as if he killed all mankind, and if anyone saved a life, it would be as if he saved the life of all mankind. And indeed, there came to them Our Messengers with…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the penalty1 for those who wage war2 against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth (to cause) corruption is none but that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. See 5:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except for those who return (repenting) before you overcome (i.e., apprehend) them. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. See 5:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means (of nearness) to Him and strive in His cause that you may succeed. O you who believe! Have Taqwa of Allah and seek the Wasilah to Him, and strive hard in His cause, so that you may be successful (5:35). Verily, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth, and as much again therewith to ransom themselves thereby from the torment on the Day of Resurrection, it would never be accepted of them. And theirs would be a painful torment (5:36). They will long to get out of the Fire, but never will they get out therefrom; and theirs will be a lasting tormen (5:37).Commanding Taqwa, Wasilah, and JihadAllah commands His faithful servants to fear Him in Taqwa, which if mentioned along with acts of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who disbelieve - if they should have all that is in the earth and the like of it with it by which to ransom themselves from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it will not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment. See 5:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will wish to get out of the Fire, but never are they to emerge therefrom, and for them is an enduring punishment. See 5:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (As for) the thief, the male and the female, amputate their hands in recompense for what they earned (i.e., committed) as a deterrent (punishment) from Allah. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise. And (as for) the male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands as a recompense for that which both committed, a punishment by way of example from Allah. And Allah is All-Powerful, All-Wise (5:38). But whosoever repents after his crime and does righteous good deeds, then verily, Allah will pardon him. Verily, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful (5:39). Know you not that to Allah (Alone) belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth! He forgives whom He wills and He punishes whom He wills. And Allah is able to do all things (5:40).The Necessity of Cutting Off the Hand of the ThiefAllah commands…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed, Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. See 5:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They ask you, (O Muḥammad), what has been made lawful for them. Say, "Lawful for you are (all) good foods and (game caught by) what you have trained of hunting animals1 which you train as Allah has taught you. So eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of Allah upon it, and fear Allah." Indeed, Allah is swift in account. They ask you what is lawful for them. Say: Lawful unto you are At-Tayyibat (the good things). And those Jawarih (beasts and birds of prey) which you have trained as hounds, training and teaching them (to catch) in the manner as directed to you by Allah; so eat of what they catch for you, but pronounce the Name of Allah over it, and have Taqwa of Allah. Verily, Allah is swift in reckoning (5:4).Clarifying the LawfulIn…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent. See 5:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O Messenger, let them not grieve you who hasten into disbelief – of those who say, "We believe" with their mouths, but their hearts believe not, and from among the Jews. (They are) avid listeners to falsehood, listening to another people who have not come to you.1 They distort words beyond their (proper) places (i.e., usages), saying, "If you are given this,2 take it; but if you are not given it, then beware." But he for whom Allah intends fitnah3 - never will you possess (power to do) for him a thing against Allah. Those are the ones for whom Allah does not intend to purify their hearts. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. (41. O Messenger! Let not those who hurry to fall into disbelief grieve you, of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (They are) avid listeners to falsehood, devourers of (what is) unlawful. So if they come to you, (O Muḥammad), judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them - never will they harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly. See 5:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But how is it that they come to you for judgement while they have the Torah, in which is the judgement of Allah? Then they turn away, (even) after that; but those are not (in fact) believers. See 5:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted (to Allah) judged by it for the Jews, as did the rabbis and scholars by that with which they were entrusted of the Scripture of Allah, and they were witnesses thereto. So do not fear the people but fear Me, and do not exchange My verses for a small price (i.e., worldly gain). And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. See 5:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We ordained for them therein a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds is legal retribution. But whoever gives (up his right as) charity, it is an expiation for him. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers (i.e., the unjust). And We ordained therein for them "Life for life, eye for eye, nose for nose, ear for ear, tooth for tooth, and wounds equal for equal. " But if anyone remits the retaliation by way of charity, it shall be for him an expiation. And whosoever does not judge by that which Allah has revealed, such are the unjust (5:45).This Ayah also chastises and criticizes the Jews…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We sent, following in their footsteps,1 Isa, the son of Maryam, confirming that which came before him in the Torah; and We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light and confirming that which preceded it of the Torah as guidance and instruction for the righteous. And in their footsteps, We sent Isa, son of Maryam, confirming the Tawrah that had come before him, and We gave him the Injil, in which was guidance and light and confirmation of the Tawrah that had come before it, a guidance and an admonition for those who have Taqwa (5:46). Let the people of the Injil judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whosoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, such are the rebellious (5:47).Allah Mentions Isa and Praises the InjilAllah said:وَقَفَّيْنَاand We sent...Meaning: We sent:عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِمin…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient. See 5:46

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have revealed to you, (O Muḥammad), the Book (i.e., the Qur’ān) in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations away from what has come to you of the truth. To each of you We prescribed a law and a method.1 Had Allah willed, He would have made you one nation (united in religion), but (He intended) to test you in what He has given you; so race to (all that is) good.2 To Allah is your return all together, and He will (then) inform you concerning that over which you used to differ. And We have sent down to you the Book (this Qur'an) in truth, confirming the Scripture that came before it and Muhayminan…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And judge, (O Muḥammad), between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations and beware of them, lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. And if they turn away - then know that Allah only intends to afflict them with some of their (own) sins. And indeed, many among the people are defiantly disobedient. See 5:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: This day (all) good foods have been made lawful, and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them. And (lawful in marriage are) chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their due compensation,1 desiring chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse or taking (secret) lovers. And whoever denies the faith - his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers. Made lawful to you this day are At-Tayyibat. The food of the People of the Scripture is lawful to you, and your food is lawful to them. (Lawful to you in marriage) are chaste women from the believers and chaste women from those who were given the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then is it the judgement of (the time of) ignorance they desire? But who is better than Allah in judgement for a people who are certain (in faith). See 5:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are (in fact) allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you - then indeed, he is (one) of them. Indeed, Allah guides not the wrongdoing people. O you who believe! Do not take friends from the Jews and the Christians, as they are but friends of each other. And if any among you befriends them, then surely, he is one of them. Verily, Allah guides not those people who are the wrongdoers (5:51). And you see those in whose hearts there is a disease, they hurry to their friendship, saying: "We fear lest some misfortune of a disaster may befall us. " Perhaps Allah may bring a victory or a decision according to His will. Then they will become…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So you see those in whose hearts is disease (i.e., hypocrisy) hastening into (association with) them, saying, "We are afraid a misfortune may strike us." But perhaps Allah will bring conquest or a decision from Him, and they will become, over what they have been concealing within themselves, regretful. See 5:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who believe will say,1 "Are these the ones who swore by Allah their strongest oaths that indeed they were with you?" Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers. See 5:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - Allah will bring forth (in place of them) a people He will love and who will love Him (who are) humble toward the believers, strong against the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of Allah and do not fear the blame of a critic. That is the favor of Allah; He bestows it upon whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing. O you who believe! Whoever from among you turns back from his religion (Islam), Allah will bring a people whom He will love and they will love Him; humble towards the believers, stern towards the disbelievers, fighting in the way of Allah, and never fearing the blame of the blamers. That is the grace of Allah which He bestows on whom He wills.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Your ally is none but Allah and (therefore) His Messenger and those who have believed - those who establish prayer and give zakāh, and they bow (in worship). See 5:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever is an ally of Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed - indeed, the party of Allah - they will be the predominant. See 5:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, take not those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement among the ones who were given the Scripture before you nor the disbelievers as allies. And fear Allah, if you should (truly) be believers. O you who believe! Do not take as friends those who take your religion for a mockery and fun from those who received the Scriptures before you, and (nor) the disbelievers; and have Taqwa of Allah if you indeed are true believers (5:57). And when you proclaim the call for the Salah, they take it (but) as a mockery and fun; that is because they are a people who understand not (5:58).The Prohibition of Being Loyal Friends with DisbelieversThis Ayah discourages and forbids taking the enemies of Islam and its people, such as the People of the Book and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when you call to prayer, they take it in ridicule and amusement. That is because they are a people who do not use reason. See 5:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "O People of the Scripture, do you resent us except (for the fact) that we have believed in Allah and what was revealed to us and what was revealed before and because most of you are defiantly disobedient?" Say: "O People of the Scripture! Do you criticize us for no other reason than that we believe in Allah, and in what has been sent down to us and in that which has been sent down before (us), and that most of you are rebellious? (5:59). Say: "Shall I inform you of something worse than that, regarding the recompense from Allah: those who incurred the curse of Allah and His wrath, and those of whom He transformed into monkeys and swine, and those who worshipped Taghut; such are worse in rank, and far more astray from the straight path (5:60).…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, when you rise to (perform) prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows and wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles. And if you are in a state of janābah,1 then purify yourselves. But if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women2 and do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful. O you who believe! When you stand (intend) to offer the Salah (the prayer), then wash your faces and your hands (forearms) up to the elbows, rub…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Shall I inform you of (what is) worse than that1 as penalty from Allah? (It is that of) those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and pigs and slaves of ṭāghūt.2 Those are worse in position and further astray from the sound way." See 5:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when they come to you, they say, "We believe." But they have entered with disbelief (in their hearts), and they have certainly left with it. And Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing. See 5:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you see many of them hastening into sin and aggression and the devouring of (what is) unlawful. How wretched is what they have been doing. See 5:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Why do the rabbis and religious scholars not forbid them from saying what is sinful and devouring what is unlawful? How wretched is what they have been practicing. See 5:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained."1 Chained are their hands, and cursed are they for what they say. Rather, both His hands are extended; He spends however He wills. And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. And We have cast among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Every time they kindled the fire of war (against you), Allah extinguished it. And they strive throughout the land (causing) corruption, and Allah does not like corrupters. The Jews say: "Allah's Hand is tied up." Be their hands tied up and be they accursed for what they uttered. Nay, both His Hands are widely outstretched. He spends as He wills. Verily, the revelation that has come to you from your Lord makes…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if only the People of the Scripture had believed and feared Allah, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Pleasure. See 5:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if only they had upheld (the law of) the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to them from their Lord (i.e., the Qur’ān), they would have consumed (provision) from above them and from beneath their feet.1 Among them are a moderate (i.e., acceptable) community, but many of them - evil is that which they do. See 5:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people. O Messenger! Convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His Message. Allah will protect you from mankind. Verily, Allah guides not the people who disbelieve (5:67).Commanding the Prophet SAW to Convey the Message; Promising Him Immunity and ProtectionAllah addresses His servant and Messenger Muhammad by the title 'Messenger' and commands him to convey all that He has sent him, a command that the Prophet SAW has fulfilled in the best manner.Al-Bukhari recorded that Aisha said, Whoever says to you that Muhammad hid any part of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "O People of the Scripture, you are (standing) on nothing until you uphold (the law of) the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to you from your Lord (i.e., the Qur’ān)." And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people. Say: "O People of the Scripture! You have nothing till you act according to the Tawrah, the Injil, and what has (now) been sent down to you from your Lord (the Qur'an)." Verily, the revelation that has come to you from your Lord makes many of them increase in rebellion and disbelief. So do not grieve for the people who disbelieve (5:68). Surely, those who believe, and those who are the Jews and the Sabians and the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who have believed (in Prophet Muḥammad SAW) and those (before him SAW) who were Jews or Sabeans or Christians - those (among them) who believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteousness - no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.1 See 5:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey"; and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts. And remember Allah's favor to you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said: "We hear and we obey." And have Taqwa of Allah. Verily, Allah is All-Knower of that which is in the breasts (5:7). O you who believe! Stand out firmly for Allah as just witnesses; and let not the enmity and hatred of others make you avoid justice. Be just, that is nearer to Taqwa; and have Taqwa of Allah. Verily, Allah is Well-Acquainted with what you do (5:8). Allah has promised those who believe and do deeds of righteousness, that for them there is forgiveness and a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:70 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: We had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel and had sent to them messengers. Whenever there came to them a messenger with what their souls did not desire, a party (of messengers) they denied, and another party they killed. Verily, We took the covenant of the Children of Israel and sent Messengers to them. Whenever there came to them a Messenger with what they themselves desired not, a group of them they called liars, and others among them they killed (5:70). They thought there will be no Fitnah (trial or punishment), so they became blind and deaf; after that Allah turned to them (with forgiveness); yet again many of them became blind and deaf. And Allah is the All-Seer of what they do (5:71).Allah reminds that He took the covenant and pledges from the Children of Israel…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they thought there would be no (resulting) punishment, so they became blind and deaf. Then Allah turned to them in forgiveness; then (again) many of them became blind and deaf. And Allah is Seeing of what they do. See 5:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:72 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Allah is the Messiah, the son of Maryam" while the Messiah has said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." Indeed, he who associates others with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers. Surely, they have disbelieved who say: "Allah is the Messiah (Isa), son of Maryam." But the Messiah said: "O Children of Israel! worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." Verily, whosoever sets up partners (in worship) with Allah, then Allah has forbidden Paradise for him, and the Fire will be his abode. And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers (5:72). Surely, they have disbelieved who say: "Allah is the third of three." And there is no god but One God (Allah).…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:73 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Allah is the third of three."1 And there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, there will surely afflict the disbelievers among them a painful punishment. See 5:72

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. See 5:72

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Messiah, son of Maryam, was not but a messenger; (other) messengers have passed on before him. And his mother was a supporter of truth. They both used to eat food.1 Look how We make clear to them the signs; then look how they are deluded. See 5:72

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:76 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Do you worship besides Allah that which holds for you no (power of) harm or benefit while it is Allah who is the Hearing, the Knowing?" Say: "How do you worship besides Allah something which has no power either to harm or to benefit you? But it is Allah Who is the All-Hearer, All-Knower (5:76). Say: "O People of the Scripture! Exceed not the limits in your religion beyond the truth, and do not follow the vain desires of people who went astray before and who misled many, and strayed (themselves) from the right path (5:77).The Prohibition of Shirk (Polytheism) and Exaggeration in the ReligionAllah admonishes those who take up rivals with Him and worship the idols, monuments and false deities. Allah states that such false deities do not deserve any degree of Divinity. Allah said:قُلْSayO Muhammad, to those…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:77 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "O People of the Scripture, do not exceed limits in your religion beyond the truth and do not follow the inclinations of a people who had gone astray before and misled many and have strayed from the soundness of the way." See 5:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:78 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of Dawud and of Isa, the son of Maryam. That was because they disobeyed and (habitually) transgressed. Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed by the tongue of Dawud and Isa, son of Maryam. That was because they disobeyed (Allah and the Messengers) and were ever transgressing (beyond the bounds) (5:78). They used not to forbid one another from the evil they committed. Vile indeed was what they used to do (5:79). You see many of them taking the disbelievers as their friends. Evil indeed is that which they have sent forward before themselves; for that (reason) Allah is wrath with them, and in torment they will abide (5:80). And had they believed in Allah, and in the Prophet and in what has been…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:79 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They used not to prevent one another from wrongdoing that they did. How wretched was that which they were doing. See 5:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is (fully) Aware of what you do. See 5:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:80 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: You see many of them becoming allies of those who disbelieved (i.e., the polytheists). How wretched is that which they have put forth for themselves in that Allah has become angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally. See 5:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:81 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and in what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies; but many of them are defiantly disobedient. See 5:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:82 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers (to be) the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant. Verily, you will find the strongest among men in enmity to the believers the Jews and those who commit Shirk, and you will find the nearest in love to the believers those who say: "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks, and they are not proud (5:82). And when they listen to what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized. They…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:83 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses. See 5:82

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:84 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And why should we not believe in Allah and what has come to us of the truth? And we aspire that our Lord will admit us (to Paradise) with the righteous people." See 5:82

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:85 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So Allah rewarded them for what they said1 with gardens (in Paradise) beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And that is the reward of doers of good. See 5:82

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:86 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - they are the companions of Hellfire. See 5:82

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:87 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful to you and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors. O you who believe! Make not unlawful the good things which Allah has made lawful to you, and transgress not. Verily, Allah does not like the transgressors (5:87). And eat of the things which Allah has provided for you, lawful and good, and have Taqwa of Allah in Whom you believe (5:88).There is No Monasticism in IslamAli bin Abi Talhah said that Ibn 'Abbas said, This Ayah [5:87] was revealed about some of the Companions of the Prophet SAW who said, 'We should cut off our male organs, abandon the desires of this life and travel in the land, just as the Ruhban (monks) do.' When the Prophet SAW heard of this…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:88 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And eat of what Allah has provided for you (which is) lawful and good. And fear Allah, in whom you are believers. See 5:87

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:89 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah will not impose blame upon you for what is meaningless1 in your oaths, but He will impose blame upon you for (breaking) what you intended of oaths. So its expiation2 is the feeding of ten needy people from the average of that which you feed your (own) families or clothing them or the freeing of a slave. But whoever cannot find (or afford it) - then a fast of three days (is required). That is the expiation for oaths when you have sworn. But guard your oaths.3 Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses (i.e., revealed law) that you may be grateful. Allah will not punish you for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will punish you for your deliberate oaths; for its expiation feed ten poor, on a scale of the Awsat of that…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds (that) for them there is forgiveness and great reward. See 5:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:90 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, (sacrificing on) stone alters (to other than Allah), and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid1 it that you may be successful. O you who believe! Khamr, Maysir, Ansab, and Azlam are a Rijs of Shaytan's handiwork. So avoid that in order that you may be successful (5:90). Shaytan wants only to excite enmity and hatred between you with Khamr and Maysir, and hinder you from the remembrance of Allah and from the Salah (the prayer). So, will you not then abstai (5:91). And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware. Then if you turn away, you should know that it is Our Messenger's duty to convey in the clearest way (5:92). Those who believe and do righteous good deeds, there is no sin on them…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:91 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist? See 5:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:92 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger and beware. And if you turn away - then know that upon Our Messenger is only (the responsibility for) clear notification. See 5:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:93 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: There is not upon those who believe and do righteousness (any) blame concerning what they have eaten (in the past) if they (now) fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, and then fear Allah and believe, and then fear Allah and do good; and Allah loves the doers of good. See 5:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:94 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you through something of the game that your hands and spears (can) reach, that Allah may make evident those who fear Him unseen. And whoever transgresses after that - for him is a painful punishment. O you who believe! Allah will certainly make a trial for you with something in the game that is well within reach of your hands and your lances, that Allah may test who fears Him in the unseen. Then whoever transgresses thereafter, for him there is a painful torment (5:94). O you who believe! Kill not game while you are in a state of Ihram, and whosoever of you kills it intentionally, the penalty is an offering, brought to the Ka'bah, of livestock equivalent to the one he killed, as adjudged by two just men among…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:95 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of iḥrām.1 And whoever of you kills it intentionally - the penalty is an equivalent from sacrificial animals to what he killed, as judged by two just men among you as an offering (to Allah) delivered to the Kaʿbah, or an expiation: the feeding of needy people or the equivalent of that in fasting, that he may taste the consequence of his matter (i.e., deed). Allah has pardoned what is past; but whoever returns (to violation), then Allah will take retribution from him. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.2 See 5:94

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:96 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you and the travelers,1 but forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in the state of iḥrām. And fear Allah to whom you will be gathered. Lawful to you is water game and its use for food – for the benefit of yourselves and those who travel, but forbidden is (the pursuit of) land game as long as you are in a state of Ihram. And have Taqwa of Allah to Whom you shall be gathered back (5:96). Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, an asylum of security and benefits for mankind, and also the Sacred Month and the animals of offerings and the garlanded, that you may know that Allah has knowledge of all that is in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:97 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah has made the Kaʿbah, the Sacred House, standing1 for the people and (has sanctified) the sacred months and the sacrificial animals and the garlands (by which they are identified). That is so you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth and that Allah is Knowing of all things. See 5:96

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:98 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Know that Allah is severe in penalty and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. See 5:96

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maaida:99 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Not upon the Messenger is (responsibility) except (for) notification. And Allah knows whatever you reveal and whatever you conceal. See 5:96

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maa'un:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَAnd withhold Al-Ma'un.This means that they do not worship their Lord well, nor do they treat His creation well. They do not even lend that which others may benefit from and be helped by, even though the object will remain intact and be returned to them. These people are even stingier when it comes to giving Zakah and different types of charity that bring one closer to Allah.Al-Mas'udi narrated from Salamah bin Kuhayl who reported from Abu Al-'Ubaydin that he asked Ibn Mas'ud about Al-Ma'un and he said, "It is what the people give to each other, like an axe, a pot, a bucket and similar items."This is the end of the Tafsir of Surat Al-Ma'un, and all praise and thanks are due to Allah.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maa'un:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For that is the one who drives away the orphan. See 107:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maa'un:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And does not encourage the feeding of the poor. See 107:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maa'un:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So woe to those who pray. See 107:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maa'un:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (But) who are heedless of their prayer1. See 107:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maa'un:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those who make show (of their deeds). See 107:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Maa'un:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And withhold (simple) assistance. See 107:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Masad:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: May the hands of Abū Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he.1 تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍPerish the two hands of Abu Lahab and perish hewas revealed, the one-eyed Umm Jamil bint Harb came out wailing, and she had a stone in her hand. She was saying, 'He criticizes our father, and his religion is our scorn, and his command is to disobey us.' The Messenger of Allah SAW was sitting in the Masjid (of the Ka'bah) and Abu Bakr was with him. When Abu Bakr saw her he said, 'O Messenger of Allah! She is coming and I fear that she will see you.' The Messenger of Allah SAW replied:إِنَّهَا لَنْ تَرَانِيVerily, she will not see me.Then he recited some of the Qur'an as a protection for himself. This is as Allah says:وَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآنَ جَعَلْنَا بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ الَّذِينَ لَا…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Masad:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: His wealth will not avail him or that which he gained. See 111:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Masad:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He will (enter to) burn in a Fire of (blazing) flame. See 111:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Masad:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And his wife (as well) - the carrier of firewood.1 See 111:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Masad:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Around her neck is a rope of (twisted) fiber. See 111:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who covers himself (with a garment).1 عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍFar from easy for the disbelievers.Meaning: it will not be easy for them. This is as Allah says:يَقُولُ الْكَافِرُونَ هَٰذَا يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌThe disbelievers will say: "This a Hard Day." (54:8)We have reported from Zurarah bin Awfa, the judge of Al-Basrah, that he lead the people in the morning prayer and he recited this Surah. Then, when he reached Allah's statement:فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِي النَّاقُورِ - فَذَٰلِكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ - عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍThen, when the Naqur is sounded. Truly, that Day will be a Hard Day – far from easy for the disbelievers.he made a moaning sound and then he fell down dead. May Allah have mercy on him.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For the disbelievers - not easy. See 74:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Leave Me with the one I created alone.1 Leave Me alone (to deal) with whom I created lonely (74:11). And then granted him resources in abundance (74:12). And children attending (74:13). And made life smooth and comfortable for him (74:14). After all that he desires that I should give more (74:15). Nay! Verily, he has been opposing Our Ayat (74:16). I shall force him to Sa'ud (74:17). Verily, he thought and plotted (74:18). So let him be cursed, how he plotted (74:19). And once more let him be cursed, how he plotted (74:20). Then he thought (74:21). Then he frowned and he looked in a bad tempered way (74:22). Then he turned back, and was proud (74:23). Then he said: "This is nothing but magic from that of old (74:24). "This is nothing but the word of a human being!…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to whom I granted extensive wealth. See 74:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And children present (with him). See 74:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And spread (everything) before him, easing (his life). See 74:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then he desires that I should add more. See 74:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No! Indeed, he has been toward Our verses obstinate. See 74:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: I will cover him with arduous torment. See 74:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, he thought and deliberated.1 See 74:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So may he be destroyed (for) how he deliberated. See 74:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Arise and warn. See 74:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then may he be destroyed (for) how he deliberated. See 74:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then he considered (again). See 74:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then he frowned and scowled. See 74:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then he turned back and was arrogant. See 74:11
