item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up.1 See 101:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then as for one whose scales are heavy (with good deeds). See 101:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He will be in a pleasant life. See 101:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But as for one whose scales are light. See 101:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: His refuge1 will be an abyss.2 See 101:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qadr:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We sent it (i.e., the Qur’ān) down during the Night of Decree. سَلَامٌ هِيَThere is peace."This means all of it is good and there is no evil in it until the coming of Fajr (dawn)."Specifying the Night of Decree and its SignsThis is supported by what Imam Ahmad recorded from 'Ubadah bin As-Samit that the Messenger of Allah SAW said:لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ فِي الْعَشْرِ الْبَوَاقِي، مَنْ قَامَهُنَّ ابْتِغَاءَ حِسْبَتِهِنَّ فَإِنَّ اللهَ يَغْفِرُ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ، وَهِيَ لَيْلَةُ وِتْرٍ: تِسْعٍ أَوْ سَبْعٍ أَوْ خَامِسَةٍ أَوْ ثَالِثَةٍ أَوْ آخِرِ لَيْلَةٍThe Night of Al-Qadr occurs during the last ten (nights). Whoever stands for them (in prayer) seeking their reward, then indeed Allah will forgive his previous sins and his latter sins. It is an odd night: the ninth, or the seventh, or the fifth, or the third or the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qadr:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree? See 97:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qadr:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months. See 97:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qadr:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The angels and the Spirit (i.e., Jibril) descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter.1 See 97:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qadr:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Peace it is1 until the emergence of dawn. See 97:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Nūn.1 By the pen and what they inscribe. إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَVerily, your Lord is the best Knower of him who has gone astray from His path, and He is the best Knower of those who are guided.Meaning: 'He knows which of the two groups are truly guided among you, and He knows the party that is astray from the truth.'

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And do not obey every worthless habitual swearer. See 68:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (And) scorner, going about with malicious gossip. See 68:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: A preventer of good, transgressing and sinful. See 68:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Cruel, moreover, and an illegitimate pretender.1 See 68:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Because he is a possessor of wealth and children. See 68:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples." See 68:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: We will brand him upon the snout.1 See 68:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the companions of the garden, when they swore to cut its fruit in the (early) morning. Verily, We have tried them as We tried the People of the Garden, when they swore to pluck the fruits in the morning (68:17). Without (saying: "If Allah wills." (18)Then there passed over it a Ta'if from your Lord while they were asleep (19)So by the morning, it became like As-Sarim (20)Then they called out (one to another as soon) as the morning broke (21)Saying: "Go to your tilth in the morning, if you would pluck (the fruits). (22)So they departed, and they were whispering (23)"No poor person shall enter upon you into it today. (24)And they went in the morning with Hard Qadirin (25)But when they saw it, they said: "Verily, we have gone astray.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Without making exception.1 See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So there came upon it (i.e., the garden) an affliction from your Lord while they were asleep. See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: You are not, (O Muḥammad), by the favor of your Lord, a madman. See 68:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it became as though reaped. See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they called one another at morning. See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Saying), "Go early to your crop if you would cut the fruit." See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So they set out, while lowering their voices. See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Saying), "There will surely not enter it today upon you (any) poor person." See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they went early in determination, (assuming themselves) able.1 See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But when they saw it, they said, "Indeed, we are lost. See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Rather, we have been deprived." See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The most moderate of them said, "Did I not say to you, 'Why do you not exalt (Allah)?'"1 See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers." See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted. See 68:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then they approached one another, blaming each other. See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "O woe to us; indeed we were transgressors. See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us (one) better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord desirous."1 See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Such is the punishment (of this world). And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew. See 68:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are the Gardens of Pleasure. Verily, for those who have Taqwa are Gardens of Delight with their Lord (68:34). Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals (68:35). What is the matter with you? How judge you (68:36). Or have you a Book wherein you learn (68:37). That you shall therein have all that you choose (68:38). Or have you oaths from Us, lasting until the Day of Judgement, that yours will be what you judge (68:39). Ask them, which of them will stand as surety for that (68:40). Or have they "partners"? Then let them bring their "partners" if they are truthful (68:41).The Reward of those Who have Taqwa and that They will Not be Treated like the CriminalsAfter Allah mentions the situation of the people of the worldly garden and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then will We treat the Muslims like the criminals? See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: What is (the matter) with you? How do you judge? See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or do you have a scripture in which you learn. See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That indeed for you is whatever you choose? See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or do you have oaths (binding) upon Us, extending until the Day of Resurrection, that indeed for you is whatever you judge? See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, you are of a great moral character. See 68:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Ask them which of them, for that (claim), is responsible. See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or do they have partners?1 Then let them bring their partners, if they should be truthful. See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Day the shin will be uncovered1 and they are invited to prostration but they (i.e., the disbelievers) will not be able. The Day when the Shin shall be laid bare and they shall be called to prostrate themselves, but they shall not be able to do so (68:42). Their eyes will be cast down and ignominy will cover them; they used to be called to prostrate themselves, while they were (68:43). Then leave Me alone with whoever denies this narration. We shall punish them gradually from directions they perceive not (68:44). And I will grant them a respite. Verily, My plan is strong (68:45). Or is it that you ask them a wage, so that they are heavily burdened with debt (68:46). Or that the Unseen is in their hands, so that they can write it down (68:47).The Terror…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. And they used to be invited to prostration while they were sound.1 See 68:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So leave Me, (O Muḥammad), with (the matter of) whoever denies this statement (i.e., the Qur’ān). We will progressively lead them (to punishment) from where they do not know.1 See 68:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And I will give them time. Indeed, My plan is firm. See 68:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or do you ask of them a payment, so they are by debt burdened down? See 68:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or have they (knowledge of) the unseen, so they write (it) down? See 68:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then be patient for the decision of your Lord, (O Muḥammad), and be not like the companion of the fish (i.e., Yunus) when he called out while he was distressed. So, wait with patience for the decision of your Lord, and be not like the Companion of the Fish when he cried out (to Us) while he was Makzum (68:48). Had not a grace from his Lord reached him, he would indeed have been (left in the stomach of the fish, but We forgave him), so he was cast off on the naked shore, while he was to be blamed (68:49). Then his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous (68:50). And verily, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes (through hatred) when they hear the Reminder (the Qur'an), and they say: Verily, he…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: If not that a favor (i.e., mercy) from his Lord overtook him, he would have been thrown onto the naked shore while he was censured.1 See 68:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So you will see and they will see. See 68:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous. See 68:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes (i.e., looks) when they hear the message, and they say, "Indeed, he is mad." See 68:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But it is not except a reminder to the worlds. See 68:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Which of you is the afflicted (by a devil). See 68:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, and He is most knowing of the (rightly) guided. See 68:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then do not obey the deniers. So, do not obey the deniers (68:8). They wish that you should compromise with them, so they (too) would compromise with you (68:9). And do not obey every Hallaf Mahin (68:10). A Hammaz, going about with Namim (68:11). Hinderer of the good, transgressor, sinful (68:12). 'Utul, and moreover Zanim (68:13). (He was so) because he had wealth and children (68:14). When Our Ayat are recited to him, he says: Tales of the men of old! (68:15). We shall brand him on the snout (nose) (68:16). Prohibition of giving in to the Pressure of the Disbelievers and Their Suggestions, and that They like to meet in the Middle of the Path Allah says, 'just as We have favored you and given you the upright legislation and great (standard of) character,'فَلَا تُطِعِ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ - وَدُّوا لَوْ…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They wish that you would soften (in your position), so they would soften (toward you). See 68:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Hour has come near, and the moon has split (in two).1 وَلَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ مِنَ الْأَنْبَاءِAnd indeed there has come to them news; in this Qur'an, there has come to them the news of the earlier nations that disbelieved in their Messengers and the torment, punishment and affliction that befell them:مَا فِيهِ مُزْدَجَرٌwherein there is MuzdajarWhich is wherein there are warnings and lessons to stop them from idolatry and persisting in denial:حِكْمَةٌ بَالِغَةٌ ۖPerfect wisdom,in that Allah guides whomever He wills and misguides whomever He wills:فَمَا تُغْنِ النُّذُرُbut warners benefit them not.but the preaching of warnings does not benefit those upon whom Allah has written misery and sealed their hearts. Who can guide such people after Allah? This Ayah is similar to Allah's statements:قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ ۖ فَلَوْ شَاءَ لَهَدَاكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَSay: "With Allah is the perfect proof and argument;…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So he invoked his Lord, "Indeed, I am overpowered, so help." See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then We opened the gates of the heaven with rain pouring down. See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And caused the earth to burst with springs, and the waters met for a matter already predestined. See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We carried him on a (construction of) planks and nails. See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Sailing under Our observation as reward for he who had been denied. See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We left it as a sign, so is there any who will remember? See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And how (severe) were My punishment and warning.1 See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have certainly made the Qur’ān easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember? See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: ʿAad denied; and how (severe) were My punishment and warning. 'Ad denied; then how was My torment and My warnings (54:18). Verily, We sent against them a violently cold (Sarsar) wind on a day of calamity, continuous (54:19). Plucking out men as if they were uprooted stems of date palms (54:20). Then, how was My torment and My warnings (54:21). And We have indeed made the Qur'an easy to understand and remember; then is there any that will remember (54:22).The Story of 'AdAllah states that 'Ad, the People of Hud, denied their Messenger, just as the people of Nuh did. So, Allah sent on them:عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًاagainst them a violently cold (Sarsar) windWhich is means, a bitterly cold and furious wind:فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍon a day of calamityWhich is against them, according to Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah and As-Suddi:مُسْتَمِرٍّcontinuousWhich is upon them because…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We sent upon them a screaming wind on a day of continuous misfortune. See 54:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if they see a sign (i.e., miracle), they turn away and say, "Passing magic."1 See 54:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Extracting the people1 as if they were trunks of palm trees uprooted. See 54:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And how (severe) were My punishment and warning. See 54:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have certainly made the Qur’ān easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember? See 54:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Thamūd denied the warning. Thamud denied the warnings (54:23). And they said: "A man, alone among us – shall we follow him? Truly, then we should be in error and distress! (54:24). "Is it that the Reminder is sent to him alone from among us? Nay, he is an insolent liar! (54:25). Tomorrow they will come to know who is the liar, the insolent one (54:26). Verily, We are sending the she-camel as a test for them. So watch them, and be patient (54:27). And inform them that the water is to be shared between (her and) them, each one's right to drink being established (by turns) (54:28). But they called their comrade and he took (a sword) and killed (her) (54:29). Then, how was My torment and My warnings (54:30). Verily, We sent against them a single Sayhah, and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And said, "Is it one human being1 among us that we should follow? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness. See 54:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Has the message been sent down upon him from among us? Rather, he is an insolent liar." See 54:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will know tomorrow who is the insolent liar. See 54:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as trial for them, so watch them and be patient.1 See 54:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And inform them that the water is shared between them,1 each (day of) drink attended (by turn). See 54:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But they called their companion,1 and he dared2 and hamstrung (her). See 54:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they denied and followed their inclinations. But for every matter is a (time of) settlement. See 54:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And how (severe) were My punishment and warning. See 54:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We sent upon them one shriek (i.e., blast from the sky), and they became like the dry twig fragments of an (animal) pen. See 54:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have certainly made the Qur’ān easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember? See 54:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The people of Lut denied the warning. The people of Lut denied the warnings (54:33). Verily, We sent against them Hasib (a violent storm of stones), except the family of Lut, them We saved in the last hour of the night (54:34). As a favor from Us. Thus do We reward him who gives thanks (54:35). And he indeed had warned them of Our punishment, but they doubted the warnings (54:36). And they indeed sought to shame his guests. So, We blinded their eyes (saying), Then taste you My torment and My warnings (54:37). And verily, an abiding torment seized them early in the morning (54:38). Then taste you My torment and My warnings (54:39). And indeed, We have made the Qur'an easy to understand and remember; then is there any that will remember (54:40). The Story of the People…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We sent upon them a storm of stones, except the family of Lut - We saved them before dawn. See 54:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: As favor from Us. Thus do We reward he who is grateful. See 54:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he had already warned them of Our assault, but they disputed the warning. See 54:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they had demanded from him his guests, but We obliterated their eyes, (saying), "Taste My punishment and warning." See 54:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And there came upon them by morning an abiding punishment. See 54:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So taste My punishment and warning. See 54:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And there has already come to them of information that in which there is deterrence. See 54:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have certainly made the Qur’ān easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember? See 54:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And there certainly came to the people of Pharaoh warning. And indeed, warnings came to the people of Fir'awn (54:41). (They) denied all Our signs, so We seized them with a punishment of the Almighty, All-Capable (54:42). Are your disbelievers better than these? Or have you immunity in the Divine Scriptures (54:43). Or say they: We are a great multitude, victorious? (54:44). Their multitude will be put to flight, and they will show their backs (54:45). Nay, but the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour will be more grievous and more bitter (54:46). The Story of Fir'awn and His People Allah the Exalted narrates to us the story of Fir'awn and his people. A Messenger came to them from Allah, Musa supported by his brother Harun. Their Messengers delivered good news if they believe, and a warning if…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They denied Our signs, all of them, so We seized them with a seizure of one Exalted in Might and Perfect in Ability. See 54:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Are your disbelievers better than those (former ones), or have you immunity in the scriptures? See 54:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or do they say, "We are an assembly supporting (each other)"? See 54:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Their) assembly will be defeated, and they will turn their backs (in retreat).1 See 54:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But the Hour is their appointment (for due punishment), and the Hour is more disastrous and more bitter. See 54:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness.1. Verily, the criminals are in error and will burn (54:47). The Day they will be dragged on their faces into the Fire (it will be said to them): Taste you the touch of Hell! (54:48). Verily, We have created all things with Qadar (54:49). And Our commandment is but one as the twinkling of an eye (54:50). And indeed, We have destroyed your likes; then is there any that will remember (54:51). And everything they have done is noted in Az-Zubur (54:52). And everything, small and large, is written down (54:53). Verily, those who have Taqwa, will be in the midst of Gardens and Rivers (54:54). In a seat of truth, near the Muqtadir King (54:55). The Destination of the Criminals Allah the Exalted states that the criminals are misguided away from…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces (it will be said), "Taste the touch of Saqar."1 See 54:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, all things We created with predestination. See 54:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Extensive wisdom - but warning does not avail (them). See 54:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye. See 54:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have already destroyed your kinds,1 so is there any who will remember? See 54:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And everything they did is in written records. See 54:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And every small and great (thing) is inscribed. See 54:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and rivers. See 54:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: In a seat of honor near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability.1 See 54:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So leave them, (O Muḥammad). The Day the Caller1 calls to something forbidding. So withdraw from them. The Day that the caller will call (them) to a terrible thing (54:6). They will come forth, with humbled eyes from (their) graves as if they were locusts spread abroad (54:7). Hastening towards the caller. The disbelievers will say: This is a hard Day (54:8). The terrible End the Disbelievers will meet on the Day of Resurrection Allah the Exalted says, 'O Muhammad, turn away from these people who, when they witness a miracle, they deny it and say that this is continuous magic.' Turn away from them and wait until:يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدَّاعِ إِلَىٰ شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍThe Day that the caller will call (them) to a terrible thing.to the Recompense and the afflictions, horrors and tremendous hardships that it brings forth:خُشَّعًا أَبْصَارُهُمْwith humbled eyesTheir…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Their eyes humbled, they will emerge from the graves as if they were locusts spreading. See 54:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Racing ahead toward the Caller. The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult Day." See 54:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The people of Nuh denied before them, and they denied Our servant and said, "A madman," and he was repelled. The people of Nuh denied (their Messenger) before them. They rejected Our servant and said: A madman!" Wazdujir (54:9). Then he invoked his Lord (saying): "I have been overcome, so help (me)! (54:10). So, We opened the gates of the heaven with water Munhamir (54:11). And We caused springs to gush forth from the earth. So, the waters met for a matter predestined (54:12). And We carried him on a (ship) made of planks and nails (Dusur (13)Floating under Our Eyes, a reward for him who had been rejected (14)And indeed, We have left this as a sign. Then is there any that will remember (15)Then how (terrible) was My torment and My warnings (16)And We have indeed made the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Ṭā, Seen, Meem.1 وَنُرِيدُ أَنْ نَمُنَّ عَلَى الَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا فِي الْأَرْضِAnd We wished to do a favor to those who were weak in the land,until His saying;يَحْذَرُونَwhich they feared.And Allah did indeed do this to them, as He says:وَأَوْرَثْنَا الْقَوْمَ الَّذِينَ كَانُوا يُسْتَضْعَفُونَAnd We made the people who were considered weakuntil His saying;يَعْرِشُونَthey erected (7:137)And Allah said:كَذَٰلِكَ وَأَوْرَثْنَاهَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَThus and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them (26:59)Fir'awn hoped that by his strength and power he would be saved from Musa, but that did not help him in the slightest. Despite his great power as a king he could not oppose the decree of Allah, which can never be overcome. On the contrary, Allah's ruling was carried out, for it had been written and decreed from past eternity that Fir'awn would meet his doom at the hands…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the heart of Musa' mother became empty (of all else). She was about to disclose (the matter concerning) him had We not bound fast her heart that she would be of the believers. And the heart of the mother of Musa became empty. She was very near to disclose his (case), had We not strengthened her heart, so that she might remain as one of the believers (28:10). And she said to his sister: Follow him." So she watched him from a far place (secretly), while they perceived not (28:11). And We had already forbidden foster suckling mothers for him, until she said: "Shall I direct you to a household who will rear him for you, and look after him in a good manner? (28:12). So We restored him to his mother, that her eye might be comforted, and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And she said to his sister, "Follow him"; so she watched him from a distance while they perceived not. See 28:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We had prevented from him (all) wet nurses before,1 so she said, "Shall I direct you to a household that will be responsible for him for you while they are to him (for his upbringing) sincere?" See 28:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So We restored him to his mother that she might be content and not grieve and that she would know that the promise of Allah is true. But most of them (i.e., the people) do not know. See 28:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when he attained his full strength and was (mentally) mature, We bestowed upon him judgement and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good. And when he reached maturity, and was complete, We bestowed on him Hukm and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good (28:14). And he entered the city when its people were unaware: and he found there two men fighting, – one of his party, and the other of his foes. The man of his (own) party asked him for help against his foe, so Musa struck him with his fist and he died. He said: "This is of Shaytan's doing, verily, he is a plain misleading enemy (28:15). He said: "My Lord! Verily, I have wronged myself, so forgive me." Then He forgave him. Verily, He is the Oft-Forgiving, the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he entered the city at a time of inattention by its people1 and found therein two men fighting: one from his faction and one from among his enemy. And the one from his faction called for help to him against the one from his enemy, so Musa struck him and (unintentionally) killed him. (Musa) said, "This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a manifest, misleading enemy." See 28:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me," and He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. See 28:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "My Lord, for the favor You bestowed upon me, I will never be an assistant to the criminals." See 28:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he became inside the city fearful and anticipating (exposure), when suddenly the one who sought his help the previous day cried out to him (once again). Musa said to him, "Indeed, you are an evident, (persistent) deviator." So he became afraid, looking about in the city, when behold, the man who had sought his help the day before, called for his help (again). Musa said to him: "Verily, you are a plain misleader! (28:18). Then when he decided to seize the man who was an enemy to both of them, the man said: "O Musa! Is it your intention to kill me as you killed a man yesterday? Your aim is nothing but to become a tyrant in the land, and not to be one of those who do right (28:19).How the Secret of this Killing Became KnownAllah tells…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when he wanted to strike the one who was an enemy to both of them, he1 said, "O Musa, do you intend to kill me as you killed someone yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land and do not want to be of the amenders." See 28:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: These are verses of the clear Book. See 28:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And a man came from the farthest end of the city, running. He said, "O Musa, indeed the eminent ones are conferring over you (intending) to kill you, so leave (the city); indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors." And there came a man running, from the farthest end of the city. He said: "O Musa! Verily, the chiefs are taking counsel together about you, to kill you, so escape. Truly, I am one of the good advisers to you (28:20). وَجَاءَ رَجُلٌ (And there came a man) He is described as being a man because he had the courage to take a different route, a shorter route than those who were sent after Musa, so he reached Musa first and said to him: "O Musa:إِنَّ الْمَلَأَ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَVerily, the chiefs are taking counsel together about you.Which is…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So he left it, fearful and anticipating (apprehension). He said, "My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people." So he escaped from there, looking about in a state of fear. He said: "My Lord! Save me from the people who are wrongdoers! (28:21). And when he went towards Madyan, he said: "It may be that my Lord guides me to the right way (28:22). And when he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found there a group of men watering, and besides them he found two women who were keeping back (their flocks). He said: "What is the matter with you?" They said: "We cannot water (our flocks) until the shepherds take (their flocks). And our father is a very old man (28:23). So he watered (their flocks) for them, then he turned back to shade, and said: "My…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when he directed himself toward Madyan, he said, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the sound way." See 28:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when he came to the water (i.e., well) of Madyan, he found there a crowd of people watering (their flocks), and he found aside from them two women holding back (their flocks). He said, "What is your circumstance?" They said, "We do not water until the shepherds dispatch (their flocks); and our father is an old man." See 28:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So he watered (their flocks) for them; then he went back to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need." See 28:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then one of the two women came to him walking with shyness. She said, "Indeed, my father invites you that he may reward you for having watered for us." So when he came to him1 and related to him the story, he said, "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people." Then there came to him one of them, walking shyly. She said: "Verily, my father calls you that he may reward you for having watered (our flocks) for us." So when he came to him and narrated the story, he said: "Fear you not. You have escaped from the people who are wrongdoers (28:25). And said one of them (the two women): "O my father! Hire him! Verily, the best of men for you to hire is the strong, the trustworthy (28:26). He said: "I intend to wed…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: One of the women said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy." See 28:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Indeed, I wish to wed you one of these, my two daughters, on (the condition) that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be (as a favor) from you. And I do not wish to put you in difficulty. You will find me, if Allah wills, from among the righteous." See 28:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "That is (established) between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I complete - there is no injustice to me, and Allah, over what we say, is Witness." See 28:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when Musa had completed the term and was traveling with his family, he perceived from the direction of the mount a fire. He said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you from there (some) information or burning wood from the fire that you may warm yourselves." Then, when Musa had fulfilled the term, and was traveling with his family, he saw a fire in the direction of At-Tur. He said to his family: "Wait, I have seen a fire; perhaps I may bring to you from there some information, or a burning firebrand that you may warm yourselves (28:29). So when he reached it, he was called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed place, from the tree: "O Musa! Verily, I am Allah, the Lord of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: We recite to you from the news of Musa and Pharaoh in truth for a people who believe. See 28:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley in a blessed spot - from the tree,1 "O Musa, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds." See 28:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (he was told), "Throw down your staff." But when he saw it writhing as if it was a snake, he turned in flight and did not return.1 (Allah said), "O Musa, approach and fear not. Indeed, you are of the secure. See 28:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Insert your hand into the opening of your garment; it will come out white, without disease. And draw in your arm close to you (as prevention) from fear, for those are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his establishment. Indeed, they have been a people defiantly disobedient." See 28:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "My Lord, indeed I killed from among them someone, and I fear they will kill me. He said: My Lord! I have killed a man among them, and I fear that they will kill me (28:33). "And my brother Harun – he is more eloquent in speech than me, so send him with me as a helper to confirm me. Verily, I fear that they will deny me (28:34). Allah said: "We will strengthen your arm through your brother, and give you both power, so they shall not be able to harm you, with Our Ayat; you two as well as those who follow you, will be the victors (28:35).How Musa Asked for the Support of His Brother and was Granted that by AllahWhen Allah commanded him to go to Fir'awn, the one who he had run away…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And my brother Harun is more fluent than me in tongue, so send him with me as support, verifying me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me." See 28:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Allah) said, "We will strengthen your arm through your brother and grant you both supremacy so they will not reach you. (It will be) through Our signs; you and those who follow you will be the predominant." See 28:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But when Musa came to them with Our signs as clear evidences, they said, "This is not except invented magic, and we have not heard of this (religion) among our forefathers." Then when Musa came to them with Our Clear Ayat, they said: "This is nothing but invented magic. Never did we hear of this among our fathers of old (28:36). Musa said: "My Lord knows best him who came with guidance from Him, and whose will be the happy end in the Hereafter. Verily, the wrongdoers will not be successful (28:37).Musa before Fir'awn and His PeopleAllah tells us how Musa and his brother Harun came before Fir'awn and his chiefs, and showed them the clear miracles and overwhelming proof that Allah had given them to confirm the truth of what they were saying about Allah being One and that…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Musa said, "My Lord is more knowing (than we or you) of who has come with guidance from Him and to whom will be succession in the home.1 Indeed, wrongdoers do not succeed." See 28:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Pharaoh said, "O eminent ones, I have not known you to have a god other than me. Then ignite for me, O Hāmān, (a fire) upon the clay1 and make for me a tower that I may look at the God of Musa. And indeed, I do think he is among the liars." Fir'awn said: O chiefs! I know not that you have a god other than me. So kindle for me (a fire), O Haman, to bake clay, and set up for me a Sarh in order that I may look at the God of Musa; and verily, I think that he (Musa) is one of the liars (28:38). And he and his armies were arrogant in the land, without right, and they thought that they would never return to Us (28:39). So, We seized him and his…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he was arrogant, he and his soldiers, in the land, without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us. See 28:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions, oppressing a sector among them, slaughtering their (newborn) sons and keeping their females alive. Indeed, he was of the corrupters. See 28:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So We took him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea.1 So see how was the end of the wrongdoers. See 28:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We made them leaders1 inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped. See 28:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We caused to overtake them in this world a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be of the despised.1 See 28:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We gave Musa the Scripture, after We had destroyed the former generations, as enlightenment for the people and guidance and mercy that they might be reminded. And indeed We gave Musa – after We had destroyed the generations of old – the Scripture as an enlightenment for mankind, and a guidance and a mercy, that they might remember (28:43).The Blessings which Allah Bestowed upon MusaAllah tells us about the blessings which He gave His servant and Messenger Musa, the speaker, may the best of peace and blessings from his Lord be upon him, He revealed the Tawrah to him after He destroyed Fir'awn and his chiefs.مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا أَهْلَكْنَا الْقُرُونَ الْأُولَىٰafter We had destroyed the generations of oldAfter the revelation of the Tawrah, no nation would again be punished with an overwhelming calamity; instead the believers were now commanded…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you, (O Muḥammad), were not on the western side (of the mount) when We revealed to Musa the command, and you were not among the witnesses (to that). And you were not on the western side (of the Mount), when We made clear to Musa the commandment, and you were not among the witnesses (28:44). But We created generations, and long were the ages that passed over them. And you were not a dweller among the people of Madyan, reciting Our Ayat to them. But it is We Who kept sending (Messengers) (28:45). And you were not at the side of At-Tur when We called. But (you are sent) as a mercy from your Lord, to give warning to a people to whom no warner had come before you, in order that they may remember or receive admonition (28:46).…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But We produced (many) generations (after Musa), and prolonged was their duration.1 And you were not a resident among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were senders (of this message).2 See 28:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you were not at the side of the mount when We called (Musa) but (were sent) as a mercy from your Lord to warn a people to whom no warner had come before you that they might be reminded. See 28:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if not that a disaster should strike them for what their hands put forth (of sins) and they would say, "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses and been among the believers?"...1 See 28:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given like that which was given to Musa?" Did they not disbelieve in that which was given to Musa before? They said, "(They are but) two works of magic supporting each other,1 and indeed we are, in both, disbelievers." But when the truth has come to them from Us, they say: "Why is he not given the like of what was given to Musa? Did they not disbelieve in that which was given to Musa of old?" They say: "Two kinds of magic, each helping the other!" And they say: "Verily, in both we are disbelievers (28:48). Say: "Then bring a Book from Allah, which is a better guide than these two, that I may follow it, if you are truthful (28:49). But if they…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Then bring a scripture from Allah which is more guiding than either of them that I may follow it, if you should be truthful." See 28:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We wanted to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them inheritors. See 28:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But if they do not respond to you - then know that they only follow their (own) desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. See 28:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have (repeatedly) conveyed to them the word (i.e., the Qur’ān) that they might be reminded. See 28:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they1 are believers in it. Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it, they believe in it (28:52). And when it is recited to them, they say: "We believe in it. Verily, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed even before it we have been from Muslims (28:53). These will be given their reward twice over, because they are patient, and repel evil with good, and spend out of what We have provided for them (28:54). And when they hear evil vain talk, they withdraw from it and say: "To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be to you. We seek not (the way of) the ignorant (28:55).The Believers among the People of the BookAllah tells us that the pious scholars among the People of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when it is recited to them, they say, "We have believed in it; indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed we were, (even) before it, Muslims (i.e., submitting to Allah)." See 28:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured and (because) they avert evil through good, and from what We have provided them they spend. See 28:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it and say, "For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace will be upon you;1 we seek not the ignorant." See 28:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, (O Muḥammad), you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the (rightly) guided. Verily, you guide not whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He knows best those who are the guided (28:56). And they say: "If we follow the guidance with you, we would be snatched away from our land." Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary, to which are brought fruits of all kinds, a provision from Ourselves, but most of them know not (28:57).Allah Guides Whom He WillsAllah says to His Messenger SAW: 'O Muhammad:لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَVerily, you guide not whom you like' meaning, 'the matter does not rest with you; all that you have to do is convey the Message, and Allah will guide whom He wills, and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they (i.e., the Quraysh) say, "If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be swept1 from our land." Have We not established for them a safe sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know. See 28:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And how many a city have We destroyed that was insolent in its (way of) living, and those are their dwellings which have not been inhabited after them except briefly.1 And it is We who were the inheritors. And how many a town have We destroyed, which was thankless for its means of livelihood! And those are their dwellings, which have not been inhabited after them except a little. And verily, We have been the heirs (28:58). And never will your Lord destroy the towns until He sends to their mother town a Messenger reciting to them Our Ayat. And never would We destroy the towns unless the people thereof are wrongdoers (28:59).The Destruction of Towns, which are Not Destroyed until Evidence is Established against ThemReferring to the people of Makkah, Allah says:وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ بَطِرَتْ مَعِيشَتَهَا ۖAnd how…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And never would your Lord have destroyed the cities until He had sent to their mother (i.e., principal city) a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not destroy the cities except while their people were wrongdoers. See 28:58

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and (his minister) Hāmān and their soldiers through them1 that which they had feared. See 28:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whatever thing you (people) have been given - it is (only for) the enjoyment of worldly life and its adornment. And what is with Allah is better and more lasting; so will you not use reason? And whatever you have been given is an enjoyment of the life of the world and its adornment, and that which is with Allah is better and will remain forever. Have you then no sens (28:60). Is he whom We have promised an excellent promise – which he will find true – like him whom We have made to enjoy the luxuries of the life of the world, then on the Day of Resurrection, he will be among those brought up (28:61).This World is Transient and the One Whose Concern is this World is Not Equal to the One Whose Concern is the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then is he whom We have promised a good promise which he will meet (i.e., obtain) like he for whom We provided enjoyment of worldly life (but) then he is, on the Day of Resurrection, among those presented (for punishment in Hell)? See 28:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (warn of) the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' which you used to claim?" And (remember) the Day when He will call to them and say: Where are My (so-called) partners whom you used to assert? (28:62). Those about whom the Word will have been fulfilled will say: "Our Lord! These are they whom we led astray. We led them astray, as we were astray ourselves. We declare our innocence before You. It was not us they worshipped (28:63). And it will be said: "Call upon your partners," and they will call upon them, but they will give no answer to them, and they will see the torment. If only they had been guided (28:64). And the Day He will call to them, and say: "What answer gave you to the Messengers? (28:65). Then…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those upon whom the word1 will have come into effect will say, "Our Lord, these are the ones we led to error. We led them to error just as we were in error. We declare our disassociation (from them) to You. They did not used to worship (i.e., obey) us."2 See 28:62

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it will be said, "Invoke your 'partners,'" and they will invoke them; but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had followed guidance! See 28:62

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) the Day He will call them and say, "What did you answer the messengers?" See 28:62

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But the information1 will be unapparent to them that Day, so they will not (be able to) ask one another. See 28:62

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But as for one who had repented, believed, and done righteousness, it is expected (i.e., promised by Allah) that he will be among the successful. See 28:62

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; not for them was the choice. Exalted is Allah and high above what they associate with Him. And your Lord creates whatsoever He wills and chooses, no choice have they. Glorified is Allah, and exalted above all that they associate (28:68). And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal, and what they reveal (28:69). And He is Allah; La ilaha illa Huwa, His is the praise in the first and in the last, and His is the decision, and to Him shall you be returned (28:70).Allah Alone is the One Who has the Power of Creation, Knowledge and ChoiceAllah tells us that He is the only One Who has the power to create and make decisions, and there is no one who can dispute with Him in that or reverse His…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare. See 28:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We inspired to the mother of Musa, "Suckle him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him (one) of the messengers." And We inspired the mother of Musa: Suckle him (Musa), but when you fear for him, then cast him into the river and fear not, nor grieve. Verily, We shall bring him back to you, and shall make him one of the Messengers (28:7). Then the household of Fir'awn picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a (cause of) grief. Verily, Fir'awn, Haman and their armies were sinners (28:8). And the wife of Fir'awn said: "A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Kill him not, perhaps he may…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:70 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him is (due all) praise in the first (life) and the Hereafter. And His is the (final) decision, and to Him you will be returned. See 28:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Have you considered:1 if Allah should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear?" Say: "Tell me! If Allah made the night continuous for you till the Day of Resurrection, which god besides Allah could bring you light? Will you not then hear? (28:71). Say: "Tell me! If Allah made the day continuous for you till the Day of Resurrection, which god besides Allah could bring you night wherein you rest? Will you not then see? (28:72). It is out of His mercy that He has made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty – and in order that you may be grateful (28:73).Night and Day are among the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:72 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the day continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you a night in which you may rest? Then will you not see?" See 28:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:73 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and (by day) seek from His bounty and (that) perhaps you will be grateful. See 28:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (warn of) the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' which you used to claim?" And the Day when He will call to them, and will say: Where are My (so-called) partners, whom you used to assert? (28:74). And We shall take out from every nation a witness, and We shall say: "Bring your proof." Then they shall know that the truth is with Allah, and the lies which they invented will disappear from them (28:75).Rebuking the IdolatorsThis is another call by way of rebuke for those who worshipped other gods besides Allah. The Lord, may He be exalted, will call to them before all the witnesses, and will say:أَيْنَ شُرَكَائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَWhere are My (so-called) partners, whom you used to assert?Meaning: in this world.وَنَزَعْنَا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيدًاAnd We shall take out from…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We will extract from every nation a witness and say, "Produce your proof," and they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and lost from them is that which they used to invent. See 28:74

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:76 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, Qārūn was from the people of Musa, but he tyrannized them. And We gave him of treasures whose keys would burden a band of strong men; thereupon his people said to him, "Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant. Verily, Qarun was of Musa's people, but he behaved arrogantly towards them. And We gave him of the treasures, that of which the keys would have been a burden to a body of strong men. Remember when his people said to him: "Do not exult. Verily, Allah likes not those who exult (28:76). "But seek, with that which Allah has bestowed on you, the home of the Hereafter, and forget not your portion of lawful enjoyment in this world; and be generous as Allah has been generous to you, and seek not mischief in the land. Verily,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:77 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But seek, through that which Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and (yet), do not forget your share of the world. And do good as Allah has done good to you. And desire not corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not like corrupters." See 28:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:78 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "I was only given it because of knowledge I have." Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him of generations those who were greater than him in power and greater in accumulation (of wealth)? But the criminals, about their sins, will not be asked.1 He said: "This has been given to me only because of the knowledge I possess." Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations, men who were stronger than him in might and greater in the amount they had collected? But the criminals will not be questioned of their sins (28:78).Allah informs us how Qarun responded to the exhortations of his people when they sought to guide him to what is good.قَالَ إِنَّمَا أُوتِيتُهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عِنْدِي ۚHe said: "This has been given to me only because of the knowledge…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:79 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So he came out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, "Oh, would that we had like what was given to Qārūn. Indeed, he is one of great fortune." So, he went forth before his people in his finery. Those who were desirous of the life of the world, said: "Ah, would that we had the like of what Qarun has been given! Verily, he is the owner of a great fortune (28:79). But those who had been given knowledge said: "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and this none shall attain except the patient (28:80).How Qarun Went forth in His Finery, and His People's CommentsAllah tells us how Qarun went forth one day before his people with his magnificent regalia; wearing his…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the family of Pharaoh picked him up (out of the river) so that he would become to them an enemy and a (cause of) grief. Indeed, Pharaoh and Hāmān and their soldiers were deliberate sinners. See 28:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:80 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But those who had been given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for he who believes and does righteousness. And none are granted it except the patient." See 28:79

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:81 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. And there was for him no company to aid him other than Allah, nor was he of those who (could) defend themselves. So, We caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling place. Then he had no group to help him against Allah, nor was he one of those who could save themselves (28:81). And those who desired his position the day before, began to say: Know you not that it is Allah Who expands the provision or restricts it to whomsoever He pleases of His servants. Had it not been that Allah was Gracious to us, He could have caused the earth to swallow us up! Know you not that the disbelievers will never be successful (28:82).How Qarun and His Dwelling Place were Swallowed up by the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:82 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who had wished for his position the previous day began to say, "Oh, how Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it! If not that Allah had conferred favor on us, He would have caused it to swallow us. Oh, how the disbelievers do not succeed!" See 28:81

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:83 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That home of the Hereafter We assign to those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth or corruption. And the (best) outcome is for the righteous. That is the home of the Hereafter, We shall assign to those who do not want to exalt themselves in the land nor cause corruption. And the good end is for those who have Taqwa (28:83). Whosoever brings good, he shall have the better thereof; and whosoever brings evil, then those who do evil deeds will only be requited for what they used to do (28:84).The Blessings of the Hereafter for the Humble BelieversAllah tells us that He has made the home of the Hereafter, and its eternal delights which will never change or fade away, for His believing, humble servants who do not rebel against the truth with pride and oppression in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:84 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Whoever comes (on the Day of Judgement) with a good deed will have better than it; and whoever comes with an evil deed - then those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except (as much as) what they used to do. See 28:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:85 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, (O Muḥammad), He who imposed upon you the Qur’ān will take you back to a place of return.1 Say, "My Lord is most knowing of who brings guidance and who is in clear error." Verily, He Who has given you the Qur'an, will surely bring you back to the return. Say: My Lord is Aware of him who brings guidance, and of him who is in manifest error (28:85). And you were not expecting that the Book would be sent down to you, but it is a mercy from your Lord. So never be a supporter of the disbelievers (28:86). And let them not turn you away from the Ayat of Allah after they have been sent down to you, and invite to your Lord and be not of idolators (28:87). And invoke not any other god along with…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:86 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you were not expecting that the Book would be conveyed to you, but (it is) a mercy from your Lord. So do not be an assistant to the disbelievers.1 See 28:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:87 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And never let them avert you from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you. And invite (people) to your Lord. And never be of those who associate others with Allah. See 28:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:88 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And do not invoke with Allah another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will be destroyed except His Face.1 His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned. See 28:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the wife of Pharaoh said, "(He will be) a comfort of the eye (i.e., pleasure) for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son." And they perceived not.1 See 28:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: I swear by the Day of Resurrection. وَلَوْ أَلْقَىٰ مَعَاذِيرَهُThough he may put forth his excuses.This is apologizing. Haven't you heard that Allah said:لَا يَنْفَعُ الظَّالِمِينَ مَعْذِرَتُهُمْThe Day when their excuses will be of no profit to wrongdoers. (40:52)and He says:وَأَلْقَوْا إِلَى اللَّهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ السَّلَمَ ۖAnd they will offer submision to Allah on that Day. (16:87)and He says:فَأَلْقَوُا السَّلَمَ مَا كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ مِنْ سُوءٍThen they will (falsely) submit: "We used not to do any evil." (16:28)and their statement:وَاللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَBy Allah, our Lord, we were not those who joined others in worship with Allah. (6:23)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Man will say on that Day, "Where is the (place of) escape?" See 75:1

item.description: No! There is no refuge. See 75:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: To your Lord, that Day, is the (place of) permanence. See 75:1

item.description: Man will be informed that Day of what he sent ahead1 and kept back.2 See 75:1

item.description: Rather, man, against himself, will be a witness.1 See 75:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Even if he presents his excuses. See 75:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Move not your tongue with it, (O Muḥammad), to hasten with it (i.e., recitation of the Qur’ān). Move not your tongue concerning to make haste therewith (75:16). It is for Us to collect it and that it be recited (75:17). And when We have recited it to you, then follow its recitation (75:18). Then it is for Us to make it clear (75:19). But no! Rather you love the present life of this world (75:20). And neglect the Hereafter (75:21). Some faces that Day shall be Nadirah (75:22). Looking at their Lord (75:23). And some faces that Day will be Basirah (75:24). Thinking that some calamity is about to fall on them (75:25).How the Prophet SAW Received the RevelationThis is Allah teaching His Messenger SAW how to receive the revelation from the angel. For verily, he (the Prophet SAW) was…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, upon Us is its collection (in your heart) and (to make possible) its recitation. See 75:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So when We have recited it (through Jibril), then follow its recitation. See 75:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then upon Us is its clarification (to you). See 75:16

item.description: And I swear by the reproaching soul1 (to the certainty of resurrection). See 75:1

item.description: No! But you (i.e., mankind) love the immediate. See 75:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And leave (i.e., neglect) the Hereafter. See 75:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Some) faces, that Day, will be radiant. See 75:16

item.description: Looking at their Lord.1 See 75:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (some) faces, that Day, will be contorted. See 75:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Expecting that there will be done to them (something) backbreaking. See 75:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No! When it (i.e., the soul) has reached the collar bones.1 Nay, when it reaches to the collarbones (75:26). And it will be said: Who can cure him? (75:27). And he will think that it was the parting (75:28). And one shank will be joined with another shank (75:29). The drive will be on that Day to your Lord (75:30). So, he neither believed nor prayed (75:31). But on the contrary, he denied and turned away (75:32). Then he walked in conceit to his family admiring himself (75:33). Woe to you! And then woe to you (75:34). Again, woe to you! And then woe to you (75:35). Does man think that he will be left neglected (75:36). Was he not a Nutfah of semen emitted (75:37). Then he became an 'Alaqah; then shaped and fashioned in due proportion (75:38). And…

item.description: And it is said, "Who will cure (him)?" See 75:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he (i.e., the dying one) is certain that it is the (time of) separation. See 75:26

item.description: And the leg is wound about the leg.1 See 75:26

item.description: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones? See 75:1

item.description: But (instead), he denied and turned away. See 75:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And then he went to his people, swaggering (in pride). See 75:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Woe to you, and woe! See 75:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then woe to you, and woe! See 75:26

item.description: Is not that (Creator) Able to give life to the dead? See 75:26

item.description: But man desires to continue in sin.1 See 75:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He asks, "When is the Day of Resurrection?" See 75:1

item.description: When the Occurrence occurs. وَالسَّابِقُونَ السَّابِقُونَAnd those foremost will be foremost.is about the Prophets (AS), while As-Suddi said that they are the residents of the utmost highs (Ahl Al-'Illiyyin, in Paradise).The meaning of foremost is that they were foremost in performing the acts of righteousness just as Allah commanded them:وَسَارِعُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُAnd march forth in the way to forgiveness from your Lord, and for Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth. (3:133)and:سَابِقُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا كَعَرْضِ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِRace with one another in hastening towards forgiveness from your Lord, and Paradise the width whereof is as the width of the heaven and the earth. (57:21)Therefore, those who rush to obey Allah in this life and are foremost in performing acts of righteousness, will be among the foremost believers honored in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the forerunners, the forerunners1. See 56:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those are the ones brought near (to Allah). See 56:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: In the Gardens of Pleasure. See 56:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: A (large) company of the former peoples. A multitude of those will be from the first ones (56:13). And a few of those will be from the later ones (56:14). (They will be) on thrones, Mawdunah (56:15). Reclining thereon, face to face (56:16). Immortal boys will go around them (serving) (56:17). With cups, and jugs, and a glass of flowing wine (56:18). Wherefrom neither Yusadda'un nor Yunzifun (56:19). And with fruit that they may choose (56:20). And with the flesh of fowls that they desire (56:21). And (there will be) Hur with wide lovely eyes (56:22). Like preserved pearls (56:23). A reward for what they used to do (56:24). No Laghw (evil vain talk) will they hear therein, nor any sinful speech (56:25). But only the saying of: Salaman! Salaman! (56:26). The Reward of the Foremost in Faith Allah states…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And a few of the later peoples. See 56:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: On thrones woven (with ornament). See 56:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Reclining on them, facing each other. See 56:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? And those on the right – how (fortunate) will be those on the right (56:27). (They will be) among Sidri Makhdud (56:28). And among Talh Mandud (56:29). And in shade Mamdud (56:30). And by water flowing constantly (56:31). And fruit in plenty (56:32). Whose supply is not cut off nor are they out of reach (56:33). And on couches, raised high (56:34). Verily, We have created them a special creation (56:35). And made them virgins (56:36). 'Urub, Atrab (56:37). For those on the right (56:38). A multitude of those will be from the first generation (56:39). And a multitude of those will be from the later generations (56:40).The Reward of Those on the RightAfter Allah mentioned the final destination of those foremost in faith, the nearest to…
