item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left? And those on the left? How will be those on the left (56:41). In Samum, and Hamim (56:42). And a shadow from Yahmum (56:43). Neither Barid nor Karim (56:44). Verily, before that, they indulged in luxury (56:45). And were persisting in great sin (56:46). And they used to say: When we die and become dust and bones, shall we then indeed be resurrected? (56:47). "And also our forefathers? (56:48). Say: "(Yes) verily, those of old, and those of later times (56:49). "All will surely be gathered together for appointed meeting of a known Day (56:50). "Then verily, – you the erring – ones, the deniers! (56:51). "You verily, will eat of the trees of Zaqqum (56:52). "Then you will fill your bellies therewith, (56:53). "And drink…

item.description: (They will be) in scorching fire and scalding water. See 56:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And a shade of black smoke. See 56:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Neither cool nor beneficial. See 56:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed they were, before that, indulging in affluence. See 56:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they used to persist in the great violation.1 See 56:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: We have created you, so why do you not believe? We created you, then why do you believe not (56:57). Do you not see the semen you emit (56:58). Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator (56:59). We have decreed death to you all, and We are not outstripped (56:60). To transfigure you and create you in (forms) that you know not (56:61). And indeed, you have already known the first form of creation, why then do you not remember (56:62).Proof that Resurrection will OccurAllah asserts that Resurrection will occur and refutes the misguided atheists who deny it, those who said:أَئِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا وَعِظَامًا أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَWhen we die and become dust and bones, shall we then indeed be resurrected? (56:47)They said this statement in denial and discounting Resurrection. Allah the Exalted said:نَحْنُ خَلَقْنَاكُمْWe created you,Meaning:…

item.description: Is it you who creates it, or are We the Creator? See 56:57

item.description: And you have already known the first creation, so will you not remember? See 56:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And have you seen that (seed) which you sow? Do you not see what you sow (56:63). Is it you that make it grow, or are We the Grower (56:64). Were it Our will, We could crumble it to dry pieces, and you would be Tafakkahun (56:65). (Saying:) "We are indeed Mughramun! (56:66). "Nay, but we are deprived! (56:67). Do you not see the water that you drink (56:68). Is it you who cause it to come down from Al-Muzn, or are We the Cause of it coming down (56:69). If We willed, We verily could make it salty; why then do you not give thanks (56:70). Do you not see the fire which you kindle (56:71). Is it you who made the tree thereof to grow, or are We the Grower (56:72). We have made it a Reminder, and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Is it you who makes it grow, or are We the grower? See 56:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: If We willed, We could make it (dry) debris, and you would remain in wonder.1 See 56:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Saying), "Indeed, we are (now) in debt. See 56:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great. See 56:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then I swear by the setting of the stars.1 Fala! I swear by the Mawaqi' of the stars (56:75). And verily that is indeed a great oath, if you but know (56:76). That (this) is indeed an honorable recitation (56:77). In a Book Maknun (56:78). Which none touches but the pure ones (56:79). A revelation from the Lord of all that exists (56:80). Is it such a talk that you are Mudhinun (56:81). And you make your provision your denial (56:82).Allah Swears to the Greatness of the Qur'anThe usage of La (in Fala) is not an extra character without meaning, as some of the scholars of Tafsir say. Rather it is used at the beginning of an oath when the oath is a negation. This is like when Aisha (RA)said, "La by Allah! Allah's Messenger SAW did not touch any…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:76 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, it is an oath - if you could know - (most) great. See 56:75

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:77 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, it is a noble Qur’ān. See 56:75

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:78 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.description: Then is it to this statement that you are indifferent. See 56:75

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:82 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:83 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then why, when it (i.e., the soul at death) reaches the throat. Then why do you not (intervene) when it reaches Al-Hulqum (56:83). And you at the moment are looking (56:84). But We are nearer to him than you, but you see not (56:85). Then why do you not – if you are not Madini (56:86). Return the soul, if you are truthful (56:87).When the Soul Reaches the Throat at the Time of Death, it Cannot be Brought back; this Proves Reckoning shall OccurAllah the Exalted said:فَلَوْلَا إِذَا بَلَغَتِThen why do you not (intervene) when it reachesWhich is in reference to the soul:الْحُلْقُومَAl-HulqumI.e., the throat, at the time of death. Allah the Exalted said in other Ayat:كَلَّا إِذَا بَلَغَتِ التَّرَاقِيَ - وَقِيلَ مَنْ ۜ رَاقٍ - وَظَنَّ أَنَّهُ الْفِرَاقُ - وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ بِالسَّاقِ - إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمَسَاقُNay, when (the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:84 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you are at that time looking on. See 56:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:85 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We (i.e., Our angels) are nearer to him than you, but you do not see. See 56:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:86 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then why do you not, if you are not to be recompensed. See 56:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:87 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Bring it back,1 if you should be truthful? See 56:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:88 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if he (i.e., the deceased) was of those brought near (to Allah). Then, if he be of the Muqarrabin (56:88). Then Rawh, Rayhan and a Garden of Delights (56:89). And if he be of those on the right (56:90). Then Salam (peace) to you from those on the right (56:91). But if he be of the denying, the erring (56:92). Then for him is an entertainment with Hamim (56:93). And entry in Hellfire (56:94). Verily, this! This is an absolute truth with certainty (56:95). So, glorify with praises the Name of your Lord, the Most Great (56:96).The Condition of People at the Time of Their DeathThese are the three types of conditions that people face upon their death. Either they are among the near believers or those below their rank on the right, or those who denied the truth,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:89 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the companions of the left - what are companions of the left?1 See 56:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:90 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:91 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then (the angels will say), "Peace for you; (you are) from the companions of the right." See 56:88

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:92 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But if he was of the deniers (who were) astray. See 56:88

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:93 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:94 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:95 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, this is the true certainty. See 56:88

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:96 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great. See 56:88

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naas:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind. مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِOf Jinn and An-Nasis an explanation of who is it that whispers into the breasts of mankind from the devils of mankind and Jinns. This is similar to Allah's saying:وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا شَيَاطِينَ الْإِنسِ وَالْجِنِّ يُوحِي بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ زُخْرُفَ الْقَوْلِ غُرُورًاAnd so We have appointed for every Prophet enemies – Shayatin among mankind and Jinn, inspiring one another with adorned speech as a delusion. (6:112)Imam Ahmad recorded that Ibn 'Abbas said, A man came to the Prophet SAW and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Sometimes I say things to myself that I would rather fall from the sky than say (aloud openly).' The Prophet SAW said:اللهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللهُ أَكْبَرٌ الْحَمْدُ للهِ الَّذِي رَدَّ كَيْدَهُ إِلَى الْوَسْوَسَةِAllah is Most Great! Allah is Most Great! All praise is…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naas:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Sovereign of mankind. See 114:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naas:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By those (angels) who extract with violence.1 فَإِذَا هُم بِالسَّاهِرَةِWhen behold, they are at As-Sahirah.Allah says:يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الْأَرْضُ غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ وَالسَّمَاوَاتُ ۖ وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِOn the Day when the earth will be changed to another earth and so will be the heavens, and they will appear before Allah, the One, the Irresistible. (14:48)and He says:وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْجِبَالِ فَقُلْ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفًا - فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا - لَّا تَرَىٰ فِيهَا عِوَجًا وَلَا أَمْتًاAnd they ask you concerning the mountains, say: "My Lord will blast them and scatter them as particles of dust. Then He shall leave them as a level smooth plain. You will see therein nothing crooked or curved." (20:105-107)and Allah says:وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ الْجِبَالَ وَتَرَى الْأَرْضَ بَارِزَةًAnd the Day We shall cause the mountains to pass away, and you will see the earth as a leveled plain. (18:47)and the…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They are (presently) saying, "Will we indeed be returned to (our) former state (of life)? See 79:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Even if we should be decayed bones?"1 See 79:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They say, "That, then, would be a losing return."1 See 79:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, it will be but one shout. See 79:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And suddenly they will be (alert) upon the earth's surface. See 79:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Has there reached you the story of Musa?. Has there come to you the story of Musa (79:15). When his Lord called him in the holy valley of Tuwa (79:16). Go to Fir'awn; verily, he has transgressed all bounds (79:17). And say to him: Would you purify yourself? (79:18). "And that I guide you to your Lord, so you should fear Him? (79:19). Then he showed him the great sign (79:20). But he denied and disobeyed (79:21). Then he turned back, striving (79:22). So he gathered and called out (79:23). Saying: "I am your lord, most high (79:24). So Allah seized him with punishing example for the Hereafter and the first (life) (79:25). In this is a lesson for whoever fears (79:26). Mentioning the Story of Musa and that it is a Lesson for Those Who fear Allah Allah informs…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But when there comes the greatest Overwhelming Calamity1. But when there comes the Greatest Catastroph (79:34). The Day when man shall remember what he strove for (79:35). And Hell shall be made apparent for whoever sees (79:36). Then for him who transgresse (79:37). And preferred the life of this world (79:38). Verily, his abode will be the Hell (79:39). But as for him who feared standing before his Lord, and forbade himself from desire (79:40). Verily, Paradise will be his abode (79:41). They ask you about the Hour when will be its appointed tim (79:42). What do you have to mention of it (79:43). To your Lord it is limited (79:44). You are only a warner for those who fear it (79:45). The Day they see it (it will be) as if they had not tarried (in this world) except…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Day when man will remember that for which he strove. See 79:34

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.description: Then indeed, Paradise will be (his) refuge. See 79:34

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naba:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: About what are they asking one another? وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًاAnd gardens that are Alfaf.Ibn 'Abbas and other said, "Alfaf means gathered." This is similar to Allah's statement:وَفِي الْأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُّتَجَاوِرَاتٌ وَجَنَّاتٌ مِّنْ أَعْنَابٍ وَزَرْعٌ وَنَخِيلٌ صِنْوَانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوَانٍ يُسْقَىٰ بِمَاءٍ وَاحِدٍ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَهَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فِي الْأُكُلِ ۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَAnd in the earth are neighboring tracts, and gardens of vines, and green crops, and date palms, growing into two or three from a single stem root, or otherwise, watered with the same water; yet some of them We make more excellent than others to eat. Verily, in these things there are Ayat for the people who understand. (13:4)

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naba:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, the Day of Judgement is an appointed time. Verily, the Day of Decision is a fixed time (78:17). The Day when the Trumpet will be blown, and you shall come forth in crowds (78:18). And the heaven shall be opened, and it will become as gates (78:19). And the mountains shall be moved away from their places and they will be as if they were a mirage (78:20). Truly, Hell is a place of ambus (78:21). A dwelling place for the Taghun (78:22). They will abide therein Ahqab (78:23). Nothing cool shall they taste therein, nor any drink (78:24). Except Hamim, and Ghassa (78:25). An exact recompense (according to their evil crimes) (78:26). For verily, they used not to look for a reckoning (78:27). But they denied Our Ayat Kidhdhaba (78:28). And all things We have recorded in a…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naba:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: "So taste (the penalty), and never will We increase you except in torment."1 See 78:17

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naba:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, for the righteous is attainment1. Verily, for those who have Taqwa, there will be a success (78:31). Hada'iq and vineyards (78:32). And Kawa'ib Atrab (78:33). And a cup Dihaq (78:34). No Laghw shall they hear therein, nor lying (78:35). Rewarded from your Lord with a sufficient gift (78:36).The Great Success will be for Those Who have TaqwaAllah informs about the happy people and what He has prepared for them of esteem, and eternal pleasure. Allah says:إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازًاVerily, for those who have Taqwa, there will be a success;Ibn 'Abbas and Ad-Dahhak both said, "A place of enjoyable recreation." Mujahid and Qatadah both said, "They are successful and thus, they are saved from the Hellfire." The most obvious meaning here is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, because Allah says after this:حَدَائِقَHada'iqAnd Hada'iq are gardens of palm trees and other things.وَأَعْنَابًا…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naba:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Gardens and grapevines. See 78:31

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naba:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And young women (companions) of equal age. See 78:31

item.description: And a full cup.1 See 78:31

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naba:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No ill speech will they hear therein or any falsehood. See 78:31

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naba:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (As) reward from your Lord, (a generous) gift (made due by) account.1 See 78:31

item.description: The Day that the Spirit (i.e., Jibril) and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak except for one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is correct. See 78:31

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naba:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is the True (i.e., certain) Day; so he who wills may take to his Lord a (way of) return.1 See 78:31

item.description: And We created you in pairs. See 78:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naba:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And made your sleep (a means for) rest. See 78:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The command of Allah is coming,1 so be not impatient for it. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is He who sends down rain from the sky; from it is drink and from it is foliage in which you pasture (animals). He it is Who sends water down from the sky; from it you drink and from it (grows) the vegetation on which you send your cattle to pasture (16:10). With it He causes crops to grow for you, the olives, the date palms, the grapes, and every kind of fruit. Verily, in this there is indeed an evident proof and a manifest sign for people who give thought (16:11).The Blessings of Rain, and Explaining How it is One of the SignsWhen Allah mentions the blessings of cattle and other animals that He has granted mankind, He then mentions how He has blessed them by sending rain down from the sky above, which has been fulfilling the…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:100 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who through him associate others with Allah. See 16:98

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:101 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse - and Allah is most knowing of what He sends down - they say, "You, (O Muḥammad), are but an inventor (of lies)." But most of them do not know. And when We change a verse in place of another - and Allah knows best what He reveals - they (the disbelievers) say: "You (O Muhammad) are but a forger." Rather, most of them know not (16:101). Say (O Muhammad); "Ruh-ul-Qudus has brought it (the Qur'an) down from your Lord with truth." for the conviction of those who believe, and as a guide and good news for the Muslims (16:102).The Idolators' Accusation that the Prophet SAW was a Liar Since Some Ayat were Abrogated, and the Refutation of their ClaimsAllah tells us of the weak minds of the idolators,…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:102 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, (O Muḥammad), "The Pure Spirit (i.e., Jibril) has brought it down from your Lord in truth to make firm those who believe and as guidance and good tidings to the Muslims." See 16:101

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:103 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him (i.e., the Prophet SAW)." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign,1 and this (recitation, i.e., Qur’ān) is (in) a clear Arabic language. And indeed We know that they (polytheists and pagans) say: "It is only a human being who teaches him." The tongue of the man they refer to is foreign, while this (the Qur'an) is (in) a clear Arabic tongue (16:103).The Idolators' Claim that the Qur'an was Taught by a Human, and the Refutation of their ClaimAllah tells us about the idolators' lies, allegations, and slander when they claimed that this Qur'an which Muhammad SAW had recited for them, was actually taught to him by a human. They referred to a foreign (i.e., non-Arab) man who lived among them as…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:104 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who do not believe in the verses of Allah - Allah will not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment. Verily, those who do not believe in Allah's Ayat (signs, or revelation), Allah will not guide them, and theirs will be a painful punishment (16:104). It is only those who do not believe in Allah's Ayat who fabricate the falsehood, and it is they who are liars (16:105).Allah tells us that He does not guide those who turn away from remembering Him and who are heedless of that which He revealed to His Messenger SAW, those who have no intention of believing in that which he has brought from Allah. This kind of people will never be guided to faith by the signs of Allah and the Message which He sent His Messengers in this world,…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:105 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They only invent falsehood who do not believe in the verses of Allah, and it is those who are the liars. See 16:104

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:106 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Whoever disbelieves in (i.e., denies) Allah after his belief...1 except for one who is forced (to renounce his religion) while his heart is secure in faith. But those who (willingly) open their breasts to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment. Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief - except one who was forced while his heart is at peace with the faith - but whoever opens their breasts to disbelief, on them is wrath from Allah, and theirs will be a terrible torment (16:106). That is because they preferred the life of this world over that of the Hereafter. And Allah does not guide the people who disbelieve (16:107). They are those upon whose hearts, hearing (ears) and sight (eyes) Allah has set a seal over. And they are the heedless (16:108).…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:107 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is because they preferred the worldly life over the Hereafter and that Allah does not guide the disbelieving people. See 16:106

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:108 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those are the ones over whose hearts and hearing and vision Allah has sealed, and it is those who are the heedless. See 16:106

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:109 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Assuredly, it is they, in the Hereafter, who will be the losers. See 16:106

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, olives, palm trees, grapevines, and of all the fruits. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought. See 16:10

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:110 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then, indeed your Lord, to those who emigrated after they had been compelled (to say words of disbelief) and thereafter fought (for the cause of Allah) and were patient - indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful. Then, verily, your Lord for those who emigrated after they were put to trials and then performed Jihad, and were patient, - after this, your Lord is indeed Forgiving, Most Merciful (16:110). (Remember) the Day when every person will come pleading for himself, and every one will be paid in full for what he did, and they will not be dealt with unjustly (16:111).The One who is Forced to Renounce Islam will be Forgiven If He does Righteous Deeds AfterwardsThis refers to another group of people who were oppressed in Makkah and whose position with their own people was weak, so…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:111 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: On the Day when every soul will come disputing (i.e., pleading) for itself, and every soul will be fully compensated for what it did, and they will not be wronged (i.e., treated unjustly). See 16:110

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:112 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah presents an example: a city (i.e., Makkah) which was safe and secure, its provision coming to it in abundance from every location, but it denied the favors of Allah. So Allah made it taste the envelopment of hunger and fear for what they had been doing. And Allah gives the example of a township (Makkah), it was secure and peaceful: its provision coming to it in abundance from every place, but it (its people) denied the favors of Allah. So Allah made it taste extreme hunger (famine) and fear, because of what they did (16:112). There has come to them a Messenger from among themselves, but they denied him, so the torment seized them while they were wrongdoers (16:113).The Example of MakkahThis example refers to the people of Makkah, which had been secure, peaceful and stable, a secure…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:113 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And there had certainly come to them a Messenger from among themselves, but they denied him; so punishment overtook them while they were wrongdoers. See 16:112

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:114 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then eat of what Allah has provided for you (which is) lawful and good. And be grateful for the favor of Allah, if it is (indeed) Him that you worship. So eat of the lawful and good food which Allah has provided for you. And be grateful for Allah's favor, if it is He Whom you worship (16:114). He has only forbidden dead flesh, blood, the flesh of swine, and any animal which is slaughtered as a sacrifice for other than Allah. But if one is forced by necessity, without willful disobedience, nor transgressing, then, Allah is Pardoning, Most Merciful (16:115). And do not describe what your tongues have lied about, saying: "This is lawful and this is forbidden," to invent lies against Allah. Verily, those who invent lies against Allah, will never succeed (16:116). A passing brief enjoyment (will…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:115 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He has only forbidden to you dead animals,1 blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced (by necessity), neither desiring (it) nor transgressing (its limit) - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. See 16:114

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:116 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And do not say about what your tongues assert of untruth, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent falsehood about Allah. Indeed, those who invent falsehood about Allah will not succeed. See 16:114

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:117 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (It is but) a brief enjoyment, and they will have a painful punishment. See 16:114

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:118 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to those who are Jews We have prohibited that which We related to you before.1 And We did not wrong them (thereby), but they were wronging themselves. And for those who are Jews, We have forbidden such things as We have mentioned to you before. And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves (16:118). Then, your Lord for those who did evil out of ignorance and afterward repent and do righteous deeds - verily, after that, your Lord is Pardoning, Most Merciful (16:119).Some Good Things were Forbidden for the JewsAfter mentioning that He has forbidden us to eat dead meat, blood, the flesh of swine, and any animal which is slaughtered as a sacrifice for others than Allah, and after making allowances for cases of necessity - which is part of making things easy for this Ummah,…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:119 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then, indeed your Lord, to those who have done wrong out of ignorance and then repent after that and correct themselves - indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful. See 16:118

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And He has subjected for you the night and day and the sun and moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason. And He has subjected the night and the day for you, and the sun and the moon; and the stars are subjected by His command. Surely, in this are proofs for people who understand (16:12). And all He has created of varying colors on the earth for you. Verily, in this is a sign for people who reflect (16:13).Signs in the Subjection of Night and Day, the Sun and the Moon, and in that which Grows on EarthAllah mentions the mighty signs and immense blessings to be found in His subjection of night and day, which follow one another; the sun and moon, which revolve; the stars,…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:120 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, Ibrahim was a (comprehensive) leader,1 devoutly obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah. Verily, Ibrahim was (himself) an Ummah, obedient to Allah, a Hanif (monotheist), and he was not one of the idolators (16:120). (He was) thankful for His favors. He (Allah) chose him and guided him to a straight path (16:121). And We gave him good in this world, and in the Hereafter he shall be of the righteous (16:122). Then, We have sent the revelation to you: Follow the religion of Ibrahim (he was a) Hanif, and he was not one of the idolators (16:123).The Khalil (Close Friend) of AllahAllah praises His servant, Messenger and close friend Ibrahim, the Imam of the Hanifs the father of the Prophets, and Allah declares Ibrahim's innocence of the idolators, Jews…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:121 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (He was) grateful for His favors. He (i.e., Allah) chose him and guided him to a straight path. See 16:120

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:122 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous. See 16:120

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:123 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then We revealed to you, (O Muḥammad), to follow the religion of Ibrahim, inclining toward truth; and he was not of those who associate with Allah. See 16:120

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:124 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The sabbath was only appointed for those who differed over it. And indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ. The Sabbath was only prescribed for those who differed concerning it, and verily, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection about what they differed over (16:124).The Prescription of the Sabbath for the JewsThere is no doubt that for every nation, Allah prescribed one day of the week for people to gather to worship Him. For this Ummah He prescribed Friday, because it is the sixth day, on which Allah completed and perfected His creation. On this day He gathered and completed His blessings for His servants. It was said that Allah prescribed this day for the Children of Israel through His Prophet Musa, but…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:125 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is (rightly) guided. Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and fair preaching, and argue with them with that which is best. Truly, your Lord best knows who has strayed from His path, and He best knows those who are guided (16:125).The Command to Invite People to Allah with Wisdom and Good PreachingAllah commands His Messenger Muhammad SAW to invite the people to Allah with Hikmah (wisdom). Ibn Jarir said: "That is what was revealed to him from the Book and the Sunnah."وَالْمَوْعِظَةِ الْحَسَنَةِand fair preachingMeaning: with exhortation and stories of the events that happened to…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:126 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if you punish (an enemy, O believers), punish with an equivalent of that with which you were harmed.1 But if you are patient - it is better for those who are patient. And if you punish them, then punish them with the like of that with which you were afflicted. But if you have patience with them, then it is better for those who are patient (16:126). And be patient, and your patience will not be, but by the help of Allah. And do not grieve over them, and do not be distressed by their plots (16:127). Truly, Allah is with those who have Taqwa, and the doers of good (16:128).The Command for Equality in PunishmentAllah commands justice in punishment and equity in settling the cases of rights. 'Abdur-Razzaq recorded that, concerning the Ayah:فَعَاقِبُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُم بِهِthen punish…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:127 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And be patient, (O Muḥammad), and your patience is not but through Allah. And do not grieve over them and do not be in distress over what they conspire. See 16:126

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:128 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good. See 16:126

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (He has subjected) whatever He multiplied for you on the earth of varying colors. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who remember. See 16:12

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it is He who subjected the sea for you to eat from it tender meat and to extract from it ornaments which you wear. And you see the ships plowing through it, and (He subjected it) that you may seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful. And He it is Who subjected the sea (to you), that you may eat from the fresh tender meat, and that you bring forth out of it ornaments to wear. And you see the ships plowing through it, that you may seek from His bounty and that you may perhaps be grateful (16:14). And He has driven firm standing mountains into the earth, lest it should shake with you; and rivers and roads, that you may guide yourselve (16:15). And (by the) landmarks; and by the stars, they guide themselves…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And He has cast into the earth firmly set mountains, lest it shift with you, and (made) rivers and roads, that you may be guided. See 16:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And landmarks. And by the stars they are (also) guided.1 See 16:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then is He who creates like one who does not create? So will you not be reminded? See 16:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. See 16:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah knows what you conceal and what you declare. And Allah knows what you conceal and what you reveal (16:19). Those whom they invoke besides Allah have not created anything, but are themselves created (16:20). (They are) dead, not alive; and they do not know when they will be resurrected (16:21).Allah tells us that He knows what is hidden in people's hearts as well as what is apparent. He will reward or punish everyone for their deeds on the Day of Resurrection. If their deeds are good then they will be rewarded, and if their deeds are evil, then they will be punished.The Gods of the Idolators are Created, they do Not CreateThen Allah tells us that the idols which people call on instead of Him cannot create anything, they are themselves created, as Al-Khalil (Ibrahim) said:أَتَعْبُدُونَ مَا تَنْحِتُونَ…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He sends down the angels, with the inspiration (i.e., revelation) of His command, upon whom He wills of His servants, (telling them), "Warn that there is no deity except Me; so fear Me." He sends down the angels with the Ruh (revelation) of His command to those servants of His whom He wills (saying): Warn mankind that none has the right to be worshipped but I, so have Taqwa of Me (16:2).Allah Sends Whomever He Wills with the Message of Tawhidيُنَزِّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ بِالرُّوحِHe sends down the angels with the Ruhrefers to the revelation. This is like the Ayat:وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِّنْ أَمْرِنَا ۚ مَا كُنتَ تَدْرِي مَا الْكِتَابُ وَلَا الْإِيمَانُ وَلَٰكِن جَعَلْنَاهُ نُورًا نَّهْدِي بِهِ مَن نَّشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَاAnd thus We have sent to you a Ruh (revelation) by Our command. You knew not what is the Book, nor…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those they invoke other than Allah create nothing, and they (themselves) are created. See 16:19

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They are (in fact) dead,1 not alive, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected. See 16:19

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Your god is one God. But those who do not believe in the Hereafter - their hearts are disapproving, and they are arrogant. Your god is one God. But for those who believe not in the Hereafter, their hearts are in denial, and they are proud (16:22). Certainly, Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Truly, He does not like the proud (16:23).None is to be Worshipped Except AllahAllah tells us that there is none to be worshipped besides Him, the One, the Unique, the Lone, the Self-Sufficient. He tells us that the hearts of the disbelievers deny that and are astonished by that:أَجَعَلَ الْآلِهَةَ إِلَٰهًا وَاحِدًا ۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَيْءٌ عُجَابٌ"Has he made the gods (all) into One God?! Verily, this is a curious thing!" (38:5)وَإِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ اشْمَأَزَّتْ قُلُوبُ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ ۖ وَإِذَا…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Assuredly, Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare. Indeed, He does not like the arrogant. See 16:22

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when it is said to them, "What has your Lord sent down?" they say, "Legends of the former peoples." And when it is said to them: What is it that your Lord has revealed?" They say: "Tales of the men of old! (16:24). They will bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also the burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge. Evil indeed is that which they shall bear (16:25).The Destruction of the Disbelievers and Intensification of their Punishment for Rejecting the RevelationAllah informs us that when it is said to those liars:مَّاذَا أَنزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ ۙ قَالُوا"What is it that your Lord has revealed?" They say,not wanting to answer:أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ"Tales of the men of old!"meaning nothing is revealed to him, what he is reciting to us is just tales of the men of…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That they may bear their own burdens (i.e., sins) in full on the Day of Resurrection and some of the burdens of those whom they misguide without (i.e., by lack of) knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear. See 16:24

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those before them had already plotted, but Allah came at (i.e., uprooted) their building from the foundations, so the roof fell upon them from above them,1 and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive. Those before them indeed plotted, but Allah struck at the foundation of their building, the roof fell down upon them from above them, and the torment overtook them from directions they did not perceive (16:26). Then, on the Day of Resurrection, He will disgrace them and will say: Where are My (so-called) partners, those over which you caused so much discord?" Those who have been given the knowledge will say: "Indeed it is a Day of disgrace and misery for the disbelievers (16:27).Discussion about what the Previous Peoples did, and what was Done to Themقَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْThose before them indeed…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them and say, "Where are My 'partners' for whom you used to oppose (the believers)?" Those who were given knowledge will say, "Indeed disgrace, this Day, and evil are upon the disbelievers". See 16:26

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The ones whom the angels take in death (while) wronging themselves,1 and (who) then offer submission, (saying), "We were not doing any evil." But, yes! Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what you used to do. Those whose lives the angels take while they are doing wrong to themselves. Then, they will (falsely) submit (saying): "We did not do any evil." (The angels will reply): "Yes! Truly, Allah is Most Knowing of what you did (16:28). "So enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein, and indeed, what an evil abode there is for the arrogant (16:29).The Condition of the Disbeliever during and after DeathAllah informs us of the state of the idolators who are doing wrong to themselves when death approaches and the angels come to seize their evil souls.فَأَلْقَوُا السَّلَمَThen, they will (falsely) submitMeaning: they will make it appear…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and how wretched is the residence of the arrogant. See 16:28

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He created the heavens and earth in truth. High is He above what they associate with Him. He has created the heavens and the earth with truth. High is He, Exalted above all that they associate as partners with Him (16:3). He has created man from a Nutfah, then behold, this same (man) becomes an open opponent (16:4).Allah is the One Who has Created the Heavens, the Earth, and ManAllah tells us about His creation of the upper realm, which is the heavens, and the lower realm, which is the earth, and everything in them. They have been created for a true purpose, not in vain, so that:لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوا بِمَا عَمِلُوا وَيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا بِالْحُسْنَىHe may requite those who do evil with that which they have done (i.e. punish them in Hell), and reward those who do good, with…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it will be said to those who feared Allah, "What did your Lord send down?" They will say, "(That which is) good." For those who do good in this world is good; and the home of the Hereafter is better. And how excellent is the home of the righteous. And (when) it is said to those who had Taqwa (piety and righteousness), What is it that your Lord has revealed?" They say: "That which is good." For those who do good in this world, there is good, and the home of the Hereafter will be better. And excellent indeed will be the home (i.e. Paradise) of those who have Taqwa (16:30). 'Adn (Eden) Paradise (Gardens of Eternity) which they will enter, under which rivers flow, in it they will have all that they wish. Thus Allah rewards those who…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Gardens of perpetual residence, which they will enter, beneath which rivers flow. They will have therein whatever they wish. Thus does Allah reward the righteous. See 16:30

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The ones whom the angels take in death, (being) good and pure; (the angels) will say, "Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do." See 16:30

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Do they (i.e., the disbelievers) await except that the angels should come to them or there comes the command of your Lord? Thus did those do before them. And Allah wronged them not, but they had been wronging themselves. Are they but waiting for the angels to come to them, or there comes the command of your Lord? Thus did those before them. And Allah did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves (16:33). Then, they were afflicted by their evil deeds, and they were surrounded by that which they used to mock (16:34).The Disbelievers' Refrain from Faith Means that They were Simply Awaiting PunishmentThreatening the idolators for their persistence in falsehood and their conceited delusions about this world, Allah says: Are these people waiting only for the angels to come and take their souls? Qatadah said:أَوْ يَأْتِيَ أَمْرُ…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So they were struck by the evil consequences of what they did and were enveloped by what they used to ridicule. See 16:33

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who associate others with Allah say, "If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped anything other than Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything through other than Him." Thus did those do before them. So is there upon the messengers except (the duty of) clear notification? And those who worshipped others with Allah said: "If Allah had so willed, neither we nor our fathers would have worshipped any but Him nor would we have forbidden anything without (a command from) Him." Those before them did the same. Then! Are the Messengers charged with anything but to clearly convey the Message (16:35). And We have indeed sent a Messenger to every Ummah (community, nation) (saying): "Worship Allah (Alone), and shun the Taghut (all false deities). " Then among them were some whom Allah…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, (saying), "Worship Allah and avoid ṭāghūt."1 And among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was (deservedly) decreed. So proceed (i.e., travel) through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers. See 16:35

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Even) if you should strive for their guidance, (O Muḥammad), indeed, Allah does not guide those He sends astray,1 and they will have no helpers. See 16:35

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they swear by Allah their strongest oaths (that) Allah will not resurrect one who dies. But yes - (it is) a true promise (binding) upon Him, but most of the people do not know. And they swear by Allah with their strongest oaths, that Allah will not raise up one who dies. Yes, (He will raise them up), a promise (binding) upon Him in truth, but most of mankind know not (16:38). In order that He may make clear to them what they differed over, and so that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars (16:39). Verily, Our Word to a thing when We intend it, is only that We say unto it: "Be!" - and it is (16:40).The Resurrection after Death is True, There is Wisdom behind it, and it is Easy for AllahAllah tells us…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (It is) so He will make clear to them (the truth of) that wherein they differ and so those who have disbelieved may know that they were liars. See 16:38

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He created man from a sperm-drop; then at once1 he is a clear adversary. See 16:3

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is but that We say to it, "Be," and it is. See 16:38

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who emigrated for (the cause of) Allah after they had been wronged - We will surely settle them in this world in a good place; but the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if only they could know. And as for those who emigrated for the cause of Allah, after they had been wronged, We will certainly give them good residence in this world, but indeed the reward of the Hereafter will be greater; if they but knew (16:41). (They are) those who remained patient, and put their trust in their Lord (16:42).The Reward of the MuhajirinAllah tells us about the reward of those who migrated for His sake, seeking His pleasure, those who left their homeland behind, brothers and friends, hoping for the reward of Allah. This may have been revealed concerning those who migrated to Ethiopia,…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (They are) those who endured patiently and upon their Lord relied. See 16:41

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed (Our message). So ask the people of the message (i.e., former scriptures) if you do not know. And We sent not (as Our Messengers) before you (O Muhammad) any but men, whom We sent revelation. So ask Ahl Adh-Dhikr, if you know not (16:43). With clear signs and Books (We sent the Messengers). And We have also revealed the Dhikr to you so that you may clearly explain to men what was revealed to them, and that perhaps they may reflect (16:44).Only Human Messengers have been SentAd-Dahhak said, reporting from Ibn 'Abbas: When Allah sent Muhammad SAW as a Messenger, the Arabs, or some of them, denied him and said, 'Allah is too great to send a human being as a Messenger.' Then Allah revealed:أَكَانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَبًا أَنْ…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (We sent them) with clear proofs and written ordinances. And We revealed to you the message (i.e., the Qur’ān) that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them and that they might give thought. See 16:43

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then, do those who have planned evil deeds feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them or that the punishment will not come upon them from where they do not perceive? Do then those who devise evil plots feel secure that Allah will not cause them to sink into the earth, or that torment will not seize them from where they do not perceive it (16:45). Or that He may punish them in the midst of their going to and fro (in their livelihood), so that there be no escape for them (from Allah's punishment) (16:46). Or that He may punish them where they fear it most? Indeed, Your Lord is full of kindness, Most Merciful (16:47).How the Guilty can Feel SecureAllah informs us about His patience, and how He delays the punishment for the sinners…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or that He would not seize them during their (usual) activity, and they could not cause failure (i.e., escape from Him)? See 16:45

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or that He would not seize them gradually (in a state of dread)?1 But indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.2 See 16:45

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have they not considered what things Allah has created? Their shadows incline to the right and to the left, prostrating to Allah, while they (i.e., those creations) are humble. Have they not observed things that Allah has created: (how) their shadows shift from right to left, prostrating to Allah while they are humble (16:48). And to Allah prostrate all that are in the heavens and all that are in the earth, the moving creatures and the angels, and they are not proud [i.e. they worship their Lord (Allah) with humility (49)They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded (50)Everything Prostrates to AllahAllah informs us about His might, majesty and pride, meaning that all things submit themselves to Him and every created being - animate and inanimate, as well as the responsible - humans and Jinns,…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels (as well), and they are not arrogant. See 16:48

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the grazing livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth1 and (numerous) benefits, and from them you eat. And the cattle, He has created them for you; in them there is warmth (warm clothing), and numerous benefits, and you eat from them (16:5). And there is beauty in them for you, when you bring them home in the evening, and as you lead them forth to pasture (in the morning) (16:6). And they carry your loads to a land that you could not reach yourselves except with great trouble. Truly, your Lord is full of kindness, Most Merciful (16:7).The Cattle are Part of the Creation of Allah and a Blessing from HimAllah reminds His servants of the blessing in His creation of An'am, this term includes camels, cows and sheep, as was explained in detail in Surat…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded. See 16:48

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah has said, "Do not take for yourselves two1 deities. He (i.e., Allah) is but one God, so fear only Me." And Allah said Do not worship two gods. Indeed, He (Allah) is only One God. Then fear Me Alone (16:51). To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth and the religion. Will you then fear any other than Allah (16:52). And whatever of blessings and good things you have, it is from Allah. Then, when harm touches you, unto Him you cry aloud for help (16:53). Then, when He has removed the harm from you, behold! some of you associate others in worship with their Lord (Allah) (16:54). So they are ungrateful for that which We have given them! Then enjoy yourselves but you will soon come to know (16:55).Allah Alone is Deserving of…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him is (due) worship constantly. Then is it other than Allah that you fear? See 16:51

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whatever you have of favor - it is from Allah. Then when adversity touches you, to Him you cry for help. See 16:51

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then when He removes the adversity from you, at once a party of you associates others with their Lord. See 16:51

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So they will deny what We have given them. Then enjoy yourselves, for you are going to know. See 16:51

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they assign to what they do not know1 (i.e., false deities) a portion of that which We have provided them. By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to invent. And they assign a portion of that which We have provided them with, to what they have no knowledge of (false deities). By Allah, you shall certainly be questioned about (all) that you used to fabricate (16:56). And they assign daughters to Allah! Glorified (and Exalted) is He (above all that they associate with Him!). And for themselves (they assign) what they desire (16:57). And when the news of (the birth of) a female (child) is brought to any of them, his face becomes dark, and he is filled with inner grief (16:58). He hides himself from the people because of the evil of what he…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they attribute to Allah daughters1 - exalted is He - and for them is what they desire (i.e., sons). See 16:56

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when one of them is informed of (the birth of) a female, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief. See 16:56

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He hides himself from the people because of the ill of which he has been informed. Should he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the ground? Unquestionably, evil is what they decide. See 16:56

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And for you in them is (the enjoyment of) beauty when you bring them in (for the evening) and when you send them out (to pasture). See 16:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the description (i.e., an attribute) of evil;1 and for Allah is the highest attribute. And He is Exalted in Might, the Wise. See 16:56

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if Allah were to impose blame on the people for their wrongdoing, He would not have left upon it (i.e., the earth) any creature, but He defers them for a specified term. And when their term has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede (it). And if Allah were to punish (all) mankind for their wrongdoing, He would not leave on it (the earth) a single moving creature, but He defers them to an appointed term; and when their term comes, they can neither delay nor advance it an hour (or a moment) (16:61). They assign to Allah that which they dislike (for themselves), and their tongues assert the lie that the better things will be theirs. No doubt the Fire is for them, and they will be forsaken (16:62).Allah does Not Immediately Punish…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they attribute to Allah that which they dislike (i.e., daughters), and their tongues assert the lie that they will have the best (from Him). Assuredly, they will have the Fire, and they will be (therein) neglected.1 See 16:61

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By Allah, We did certainly send (messengers) to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds attractive to them. And he is their (i.e., the disbelievers) ally today (as well), and they will have a painful punishment. By Allah, We indeed sent (Messengers) to the nations before you, but Shaytan made their deeds seeming fair to them. So today he is their helper, and theirs will be a painful torment (16:63). And We have not revealed the Book to you, except that you may clearly explain to them those things in which they differ, and (as) a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe (16:64). And Allah sends water down from the sky, then He revives the earth with it after its death. Surely that is a sign for people who listen (16:65).Finding Consolation in the Reminder of…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have not revealed to you the Book, (O Muḥammad), except for you to make clear to them that wherein they have differed and as guidance and mercy for a people who believe. See 16:63

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah has sent down rain from the sky and given life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who listen. See 16:63

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, for you in grazing livestock is a lesson. We give you drink from what is in their bellies - between excretion and blood - pure milk, palatable to drinkers. And there is indeed a lesson for you in the An'am (cattle). We have made a drink for you out of what is in its belly, from between excretions and blood, pure milk; palatable to the drinkers (16:66). And from the fruits of date palms and grapes, you derive strong drink and a goodly provision. There is indeed a sign in this for those of reason (16:67).Lessons and Blessings in Cattle and the Fruit of the Date-palm and Grapevineوَإِنَّ لَكُمْthere is for youO mankind -فِي الْأَنْعَامِin the cattle - meaning camels, cows and sheep:لَعِبْرَةًa lessonmeaning a sign and an evidence of the wisdom, power, mercy and kindness of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you take intoxicant and good provision.1 Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason. See 16:66

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And your Lord inspired to the bee, "Take for yourself among the mountains, houses (i.e., hives), and among the trees and (in) that which they construct. And your Lord inspired the bee, saying: Take you habitations in the mountains and in the trees and in what they (humans) erect (16:68). "Then, eat of all fruits, and follow the routes that your Lord made easy (for you)." There comes forth from their bellies, a drink of varying colors, in which there is a cure for men. There is indeed a sign in that for people who reflect (16:69).In the Bee and its Honey There is Blessing and a LessonWhat is meant by inspiration here is guidance. The bee is guided to make its home in the mountains, in trees and in structures erected by man. The bee's home is a solid…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then eat from all the fruits1 and follow the ways of your Lord laid down (for you)." There emerges from their bellies a drink, varying in colors, in which there is healing for people. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought. See 16:68

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they carry your loads to a land you could not have reached except with difficulty to yourselves. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful. See 16:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:70 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah created you; then He will take you in death. And among you is he who is reversed to the most decrepit (old) age so that he will not know, after (having had) knowledge, a thing. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Competent. And Allah created you and then He will cause you to die; and among you there are some who are sent back to senility, so that they know nothing after having known (much). Truly, Allah is Knowing, capable of all things (16:70).In Man There is a LessonAllah tells us that He is controlling the affairs of His servants. He is the One Who created them out of nothing, then He will cause them to die. But there are some of them that He allows to grow old, which is a physical weakness, as Allah says:اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُم…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah has favored some of you over others in provision. But those who were favored (i.e., given more) would not hand over their provision to those whom their right hands possess (i.e., slaves) so they would be equal to them therein.1 Then is it the favor of Allah they reject? And Allah honored some of you over others with wealth and properties. Then, those who are so honored will by no means hand over their wealth and properties to those (captives of war) whom their right hands possess, so that they may be equal with them in that. Do they then deny the favor of Allah (16:71).There is a Sign and a Blessing in Matters of People's LivelihoodAllah explains to the idolators the ignorance and disbelief involved in their claim that Allah has partners while also admitting that these…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:72 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah has made for you from yourselves mates and has made for you from your mates sons and grandchildren and has provided for you from the good things. Then in falsehood do they believe and in the favor of Allah they disbelieve? And Allah has made for you mates of your own kind, and has made for you, from your mates, sons and grandsons, and has granted you good provisions. Do they then believe in false deities and deny favor of Allah (16:72).Among His Blessings and Signs are Mates, Children and GrandchildrenAllah mentions the blessing He has bestowed upon His servant by giving them mates from among themselves, mates of their own kind. If He had given them mates of another kind, there would be no harmony, love and mercy between them. But out of His mercy He has…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:73 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they worship besides Allah that which does not possess for them (the power of) provision from the heavens and the earth at all, and (in fact), they are unable. And they worship others besides Allah such as do not have power to grant them any provision from the heavens or the earth nor the ability to do so (16:73). So do not give examples on behalf of Allah. Truly, Allah knows and you know not (16:74).Denouncing the Worship of Anything Besides AllahAllah tells us about the Mushrikin who worship others besides Him, even though He alone is the bountiful Provider, the Creator and Sustainer, without partners or associates, but they still worship idols and make rivals for Him. He says:مَا لَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ رِزْقًا مِّنَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ شَيْئًاsuch as do not have power to grant them any provision from…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So do not assert similarities to Allah.1 Indeed, Allah knows and you do not know. See 16:73

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah presents an example: a slave (who is) owned and unable to do a thing and he to whom We have provided from Us good provision, so he spends from it secretly and publicly. Can they be equal? Praise to Allah! But most of them do not know. Allah gives the example of a servant under the possession of another, he has no power of any sort, and a man on whom We have bestowed good provisions from Us, and he spends from that secretly and openly. Can they be equal? (By no means). All the praises and thanks are to Allah. Nay! (But) most of them know not (16:75).The Example of the Believer and the Disbeliever, or the Idol and the True GodAl-'Awfi reported that Ibn 'Abbas said: "This is the example which Allah gives of the disbeliever and…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:76 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah presents an example of two men, one of them dumb and unable to do a thing, while he is a burden to his guardian. Wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who commands justice, while he is on a straight path? And Allah gives an example of two men, one of them dumb, who has no power over anything, and he is a burden on his master; whichever way he directs him, he brings no good. Is such a man equal to one who commands justice, and is himself on the straight path (16:76).Another ExampleMujahid said, "This also refers to idols and the True God, may He be exalted." Meaning that the idol is dumb and cannot speak or say anything, good or otherwise. It cannot do anything at all, no words,…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:77 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to Allah belongs the unseen (aspects) of the heavens and the earth. And the command for the Hour is not but as a glance of the eye or even nearer. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent. And to Allah belongs the Unseen of the heavens and the earth. And the matter of the Hour is not but as a twinkling of the eye, or even nearer. Truly, Allah is able to do all things (16:77). And Allah has brought you out from the wombs of your mothers while you knew nothing. And He gave you hearing, sight, and hearts, that you might give thanks (16:78). Do they not see the birds held (flying) in the midst of the sky None holds them up but Allah. Verily, in this are clear signs for people who believe (16:79).The Unseen Belongs…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:78 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah has extracted you from the wombs of your mothers not knowing a thing, and He made for you hearing and vision and hearts (i.e., intellect) that perhaps you would be grateful. See 16:77

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:79 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Do they not see the birds controlled in the atmosphere of the sky? None holds them up except Allah. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe. See 16:77

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (He created) the horses, mules and donkeys for you to ride and (as) adornment. And He creates that which you do not know. And (He has created) horses, mules and donkeys for you to ride, and as an adornment. And He creates (other) things of which you have no knowledge (16:8).This refers to another category of animals that Allah has created as a blessing for His servants, horses, mules and donkeys, all of which He made for riding and adornment.This is the main purpose for which these animals were created. It was reported in the Two Sahihs that Jabir bin 'Abdullah said: "The Messenger of Allah SAW forbade us to eat the meat of domestic donkeys, but he allowed us to eat the meat of horses."Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud reported with two chains of narration, each of which…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:80 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah has made for you from your homes a place of rest and made for you from the hides of the animals tents which you find light on your day of travel and your day of encampment; and from their wool, fur and hair is furnishing and enjoyment (i.e., provision) for a time. And Allah had made your homes a place of rest for you, and made dwellings for you out of the hides of the cattle which you find so light when you travel and when you camp; and furnishings and articles of convenience out of their wool, fur, and hair - comfort for a while (16:80). And Allah has made shade for you out of that which He has created, and He has made places of refuge in the mountains for you, and He has made garments…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:81 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah has made for you, from that which He has created, shadows (i.e., shade) and has made for you from the mountains, shelters and has made for you garments which protect you from the heat and garments (i.e., coats of mail) which protect you from your (enemy in) battle. Thus does He complete His favor upon you that you might submit (to Him). See 16:80

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:82 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But if they turn away, (O Muḥammad) - then only upon you is (responsibility for) clear notification. See 16:80

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:83 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They recognize the favor of Allah; then they deny it. And most of them are disbelievers. See 16:80

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:84 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) the Day when We will resurrect from every nation a witness (i.e., their prophet). Then it will not be permitted to the disbelievers (to apologize or make excuses), nor will they be asked to appease (Allah). And on the Day when We resurrect a witness from each nation, then those who disbelieve will not be given leave, nor will they be allowed (to return to the world) to repent and ask for Allah's forgiveness.) 85. And once those who did wrong see the torment, it will not decrease for them, nor will they be given respite (16:84). And when those who associated partners with Allah see their partners, they will say: Our Lord! These are our partners whom we used to call upon besides you." But they will throw back their statement at them (saying): "You indeed are…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:85 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when those who wronged see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved. See 16:84

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:86 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when those who associated others with Allah see their "partners," they will say, "Our Lord, these are our partners (to You) whom we used to invoke (in worship) besides You." But they will throw at them the statement, "Indeed, you are liars." See 16:84

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:87 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they will impart to Allah that Day (their) submission, and lost from them is what they used to invent. See 16:84

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:88 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those who disbelieved and averted (others) from the way of Allah - We will increase them in punishment over (their) punishment for what corruption they were causing. See 16:84

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:89 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) the Day when We will resurrect among every nation a witness over them from themselves (i.e., their prophet). And We will bring you, (O Muḥammad), as a witness over these (i.e., your nation). And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things and as guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.1 And on the Day when We resurrect a witness from each nation from among themselves, and We bring you (O Muhammad) as a witness against these. And We have revealed the Book (the Qur'an) to you as an explanation of everything, a guidance, a mercy, and good news for the Muslims (16:89).Every Prophet will Bear Witness against his Nation on the Day of ResurrectionAllah addressed His servant and Messenger Muhammad SAW, saying:وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيدًا عَلَيْهِم مِّنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And upon Allah1 is the direction of the (right) way, and among them (i.e., the various paths) are those deviating. And if He willed, He could have guided you all. And it is up to Allah to show the right way. But there are ways that stray. And had He willed, He would have guided you all (16:9).Explanation of the Different Religious PathsWhen Allah mentioned the animals which may be used for the purpose of physical journeys, He also referred to the moral, religious routes that people may follow. Often in the Qur'an there is a shift from physical or tangible things to beneficial spiritual and religious matters, as when Allah says:وَتَزَوَّدُوا فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ الزَّادِ التَّقْوَىٰAnd take a provision (with you) for the journey, but the best provision is Taqwa (piety, righteousness). (2:197)And:يَا بَنِي آدَمَ قَدْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاسًا يُوَارِي…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:90 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving (help) to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded. Verily, Allah orders justice and kindness, and giving (help) to the relatives, and He forbids immoral sins, and evil and tyranny. He admonishes you, so that perhaps you may take heed (16:90).The Command to be Fair and KindAllah tells us that He commands His servant to be just, i.e., fair and moderate, and that He encourages kindness and good treatment. As He says:وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُم بِهِ ۖ وَلَئِن صَبَرْتُمْ لَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لِّلصَّابِرِينَAnd if you punish them, then punish them with the like of that with which you were afflicted. But if you have patience with them, then it is better for those who are patient. (16:126)وَجَزَاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:91 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have taken it, (O believers), and do not break oaths after their confirmation while you have made Allah, over you, a security (i.e., witness). Indeed, Allah knows what you do. And fulfill the covenants (taken in the Name of) Allah when you have taken them, and do not break the oaths after you have confirmed them - and indeed you have appointed Allah as your guarantor. Verily, Allah knows what you do (16:91). And do not be like the one who undoes the thread which she has spun, after it has become strong, by taking your oaths as a means of deception among yourselves when one group is more numerous than another group. Allah only tests you by this, and on the Day of Resurrection, He will certainly clarify that which used…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:92 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And do not be like she who untwisted her spun thread after it was strong (by) taking your oaths as (means of) deceit between you because one community is more plentiful (in number or wealth) than another community.1 Allah only tries you thereby. And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ. See 16:91

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:93 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if Allah had willed, He could have made you (of) one religion, but He sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills.1 And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do. And had Allah willed, He would have made you (all) one nation, but He allows whom He wills to stray and He guides whom He wills. But you shall certainly be called to account for what you used to do (16:93). And do not make your oaths a means of deception among yourselves, resulting in the slip of a foot after it was firmly planted, and you taste the evil of having hindered from the path of Allah, and you will suffer a terrible punishment (16:94). And do not use an oath by Allah for the purchase of little value, what is with…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:94 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
