item.description: And do not take your oaths as (means of) deceit between you, lest a foot slip after it was (once) firm, and you would taste evil (in this world) for what (people) you diverted from the way of Allah,1 and you would have (in the Hereafter) a great punishment. See 16:93

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:95 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price. Indeed, what is with Allah is best for you, if only you could know. See 16:93

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:96 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Whatever you have will end, but what Allah has is lasting. And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do. See 16:93

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:97 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward (in the Hereafter) according to the best of what they used to do. Whoever does righteous deeds - whether male or female - while he (or she) is a believer; then We will certainly give them a good life, and We will certainly grant them their rewards in proportion to the best of what they used to do (16:97).Righteous Deeds and their RewardThis is a promise from Allah to those Children of Adam, male or female, who do righteous deeds - deeds in accordance with the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet SAW, with a heart that believes in Allah and His Messenger SAW, while believing…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:98 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So when you recite the Qur’ān, (first) seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the expelled (from His mercy). So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge with Allah from Shaytan, the outcast (16:98). Verily, he has no power over those who believe and put their trust only in their Lord (16:99). His power is only over those who obey and follow him (Shaytan), and those who join partners with Him (Allah) (16:100).The Command to Seek Refuge with Allah before Reciting the Qur'anThis is a command from Allah to His servants upon the tongue of His Prophet SAW, telling them that when they want to read Qur'an, they should seek refuge with Allah from the cursed Shaytan. The Hadiths mentioned about seeking refuge with Allah (Isti'adhah), were quoted in our discussion at the beginning of this Tafsir, praise be to Allah.…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:99 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, there is for him no authority over those who have believed and rely upon their Lord. See 16:98

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By the star when it descends. إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْيٌ يُوحَىٰIt is only a revelation revealed.Which is means, he only conveys to the people what he was commanded to convey, in its entirety without additions or deletions. Imam Ahmad recorded that Abu Umamah said that he heard the Messenger of Allah SAW say:لَيَدْخُلَنَّ الْجَنَّةَ بِشَفَاعَةِ رَجُلٍ لَيْسَ بِنَبِيٍّ مِثْلُ الْحَيَّيْنِ - أَوْ مِثْلُ أَحَدِ الْحَيَّيْنِ - رَبِيعَةَ وَمُضَرَVerily, numbers similar to the two tribes, or one of them, Rabi'ah and Mudar, will enter Paradise on account of the intercession of one man, who is not a Prophet.A man asked, "O Allah's Messenger! Is not Rabi'ah a subtribe of Mudar." The Prophet SAW said:إِنَّمَا أَقُولُ مَا أَقُولُI said what I said.Imam Ahmad recorded that 'Abdullah bin 'Amr said, I used to record everything I heard from the Messenger of Allah SAW…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he revealed to His Servant1 what he revealed (i.e., conveyed). See 53:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The heart1 did not lie (about) what it saw. See 53:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So will you dispute with him over what he saw? See 53:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he certainly saw him in another descent.1 See 53:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: At the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary. See 53:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Near it is the Garden of Refuge (i.e., Paradise). See 53:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When there covered the Lote Tree that which covered (it).1 See 53:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The sight (of the Prophet SAW) did not swerve, nor did it transgress (its limit). See 53:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He certainly saw of the greatest signs of his Lord. See 53:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So have you considered al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā? Have you then considered Al-Lat, and Al-'Uzza (53:19). And Manat, the other third (53:20). Is it for you the males and for Him the females (53:21). That indeed is a division most unfair (53:22). They are but names which you have named - you and your fathers - for which Allah has sent down no authority. They follow but a guess and that which they themselves desire, whereas there has surely come to them the guidance from their Lord (53:23). Or shall man have what he wishes (53:24). But to Allah belongs the last (Hereafter) and the first (the world) (53:25). And there are many angels in the heavens, whose intercession will avail nothing, except after Allah has given leave for whom He wills and is pleased with (53:26).Refuting Idolatry, Al-Lat and Al-'UzzaAllah…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Your companion (i.e., Muḥammad) has not strayed, nor has he erred. See 53:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Manāt, the third - the other one?1 See 53:19

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Is the male for you and for Him the female? See 53:19

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That, then, is an unjust division.1 See 53:19

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They are not but (mere) names you have named them - you and your forefathers - for which Allah has sent down no authority. They follow not except assumption and what (their) souls desire, and there has already come to them from their Lord guidance. See 53:19

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or is there for man whatever he wishes? See 53:19

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Rather, to Allah belongs the Hereafter and the first (life). See 53:19

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And how many angels there are in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except (only) after Allah has permitted (it) to whom He wills and approves. See 53:19

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels female names. Verily, those who believe not in the Hereafter, name the angels with female names (53:27). But they have no knowledge thereof. They follow but conjecture, and verily, conjecture is no substitute for the truth (53:28). Therefore withdraw from him who turns away from Our Reminder and desires nothing but the life of this world (53:29). That is what they could reach of knowledge. Verily, your Lord is He, Who knows best him who goes astray from His path, and He knows best him who receives guidance (53:30).Refuting the Claim of the Idolators that the Angels are Allah's DaughtersAllah the Exalted admonishes the idolators for calling the angels female names and claiming that they are Allah's daughters. Allah is far removed from what they ascribe to Him.…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they have thereof no knowledge. They follow not except assumption, and indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all. See 53:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So turn away from whoever turns his back on Our message and desires not except the worldly life. See 53:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Nor does he speak from (his own) inclination. See 53:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is their sum of knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided. See 53:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth - that He may recompense those who do evil with (the penalty of) what they have done and recompense those who do good with the best (reward). And to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth, that He may requite those who do evil with that which they have done, and reward those who do good, with what is best (53:31). Those who avoid great sins and Al-Fawahish (immoral sins) except Al-Lamam – verily, your Lord is of vast forgiveness. He knows you well when He created you from the earth (Adam), and when you were fetuses in your mothers' wombs. So, ascribe not purity to yourselves. He knows best him who has Taqwa (53:32).Allah Knows Every…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, only (committing) slight ones. Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness. He was most knowing of you when He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim yourselves to be pure; He is most knowing of who fears Him. See 53:31

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have you seen the one who turned away. Did you observe him who turned away (from Islam) (53:33). And gave a little, then stopped (53:34). Is with him the knowledge of the Unseen so that he sees (53:35). Or is he not informed with what is in the Suhuf of Musa (53:36). And of Ibrahim who fulfilled all that (53:37). That no burdened person (with sins) shall bear the burden (sins) of another (53:38). And that man can have nothing but what he does (53:39). And that his deeds will be seen (53:40). Then he will be recompensed with a full and the best recompense (53:41).Chastising Those Who Disobey Allah and Stop Giving CharityAllah the Exalted chastises those who turn away from His obedience:فَلَا صَدَّقَ وَلَا صَلَّىٰ - وَلَٰكِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰSo he (the disbeliever) neither believed nor prayed! But on…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And gave a little and (then) refrained? See 53:33

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so he sees?1 See 53:33

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or has he not been informed of what was in the scriptures of Musa. See 53:33

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (of) Ibrahim, who fulfilled (his obligations). See 53:33

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. See 53:33

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that there is not for man except that (good) for which he strives. See 53:33

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is not but a revelation revealed. See 53:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that his effort is going to be seen. See 53:33

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense. See 53:33

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that to your Lord is the finality. And that to your Lord is the End (53:42). And that it is He Who makes laugh, and makes weep (53:43). And that it is He Who causes death and gives life (53:44). And that He creates the pairs, male and female (53:45). From Nutfah when it is emitted (53:46). And that upon Him is another bringing forth (Resurrection) (53:47). And that it is He Who Aghna and Aqna (53:48). And that He is the Lord of Ash-Shi'ra (53:49). And that it is He Who destroyed the former 'Ad (53:50). And Thamud. He spared none of them (53:51). And the people of Nuh aforetime. Verily, they were more unjust and more rebellious and transgressing (53:52). And He destroyed the overthrown cities (53:53). So, there covered them that which did cover (53:54). Then…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that it is He who makes (one) laugh and weep. See 53:42

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that it is He who causes death and gives life. See 53:42

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that He creates the two mates - the male and female. See 53:42

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: From a sperm-drop when it is emitted. See 53:42

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that (incumbent) upon Him is the other (i.e., next) creation. See 53:42

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that it is He who enriches and suffices. See 53:42

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that it is He who is the Lord of Sirius.1 See 53:42

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Taught to him by one intense in strength (i.e., Jibril). He has been taught by one mighty in power (53:5). Dhu Mirrah then he Istawa (53:6). While he was in the highest part of the horizon (53:7). Then he approached and came closer (53:8). And was at a distance of two bows' length or less (53:9). So (Allah) revealed to His servant whatever He revealed (53:10). The heart lied not in what he saw (53:11). Will you then dispute with him about what he saw (53:12). And indeed he saw him at a second descent (53:13). Near Sidrat Al-Muntaha (53:14). Near it is the Paradise of Abode (53:15). When that covered the lote tree which did cover it (53:16). The sight turned not aside, nor it transgressed beyond the limit (53:17). Indeed he saw of the greatest Ssgns of his…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that He destroyed the first (people of) ʿAad. See 53:42

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Thamūd - and He did not spare (them). See 53:42

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the people of Nuh before. Indeed, it was they who were (even) more unjust and oppressing. See 53:42

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the overturned towns1 He hurled down. See 53:42

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And covered them by that which He covered.1 See 53:42

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then which of the favors of your Lord do you doubt? See 53:42

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: This (Prophet SAW) is a warner from (i.e., like) the former warners. This is a warner from the warners of old (53:56). The Azifah draws near (53:57). None besides Allah can avert it (53:58). Do you then wonder at this recitation (53:59). And you laugh at it and weep not (53:60). While you are Sāmidūn (53:61). So fall you down in prostration to Allah and worship Him (53:62).A Warning and Exhortation, the Order to Prostrate and to be HumbleAllah said:هَٰذَا نَذِيرٌThis is a warnerin reference to Muhammad SAW:مِنَ النُّذُرِ الْأُولَىٰfrom the warners of old.means, just like the warners of old, he was sent as a Messenger as they were sent as Messengers. Allah the Exalted said:قُلْ مَا كُنْتُ بِدْعًا مِنَ الرُّسُلِSay: "I am not a new thing among the Messengers." (46:9)Allah said;أَزِفَتِ الْآزِفَةُThe Azifah draws near.that which is near, the…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Approaching Day has approached. See 53:56

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Of it, (from those) besides Allah, there is no remover. See 53:56

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then at this statement do you wonder? See 53:56

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: One of soundness.1 And he rose to (his) true form.2 See 53:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you laugh and do not weep. See 53:56

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: While you are proudly sporting?1 See 53:56

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So prostrate to Allah and worship (Him). See 53:56

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: While he was in the higher (part of the) horizon.1 See 53:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then he approached and descended. See 53:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer. See 53:5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Ṭā, Seen.1 These are the verses of the Qur’ān (i.e., recitation) and a clear Book. وَإِنَّكَ لَتُلَقَّى الْقُرْآنَ مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍAnd verily, you are being taught the Qur'an from One, All-Wise, All-Knowing.وَإِنَّكَAnd verily, youO Muhammad. Qatadah said:لَتُلَقَّىare being taught"Are receiving."الْقُرْآنَ مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍthe Qur'an from One, All-Wise, All-Knowing.from One Who is Wise in His commands and prohibitions, and Who knows all things, major and minor. Whatever He says is absolute Truth, and His rulings are entirely fair and just, as Allah says:وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا ۚAnd the Word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice (6:115)

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (he was told), "Throw down your staff." But when he saw it writhing as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not return.1 (Allah said), "O Musa, fear not. Indeed, in My presence the messengers do not fear. See 27:7

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Otherwise, he who wrongs, then substitutes good after evil - indeed, I am Forgiving and Merciful. See 27:7

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And put your hand into the opening of your garment (at the breast); it will come out white without disease. (These are) among the nine signs (you will take) to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they have been a people defiantly disobedient." See 27:7

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But when there came to them Our visible signs, they said, "This is obvious magic." See 27:7

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they rejected them, while their (inner) selves were convinced thereof, out of injustice and haughtiness. So see how was the end of the corrupters. See 27:7

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We had certainly given to Dawud and Sulayman knowledge, and they said, "Praise (is due) to Allah, who has favored us over many of His believing servants." And indeed We gave knowledge to Dawud and Sulayman, and they both said: "All praise be to Allah, Who has preferred us above many of His believing servants! (27:15). And Sulayman inherited from Dawud. He said: "O mankind! We have been taught the language of birds, and we have been given from everything. This, verily, is an evident grace (27:16). And there were gathered before Sulayman his hosts of Jinn and men, and birds, and they all were set in battle order (marching forward) (27:17). Till, when they came to the valley of the ants, one of the ants said: "O ants! Enter your dwellings, lest Sulayman and his armies should crush…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Sulayman inherited Dawud. He said, "O people, we have been taught the language of birds, and we have been given from all things. Indeed, this is evident bounty." See 27:15

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And gathered for Sulayman were his soldiers of the jinn and men and birds, and they were (marching) in rows. See 27:15

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings that you not be crushed by Sulayman and his soldiers while they perceive not." See 27:15

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So (Sulayman) smiled, amused at her speech, and said, "My Lord, enable me1 to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve. And admit me by Your mercy into (the ranks of) Your righteous servants."2 See 27:15

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: As guidance and good tidings for the believers. See 27:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he took attendance of the birds and said, "Why do I not see the hoopoe - or is he among the absent? He inspected the birds, and said: "What is the matter that I see not the hoopoe? Or is he among the absentees? (27:20). "I will surely punish him with a severe torment or slaughter him, unless he brings me a clear reason (27:21).The Absence of the HoopoeMujahid, Sa'id bin Jubayr and others narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and others that the hoopoe was an expert who used to show Sulayman where water was if he was out in open land and needed water. The hoopoe would look for water for him in the various strata of the earth, just as a man looks at things on the surface of the earth, and he would know just how far…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him unless he brings me clear authorization."1 See 27:20

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But he (i.e., the hoopoe) stayed not long and said, "I have encompassed (in knowledge) that which you have not encompassed, and I have come to you from Sheba with certain news. But (the hoopoe) stayed not long, he said: I have grasped which you have not grasped and I have come to you from Saba' with true news (27:22). "I found a woman ruling over them, she has been given all things, and she has a great throne (27:23). "I found her and her people worshipping the sun instead of Allah, and Shaytan has made their deeds fair seeming to them to prevent them from the way, so they have no guidance (27:24). So they do not prostrate themselves before Allah, Who brings to light what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and knows what you conceal…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, I found (there) a woman ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne. See 27:22

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from (His) way, so they are not guided. See 27:22

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (And) so they do not prostrate to Allah, who brings forth what is hidden within the heavens and the earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare. See 27:22

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah - there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Great Throne." See 27:22

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Sulayman) said, "We will see whether you were truthful or were of the liars. (Sulayman) said: "We shall see whether you speak the truth or you are (one) of the liars (27:27). "Go you with this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then draw back from them and see what they return (27:28). She said: "O chiefs! Verily, here is delivered to me a noble letter, (27:29). "Verily, it is from Sulayman, and it (reads): 'In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful; (27:30). 'Be you not exalted against me, but come to me submitting (as Muslims).' (27:31).Sulayman's Letter to BilqisAllah tells us what Sulayman said to the hoopoe when he told him about the people of Saba' and their queen:قَالَ سَنَنْظُرُ أَصَدَقْتَ أَمْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ(Sulayman) said: "We shall see whether you speak the…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them. Then leave them and see what (answer) they will return." See 27:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: She said, "O eminent ones, indeed, to me has been delivered a noble letter. See 27:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Who establish prayer and give zakāh, and of the Hereafter they are certain (in faith). See 27:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, it is from Sulayman, and indeed, it is (i.e., reads): 'In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. See 27:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Be not haughty with me but come to me in submission (as Muslims).'" See 27:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: She said, "O eminent ones, advise me in my affair. I would not decide a matter until you witness (for) me."1 She said: "O chiefs! Advise me in case of mine. I decide no case till you are present with me (27:32). They said: "We have great strength, and great ability for war, but it is for you to command; so think over what you will command (27:33). She said: "Verily, kings, when they enter a town, they destroy it and make the most honorable among its people the lowest. And thus they do (27:34). "But verily, I am going to send him a present, and see with what (answer) the messengers return (27:35).Bilqis Consults with Her ChiefsWhen she read Sulayman's letter to them and consulted with them about this news, she said:يَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِي فِي أَمْرِي مَا كُنْتُ…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "We are men of strength and of great military might, but the command is yours, so see what you will command." See 27:32

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: She said, "Indeed kings - when they enter a city, they ruin it and render the honored of its people humbled. And thus do they do. See 27:32

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But indeed, I will send to them a gift and see with what (reply) the messengers will return." See 27:32

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So when they came to Sulayman, he said, "Do you provide me with wealth? But what Allah has given me is better than what He has given you. Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift. So, when (the messengers with the gift) came to Sulayman, he said: "Will you help me in wealth? What Allah has given me is better than that which He has given you! Nay, you rejoice in your gift! (27:36). "Go back to them. We verily, shall come to them with armies that they cannot resist, and we shall drive them out from there in disgrace, and they will be abased (27:37).The Gift and the Response of SulaymanMore than one of the scholars of Tafsir among the Salaf and others stated that she sent him a huge gift of gold, jewels, pearls and other…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Return to them, for we will surely come to them with soldiers that they will be powerless to encounter, and we will surely expel them therefrom in humiliation, and they will be debased." See 27:36

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Sulayman) said, "O assembly (of jinn), which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?" He said: O chiefs! Which of you can bring me her throne before they come to me surrendering themselves in obedience (as Muslims)? (27:38). An 'Ifrit from the Jinn said: "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place. And verily, I am indeed strong and trustworthy for such work (27:39). One with whom was knowledge of the Scripture, said: "I will bring it to you within the twinkling of an eye!" Then when he saw it placed before him, he said: "This is by the grace of my Lord – to test me whether I am grateful or ungrateful! And whoever is grateful, truly, his gratitude is for himself; and whoever is ungrateful, certainly my…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: A powerful one from among the jinn said, "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed, I am for this (task) strong and trustworthy." See 27:38

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have made pleasing to them their deeds, so they wander blindly. See 27:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Said one who had knowledge from the Scripture, "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." And when (Sulayman) saw it placed before him, he said, "This is from the favor of my Lord to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful - his gratitude is only for (the benefit of) himself. And whoever is ungrateful - then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous." See 27:38

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Disguise for her her throne; we will see whether she will be guided (to truth) or will be of those who is not guided." He said: Disguise her throne for her that we may see whether she will be guided, or she will be one of those not guided (27:41). So when she came, it was said, "Is your throne like this" She said: "As though it were the very same." And he said, "Knowledge was bestowed on us before her, and we had submitted to Allah (as Muslims) (27:42). And Saddaha that which she used to worship besides Allah has prevented her (from Islam), for she was of a disbelieving people (27:43). It was said to her: "Enter As-Şarḥ," but when she saw it, she thought it was a pool, and she (tucked up her clothes) uncovering…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So when she arrived, it was said (to her), "Is your throne like this?" She said, "(It is) as though it was it." (Sulayman said), "And we were given knowledge before her, and we have been Muslims (in submission to Allah). See 27:41

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that which she was worshipping other than Allah had averted her (from submission to Him). Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people." See 27:41

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: She was told, "Enter the palace." But when she saw it, she thought it was a body of water1 and uncovered her shins (to wade through). He said, "Indeed, it is a palace (whose floor is) made smooth with glass." She said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds." See 27:41

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We had certainly sent to Thamūd their brother Ṣāliḥ, (saying), "Worship Allah," and at once they were two parties conflicting. And indeed We sent to Thamud their brother Salih, (saying): "Worship Allah." Then look! They became two parties quarreling with each other (27:45). He said: "O my people! Why do you seek to hasten the evil before the good Why seek you not the forgiveness of Allah, that you may receive mercy? (27:46). They said: "We augur an omen from you and those with you." He said: "Your omen is of Allah; nay, but you are a people that are being tested (27:47).Salih and ThamudAllah tells us about Thamud and how they responded to their Prophet Salih, when Allah sent him to call them to worship Allah alone, with no partner or associate.فَإِذَا هُمْ فَرِيقَانِ يَخْتَصِمُونَThen look! They became…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "O my people, why are you impatient for evil before (i.e., instead of) good?1 Why do you not seek forgiveness of Allah that you may receive mercy?" See 27:45

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "We consider you a bad omen, you and those with you." He said, "Your omen (i.e., fate) is with Allah. Rather, you are a people being tested."1 See 27:45

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And there were in the city nine family heads causing corruption in the land and not amending (its affairs). And there were in the city nine Rahtin, who made mischief in the land, and would not reform (27:48). They said: Swear one to another by Allah that we shall make a secret night attack on him and his household, and thereafter we will surely say to his near relatives: 'We witnessed not the destruction of his household, and verily, we are telling the truth.' (27:49). So, they plotted a plot, and We planned a plan, while they perceived not (27:50). Then see how was the end of their plot! Verily, We destroyed them and their nation all together (27:51). These are their houses in utter ruin, for they did wrong. Verily, in this is indeed an Ayah for people who…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Take a mutual oath by Allah that we will kill him by night, he and his family. Then we will say to his executor,1 'We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed, we are truthful.'" See 27:48

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those are the ones for whom there will be the worst of punishment, and in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers. See 27:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, while they perceived not. See 27:48

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then look how was the outcome of their plan - that We destroyed them and their people, all. See 27:48

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So those are their houses, desolate because of the wrong they had done. Indeed in that is a sign for people who know. See 27:48

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah. See 27:48

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) Lut, when he said to his people, "Do you commit immorality1 while you are seeing?2 And (remember) Lut! When he said to his people: Do you commit immoral sins while you see? (27:54). "Do you practice your lusts on men instead of women? Nay, but you are a people who behave senselessly (27:55). There was no other answer given by his people except that they said: "Drive out the family of Lut from your city. Verily, these are men who want to be clean and pure! (27:56). So, We saved him and his family, except his wife. We destined her to be of those who remained behind (27:57). And We rained down on them a rain. So, evil was the rain of those who were warned (27:58).Lut and His PeopleAllah tells us about His servant and Messenger Lut…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Do you indeed approach men with desire instead of women? Rather, you are a people behaving ignorantly." See 27:54

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But the answer of his people was not except that they said, "Expel the family of Lut from your city. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure." See 27:54

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So We saved him and his family, except for his wife; We destined her to be of those who remained behind. See 27:54

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We rained upon them a rain (of stones), and evil was the rain of those who were warned. See 27:54

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, (O Muḥammad), "Praise be to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen. Is Allah better or what they associate with Him?" Say : Praise and thanks be to Allah, and peace be on His servants whom He has chosen! Is Allah better, or what they ascribe as partners? (27:59). Is not He Who created the heavens and the earth, and sends down for you water from the sky, whereby We cause to grow wonderful gardens full of beauty and delight? It is not in your ability to cause the growth of their trees. Is there any god with Allah? Nay, but they are a people who ascribe equals (27:60).The Command to Praise Allah and Send Blessings on His MessengersAllah commands His Messenger SAW to say:الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِPraise and thanks be to Allah,Meaning: for His innumerable blessings upon…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, (O Muḥammad), you receive the Qur’ān from one Wise and Knowing. See 27:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (More precisely), is He (not best) who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you rain from the sky, causing to grow thereby gardens of joyful beauty which you could not (otherwise) have grown the trees thereof? Is there a deity with Allah?1 (No), but they are a people who ascribe equals (to Him). See 27:59

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Is He (not best) who made the earth a stable ground and placed within it rivers and made for it firmly set mountains and placed between the two seas a barrier? Is there a deity with Allah? (No), but most of them do not know. Is not He Who has made the earth as a fixed abode, and has placed rivers in its midst, and has placed firm mountains therein, and has set a barrier between the two seas (of salt and sweet water)? Is there any ilah (god) with Allah? Nay, but most of them know not (27:61).Allah says:أَمَّنْ جَعَلَ الْأَرْضَ قَرَارًاIs not He Who has made the earth as a fixed abode,Meaning: stable and stationary, so that it does not move or convulse, because if it were to do so, it would not be a good place for…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Is He (not best) who responds to the desperate one when he calls upon Him and removes evil and makes you inheritors of the earth?1 Is there a deity with Allah? Little do you remember. Is not He Who responds to the distressed one, when he calls on Him, and Who removes the evil, and makes you inheritors of the earth, generations after generations? Is there any god with Allah? Little is that you remember (27:62).Allah points out that He is the One upon Whom people call in times of difficulty, and He is the One to Whom they turn when calamity strikes, as He says elsewhere:وَإِذَا مَسَّكُمُ الضُّرُّ فِي الْبَحْرِ ضَلَّ مَنْ تَدْعُونَ إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ ۖAnd when harm touches you upon the sea, those that you call upon vanish from you except Him (17:67)ثُمَّ إِذَا مَسَّكُمُ الضُّرُّ فَإِلَيْهِ تَجْأَرُونَThen,…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Is He (not best) who guides you through the darknesses of the land and sea and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy? Is there a deity with Allah? High is Allah above whatever they associate with Him. Is not He Who guides you in the darkness of the land and the sea, and Who sends the winds as heralds of glad tidings, going before His mercy? Is there any god with Allah? Exalted be Allah above all that they associate as partners!) Allah say (27:63).أَمَّنْ يَهْدِيكُمْ فِي ظُلُمَاتِ الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِIs not He Who guides you in the darkness of the land and the sea,Meaning: by means of what He has created of heavenly and earthly signposts. This is like the Ayah:وَعَلَامَاتٍ ۚ وَبِالنَّجْمِ هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَAnd landmarks and by the stars, they guide themselves. (16:16)وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Is He (not best) who begins creation and then repeats it and who provides for you from the heaven and earth? Is there a deity with Allah? Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful." Is not He Who originates creation, and shall thereafter repeat it, and Who provides for you from heaven and earth? Is there any god with Allah? Say: Bring forth your proofs, if you are truthful (27:64). He is the One Who, by His might and power, originates creation and then repeats it. This is like the Ayat:إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ - إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُVerily, the punishment of your Lord is severe and painful. Verily, He it is Who begins and repeats. (85:12-13)وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ ۚAnd He it is Who originates the creation, then He will repeat it;…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except Allah, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected." Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the Unseen except Allah, nor can they perceive when they shall be resurrected (27:65). Nay, their knowledge will perceive that in the Hereafter. Nay, they are in doubt about it. Nay, they are in complete blindness about it (27:66).The One Who Knows the Unseen is AllahAllah commands His Messenger SAW to inform all of creation that no one among the dwellers of heaven and earth knows the Unseen, except Allah.إِلَّا اللَّهُexcept AllahThis is an absolute exception, meaning that no one knows this besides Allah, He is alone in that regard, having no partner in that knowledge. This is like the Ayat:وَعِنْدَهُ مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا هُوَ ۚAnd with…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Rather, their knowledge is arrested concerning the Hereafter. Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are, concerning it, blind. See 27:65

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who disbelieve say, "When we have become dust as well as our forefathers, will we indeed be brought out (of the graves)? And those who disbelieve say: When we have become dust – we and our fathers – shall we really be brought forth? (27:67). "Indeed we were promised this – we and our forefathers before, verily, these are nothing but tales of ancients (27:68). Say to them: "Travel in the land and see how has been the end of the criminals (27:69). And grieve you not over them, nor be straitened (in distress) because of what they plot (27:70).Scepticism about the Resurrection and Its RefutationAllah tells us about the idolators who deny the Resurrection, considering it extremely unlikely that bodies will be re-created after they have become bones and dust. Then He says:لَقَدْ وُعِدْنَا هَٰذَا نَحْنُ وَآبَاؤُنَا…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: We have been promised this, we and our forefathers, before. This is not but legends of the former peoples." See 27:67

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, (O Muḥammad), "Proceed (i.e., travel) through the land and observe how was the end of the criminals." See 27:67

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Mention) when Musa said to his family, "Indeed, I have perceived a fire. I will bring you from there information or will bring you a burning torch that you may warm yourselves." (Remember) when Musa said to his household: Verily, I have seen a fire; I will bring you from there some information, or I will bring you a burning ember, that you may warm yourselves (27:7). But when he came to it, he was called: "Blessed is whosoever is in the fire, and whosoever is round about it! And glorified be Allah, the Lord of all that exists (27:8). "O Musa! Verily, it is I, Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise (27:9). "And throw down your stick!" But when he saw it moving as if it were a snake, he turned in flight, and did not look back. (It was…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:70 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And grieve not over them or be in distress from what they conspire. See 27:67

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they say, "When is (the fulfillment of) this promise, if you should be truthful?" And they say: "When this promise, if you are truthful? (27:71). Say: "Perhaps that which you wish to hasten on, may be close behind you (27:72). Verily, your Lord is full of grace for mankind, yet most of them do not give thanks (27:73). And verily, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they reveal (27:74). And there is nothing hidden in the heaven and the earth but it is in a Clear Book (27:75).Allah tells us about how the idolators asked about the Day of Resurrection, but thought it unlikely that it would ever come to pass.وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا الْوَعْدُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَAnd they say: "When (will) this promise (be fulfilled), if you are truthful?"Allah said, responding to them:قُلْSay'O Muhammad,'عَسَىٰ أَنْ يَكُونَ…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:72 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Perhaps it is close behind you (i.e., very near) - some of that for which you are impatient. See 27:71

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:73 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, your Lord is the possessor of bounty for the people, but most of them are not grateful." See 27:71

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare. See 27:71

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And there is nothing concealed1 within the heaven and the earth except that it is in a clear Register.2 See 27:71

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:76 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, this Qur’ān relates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they disagree. Verily, this Qur'an narrates to the Children of Israel most of that in which they differ (27:76). And truly, it is a guide and a mercy for the believers (27:77). Verily, your Lord will decide between them by His judgement. And He is the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing (27:78). So, put your trust in Allah; surely, you are on manifest truth (27:79). Verily, you cannot make the dead to hear nor can you make the deaf to hear the call, when they flee, turning their backs (27:80). Nor can you lead the blind out of their error. You can only make to hear those who believe in Our Ayat, so they submit (became Muslims) (27:81).The Qur'an Tells the Story of the Differences among the Children…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:77 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, it is guidance and mercy for the believers. See 27:76

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:78 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them by His (wise) judgement. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. See 27:76

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:79 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So rely upon Allah; indeed, you are upon the clear truth. See 27:76

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But when he came to it, he was called, "Blessed is whoever is at the fire and whoever is around it. And exalted is Allah, Lord of the worlds. See 27:7

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:80 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, you will not make the dead hear, nor will you make the deaf hear the call when they have turned their backs retreating. See 27:76

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:81 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you cannot guide the blind away from their error. You will only make hear those who believe in Our verses so they are Muslims (i.e., submitting to Allah). See 27:76

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:82 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when the word (i.e., decree) befalls them,1 We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them, (saying) that the people were, of Our verses, not certain (in faith). And when the Word is fulfilled against them, We shall bring out from the earth a beast for them, to speak to them because mankind believed not with certainty in Our Ayat (27:82).The Emergence Of the Beast Of the EarthThis is the beast which will emerge at the end of time, when mankind has become corrupt and neglected the commands of Allah and changed the true religion. Then Allah will cause a beast to emerge from the earth. It was said that it will be brought from Makkah, or from somewhere else, as we shall discuss in detail below, if Allah wills. The beast will speak…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:83 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (warn of) the Day when We will gather from every nation a company of those who deny Our signs, and they will be (driven) in rows. And (remember) the Day when We shall gather out of every nation a Fawj of those who denied Our Ayat, and they shall be driven (27:83). Till, when they come, He will say: Did you deny My Ayat whereas you comprehended them not by knowledge, or what was it that you used to do? (27:84). And the Word will be fulfilled against them, because they have done wrong, and they will be unable to speak (27:85). See they not that We have made the night for them to rest therein, and the day sight-giving? Verily, in this are Ayat for the people who believe (27:86).Gathering the Wrongdoers on the Day of ResurrectionAllah tells…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:84 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Until, when they arrive (at the place of Judgement), He will say, "Did you deny My signs while you encompassed them not in knowledge, or what (was it that) you were doing?" See 27:83

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:85 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the decree will befall them1 for the wrong they did, and they will not (be able to) speak. See 27:83

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:86 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Do they not see that We made the night that they may rest therein and the day giving sight? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe. See 27:83

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:87 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (warn of) the Day the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified except whom Allah wills. And all will come to Him humbled. And (remember) the Day on which the Trumpet (Şūr) will be blown – and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth, will be terrified except him whom Allah wills. And all shall come to Him, humbled (27:87). And you will see the mountains and think them solid, but they shall pass away as the passing away of the clouds. The work of Allah, Who perfected all things, verily, He is well-acquainted with what you do (27:88). Whoever brings a good deed, will have better than its worth; and they will be safe from the terror on that Day…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:88 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you see the mountains, thinking them motionless,1 while they will pass as the passing of clouds. (It is) the work of Allah, who perfected all things. Indeed, He is Aware of that which you do. See 27:87

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:89 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Whoever comes (at Judgement) with a good deed will have better than it, and they, from the terror of that Day, will be safe. See 27:87

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O Musa, indeed it is I - Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise." See 27:7

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:90 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever comes with an evil deed1 - their faces will be overturned into the Fire, (and it will be said), "Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?" See 27:87

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:91 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Say, O Muḥammad), "I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city,1 who made it sacred and to whom (belongs) all things. And I am commanded to be of the Muslims (i.e., those who submit to Allah). I have been commanded only to worship the Lord of this city, Who has sanctified it and to Whom belongs everything. And I am commanded to be from among the Muslims (27:91). And that I should recite the Qur'an, then whosoever receives guidance, receives it for the good of himself; and whosoever goes astray, say (to him): "I am only one of the warners (27:92). And say: "All the praises and thanks be to Allah. He will show you His Ayat, and you shall recognize them. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do (27:93).The Command to Worship…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:92 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to recite the Qur’ān." And whoever is guided is only guided for (the benefit of) himself; and whoever strays - say, "I am only (one) of the warners." See 27:91

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:93 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And say, "(All) praise is (due) to Allah. He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do." See 27:91

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nasr:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest.1 إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالْفَتْحُWhen there comes the help of Allah and the Conquest.was revealed, the Messenger of Allah SAW said:نُعِيَتْ إِلَيَّ نَفْسِيMy death has been announced to me.And indeed he died during that year." Ahmad was alone in recording this Hadith. Al-Bukhari recorded that Aisha said, "The Messenger of Allah SAW used to say often in his bowing and prostrating:سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَا وَبِحَمْدِكَ اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِيGlory to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me.He did this as his interpretation of the Qur'an (i.e., showing its implementation)." The rest of the group has also recorded this Hadith except for At-Tirmidhi. Imam Ahmad recorded from Masruq that Aisha said, "The Messenger of Allah SAW used to often say towards the end of his life:سُبْحَانَ…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nasr:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes. See 110:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nasr:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then exalt (Him) with praise of your Lord and ask forgiveness of Him. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of Repentance.1 See 110:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom1 you ask one another,2 and the wombs.3 Indeed Allah is ever,4 over you, an Observer.5

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who devour the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming into their bellies fire. And they will be burned in a Blaze (i.e., Hellfire). See 4:7

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:100 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever emigrates for the cause of Allah will find on the earth many (alternative) locations and abundance. And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger and then death overtakes him - his reward has already become incumbent upon Allah. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful. See 4:97

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:101 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer,1 (especially) if you fear that those who disbelieve may disrupt (or attack) you.2 Indeed, the disbelievers are ever to you a clear enemy. And when you Darabtum in the land, there is no sin on you if you shorten the Salah if you fear that the disbelievers may put you in trial, verily, the disbelievers are ever unto you open enemies (4:101).Salat Al-Qasr, Shortening the PrayerAllah said:وَإِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِAnd when you Darabtum in the land,meaning if you travel in the land. In another Ayah, Allah said:عَلِمَ أَن سَيَكُونُ مِنكُم مَّرْضَىٰ وَآخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ اللَّهِHe knows that there will be some among you sick, others Yadribuna (traveling) through the land, seeking of Allah's bounty... (73:20)Allah's statement:فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:102 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when you (i.e., the commander of an army) are among them and lead them in prayer,1 let a group of them stand (in prayer) with you and let them carry their arms. And when they have prostrated, let them be (in position) behind you and have the other group come forward which has not (yet) prayed and let them pray with you, taking precaution and carrying their arms. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and your baggage so they could come down upon you in one (single) attack. But there is no blame upon you, if you are troubled by rain or are ill, for putting down your arms, but take precaution. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment. When you (O Messenger Muhammad SAW) are among them, and lead them in…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:103 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, or (lying) on your sides. But when you become secure, re-establish (regular) prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times. When you have finished the Salah, remember Allah standing, sitting down, and on your sides, but when you are free from danger, perform the Salah. Verily, Salah is kitaban on the believers at fixed hours (4:103). And don't be weak in the pursuit of the enemy; if you are suffering (hardships) then surely they (too) are suffering (hardships) as you are suffering, but you have a hope from Allah (for the reward, i.e. Paradise) that for which they hope not; and Allah is Ever All-Knowing, All-Wise (4:104).The Order for Ample Remembrance After the Fear PrayerAllah commands Dhikr after finishing the Fear prayer, in…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:104 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you should be suffering - so are they suffering as you are suffering, but you expect from Allah that which they expect not. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise. See 4:103

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:105 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We have revealed to you, (O Muḥammad), the Book in truth so you may judge between the people by that which Allah has shown you. And do not be for the deceitful an advocate. Surely, We have sent down to you (O Muhammad SAW) the Book in truth that you might judge between men by that which Allah has shown you, so be not a pleader for the treacherous (4:105). And seek the forgiveness of Allah, certainly, Allah is Ever Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful (4:106). And argue not on behalf of those who deceive themselves. Verily, Allah does not like anyone who is a betrayer, sinner (4:107). They may hide (their crimes) from men, but they cannot hide (them) from Allah; for He is with them (by His knowledge), when they plot by night in words that He does not…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:106 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful. See 4:105

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:107 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves. Indeed, Allah loves not one who is a habitually sinful deceiver. See 4:105

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:108 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They conceal (their evil intentions and deeds) from the people, but they cannot conceal (them) from Allah, and He is with them (in His knowledge) when they spend the night in such as He does not accept of speech. And ever is Allah, of what they do, encompassing. See 4:105

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:109 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Here you are - those who argue on their behalf in (this) worldly life - but who will argue with Allah for them on the Day of Resurrection, or who will (then) be their representative? See 4:105

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah instructs you concerning your children (i.e., their portions of inheritance): for the male, what is equal to the share of two females. But if there are (only) daughters, two or more, for them is two thirds of one's estate.1 And if there is only one, for her is half. And for one's parents, to each one of them is a sixth of his estate if he left children. But if he had no children and the parents (alone) inherit from him, then for his mother is one third. And if he had brothers (and/or sisters), for his mother is a sixth,2 after any bequest he (may have) made or debt.3 Your parents or your children - you know not which of them are nearest to you in benefit. (These shares are) an obligation (imposed) by Allah. Indeed, Allah is…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:110 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever does a wrong or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful. And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but afterwards seeks Allah's forgiveness, he will find Allah Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.) 111. And whoever earns sin, he earns it only against himself. And Allah is Ever All-Knowing, All-Wise (4:110). And whoever earns a fault or a sin and then blames it on someone innocent, he has indeed burdened himself with falsehood and a manifest sin (4:111). Had not the grace of Allah and His mercy been upon you, a party of them would certainly have made a decision to mislead you, but they mislead none except their own selves, and no harm can they do to you in the least. Allah has sent down to you the Book, and the Hikmah, and…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:111 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever earns (i.e., commits) a sin only earns it against himself. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise. See 4:110

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:112 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But whoever earns an offense or a sin and then blames it on an innocent (person) has taken upon himself a slander and manifest sin. See 4:110

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:113 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if it was not for the favor of Allah upon you, (O Muḥammad), and His mercy, a group of them would have determined to mislead you. But they do not mislead except themselves, and they will not harm you at all. And Allah has revealed to you the Book and wisdom and has taught you that which you did not know. And ever has the favor of Allah upon you been great. See 4:110

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:114 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: No good is there in much of their private conversation, except for those who enjoin charity or that which is right or conciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking means to the approval of Allah - then We are going to give him a great reward. There is no good in most of their secret talks save (in) him who orders Sadaqah, or goodness, or conciliation between mankind; and he who does this, seeking the good pleasure of Allah, We shall give him a great rewar (4:114). And whoever contradicts and opposes the Messenger after the right path has been shown clearly to him, and follows other than the believers' way, We shall keep him in the path he has chosen, and burn him in Hell what an evil destination (4:115).Righteous Najwa, Secret TalkAllah said:لَّا خَيْرَ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِّن…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:115 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken1 and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination. See 4:114

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:116 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray. Verily, Allah forgives not (the sin of) setting up partners (in worship) with Him, but He forgives whom He wills, sins other than that, and whoever sets up partners in worship with Allah, has indeed strayed far away (4:116). They invoke nothing but female deities besides Him (Allah), and they invoke nothing but Shaytan, a persistent rebel (4:117). Allah cursed him. And he (Shaytan) said: I will take an appointed portion of your servants (4:118). "Verily, I will mislead them, and surely, I will arouse in them false desires; and certainly, I will order them to slit the ears of cattle, and indeed I will order them to…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:117 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They call upon instead of Him none but female (deities), and they (actually) call upon none but a rebellious Satan. See 4:116

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:118 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Whom Allah has cursed. For he had said, "I will surely take from among Your servants a specific portion. See 4:116

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:119 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And I will mislead them, and I will arouse in them (sinful) desires, and I will command them so they will slit the ears of cattle, and I will command them so they will change the creation of Allah." And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly sustained a clear loss. See 4:116

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And for you is half of what your wives leave if they have no child. But if they have a child, for you is one fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they (may have) made or debt. And for them (i.e., the wives) is one fourth if you leave no child. But if you leave a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you (may have) made or debt. And if a man or woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants but has a brother or a sister, then for each one of them is a sixth. But if they are more than two, they share a third,1 after any bequest which was made or debt, as long as there is no detriment (caused).2 (This is) an ordinance from Allah, and Allah…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:120 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He (i.e., Satan) promises them and arouses desire in them. But Satan does not promise them except delusion. See 4:116

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:121 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The refuge of those will be Hell, and they will not find from it an escape. See 4:116

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:122 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But the ones who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. (It is) the promise of Allah, (which is) truth, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement. See 4:116

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:123 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It (i.e., Paradise) is not (obtained) by your wishful thinking nor by that of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does a wrong will be recompensed for it, and he will not find besides Allah a protector or a helper. It will not be in accordance with your desires, nor those of the People of the Scripture, whosoever works evil, will have the recompense thereof, and he will not find any protector or helper besides Allah (4:123). And whoever does righteous good deeds, male or female, and is a believer, such will enter Paradise and not the least injustice, even to the size of a Naqir, will be done to them (4:124). And who can be better in religion than one who submits his face (himself) to Allah; and he is a Muhsin (a doer of good). And follows the…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:124 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, (even as much as) the speck on a date seed. See 4:123

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:125 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Ibrahim, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Ibrahim as an intimate friend. See 4:123

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:126 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And ever is Allah, of all things, encompassing. See 4:123

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:127 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they request from you, (O Muḥammad), a (legal) ruling concerning women. Say, "Allah gives you a ruling about them and (about) what has been recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan girls to whom you do not give what is decreed for them1 - and (yet) you desire to marry them - and concerning the oppressed among children and that you maintain for orphans (their rights) in justice." And whatever you do of good - indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of it. They ask your legal instruction concerning women. Say: Allah instructs you about them, and about what is recited unto you in the Book concerning the orphan girls whom you give not what they deserve and yet whom you desire to marry, and the children who are weak and oppressed, and that you stand firm for…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:128 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion, there is no sin upon them if they make terms of settlement between them - and settlement is best. And present in (human) souls is stinginess.1 But if you do good and fear Allah - then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Aware. And if a woman fears cruelty or desertion on her husband's part, there is no sin on them both if they make terms of peace between themselves; and making peace is better. And human souls are swayed by greed. But if you do good and have Taqwa, verily, Allah is Ever Well-Acquainted with what you do (4:128). You will never be able to do perfect justice between wives even if it is your ardent desire, so do not incline too much to one of…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:129 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And you will never be able to be equal (in feeling) between wives, even if you should strive (to do so). So do not incline completely (toward one) and leave another hanging.1 And if you amend (your affairs) and fear Allah - then indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful. See 4:128

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: These are the limits (set by) Allah, and whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be admitted by Him to gardens (in Paradise) under which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein; and that is the great attainment. These are the limits (set by) Allah, and whosoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, will be admitted to Gardens under which rivers flow (in Paradise), to abide therein, and is the great success (4:13). And whosoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, and transgresses His (set) limits, He will cast him into the Fire, to abide therein; and he shall suffer a disgraceful torment (4:14).Warning Against Transgressing the Limits for InheritanceMeaning, the Fara'id are Allah's set limits. This includes what Allah has alloted for the heirs, according to the degree of relation they have to the deceased, and their degree of dependency on him. Therefore,…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:130 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But if they separate (by divorce), Allah will enrich each (of them) from His abundance. And ever is Allah Encompassing and Wise. See 4:128

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:131 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We have instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and yourselves to fear Allah. But if you disbelieve - then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy. And to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth. And verily, We have recommended to the People of the Scripture before you, and to you that you have Taqwa of Allah. But if you disbelieve, then unto Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth, and Allah is Ever Rich (free of any needs), Worthy of all praise (4:131). And to Allah belongs all…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:132 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.1 See 4:131

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:133 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: If He wills, He can do away with you, O people, and bring others (in your place). And ever is Allah competent to do that. See 4:131

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:134 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Whoever desires the reward of this world - then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing. See 4:131

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:135 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both.1 So follow not (personal) inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort (your testimony) or refuse (to give it), then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Aware. O you who believe! Stand out firmly for justice, as witnesses to Allah, even though it be against yourselves, or your parents, or your kin, be he rich or poor, Allah is a better Protector to both. So follow not the lusts, lest you may avoid justice; and if you 'Talwū' or 'Tu'ridū', it, verily, Allah is Ever Well-Acquainted with what you do (4:135).Commanding Justice and Conveying the Witness for AllahAllah commands His…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:136 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, believe1 in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that He sent down upon His Messenger and the Scripture which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray. O you who believe! Believe in Allah, and His Messenger, and the Book (the Qur'an) which He has sent down to His Messenger, and the Scripture which He sent down to those before; and whosoever disbelieves in Allah, His Angels, His Books, His Messengers, and the Last Day, then indeed he has strayed far away (4:136).The Order to Have Faith after BelievingAllah commands His faithful servants to adhere to all the elements of faith, its branches, pillars and cornerstones. This is not stated as mere redundancy, but from the view of…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:137 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, those who have believed then disbelieved, then believed then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief - never will Allah forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way. Verily, those who believe, then disbelieve, then believe (again), and (again) disbelieve, and go on increasing in disbelief; Allah will not forgive them, nor guide them on the (right) way (4:137). Give to the hypocrites the tidings that there is for them a painful torment (4:138). Those who take disbelievers for friends instead of believers, do they seek honor with them? Verily, then to Allah belongs all honor (4:139). And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being denied and mocked at, then sit not with them, until they engage in talk other than that; certainly in that case…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:138 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Give tidings to the hypocrites that there is for them a painful punishment. See 4:137

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:139 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those who take disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek with them honor (through power)? But indeed, honor belongs to Allah entirely.1 See 4:137

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits - He will put him into the Fire to abide eternally therein, and he will have a humiliating punishment. See 4:13

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:140 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
