item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And there had already strayed before them most of the former peoples. And indeed most of the earlier ones went astray before them (37:71). And indeed We sent among them warners (37:72). Then see what was the end of those who were warned (37:73). Except the chosen servants of Allah (37:74).Allah tells us that most of the previous nations went astray, worshipping other gods alongside Allah. He states that He sent among them warners to alert them to the anger, wrath and vengeance of Allah towards those who disbelieve in Him and worship others besides Him. He tells us that they persisted in their opposition to their Messengers and their disbelief in them, so He destroyed those who disbelieved in Him and saved the believers and caused them to prevail. Allah says:فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ - إِلَّا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Nuh had certainly called Us, and (We are) the best of responders. And indeed Nuh invoked Us, and We are the best of those who answer (37:75). And We rescued him and his family from the great distress (37:76). And, his progeny, them We made the survivors (37:77). And left for him (a goodly remembrance) among the later generation (37:78). Salam (peace!) be upon Nuh among the all creatures! (37:79). Verily, thus We reward the gooddoers (37:80). Verily, he (Nuh) was one of Our believing servants (37:81). Then We drowned the others (37:82). Nuh and His People When Allah tells us about how most of the early people went astray from the path of salvation, He starts the detailed explanation of that with the story of Nuh and the rejection of his people. Only a few of Nuh's people…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:83 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, among his kind was Ibrahim. And verily, among those who followed his way was Ibrahim (37:83). When he came to his Lord with a Salim heart (37:84). When he said to his father and to his people: What is it that which you worship? (37:85). "Is it a falsehood – gods other than Allah – that you desire? (37:86). "Then what think you about the Lord of the all that exists? (37:87). The Story of Ibrahim and His People Ali bin Abi Talhah reported that Ibn 'Abbas (RA):وَإِنَّ مِنْ شِيعَتِهِ لَإِبْرَاهِيمَAnd verily, among those who followed his ways was Ibrahim.means, he was one of the followers of his religion. Mujahid said, "He was following his path and his way."إِذْ جَاءَ رَبَّهُ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍWhen he came to his Lord with a Salim heart.Ibn 'Abbas (RA), said, "This means that…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:88 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he cast a look at the stars. Then he cast a glance at the stars (37:88). And he said: "Verily, I am sick (37:89). So they turned away from him and departed (37:90). Then he turned to their gods and said: "Will you not eat? (37:91). "What is the matter with you that you speak not? (37:92). Then he turned upon them, striking (them) with (his) right hand (37:93). Then they came hastily towards him (37:94). He said: "Worship you that which you (yourselves) carve? (37:95). "While Allah has created you and what you make! (37:96). They said: "Build for him a building and throw him into the blazing fire! (37:97). So, they plotted a plot against him, but We made them the lowest (37:98).Ibrahim (AS), said this to his people so that he could stay behind in the…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:99 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (then) he said, "Indeed, I will go to (where I am ordered by) my Lord; He will guide me. And he said: Verily, I am going to my Lord. He will guide me (37:99). "My Lord! Grant me (offspring) from the righteous (37:100). So, We gave him the glad tidings of a forbearing boy (37:101). And, when he (his son) was old enough to walk with him, he said: "O my son! I have seen in a dream that I am slaughtering you. So look what you think!" He said: "O my father! Do that which you are commanded, if Allah wills, you shall find me of the patient (37:102). Then, when they had both submitted themselves, and he had laid him prostrate on his forehead (37:103). We called out to him: "O Ibrahim! (37:104). "You have fulfilled the…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah,1 and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الَّذِينَ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّاVerily, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in rows (ranks)"Before Allah's Messenger SAW began the battle against the enemy, he liked to line up his forces in rows; in this Surah, Allah teaches the believers to do the same."He also said that Allah's statement:كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيَانٌ مَرْصُوصٌas if they were a solid structure.means, its parts are firmly connected to each other; in rows for battle. Muqatil bin Hayyan said, "Firmly connected to each other." Ibn 'Abbas commented on the meaning of the Ayah:كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيَانٌ مَرْصُوصٌas if they were a solid structure.by saying, "They are like a firm structure that does not move, because its parts are cemented to each other."

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? O you who believe! Shall I guide you to a trade that will save you from a painful torment (61:10). That you believe in Allah and His Messenger, and that you strive hard and fight in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives, that will be better for you, if you but know (61:11). (If you do so) He will forgive you your sins, and admit you into Gardens under which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in 'Adn (Eternal) Paradise; that is indeed the great success (61:12). And also (He will give you) another (blessing) which you love, help from Allah and a near victory. And give glad tidings to the believers (61:13).The Trade that Saves One…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (It is that) you believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you only knew. See 61:10

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He will forgive for you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great attainment. See 61:10

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (you will obtain) another (favor) that you love - victory from Allah and an imminent conquest; and give good tidings to the believers. See 61:10

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O you who have believed, be supporters of Allah, as when Isa, the son of Maryam, said to the disciples, "Who are my supporters for Allah?" The disciples said, "We are supporters of Allah." And a faction of the Children of Israel believed and a faction disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant. O you who believe! Be you helpers (in the cause) of Allah as said Isa, son of Maryam, to the Hawariyyin (the disciples): "Who are my helpers (in the cause) of Allah?" The Hawariyyun said: "We are Allah's helpers" (i.e., we will strive in His cause!). Then a group of the Children of Israel believed and a group disbelieved. So, We gave power to those who believed against their enemies, and they became the victorious (uppermost) (61:14).Muslims are Always the…

item.description: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? See 61:1

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention, O Muḥammad), when Musa said to his people, "O my people, why do you harm me while you certainly know that I am the messenger of Allah to you?" And when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people. And when Musa said to his people: "O my people! Why do you annoy me while you know certainly that I am the Messenger of Allah to you? So, when they turned away (from the path of Allah), Allah turned their hearts away (from the right path). And Allah guides not the people who are rebellious (61:5). And (remember) when Isa, son of Maryam, said: "O Children of Israel! I am the Messenger of Allah unto you, confirming the Tawrah (which came) before me, and giving glad tidings of a…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) when Isa, the son of Maryam, said, "O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Aḥmad."1 But when he came to them with clear evidences, they said, "This is obvious magic."2 See 61:5

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And who is more unjust than one who invents about Allah untruth while he is being invited to Islām. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. And who does more wrong than the one who invents a lie against Allah, while he is being invited to Islam? And Allah guides not the people who are wrongdoers (61:7). They intend to put out the Light of Allah with their mouths. But Allah will bring His Light to perfection even though the disbelievers hate (it) (61:8). He it is Who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it victorious over all religions even though idolators hate (it) (61:9).The Most Unjust among All PeopleAllah said:وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَىٰ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُوَ يُدْعَىٰ إِلَى الْإِسْلَامِ ۚAnd who does more wrong than the one who invents a…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it. See 61:7

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, although those who associate others with Allah dislike it. See 61:7

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Alif, Lām, Meem.1 تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتَابِ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِThe revelation of the Book in which there is no doubt,means, there is no doubt whatsoever that it has been revealed:مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَfrom the Lord of all that exists.Then Allah tells us about the idolators:أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَاهُ ۚOr say they: "He has fabricated it?": they say, he has fabricated it, i.e., he has made it up by himself.بَلْ هُوَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْمًا مَا أَتَاهُمْ مِنْ نَذِيرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَNay, it is the truth from your Lord, so that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you, in order that they may be guided.means, in order that they may follow the truth.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they say, "When we are lost (i.e., disintegrated) within the earth, will we indeed be (recreated) in a new creation?" Rather, they are, in the meeting with their Lord, disbelievers. And they say: When we are lost in the earth, shall we indeed be created anew?" Nay, but they deny the meeting with their Lord (32:10). Say: "The angel of death, who is set over you, will take your souls. Then you shall be brought to your Lord (32:11). Refutation of Those Who think the Resurrection is unlikely to happen Allah tells us how the idolators thought it unlikely that the resurrection would ever come to pass, and how they said:أَإِذَا ضَلَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِWhen we are lost in the earth,Meaning: 'when our bodies have been scattered and have disintegrated and dispersed in the earth,'أَإِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍshall we indeed…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will take you. Then to your Lord you will be returned." See 32:10

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: If you could but see when the criminals are hanging their heads before their Lord, (saying), "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us (to the world); we will work righteousness. Indeed, we are (now) certain." And if you only could see when the criminals shall hang their heads before their Lord (saying): Our Lord! We have now seen and heard, so send us back that we will do righteous good deeds. Verily, we now believe with certainty (32:12). And if We had willed, surely We would have given every person his guidance, but the Word from Me took effect, that I will fill Hell with Jinn and mankind together (32:13). Then taste because of your forgetting the meeting of this Day of yours. Surely, We too will forget you, so taste you the abiding torment for what…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, but the word1 from Me will come into effect (that) "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together. See 32:12

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So taste (punishment) because you forgot the meeting of this, your Day; indeed, We have (accordingly) forgotten you. And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do." See 32:12

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Only those believe in Our verses who, when they are reminded by them, fall down in prostration and exalt (Allah) with praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant. Only those believe in Our Ayat, who, when they are reminded of them, fall down prostrate, and glorify the praises of their Lord, and they are not proud (32:15). Their sides forsake their beds, to invoke their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend out of what We have bestowed on them (32:16). No person knows what is kept hidden for them of delights of eyes as a reward for what they used to do (32:17).The State of the People of Faith and Their RewardAllah states:إِنَّمَا يُؤْمِنُ بِآيَاتِنَاOnly those believe in Our Ayat,means, who accept them as true:الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُوا بِهَا خَرُّوا سُجَّدًاwho, when they are reminded of them,…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Their sides part (i.e., they arise) from (their) beds; they supplicate their Lord in fear and aspiration, and from what We have provided them, they spend.1 See 32:15

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes (i.e., satisfaction) as reward for what they used to do. See 32:15

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient? They are not equal. Is then he who is a believer like him who is rebellious? Not equal are they (32:18). As for those who believe and do righteous good deeds, for them are Gardens of Abode as an entertainment for what they used to do (32:19). And as for those who rebel, their abode will be the Fire, every time they wish to get away therefrom, they will be put back thereto, and it will be said to them: Taste you the torment of the Fire which you used to deny (32:20). And verily, We will make them taste of the near lighter torment prior to the greater torment, in order that they may return (32:21). And who does more wrong than he who is reminded…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them will be the Gardens of Refuge as accommodation for what they used to do. See 32:18

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (This is) the revelation of the Book about which there is no doubt from the Lord of the worlds. See 32:1

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But as for those who defiantly disobeyed, their refuge is the Fire. Every time they wish to emerge from it, they will be returned to it while it is said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny." See 32:18

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We will surely let them taste the nearer punishment1 short of the greater punishment that perhaps they will return (i.e., repent). See 32:18

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord; then he turns away from them? Indeed We, from the criminals, will take retribution. See 32:18

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We certainly gave Musa the Scripture, so do not be in doubt over his meeting.1 And We made it (i.e., the Torah) guidance for the Children of Israel. And indeed We gave Musa the Scripture. So, be not you in doubt of meeting him. And We made it a guide to the Children of Israel (32:23). And We made from among them, leaders, giving guidance under Our command, when they were patient and used to believe with certainty in Our Ayat (32:24). Verily, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection, concerning that wherein they used to differ (32:25).The Book of Musa and the Leadership of the Children of IsraelAllah tells us that He gave the Book – the Tawrah – to His servant and Messenger Musa (AS).فَلَا تَكُنْ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِنْ لِقَائِهِSo, be not you…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and (when) they were certain of Our signs. See 32:23

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ. See 32:23

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, (as) they walk among their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs; then do they not hear? Is it not a guidance for them: how many generations We have destroyed before them in whose dwellings they do walk about? Verily, therein indeed are signs. Would they not then listen (32:26). Have they not seen how We drive water to the dry land that has no vegetation, and therewith bring forth crops providing food for their cattle and themselves? Will they not then see (32:27).Learning the Lessons of the PastAllah says: will these people who deny the Messengers not learn from the nations who came before them, whom Allah destroyed for their rejection of His Messengers and their opposition to what the Messengers brought them of the straight…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have they not seen that We drive water (in clouds) to barren land and bring forth thereby crops from which their livestock eat and (they) themselves? Then do they not see? See 32:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they say, "When will be this conquest,1 if you should be truthful?" They say: "When will this Fath be, if you are telling the truth? (32:28). Say: "On the Day of Al-Fath, no profit will it be to those who disbelieve if they (then) believe! Nor will they be granted a respite (32:29). So turn aside from them and await, verily, they (too) are awaiting (32:30).How the Disbelievers Sought to Hasten on the Punishment, and what Happened to ThemAllah tells us how the disbelievers sought to hasten on the punishment, and to bring the wrath and vengeance of Allah upon themselves, because they thought this punishment would never happen, and because of their disbelief and stubbornness.وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا الْفَتْحُThey say: "When will this Fath be..."Meaning: 'when will you prevail over us, O Muhammad, since you claim that there will…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, (O Muḥammad), "On the Day of Conquest the belief of those who had disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved." See 32:28

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or do they say, "He invented it"? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, (O Muḥammad), that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you (so) perhaps they will be guided. See 32:1

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So turn away from them and wait. Indeed, they are waiting. See 32:28

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne.1 You have not besides Him any protector or any intercessor; so will you not be reminded? Allah it is He Who has created the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them in six Days. Then He Istawa over the Throne. You have none, besides Him, as a protector or an intercessor. Will you not then remember (32:4). He directs the command from the heavens to the earth; then it will go up to Him, in one Day, the space whereof is a thousand years of your reckoning (32:5). That is He, the All-Knower of the unseen and the seen, the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful (32:6).Allah is the Creator and Controller of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He arranges (each) matter from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count. See 32:4

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. See 32:4

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Who perfected everything which He created and began the creation of man from clay. Who made everything He has created good and He began the creation of man from clay (32:7). Then He made his offspring from semen of despised water (32:8). Then He fashioned him in due proportion, and breathed into him the soul; and He gave you hearing, sight and the sense of deduction. Little is the thanks you give (32:9).The Creation of Man in StagesAllah tells us that He has created everything well and formed everything in a goodly fashion. Malik said, narrating from Zayd bin Aslam:الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ ۖWho made everything He has created goodmeans, "He created everything well and in a goodly fashion." When Allah mentions the creation of the heavens and the earth, He follows that by mentioning the creation of man.…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then He made his posterity out of the extract of a liquid disdained. See 32:7

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then He proportioned him and breathed into him from His (created) soul1 and made for you hearing and vision and hearts (i.e., intellect); little are you grateful. See 32:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By the sun and its brightness. وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دَسَّاهَاAnd indeed he fails who Dassaha.Meaning: to conceal it. This means that he makes it dull, and he disregards it by neglecting to allow it to receive guidance. He treats it in this manner until he performs acts of disobedience and he abandons obedience of Allah.It also could mean that he is indeed successful whose soul Allah purifies, and he has failed whose soul Allah corrupts. This is like what was reported by Al-'Awfi and Ali bin Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas.At-Tabarani recorded that Ibn 'Abbas said, The Messenger of Allah SAW used to stop whenever he recited this Ayah:وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّاهَا - فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَاBy Nafs, and Ma Sawwaha (Who apportioned it). Then He showed it its Fujur and its Taqwa.Then he would say:اللّٰهُمَّ آتِ نَفْسِي تَقْوَاهَا، أَنْتَ وَلِيُّهَا وَمَوْلَاهَا،…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he has failed who instills it (with corruption). See 91:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Thamūd denied (their prophet) by reason of their transgression. Thamud denied through their transgression (91:11). When their most wicked went forth (91:12). But the Messenger of Allah said to them: Be cautious! That is the she-camel of Allah! (Do not harm it) and (bar it not from having) its drink! (91:13). Then they denied him and they killed it. So their Lord destroyed them because of their sin, Fasawwaha (91:14). And He feared not the consequences thereof (91:15). The Rejection of Thamud and Allah's Destruction of Them Allah informs that Thamud rejected their Messenger because of the injustice and transgression they practiced. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah and others. Therefore, this resulted in a rejection in their hearts for the guidance and conviction their Messenger came to them with. إِذِ انبَعَثَ أَشْقَاهَا (When their most wicked went forth.) meaning,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When the most wretched of them was sent forth.1 See 91:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the messenger of Allah (i.e., Ṣāliḥ) said to them, "(Do not harm) the she-camel of Allah or (prevent her from) her drink." See 91:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But they denied him and hamstrung1 her. So their Lord brought down upon them destruction for their sin and made it equal (upon all of them). See 91:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And He does not fear the consequence thereof.1 See 91:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (by) the moon when it follows it. See 91:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (by) the day when it displays it.1 See 91:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (by) the night when it covers (i.e., conceals) it. See 91:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (by) the sky and He who constructed it. See 91:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (by) the earth and He who spread it. See 91:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (by) the soul and He who proportioned it.1 See 91:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And inspired it (with discernment of) its wickedness and its righteousness. See 91:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He has succeeded who purifies it. See 91:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Did We not expand for you, (O Muḥammad), your breast?1 وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَAnd have We not raised high your fame?Mujahid said, "I (Allah) am not remembered except that you are remembered with Me: I bear witness that there is no God worthy of worship except Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."Qatadah said, "Allah raised his fame in this life and in the Hereafter. There is no one who gives a sermon, declares the Testimony of Faith (Shahadah), or prays a prayer (Salah) except that he proclaims it: I bear witness that there is no God worthy of worship except Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."Ease after DifficultyConcerning Allah's saying:فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا - إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًاVerily along with every hardship is relief. Verily along with every hardship is relief.Allah informs that with difficulty…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We removed from you your burden.1 See 94:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Which had weighed upon your back. See 94:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And raised high for you your repute. See 94:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For indeed, with hardship (will be) ease (i.e., relief). See 94:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, with hardship (will be) ease. See 94:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So when you have finished (your duties), then stand up (for worship). See 94:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And to your Lord direct (your) longing. See 94:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Ṭā, Seen, Meem.1 وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُAnd verily your Lord, He is truly the All-Mighty,means, the One Who has power over all things, to subdue and control them:الرَّحِيمُthe Most Merciful.means, towards His creation, for He does not hasten to punish the one who sins, but He gives him time to repent, and if he does not, then He seizes him with a mighty punishment. Abu Al-'Aliyah, Qatadah, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas and Ibn Ishaq said: "He is Almighty in His punishment of those who went against His commands and worshipped others besides Him." Sa'id bin Jubayr said: "He is Most Merciful towards those who repent to Him and turn to Him."

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention) when your Lord called Musa, (saying), "Go to the wrongdoing people. And (remember) when your Lord called Musa (saying): "Go to the people who are wrongdoers (26:10). "The people of Fira'wn. Will they not have Taqwa? (26:11). He said: "My Lord! Verily, I fear that they will deny me, (26:12). "And my breast straitens, and my tongue expresses not well. So send for Harun (26:13). "And they have a charge of crime against me, and I fear they will kill me (26:14). (Allah) said: "Nay! Go you both with Our signs. Verily, We shall be with you, listening (26:15). "And go both of you to Fira'wn, and say: 'We are the Messengers of the Lord of Al-'Alamin, (26:16). 'So allow the Children of Israel to go with us.' (26:17). (Fir'awn) said (to Musa): "Did we not bring you…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:100 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So now we have no intercessors. See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:101 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And not a devoted friend. See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:102 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then if we only had a return (to the world) and could be of the believers..."1 See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:103 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers. See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:104 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:105 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The people of Nuh denied the messengers.1 The people of Nuh denied the Messengers (26:105). When their brother Nuh said to them: Will you not have Taqwa? (26:106). "I am a trustworthy Messenger to you (26:107). "So have Taqwa of Allah, and obey me (26:108). "No reward do I ask of you for it; my reward is only from the Lord of all that exists (26:109). "So have Taqwa of Allah, and obey me (26:110).Nuh's Preaching to His People, and Their ResponseHere Allah tells us about His servant and Messenger Nuh (AS), who was the first Messenger sent by Allah to the people of earth after they started to worship idols. Allah sent him to forbid that and to warn people of the consequences of idol worship. But his people belied him and continued their evil practice of worshipping idols…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:106 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When their brother Nuh said to them, "Will you not fear Allah? See 26:105

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:107 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. See 26:105

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:108 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So fear Allah and obey me. See 26:105

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:109 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds. See 26:105

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The people of Pharaoh. Will they not fear Allah?" See 26:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:110 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So fear Allah and obey me." See 26:105

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:111 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Should we believe you while you are followed by the lowest (class of people)?" They said: Shall we believe in you, when the inferior follow you? (26:111). He said: "And what knowledge have I of what they used to do? (26:112). "Their account is only with my Lord, if you could (but) know (26:113). "And I am not going to drive away the believers (26:114). "I am only a plain warner (26:115).The Demand of the People of Nuh and His ResponseThey said: "We do not believe in you, and we will not follow you and become equal to the meanest of the people, who follow you and believe in you, and they are the lowest among us."قَالُوا أَنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ وَاتَّبَعَكَ الْأَرْذَلُونَ - قَالَ وَمَا عِلْمِي بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَThey said: "Shall we believe in you, when the inferior follow…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:112 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "And what is my knowledge of what they used to do? See 26:111

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:113 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Their account is only upon my Lord, if you (could) perceive. See 26:111

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:114 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And I am not one to drive away the believers. See 26:111

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:115 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: I am only a clear warner." See 26:111

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:116 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "If you do not desist, O Nuh, you will surely be of those who are stoned." They said: If you cease not, O Nuh you will surely be among those stoned (26:116). He said: "My Lord! Verily, my people have denied me (26:117). "Therefore judge You between me and them, and save me and those of the believers who are with me (26:118). And We saved him and those with him in the laden ship (26:119). Then We drowned the rest thereafter (26:120). Verily, in this is indeed a sign, yet most of them are not believers (26:121). And verily your Lord, He is indeed the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful (26:122).His People's Threat, Nuh's Prayer Against Them, and Their DestructionNuh stayed among his people for a long time, calling them to Allah night and day, in secret and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:117 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me. See 26:116

"And when you seize (somebody), seize you (him) as tyrants (26:130). "So have Taqwa of Allah, and obey me (26:131). "And have Taqwa of Him, fear Him Who has aided you with all (good things) that you know (26:132). "He has aided you with cattle and children (26:133). "And gardens and springs…

And verily your Lord, He is indeed the Almighty, the Most Merciful (26:140).The Response of the People of Hud, and Their PunishmentAllah tells us how the people of Hud responded to him after he had warned them, encouraged them, and clearly explained the truth to them.قَالُوا سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْنَا أَوَعَظْتَ أَمْ لَمْ تَكُن مِّنَ الْوَاعِظِينَThey said: "It is the same to us…

item.description: They said, "You are only of those affected by magic. They said: "You are only of those bewitched! (26:153). "You are but a human being like us. Then bring us a sign if you are of the truthful (26:154). He said: "Here is a she-camel: it has a right to drink (water), and you have a right to drink (water) (each) on a day, known (26:155). "And touch her not with harm, lest the torment of a Great Day should seize you (26:156). But they killed her, and then they became regretful (26:157). So, the torment overtook them. Verily, in this is indeed a sign, yet most of them are not believers (26:158). item.description: The people of Lut denied the messengers. The people of Lut denied the Messengers (26:160). When their brother Lut said to them: "Will you not have Taqwa? (26:161). "Verily, I am a trustworthy Messenger to you (26:162). "So, have Taqwa of Allah, and obey me (26:163). "No reward do I ask of you for it; my reward is only from the Lord of all that exits (26:164).Lut and His CallHere Allah tells us about His servant and Messenger Lut (AS). He was Lut bin Haran bin Azar, the nephew of Ibrahim Al-Khalil, upon him be peace. Allah sent him to a mighty nation during the lifetime of Ibrahim (AS). They lived in Sadum (Sodom) and its environs, where Allah destroyed them and turned the area into a putrid, stinking lake, which is well-known in the land of Al-Ghur (the Jordan…

When Shu'ayb said to them: "Will you not have Taqwa? (26:177). "I am a trustworthy Messenger to you (26:178). "So, have Taqwa of Allah, and obey me (26:179). "No reward do I ask of you for it; my reward is only from the Lord of Al-'Alamin (26:180).Shu'ayb and His Preaching to the Dwellers of Al-AykahThe companions of Al-Aykah were the people of Madyan, according to the most correct view. The Prophet of Allah Shu'ayb was one of them, but it does not say here, their brother Shu'ayb, because they called themselves by a name denoting their deification of Al-Aykah, which was a tree which they used to worship; it was said that it was a group of trees which…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:181 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Give full measure and do not be of those who cause loss. "Give full measure, and cause no loss (to others) (26:181). "And weigh with the true and straight balance (26:182). "And defraud not people by reducing their things, nor do evil, making corruption and mischief in the land (26:183). "And have Taqwa of Him Who created you and the generations of the men of old (26:184).The Command to Give Full MeasureAllah commanded them to give full measure, and forbade them to give short measure. He said:أَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ وَلَا تَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُخْسِرِينَGive full measure, and cause no loss.Meaning: 'when you give to people, give them full measure, and do not cause loss to them by giving them short measure, while taking full measure when you are the ones who are taking. Give as you take, and take as you give.'وَزِنُوا…

Indeed that was the torment of a Great Day (26:189). Verily, in this is indeed a sign, yet most of them are not believers (26:190). In the plain Arabic language (26:195).The Qur'an Was Revealed by AllahHere Allah tells us about the Book which He revealed to His servant and Messenger Muhammad SAW.وَإِنَّهُAnd truly, thisrefers to the Qur'an, which at the beginning of the Surah was described as:وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّنَ الرَّحْمَٰنِ مُحْدَثٍand never comes there unto them a Reminder as a recent revelation from the Most Gracious... (26:5)لَتَنزِيلُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَis a revelation from the Lord of Al-'Alamin.means, Allah has sent it down to you and revealed it to you.نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُWhich the trustworthy…

And he had recited it unto them, they would not have believed in it (26:199).The Qur'an Was Mentioned in the Previous ScripturesAllah says: this Qur'an was mentioned and referred to in the previous Scriptures that were left behind by their Prophets who foretold it in ancient times and more recently. Allah took a covenant from them that they would follow it, and the last of them stood and addressed his people with the good news of Ahmad:وَإِذْ قَالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ إِنِّي رَسُولُ…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:200 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Thus have We inserted it (i.e., disbelief) into the hearts of the criminals. Thus have We caused it to enter the hearts of the criminals (26:200). They will not believe in it until they see the painful torment (26:201). It shall come to them of a sudden, while they perceive it not (26:202). Then they will say: Can we be respited? (26:203). Would they then wish for Our torment to be hastened on (26:204). Think, if We do let them enjoy for years (26:205). And afterwards comes to them that which they had been promised (26:206). All that with which they used to enjoy shall not avail them (26:207). And never did We destroy a township but it had its warner (26:208). By way of reminder, and We have never been unjust (26:209).The Deniers Will Never Believe Until They See…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:201 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment. See 26:200

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:202 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it will come to them suddenly while they perceive (it) not. See 26:200

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:203 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they will say, "May we be reprieved?" See 26:200

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:204 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So for Our punishment are they impatient? See 26:200

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:205 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then have you considered if We gave them enjoyment for years. See 26:200

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:206 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And then there came to them that which they were promised? See 26:200

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:207 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They would not be availed by the enjoyment with which they were provided. See 26:200

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:208 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We did not destroy any city except that it had warners. See 26:200

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:209 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: As a reminder; and never have We been unjust. See 26:200

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So I fled from you when I feared you. Then my Lord granted me judgement (i.e., wisdom and prophethood) and appointed me (as one) of the messengers. See 26:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:210 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the devils have not brought it (i.e., the revelation) down.1 And it is not the Shayatin (devils) who have brought it down (26:210). Neither would it suit them nor are they able (26:211). Verily, they have been removed far from hearing it (26:212).The Qur'an Was Brought Down by Jibril, Not ShaytanAllah tells us about His Book, which falsehood cannot approach from before or behind it, sent down by the All-Wise, Worthy of all praise. He states that it has been brought down by the trustworthy Ruh (i.e., Jibril) who is helped by Allah:وَمَا تَنَزَّلَتْ بِهِ الشَّيَاطِينُAnd it is not the Shayatin who have brought it down.Then He tells us that it could not be the case for three reasons that the Shayatin brought it down. One is that it would not suit them, i.e., they have no desire to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:211 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is not allowable for them, nor would they be able. See 26:210

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:212 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed they, from (its) hearing, are removed.1 See 26:210

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:213 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So do not invoke1 with Allah another deity and (thus) be among the punished. So, invoke not with Allah another god lest you should be among those who receive punishment (231)And warn your tribe of near kindred (26:214). And be kind and humble to the believers who follow you (26:215). Then if they disobey you, say: I am innocent of what you do (26:216). And put your trust in the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful (26:217). Who sees you when you stand up (26:218). And your movements among those who fall prostrate (26:219). Verily, He, only He, is the All-Hearer, the All-Knower (26:220).The Command to Warn His Tribe of Near KindredHere Allah commands (His Prophet SAW) to worship Him alone, with no partner or associate, and tells him that whoever associates others in worship with Him, He will punish them. Then…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:214 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And warn, (O Muḥammad), your closest kindred. See 26:213

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:215 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And lower your wing (i.e., show kindness) to those who follow you of the believers. See 26:213

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:216 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if they disobey you, then say, "Indeed, I am disassociated from what you are doing." See 26:213

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:217 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And rely upon the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. See 26:213

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:218 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Who sees you when you arise.1 See 26:213

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:219 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And your movement among those who prostrate.1 See 26:213

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And is this a favor of which you remind me - that you have enslaved the Children of Israel?" See 26:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:220 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing. See 26:213

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:221 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? Shall I inform you upon whom the Shayatin descend (26:221). They descend on every lying, sinful person (Athim) (26:222). Who gives ear, and most of them are liars (26:223). As for the poets, the astray follow them (234)See you not that they speak about every subject in their poetry (26:225). And that they say what they do not do (26:226). Except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and remember Allah much and vindicate themselves after they have been wronged. And those who do wrong will come to know by what overturning they will be overturned (26:227).Refutation of the Fabrications of the IdolatorsHere Allah addresses those idolators who claimed that what was brought by the Messenger SAW was not the truth but was merely something that he had made up by…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:222 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They descend upon every sinful liar. See 26:221

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:223 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They pass on what is heard,1 and most of them are liars. See 26:221

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:224 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the poets - (only) the deviators follow them. See 26:221

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:225 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Do you not see that in every valley they roam.1 See 26:221

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:226 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that they say what they do not do?. See 26:221

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:227 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except those (poets) who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allah often and defend (the Muslims)1 after they were wronged. And those who have wronged are going to know to what (kind of) return they will be returned. See 26:221

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Said Pharaoh, "And what is the Lord of the worlds?" Fir'awn said: "And what is the Lord of Al-'Alamin (26:23). (Musa) said: "The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, if you seek to be convinced with certainty (26:24). (Fir'awn) said to those around: "Do you not hear (what he says)? (26:25). (Musa) said: "Your Lord and the Lord of your ancient fathers! (26:26). (Fir'awn) said: "Verily, your Messenger who has been sent to you is a madman! (26:27). (Musa) said: "Lord of the east and the west, and all that is between them, if you did but understand! (26:28).Allah Tells us about the Disbelief, Rebellion, Oppression and Denial of Fir'awn, As He Says:وَمَا رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ(Fir'awn said:) "And what is the Lord of the 'Alamin"This is because he used to say to his people:مَا…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "The Lord of the heavens and earth and that between them, if you should be convinced." See 26:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Pharaoh) said to those around him, "Do you not hear?" See 26:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "Your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers." See 26:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Pharaoh) said,1 "Indeed, your 'messenger' who has been sent to you is mad." See 26:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "Lord of the east and the west and that between them, if you were to reason." See 26:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Pharaoh) said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely place you among those imprisoned." He said: If you choose a god other than me, I will certainly put you among the prisoners (26:29). He said: "Even if I bring you something manifest? (26:30). He said: "Bring it forth then, if you are of the truthful! (26:31). So he threw his stick, and behold, it was a serpent, manifest (26:32). And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to all beholders (26:33). He said to the chiefs around him: "Verily, this is indeed a well-versed sorcerer (26:34). "He wants to drive you out of your land by his sorcery: what is it then that you command? (26:35). They said: "Put him off and his brother (for a while), and send callers to the cities;…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Perhaps, (O Muḥammad), you would kill yourself with grief that they will not be believers. See 26:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "Even if I brought you something (i.e., proof) manifest?" See 26:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Pharaoh) said, "Then bring it, if you should be of the truthful." See 26:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So (Musa) threw his staff, and suddenly it was a serpent manifest.1 See 26:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he drew out his hand; thereupon it was white for the observers. See 26:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Pharaoh) said to the eminent ones around him, "Indeed, this is a learned magician. See 26:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He wants to drive you out of your land by his magic, so what do you advise?" See 26:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Postpone (the matter of) him and his brother and send among the cities gatherers. See 26:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Who will bring you every learned, skilled magician." See 26:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So the magicians were assembled for the appointment of a well-known day.1 So, the sorcerers were assembled at a fixed time on a day appointed (26:38). And it was said to the people: "Are you (too) going to assemble? (26:39). "That we may follow the sorcerers if they are the winners (26:40). So, when the sorcerers arrived, they said to Fir'awn: "Will there surely be a reward for us if we are the winners? (26:41). He said: "Yes, and you shall then verily be of those brought near (to myself) (26:42). Musa said to them: "Throw what you are going to throw! (26:43). So, they threw their ropes and their sticks, and said: "By the might of Fir'awn, it is we who will certainly win! (26:44). Then Musa threw his stick, and behold, it swallowed up all that they falsely…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it was said to the people, "Will you congregate. See 26:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: If We willed, We could send down to them from the sky a sign for which their necks would remain humbled.1 See 26:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That we might follow the magicians if they are the predominant?" See 26:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when the magicians arrived, they said to Pharaoh, "Is there indeed for us a reward if we are the predominant?" See 26:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Yes, and indeed, you will then be of those near (to me)." See 26:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Musa said to them, "Throw whatever you will throw." See 26:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So they threw their ropes and their staffs and said, "By the might of Pharaoh, indeed it is we who are predominant." See 26:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then Musa threw his staff, and at once it devoured what they falsified. See 26:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So the magicians fell down in prostration (to Allah). See 26:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds. See 26:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Lord of Musa and Harun." See 26:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Pharaoh) said, "You believed him (i.e., Musa) before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic, but you are going to know. I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you all." He said: You have believed in him before I give you leave. Surely, he indeed is your chief, who has taught you magic! So verily, you shall come to know. Verily, I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you all (26:49). They said: "No harm! Surely, to our Lord we are to return (26:50). "Verily, we really hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins, as we are the first of the believers (26:51).Between Fir'awn and the SorcerersHis threats against them resulted…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And no mention (i.e., revelation) comes to them anew from the Most Merciful except that they turn away from it. See 26:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "No harm. Indeed, to our Lord we will return. See 26:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, we aspire that our Lord will forgive us our sins because we were the first of the believers." See 26:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We inspired to Musa, "Travel by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued." And We revealed to Musa, saying: "Depart by night with My servants, verily, you will be pursued (26:52). Then Fir'awn sent callers to (all) the cities (26:53). (Saying): "Verily, these indeed are but a small band (26:54). "And verily, they have done what has enraged us (26:55). "But we are a host all assembled, amply forewarned (26:56). So, We expelled them from gardens and springs (26:57). Treasures, and every kind of honorable place (26:58). Thus and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them (26:59).The Exodus of the Children of Israel From EgyptAfter Musa stayed in Egypt for a long time, and the proof of Allah was established against Fir'awn and his chiefs, yet they were still arrogant and stubborn, then there was…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then Pharaoh sent among the cities gatherers.1 See 26:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (And said), "Indeed, those are but a small band. See 26:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, they are enraging us. See 26:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, we are a cautious society..." See 26:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So We removed them from gardens and springs. See 26:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And treasures and honorable station1. See 26:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Thus. And We caused to inherit it the Children of Israel. See 26:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For they have already denied, but there will come to them the news of that which they used to ridicule. See 26:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So they pursued them at sunrise. So, they pursued them at sunrise (26:60). And when the two hosts saw each other, the companions of Musa said: "We are sure to be overtaken (26:61). (Musa) said: "Nay, verily with me is my Lord. He will guide me (26:62). Then We revealed to Musa (saying): "Strike the sea with your stick." And it parted, and each separate part became like huge mountain (26:63). Then We brought near the others to that place (26:64). And We saved Musa and all those with him (26:65). Then We drowned the others (26:66). Verily, in this is indeed a sign, yet most of them are not believers (26:67). And verily your Lord, He is truly the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful (26:68).Fir'awn's Pursuit and Expulsion of the Children of Israel, and How He and His People Were…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when the two companies saw one another, the companions of Musa said, "Indeed, we are to be overtaken!" See 26:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me." See 26:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then We inspired to Musa, "Strike with your staff the sea," and it parted, and each portion was like a great towering mountain. See 26:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We advanced thereto the others (i.e., the pursuers). See 26:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We saved Musa and those with him, all together. See 26:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then We drowned the others. See 26:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers. See 26:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. See 26:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And recite to them the news of Ibrahim. And recite to them the story of Ibrahim (26:69). When he said to his father and his people: "What do you worship? (26:70). They said: "We worship idols, and to them we are ever devoted (26:71). He said: "Do they hear you when you call? (26:72). "Or do they benefit you or do they cause harm? (26:73). They said: "(Nay) but we found our fathers doing so (26:74). He said: "Do you observe that which you have been worshipping – (26:75). "You and your ancient fathers? (26:76). "Verily, they are enemies to me, save the Lord of Al-'Alamin, (26:77).How the Close Friend of Allah, Ibrahim Spoke out Against ShirkHere Allah tells us about His servant, Messenger and Close Friend, Ibrahim, upon him be peace, the leader of the pure monotheists. Allah commanded…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Did they not look at the earth - how much We have produced therein from every noble kind? See 26:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:70 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?" See 26:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "We worship idols and remain to them devoted." See 26:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:72 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Do they hear you when you supplicate? See 26:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:73 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or do they benefit you, or do they harm?" See 26:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "But we found our fathers doing thus." See 26:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Then do you see what you have been worshipping. See 26:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:76 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: You and your ancient forefathers? See 26:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:77 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds.1 See 26:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:78 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Who created me, and He (it is who) guides me. Who has created me, and it is He Who guides me (26:78). And it is He Who feeds me and gives me to drink (26:79). And when I am ill, it is He Who cures me (26:80). And Who will cause me to die, and then will bring me to life (26:81). And Who, I hope, will forgive me my faults on the Day of Recompense (26:82).Ibrahim Mentions Allah's Kindness Towards HimIbrahim said, I will not worship any but the One Who does these things:الَّذِي خَلَقَنِي فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِWho has created me, and it is He Who guides me.He is the Creator Who has decreed certain things to which He guides His creation, so each person follows the path which is decreed for him. Allah is the One Who guides whomsoever…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:79 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it is He who feeds me and gives me drink. See 26:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers. See 26:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:80 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when I am ill, it is He who cures me. See 26:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:81 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And who will cause me to die and then bring me to life. See 26:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:82 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And who I aspire that He will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense." See 26:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:83 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (And he said), "My Lord, grant me authority and join me with the righteous. My Lord! Bestow Hukm on me, and join me with the righteous (26:83). And grant me an honorable mention in later generations (26:84). And make me one of the inheritors of the Paradise of Delight (26:85). And forgive my father, verily, he is of the erring (26:86). And disgrace me not on the Day when they will be resurrected (26:87). The Day whereon neither wealth nor sons will avail (26:88). Except him who brings to Allah a clean heart (26:89).The Prayer of Ibrahim for Himself and for His FatherHere Ibrahim, upon him be peace, asks his Lord to give him Hukm. Ibn 'Abbas said, "This is knowledge."وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَand join me with the righteous.means, 'make me one of the righteous in this world and the Hereafter.' This…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:84 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And grant me a mention (i.e., reputation) of honor among later generations. See 26:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:85 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And place me among the inheritors of the Garden of Pleasure. See 26:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:86 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And forgive my father. Indeed, he has been of those astray. See 26:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:87 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And do not disgrace me on the Day they are (all) resurrected. See 26:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:88 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Day when there will not benefit (anyone) wealth or children. See 26:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:89 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But only one who comes to Allah with a sound heart." See 26:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. See 26:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:90 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Paradise will be brought near (that Day) to the righteous. And Paradise will be brought near to those who had Taqwa (26:90). And the (Hell) Fire will be placed in full view of the astray (26:91). And it will be said to them: "Where are those that you used to worship (26:92). "Instead of Allah? Can they help you or help themselves? (26:93). Then they will be thrown on their faces into it (the Fire), they and the astray (26:94). And all of the hosts of Iblis together (26:95). They will say while contending therein (26:96). "By Allah, we were truly in a manifest error (26:97). "When we held you as equals with the Lord of all that exists; (26:98). "And none has brought us into error except the criminals (26:99). "Now we have no intercessors, (26:100). "Nor a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:91 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Hellfire will be brought forth for the deviators. See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:92 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it will be said to them, "Where are those you used to worship. See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:93 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Other than Allah? Can they help you or help themselves?" See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:94 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So they will be overturned into it (i.e., Hellfire), they and the deviators. See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:95 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the soldiers of Iblees, all together. See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:96 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will say while they dispute therein. See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:97 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: "By Allah, we were indeed in manifest error. See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:98 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When we equated you with the Lord of the worlds. See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:99 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And no one misguided us except the criminals. See 26:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Ḥā, Meem. وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَAnd as for those who take as protecting friends others besides HimThis refers to the idolators:اللَّهُ حَفِيظٌ عَلَيْهِمْAllah is Hafiz over them.Meaning: He is Witness to their deeds, recording and enumerating them precisely, and He will requite them for them in full.وَمَا أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِوَكِيلٍand you are not a trustee over them.Meaning: 'you are just a warner, and Allah is the Trustee of all affairs.'

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And in anything over which you disagree - its ruling is (to be referred) to Allah. (Say), "That is Allah, my Lord; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back."1 See 42:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (He is) Creator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you from yourselves, mates, and among the cattle, mates; He multiplies you thereby. There is nothing like unto Him,1 and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.2 See 42:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He extends provision for whom He wills and restricts (it). Indeed He is, of all things, Knowing. See 42:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Nuh and that which We have revealed to you, (O Muḥammad), and what We enjoined upon Ibrahim and Musa and Isa - to establish the religion and not be divided therein. Difficult for those who associate others with Allah is that to which you invite them. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back (to Him). He (Allah) has ordained for you the same religion which He ordained for Nuh, and that which We have revealed to you, and that which We ordained for Ibrahim, Musa and Isa saying you should establish religion and make no divisions in it. Intolerable for the idolators is that to which you call them. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills, and guides unto Himself who turns…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And if not for a word1 that preceded from your Lord (postponing the penalty) until a specified time, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, those who were granted inheritance of the Scripture after them are, concerning it, in disquieting doubt. See 42:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So to that (religion of Allah) invite, (O Muḥammad),1 and remain on a right course as you are commanded and do not follow their inclinations but say, "I have believed in what Allah has revealed of scripture (i.e., the Qur’ān), and I have been commanded to do justice among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you your deeds.2 There is no (need for) argument between us and you.3 Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the (final) destination." So unto this then invite (people), and stand firm as you are commanded, and follow not their desires but say: I believe in whatsoever Allah has sent down of the Book and I am commanded to do justice among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us our deeds…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And those who argue concerning Allah after He has been responded to1 - their argument is invalid with their Lord, and upon them is (His) wrath, and for them is a severe punishment. And those who dispute concerning Allah, after it has been accepted, of no use is their dispute before their Lord and on them is wrath, and for them will be a severe torment (42:16). It is Allah Who has sent down the Book in truth, and the Balance. And what can make you know that perhaps the Hour is close at hand (42:17). Those who believe not therein seek to hasten it, while those who believe are fearful of it, and know that it is the very truth. Verily, those who dispute concerning the Hour are certainly in error far away (42:18).A Warning to Those Who Dispute…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is Allah who has sent down the Book in truth and (also) the balance (i.e., justice). And what will make you perceive? Perhaps the Hour is near. See 42:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Those who do not believe in it are impatient for it,1 but those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in extreme error. See 42:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah is Subtle1 with His servants; He gives provision to whom He wills. And He is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might. Allah is very Gracious and Kind to His servants. He gives provisions to whom He wills. And He is the All-Strong, the Almighty (42:19). Whosoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We give him increase in his reward, and whosoever desires the reward of this world, We give him thereof, and he has no portion in the Hereafter (42:20). Or have they partners with Allah who have instituted for them a religion which Allah has not ordained? And had it not been for a decisive Word, the matter would have been judged between them. And verily, for the wrongdoers there is a painful torment (42:21). You will see the wrongdoers fearful of that which they have earned, and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: ʿAyn, Seen, Qāf.1 See 42:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We increase for him in his harvest (i.e., reward). And whoever desires the harvest (i.e., benefits) of this world - We give him thereof, but there is not for him in the Hereafter any share. See 42:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or have they partners (i.e., other deities) who have ordained for them a religion to which Allah has not consented? But if not for the decisive word,1 it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment. See 42:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, and it will (certainly) befall them. And those who have believed and done righteous deeds will be in lush regions of the gardens (in Paradise) having whatever they will in the presence of their Lord. That is what is the great bounty. See 42:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is that of which Allah gives good tidings to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say, (O Muḥammad), "I do not ask you for it (i.e., this message) any payment (but) only good will through (i.e., due to) kinship." And whoever commits a good deed - We will increase for him good therein. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative.1 That is whereof Allah gives glad tidings to His servants who believe and do righteous good deeds. Say: "No reward do I ask of you for this except to be kind to me for my kinship with you." And whoever earns a good righteous deed, We shall give him an increase of good in respect thereof. Verily, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Ready to appreciate (42:23). Or say they: "He has invented a lie against Allah?" If Allah willed,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or do they say, "He has invented about Allah a lie"? But if Allah willed, He could seal over your heart.1 And Allah eliminates falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts. See 42:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds, and He knows what you do. And He it is Who accepts repentance from His servants, and forgives sins, and He knows what you do (42:25). And He answers those who believe and do righteous good deeds, and gives them increase of His bounty. And as for the disbelievers, theirs will be a severe torment (42:26). And if Allah were to extend the provision for His servants, they would surely rebel in the earth, but He sends down by measure as He wills. Verily, He is, in respect of His servants, the Well-Aware, the All-Seer (42:27). And He it is Who sends down the rain after they have despaired, and spreads His mercy. And He is the Wali, Worthy of all praise (42:28).Allah Accepts Repentance and Responds…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And He answers (the supplication of) those who have believed and done righteous deeds and increases (for) them from His bounty. But the disbelievers will have a severe punishment. See 42:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if Allah had extended (excessively) provision for His servants, they would have committed tyranny throughout the earth. But He sends (it) down in an amount which He wills. Indeed He is, of His servants, Aware and Seeing. See 42:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy. See 42:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and earth and what He has dispersed throughout them of creatures. And He, for gathering them when He wills, is competent.
