item.description: When We inspired to your mother what We inspired. See 20:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Saying), 'Cast him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank; there will take him an enemy to Me and an enemy to him.' And I bestowed upon you love from Me1 that you would be brought up under My eye (i.e., observation and care). See 20:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: A revelation from He who created the earth and highest heavens. See 20:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (And We favored you) when your sister went and said, 'Shall I direct you to someone who will be responsible for him?' So We restored you to your mother that she might be content and not grieve. And you killed someone,1 but We saved you from retaliation and tried you with a (severe) trial. And you remained (some) years among the people of Madyan. Then you came (here) at the decreed time, O Musa. "When your sister went and said: 'Shall I show you one who will nurse him' So We restored you to your mother, that she might cool her eyes and she should not grieve. Then you did kill a man, but We saved you from great distress and tried you with a heavy trial.", Then you stayed a number of years with the people of Madyan. Then…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And I produced you for Myself.1 See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Go, you and your brother, with My signs and do not slacken in My remembrance. See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Our Lord, indeed we are afraid that he will hasten (punishment) against us or that he will transgress." Both of them said: Our Lord! Verily, we fear lest he should hasten to punish us or lest he should transgress (20:45). He (Allah) said: "Fear not, verily, I am with you both, hearing and seeing (20:46). "So go you both to him, and say: 'Verily, we are both Messengers of your Lord, so let the Children of Israel go with us, and torment them not; indeed, we have come with a sign from your Lord! And peace will be upon him who follows the guidance! (20:47). 'Truly, it has been revealed to us that the torment will be for him who denies, and turns away.' (20:48).Musa's Fear of Fir'awn and Allah's Strengthening HimAllah, the Exalted, informs that Musa and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Allah) said, "Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see. See 20:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So go to him and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace1 will be upon he who follows the guidance. See 20:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies and turns away.'" See 20:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Pharaoh) said, "So who is the Lord of you two, O Musa?" Fir'awn said: "Who then, O Musa, is the Lord of you two (20:49). (Musa) said: "Our Lord is He Who gave to each thing its form and nature, then guided it aright (20:50). (Fir'awn) said: "What about the generations of old (20:51). Musa said: "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord, in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets (20:52).The Conversation between Musa and Fir'awnAllah, the Exalted, informs about Fir'awn that he said to Musa, in his rejection of the existence of a Supreme Maker and Creator, Who is the God of everything and his own Lord and Owner:فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يَا مُوسَىٰWho then, O Musa, is the Lord of you two?meaning "Who is the one who called you forth and sent you For verily, I do not…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The Most Merciful (who is) above the Throne established.1 See 20:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided (it)." See 20:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Pharaoh) said, "Then what is the case of the former generations?" See 20:49

item.description: (Musa) said, "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets." See 20:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (It is He) who has made for you the earth as a bed (spread out) and inserted therein for you roadways and sent down from the sky, rain and produced thereby categories of various plants. Who has made earth for you like a bed; and has opened ways for you therein, and has sent down water (rain) from the sky. And We have brought forth with it various kinds of vegetation (20:53). Eat and pasture your cattle; verily, in this are Ayat for men of understanding (20:54). Thereof We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you out once again (20:55). And indeed We showed him (Fir'awn) all Our Ayat, but he denied and refused (20:56).The Completion of Musa's Reply to Fir'awnThis is from the completion of Musa's speech concerning the description…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Eat (therefrom) and pasture your livestock. Indeed in that are signs for those of intelligence. See 20:53

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: From it (i.e., the earth) We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will extract you another time. See 20:53

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We certainly showed him (i.e., Pharaoh) Our signs - all of them - but he denied and refused. See 20:53

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Musa? He (Fir'awn) said: Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Musa? (20:57). "Then verily, we can produce magic the like thereof; so appoint a meeting between us and you, which neither we nor you shall fail to keep, in an open place where both shall have a just and equal chance (20:58). (Musa) said: "Your appointed meeting is the day of the festival, and let the people assemble when the sun has risen (forenoon) (20:59).Fir'awn Describes Musa's Proofs As being Magic and Their Agreement to Hold a ContestAllah, the Exalted, informs of what Fir'awn said to Musa when he showed him the great proof. This great sign to Fir'awn was Musa casting down his…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then we will surely bring you magic like it, so make between us and you an appointment, which we will not fail to keep and neither will you, in a place assigned."1 See 20:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "Your appointment is on the day of the festival when the people assemble at mid-morning."1 See 20:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them and what is under the soil. See 20:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So Pharaoh went away, put together his plan, and then came (to Musa). So Fir'awn withdrew, devised his plot and then came back (20:60). Musa said to them: "Woe unto you! Invent not a lie against Allah, lest He should destroy you completely by a torment. And surely, he who invents a lie (against Allah) will fail miserably.") (62 Then they debated one with another what they must do, and they kept their talk secret (61)They said: "Verily, these are two magicians. Their object is to drive you out from your land with magic, and to take you away from your exemplary way. (62)"So devise your plot, and then assemble in line. And whoever overcomes this day will be indeed successful. (63)The Meeting of the Two Parties, Musa's Propagation of the Message and the MagiciansAllah, the Exalted informs that when…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Musa said to them (i.e., the magicians summoned by Pharaoh), "Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allah or He will exterminate you with a punishment; and he has failed who invents (such falsehood)." See 20:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So they disputed over their affair among themselves and concealed their private conversation. See 20:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Indeed, these are two magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and do away with your most exemplary way (i.e., religion or tradition). See 20:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So resolve upon your plan and then come (forward) in line. And he has succeeded today who overcomes." See 20:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "O Musa, either you throw or we will be the first to throw." They said: "O Musa! Either you throw first or we be the first to throw? (20:65). (Musa) said: "Nay, throw you (first)!" Then behold! their ropes and their sticks, by their magic, appeared to him as though they moved fast (20:66). So Musa conceived fear in himself (20:67). We (Allah) said: "Fear not! Surely, you will have the upper hand (20:68). "And throw that which is in your right hand! It will swallow up that which they have made. That which they have made is only a magician's trick, and the magician will never be successful, to whatever amount (of skill) he may attain (20:69). So the magicians fell down prostrate. They said: "We believe in the Lord of Harun and Musa (20:70).The Competition, Musa's…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "Rather, you throw." And suddenly their ropes and staffs seemed to him from their magic that they were moving (like snakes). See 20:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he sensed within himself apprehension, did Musa. See 20:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: We (i.e., Allah) said, "Fear not. Indeed, it is you who are superior. See 20:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have crafted. What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he is." See 20:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if you speak aloud - then indeed, He knows the secret and what is (even) more hidden. See 20:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:70 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So the magicians fell down in prostration.1 They said, "We have believed in the Lord of Harun and Musa." See 20:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Pharaoh) said, "You believed him (i.e., Musa) before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in (giving) punishment and more enduring." (Fir'awn) said: Believe you in him before I give you permission? Verily, he is your chief who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of date palms, and you shall surely know which of us can give the severe and more lasting torment (20:71). They said: "We prefer you not over what have come to us of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:72 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Never will we prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and (over) He who created us.1 So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life. See 20:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:73 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us (to do) of magic. And Allah is better and more enduring."1 See 20:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal - indeed, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live. Verily, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, then surely, for him is Hell, wherein he will neither die nor live (20:74). But whoever comes to Him as a believer, and has done righteous good deeds, for such are the high ranks (20:75). 'Adn Gardens, under which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, and such is the reward of those who purify themselves (20:76).The Magicians Admonish Fir'awnThe clear intent of this is to be a completion of what the magicians admonished Fir'awn with. They warned him of the vengeance of Allah and His eternal and everlasting punishment. They also encouraged him to seek Allah's eternal and endless reward. They said:إِنَّهُ مَن يَأْتِ رَبَّهُ مُجْرِمًاVerily, whoever comes…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds - for those will be the highest degrees (in position). See 20:74

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:76 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And that is the reward of one who purifies himself.1 See 20:74

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:77 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We had inspired to Musa, "Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path through the sea; you will not fear being overtaken (by Pharaoh) nor be afraid (of drowning)." And indeed We revealed to Musa: Travel by night with My servants and strike a dry path for them in the sea, fearing neither to be overtaken nor being afraid (20:77). Then Fir'awn pursued them with his hosts, but the sea (Al-Yamm) completely overwhelmed them and covered them up (20:78). And Fir'awn led his people astray, and he did not guide them (20:79).The Children of Israel Leave EgyptAllah, the Exalted, informs that He commanded Musa to journey at night with the Children of Israel, when Fir'awn refused to release them and send them with Musa. He was to take them away from Fir'awn's captivity. Allah…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:78 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them.1 See 20:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:79 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide (them). See 20:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Allah - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names. See 20:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:80 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We made an appointment with you1 at the right side of the mount, and We sent down to you manna and quails. O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you on the right side of the Mount, and We sent down to you manna and quail (20:80). (Saying) eat of the Tayyibat wherewith We have provided you, and commit no transgression or oppression therein, lest My anger should justly descend on you. And he on whom My anger descends, he is indeed perished (20:81). And verily, I am indeed forgiving to him who repents, believes and does righteous deeds, and then Ihtad (20:82).A Reminder for the Children of Israel of Allah's Favors upon ThemAllah reminds of His tremendous favors upon…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:81 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Saying), "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you and do not transgress (or oppress others) therein, lest My anger should descend upon you. And he upon whom My anger descends has certainly fallen (i.e., perished)." See 20:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:82 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance. See 20:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:83 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Allah said), "And what made you hasten from your people, O Musa?" And what made you hasten from your people, O Musa (20:83). He said: "They are close on my footsteps, and I hastened to You, O my Lord, that You might be pleased (20:84). (Allah) said: "Verily, We have tried your people in your absence, and As-Samiri has led them astray (20:85). Then Musa returned to his people in a state of anger and sorrow (Asif). He said: "O my people! Did not your Lord promise you a fair promise? Did then the promise seem to you long in coming? Or did you desire that wrath should descend from your Lord on you, that you broke your promise to me? (20:86). They said: "We broke not the promise to you, of our own will, but we were made to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:84 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "They are close upon my tracks, and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You be pleased." See 20:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:85 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Allah) said, "But indeed, We have tried your people after you (departed), and the Sāmirī1 has led them astray." See 20:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:86 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved.1 He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise?2 Then, was the time (of its fulfillment) too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord descend upon you, so you broke your promise (of obedience) to me?" See 20:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:87 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "We did not break our promise to you by our will, but we were made to carry burdens from the ornaments of the people (of Pharaoh), so we threw them (into the fire), and thus did the Sāmirī throw." See 20:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:88 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he extracted for them (the statue of) a calf which had a lowing sound, and they said, "This is your god and the god of Musa, but he forgot." See 20:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:89 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Did they not see that it could not return to them any speech (i.e., response) and that it did not possess for them any harm or benefit? See 20:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And has the story of Musa reached you?. And has there come to you the story of Musa (20:9). When he saw a fire, he said to his family: Wait! Verily, I have seen a fire; perhaps I can bring you some burning brand therefrom, or find some guidance at the fire (20:10).A Discussion of the Message of MusaFrom this point, Allah begins to mention the story of Musa, how revelation began to come to Him, and Allah's speaking directly to him. This occurred after Musa had completed the time agreed upon between he and his father-in-law that he would herd sheep. He was traveling with his family, and it has been said that he was headed for the land of Egypt, after having been away from it for more than ten years. He had his wife with him and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:90 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Harun had already told them before (the return of Musa), "O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order." And Harun indeed had said to them beforehand: "O my people! You are being tried in this, and verily, your Lord is (Allah) the Most Gracious, so follow me and obey my order (20:90). They said: "We will not stop worshipping it, until Musa returns to us (20:91).Harun Prohibits them from Worship of the Calf and the Persistence of the Children of Israel in Doing soAllah, the Exalted, informs of Harun's attempt to prohibit them from worshipping the calf and his telling them that this was only a test for them. He told them that their Lord was the Most Beneficent, Who created everything…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:91 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "We will never cease being devoted to it (i.e., the calf) until Musa returns to us." See 20:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:92 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray. (Musa) said: O Harun! What prevented you when you saw them going astray; (20:92). "That you followed me not (according to my advice to you)? Have you then disobeyed my order? (20:93). He (Harun) said: "O son of my mother! Seize (me) not by my beard, nor by my head! Verily, I feared lest you should say: 'You have caused a division among the Children of Israel, and you have not respected my word!' (20:94).What Happened between Musa and Harun after Musa ReturnedAllah informs of what happened when Musa returned to his people and saw the great matter that had taken place among them. With this he became filled with anger and he threw down the Divine Tablets that he had in his hand. Then, he grabbed…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:93 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: From following me? Then have you disobeyed my order?" See 20:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:94 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Harun) said, "O son of my mother, do not seize (me) by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You caused division among the Children of Israel, and you did not observe (or await) my word.'" See 20:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:95 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "And what is your case, O Sāmirī?" (Musa) said: And what is the matter with you. O Samiri? (20:95). (Samiri) said: "I saw what they saw not, so I took a (Qabdah) handful (of dust) from the (hoof) print of the messenger and threw it. Thus my inner self suggested to me (20:96). Musa said: "Then go away! And verily, your (punishment) in this life will be that you will say: 'Touch me not;' and verily, you have a promise that will not fail. And look at your god to which you have been devoted. We will certainly burn it, and scatter its particles in the sea (20:97). Your God is only Allah, there is no God but Him. He has full knowledge of all things (20:98).How As-Samiri Made the CalfMusa said to As-Samiri, "What caused you to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:96 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: He said, "I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful (of dust) from the track of the messenger1 and threw it,2 and thus did my soul entice me." See 20:95

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:97 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Musa) said, "Then go. And indeed, it is (decreed) for you in (this) life to say, 'No contact.'1 And indeed, you have an appointment (in the Hereafter) you will not fail to keep. And look at your 'god' to which you remained devoted. We will surely burn it and blow it (i.e., its ashes) into the sea with a blast. See 20:95

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:98 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Your god is only Allah, except for whom there is no deity. He has encompassed all things in knowledge." See 20:95

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:99 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Thus, (O Muḥammad), We relate to you from the news of what has preceded. And We have certainly given you from Us a message (i.e., the Qur’ān). Thus We relate to you some information of what happened before. And indeed We have given you from Us a Reminder (20:99). Whoever turns away from it, verily, they will bear a heavy burden on the Day of Resurrection (20:100). They will abide in that – and evil indeed will it be that load for them on the Day of Resurrection (20:101).The Entire Qur'an is the Remembrance of Allah and Mentioning the Punishment of Those Who Turn Away from ItAllah, the Exalted, is saying to Prophet Muhammad SAW, 'We have told you (O Muhammad) the story of Musa and what happened with him, Fir'awn and his armies, just as it actually happened. Likewise,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Yā, Seen.1 لَقَدْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَىٰ أَكْثَرِهِمْIndeed the Word has proved true against most of them,Ibn Jarir said, The punishment has become inevitable for most of them, because Allah has decreed in the Mother of the Book (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz) that they will not believe.فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَso they will not believe.in Allah, or in His Messengers.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe. See 36:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: You can only warn one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and noble reward. See 36:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth and what they left behind, and all things We have enumerated in a clear register. See 36:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And present to them an example: the people of the city, when the messengers came to it. And put forward to them a similitude; the Dwellers of the Town, when there came Messengers to them (36:13). When We sent to them two Messengers, they denied them both; so We reinforced them with a third, and they said: "Verily, we have been sent to you as Messengers (36:14). They said: "You are only human beings like ourselves, and the Most Gracious has revealed nothing. You are only telling lies (36:15). The Messengers said: "Our Lord knows that we have been sent as Messengers to you, (36:16). "And our duty is only to convey plainly (36:17).The Story of the Dwellers of the Town and Their Messengers, a Lesson that Those Who Belied Their Messengers were DestroyedAllah says, 'O Muhammad, tell your people…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: When We sent to them two but they denied them, so We strengthened (them) with a third, and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers to you." See 36:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has not revealed a thing. You are only telling lies." See 36:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Our Lord knows that we are messengers to you. See 36:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And we are not responsible except for clear notification." See 36:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you, from us, a painful punishment." They (people) said: For us, we see an evil omen from you; if you cease not, we will surely stone you, and a painful torment will touch you from us (36:18). They (Messengers) said: "Your evil omens be with you! Because you are admonished? Nay, but you are a people mischievous.") Then the people of the city said to the (36:19). إِنَّا تَطَيَّرْنَا بِكُمْ (For us, we see an evil omen from you;) meaning, 'we do not see in your faces any sign of good for our lives.' Qatadah said, "They were saying, 'if something bad befalls us, it will be because of you.'" Mujahid said, "They were saying: People…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They said, "Your omen (i.e., fate) is with yourselves. Is it1 because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people." See 36:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: By the wise1 Qur’ān. See 36:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And there came from the farthest end of the city a man, running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers. And there came a man running from the farthest part of the town. He said, "O my people! Obey the Messengers (36:20). "Obey those who ask no wages of you, and who are rightly guided (36:21). "And why should I not worship Him Who has created me and to Whom you shall be returned (36:22). "Shall I take besides Him gods? If the Most Gracious intends me any harm, their intercession will be of no use for me whatsoever, nor can they save me (36:23). "Then verily, I should be in plain error (36:24). "Verily, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me! (36:25).Quoting what reached him from Ibn 'Abbas, Ka'b Al-Ahbar and Wahb bin Munabbih –…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Follow those who do not ask of you (any) payment, and they are (rightly) guided. See 36:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And why should I not worship He who created me and to whom you will be returned? See 36:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Should I take other than Him (false) deities (while), if the Most Merciful intends for me some adversity, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me? See 36:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, I would then be in manifest error. See 36:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me." See 36:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It was said, "Enter Paradise."1 He said, "I wish my people could know. It was said: "Enter Paradise." He said: "Would that my people knew (36:26). "That my Lord (Allah) has forgiven me, and made me of the honored ones! (36:27). And We sent not against his people after him an army from the heaven, nor was it needful for Us to send (such a thing) (36:28). It was but one 'Şayḥah' and lo! they (all) were still (36:29).Muhammad bin Ishaq reported from some of his companions from Ibn Mas'ud (RA), that they stamped on him until his intestines came out of his back passage. Allah said to him:ادْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ"Enter Paradise."so he entered it with all its bountiful provision, when Allah had taken away from him all the sickness, grief and exhaustion of this world. Mujahid said, It was said…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Of how my Lord has forgiven me and placed me among the honored." See 36:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We did not send down upon his people after him any soldiers from the heaven, nor would We have done so. See 36:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It was not but one shout,1 and immediately they were extinguished. See 36:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed you, (O Muḥammad), are from among the messengers. See 36:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: How regretful for the servants. There did not come to them any messenger except that they used to ridicule him. Alas for mankind! There never came a Messenger to them but they used to mock at him (36:30). Do they not see how many of the generations We have destroyed before them? Verily, they will not return to them (36:31). And surely, all – everyone of them will be brought before Us (36:32).Woe to the Disbelievers!Ali bin Abi Talhah reported that Ibn 'Abbas commented on the Ayah:يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ ۚAlas for mankind!This means, woe to mankind! Qatadah said:يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ ۚAlas for mankind!means, "Alas for mankind, who have neglected the command of Allah."The meaning is that they will feel regret and sorrow on the Day of Resurrection. When they see the punishment with their own eyes; they will…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have they not considered how many generations We destroyed before them - that they to them1 will not return? See 36:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And indeed, all of them will yet be brought present before Us. See 36:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And a sign for them is the dead earth. We have brought it to life and brought forth from it grain, and from it they eat. And a sign for them is the dead land. We give it life, and We bring forth from it grains, so that they eat thereof (36:33). And We have made therein gardens of date palms and grapes, and We have caused springs of water to gush forth therein (36:34). So that they may eat of the fruit thereof – and their hands made it not. Will they not then give thanks (36:35). Glory be to Him Who has created all the pairs of that which the earth produces, as well as of their own kind, and of that which they know not (36:36).Proof of the Creator of the Universe and of Life after DeathAllah,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We placed therein gardens of palm trees and grapevines and caused to burst forth therefrom some springs. See 36:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That they may eat of His fruit.1 And their hands have not produced it,2 so will they not be grateful? See 36:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Exalted is He who created all pairs1 - from what the earth grows and from themselves and from that which they do not know. See 36:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And a sign for them is the night. We remove1 from it the (light of) day, so they are (left) in darkness. And a sign for them is the night. We withdraw therefrom the day, and behold, they are in darkness (36:37). And the sun runs on its fixed course for a term (appointed). That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing (36:38). And the moon, We have decreed for it stages, till it returns like the old dried curved date stalk (36:39). It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day. They all float, each in an orbit (36:40).Among the Signs of the Might and Power of Allah are the Night and Day, and the Sun and MoonAllah tells us of further proof of His great might and power, which…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the sun runs (on course) toward its stopping point. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. See 36:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the moon - We have determined for it phases, until it returns (appearing) like the old date stalk. See 36:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: On a straight path. See 36:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is not allowable (i.e., possible) for the sun to reach the moon, nor does the night overtake the day, but each, in an orbit, is swimming. See 36:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And a sign for them is that We carried their forefathers1 in a laden ship. And an Ayah for them is that We bore their offspring in the laden ship (36:41). And We have created for them of the like thereunto, on which they ride (36:42). And if We will, We shall drown them, and there will be no shout for them, nor will they be saved (36:43). Unless it be a mercy from Us, and as an enjoyment for a while (36:44).Among the Signs of Allah is that He Carried Them in the Laden ShipAllah tells us: another sign for them of His might and power is that He has subjugated the sea to carry ships, including – most significantly – the ship of Nuh (AS), in which Allah saved him and the believers, apart from whom none of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We created for them from the likes of it that which they ride. See 36:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if We should will, We could drown them; then no one responding to a cry would there be for them, nor would they be saved. See 36:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:44 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Except as a mercy from Us and provision for a time. See 36:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:45 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But when it is said to them, "Beware of what is before you and what is behind you;1 perhaps you will receive mercy..."2 And when it is said to them: "Beware of that which is before you, and that which is behind you, in order that you may receive mercy (36:45). And never came an Ayah from among the Ayat of their Lord to them, but they did turn away from it (36:46). And when it is said to them: "Spend of that with which Allah has provided you," those who disbelieve say to those who believe: "Shall we feed those whom, if Allah willed, He would have fed? You are only in a plain error (36:47).The Misguidance of the IdolatorsAllah tells us how the idolators persisted in their misguidance and in not paying attention to the sins that they…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:46 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they are from it turning away. See 36:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:47 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when it is said to them, "Spend from that which Allah has provided for you," those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Should we feed one whom, if Allah had willed, He would have fed? You are not but in clear error." See 36:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:48 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" And they say: When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful? (36:48). They await only but a single 'Şayḥah' which will seize them while they are disputing (36:49). Then they will not be able to make bequest, nor they will return to their family (36:50). The Disbelievers thought that the Day of Resurrection would never come to pass Allah tells us how the disbelievers thought that the Day of Resurrection would never come to pass, as they said: مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا الْوَعْدُ ("When will this promise be fulfilled...")يَسْتَعْجِلُ بِهَا الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهَا ۖThose who believe not therein seek to hasten it (42:18)Allah says:مَا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً تَأْخُذُهُمْ وَهُمْ يَخِصِّمُونَThey await only but a single 'Şayḥah' which will seize them while they are disputing!Meaning: they are…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:49 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They do not await except one blast1 which will seize them while they are disputing. See 36:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:5 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (This is) a revelation of the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. See 36:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:50 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they will not be able (to give) any instruction, nor to their people can they return. See 36:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:51 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And the Horn will be blown;1 and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. And the Trumpet will be blown and behold from the graves they will come out quickly to their Lord (36:51). They will say: Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our place of sleep." (It will be said to them): "This is what the Most Gracious had promised, and the Messengers spoke truth! (36:52). It will be but a single 'Şayḥah', so behold they will all be brought up before Us (36:53). This Day, none will be wronged in anything, nor will you be requited anything except that which you used to do (36:54). The Trumpet Blast of the Resurrection This will be the third blast of the trumpet, the trumpet blast of the resurrection when people will come forth…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:52 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?" (The reply will be), "This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth." See 36:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:53 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It will not be but one blast, and at once they are all brought present before Us. See 36:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:54 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So today (i.e., the Day of Judgement) no soul will be wronged at all, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do. See 36:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:55 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed the companions of Paradise, that Day, will be amused in (joyful) occupation. Verily, the dwellers of the Paradise, that Day, will be busy with joyful things (36:55). They and their wives will be in pleasant shade, reclining on thrones (36:56). They will have therein fruits and all that they ask for (36:57). (It will be said to them): "Salam (Peace!)" – a Word from the Lord, Most Merciful (36:58).The Life of the People of ParadiseAllah tells us that on the Day of Resurrection, when the people of Paradise have reached the arena of judgement, and have settled in the gardens of Paradise, they will be too preoccupied with their own victory and new life of eternal delights to worry about anyone else. Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Ismail bin Abi Khalid said, They will be too busy to think about the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:56 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They and their spouses - in shade, reclining on adorned couches. See 36:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:57 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For them therein is fruit, and for them is whatever they request (or wish). See 36:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:58 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (And) "Peace," a word from a Merciful Lord. See 36:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:59 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Then He will say), "But stand apart today, you criminals.1 (It will be said): "And O you the criminals! Get you apart this Day (36:59). "Did I not command you, O Children of Adam, that you should not worship Shaytan? Verily, he is a plain enemy to you (36:60). "And that you should worship Me. That is the straight path (36:61). "And indeed he did lead astray a great multitude of you. Did you not then understand? (36:62).The Isolation of the Disbelievers and Their Rebuke on the Day of ResurrectionAllah tells us what the end of the disbelievers will be on the Day of Resurrection, when He commands them to get apart from the believers, i.e., to stand apart from the believers. This is like the Ayat:وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا مَكَانَكُمْ أَنْتُمْ وَشُرَكَاؤُكُمْ ۚ فَزَيَّلْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ ۖAnd…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:6 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are unaware. See 36:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:60 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - (for) indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. See 36:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:61 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And that you worship (only) Me? This is a straight path. See 36:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:62 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he had already led astray from among you much of creation, so did you not use reason? See 36:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:63 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: This is the Hellfire which you were promised. This is Hell which you were promised (36:63). Burn (enter) therein this Day, for that you used to disbelieve (36:64). This Day, We shall seal up their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their legs will bear witness to what they used to earn (36:65). And if it had been Our will, We would surely have wiped out their eyes, so that they would struggle for the path, how then would they see (36:66). And if it had been Our will, We could have transformed them in their places. Then they would have been unable to go forward (move about) nor they could have turned back (36:67).On the Day of Resurrection, it will be said to the disbelievers among the sons of Adam, after Hell has been shown to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:64 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (Enter to) burn therein today for what you used to deny."1 See 36:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:65 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: That Day, We will seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify about what they used to earn. See 36:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:66 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if We willed, We could have obliterated their eyes, and they would race to (find) the path, and how could they see?1 See 36:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:67 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if We willed, We could have deformed them, (paralyzing them) in their places so they would not be able to proceed, nor could they return.1 See 36:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:68 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he to whom We grant long life We reverse in creation;1 so will they not understand? And he whom We grant long life – We reverse him in creation. Will they not then understand (36:68). And We have not taught him poetry, nor is it suitable for him. This is only a Reminder and a plain Qur'an (36:69). That he or it may give warning to him who is living, and that Word may be justified against the disbelievers (36:70).Allah tells us that the longer the son of Adam lives, the more he becomes weak after being strong, and incapable after being able and active This is like the Ayah:اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ ضَعْفٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ضَعْفٍ قُوَّةً ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ ضَعْفًا وَشَيْبَةً ۚ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ ۖ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْقَدِيرُAllah is He Who created…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:69 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We did not give him (i.e., Prophet Muḥammad SAW) knowledge of poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is not but a message and a clear Qur’ān. See 36:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:7 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Already the word (i.e., decree) has come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe. See 36:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:70 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: To warn whoever is alive1 and justify the word (i.e., decree) against the disbelievers. See 36:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:71 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Do they not see that We have created for them from what Our hands1 have made, grazing livestock, and (then) they are their owners? Do they not see that We have created for them of what Our Hands have fashioned, the cattle, so that they are their owners (36:71). And We have subdued them unto them so that some of them they have for riding and some they eat (36:72). And they have (other) benefits from them, and (they get to) drink. Will they not then be grateful (36:73).There is a Sign and a Blessing in CattleAllah mentions the blessing that He has bestowed upon His creation by subjugating these cattle for their use.فَهُمْ لَهَا مَالِكُونَso that they are their owners.Qatadah said, "They are their masters." Meaning, He has made them subdue them. So they are submissive towards them and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:72 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have tamed them for them, so some of them they ride, and some of them they eat. See 36:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:73 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And for them therein are (other) benefits and drinks, so will they not be grateful? See 36:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:74 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But they have taken besides Allah (false) deities that perhaps they would be helped. And they have taken besides Allah, gods, hoping that they might be helped (36:74). They cannot help them, but they will be brought forward as a troop (against those who worshipped them) (36:75). So, let not their speech then grieve you. Verily, We know what they conceal and what they reveal (36:76).The Gods of the Idolators are Not Able to Help ThemAllah denounces the idolators for taking the idols as gods alongside Allah, hoping that those gods will help them and provide for them and bring them closer to Allah. Allah says:لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَهُمْThey cannot help them,Meaning: those gods cannot help their worshippers; they are too weak, too insignificant and too powerless. Rather they cannot even help themselves or take revenge on those who want to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:75 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: They are not able to help them, and they (themselves) are for them soldiers in attendance.1 See 36:74

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:76 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare. See 36:74

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:77 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Does man not consider that We created him from a (mere) sperm-drop - then at once1 he is a clear adversary? Does not man see that We have created him from Nutfah. Yet behold he (stands forth) as an open opponent (36:77). And he puts forth for Us a parable, and forgets his own creation. He says: "Who will give life to these bones after they are rotten and have become dust? (36:78). Say: "He will give life to them Who created them for the first time! And He is the All-Knower of every creation! (36:79). He Who produces for you fire out of the green tree, when behold you kindle therewith (36:80).The Denial of Life after Death, and the Refutation of this IdeaMujahid, 'Ikrimah, 'Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, As-Suddi and Qatadah said, Ubayy bin Khalaf, may Allah curse him, came…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:78 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And he presents for Us an example1 and forgets his (own) creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are disintegrated?" See 36:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:79 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time; and He is, of all creation, Knowing." See 36:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:8 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they are to their chins, so they are with heads (kept) aloft. Verily, We have put on their necks iron collars reaching to the chins, so that their heads are raised up (36:8). And We have put a barrier before them, and a barrier behind them, and We have covered them up, so that they cannot see (36:9). It is the same to them whether you warn them or you warn them not, they will not believe (36:10). You can only warn him who follows the Reminder, and fears the Most Gracious unseen. Bear you to such one the glad tidings of forgiveness, and a generous reward (36:11). Verily, We give life to the dead, and We record that which they send before (them), and their traces and all things We…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:80 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: (It is) He who made for you from the green tree, fire, and then from it you ignite. See 36:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:81 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth Able to create the likes of them? Yes, (it is so); and He is the Knowing Creator. Is not He Who created the heavens and the earth, able to create the like of them? Yes, indeed! He is the All-Knowing Supreme Creator (36:81). Verily, His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be!" – and it is (36:82). So glorified be He and exalted (above all that they associate with Him), and in Whose Hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you shall be returned (36:83).Allah points out His great might and power in that He created the seven heavens with all their stars and planets, and the seven earths with everything in them of mountains, sands, oceans and wildernesses, and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:82 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, "Be," and it is. See 36:81

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:83 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So exalted is He in whose hand is the realm of all things, and to Him you will be returned. See 36:81

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:9 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see. See 36:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:1 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Alif, Lām, Rā.1 These are the verses of the wise2 Book. أَكَانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَبًاIs it a wonder for mankind...Allah's statement;أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْthat they shall have with their Lord the rewards of their good deedsScholars have differed over the meaning of the reward for the good deeds in this Ayah:وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍand give good news to those who believe that they shall have with their Lord the rewards of their good deeds.Ali bin Abi Talhah reported that Ibn 'Abbas said about this Ayah, "Eternal happiness has been written for them." Al-'Awfi reported that Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the good reward for what they have done." Mujahid said: "It is their good deeds – their prayers, fasting, charity, and glorification." He then said, "And Muhammad SAW will intercede for them." Allah said:قَالَ الْكَافِرُونَ إِنَّ…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:10 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Their call therein will be, "Exalted are You, O Allah," and their greeting therein will be, "Peace." And the last of their call will be, "Praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds!" See 10:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:100 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it is not for a soul (i.e., anyone) to believe except by permission of Allah, and He will place defilement1 upon those who will not use reason. See 10:99

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:101 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Observe what is in the heavens and the earth." But of no avail will be signs or warners to a people who do not believe. Say: Behold all that is in the heavens and the earth." But neither Ayat nor warners benefit those who do not believe (10:101). Then do they wait save for the likes of the days of men who passed away before them Say: "Wait then, I am waiting with you among those who wait (10:102). Then We save Our Messengers and those who believe! Thus it is incumbent upon Us to save the believers (10:103).The Command to Reflect upon the Creation of the Heavens and the EarthAllah, the Exalted, guides His servants to reflect upon His blessings. What Allah has created in the heavens and the earth is part of the clear signs for those…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:102 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So do they wait except for like (what occurred in) the days of those who passed on before them? Say, "Then wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait." See 10:101

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:103 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then We will save Our messengers and those who have believed. Thus, it is an obligation upon Us that We save the believers.1 See 10:101

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:104 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, (O Muḥammad), "O people, if you are in doubt as to my religion - then I do not worship those which you worship besides Allah; but I worship Allah, who causes your death. And I have been commanded to be of the believers. Say: O people! If you are in doubt about my religion - I will never worship those whom you worship besides Allah, rather, I will worship Allah, the One Who cause you to die. And I was commanded to be one of the believers (10:104). And (I was commanded), "Direct your face toward the Hanif (monotheism) religion, and not be one of the idolators (10:105). "And do not invoke besides Allah what will not benefit you nor harm you. For if you did, you would certainly be one of the wrongdoers (10:106). And if Allah touches…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:105 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (commanded), 'Direct your face (i.e., self) toward the religion, inclining to truth, and never be of those who associate others with Allah. See 10:104

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:106 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And do not invoke1 besides Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you did, then indeed you would be of the wrongdoers.'"2 See 10:104

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:107 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him; and if He intends for you good, then there is no repeller of His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. See 10:104

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:108 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord, so whoever is guided is only guided for (the benefit of) his soul, and whoever goes astray only goes astray (in violation) against it. And I am not over you a manager." Say: O people! Now the truth has come to you from your Lord. So whoever receives guidance, he does so for the good of himself. And whoever goes astray, he does so at his own loss. And I am not set over you as a guardian (10:108). And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah gives judgment. And He is the best of the judges (10:109). Allah, the Exalted, commands His Messenger SAW to inform the people that that which he has brought them from Allah is the truth. It is a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:109 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And follow what is revealed to you, (O Muḥammad), and be patient until Allah will judge. And He is the best of judges. See 10:108

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:11 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if Allah was to hasten for the people the evil (they invoke)1 as He hastens for them the good, their term would have been ended for them.2 But We leave the ones who do not expect the meeting with Us, in their transgression, wandering blindly. And were Allah to hasten for mankind the evil as He hastens for them the good then they would have been ruined. So We leave those who expect not their meeting with Us, in their trespasses, wandering blindly in distraction (10:11).Allah does Not Respond to the Requests for Evil like He does with the Requests for GoodAllah tells us about His Forbearance and Benevolence with His servants. He does not respond to them when they pray with evil intentions against themselves, their wealth or their children during times of grief or anger. He knows…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:12 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when affliction touches man, he calls upon Us, whether lying on his side or sitting or standing; but when We remove from him his affliction, he continues (in disobedience) as if he had never called upon Us to (remove) an affliction that touched him. Thus is made pleasing to the transgressors that which they have been doing. And when harm touches man, he invokes Us, lying on his side, or sitting or standing. But when We have removed his harm from him, he passes on as if he had never invoked Us for a harm that touched him! Thus it is made fair seeming to the wasteful that which they used to do (10:12).Man Remembers Allah at Times of Adversity and Forgets Him at Times of ProsperityAllah tells us about man and how he becomes annoyed and worried when…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:13 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And We had already destroyed generations before you when they wronged, and their messengers had come to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe. Thus do We recompense the criminal people. And indeed, We destroyed generations before you when they did wrong, while their Messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they were not such as to believe! Thus do We requite the people who are criminals (10:13). Then We made you successors after them, generations after generations in the land, that We might see how you would work (10:14).The Admonition Held in the Destruction of the Previous GenerationsAllah tells us about what happened to past generations when they belied the Messengers and the clear signs and proofs the latter brought to them. Allah then made this nation successors after them. He sent to them a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:14 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Then We made you successors in the land after them so that We may observe how you will do. See 10:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:15 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, "Bring us a Qur’ān other than this or change it." Say, (O Muḥammad), "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day." And when Our clear Ayat are recited unto them, those who hope not for their meeting with Us, say: "Bring us a Qur'an other than this, or change it." Say: "It is not for me to change it on my own accord; I only follow that which is revealed unto me. Verily, I fear the torment of the Great Day (the Day of Resurrection) if I were to disobey my Lord…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:16 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you, for I had remained among you a lifetime before it.1 Then will you not reason?" See 10:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:17 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: So who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed. So who does more wrong than he who forges a lie against Allah or denies His Āyāt? Surely, the criminals will never be successful (10:17).Allah says that no one is more wrong, unjust and arrogant than he who invented a lie against Allah, forged claims about Allah, or claimed that Allah has sent a message to him but his claim was not true.No one is more of a criminal or has committed greater wrong than such a person. Liars cannot be confused with Prophets. Anyone who claims such a thing, whether lying or telling the truth, will necessarily be supported by Allah with proofs and signs of his falsehood or truthfulness. The difference between Muhammad SAW and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:18 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they worship other than Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them, and they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah." Say, "Do you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?" Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him. And they worship besides Allah things that harm them not, nor profit them, and they say: These are our intercessors with Allah." Say: Do you inform Allah of that which He knows not in the heavens and on the earth?" Glorified and Exalted is He above all that which they associate as partners (with Him) (10:18). Mankind were but one community, then they differed (later); and had not it been for a Word that went forth before from your Lord, it would have been settled between them regarding…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:19 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And mankind was not but one community (united in religion), but (then) they differed. And if not for a word1 that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them (immediately) concerning that over which they differ. See 10:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:2 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Have the people been amazed that We revealed (revelation) to a man from among them, (saying), "Warn mankind and give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a (firm) precedence of honor1 with their Lord"? (But) the disbelievers say, "Indeed, this is an obvious magician." See 10:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:20 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And they say, "Why is a sign not sent down to him from his Lord?" So say, "The unseen is only for Allah (to administer), so wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait." And they say: How is it that not a sign is sent down on him from his Lord?" Say: "The Unseen belongs only to Allah, so wait you, verily, I am with you among those who wait (10:20).The Idolators Requested a MiracleThese stubborn, lying disbelievers said, "Why would not a sign be revealed to Muhammad from his Lord." They meant a sign such as given to Salih. Allah sent the she-camel to Thamud. They wanted Allah to change the mount of As-Safa into gold or remove the mountains of Makkah and replace them with gardens and rivers. Allah is capable of doing all of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:21 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And when We give the people a taste of mercy after adversity has touched them, at once they conspire against Our verses. Say, "Allah is swifter in strategy." Indeed, Our messengers (i.e., angels) record that which you conspire. And when We let mankind taste mercy after some adversity has afflicted them, behold! They take to plotting against Our Ayat! Say: Allah is more swift in planning!" Certainly, Our messengers (angels) record all of that which you plot (10:21). He it is Who enables you to travel through land and sea, till when you are in the ships, and they sail with them with a favorable wind, and they are glad therein, then comes a stormy wind and the waves come to them from all sides, and they think that they are encircled therein. Then they invoke Allah, making their faith…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:22 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea until, when you are in ships and they sail with them1 by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes a storm wind and the waves come upon them from every place and they expect to be engulfed, they supplicate Allah, sincere to Him in religion, "If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful." See 10:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:23 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But when He saves them, at once they commit injustice1 upon the earth without right. O mankind, your injustice is only against yourselves, (being merely) the enjoyment of worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do. See 10:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:24 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: The example of (this) worldly life is but like rain which We have sent down from the sky that the plants of the earth absorb - (those) from which men and livestock eat - until, when the earth has taken on its adornment and is beautified and its people suppose that they have capability over it, there comes to it Our command by night or by day, and We make it as a harvest,1 as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We explain in detail the signs for a people who give thought. Verily, the parable of the life of the world is as the water which We send down from the sky; so by it arises the intermingled produce of the earth of which men and cattle eat: until when the earth is clad in its adornments…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:25 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And Allah invites to the Home of Peace (i.e., Paradise) and guides whom He wills to a straight path. See 10:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:26 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For them who have done good is the best (reward) - and extra.1 No darkness will cover their faces, nor humiliation. Those are companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally. For those who have done good is the best, and even more. Neither darkness nor dust nor any humiliating disgrace shall cover their faces. They are the dwellers of Paradise, they will abide therein forever (10:26).The Reward of the Good-DoersAllah states that those who do good in this world – by having faith and performing righteous deeds – will be rewarded with a good reward in the Hereafter. Allah said:هَلْ جَزَاءُ الْإِحْسَانِ إِلَّا الْإِحْسَانُIs there any reward for good other than good? (55:60)Then Allah said:وَزِيَادَةٌand even more.the reward on the good deeds multiplied ten times to seven hundred times and even more on top of that. This reward includes…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:27 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: But they who have earned (blame for) evil doings - the recompense of an evil deed is its equivalent, and humiliation will cover them. They will have from Allah no protector. It will be as if their faces are covered with pieces of the night - so dark (are they). Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. And those who have earned evil deeds, the recompense of an evil deed is the like thereof, and humiliating disgrace will cover them (their faces). No defender will they have from Allah. Their faces will be covered as it were with pieces from the darkness of night. They are the dwellers of the Fire, they will abide therein forever (10:27).The Reward of the Wicked CriminalsAfter Allah told us about the state of those happy people who have done…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:28 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And (mention, O Muḥammad), the Day We will gather them all together - then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, "(Remain in) your place, you and your 'partners.'"1 Then We will separate them,2 and their "partners" will say, "You did not used to worship us.3 And the Day whereon We shall gather them all together, then We shall say to those who did set partners in worship with Us: "Stop at your place! You and your partners." Then We shall separate them, and their partners shall say: "It was not us that you used to worship (10:28). "So sufficient is Allah as a witness between us and you that we indeed knew nothing of your worship of us (10:29). There! Every person will know (exactly) what he had earned before and they will be brought back…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:29 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And sufficient is Allah as a witness between us and you that we were of your worship unaware." See 10:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:3 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne,1 arranging the matter (of His creation). There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Then will you not remember? Surely, your Lord is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days and then rose over (Istawa) the Throne, arranging the affair (of all things). No intercessor (can plead with Him) except after He permits. That is Allah, your Lord; so worship Him (alone). Then, will you not remember (10:3).Allah is the Creator Who Arranges the Affairs of the UniverseAllah tells us that He is the Lord of the entire existence. He tells us that He created the heavens and the earth in six days. It was said:…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:30 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: There, (on that Day), every soul will be put to trial for what it did previously, and they will be returned to Allah, their master, the Truth, and lost from them is whatever they used to invent. See 10:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:31 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight and who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living and who arranges (every) matter?" They will say, "Allah," so say, "Then will you not fear Him?" Say: Who provides for you from the sky and the earth? Or who owns hearing and sight? And who brings out the living from the dead and brings out the dead from the living? And who disposes of the affairs?" They will say: "Allah." Say: "Will you not then be afraid (of Allah's punishment)? (10:31). Such is Allah, your Lord in truth. So after the truth, what else can there be, save error? How then are you turned away (10:32). Thus is the Word of your Lord justified against…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:32 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: For that is Allah, your Lord, the Truth. And what can be beyond truth except error? So how are you averted? See 10:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:33 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Thus the word (i.e., decree) of your Lord has come into effect upon those who defiantly disobeyed - that they will not believe. See 10:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:34 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Are there of your 'partners' any who begins creation and then repeats it?" Say, "Allah begins creation and then repeats it, so how are you deluded?" Say: "Is there of your partners one that originates the creation and then repeats it?" Say: "Allah originates the creation and then He repeats it. Then how are you deluded away (from the truth)? (10:34). Say: "Is there of your partners one that guides to the truth?" Say: "It is Allah Who guides to the truth. Is then He Who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who finds not guidance (himself) unless he is guided? Then, what is the matter with you? How judge you? (10:35). And most of them follow nothing but conjecture. Certainly, conjecture can be of no avail against the truth. Surely, Allah is All-Aware…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:35 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Say, "Are there of your 'partners' any who guides to the truth?" Say, "Allah guides to the truth. So is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed or he who guides not unless he is guided? Then what is (wrong) with you - how do you judge?" See 10:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:36 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And most of them follow not except assumption. Indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do. See 10:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:37 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And it was not (possible) for this Qur’ān to be produced by other than Allah, but (it is) a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of the (former) Scripture, about which there is no doubt,1 from the Lord of the worlds. And this Qur'an is not such as could ever be produced by other than Allah but it is a confirmation of (the revelation) which was before it, and a full explanation of the Book – wherein there is no doubt – from the Lord of all that exists (10:37). Or do they say: He has forged it?" Say: "Bring then a Surah like unto it, and call upon whomsoever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful! (10:38). Nay, they have belied the knowledge whereof they could not comprehend and what has not yet been…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:38 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Or do they say (about the Prophet SAW), "He invented it?" Say, "Then bring forth a sūrah like it and call upon (for assistance) whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful." See 10:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:39 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: Rather, they have denied that which they encompass not in knowledge and whose interpretation has not yet come to them. Thus did those before them deny. Then observe how was the end of the wrongdoers. See 10:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:4 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: To Him is your return all together. (It is) the promise of Allah (which is) truth. Indeed, He begins the (process of) creation and then repeats it that He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds, in justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to deny. To Him is the return of all of you. The promise of Allah is true. It is He Who begins the creation and then will repeat it, that He may reward with justice those who believed and did deeds of righteousness. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of boiling fluids and painful torment because they used to disbelieve (10:4).The Return of Everything is to AllahAllah tells us that the return of the creatures on the Day…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:40 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And of them are those who believe in it, and of them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters. See 10:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:41 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And if they deny you, (O Muḥammad), then say, "For me are my deeds, and for you are your deeds. You are disassociated from what I do, and I am disassociated from what you do." And if they belie you, say: For me are my deeds and for you are your deeds! You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do! (10:41). And among them are some who listen to you, but can you make the deaf to hear – even though they apprehend not (10:42). And among them are some who look at you, but can you guide the blind – even though they see not (10:43). Truly, Allah wrongs not mankind in aught; but mankind wrong themselves (10:44).The Command to be Free and Clear from the IdolatorsAllah said to His Prophet SAW:…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:42 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And among them are those who listen to you. But can you cause the deaf to hear (i.e., benefit from this hearing), although they will not use reason? See 10:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:43 with Tafsir Tafsir Ibn Kathir
item.description: And among them are those who look at you. But can you guide the blind although they will not (attempt to) see? See 10:41
