item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:116 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But as for those who disbelieve, never shall their possessions (A warning to those puffed with worldly prosperity and proud of their flourishing families.) nor their children, avail them anything, against God; They shall be the inmates of the Hell-fire, therein they shall abide (Refer to Verses 3:178, 9:34.) . The Holy Qur'an has repeatedly prophesied about the failure of the enemies of Islam. The similitude given in these verses is comparable to that given in 68:17 - 68:33.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:117 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The likeness of what they (Refer to Verses 3:115, 68:17 - 68:35. No amount of charity without the right belief can be of any avail to anyone.) spend in this life of the world is like that of a freezing wind, which smiteth upon the tilth of a people who have wronged themselves and destroyed it; God did no injustice to them, it was they who are doing injustice to themselves. See 3:116

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:118 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who have believed! take not intimates (Friend.) , other than your fellow-believers, They (Those other than believers.) will not fail to corrupt (To make mischief, to harm, cause trouble.) you; they wish what distresseth you (the most); Their spite hath already shewn itself out of their mouths, but that which is concealed in their breasts (Hearts.) is greater still; indeed We have made clear the signs unto you, if ye would understand (Refer to Verses 6:7 - 6:9.) . These two verses lay down the caution to be observed against the enemies and their relations, regarding the toleration desirable to be exercised with those of the enemies who have not taken any initiative or joined any offensive against the Muslims. It is a warning as well, against close and intimate relations with those who are hostile to Islam…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:119 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Lo! Ye are those who love them, but they love you not though ye believe in the entire Book, and when they meet you, they say: "We believe"; but when they are apart, they bite their finger's ends at you in rage against you; Say (O' Apostle Muhammad!)" "Die ye in your rage;" Verily God well-knoweth whatever is in (people's) breasts (Refer to Verse 14:9.) . See 3:118

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) to those who disbelieve "ye shall be vanquished and gathered together unto Hell; (what) a wretched resting place (it shall be)" The Jews of 'Bani Qaniqaa' who lived in the suburbs of Madina got greatly alarmed by the crushing and the decisive victory the Muslims won at Badr and became active to do everything possible to prevent the growing power of the Muslims. They inflamed the fire already burning in the hearts of Quraish to a speedy revenge. Kaab Ibn Ashraf went to Mecca with a delegation to instigate the Quraish against the Muslims, stimulating the feelings of their tribal honour and their grief for their chiefs killed in the battle of Badr. From Mecca went Abu-Sufiyan to Madina and staying with 'Salam Ibn-Mishkan', entered into pledges of mutual help, and finalised the plans for…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:120 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If any good (even) toucheth, you it grieveth them, and if ill afflicteth you, they rejoice at it; But if ye be patient and guard yourselves (against evil) their craft (Scheme-Plotting.) shall not harm you; for verily whatever they do, God is comprehensive of (it). This is another prophecy with the assurance that the deceitful plans of the enemies will not be of any detriment to the Muslims-but the condition being that the Muslims should be patient and guard themselves against evil (practice piety).

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:121 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when thou didst set forth from thy family at early dawn that thou prepare for the believers the encampment for the battle (The battle of 'Badr'.) ; and God is The Hearer (Ar. 'Sami' All-Hearing.) , The Knower (Ar. 'Aleem' All Knowing.) . This is an extract of: The Holy Quran: A Translation with Commentary is an English translation of the Quran by A.F. Badshah Husain. It was published in 1931 by the Moayyedul uloom Association in Lucknow."It is to the events of the famous battle of Uhud that this and the following sections are mainly devoted. In the third year of the Hijra the Meccans marched against the Muslims of Medina with an army three thousand strong. Being utterly foiled and defeated at Badr the desire to punish the Musalmans was keener than ever. The Meccan chief Abu…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:122 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Remember O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) When two groups of you (Muslims.) had thought to flinch, and God was the Guardian (Protector.) of both; in God should the believers trust. The two tribes referred to here, were Banu Salma and Banu Harisa (B. H.). The details of the events are long. When the companions had tied away, 'Ali was fighting hard to save the Holy Prophet and Islam. The voice of the Messenger Angel of God viz. Gabriel was heard from the heavens: -"La Fata illa 'Ali, La saif illa Zulfiqar." (M.S.)There is no (victorious) youth save 'Ali, i.e., There is no sword (weapon of success) except the 'Zulfiqar' (the Sword of 'Ali).

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:123 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed God hath succoured you at 'Badr' when ye were contemptibly weak (Refer to Verse 8:9.) ; so take shelter in God, so that ye may be thankful. The Battle of Badr is well-known in the Islamic history in which the whole strength of the Muslims could be numbered only to 313 of ill-equipped and almost famished men.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:124 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Remember O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) when thou (The Holy Prophet.) didst say to the believers, "Doth it not suffice you that your Lord should help (Refers to the divine help rendered at the Battle of Badr.) you with three thousand angels sent down (from heaven)? (Refer to Verse 8:9, 8:142.)" The enemy was 1,000 strong of the completely equipped and fully prepared forces of the Meccans1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:125 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Aye! if ye be steadfast (Some of the companions of the Holy Prophet did not abide by this in the battle fields- they gave way and took shelter not in God but in running away from the battle field deserting the Holy Prophet (in Uhud and Hunayn, Khaybar Etc). Refer to Verses 3:151, 3:152, 3:154.) and take shelter in God and if the enemy come upon you in this very dashing manner, your Lord will help you with five thousand (such) angels distinguished (Ar. 'Musawwameen' distinguished with marks. Also 'Musawwimeen' dashing - havoc making.) who will be (fully equipped). The fact is clearly and plainly explained here that the Muslims were helped by God with a thousand angels. This has been interpreted by the Ahmadi Commentator, to be only a figurative expression, and the sending down of the angels he…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:126 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God did not effect this but as good tidings for you, and that thereby your hearts might rest assured (Tranquil your hearts) ; and (there) is no succour but from God, the Mighty (All- Mighty) , the Wise (The All wise) . The angels sent down to the aid of the Muslims were not to actually fight but to join the Muslim forces in their strength by which the Muslims themselves were encouraged and heartened to fight and the enemy was frightened with the overwhelming number that appeared to them.There is a meaningful point in God's sending the angels to join the forces of the Muslims for the enemy on the opposite side were the infidels and the Satanic forces of fiendish zeal were with the enemy, and it was just and necessary that the Muslims also had been strengthened…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:127 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That He might cut off a part (A side) of those who believe not or cast them down so that they may retire disappointed. See 3:126

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:128 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nothing of the authority is for thee at all, whether He turneth unto them (mercifully) or chastiseth them, for verily, they are transgressors. This Verse indicates that the Holy Prophet, even in the worst of the miseries inflicted upon him, was ever concerned with the salvation of mankind. When he was so badly attacked by infidels and the hidden enemies of his, the hypocrites, in his own camp, professing themselves to be his companions, had deserted him in the heat of the battle, and he had fallen into a pit grievously wounded, even in that state of agony, he was so much mindful of, and concerned with the future of the people, that this Verse was revealed to say that he need not worry himself about the salvation of his enemies for God was fully aware of the unbounded mercy…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:129 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God's is whatever is in the heavens and whatever in the earth; He forgiveth whomsoever He pleaseth and punisheth whomsoever He pleaseth, for, Verily, God is the Oft-Forgiving (Ar. 'Ghafoor') , the Merciful (Ar. 'Raheem') . This Verse sounds a caution against the absolute propriety and the absolute independence of God whose pardon or punishment being meted out at His own will and pleasure.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed, there was a sign for you in the two hosts (which) met together in the (The Battle of Badr.) encounter; one host fighting in the path of God and the other disbelieving, (they') (The believers saw the dis-believers as only double in number.) saw them twice their number with their (own) sight (Refer to Verses. 8:44, 8:66.) of the eye; Verily God aideth with His (As Moses was aided by Aaron the Holy Prophet was aided with Ali who displayed the most, his faith in God on all occasions of the fight in the way of the Lord and remained steadfast, even when the Companions deseited the Holy Prophet and had fled away.) aid whomsoever He liketh; Indeed in this there is a lesson for those who have (sound) sight (The Conscience intact.) In the Battle of 'Badr' the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:130 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! Devour not interest doubling it over and again, and take shelter in God that ye may be successful. 'Az'aafan Muza'afah', i.e., multiplying over and above. Those who want to mean by this, only the compound interest to be forbidden and not the simple interest, interpret the words as ever and ever again, whereas the correct meaning of the words renders both the compound as well as the simple one to be forbidden. The term 'Az'aafan' meaning multiplying, refers to the amount and the term 'Muza'afan' meaning over and above refers to the term. (M.S. TH. etc.). This is to stop developing of ignoble egoistic vices in man which mar the moral progress and ruin the economic welfare of the individual members of the human society.(Note: What the banks in modern days award to their clients which…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:131 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Fear ye the Hell-fire that is prepared for the disbelievers. Inviting mankind to guard themselves against evil and to seek pardon and to hasten to forgive others.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:132 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And obey God and the Apostle (Muhammad) that ye may be shown Mercy. See 3:131

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:133 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And hasten unto (the means to obtain) forgiveness from your Lord (Refer to Verse 57:21.) and Paradise vast (Extent of which.) as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the pious (Who guard themselves against evil) ones. See 3:131

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:134 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who spend (The All-Perfect models divinely set up for the guidance of man in this regard, are the holy Ahl Al-Bayt purified by God himself. Refer to Verse 33:33.) (in alms) alike in prosperity and straitness, and who restrain (their) anger, and forgive (the faults of) men; for God loveth those who do good (Ar. 'Mohsineen.) (to others). Declared the Holy Prophet that "A charitable one is near to God (loved by God), near to Paradise (entitled to Paradise) and near to men (loved by the public), a miser is far away from God (hated by God), far away from Paradise (not entitled to Paradise), and far away from the public (hated by the public).""A charitable illiterate is more lovable with God than a miserly scholar."It is noteworthy as to how Islam aims at a voluntary restraint of anger,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:135 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who, when they do a shameful deed or commit a wrong to their (own) selves, remember God and implore for pardon for their sins; and who forgiveth sins except God? And who persist not (intentionally), in what they have done (The evil already committed unintentionally.) (amiss) while they know it. Sinning according to Islam is being cruel to one's own self for the sinner corrupts his own soul and entitles it to punishment.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:136 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: As for these, their reward is pardon from their Lord and gardens 'neath which rivers flow to abide therein; And excellent is the reward of those who act (righteously). The last words of this Verse indicate the importance that Islam stresses upon action in faith against mere ideological or theoretical belief.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:137 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed, there have already been before you examples, travel ye therefore in the earth and see what hath been the end of the rejecters (Those who disbelieve in the apostles of God) of (the Apostles of God) (This Verse clearly indicates how like the Israelites, most of the early converts to Islam were weak in faith, and how at every step the Israelites were assured by God thro' Moses, these converts to Islam were assured by God through the Holy Prophet-and how in spite of the divine assurance even some prominent Companions deserted the Holy Prophet, ran away from the battle fields leaving him in the midst of the enemies -Not once but repeatedly. (For the personnel see history)) 'Sunan', i.e., Ways and the matter of dealings. Here meaning God's ways of dealing with the righteous and the sinful ones.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:138 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This is (only) a clear statement (of events) for mankind, and a guidance and admonition for the pious ones. (Refer to Verses 3:143, 3:152.) It is a clear declaration that the Holy Qur'an can be a guidance not for all but only for the pious ones. A similar exposition has been made in 2:2. The question arises as to who are the pious ones, i.e., those who guard themselves against evil. The greatest evil is 'shirk' associating anything with God in authority. Hence the term 'Muttaqin' in its fulness applies to none but the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt who never even once adorned anybody besides God. And to know the correct identification of the 'Muttaqin' one must refer to 2:177.Hence it could be said that the Holy Qur'an was sent directly for the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt and mankind has to receive…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:139 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And lose (Slack not - Be steadfast.) ye not heart and grieve ye not, for ye shall gain the upper hand, if ye (only) be (true) believers (Refer to Verses 2:2; 2:177; 45:20.) On return to Madina from the Battle of Uhud the relatives mourned very much for those martyred and felt for the wounded ones. This Verse was revealed saying not to lose heart for any setback or grieve for any loss, prophesying the ultimate triumph, if they be sincere believers in God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It has been) made to seem attractively fair unto men, the love of the lusts for women and sons and the hoarded treasures of gold and silver and well-bred horses (Beautiful and Luxurious Conveyances like the costly cars of the modern days.) and cattle and tilth (The Zamindaries and the landed properties.) ; this is the provision of the life of this world, while God! Verily with Him is the best destination The words used in this verse are to be carefully noted, and the verse as a whole to be studied and understood with the meaning of the words and their construction. Mark the words 'love of desires' i.e. the mad passion to own things for the sake of owning them. Things necessary for life must be owned, the love to own such good things for use in the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:140 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If a wound hath afflicted you, a wound similar hath also afflicted the people (disbelievers); And these days (of varying fortunes) We bring about among men by turns, And that God may know (Make known or distinguished.) those who have (sincerely) believed, and that He may take witnesses (Martyr.) from among you; and God loveth not the unjust (Refer to Verse 29:3.) . The people fighting for Islam were not the only or exclusive sufferers, for the enemy had also suffered similar afflictions in spite of the tremendous strength and overwhelming power it had gathered, in spite of which had suffered the humiliating defeat.Those days or the events of success and defeat, gain and loss, and joy and afflictions are repeated as tests or trials to prove or to make manifest or to disclose for the knowledge of the others,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:141 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And that God may purge those who believe and destroy the infidels. Certainly, the genuine supporters of the Truth who stood by the Holy Prophet were proved at Uhud, against the hypocrites who deserted him and Islam and had run away, so far away from the battle-field that some of them did not return to Madina until three days after the event.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:142 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Imagine ye (O' Muslims!) that ye (all) would enter Paradise? When God knoweth (Distinguisheth.) yet not those (of you) who strove hard among you (in His way) and knoweth (Distinguisheth.) (also) the steadfast (Refer to Verse 47:31.) ? See 3:141

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:143 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And ye did indeed desire for death ere ye met it, so indeed ye have now seen it, even while ye look (Why do ye then flinch now?) (at it). After the Battle of Badr, when people heard of the miraculous victory the 313 Muslims had been blessed with against the fully equipped forces of 1,000 of the infidels, they had repentantly desired to have had been in the battle-field to have the distinguished honour of being either among the victors or among the martyrs. Now when the people mourned so much for those killed in Uhud and felt for the wounded ones in that battle, the Holy Prophet gave out the revelation of this Verse saying that they coveted to quote death and now when the occasion for it had occurred, they complainingly mourned for the dead and feel…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:144 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And Muhammad is not but an Apostle (In every word and action only apostolic, acting directly & implicitly under the divine will. Refer to Verses 53:2 - 53:5; 10:15; 47:2; 48:29; 3:138; 3:152.) , (Other) apostles have already passed away prior to him; Therefore, if he dieth or be slain, will ye turn upon your heels (Reference to the companions & the others who ran away from the battle fields and gave a false cry to the others 'Muhammad is dead return ye to your previous Creed (of idolatry)'. For the personal see history.) ? And he who turneth upon his heels will by no means do harm to God in the least, and shortly will God reward the grateful ones. This Verse was revealed in reply to the excuse given to the Holy Prophet by those who had fled…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:145 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is not for any soul to die except by God's permission, (according to) the Book (Ar. 'Kitaban'. See Verses 2:2; 2:177; 6:7; 13:38, 15:4; 39:23;45:20;46:30; 62:2; 78:29.) that fixes the term (of life); He who desireth (his) reward in this world, We give him thereof and he who desireth (his) reward in the hereafter, We give him thereof! And shortly We shall reward the grateful ones. This is said to tell the Muslims that death is wholly at the decision of God which is fixed in case of every individual. None can ever escape it, if it has to come at any moment fixed by God and none can hasten it, if it has not been destined by God to come. This is to encourage and prepare the believers for any fight in the cause of Truth. This same…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:146 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: How many a prophet hath fought with whom were myriads of Godly (Ar. 'Rabbiyoon'.) men, and they lost not heart at what befell (Inflicted.) them in the way of God nor did they weaken, nor did they demean (Abased.) themselves (before their enemies); And God loveth the steadfast (Patient ones.) ones. How many apostles of God have fought for truth along with myriads, huge armies of several thousands (M.S. T.S. etc.). But Sale, Palmer and Rodwell have wrongly interpreted this as: "How many prophets have encountered those who had myriads of troops." None of the other commentators have taken this meaning.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:147 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And their saying was nothing but that they prayed "O' Our Lord! forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs and set our feet firm and help us against the disbelieving people." This was the prayer of every apostle of God who fought for the cause of Right and died for it. Verse 147 says that such praying godly souls were granted the good both of this life and the hereafter.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:148 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God gave them the reward in this world and an excellent reward of the hereafter; And verily God loveth those who do good (Ar. Mohsineen.) (to others). See 3:147

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:149 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! if ye obey the disbelievers they will make you to turn on your heels so ye will turn back losers. Warning the Muslims against yielding themselves to the infidels for they would persecute them and would not rest until the Muslims renounce their faith. This is said to have been revealed when the Jews of Bani Qaniqaa endeavoured to set up quarrels between the two Muslim tribes Aus and Khazraj of the Ansars.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Shall I tell you of what is better than these?; for those who take shelter (The pious.) in God are gardens with their Lord, beneath which flow rivers, to abide in them and mates pure, and God's pleasure; and verily God is well aware of the servants" The life after death is only a continuation of the present life, heading towards the state of realisation and spiritual perfection which, is in store for every human soul but only for those sincerely desirous and have duly endeavoured for it. The march of life in the spiritual realm after death is only of upward trend, without any liability of going down if one does not go up, a stationary condition is also possible. To qualify for the bliss in the life after death, the essential condition is…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:150 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! God is your Guardian and He is the Best of the Helpers. Assuring the Muslims of God's help if they be sincere and steadfast in their faith, for God alone is their Lord and the Best Helper.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:151 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We will cast a dread into the hearts of the disbelievers because they have associated with God, that for which He hath sent down no authority and their abode shall be the fire (Hell.) ; And how bad is the abode of the unjust. God's work was quite obvious in Uhud. The enemy, i.e., the Meccans, were in four times greater number and were fully prepared and completely equipped. The Muslims were only one fourth the strength of their enemy. After themselves plunging into the most miserable and disadvantageous state owing to their own blunder, were in a miserable chaos and in a hopeless disorder liable to be very easily crushed and wiped out for ever. The enemy chose to fly away from the field terror-stricken and made their way back to Mecca dreading the Muslims who were themselves labouring…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:152 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed hath God made (Fulfil.) good to you His promise, when ye were extirpating them (The enemy at 'Uhud'.) by His permission, till when ye flinched (Disobeyed orders Refer to Verse 121.) and disputed about the command, and ye disobeyed, after that (He) had showed you that which ye loved; Of you some desire this world, and some hereafter, Then Ye turned you away from them (ran away), so that He may test (Make distinguished, Prove. Refer to Verse 3:139; 29:3; 67:2.) (prove) you (in the sincerity of your faith): and (in spite of this) He hath forgiven you; And verily God is the Lord of Grace (Gracious- full of grace Refer to Verses 3:139, 29:3, 67:2.) for the believers. (Refer to Verse 3:124; 3:138; 3:152 and 3:143.) This refers to the promise of help from God saying that…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:153 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Remember when ye ran (In the battle of Uhud -when all the Companions of the Holy Prophet fled away-only 'Ali and few others stood with him- and fought turning the defeat into victory for Islam. Refer to Verses 3:121; 3:151, 3:154.) off precipitately on the heights and (even) looked (Did not care for any one of them behind even for the Holy Prophet.) not back any one, while the Apostle (Muhammad) calling you from the rear! So He hath inflicted (upon) you with anguish after anguish (Or in exchange for sorrow.) , that ye might (learn) not to grieve at what ye lose (The booty.) , nor at what befell you; and God is (fully) aware of what ye do (The same deserters after the Holy Prophet posed themselves as the greatest devotees of God. the chiefs of the people…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:154 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then after the anguish God sent down security upon you: (in the form of) slumber over-come upon a group of you, while the other group who cared only for their own selves-thinking quite unjustly about God; thoughts of ignorance; Say they "Is there anything (Any share.) for us in the authority?" Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Verily the authority resteth wholly (In its entirety- Legislative, judiciary and administrative.) with God;" They hid in their selves what they would not reveal unto thee, Say they "Had we had anything (Any share.) in the authority (God's own, Belongs only to God. Refer to Verse 42:38.) , we would not have been slain at this place;" Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!)"Had ye remained in your homes they who were decreed to be slain would have gone forth to the places where they (now)…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:155 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily those of you who turned back on the day (Refer to Verse 138 143 152 When all companions ran away from the battle field deserting the Holy Prophet, and disappeared for days together. Only 'Ali Ibn Abu Talib and Hamza stood fast- Humza was martyred and 'Ali with a few others turned the defeat into a victory for Islam. For details see history.) (of Uhud) when the hosts met, (it was) only Satan made them slip on account of some of their (sinful) actions; But indeed God hath pardoned them; For God is Oft-Forgiving, Forbearing. The delinquency on the part of the deserters at Uhud was due to the hearts having been conditioned for ages together in idolatry and Satan still having easy access to their hearts which had still an opening in them for distrust to enter into…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:156 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' Ye who believe! be ye not like the disbelievers who said of their brethren when they travel in the earth or engaged in fight (in the way of God) "Had they been with us they would not have died and had not been slain" so that God may make this an intense regret in their hearts; and it is God Who giveth life and causeth to die; and God beholdeth what all ye do. By "their brethren" means the infidels relatives and friends who had embraced Islam and who were not safe while travelling and those who had to lay down their lives in the battles.The Muslims who deserted the Holy Prophet in Uhud and ran back to Madina were taunted by the infidels there saying that they (Muslims) would not have suffered or been slain if they had…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:157 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if ye be slain in the way of God or die, then pardon from God and mercy is better than all that they amass. The reward promised for dying in the cause of truth, is for the life after death. This indicates how much a Muslim has to be sure and convinced of the faith in God and the return for supporting God's cause, even at the cost of his own life. This is clear evidence of the actual realistic effect the teachings of the Holy Prophet had impressed upon the hearts of his followers within the few years of his mission. The true Muslims were now ready to lay down even their lives to seek God's pardon and His mercy.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:158 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For if ye die or be slain, Verily unto God (only) shall ye be gathered. See 3:157

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:159 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus it is a mercy of God that thou (The Holy Prophet.) art lenient unto them: Hadst thou been severe and hard-hearted, they would surely have dispersed away from around thee; Therefore forgive them and seek pardon for them; and take (Just to please them. Refer to Verse 42:38.) their counsel in the affair; But when thou art resolved, then put thou thy trust in God (And act.) ; For God loveth those who trust (in Him). The deserters in Uhud actually deserved to be punished but even in view of the grant ofpardon to them there remains no room for the recipients of the pardon to say that they actually deserved it or that they had been honourably acquitted of the charges against them. It is only that the punishment has been offered to be condoned and not the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who pray saying "O' Our Lord! Indeed, we believe, so forgive us our sins and save us from the torment of the (Hell) fire" The prayer is nothing but a preparation for the life hereafter. No radical change is possible in the spirituality of the individual, unless one endeavours hard for it and feels remorse for his failure in maintaining the original attachment to those who have earned God's pleasure and thus become one of the beloved or the blessed ones of God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:160 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Remember O' ye Believers!) If God helpeth you, none shall overcome you; but if He forsaketh you, who is he that would help you after that? On God then should the believers rely. The concluding word of the Verse is a suggestive statement about the believers depending upon none else but God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:161 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is not (Attributable to.) for any prophet (of God) to defraud; and he who defraudeth shall bring with him what he hath defrauded on the day of the Resurrection; Then shall every soul be paid what he hath earned and they shall not be dealt with unjustly. A cloth of some value was found missing from the booty collected at Badr. The hypocrites wanted to insinuate saying that the Holy Prophet might have appropriated it for himself without the knowledge of his people. This Verse is said to have been revealed on this occasion, but it is placed here to fit in with relation to unfaithfulness of the Archers posted at the pass in Uhud who doubting about their being deprived of their share in the booty left their position and got themselves busy in the plunder which brought…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:162 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is then he who abideth by the pleasure of God, like him who hath brought on himself the wrath from God, and whose abode shall be Hell? What an evil destination (it is). He who tenaciously follows the pleasure of God must necessarily in all arguments of logic be the one described in:"And of mankind is he who would sell himself, seeking the pleasure of God; and God hath compassion on (His) bond-men." (2:207)The one who stood by the Holy Prophet fighting in the cause of God to the end. And he who has made himself deserving of the wrath of God must naturally be those who fled away from the battle-field described in 8:16 and Verse 154."Whoso on that day turneth his back to them, unless manoeuvring for battle or intent to join a company, he truly hath incurred…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:163 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They are of diverse ranks with God; and verily God beholdeth what (all) they do. Faith as well as infidelity has varying degrees of reward and punishment from God. As all the righteous are not of one and the same level, infidelity or evil has also got various degrees of gravity.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:164 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed God hath conferred His favour upon the believers when He raised up an apostle Recite (Muhammad) among them from their own selves, to rehearse (Recite.) unto them His signs, and to purify them (Ahl Al-Bayt not included were purified by the God himself. Refer to Verse 33:33.) , and to teach them the Book (Qur'an) and Wisdom; though before this they were in manifest error (Refer to Verses 2:129, 2:151, 49:17, 62:2.) . The people who assist the Holy Prophet and suffer for the cause of Islam need not think that they are in the least obliging him in any way. On the contrary the people are informed that they are under the obligation of God for His guiding them to the right path of life on earth through the Holy Prophet whose sufferings are all on their behalf…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:165 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! When a misfortune befell you (at Uhud) while ye had already inflicted twice as much (on the disbelievers)', ye said "Whence is this?" Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "this is from your selves; Verily God hath power over all things." The infidels had suffered twice as much-once in Badr and again at Uhud.There were many half-hearted converts to Islam who began to waver after the disaster of Uhud. Their faith resembled that of those who followed Moses who doubted and returned to infidelity at the slightest untoward happening or at their facing any difficult situation. The disaster was due to their own delinquency and love of booty.All who had joined the ranks of the Muslims were not sincere1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:166 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what befell you on the day when the two hosts met, was by God's permission and that He might know (Distinguish.) (test) the believers. ('That God may know')-i.e., that God might make it known-or obvious to the others.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:167 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And that He might know (Distinguish.) the hypocrites (There were three groups of the people 1) The believers 2) The Dis-believers 3) The Hypocrites. But there is no mention at all of the third group the hypocrites after the Holy prophet. There is a complete chapter on the hypocrites' chap 63. Is it that they waited for the departure of the Holy Prophet and at it they all became sincere believers or at any time they all died a wholesale death none says anything about them. Or those who turned hostile to the House of the Holy Prophet and Inflicted miseries on the Ahl Al-Bayt were the hypocrites referred in the Holy Qur'an. Chap: 63.) ; and was said unto them (The hypocrites - Who played double game.) "Come! Fight in the way of God! or (at least) repel (the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:168 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (These are those) who said unto their brethren while themselves sat (at home) "Had they (the Martyrs) obeyed us, they had not been slain;" Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Ward off' from yourselves death if ye be truthful." The hypocrites taunted against the martyrs of Uhud that if they (the martyrs) had stayed behind with them obeying them (the hypocrites) they would not have been killed. It is obvious by these verses, under what a hostile atmosphere, both openly and concealed, the Holy Prophet carried out his mission.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:169 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Reckon not those who are slain in the way of God, to be dead; Nay! alive (Thus, the honour or Salutation to the martyrs is not the honour and salutation to the dead but to the alive.) they are with their Lord being sustained. This Verse establishes beyond all doubts, the immortality of those who lay down their lives in the way of God, their being alive and getting their sustenance from their Lord. It is a clear and a plain reply to answer the critics against honouring those who have died in God's way. The Ahmadi commentator has quietly passed over this Verse without any interpretation for the meaning is too obvious and plain to bear any figurative interpretation1.So far as personal immortality is concerned the case of martyrs, and other holy men is not distinct from the personal…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The patient, and the truthful, and the devout (ones), and those who spend (in the way of God) and those who seek forgiveness e're (Before.) dawn This verse gives the qualities that entitle one to the grace of God, and gives the clue to the special potency and effectiveness of prayer in the early hours of the dawn.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:170 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Rejoicing in what God of His Grace hath granted them, rejoicing for those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that no fear shall come on them nor shall they grieve. See 3:169

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:171 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They rejoice in the Grace (What they have received from the Lord.) from God and (His) bounty (The realisation of God's reward for all believers.) and in fact, God suffereth not to be lost the reward of the Believers. See 3:169

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:172 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (As far) those who did respond (Read this in the light of Verses 3:138, 3:143 and 3:152 with the notes thereon.) to the call of God and the Apostle (Muhammad) (even) after wounds inflicted on them; such of those who do good (to others) and guard (them-selves) against evil, shall have a great reward. The Muslims pursued the Meccan army to about eight miles away to a place, 'Hamra al-Asad.' The Meccans in spite of their overwhelming numbers, dared not to encounter the Muslims, this could not be but by the heavenly awe caused for the purpose.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:173 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those unto whom said the people (Read this in the light of Verses 3:138, 3:143 and 3:152 with the notes thereon.) , "Verily have the people mustered (strong) against you, therefore fear them!" It only increased their faith; and said they, "God is (quite) sufficient for us and the most excellent Protector is (He)." While retreating Abu-Sufyan the chief of the Meccan army had challenged to attack next year at Badr. The challenge was accepted by 'Ali saying, 'God is sufficient for us.' At the appointed time the Holy Prophet went out with his followers to meet the Meccans, but they did not appear.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:174 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They returned, therefore, with the favour from God and (His) Grace. Without any evil even touching them and they followed the pleasure of God; and God is the Lord of Mighty Grace. See 3:173

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:175 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is only that Satan frighteneth (Against Supporting the Holy Prophet.) his friends (against supporting the Prophet), Fear them not! but fear ye Me! If ye be (true) believers (Refer to Verses 3:138, 3:143 and 3:152.) . See 3:173

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:176 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Let not those grieve thee, who vie in haste in infidelity, verily, never shall they harm God one whit; God intendeth that He assigneth not for them any share in the life hereafter; For them is a great chastisement. This is a prophetic assurance to the Holy Prophet that the people who aid the infidels will never be successful in inflicting any loss either to the cause of God, i.e., Islam or to the Holy Prophet himself.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:177 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily those who purchase (Refer to Verse 3:185.) infidelity at the cost of faith, never shall they harm God one whit! For them is a painful chastisement. See 3:176

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:178 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Let not those who disbelieve think that our giving them respite is good for their selves; We only give respite to them that they may increase in sins, and for them is a disgraceful chastisement. Let not the believers be beguiled by the infidels prospering in any way in this world, if they do, thinking that they are blessed by God, or their infidelity has been neglected by God. Their prosperity is nothing but an opportunity to them, to increase their infidelity as much as they might like to do. The ultimate end of all that, will be a disgraceful chastisement. It is just to allow the cup of their iniquity to be full and the appetite for sin, to grow more and more as the individual goes on from sin to sin. The natural consequence is that the sinner…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:179 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is not for God to leave the believers in the state in which ye are, until He hath distinguished (Refer to Verse 8:37.) the wicked (Ar. 'Khabees' The impure.) from the good (Ar. 'Tayyab' The pure.) and it is not for God to acquaint you with the unseen; But God chooseth from the Apostles whomsoever He pleaseth. So ye believe then in God and His apostles: and if ye believe and Guard yourselves (against evil) then for you is a great reward. God did not will leave the believers to remain mixed with the hypocrites and the infidels as they were, but to separate the believer from their counter.In regards to the knowledge of the unseen. The Holy Prophet announced that he knew every true believer from the non-believers to the Day of Judgment. The hypocrites ridiculed the claim…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God (Refer to: 57:25, 3:6, 4:162 5:8 15:27 29:49. Refer to Verses 2:112; 3:84; 42:14.) (Himself) witnesseth that there is no god but HE, and (so do) the angels and those possessed of knowledge, (See note to Verse 6 for 'Rasikhoona fil ilm'.) standing firm for justice (Not inclined to any extreme.) ; (there is) no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise God Himself witnessing to His Own Unity, is quite logical and meaningful, for unless God Himself, out of His Infinite Mercy, declares to us about His Own Existence, how can any of His creation by itself ever know about the truth about Him.All that we can say is, that God, there can be One and only One God and never more than One.'Qaiman-bil-qist' standing or established firmly for justice and maintaining it. In the first place, any…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:180 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And let not those who are niggardly in giving what God hath granted them of His Grace, reckon it is good for them; Nay! it is bad for them; That which they have been niggardly of, shall shortly be clung to their necks on the Day of Resurrection; And God's (alone) is the heritage of the heavens and the earth, And Verily God, of what ye do, is fully aware (Refer to Verses 3:115; 3:183; 9:36.) . The condemnation of niggardliness given in this Verse is a pen-picture of the godly mind of the Holy Prophet which was full of care and pain for the needy. Charity purifies our character. There cannot be a greater admonition to the miser against his withholding that which he can easily spare from his wealth, for the needy. Whatever kind of wealth one hoards…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:181 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Surely hath God heard the saying of those who say "Aye, God is poor, and we are rich (This is the Jewish mentality and attitude which is true of people attaching importance to temporal possessions, power and wealth who fail to value the Spiritual and Godly force and power. Refer to Verses 2:247; 5:64; 47:38.) " Certainly, shall we record what they say and their slaying the Prophets unjustly and We shall say "Taste ye the torment of burning." Charity or spending money to help the cause of truth or to help the needy is metaphysically described in Islam as giving to God Himself. Subscriptions were raised by the Muslims to defend Islam against the unprovoked aggressions from the Non-Muslims, terming such monetary help to the cause of the faith as a goodly loan to God:"Who is it that will…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:182 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This, is for what your (own) hands have forwarded before you and because God is not (in the least) unjust to (the) servants. Here the infidels are warned saying: 'do not think that your evil deeds end here and have no echo in your life hereafter. God is All-Just every evil doer shall be duly punished.'"Whoso doeth right it is for his self and who doeth wrong it is against it. And thy Lord is not at all a tyrant to His slaves." (41:46)"Whoso doeth right, it is for his self, and whoso doeth wrong, it is against it. And then unto your Lord ye will be brought back." (45:15)"And whoso doeth good of an atom's weight will see it then." (99:7)"And whoso doeth evil an atom's weight will see it then." (99:8)

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:183 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (To those) who say, "Verily God hath covenanted with us that we believe not in any apostle until he presenteth to us an offering which is devoured by fire (from heaven)', Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Indeed did come unto you apostles before me with miracles and with that which ye (now) said; Why then did ye slay them? if ye be truthful (Refer to Verse 35:25.) ." The Mosaic law had burnt offerings Lev. 1/9. Lev. 8/18, Deut. 33/10."But his inwards and his legs shall he wash in water, and the priest shall burn all on the altar, to be a burnt sacrifice, an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the Lord." Lev. 1/9."And he brought the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands upon the head of the ram."…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:184 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they belie thee; then verily have already been belied apostles before thee (who) came with clear evidences (miracles) and the scriptures and the illuminating Book (The Book of one and the same. All the different Scriptures are the various aspects or the versions of one and the same Universal Book. Refer to verse 15:1.) . 'Zabur', the Scriptures given to Apostles of God and the illuminating Book may be the 'Torah' given to Moses and 'Evangel' given to Jesus which contained clear guidance.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:185 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Every self-tastes (Everything besides God is ever undergoing change after change. Thus, everything save God is ever tasting death. Nothing besides God is permanent or stationary in its existence. Permanence absolute is only for God and for none besides Him.) death; and verily ye shall be paid in full your recompenses on the Day of Resurrection; and whoso is removed away from the (Hell) fire and admitted into Paradise, has indeed gained his object; and the life of this world is not, but a provision of vanity (Ar. 'Ghoroor'.) . 'Kullu nafsin' - A strong conviction about the certainty of death makes one automatically reform himself and if he be sufficiently wise to get prepared for the inevitable event and be ready to meet it, with all the preparedness one wants for himself, lest it may surprise him when he…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:186 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Certainly ye shall be tried in your possessions and in your (own) selves; and certainly ye shall hear from those who have been given the Book before you and those who join other gods with God, much annoyance; and if ye be patient and guard yourselves (against evil) then verily that is a matter of (very great) resolve (Result of firm determination of affairs.) . This happened and is still happening in a constitutional way-Muslims are still persecuted and their properties confiscated, their lives have been mercilessly taken for their merely being Muslims.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:187 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (Recall thou O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) when God took a pledge (Compare this to the pledge taken from the Muslims at 'Ghadir Khumm' under Verse 5:67.) from those who were given the Book; "Ye shall surely make it known to mankind and ye shall not hide it (The Book.) ; then they cast it behind their backs and bought (Exchanged it for a small return.) therewith a small price (See Verse 176.) ; How bad (then is what they purchase (Bargain.) )." Refers to those who had been given the Scriptures viz. the Jews and Christians. The covenant was to make known to the people the description of the Last Apostle of God which had been given in their holy books, but they did not abide by it for the sake of worldly profit which act is condemned as…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:188 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Think not that those who rejoice for what they have brought on and love that they be praised for what they have not done, and think not that they would escape the chastisement; for them is a grievous torment (Compare to Verse 3:177.) . See 3:187

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:189 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God's (alone) is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth; and God hath power over all things (Refer to Verse 3:179.) . This Verse is a repeated assertion of the idea given in the concluding words of Verse 179.This idea has been repeatedly mentioned at the end of many other verses to sink it deep into the minds of men and women that there is none for them to worship except God who alone is the Creator Lord Master of the whole universe.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the religion with God is ISLAM (Total Submission to God's will.) (Submission to God's will), and those whom the Book had been given (Reference is to those who after believing in the Book of God and then differed from it - applicable to those who differed after embracing Islam. Refer to Verses 85 and 86.) did not differ but after the knowledge (of the Truth) had come unto them, out of envy among themselves; and whosoever disbelieveth in the signs (Including the apostles and the Holy Imams.) of God, then, verily, God is quick in reckoning 'Al-Islam' literally means surrender or submission. As the name of the religion, Islam, means - surrender or the submission of the self of the adherent to the will of the Lord. The act of submission to God is referred to in Verse 2:112…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:190 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, in the creation of the heavens and the earth a nd the alternation of the night and the day, there are signs for men who possess wisdom. Though the attention insisted towards the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the change with night and day, seem to be very simple but the awakened mind, particularly of the scientists with the knowledge of the heavenly bodies and the constellations and those who are busy in their study of the deposits of the earth etc., know the significance of this drawing of the attention towards the factors mentioned in this Verse.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:191 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who remember God standing, and sitting and reclining on their sides and think (seriously) in the creation of the heaven and the earth, saying "O' Our Lord! Thou hast not created (all) this in vain! Glory be to Thee! Save us then from the torment of the (Hell) fire." Mark the high position of the sincerity and the adoration these worshippers have, in the view of God that the words of their utterance of His glory, have been absorbed as it were in the revelation. They remain so much wholly engrossed in remembering the Lord that every moment of their lives in whatever activity they may be, they are mindful of God's glory, and they adorn it celebrating its praise which is commended in this Verse.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:192 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' Our Lord! Whomsoever Thou causeth to enter the (Hell) fire, surely, Thou hast put him to disgrace; there is not, for the unjust, any of the helpers. These verses contain the words of the prayer of those mentioned in the preceding Verse.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:193 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' Our Lord! We have indeed heard the voice of a Crier (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) (Apostle), calling (us) unto faith, saying "Believe ye in your Lord!" and we did believe. O' Our Lord! therefore "Forgive us then our sins and remove away from us our evil deeds, and cause (Fulfil or conclude the term of life.) us to die with the virtuous ones. (Refer to Verses 23:109; 40:7; 3:16.) " See 3:192

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:194 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' Our Lord! and give us what Thou didst promise us through thy apostles, and disgrace us not on the Day of Resurrection; Verily, Thou breakest not Thy promise. See 3:192

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:195 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So their Lord did respond to them (saying) "I will not suffer the work of any of you that worketh to be lost, be he male or female (Men and Women equally rewardable and punishable for the good and the evil they do in this life.) , the one of you being from the other, They, therefore, who did migrate and were turned out of their homes and suffered in My way and who fought and were slain, I will most certainly blot out their sins from them, and I will most certainly admit them into gardens beneath which flow streams; A reward from God! and God! Verily with Him (only) is the Excellent Reward (Refer to Verse 16:96.) ." There is no distinction of sex in according the reward for righteousness. A righteous one shall be duly rewarded. This…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:196 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Let not deceive (Enamour.) thee (Address to the Muslims i.e. those who follow thee.) the (prosperous) going about (In glamour and pride.) of those who disbelieve in the cities (The prosperous one in the cities. A warning sounded to the people through the Holy Prophet against getting misled by the prosperity of the disbelievers.) . See 3:195

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:197 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: A brief enjoyment (it is)! Thereafter their abode is Hell and how bad the resting place (it is)! See 3:195

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:198 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But as to those who fear (the wrath of) their Lord, for them are the gardens beneath which flow the rivers, therein shall they abide for ever. Such is their reception (Entertainment.) with God; and whatever is with God is the best for the righteous ones. See 3:195

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:199 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And Verily among the people of the Book are those who believe in God, and in what (The Holy Qur'an.) hath been sent down unto you and in what hath been sent down unto them, humbling (Ar. 'Khusho'.) themselves before God, They sell not the signs of God for a mean price; These! for them is their recompense with their Lord; aye! God is quick in reckoning. See 3:195

item.description: This, because they say "The (Hell) fire shall by no means touch us but for (some) numbered (Counted.) days, and deceiveth them in the matter of their religion what they have forged (Applicable to the modern days irreligious arrogants and their conjectures.)" In continuation of the same line of argument, the verse condemns the people of the Book who seek judicial favour other than what is established by the scripture. The mental background for this rebellious tendency of the people of the Book, is the fanciful belief that the ultimate salvation rests in the mere declaration of the faith, for misdeeds and wrong actions, if there be any punishment, it would be only temporary.This concocted fanciful vanity will disappear with reference to what is said in the preceding verse of the interrelation of the action and the notion. (A.P.)

item.description: Said he (Zachariah.) "My Lord! appoint (Fix.) Thou a sign for me;" Said He (God.) "The Sign for Thee shall be that thou shalt not speak unto men for three days except by signs; and remember God much and glorify Him in the evening and (early) (in) the day break. (Refer to: 19:10.)" Zachariah in his surprise wanted a sign of God's promise being actually fulfilled in his hopeless age. He was informed that the sign would be that he would not be able to speak for three days. The demand for a sign was not due to any incredulity on the part of Zachariah but it was owing to his curiosity to know as to how it will come to pass (i.e., how he and his wife would be rejuvenated). Verily Thou art the Gatherer of mankind unto the Day (of Judgment) about which there is no doubt; (Be Merciful to us then); Verily God faileth not His promise The prayer in this verse and in the preceding one, refers to the ideal or the life-object of those 'Raasikhoona fil ilm.' They pray for their welfare in the life hereafter and on the Day of Judgment This prayer itself speaks loudly that the object of the lives of those 'Raasikhoona fil ilm' is nothing connected with their welfare in this life which, they know it for certain, is nothing but a passing show.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:90 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily (Refer to: 4:137.) , those who disbelieve after their believing, then increase in their infidelity; never shall their repentance be accepted, and these are they who have gone astray Like the Jews who believed in Moses and Torah and disbelieved in Jesus and the Evangel, and added to their disbelief by disbelieving in the Holy Prophet Muhammad. This verse has an application also to those who believed in the Holy Prophet and again they disbelieved and they further insisted upon their infidelity or disbelief, never will their repentance be accepted.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:91 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, never shall be accepted even earthful of gold from any of them, if he should offer it in ransom, these, for them awaiteth a painful torment and for them (there shall be) no helpers This indicates the gravity or the seriousness of the sin and the definite decision or the finality of the decree of the punishment for it.This is a warning against those who think that by their lavish charities and extravagance, they can secure the pleasure of God and the bliss in the hereafter, though they had disregarded God's laws and commands in this life1. It shows that the quantity of the charity for the redemption from the divine punishment, is of no use with a rebellious heart and indifferent attitude towards God's commandments and laws, and no…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:92 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Never shall ye attain to righteousness until ye give (With love willingly. Refer to Verse 2:254.) away (in the way of your Lord) of what ye love (Note: no particular Commodity is mentioned But that which is loved the most.) ; and of whatsoever ye give, Verily, God knoweth it. This Verse rings the death-knell of the vain glory of the one, be he from any class of the social order or of any descent or of any status or position, who poses as a righteous one without being duly selfless. Mark the wide implication of the word 'of whatsoever ye love.' The Verse fixes no special commodity to be given away, nor does it prescribe any particular limit. In regards to that which is to be given is left to the degree of the attachment of the individual to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:93 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: All food was allowed (Refer to Verse 6:146.) to the children of Israel except what Israel (Israel, the other name of Isaac the Second Son of Abraham.) (Jacob) had (himself) forbidden before the Torah (Pentateuch -the Scripture given to Moses Ar. 'Taurat.) (Pentateuch); was sent down; Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad to the Jews) "Bring ye hither then the Torah and read it (out), if ye be truthful." The Jews objected to the use of certain foodstuffs by the Muslims, whereas in the original Law of Moses all such foods had been allowed. But the Jews did not possess the whole of the Law, except a few traditions, reminiscences and some distorted fragments of the original scripture left behind by Moses. The Jewish faith was based upon an admixture of reliable and unreliable extracts and their own folklore. Hence the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:94 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then whoever fabricateth (forge- concoct. Refer to Verse 61:7.) a lie about God, after this, these it is that are the unjust. Changing the meaning of the word of God or the word of His apostles, is fabricating a lie against God and those who do this are the unjust ones or the tyrants. This refers to the Jews who misinterpreted the meaning of the Law or the teachings of Moses. The implication of this decree against the act, extends to everyone who commits it, be that in the later age, even among the Muslims.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:95 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "God hath spoken the Truth, follow therefore the creed (Ar. 'Millat'.) (Islam) of Abraham the upright (Ar. 'Hanif.) in faith; and he was not of the polytheists (Ar. 'Mushrikeen'. Those who associate others with God in authority. Refer to Verses 2:130, 2:135.) ". Abraham's faith in God, has been declared as an ideal and Abraham a model for all true believers in God. The Islamic belief rests upon the Absolute indivisible Unity without any distinction between the entity and the attributes, which was also the faith of Abraham1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:96 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily (Refer to Verses 2:125, 2:127 22:29, 22:33.) , the First House (The Kaba, Ar. 'Awwala Baitin'. For Ahl Al-Bayt, see 33:33.) made for mankind is the one at Mecca, Blessed and a Guidance for the worlds. 'Bakka' i.e., 'Mecca'-derived from 'Taba'k' i.e., crowding of men. The other version is that the name of the place has been derived from the meaning 'Breaking of the neck', for, whenever it was invaded by any tyrant, his neck had been broken i.e., he was defeated and crushed. Another version is that 'Bakka' means the Holy House of the 'Ka'ba'. It is reported that it relates to the House of Worship of the True God, on earth that was providentially raised even before Abraham, and Abraham and Ishmael only renewed and cleaned it. The antiquity of the Ka'ba has been admitted by Sir…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:97 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In it are clear signs; the standing place of Abraham; and whoever entereth it is secure (This Security was denied to the third Holy Husayn, son of 'Ali and Fatimah - the Grandson of the Holy Prophet.) ; and (purely) for God, is incumbent (God's decree.) upon mankind, the pilgrimage to the House, for those who can afford to journey thither; And whoever denieth then Verily (He should know.) , God is 'Self-sufficiently (Ar. 'Ghani'- Totally Needless- Free from needs. Refer to Verse 2:125.) independent of the worlds. 'The Open or the Clear signs' Every enemy of the Truth who attempted to invade the place or to take possession of it, was made to suffer a crushing defeat. The sincere devotees of God pray around it.'Standing place of Abraham.' The stone upon which Abraham, the Model Believer in the Only…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:98 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "O' People (Those given heavenly Scriptures through the apostles from God.) of the Book! why disbelieve ye the Signs of God? While Verily, God is a witness upon what ye do." It is an exhorting note of warning and guidance to those already given the holy scriptures through the previous apostles from God-particularly the Jews and the Christians who in spite of their knowledge of the truthfulness of the mission of the Holy Prophet and Islam, which had been foretold in their holy Books, defy, and disbelieve in it.Wherever Qur'an addresses the people of the Book and reproaches them for their mischievous deviation from the Right Path commonly prescribed by all the scriptures, it should not be taken as confined only to the Jews and the Christians who opposed Islam and the Holy Prophet at…

item.title: bil-Quran: Aal-i-Imraan:99 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "O' people of the Book! why hinder ye, him who believeth, from the path of God? and seek to make it crooked? whereas ye are its witness (Know it – Aware of.) ; And God is not heedless of what ye do." See 3:98

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He frowned and he turned away The occasion for the revelation of this chapter was a historic incident which took place. Once the Holy Prophet was with some chieftains of the Quraish when Abdullah Ibn-Maktoom who was blind and was one of the intimate companions of the Holy Prophet came to the Holy Prophet. The Holy Prophet received him with honour and pleasure and gave him the place closest to him. Since Abdullah was poor and blind, the chieftains of the Quraish looked down upon him, and did not like the honour done and the place given to him by the Holy Prophet in their own presence and one of them frowned at Abdullah and sat turning his back to him. This displeased God, and Gabriel brought this Surah and revealed it to the Holy Prophet then and there.This Surah…

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: From him wilt thou be indifferent See 80:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! but it (the Qur'an) is a reminder The Reminder (The Holy Qur'an) from God or the faith it preaches, is universal in its application - none should be excluded on the merit of any worldly calculation of wealth or poverty, the individual being high or low. The craving for spiritual growth, if with the necessary earnestness, must be given preference if it be needed.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So, let whosoever pleaseth, mind it The choice to accept the Holy Qur'an as the Word of God and to abide by it, is left to every individual man and woman.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It is written) in the Books (Sohof.) greatly honoured. (Refer to: 56:77, 56:78.) The truth about the Unity of God had been in all the previously revealed scriptures which are undoubtedly the honoured scripts.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Exalted high, purified See 80:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In the hands (Scribes.) of the deputy (The divine representative entities - either angels, or the prophets or the Imams.) angels i.e., The Holy Books have been either in the hands of the angels who conveyed them to the apostles of God or in the hands of those who have been purified by God Himself1. i.e., the purified ones are only the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt, i.e., the Holy Prophet, his godly daughter Lady Fatimah and the Twelve Holy Imams viz., Ali, his two sons, Hasan and Husayn, and nine Holy Imams in the seed of Husayn.The angels or those pious ones who preserved the Word of God in its original purity, recorded in writing.The divine representative entities are either angels, prophets or the Imams. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Noble, virtuous The quality of the scribes. There can never be any other than those whom God Himself purified1, i.e., the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Cursed be man! How ungrateful is he? The trend of the address, which is to those who disbelieve the Holy Qur'an, clearly indicates that the matter of this Surah is an admonition to the disbelievers or those half-hearted converts who still, even after embracing the faith, lacked conviction, as one of them proved and himself declared to be the doubter about bonafide of the Holy Prophet's position as the apostle of God on the day of Hudaibiyya.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Of" what (What an insignificant thing.) thing did He (God.) create him? Man is reminded of his humblest origin as a life germ and the ultimate and as the dust, to be raised again at the will of the Lord. About the origin of man1 - About man's rising again2.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Of a Seminal - a drop (Refer to: 76:2, 86:6.) ; He created him, then fixed its measure See 80:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Because came unto him the blind man The blind man is the reference to Abdullah Ibn Maktoom. Note the address is to the second person, i.e., to the Holy Prophet, but it is meant for the companion.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (And) then the way (for him) He made it easy (Refer to: 76:3.) See 80:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then He causeth him to die, and got him buried See 80:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then, when He willeth, He will again raise (Refer to: 22:55.) him (to life) See 80:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! he hath fulfilled not what He (God.) bade him Refers to man's deviating from the right path of the faith and the prescribed conduct of life.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then, let man look at his food Man is reminded of the bounties of God, showered on him, upon which rests his life and the life of all the creatures serving Him.About the provision made for man, of the cattle1.The Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq says concerning verse 24: ''Man should also look at the knowledge which he obtains and not to see from what source he gets it" The Creator who was so careful about providing man with physical sustenance undoubtedly will be much more careful about providing proper nourishment for his mental and spiritual development. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That it was We Who poured down water in an abundant pouring See 80:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then We cleft the earth, with a (necessary) cleaving See 80:24

item.description: And caused We to grow' therein the grain See 80:24
