item.description: And grapes and the vegetables See 80:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Olive and the Palm See 80:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what maketh thee to know that he would cleanse himself The questioning in this verse clearly indicates that the doubt about Abdullah being benefited by the talk with the Holy Prophet or not, could have been in the mind of one who had not yet embraced the faith, and which could never have occurred to an Apostle of God who has been sent to preach the faith to one and all, irrespective of any worldly position of the people. The questioning clearly indicates that the addressee was someone other than the Holy Prophet. The factor which this verse wants to preach, i.e., no spiritual value should be assigned to material wealth and the prospects of guidance being effective or not, should not be measured by any one's economic position in life or his influence in the society.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And gardens enclosed, thick with trees See 80:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And fruits and the herbage See 80:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: A provision (Refer to: 79:33.) for you and your cattle See 80:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But when cometh the deafening Trumpet Blast This verse repeats the warning to man against the great Day of Judgment, which is sure to come, relating how violent will be the dawn of the day and in what agony and tumult will be mankind that everyone will be for himself forgetting the closest ties of even the nearest relations, his own parents, spouses and issues. No friend will even enquire about a friend1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That day man will fly from his (own) brother See 80:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (from) his mother and (from) his father See 80:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (from) his wife and (his) children See 80:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For every man (Every one of them.) of them on that day will have a concern enough to make him heedless (of others) See 80:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (there shall be) faces on that day radiant This will be the state of the happiness and the joy of the faithful and the righteous ones.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Laughing, joyous See 80:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or he warned, and profiteth him the warning? What is wanted to acquire knowledge is the will to learn. This essential urge in any poor man, may help him to grow more in spiritual excellence than the arrogant self-exalting wealthy one puffed up of his riches and position.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (there shall be) faces on that day on them shall be dust This refers to the fate of the disbelievers and the wicked ones.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Darkness shall cover them See 80:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These are they who are the disbelievers, the wicked See 80:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: As for him who thinketh himself independent (on account of his wealth) It is the poor who by nature or necessity, turn to God and become godly to earn His grace and mercy which they need very badly. The arrogant wealthy ones in their self-sufficiency always rebel against the laws of God and transgress the prescribed limits and if they ever join the ranks of faithful, it would be only when it profits them and gives them an advantageous position in their life and society or for the promotion of their worldly interest. Faith needs humility and naturally goes with meekness and the humble.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Unto him dost thou attend The divine will is opposed to any attention paid to such arrogant one who looked down at Abdullah Ibn-Maktoom for his poverty and being blind and helpless.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It shall be no blame on thee if cleansed not himself It was not the concern of anyone if the poor man did not benefit himself by the preachings of the Holy Prophet.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But as to him (Abdullah ibn Makhtoom.) who cometh unto thee striving in earnest The reference is to Abdullah Ibn-Maktoom.

item.title: bil-Quran: Abasa:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And feareth he (at heart) Attention should be paid first to the one who comes striving with earnestness, be he poor and lowly in his position, it is nothing to do with his receiving the knowledge, he comes for.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) By the Noonday (Radiation) (Brightness) (Refer to: 94:5, 94:6.) 'Doha', i.e., the glory of the earliest moments of the dawn that heralds the arrival of the light of the sun, which gradually increases in its brightness and heat1. It is practically the resurrection of the light of the day and its activities when after dark, stillness or quietness of the night, the life on earth is once again quickened. The darkness of the night does not mean that God has forsaken the light for all times and similarly the stillness or the quietness of the night does not mean that the daily life and its activities have once for all been forsaken.The darkness, and its quietness, has to go and in its place light and activity has again to be returned. The darkness and its quietness…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And as to the beggar, chide him not! 'Sayil', i.e., a seeker need not always be a Begger asking for any pecuniary charity. It may as well refer to the seeker of knowledge. Taking the meaning as a Begger, we are warned against rebuking them or treating them with the least hardship or scorn.The Holy Prophet said that ''If any seeker comes to thee even mounted on a horse even then, return him not disappointed. Even then he has a right over thee to help him as much as thou canst do it"Though begging is condemned in Islam, yet as the Holy Prophet has suggested in one of his sayings - If a person gives up his self-respect and stretches out his hand in begging, he should not be further humiliated by being chided. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And as to the bounties of thy Lord, thou announce (Or remember or Let mankind know that it is God who bestows bounties and grace and none else.) (them unto others) Man is enjoined to be always grateful and thankful to God's grace and bounties and be mindful of his grace and mercy. He who does not thank for a little will not thank for much also. Man must always be celebrating the grace and the bounties he receives from the Lord, before the others.To make it known to the people by contribution - not boastfully. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the Night when it darkeneth (Refer to: 94:5, 94:6.) ! Things or qualities are understood better by the contrast with their opposites. The darkness, the silence, the stillness of the night is mentioned to compare and contrast with the light, the life and the activity of the day. An insight into the marvels of the phenomenon active on the wonderful forces of nature, will help man to realise the real significance of bringing such daily occurrences to witness the greatness and the Glory of the Almighty Author of the Universe.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hath forsaken not thee thy Lord, nor hath He been displeased (with thee)! In the early stages of the ministry, there was some suspense or a short interval between a revelation and another. The pagans of Mecca taunted that God had forsaken the Holy Prophet and started a slander to the effect. But neither this nor even the worst of the torturous persecution had in the least affected the feelings of the Holy Prophet, though an apostle of God like Jesus is reported by the Christians themselves to have cried in the agony, ''My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?"1 the Crier was not in fact Jesus, the Spirit of God, but the one crucified in his stead.The brief pause is said to be only of a short duration viz. two or three days (SB.). The occasion was…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily the end is better for thee than the beginning (of life) (For in spite of the ups and downs, he is in constant progress towards infinite perfection. See 20:114.) ! This refers to the great promise of the Lord to the Holy Prophet that greatness in this world and also in the hereafter, will be his.Because in spite of the ups and downs, he is in constant progress towards infinite perfection1. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And soon will give thee thy Lord that thou shalt be well pleased! The grant to the utmost satisfaction or the pleasure of the Holy Prophet, could never be restricted to anything of this material world, which is low, mean and strictly temporary. It is the right of intercession for the sinners. It is said that the Holy Prophet said that he will not be pleased even if a single believer in God, is left unredeemed of his sins and admitted to the bliss in the heaven. The granting mentioned, is indefinite, anything indefinitely mentioned means everything possible under the term. The grant or the gift is always according to the position or the greatness or the excellence of the giver. The one who grants here is the All-Merciful, All-Mighty and All-Divine and the Omnipresent Being with all His divine…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Found He not thee an orphan, and sheltered (thee) (Refer to: 4:113, 53:2.) ? Commentators say that this is a reference to the providential protection which was divinely arranged for the Holy Prophet through guardian after guardian when he was orphaned. Only a few days after the Holy Prophet's birth his father Abdullah passed away and he was taken into the care of his grandfather Abdul Muttalib and when he was only of two years, his mother Amina Bint Wahab also left this world. And when he was of eight years his grandfather Abdul Muttalib departed handing over the charge of his grandson the Hob, Prophet, to his son Abu Talib (Ali's father). And it was the protection of Abu Talib (Ali's father) that was a providential plan to give the Holy Prophet the protection he needed from the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (He) found thee in loss (and immediately) guided thee Mere common sense would suggest to any learned one to take the meaning of every word in its proper context or study any event with its background. The meaning of the word 'Zall' is taken as ignorant, whereas it means also lost and in view of the common story connected with the interpretation of this verse, it means only lost. What the common story says is that when Halima the nurse to the Holy Prophet, started on her journey to Mecca to restore the young Muhammad to his grandfather, she left him at a place at the outskirts of the town and went into the desert to answer the call of nature. When she returned, she did not find the holy child in the place where she had left. Getting…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (He) found thee in need, and (immediately) made thee independent Commentators interpret this verse as a reference to the pecuniary provisions which the Holy Prophet received from the wealth of his wife Khadija and what he got through the leftover of the enemies, he dedicated for the defensive battles. But it would be too low and even a very mean estimate of the provision which God says that He has made for the Holy Prophet. God's provision would be in accordance with God's Greatness and glory. The Eighth Holy Imam Ali Ibn Musa ar-Riza says that the word 'Yateem' here means lonely. The Holy Prophet was lonely, alone without any friends or sympathisers and God directed the hearts of men and got the people around him as his devotees.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dhuhaa:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So, unto an orphan, oppress (People addressed through the Prophet.) not! The address is to the Holy Prophet, but it is an ordinance for the believers in particular and mankind as a whole.The Holy Prophet said that ''he who pleases an orphan, I shall be pleased with him on the day of Judgment" Again the Holy Prophet said ''He who maintains an orphan in honour, he and I will be together in heaven". While saying this he raised his palm and showed his two fingers and said ''as these two fingers are together".

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ha. Mim. (H. M.) Ha, Meem (H. M.) refer to verse 2:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So await thou the day when the heaven shall give out a smoke clearly visible, When the Quraysh became too hard-hearted and inflicted heartless, torturous and mortifying persecution upon those who embrace the Truth, God, made the tyrants taste some years of drought as in the time of Joseph, (i.e., seven years). A distressful famine overtook the people when they ate the corpses of dead dogs and the bones of the dead bodies. They ate even the skin of the dead animals soaked in their blood. The famine had reduced the people to bones and affected their eyesight and consequently when they looked up, they saw a smoke between their eyes and the sky. At last, when the people came to the Holy Prophet and implored him to pray to God for the relief which he did and got the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ad-Dukhaan:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Enveloping the people; This will be painful chastisement. When the people would come to the Holy Prophet and implore him to pray and get them the relief, and he would pray and get it from the Lord.It does not refer to the final resurrection day but to one of the earlier calamities which will overtake mankind for their failure to abide by the Last Apostle. The difference is that since the mission of the other apostles were limited to particular peoples and ages, the calamities also were limited to the people concerned. But since the mission of the Last Apostle is universal the calamity also will naturally be enveloping the humanity as a whole, to which the ancient prophets had hinted. The details are given by the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt about the calamities. (A.P.)

Whenever he wrote any letter he began 'In the name of Allah the Lord of the land and the seas, the sun and the wind'.When his son was slain at Madina and he came over to Madina to destroy the town, two men of the Bani Qurayẓah Tribe named Ka'b and…

item.description: (Becoming) a command from unto Us; Verily, We are the senders (of mercy and peace). And it is God alone Who commissions His chosen men with the apostleship and sends them into the world. This makes the point very clear that neither a spiritual guide is made in this world nor is it a matter of promotion for anyone to earn, by his efforts in the life in this world but a grace of God endowed by God Himself with the native excellence of body and soul essential for the purpose, and then the individual is sent into the world.The same is the case with Imamat, i.e., the office of the charge of the Divine Guidance,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And in 'Ad: when sent We upon them the desolating (Unproductive, futile.) (blast of violent') wind (Refer to Verses 46:21 - 46:26.) Refer to the commentary of Sura ad-Dukhan, 44:21 - 44:26 for the people of Ad.

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It left not aught upon which it came, but turned it like (rotten) dust See 51:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And in Thamood: when it was said unto them; "Avail ye your- selves for a while (Refer to Verses 7:73 - 7:79; 11:65.)" See commentary of Sura al-'Araf, 7:73 - 7:79 for the people of Thamud.

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But rebelled they against the command of their Lord, so seized them the rumbling, while they were yet looking on (Refer to Verses 7:70; 11:67.) See 51:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then they could not even rise (on their feet), nor could they help themselves See 51:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the people of Noah before (that)', Verily they were wicked people Refer to the commentary of Sura al-'Araf, 7:59 to 7:64 for the people of Nuh.

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the heaven, We did raise it up with (Our) Might, and verily We are the expanders (of it) expanse (This indicates the expandability of the Space - discarding the fixity of the present limitations (AP).) ? This indicates that although the frontiers of space are confined, they are not fixed. They can be expanded (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the earth, We did spread it out (like a carpet), how Excellent (are We) the Spreaders (thereof)? (Refer to Verse 2:22.) See 51:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of everything have We created in pairs, that ye may reflect (Refer to Verse 36:36.) ? What is created is in pairs. The parity may refer to the composite nature of the created beings or the positive and the negative in phenomenon in the order of creation (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily what ye are threatened with, is certainly true, The promise that death is not the end of the life. There is Resurrection on the Day of the Final Judgment with mercy and forgiveness to the penitent and justice and punishment to the rebellious - with an eternal life of bliss for the righteous and similarly everlasting punishment to the disbelievers and the wicked.

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So fly (Seek refuge, Turn to.) ye unto God! Verily I am unto you a plain (Open.) Warner So that ye may remember that the Absolute One from all respects and aspects, is God (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Set ye not with God any other god; Verily I am unto you a plain (Open.) Warner See 51:50

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Even so there came not unto those before them an apostle but said they (of him): 'A sorcerer or a mad man' (Refer to Verses 38:4; 44:14 and 51:39.) The ways of evil in dealing with the messengers of Allah were similar in all ages1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Have they charged this unto one another? Nay! they are rebellious (Inordinate transgressors of the law – applicable also to those who break the Islamic Laws.) people See 51:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then turn thou thy back upon them for thou art not to be blamed Verse 54 gives the impression that Allah might send a destructive visitation as manifestation of His wrath, but the next verse quells this apprehension. The guidance may be general in appearance, but it is directed towards man as an individual so that free from collective opinion or pressure, he may submit to the commands of Allah according to his ability and achieve success by following the divine plan (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And remind thou, for verily reminding profiteth the believers (Refer to Verses 21:16; 38:27; 67:2.) This indicates that the guidance may be general in appearance but actually meant for particular persons who get benefited (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And created not I, the Jinn and the humans, but that they may worship (To live in submission to the Lord.) (Me) The Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq said that God did not create men but to know, mho with the proper knowledge, automatically surrenders himself to Him – and without knowledge the adoration could never, in the true sense of it, be an adoration. Besides the actual meaning of adoration, is not the performance of any rituals or only the few prescribed formal prayers recited by the mouth but the actual surrender of the ego in an individual, disciplining it, to act only in consonance with the expressed will of the Lord, through abiding with His prescribed law.The whole life-activity of the individual, should be nothing but the fulfilment of the will of the Lord. It is…

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: I desire (Demand.) not from them any sustenance, nor do I desire that they should feed Me Providing sustenance for the creatures, is equal to feeding God Himself for the creatures, all put together, constitute one family of God's creation. Hence serving the creation is serving God.It clears that the object of creation - worship and obedience, is of no advantage or benefit to God. On the contrary, it is in the interest of the creatures to become the manifestation, of His will and Command (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, God He (alone) is the Bestower of sustenance, the Lord of the unbreakable strength See 51:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So, verily those who are unjust shall have a share (of the burden) like unto the share (of the burden) which had their fellows (of old), Therefore, let them ask Me not to hasten it on (Those who do not comply to the requirement of perfect obedience.) Those who did not comply to the requirement of obedience.'Dhanoob' literally a bucket full of water tied to the end of a rope like a tale figuratively used as the consequence of misdeeds and disobedience tied to the rope of one's life (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily the Judgment shall surely come to pass. See 51:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therefore, Woe unto those who disbelieve because of their day which they are promised! See 51:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And by the heaven with its starry highways, At a time, even centuries after which, the world did not know that the earth was round, it was not a difficulty but an impossibility for any one save the All-Knowing Author of the Universe to disclose the knowledge about the ways or orbits in the heavens. Let any intelligent seeker of knowledge from the Holy Qur'an reflect on the time taken by the non-Muslim world with all their scientific efforts and exertions to enquire into the elementary phenomenon of the working of the nature in the heavens visible over our own heads. How many centuries after, we are informed by our greatest scientists about the stars in the heavens, that there are the orbit around which revolve the planets, even this our sun being the centre for the earth and the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily ye are in discordance in what ye say, The variance referred to, is in their false imagination about the Holy Prophet and the Holy Qur'an, some said that the Holy Prophet was sorcerer, a mad-man, one overcome by a jinn and about the Holy Qur'an they said it was an enchanting poetry, it was the collection of the stories of the ancient people borrowed from the old people. About the Resurrection they believed it to be an impossibility.

item.title: bil-Quran: Adh-Dhaariyat:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He will be turned away from it who is to be turned away. See 51:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the snorting chargers! Verses 1-5 are the mystic symbols of some event of special importance. Commentators have given some imaginary interpretation to the symbolic use of the words. The truth is that the Surah as a whole was revealed on a particular occasion of special importance. The Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq says that the tribes of Bani Saleem collected a huge force to make a sudden and a very heavy attack on Madina, to kill the Muslims and to arrest the Holy Prophet and then to torture him. On receiving the news of this gathering of the hostile forces the Holy Prophet sent an army under one of his companions who ran away from the field and returned utterly defeated suffering a heavy loss and owing to his running away from the field, many of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall be made manifest whatever is in the breasts (hearts)? Whatever is hidden, be that the motives and the thoughts concealed in the minds, will be made manifest.'Sodoor' used by Qur'an is the seat of the feelings and emotion. The passage shows that our feelings and emotions develop into concrete form in the life form. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, their Lord, that day concerning them, will be fully aware! On the Day of Judgment everything will be open and known to the Lord Who is ever Vigilant and Knowing everything, manifest and concealed.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those that dash off (their hoofs) striking fire The march being in the night, creating bright sparks of fire by the striking of the hoofs of the chargers on the rocky soil on which they marched.The reference is to the expedition of the believers led by 'Ali, surrounding the enemy by surprise in the early hours of dawn - for this justification of the action explains the ungrateful attitude of the enemy who treacherously violated the Treaty of Peace with the Holy Prophet and killed in cold blood several Muslims (Ghazwa al-Zatus-Salasal). (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those that scour to the attack at morn! The chargers of those who attacked the enemy at dawn, for Ali had made the attack on the enemy in the early hours of dawn and had taken the enemy by surprise.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And stir thereby the dust aloft The dust raised by the rush of the chargers, on the enemy, all of a sudden.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And penetrate through (the foe) all of them The actual fall of the believers on the enemy's forces, with the consolidated heaviest pressure on them.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, man unto his Lord is ungrateful The Holy Prophet said the 'Kanud' is the one who eats alone and obstructs others receiving anything from anybody, i.e., grossly selfish - He who receives gifts and wages, war against the benefactor himself - reference to the enemies of Islam - who though under the obligation of the grace of God, reject the belief in Him and wage war on the believers.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily, He (God.) is a witness unto that The selfish and the ungrateful disbeliever proves his selfishness and ingratitude by his own deeds without the necessity of evidence from anybody else.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily, in the love of wealth, he is violent (Vehement – Hard. The Arabs called a Niggard 'Shadeed' (MS).) See 100:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Aadiyaat:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Knoweth he not when, what is in the graves is raised (to life) The interrogation is for an emphatic assertion that man will surely be raised from the grave and let man know and remember that everything will be resurrected.Grave stands for the place which covers the corpse from the sight of mankind. And the verse shows that whatever may be the nature of the grave, it retains something of the deceased one - whether it is soul or body - is subject to the resurrection. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ha Mim (H. M.) (Refer to note about the verse 2:1.) See 46:3

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "See ye? If (this Qur'an) be from God and ye disbelieve in it, (although) hath borne witness a witness from among the children (OT. Deut. 18/18,18/19.) of Israel, on its similarity (with the previous scriptures), and hath (also him-self) believed (in it), and yet ye in pride exalt yourselves; Verily God guideth not the unjust people." 'The witness from among the Children of Israel' (46:10). Some commentators think that a reference to Abdullah Ibn Salam, an Israelite scholar who embraced Islam of his own accord.Reference is to Moses who bore witness and prophesied the advent of the Holy Prophet from among the brethren of Israel-similar to Moses himself. Some commentators think it to refers to Abdullah Ibn Salam-and it should be remembered that the evidence of a fallible source can be of no use to prove the truth…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say those who disbelieve about those who believe; "Had it been good, they would have gone not ahead of us unto it: "Since they seek not to be guided aright by it; say they: "This is a lie of old:" (Reference to the usual arrogance of the aristocratic class.)" When the tribes of Jehniah, Mehniah, Alama and Gaffar embraced Islam, the tribes of Banu-Admir, Ghatfan, Asad and Ashja said if there had been any truth in Islam we would not have allowed others to supersede us in embracing it. "We would have been the first to accept the faith." This verse was revealed about this event. It was a taunt upon the poor ones among the early converts to Islam viz., Ammar, Sohaib and Ibn Mas'ood – saying if there had been any good in Islam it would have…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And before it (i.e., before the Qur'an.) the Book of Moses (the Pentateuch ('Taurat' i.e. the Law.) ) was a guide and a mercy: and this (Qur'an) is a Book confirmeth (the previous scriptures), in the Arabic language that it may warn those who are unjust; and (contains) glad-tidings for the doers of good The Holy Qur'an has the same regard for the Laws given to Moses as had Jesus - Math. 5-17."Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil." Math. 5/17The Holy Qur'an is the exposition of the truth in the Arabic language.Islam never labours under any linguistic prejudices—whatever language, truth might have beenrevealed through any of the apostles of God, in any part of the world, Islam regards it, and respects it and informs…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who say: "Our Lord is God," (This is what said Jesus: "Hear O' Israel! the Lord our God is one Lord" N. T. Mark 12/29.) and are firm aright, then no fear shall be on them nor shall they grieve; The faith in God has to be declared in words and also proved by its practice in the daily life which means, the confirmation of the faith. One has not only to pronounce the belief in words but also to be steadfast on it, in the hours of trials in this life. The greatest example of faith and the steadfastness on it, could be found nowhere in the world, save in Husayn and his faithful comrades in Karbala.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These shall be inmates of the garden, abiding in it; a recompense for what they did See 46:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We have enjoined on man goodness unto his parents; Did bear him his mother with pain and she delivered him with pain; And bearing him and weaning him is thirty months (Refer to verse 2:233.) ; Until when he attaineth his maturity and reacheth forty years, sayeth he: "My Lord! arouse (Grant me.) me that I may give thanks for Thy bounties which Thou hath bestowed on me and my parents and that I may do good which pleaseth Thee and do good unto me in respect of my offspring; Verily I turn unto Thee (repentant)., and verily I am one of the Muslims (Who submit themselves to God.)" The maximum period of breast feeding for a child is 2 years by which time the child is equipped by nature with the set of teeth enabling it to chew…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These are they from whom We accept the best of what they have done and pass by their evils, (they shall be) among the inmates of the Garden; (this is that) promise of truth which they were used to be promised (Note: Even the best deeds will be accepted only from the pious ones and not from all.) . See 46:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And he who sayeth unto his parents: "Fie on ye both! Promise ye me that I shall be brought forth (from the grave alive) when have passed away generations before me?" and they both implore for God's aid, (saying): "Woe unto thee! Believe thou; for verily the promise of God is true;" Then will he say: "This is naught but stories of the ancients." This is a reference to the disbelief in the Resurrection. They held the truth about it as the legends of the ancients.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These are they against whom the sentence hath been proved among the peoples of the jinn and the men that have passed away before them; verily they were the losers. See 46:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And for all (are ranks) (assigned) according to what they did, and that He (God.) may (fully) recompense their deeds, and they shall not be done any injustice. Though the return for evil would be equal to the degree of the evil but the reward for good will be far more than its merit and this would be due to the infinite mercy of God1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The descent (of the revelation) of this Book (Qur'an) (is) from God, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise See 46:3

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on the day when shall be exposed those who dis-believed to the fire: (it will be said unto them): "Ye did away with your good things in your life of the world and ye took your fill of pleasure in them; This day therefore ye shall be recompensed with shameful chastisement for what ye used to act in arrogance (Prided unjustly.) in the earth without any right, and for what ye used to transgress." On the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers would be at the hell-fire, it will be told to them that during their lifetime in the world they were greedy, and covetously enjoyed the pleasures of the world, sacrificing their spiritual interest for the material enjoyment. They will be told that they will have to pay the price of their choice and for the pride they…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And remember (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) of the brother of 'Ad when he warned his people of 'Al-Ahqaf' (The Sandhills.) and (while) indeed warners have been before him and after him (saying) "Worship ye not but God! Verily, I fear for you the chastisement of a grievous day. (Refer to verse 7:65.)" 'Hiqf' means a raised spot in the desert – 'Ahqaf' is the plural. The place under reference is said to have been located in Yeman near Hadramut at the shores of the Sea of Omman. The reference is to the experience of the apostle Hud who was from the people Aad, commissioned to warn the people against their polytheistic faith and conduct. Since he was not a stranger but one of their own brethren as the Holy Prophet was to his brethren the Qurayshites. The people lived in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "What! Come thou unto us to turn us away from our gods? Then bring (The Chastisement.) thou on us what thou threateneth us with, if thou art of the truthful ones." See 46:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: "The knowledge (of it) is only with God, I only convey unto you the message which I am sent with, but I see you a people who are ignorant." See 46:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So when they saw (the punishment in the form of) a cloud advancing (Spreading.) unto their valleys, they said: "This is a cloud which will give us rain;" Nay! it is (the calamity) what ye sought to hasten on; a blast of a violent wind in which is a painful chastisement, The people were punished with a drought for three or seven years. Hud used to continuously admonish the people saying: "Believe ye in God and repent ye for your sins, ye mill have rain from God." The people increased only in adamance. A man named Qais Ibn Ghurrus even ridiculed Hud and said, "We want the punishment from thy God and not His rain." One of the chiefs of the people named Muzmad who had believed in Hud, admonished the people saying, "Nothing would bring rain for you from…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Destroying every thing by the command of its Lord; So became they not to be seen save their dwellings; Thus do We recompense the guilty people (Totally destroyed – nothing but their ruined dwellings to be seen – No trace of theirs.) . The whole habitation with all its inhabitants, men and animals and even the houses of the people, were blown out, and the place became totally desolated. Heaps of sand were thrown over the habitation with its inmates. The blast continued for seven nights and eight days and ultimately the whole habitation turned into mounds of sand with the inhabitants in their dwellings, buried underneath.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And certainly had We firmly established them, what We established not ye in it, and We had given them ears, and eyes and hearts; but availed not them aught their ears nor their eyes nor their hearts, (The Centre of intellect & emotions.) since they gainsaid the signs of God, and they were encircled by what they used to mock at (Refer to verse 45:33.) . See 46:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We destroyed of the towns which are around you, and We did display (Repeat.) Our signs that they might turn (Repent and amend.) (unto Us). May refer to the ancient habitations in the Arabian Peninsula or around it. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: unto God? Nay! but they failed them, and this was their lie and what they used to forge. See 46:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when turned We unto thee a party of jinn (Refer to note about verse on Jinn.) who (quietly) listened to the Qur'an when came they unto it, said they: "Be ye silent! (and listen)?" then when was finished (the recital), returned they unto their people warning (them against (Or against evil living. This clearly indicates that Jinn were also a generation like mankind and are influenced by the Word of God. See Note on jinn, and the other reference to them in the Qur'an.) the wrath of God) (Refer to verses 72:1, 55:33, 6:130.) About the people worshipping the jinn in the place of God, see verse 6:100. The jinns are, acceptedly spiritual beings. One of such beings is referred to here - See note on Jinn. See verse 2:41 about the Book the Holy Qur'an verifying the previously…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We created not the heavens and the earth and what is between them two, save with truth and (for) a determined term; But those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned of Everything created by God the All-Wise Lord of the Universe, must naturally have a purpose which shall be fulfilled. Thus, everything has a fixed age to exist. Nothing is permanent and shall pass away with the fulfilment of the purpose of the Creator. As the Universe had a beginning, there shall also be an end of it. But the disbelievers turn aside from what they are warned of.The previous Sura begins with the presentation of the heavenly and terrestrial signs in the order of creation and here begins with the assertion of the purposefulness of the order of creation. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (the Jinns): "O' ye our people! Verily, have we listened unto a Book sent down (from God) after Moses, verifying what is before it, guiding unto the truth and unto a path straight aright." Ibn Abbas says once the Holy Prophet said that he was commanded by God to recite the Holy Qur'an to the jinns and to warn them. He asked his companions as to who would like to accompany him to the recital. None uttered a word save Ibn Mas'ood. The Holy Prophet asked thrice but every time there was silence and none replied - Ibn Mas'ood says that he was taken to the cave called Sheb-e-Haihoon which is on the top of a mountain near Mecca. Arriving at the place the Holy Prophet drew a circle round Ibn Mas'ood and commanded him never under any circumstances…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye our people! Respond ye (all) unto the Summoner unto God and believe ye in Him, He will forgive you of your sins, and guard you against a painful chastisement. See 46:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whosoever respondeth not unto the Summoner unto God, yet he can frustrate not God's will in the earth, and there shall not be for him, other than Him (God.) , any guardians; these are in manifest error Qummi says that the Holy Prophet once went to the market place, Akkaza, along with Zaid Ibn Haritha to preach the message of Islam, on his way back to Mecca he stayed in the valley of Najbah for the night and when he recited the Holy Qur'an, there also assembled some jinns, one of the groups carried the message of Islam to his kind. (MS. UB).It is said that among the jinns there are believers and disbelievers, good and wicked.It is a proof positive that the Holy Prophet was a warner to the jinns as well as to mankind.It is an assurance…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therefore (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) bear thou up with patience, as did the apostles endowed with constancy (Fortitude.) and seek thou not to hasten for them (their doom); On the day when they will see what they have been promised, (it shall be unto them) as if they tarried not but (for only) an hour of the day; (a clear) Deliverance! (this is)! then shall be destroyed (Not total annihilation but the loss of happiness (A.P.).) any but the transgressing people. The duty of the apostle of God ends with his preaching the truth, i.e., conveying the message in the clearest possible terms and then it becomes the responsibility of the people to accept and follow it or to reject it. As those who accept the truth would surely be rewarded, those who reject it would naturally be punished with…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "Have ye seen what ye called upon besides God? Show me what of the earth did they create; or for them is there any share in the heavens? (i.e. in the creation of the heavens.) Bring me a book ere this (Qur'an.) or traces of knowledge, if ye be truthful." When the false gods have neither created anything in the earth nor have they any share in the heaven on what right should they be worshipped. Most polytheists thoughtlessly get worshipping the imaginary gods just following the ancestral customs. The same is the case with the majority among the Muslims that they blindly follow unqualified and self-appointed leaders.Otherwise, untampered common sense, would never choose any one against the Ahl Al-Bayt, who only are the purified ones by God Himself1, and against the several universally acknowledged…

item.description: And who is more astray than he who calleth upon besides God, unto such who (The false deities.) will respond not unto him till the Day of Judgment, and they, (The false deities.) of their invocations are not conscious See 46:4

item.description: And when people shall be gathered together (on the Day of Reckoning) they shall be hostile unto them, and shall be the deniers of their (The devotees-the heathens.) worship (unto them) See 46:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when Our clear signs are recited unto them, say those who disbelieve about the truth when it cometh unto them, this is an open sorcery (Refer to verses 6:125; 37:14, 37:15.) Whenever truth was conveyed to them, they called it sorcery and treated it with derision and ridicule.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or they do say: "He hath forged it?" Say thou (then O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "If I have forged it, then ye have not aught for me against (the wrath of) God. He knoweth best what (all) ye utter (pass through - go deep into discussion.) (in mocking) about it; Sufficeth He a witness between me and you; and He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful" This is an argument based on what is laid down in 69:44 - 69:47, i.e., God will never allow any imposter to flourish - but He will expose his fallacious claims.Pass through - go deep in discussion. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahqaf:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "I am not the first (6:50, 7:188, 10:49, 46:9. Refer to verses 40:78, 6:84 - 6:88.) of the apostles (from God), I know not what will be done unto me (Refer to verse 7:188.) , nor (what will be done) unto you; I follow not anything save what hath been revealed unto me, and I am not but an open warner (Thus, every action of the Holy Prophet was the execution of the divine will, as every word of his was the revelation from the Lord. Refer to note about verses 53:3 & 53:4.) ." What the Holy Prophet preached to the polytheist world, i.e., the Unity of God was nothing new or nothing of his own innovation but the same truth which every other apostle of God preceding him had brought and preached -…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' Our Prophet (Muhammad!): "Fear thou (The Prophet addressed for the followers.) God (alone), and obey not the disbelievers and the hypocrites; Verily God is All-Knowing, All-Wise," After the migration of the Holy Prophet and the Muslims from Mecca and their settling down at Medina, the Jews in Medina got envious of the wonderful progress Islam was making and the hold of the city and its affairs along with the leadership of the people passing into the hands of the Holy Prophet. Some of them who were proven to be treacherous, had to be expelled out of the city and the rest who embraced Islam were only hypocrites under Abdullah ibn Ubayy who was their ringleader.In the fifth year A.H. the heathens of Mecca got into an alliance with the disbelievers in central Arabia, along with the Jews and planned…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When came they upon you from above (Openly, i.e., the heathens.) you and from below (The hidden enemies i.e. the Hypocrites and those of the wavering converts.) you, and were turned dull the eyes, and reached to the throats the hearts, and ye did imagine about God diverse thoughts. This verse refers to the awe-stricken state of the Muslims at the sight of the formidable forces of the enemy.The reference is to the battle of 'Ahzab' known as 'Khandaq' which was one of the great trials as referred by this verse (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: There were tried (Refer to note on verses 3:139, 9:64, 29:2 - 29:4 & 67:2.) the believers and they were shaken a tremendous shaking. The reference here is to the event of the battle of the Ditch which was a trial or a test for the believers, in which every Muslim was shaken by the awful situation. It is now for the intelligent students of the Holy Qur'an to judge about the faith of those who stood dumb and lifeless like statues when 'Amr ibn 'Abd Wudd challenged to fight him and the Holy Prophet repeatedly asked the Muslims if any one of them would fight the enemy of Islam. It is a fact of history that in the ranks there were all the companions and none stirred from his place.It indicates that the term 'Mu'minin' applies to those who…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when began to say the hypocrites and those in whose hearts was disease that: "Promised us not God and His Apostle but (it was only) a deception." (Similar was the doubt at Sulh-e-Hudaybiyyah.) The hypocrites had doubted about the assurance given to them by the Holy Prophet about the ultimate victory Islam would have. The weak in faith, were led by the circumstances which had no indication of the least success against the most formidable forces of the enemy and thus had said that the promise of victory extended to them was only a deceptive measure merely to encourage them to face the hopeless situation.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when said a party of them: "O' ye the people of Yathrib! (The former name of the town which after the Migration of the Holy Prophet to it, was renamed Medinat al-Nabi - Now called only Medina.) There is no place for you to stand, so return ye," and a party of them asked permission of the Prophet saying: "Verily our houses are exposed (to destruction)," and they were not exposed (to destruction): they only intended to flee away. A group of the Muslims, misled by the defeatist rumours spread by the hypocrites, had suggested to the others to leave Islam and return to idolatry or to leave the ranks of the Muslims and go back to their homes. And some, under the false pretext of taking care of their undefended homes, wanted to leave the ranks and go…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And had the entry been made upon them from all sides (of the City), and had they been incited to treachery, they would certainly have brought it to pass, with only a short time had they stayed. The hearts of the weak in faith had been so otherwise much affected by the dejection that had dawned upon them by the disheartening rumours and they had been reduced to so much of unfaithfulness that if the enemy had by chance penetrated into the city and called them to fight the Muslims, they were so much degenerated in faith that they would not have in the least delayed in doing it.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed they had made a covenant with God before (that) they would turn (Reference to the Companions of the Holy Prophet and the others running away from the battlefield at Uhud.) not their backs; And the covenant with God shall be inquired of. After their desertion at the battle of Uhud, they had repented and had promised never again to desert the faith and they had solemnly promised to fight for Islam.The reference here alluding to deserters at the battle of Uhud, indicates that the group of such weak in faith and the hypocrites consisted of also those who had run away from the battle of Uhud, leaving the Holy Prophet to his fate in the midst of the bloodthirsty enemies. As to who were those who ran away from the field of Uhud, one should refer to some…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) "Never shall benefit you the flight, if ye flee away from death or slaughter, and (even) then ye will not be allowed to enjoy yourselves but (only) a little" Ali says: "Ayyu yawmayya min al-mawt afriru? Yawmun la yuqaddar am yawmun qad quddir?"i.e., Which of the two days I should run away from death - the day not destined or the day destined? (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Who is he that can screen you from God if intendeth He unto you any evil or intendeth He unto you mercy?" And they will find not for themselves other than God any guardian or helper. See 33:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed knoweth God those who hinder others (Refers to the activities of the hypocrites on the day of the battle of Khandaq (The Ditch).) among you and those who say unto their brethren "Come hither unto us," and they come not to fight but a little, A man from the Muslim ranks who had been in the city, found one of his brothers sitting, enjoying the drink of wine. The man said: "You are enjoying at home while the Holy Prophet is facing the arrows and the swords of the enemy. I shall inform the Holy Prophet of your conduct." By the time the man came to the Holy Prophet the Messenger Angel informed the Holy Prophet of everything about the man enjoying at home.It indicates that there were people who were not inclined to fight and used to persuade…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Being niggardly unto you, but when cometh fear, thou wilt see them looking unto you, their eyes rolling (A pen picture of the people as a whole in the state of fright where Ali alone fought the enemy and won the victory for Islam.) like the one on whom death hath cast its shadow and when passeth away the fear, they smite you with sharp tongues, being niggardly of the good things; These have believed not, (Indicates the strength of the faith of the converts and the fate of their good deeds.) and so God hath made their deed in vain; and this for God is easy. This was the actual position of most of the companions of the Holy Prophet whose weakness in faith and hypocrisy was clearly proved on several occasions when Islam had to fight for its…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And follow thou (Refer to note on verse 53:3 & 53:4. This clearly indicates that whatever the Holy Prophet utters or acts was the revealed will of the Lord.) what is revealed unto thee from thy Lord; Verily God is, of what ye do, well-aware, Man under any circumstances should not give up fearing evil, for man is apt to misjudge. The full knowledge of the facts is only with God who knows everything hidden and manifest.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Think they the allies have not gone, and should the clans come (again) they would fain be dwelling with the wandering arabs in the desert, seeking news (Pictures the state of the mind of the hypocrites in Medina. They actually did it at Uhud and Hunayn.) about you; and had they been amidst you, they would fight not but a little. This verse draws a vivid picture of the state of mortal fright that had dawned on the hypocrites. The description starts from verse 33:12 in which it is said that they were so much awe-stricken by the formidable strength of the enemy that even before the actual conflict, they thought that all was over. They were not only themselves disloyal but also infected the others and prepared them to withdraw from the ranks.1 If the enemy had even entered…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed (there) is for you in the Apostle of God (Muhammad) an excellent pattern (Believes in God and seeks His pleasure.) (of conduct) for him who hopeth in God and the latter day (The life hereafter - the day of judgment.) and remembereth God much. From this verse starts the description of the minds of the sincere believers. In the Holy Prophet, God has presented a beautiful pattern of conduct and character for the one who aspires for the mercy of the Lord and hopes in the success or victory in the ultimate. When the enemy advanced towards Medina, the Holy Prophet told the Muslims never to get frightened by the huge number of the enemy and assured them or prophecy of the victory in the ultimate which promise or prophecy was doubted by the hypocrites to be a deceptive…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when saw the believers the allies, said they: "This is what God promised unto us and His Apostle and God and His Apostle had spoken the truth;" and it increased not in them but faith and submission. Here it is given as to how the mind of the sincere ones in faith in contrast to that of the hypocrites and the weak in faith, viewed the situation of the enemy's attack. The faithful ones seeing the enemy's presence, instead of getting dejected and perturbed, awaited the fulfilment of the promise of God about the ultimate triumph of Islam over all its enemies.1 Every one of such true ones, remembered the words of the promise. When the Holy Prophet struck at the immovable rock that appeared while digging the Ditch, people had seen in the flashes of the light that…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Of the believers are the men who are true to what they covenanted with God; of them is he who hath fulfilled (Refers to those who stood fast with the Holy Prophet up to the end - and those who ran away from the battlefields do not come under this category.) his vow and of them is he who awaiteth (its fulfilment); and they have changed not in the least, The Fifth Holy Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, in the interpretation of this verse said, that those who had fulfilled their promise to be steadfast in defending the truth and had become martyrs, were Hamza, son of Abdul Muttalib, Jafar, son of Abu Talib and the one who waited for his turn to be martyred for the same cause, was Ali son of Abu Talib. item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That God may recompense the truthful ones for their truth, and chastise the hypocrites if He willeth or turn unto them (merciful); Verily God is Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful. This is one of the clear proofs that the companions of the Holy Prophet were of different grades in faith. The first and the foremost are the true believers as depicted in verse 33:23 whose success in the life hereafter is assured beyond doubt in verse 33:24 and the hypocrites who are subject to punishment or forgiveness. However, all the companions cannot be the Guiding Stars to be followed. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God turned back those who disbelieve in their rage, they achieved not any advantage; and God did suffice for the believers in fighting; for God is All-Strong, the Almighty. The Omnipotent Lord made the furious enemy to avail of nothing, in spite of the joint efforts of all the allies together viz. the Bedouins of the interior, the envious and the hostile Jews from Medina and the treacherous hypocrites. All plans, intrigues and plots were frustrated, though on the occasion every one of the Muslims was awfully dreading the very sight of the formidable strength of the enemy the one single-handed combat of Ali with Amr ibn Abd Wudd was made sufficient to render the enemy dejected and disheartened and to create dissensions and discord among themselves and to add to their dejection and the discomfiture, there came from…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He drove down those of the people of the Book who backed them (The Meccan polytheists - Reference to the Battle of Banu Qurayza.) from their fortresses, and He cast awe into their hearts, some ye killed and took ye captives of the other part (of them) When the confederates had fled away in chaos and dismay the Holy Prophet could have ordered to chase the fleeing enemy and effect a wholesale slaughter but he commanded quiet return to Medina and when he had just returned home and had not yet washed his face, the Messenger Angel Gabriel appeared and conveyed the will of the Lord not even to tarry for the afternoon prayers but to immediately proceed towards the Jewish Tribe of Banu Qurayza who had broken the solemn covenant they had entered into with the Holy Prophet…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He made you to inherit their land and their dwellings and their properties, and a land (Refer to verses 59:2 - 59:7.) which ye have not yet set your foot; And God is Powerful over all things. See 33:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' Our Prophet (Muhammad!) Say thou unto thy wives: "If ye desire (the enjoyment of) the life of this world and its adornment, come then I will provide for you and allow you to depart (For they had become intolerably troublesome to the Holy Prophet, the separation was offered to these.) a goodly departing." When the Holy Prophet returned home after the victory at Khaybar, his wives asked him to distribute the booty among them. The Holy Prophet said that he had distributed it as commanded by God. They said, "Dost thou not know that after thy death we could not be married to anyone else?" God desired the Holy Prophet through this verse to admonish them. The Holy Prophet left them to themselves for about nineteen days and remained at the 'Mashrabat Umm Ibrahim.' Of the women whom the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if ye desire God and His Apostle and the abode in the hereafter, then verily God hath prepared for the good (Refer to note on verse 33:28.) among you a great recompense. In this verse there is the promise of the great heavenly reward to the righteous and the faithful ones among the wives of the Holy Prophet the object of whose alliance with the Holy Prophet was not owning any riches or any fortune but to please God and His Holy Apostle Muhammad and to achieve the blissful life in the ultimate.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And rely thou on God (alone), and God is sufficient a Protector. Man should always depend upon God and believe in the sufficiency of God's protection and help.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' wives of the Prophet! whosoever of you committeth an open (Not adultery as they have been cleared of their charge. Refer to note on verse 33:28.) indecency double will be the chastisement for her; and this for God is easy. It is to be noted by the critics of the Holy Prophet and Islam that whatever the Holy Prophet got as the booty in the several defensive battles was in his hands; and at his independent and exclusive disposal he could have appropriated everything to his personal use or for the use of his wives and the other relatives.Any indecency on the part of his wives was warned against to be penalised with double the ordinary punishment. Because being under the direct control and the guidance of the Holy Prophet, they ought to have been benefited by the close…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whoever of you is obedient to God and His Apostle and doeth good, We will give her recompense twice, and We have prepared for her an honour able sustenance. The term double reward mentioned here does not mean twice but a greater reward. They earn this grace of God for their denying themselves the ordinary comforts of life and their remaining faithful to the Holy Prophet abiding by his guidance. As they are entitled to an increased punishment for any ordinary indecency, similar increase they are also entitled to a similar increase in the reward for their virtues.1This indicates that some of the wives of the Holy Prophet were not of the standard. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye wives of the Prophet! ye are not like any other women if ye guard (yourselves) against evil, and be not soft in (your) speech lest lusteth after you he in whose heart is a disease, and speak ye a plain speech. The wives of the Holy Prophet are informed of their unique position to be the models of righteousness among the women. It has been made quite clear that mere alliance with the Holy Prophet will never suffice them without the righteousness expected of their position. They are warned to be guarded when they talk gently to any people lest their kindness and gentle voice might be misunderstood and taken a wrong advantage of, by the evil-minded ones. All these go to show that every woman being merely the wife of any apostle of God would never be…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And stay ye in your abodes and display not your finery like the display of the ignorance of yore, and establish ye prayer and give away the poor-rate, and obey God and His Apostle; Verily, verily God intendeth but to keep off (Not allowed even to approach.) from you (every kind of) uncleanness O' ye the People of the House, and purify you (with) a thorough purification. (With the event of 'Kisa' (the Mantle) reported also by Umm al-Mu'minin – A'isha & Umm Salamah - and at the historic 'Mubahila' the Holy Prophet pointed out, as only Ali, Fatima, Hasan and Husayn being the Ahl al-Bayt.) item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And remember ye what is recited in your abodes of the signs of God and wisdom; verily God is Benignant, All-Aware. Here the wives of the Holy Prophet in particular are admonished to remember what is recited in their houses, i.e., what the Holy Prophet preaches to them in particular, and also the Word of God, the Qur'an, specially about the discipline prescribed for women. One has to refer to history to know which of the wives of the Holy Prophet violated this ordinance.The concluding words of the verse are a warning saying that whatever the wives of the Holy Prophet in particular and the women in general do, is always open to God's knowledge.Here the gender changes - the address in plural feminine and the reference is to houses and not to the House referred to in verse 33:33…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the Muslim men and the Muslim women and the believing men and the believing women and obedient men and the obedient women, and the truthful men and the truthful women, and the patient men, and the patient women, and the humble men and the humble women, and the alms-giving men and the alms-giving women, and the fasting men and the fasting women, and the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard (their private parts), and the men who remember God much and the women who remember God (much), for them hath been prepared forgiveness and a great recompense. It is said that Asma' bint Umays, the wife of Jafar at-Tayyar (Ja'far ibn Abi Talib) after her return from Abyssinia, expressed her disappointment for there was no mention of the women in the Word of God…

item.description: And it is not for a believer man or woman to have any choice in their affair when God and His Apostle have decided a matter; and whoever disobeyeth God and His Apostle, indeed he hath strayed off a manifest straying. item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when thou didst say on him whom God hath bestowed (His) bounty and unto whom thou hast shown (thy) favour "Keep unto thyself thy wife and fear God," But thou didst hide in thy self what God wouldst bring to light, and thou didst (Refer to note on verse 5:54.) fear the people; and God hath greater right that thou shouldst fear Him. But when Zayd hath concluded his concern with her (i.e., divorced her) We joined her (in wedlock) as thy wife, so that there should not be a difficulty for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons, when they have concluded their concerns with them (i.e., have divorced them); and the command of God shall be carried out. item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the Prophet is no blame in doing what hath been ordained by God unto him, and such hath been the way of God with those who have passed before, and the behest of God is a decree irrevocable, Having more than one wife was not peculiar only with the Holy Prophet, but his predecessors were also allowed to have a great number of wives viz. David, Solomon and the other apostles of God and even the great rishis1 - including the father of Rama and Lakshman had more than one wife. Islam on the other hand controlled and restricted it with such an ordinance that strictly observing the law, one can have only one.This also supports the fact that the apostleship and the prophethood does not deprive the person and the members of his family from the ordinary human…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ahzaab:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who convey the messages of God and fear Him, and fear not any one but God; and sufficient is God to take account. Man's responsibility, particularly that of the apostle, is to God and not to anybody else. None has any option of using his wisdom or discretion in executing the will of God viz. while discharging the duty of conveying God's message, the apostle has to fear none but God.What the Holy Prophet apprehended in regard to receiving Zaynab in wedlock was not his fear of the people but the people being misled by the false propaganda of the hypocrites against Islam and himself and waited for the revelation of the divine will for he was the one who never spoke or acted save what was revealed to him.1 When God's Command was revealed through this verse, the…
