Isiah 43/10."For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:103 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Vision perceiveth (Even vision comprehend Him not.) Him not, and He perceiveth (all) vision (Refer to Verses 7:63; 22:63; 12:100; 42:19.) ; He is the Subtle (All pervading.) , the All-Aware. Man is in a material body, given material eyes which can see only matter and material beings.Man cannot sec even the air and the electrical energy the existence of which none can ever deny. God is not matter. He is neither spirit but the Creator of spirit. Hence God can never be seen by anyone either in this life or in any other state of it in the hereafter. His existence can only be realised by heart. He is the 'Infinite', Absolute, Abstract, never at all can he be perceived by any finite being. Hence if anyone claims to have seen God or to see Him in future, in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:104 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed, have come unto you (clear) proofs from your Lord, whosoever therefore seest (Gets guided by them.) it, it is for his own self; and whosoever be (wilfully) blind then it is against him; I am not over you a keeper (Refer to Verses 20:124 - 20:126.) . This is a clear proof that Islam preaches the truth and leaves the question of its acceptance or rejection to every individual man or woman without any compulsion. Islam gives the freedom of thought as a test of the correct use of the unique native endowments of intellect and reasoning given exclusively to the human species in the physical world to be rewarded or punished for the discretion or the indiscretion used by every individual - with the right course revealed against the wrong one and the truth made manifest from falsehood1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:105 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thus do We display (To explain – to make clearer.) the signs and that they may say "Thou hast been taught and that We may make it clear to people who know." See 6:104

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:106 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Follow (The address is to the people through the Holy Prophet.) thou what hath been revealed unto thee from thy Lord; There is no god but He, turn thee away from the polytheists. Following is the concluding part of this Verse. Some commentators take this Verse even as God's commandment to the Holy Prophet to leave Mecca and migrate to Medina.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:107 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And had God (so) pleased, they would not have associated (others) with Him; and We have not made thee (The Holy Prophet.) a keeper over them, nor art thou (The Holy Prophet.) over them a guardian. See 6:106

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:108 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And abuse ye not those whom they invoke besides God, lest they abuse God in transgression (Exceeding the limit.) without knowledge. Thus, have We made fair-seeming (The passage apparently makes God responsible for the fair- seemingness of the deeds of the infidels but actually their own short-coming itself is responsible for it. Refer to note on action and reaction in Sura al-Fatiha, "Iyyaka Na'budu" (1:5).) to every people their deeds, then unto their Lord is their return, so He will inform them of what they did. In the beginning, the faithful used to speak ill of the idols and the idolators. The heathens of Mecca found the Holy Prophet safe under the protection of Abu Talib whom every one of the pagans of Mecca and its surroundings held in high regard and veneration. The idolators of Mecca decided to go…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:109 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they swear by God with the strongest of their oaths that if came unto them a sign, they would most certainly believe in it; Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Verily signs are with God, but what should make ye know that when it cometh, they will not believe (Refer to Verses 6:112; 7:146.) ." Once the disbelievers approached the Holy Prophet and said, 'like Moses, Saleh, and Jesus, you also show us some miracles' The Holy Prophet asked them if they would believe in case a miracle is wrought at which the disbelievers promised taking serious oaths. The Holy Prophet was about to pray to God for some miracle when the Angel Gabriel appeared and conveyed this Verse - saying that if the infidels did not believe in spite of the miracle sought by them a visitation from heaven…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Travel (Encouraging the study of the terrestrial conditions - and the fate of the wicked ones - and draw lessons from it.) ye in the earth; then see ye what hath been the end of the beliers (of our apostles')." See 6:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:110 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We will turn (aside) their hearts and their visions, even as they did not believe in it the first time, and We will leave them in their contumacy (Inordinacy. Refer to note on action and reaction in Sura al-Fatiha, "Iyyaka Na'budu" (1:5).) , wandering blindly on. The estrangement of the heart due to the hostile attitude towards the truth, and the wandering away from the right path, refusing to believe in the signs interpreted as the turning away of the hearts as the natural consequence of the inordinacy which is in other words God's deed of punishment earned by the disbelievers.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:111 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And had We sent down unto them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them and (even if) We had gathered all things before them, (even then) they would not believe unless that God (so) pleaseth but most of them (deliberately) ignore (This is a continuation of Verse 6:110. Refer to Verse 41:29.) . This refers to the repulsive nature in the disbelievers whether the signs (miracles) demanded by them or covers furthermore than the demanded ones are given, they will not believe, unless the creative will of God is used which means compulsion which is not to be applied with regard to guidance.The ignorance here means, the most people's thinking that their actions as under the divine compulsion and very few realise the chance given to man in this world to use his own choice about belief and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:112 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thus did We make for every apostle an enemy, the devils from among men and jinn, inspire some of them unto the others tinsel discourses to deceive (them); and had thy Lord pleased they would not have done it, therefore leave them and what they forge (Refer to Verses 6:50 & 41:29.) . Besides the repulsive nature mentioned in Verse 6:111, the false suggestion exchanged between the devilish agencies in the human form or unseen beings is referred to as another preventive cause. All this is done under the free choice given to man. God does not utilise His creative will to effect the prevention.To the devilish suggestion - wickedness. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:113 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So that, may incline unto it (The devilish suggestions- wickedness.) , the hearts of those who believe not in the (life) hereafter, so that they may be well pleased with it, and that they may earn what they do earn (of the evil). See 6:112

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:114 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Should other than God I (The Holy Prophet.) seek a Judge, and when He it is Who hath sent down unto you the Book (the Qur'an) (fully) explained (Made plain.) ? And those whom We have given them the Book know that it hath been sent down from thy Lord with truth, so be thou (People addressed through the Prophet.) not of those who doubt. See 6:112

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:115 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And perfect (Because perfection is finalised.) is the word of thy Lord in truth and justice; There is none who can change His words, and He is the All-Hearing and the All Knowing (Refer to Verse 6:34.) . The fulfilment of the word may mean the promise of raising a prophet-like Moses, and the sending of the Comforter, the Spirit of Truth, the Holy Ghost See"I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.""And it shall come to pass, that whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him." Deut. 18/18, 19."But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:116 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if thou (O' man! (address is not to the Holy Prophet).) obey most of those in the earth, they will lead thee astray from God's way; they follow not but conjecture (This condemns the weak and the false thinking of the majority of the people. Refer to Verse 53:23.) , they only (falsely) guess. See 6:115

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:117 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, thy Lord, He knoweth best who strayeth away from His way, and knoweth best those who follow the right guidance. See 6:115

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:118 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therefore, eat ye (the meat) of that over which hath been mentioned the name of God, if ye be believers in His signs. This injunction to eat only that on which God's name has been invoked means also not to eat that on which God's name has not been invoked. This was given in reply to the criticism of the idolaters who ate the dead animals and attacked the Muslims saying, 'Ye eat which ye yourself kill and ye eat not what God Himself has killed'. It is a known fact that eating of the animals died of some disease is harmful to the health of man.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:119 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what hath happened to you that ye eat not (meat) of that over which hath been mentioned (Allah) the name of God, while He hath indeed made plain to you what He hath forbidden unto you, excepting what ye were compelled to; and many would lead people astray by their vain desires without knowledge; Verily, thy Lord knoweth best the transgressors. Under circumstances of helplessness, one is allowed to eat even the forbidden things. This sanction indirectly proves the validity of the provision of 'Taqiah.'According to Ahl Al-Bayt, this chapter was revealed as what appeared at Mecca. According to Sunni Commentators the six or three Verses of this chapter were revealed at Madina and were put in the Chapter by Holy Prophet's order, i.e., Verse 6:92, 6:93 and 6:94 and Verse 6:152, 6:153, 6:154. It is obvious that the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say! "To whom belongeth what is in the heavens and the earth?" Say thou "To God; He hath prescribed (With the explanation of the universe being God's and there being a collective stage when all will be viewed together. It is inevitable that His treatment to all will be based only on His grace. (A.P.).) mercy on Himself; Most certainly He will gather you on the Resurrection Day, there is no doubt about it; (As for) those who have lost (ruined) their selves, they will not believe." This Verse refers to the ever-ready and all-encompassing mercy of the All-Merciful Lord, giving hopes of pardon for those who repent for their past evils and turn to piety and goodness amending their behaviour and giving up the evils.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:120 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And leave ye, open and secret sins; verily those who earn sin, soon will they be recompensed with what they earned. Sins committed by the physical organs imply open sins and the evils connected with mind, i.e., thinking, are referred to as secret or hidden sins. Islam detests and forbids both kinds of sins. To the infidels, adultery committed in secret was not condemnable. It is a mean standard of morals.There is another note of commentary in M.S. which speaks of the glorious heights to which the Holy Prophet aims to take man from the depth of the degradation of this earthly life. It says that to a real or a genuine lover of God, his getting even thoughtful of the manifest bounties of God, in this earthly life is open sinning, and getting too much mindful of the unseen…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:121 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And eat ye not of that on which God's name (Allah) was not mentioned, while Verily it was transgression; and verily Satans inspire (Note the term 'Wahi' is also used for the satanic inspirations to the wicked ones.) unto their friends, that they should contend with you, and if ye obey them, verily ye be polytheists (Thus who associate others with God in His absoluteness and authority, for details Refer to 'Fiqh'. Note: - Following dictates of Satan & his friends the wicked in using forbidden food is declared Polytheism 'Shirk. Refer to Verse 6:50.) . The infidels who used to eat the dead animals once asked 'O' Muhammad! the sheep which dies, who kills it? The Holy Prophet replied: 'The Creator!' The infidels said, 'How wonderful is it that ye eat what ye slaughter and abstain from what God…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:122 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is he who was dead, then We raised him to life and made for him a light by which he walketh among the people, like unto him whose similitude is that of one in utter darkness whence he cannot come forth? Thus hath been made fair seeming for the disbelievers what they did. Here ignorance is compared to death and the guidance to life, referring to those who were dead in conscience and were guided aright. Life and death are defined to be of two kinds:(1) The Corporeal Life and the Corporeal Death,(2) the Mental Life, i.e., the awakening of the right consciousness and the Mental Death, i.e., the loss of it.This Verse is said to have been revealed - about Hazrat Hamza - who once when returning home from a hunting trip, heard of Abu Jahl's misbehaviour with the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:123 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus made (In the manner of those who are in darkness, satisfied with their own deeds.) We in every town great ones to be its guilty ones, that they may plot therein; and they plot not but against their own selves and they perceive not. 'Ja'alna' i.e., We made. This Verse means 'Sayirna', i.e., We caused - The chief men of Mecca planned against the life of the Holy Prophet - so the chiefs every tribe are guilty. It is the divine plan to allow the powerful men to act against God's Plan and then to show the Omnipotence of God's will, which notwithstanding all the efforts of the most powerful, is always done.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:124 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when cometh unto them (The criminal dignitaries. Refer to Verses 37:12 - 37:15; 46:7.) a sign, they say: "Never will we believe until We (We also are given revelations not only you.) are given the like of what was given unto the apostles of God," God knoweth (This is a brief reply to the many questions about God's choice of a particular lineage for prophethood and His Vicegerency. (Imamat).) best where to place His apostleship: Soon shall befall those who are guilty, humiliation (This is a prophecy about the undignified end of such people.) from God and severe chastisement for what they cunningly plot. According to Tibyan, one day Walid bin Mughairah said to the Holy Prophet that if in fact there was any apostleship, it should have come to Mughairah for he was superior to the Holy Prophet…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:125 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whomsoever willeth God that He should guide him aright, He expandeth (A figurative expression pointed out in Verse 6:112 regarding the receptivity in some and the repulsive nature in some. Refer to Verse 6:112 as for the attribution of the difference to the will of God. Ref to note on Sura 1 regarding the divine action and the reaction. Refer to Verse 4:79.) his breast for Islam, and whomsoever He intendeth to leave straying, He maketh his breast straitened and narrow as though he is climbing into the very skies. Thus, doth God layeth gnominious chastisement on those who believe not (Refer to Verse 6:112.) . The words meaning 'And whomsoever God wills He should cause him to go__astray' never meant that God renders the disbelievers incapable of believing aright. It means that those who disbelieve are allowed to go…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:126 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And this (The Qur'anic path, Islam.) is the path of thy Lord, a Straight (The Right one - God's dealing with the people with recipiency and those with repulsive nature. Refer to Verse 6:126. Hence with the receptivity mentioned in the previous Verse are made the objects of the revelation i.e., the recipients of the Divine Communications.) path. Indeed, have We made clear the signs for the people who take heed. See 6:125

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:127 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For them shall be the abode of peace with their Lord, and He is their Guardian because of what they used to do. See 6:125

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:128 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on the day when He shall gather them all together (and say): "O' assembly of jinn! Ye increased your strength (by seducing a great number) from men;" And will say their friends among the men: "O' Our Lord! Some of us profited by others and We have reached our term which Thou didst appoint for us;" He shall say. "The (Hell) fire is your abode, be ye the dwellers therein, save what pleaseth God; "Verily thy Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing (Refer to Verse 55:33.) ." The actual meaning of the word ''Jinn' is the ethereal, invisible beings, i.e., the spirit of evil like the angels who are the spirit of goodness. The existence of such beings is an accepted fact, but the word 'Jinn' need not mean one and the same everywhere, as it is also used figuratively for…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:129 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thus do We make some of iniquitous to befriend (Some means by this also to control or govern the others.) the others because of what they earned. See 6:128

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And to Him belongeth whatever dwelleth in the night and the day; And He is the All-Hearing and the All-Knowing. See 6:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:130 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' assembly of jinn and men! did not come unto you apostles from among you, relating to you My signs and warning you of the meeting of this day (of requital') of yours?" They shall say: "We bear witness against Ourselves;" And this world's life deceived them, and they shall bear witness against their (own) selves that they were disbelievers (Refer to Verse 6:129 and also 41:25; 46:29 - 46:31; 55:33; 72:1 This clearly indicates the Jinns also had apostles from among their own kind.) . The address in this Verse both to the 'Jinn' as well as men, indicates that apostles among the 'Jinn' also must have come, though their names have not been mentioned in the Holy Qur'an. And the Verse 'We have sent a guide to every people' indicates that the people of the 'Jinn' must also…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:131 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This because thy Lord destroyeth not any town un-justly whilst their occupants were negligent (This indicates that people of every town are given the warning and respite before they are punished and they only neglect the warnings and the respite graciously given to them.) . This Verse clearly indicates that the 'Jinn' also must have had the guidance from God through some apostles from among them.This asserts that as a principle, no one is punishable before the Divine Order is communicated to him, but they will not be exempted from the natural consequences, though not punishable for their disobedience. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:132 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And for all are degrees in accordance with what they do; and thy Lord is not heedless of what they do. See 6:131

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:133 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thy Lord is Self-Sufficient, full of Mercy; If He pleaseth He may take you away and make successors after you, whomsoever He pleaseth, even as He raised you up from the posterity of other people (This needs a reflection on the gradual development and the progress of the human race on earth and the fate of the rebellious ones of the people of yore.) . See 6:131

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:134 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily what ye are promised, will certainly come to pass, and ye cannot make (God) helpless (Prevent or defeat.) (against it). The word 'Too'adoon' literally meaning promised-Here means threatened with, i.e., with the chastisement and the Day of Judgement on which every proved convict shall be punished and nothing would be of any avail to the infidels to stop God from taking the action against them.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:135 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say! "O' My people (Address to those who are obstinate, The proud ones of their wealth and the worldly positions) ! Act ye according to your ability; verily I too act, then soon will ye know for whom (of us) will be the abode (Whatever be the vicissitude, the ultimate is with the righteous ones. Refer to Verse 28:83 - The abode stands for the ultimate resting which is only for the righteous.) of the (good) end (of bliss); Verily shall not succeed the unjust (Refer to Verses 6:124 - 6:138.) ." It is by way of a satire and a warning, it is told to the infidels, to act as they like and the Holy Prophet would act as he has been commanded by God to do, and the infidels would soon know whose is the success in the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:136 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They assign unto God from what He hath created of tilth and cattle, and say: "This is for God, according to their assertion, and this for our associates (Their associate false gods whom they associate with the Lord.) , then what is for their associates reacheth not unto God, and whatever be for God, it reacheth their associates; (How) evil is what they judge!" The reference in this Verse is to the custom among the idolatrous Arabs that they used to set apart certain portion of their corn-fields and their cattle for God and another portion for their idols-and if any of the cattle they find growing fat, they used to get it exchanged with some lean one from the share of the idols. If anything already allotted by them for God, by chance gets into the share of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:137 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thus (Connects to the previous Verse the custodian a of the temple and not the idols.) their "Associates have made fair-seeming to most of the polytheists the slaying of their (own) children that they may cause them to perish (Which leads only the destruction.) , and confound unto them their religion, and if God hath desired (If God had only willed, He would have forced them not to do it, but this life is the state of freedom of free choice and not of compulsion.) they would not have done so, therefore leave them and what they forge." There was no limit to the brutal barbarism of the people of pre-Islamic age of ignorance female children were buried alive-there was also the practice of offering human sacrifices to the idols-sometimes they vowed that if they had a number of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:138 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "These cattle and tilth are a taboo (consecrated): None shall eat them save as we (God i.e. as God pleases.) please" (this is) according to their own Assertion (Fancy.) , and (there are) cattle whose backs are forbidden and cattle they mention not (Allah) God's name on them-forging (The forging refers to what they falsely assert.) a lie against Him (God.) , soon will He (God.) requite them for what they forge (Refer to Verses 6:136; 5:103.) . The people used to divide their cattle, and the tilth offered to God in three purposeful categories:The cattle which none ate.Those on whose back, they neither rode nor did they load1.Those which were offered to the idols-and at the time of slaughter they never even mention the name of God-and the wonder is that they attributed all these actions…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:139 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they say: "What is in the wombs of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives (Females, women.) and if it be still (Born dead.) born, then all (Both males and the females.) of them, in it are partners;" soon will He recompense them for (falsely) attributing to God; Verily He is All-Wise, All-Knowing. If the cattle allotted to the idols bear any issue, it was appropriated exclusively for their males and forbidden for their women. So did the people use to fabricate peculiar beliefs and superstitious dogmas.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say, "Shall I take a guardian besides God, the Originator of the heavens and the earth? while He feedeth (Sustains.) (others) and is not (Himself) fed (Not Sustained.) Say! "I (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) am commanded to be the first who submitteth himself (to God) (Refer to Verse 39:12.) " and be not thou (The Prophet addressed for the people.) of the polytheists (Those who associate others with God in authority.) ." Some critics say that this passage and the other similar ones which present the Holy Prophet as the first Muslim1 mean that the Holy Prophet was also a convert before which he was not a Muslim. This is wrong for Islam is a term which has been used in Qur'an to mean absolute submission to the will of God and in this sense this has been used to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:140 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed, are lost those who slay their children foolishly without knowledge and prohibit (Applicable to stopping conception and causing abortions under the modern family planning and otherwise.) they what God hath given them, forging falsehood against God. Indeed, they have gone astray and they are not guided aright. Refers to the Arab custom of burying alive female babies based on the two fanciful considerations (1) the economical and (2) the social shame-the females being unable by themselves to cam the livelihood was considered as inferior to the male issues; thus, an economical burden on the males and also as subject to the molestations by the males. Besides these they offered a male issue to the deities on the altar.With regard to the social and the ritual consideration of paganism, the modern materialism has gone to the other extreme making the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:141 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He it is who produceth gardens (of vine) trellised and untrellised, and date palms and tilth of various (kinds of food produce) and olives and pomegranates, similar (in kind) and different (in variety), eat ye of its fruit when it fruiteth (Yields the fruits.) and give ye His (God's) share ('Zakaat' the fixed poor- rate and 'Khums' the prescribed l/5th of the net profit- Ref to 'Fiqha'.) , on the day of its reaping, and act ye not extravagantly; Verily He loveth not the extravagant (ones) (This roots out and rules out all the man-made barriers created on the economic consideration of a state preventing people to move as they need to be benefited by God's provision on the earth and the ritual prohibition in this regard and establishes the right of God i.e. the prescribed poor-rate and charity…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:142 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of cattle are some bearers of burden and some (low fit only) for spreading (bed-or for staying.) ; eat ye of what God provideth you with, and follow ye not the footsteps of Satan; verily he is your declared enemy (Refer to Verses 2:168; 16:5, 16:66 40:79.) . 'Farsh' is derived from 'Farasha' meaning he spread, i.e., animals fit for slaughter because for slaughtering, they are thrown down or because bed is made out of their wool. 'Hamulah' might mean larger animals like camel and 'Farsh' smaller animals like the sheep and the young ones of camels for their being smaller in statute and thus nearer to the ground. (M.S.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:143 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Take) Eight in pairs-two of sheep and two of goats; Say: "Hath He forbidden the two males or the two females or what is contained in the wombs of the two females? Inform me with knowledge, if ye be truthful (Refer to Verses 5:103; 10:59; 16:116.) ." The Arabs under the influence of idolatry held certain animals which were lawful, to be unlawful and similarly certain unlawful animals, as lawful. Such superstitious belief and practice is condemned.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:144 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of the two camels and of the two oxen; say, the two males hath He forbidden or the two females or that which contain the (wombs) of the two females? or were ye witnesses when God did enjoin this;" Who, then is more unjust than he who forgeth (Applicable also to all kinds of conjectures about the divine affairs and authorities and matters of religion without proper knowledge of it-It is as well a warning against the modern irreligious rebellious talks. (A.P.).) a lie against God to lead astray mankind without knowledge? Verily guideth not God a people who are unjust (Refer to Verses 6:12; 6:21; 6:54; 6:58; 6:94; 6:158; 39:32.) . The reason for prohibiting the use of what dies of itself, and blood and swine's flesh is given on the things being unclean affecting the physical health…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:145 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "I find not in what hath been revealed unto me anything forbidden to an eater to eat except it be died of itself, or blood poured forth or flesh of swine for verily that is unclean or a transgression,(a) slain invoking the name of other than Allah (God), but (even so) if one is forced (Forced not by friends or the socials in clubs but by the enemy or made helpless against the use.) (to eat it) not lusting nor (wilfully) transgressing the limits, then verily thy Lord is Oft-Forgiving, All-Merciful (Refer to Verses 2:173; 5:3.) ." See 6:144

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:146 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And unto those who were Jews forbade We every animal having undivided hoof, and of oxen and sheep forbade We unto them the fat of both, save what is upon their backs or the entrails or what is mixed with bones; this We recompensed (Temporary prohibition for a local reason.) them for their rebellion, and verily We are truthful. 'Zufr' means talons and claws. 'Zi-zufr' means every beast or bird which has not divided toes as has the camel, ostrich, goose and duck.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:147 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If they belie thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) then say (though) "thy Lord is full of Mercy all-embracing but His wrath shall not be returned from the people who are guilty (Refer to Verse 3:92.) ." 'Zu-Rahmat', i.e., Lord of Mercy-the people who even rejected the true faith, offered to them by the Holy Prophet were destroyed. Sometimes their punishment had only been postponed with a respite. The concluding words clearly sav that such rebels against God will not always escape the return for their infidelity.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:148 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who are polytheists will say: "Had (The fallacy in the argument of the polytheists is that they have omitted the fact that there is no compulsion on the part of God with regard to the human action in this life. The divine will in this regard is always legislative and not creative. Refer to note in the margin of Verse 6:138.) God wished we would not have associated (aught with Him) nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden (to ourselves) anything." So did belie those before them until they tested Our wrath; Say thou: "Have ye with you any knowledge? Then produce ye that unto us, ye follow naught but conjecture and ye utter naught but guessing (Talk with no authority.) ." See 6:147

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:149 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Then, God's (alone) is the argument decisive; Had God wished He would surely have guided you all aright." The polytheist used to say that if God had willed, they would all have been guided. God had not willed so. They even attributed their going astray to God's will. This is said against the argument of the polytheists that God never misleads men, but on the other hand He sends apostle after apostle to guide man on the right path of truth. Man has been created with a free will to use his discretion to thankfully accept the guidance from God or to ungratefully reject it1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say! (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Verily I fear should I disobey my Lord, the chastisement of a great Day." See 6:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:150 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Bring ye your witnesses who bear witness that God hath forbidden this," then (even) if they bear witness, bear thou not witness with them; and follow not thou the inclinations of those who belie Our signs; and those who believe not in the hereafter, and while they with their Lord equalize (In authority.) (others). See 6:149

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:151 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) "Come ye! I will recite (unto) you what your Lord hath forbidden to you that ye associate not with Him anything and to ( your) parents be good, and slay (Applicable to the unwarranted and 'Family Planning'.) ye not your children for (fear of) poverty; We provide for you and for them, and draw ye not near unto shameful (Referable to the unnatural methods of preventing conception.) deeds, that which be apparent and that which be concealed, and kill ye not the soul which God hath forbidden save for justice; This He enjoineth you with, so that ye may understand." The injunction to parents not to slay their children for fear of the inability to maintain them owing to poverty, can as well be inferred as a condemnation of 'birth control' which by some modern…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:152 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And approach ye not the property of an orphan save that be in the best manner till he attaineth his maturity; Give ye full measure and full weight in (perfect) justice; We task not a soul but according to his ability, and when ye speak be just; though it be against a kinsman; and fulfil ye God's covenant (This serves as a reminder as well as a warning to the Muslims particularly about the Last Covenant taken from them by God through His apostle the Holy Prophet on 18th Dhu 'l-Hijja 10 AH at 'Ghadir Khumm'.) ; This He enjoineth you with so that ye may be mindful (Refer to Verse 4:6, 17:34.) . The warning against approaching the property of any orphan save in the best manner, is a provision for improving the interest of the orphan in the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:153 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (know ye) Verily this My path, is the straight (right) one, so ye follow it, and follow ye not (other) ways for they will scatter you away from His path; this doth He enjoin you with, so that ye may guard (yourselves against evil) (Refer to Verse 6:160.) . The Right or the Straight path referred to in this Verse is what the Holy Prophet showed to mankind at the conclusion of his apostolic mission, saying:I leave behind me Two weighty things, the Book of God, i.e., the Holy Qur'an, and my 'Ahl Al-Bayt' (i.e., the divinely chosen ones of my family, i.e., the Lady of Light Fatema and the Twelve Holy Imams). If ye hold fast to these two, never, never shall ye be led astray, never shall these two, i.e., the Holy Qur'an and the Ahl Al-Bayt…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:154 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Besides, We gave Moses the Book completing (our favours) on those who would do good and explaining all things in details, and a guidance and a mercy, so that in the meeting (The day of resurrection and for the Final Judgement. Refer to Verse 35:42.) of their Lord they may believe. By 'all things' meaning everything needed for the guidance of the Israelites of Moses' time, which includes the prophecy relating to the advent of the Holy Prophet Muhammad. Deut. 18/18-19.1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:155 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And this (Qur'an) is a Book, We have sent it down, blessed, so follow it, and guard (your-selves against evil) so that ye may be done mercy (Receive God's mercy.) . It should be noted that all the previous revelations being only for the time, and not a complete code for all times, were not called a complete Book and it is the Holy Qur'an which is presented as a complete Book. Besides, there is the quality of the book mentioned as 'Mubarak', i.e., a blessing-a blessing is continued grace of God which infers that this is the Book which shall for ever remain a blessing for mankind in general and its adherents in particular.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:156 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Lest ye (Polytheists) should say "that the Book (from God) was sent down unto two parties (This indicates that the previous Scriptures were sectional, not universal, which fact is confirmed by several passages of the Qur'an pointing out that Moses and Jesus were sent but only to the Children of Israel-This is clearly and openly acknowledged by the Bible of the Christian church and the national character of the belief in godhead as presented in the Old and the New Testaments Math-15/22-26 10/5 - John- 16/5-14 Etc.) (the Christians and the Jews) before us, and verily we were of what they read, unaware." See 6:155

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:157 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or (lest) ye should say: "Had only been sent unto us a book we should have been better guided than they;" so indeed hath (now) come unto you a manifest proof from your Lord, and guidance and mercy; who then is more unjust than he who belieth the signs of God and turneth away from them? Soon shall We recompense those who turn away from Our signs with an evil chastisement for what they used to turn away (Refer to Verses 7:5, 6:21, 6:94, 6:145, 39:92.) . Believing in God's signs - A sign is a certain action or a thing through which a certain person or a meaning is understood. There is nothing in the world which does not give any lead toward the existence of God. Thus, everything in the universe, is God's sign, but sign to sign…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:158 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They wait not but (to see) that (Refer to the adamance of the disbelievers.) come unto them the angels, or cometh thy Lord (Himself), or that come (unto them) some signs of thy Lord; on the day when come (i.e. the good deeds of the one who believed but acted only after the sign.) some of the signs of thy Lord, its faith shall profit not a soul which believed not before, or earned good through its faith; Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) "Wait ye! Verily We too are waiting (Refer to Verse 7:5.) ." Coming of the angels, means the coming of the angels of death or of the angels to execute the decree of the doom of the disbelievers and the coming of the Lord means the dawn of the Day of the Final Judgment.The pagans used to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:159 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily those who divided their religion and became parties, thou hast no concern with anything of them; their affair is with God only, then will He inform them of what they did (Refer to Verse 6:154.) . This refers to sectarianism in all religions, i.e., accepting a part and rejecting the other or, misinterpreting the Word of God by one's own imagination and not following the meaning rendered by the authentic sources commissioned by God. The best and the only authority about God, godliness and the correct interpretation of the Word of God after the Holy Prophet are the Holy Imams. Referring only to this fact, the Holy Prophet had declared:"The likeness of my Ahl Al-Bayt is that of the Ark of Noah, He who got into it was safe and he who turned away from it, was drowned and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: From whomsoever it (the Chastisement) is averted on that day, indeed He (God.) had mercy ('Rahimiyat' not 'Rahmaniyat'.) on him; and this will be the manifest triumph (Salvation.) ". See 6:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:160 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whosoever cometh with a good (deed) for him shall be ten (According to God's grace.) like it; and whosoever cometh with an evil (deed) he shall be recompensed not but with the like (According to God's Justice.) of it, and they shall not be dealt with unjustly. This Verse announces only the maximum amount of punishment for evil and the minimum reward for virtue otherwise the Holy Prophet had announced a greater encouragement to those who desire to build up goodness for themselves saying that every evil will be recompensed with the like of it, whereas a virtue of or a goodness will get from the All-Merciful Lord, a tenfold or a seventy-hundred-fold reward. Thus, while Islam warns man and woman against the divine justice, which will not spare any offender from being punished, it also gives the glad tidings…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:161 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) "Verily my Lord hath guided me unto the straight (right) path (Islam-i.e. Absolute submission to the divine will.) ; the established (Which never changes – unimpeachable.) religion, the faith of Abraham, the upright one; and he (Abraham.) was not of the polytheists." See 6:160

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:162 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "Verily my prayer and my sacrifice, my life and my death, (are all, only) for God, the Lord of the worlds (This is what the term Islam inspires and demands of every Muslim. That every act of his in this life secular or religious- to be exclusively for God. Refer to Verse 2:156.) ." The highest goal of human life is the Law of God which alone must be the mainspring or the generative factor of every word and deed of a man or a woman in this life. Be that the love of one's self, of one's family and children, love of one's friends and relatives, the law of one's country and countrymen, the lover of wealth or any other requisition in this life, if motivated and contributed for the love of God, there cannot be anything more…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:163 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: No associate (In the devotion of The Holy Prophet to Him.) (is there) for Him; and this I am commanded, I am the first of the Muslims (i.e., those who submit to God) (Refer to Verse 6:14.) . This Verse clearly says that the first, i.e., the ideal or the perfect model of a true Muslim, was the Holy Prophet himself.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:164 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "Shall I seek other than God a Lord? While He is the Lord of all things; and no soul earneth (any evil deed) but against itself; and no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another; then unto your Lord is your return, so He will inform you of what ye used to differ (about) (Refer to Verses 2:48; 2:123; 2:254; 17:15; 35:18; 39:7; 53:38; 53:39.)" Islam does not allow any belief in any unconditional redemption of any one, merely at his or her believing in any prophet or saint. The belief that any one has purchased the salvation of the sinners by his sacrifices, renders God helpless against the wrongs and the offences committed in His Kingdom and deprives God of any power or right even to question any offender. With this belief, any one will be…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:165 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He (God.) it is who hath made you (His) Vicegerent in the earth and raised some of you above others in grades, that He may try you in what He gave you; Verily thy Lord is quick in the requital (of evil) and (yet) verily He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Merciful. The word 'Khalif' meaning the deputies of God, i.e., man or woman, has been created to manifest the divine attributes in his or her life. If one remains conscious of this great assignment and tries to be true to the trust, it will be quite sufficient to reach the divinely destined goal of the bliss of the glorious heights of the divinity in store for every faithful one, man or woman.There are some who assert that every believer is a vicegerent of God. Based on this theory they…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if God toucheth thee with affliction, none can remove it but He; and if He toucheth thee with Good, then He hath power over all things. Meaning the soul, the Only and the Supreme Master doing good or harming anyone, whose decision is ever irrevocable, is God and none else. Hence man needs to love or to fear only God and no other authority and to depend only on Hint and on none else.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He is the Supreme (Lord) above (In authority with wisdom and awareness.) His servants (Creatures.) ; and He is the All-Wise and the All-Aware. See 6:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say! (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "What thing is the weightiest in testimony?" Say thou: "God is witness between me and you; and hath been revealed unto me this Qur'an (As the divine evidence.) that I may warn you with it, and whomsoever it reacheth (Indicates the. universality of 'the mission of the Holy Prophet compared to that of those before him.) ; Do ye really bear witness that there are other gods with God?" Say thou: "I bear not (such) witness"! Say thou: Verily, Verily He is only one God and Verily I am away from that which ye associate (with Him) (Refer to Verse. 6:92. O. T. Deut. 5/4.) . 'Man Balagha ainnakum' clearly denotes that the Holy Prophet's mission was not confined or restricted to anyone particular people or place but to mankind as a whole for all…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He it is Who Created you of clay, then decreed the term (In Arabic Ajl. Refer to Verse 82:7.) (of your life); and the term determined (Lit. fixed time for resurrection or judgment.) is with Him and yet (In spite of all the changes obvious to you.) ye doubt (About the fixity of the term.) (thereof). 'Created you', 'You' stands for Adam the Progenitor of the human species or every human being, or the address can be to any creature on earth. The origin of every earthly thing is from clay. The first term is the life until death and the second one, is the resurrection. However, all men are created from clay or dust.Man as an individual as well as a specie, in the course of his creation passes through stages from the embryo to full grown babe, a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those whom We have given the Book recognise him (Muhammad), as they recognise their (own) sons; (yet) those who have lost (Ruined.) their selves, they will not believe. As none can fail to recognize his own son, the prophecies about and the identification of the Holy Prophet was so doubtlessly clear in the ancient scriptures, particularly in the scriptures of the Jews and the Christians and no prophet answering the given description had ever appeared anywhere in the world. The Jews and the Christians had no reasons at all, or there was not the least difficulty for them to recognize the genuine apostolic personality of the Holy Prophet.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And who is more unjust than he who forgeth a lie against God or (he who) giveth the lie to His signs; verily the unjust will not succeed (Refer to Verses 6:94; 6:144; 6:158; 39:32.) . Forging lies against God means saying or believing in things falsely relating them to God, viz. God having a son or sons and daughters or God having delegated His authority to anyone else to act on His behalf - and the similar other heathenic belief.The tone of the set of Verses 6:21 - 6:25 is that of a conversation between two persons before whom the whole scene of the ultimate days was present, as going on before them. With regard to God it is obvious and with regard to the Holy Prophet will be obvious if one grasps the meaning of the actual significance…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on the day (of Judgment) We shall gather them all together, then We shall say to those who associated others (With God.) "Where are your associate-gods whom ye used to conject?" See 6:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then their excuse (In Arabic 'Fitna', the mischief of their disbelief will not be there.) would be nothing but that they would say: "By God, Our Lord! we were not polytheists." 'Fitna', i.e., the lie they uttered or their disbelief would not remain any longer, but they would say 'By our Lord, ire are not polytheists.'

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Behold (In Arabic 'Unzur' Lit. See - This indicates that the whole scene of the day was visualised before the Holy Prophet or he could himself visualise it. Otherwise to Command with something impossible to be implemented will be meaningless.) ! how they lie against their own selves, and that which they forged has passed away from them. See 6:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of them are those who hearken unto thee, and We have cast veils over their hearts lest they understand it, and a heaviness into their ears; and together (even) if they see every (All the signs i.e. all miracles together.) sign they will not believe in it; to the extent that when they come (Refer to Verse 47:16.) to thee they only dispute with thee, those who disbelieve say: "This is naught but the legends (Refer to Verses 68:15; 83:13.) of the ancients." This and the succeeding two Verses indicate that veils were cast over their hearts because they were determined not to believe even if all the signs, i.e., miracles were shown to them. They used to visit the Holy Prophet not to listen to what he said but to dispute with him and to create doubts in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They prohibit (others) from it, and (themselves) keep far away from it; they only destroy their own selves, and (yet) they perceive (it) not. See 6:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And couldst thou see when they are made confronting (Stop at.) the (Hell) fire, then they shall say, "Would that we were sent back and we would not belie the signs of our Lord, and we would be of the believers.''" See 6:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay, it has been manifested to them what they did conceal before; and if they were sent back they would certainly return to what they were forbidden and most certainly they are liars (Refers to the possibility of any improvement or expiation through transmigration because of the inherent nature, every soul will always reveal itself in whatever form it may assume.) . See 6:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they say: "there is nothing (beyond') this our life in this world, and we are not to be raised again (This doctrine applies to those who totally deny the life hereafter or believe that they will only be sent back to another earthly form.) ." See 6:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (While.) He is God in the heavens and in the earth! He knoweth your secrets and your disclosures! and He knoweth what ye earn (for yourselves by your deeds). This is a repeated assertion of the Unity of God, the Only Creator, Lord, Cherisher of the Universe. He is the Knower of everything, be it hidden or manifest. Hidden and manifest are the two terms that are related only to man; for, to God nothing can be hidden for He is the maker of everything. Everything is in His view, and nothing is out of His knowledge. His knowledge envelops everything1. This is a warning as well, meaning, let not anyone think that what one does can ever be a secret from the All-Knowing Lord.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And couldst thou see when they are made to stand before their Lord ('Ba'eb' i.e. resurrection is an evolutionary stage from the Terrestrial life into a heavenly and a non-physical or non-material realm in which one feels his pretence before God (A.P.).) , He will say: "Is this not the truth?" They will say: "Yes! by Our Lord!" He will say: "Taste ye then the chastisement for what ye did (Used to.) disbelieve." See 6:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed, are losers, they who disbelieved the meeting (Not seeing, but Communion in some way appropriate to his absoluteness and our finiteness.) of God, until cometh suddenly upon them the hour ('Sa'a' i.e. the Hour i.e. of the Doom.) (of Resurrection)', They will say: "O' Our grief for our neglecting it!" And they shall bear their burdens on their backs; Is it not evil indeed what they shall bear. Feeling of sorrow or pleasure for the past actions, is one of the main features of the life here after, which is absent in the doctrine of transmigration (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the life of this world is naught but play and vain sport; and certainly the abode of the hereafter, is the best for those who guard (themselves against evil); Do ye not then understand (Refer to Verses 29:64; 47:36; 57:20.) ? See 6:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed, We know, it certainly grieveth thee that which they say, but verily it is not thee (The Holy Prophet) (that) they belie, but (it is) the signs of God, the wrong doers deny. The Holy Prophet had already impressed even upon the worst of his enemies, his truthfulness, and everyone, be he his foe or a friend, had acknowledged him as 'Sadiq', i.e., the Truthful and 'Al-Ameen' - the Trustworthy. He had already earned from the people as a whole these titles even from the very beginning of his life, before his declaring his apostleship.Hence the people's now rejecting his message, is not that they mean him a liar, but it was a denial of the bonafide of the Divine Revelation. The world around him had unanimously vouched that he had never even once been guilty of having uttered…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And most certainly were belied (Our) apostles before thee, but they were patient on their being belied and were persecuted until came to them Our help; and none can alter the words ('Words' stands here for God's will Creative or Legislative. Here refers to the decision about His Prophets. Refer to Verses 58:21; 37:171; 37:172.) of God; And most certainly hath come to thee the tidings about the apostles (from Us) (Refer to Verses 6:116; 37:171; 37:172; 38:21.) . 'There is none to change the Words of God.' The word of God means God's promises of sending the necessary help to His Apostles. It is a prophecy to say that as the apostles before the Holy Prophet were helped, he would also be surely helped.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if their turning away be hard upon thee (The address though apparently is to the Holy Prophet, but it is obvious that it cannot be a man of realisation like the Holy Prophet will never feel straitened. The address in fact is to the followers of the Holy Prophet who felt straitened for the people's turning away.) , then if thou canst seek an opening (to go down) into the earth or a ladder (to ascend up) to heaven so that thou bringeth them a sign (a miracle) (it will be in vain) But if only God desireth, certainly would He have gathered them all on the (right) guidance, so be not thou of the ignorants (Refer to Verse 52:38.) . This Verse is in reply to the extraordinary anxiety of the Holy Prophet to take all the people…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, only those will accept thee, who listen (to the Word of God); and (as to) the dead, God will raise them, then unto Him will they return (Refer to Verses 39:17; 39:18.) . Only those who listen, sincerely interested in knowing the truth, will believe. As for those who do not listen, they are like the dead and God will surely raise the dead on the Day of Resurrection. Then they will believe but it will be of no avail to them.Refers to the actual purpose of the apostolic preaching in spite of its being universal but the object is the guidance of those who have aptitude for development and progress. The sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq said to his disciples 'Increase not your number by calling all sorts of people into your fold irrespective of their…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they say: "Why is not a sign sent down unto him from his Lord?" Say! "Verily God is able to send down a sign but most (Majority Condemned.) of them know not (The Sign referred to in this Verse is the same adverted to in Verse 6:35.) ." See 6:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: There is not an animal that walketh upon the earth, not a bird that flieth with its two wings, but they are communities the like of you; We have not neglected ('Tafreet' Overstepping by total negligence or by misplacing it. Everything has been in its proper place in the Book of Creation of which Qur'an is the microform (A.P.). Refer to Verses 7:57; 7:58.) in the Book (The Qur'an), anything, then unto their Lord shall they (all) be gathered (in the end). Even the animals that walk on earth as well as those who fly, i.e., the birds, will be brought to account for the duties entrusted to them according to the native endowments, they are provided with.'Kitab' here means the Book called 'Lawh al-Mahfooz, i.e., the Divinely Secured Tablet.Most of the commentators are of opinion that the word 'Book'…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they who belied Our signs are deaf (The preaching will not avail them.) and dumb, in utter darkness; whom God pleaseth He alloweth them to go astray; and whom He pleaseth (Refer to Verse. 3:1. God's pleasure is conditioned with the aptitude of every individual. (A.P.).) , He doth put them on the straight (Right.) path. See 6:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: There came not unto them any sign from the signs of their Lord but they turned away from it. 'Aayaat' means signs, revelations, communications - Every Prophet or Apostle and every divinely commissioned successor of the Holy Prophet (i.e., the Imams) all were the 'Aayaat', i.e., the signs through whom God and godliness was manifested into this world.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Think ye that if cometh to you the chastisement (Any unexpected hardship even in this life.) of God, or cometh to you the Hour (hour of hardship even in this life.) (of resurrection), will ye call (for help) other than God, (say ye it out) if ye are truthful." See 6:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay, Him (God.) will ye call (At the time of distress.) upon, and He cleareth (Deliver - give an opening relief.) away which ye pray for unto Him if He pleaseth, and ye would forget (the false gods') ye set up (with Him). This Verse gives out an inherent characteristic in every human being, be he a believer in God or an unbeliever, a Unitarian or a polytheist, that in the state of a total helplessness while in distress, when one finds none to help him, the inner self in him, is liberated from the restrictions of the individual's personal views, and commands him to call upon the ever-present Omnipotent One and the liberated mind automatically calls Him for the rescue.Once a man asked the Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq, to show God to him. The Holy Imam…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And most certainly We sent (apostles) unto peoples before thee, then We caught them in distress and adversity, in order they might humble themselves (Refer to Verses 4:164; 10:47; 16:36; 15:24; 13:7; 40:78.) . Islam is the only religion in the world which recognizes and pays equal regard to all the apostles of God preceding the Holy Prophet1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Yet why did they not, when our punishment came to them, humble themselves? but their hearts were hardened and the devil made fair-seeming for them, what they did act (Refer to Verse 26:4.) . See 6:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when they forgot that which they had been admonished (Reminded of.) , We opened for them the doors of all things (of enjoyments); until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We caught them suddenly, when lo! they were in utter despair. Opening of the doors of all things, meaning bounties, were bestowed on them in abundance and when surrounded by the abundant provision, they forgot the Lord. They were visited by a sudden visitation, and they were completely destroyed.It is reported of the Holy Prophet that he said: 'When ye see anyone in spite of his continuous sinfulness is more and more blessed with bounties from God - then be sure that he is only given the respite and an opportunity either to repent and return to the right path or to be surprised by a sudden…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So, the roots (Even the last remnant removed.) of the people who were unjust (Wrong doers.) were cut (Removed from the existence.) off; and all praise is God's the Lord of the worlds. Dabir is the root - meaning the fast man. They were so completely destroyed to the last one of them that not a single one of them was spared.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "Think ye, that if God taketh away your hearing and your sight and sealeth on your hearts, who is the god other than God that can bring (Restore.) it (again) to you?" See thou, how We display (explaining) the signs yet they turn aside. 'Nasarrifu' i.e., How' we argue to admonish in variant ways, sometimes with advice, and sometimes with warnings, i.e., in diversified ways.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) "Think ye, if the chastisement (When the calamities come even the good are also enveloped along with the evil ones, but for being recompensed in the here-after the calamity is not destructive for the good ones as it is for the evil ones.) of God cometh to you suddenly or openly, will any be destroyed but the unjust (The wrong doers.) people?" See 6:46

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We send not messengers but (as) heralds with glad tidings and warners; then whoever believeth and acteth (Note that acting aright or amending one's own conduct has been essential with the faith or belief.) aright, they shall have no fear (For having the eternal bliss and security.) , nor shall they grieve. See 6:46

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (as for) those who belie our signs, chastisement shall afflict them for what they used to transgress. See 6:46

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They have indeed belied the truth when it came to them; therefore, very soon the tidings (News- Tidings, i.e. about the Truth.) will come (be known) to them of what they mocked at. See 6:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "I do not say unto you (that) with (All that was possessed by the Holy Prophet, was God's and not his.) me are the treasures (Refer to Verses 52:37; 52:38; 7:187.) of God, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say unto you that I am an angel; I follow not but what is revealed unto me;" Say, "Are the blind and the seeing (Refer to Verses 5:100; 13:16; 39:9; 47:14.) alike; Do ye not then reflect?" This Verse speaks out the unique sublimity and selflessness of the Holy Prophet. He did not want the people to take him as other than a man. He never gave any room in any of his utterances about his own self which would in the least mislead the people to raise him to godhead, neither during…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And warn thou with it (What is revealed. Refer to Verse 6:50.) , the Qur'an those who fear that they shall be gathered unto their Lord (Thinking that) there shall not be for them, besides Him, any guardian or an intercessor, happily they may guard (themselves against evil). This passage indicates that the prophetic warning, avails only those who are afraid of being brought to the presence of God, with none besides Him to help or intercede. People with such bent of mind are apt to develop piety in them. The negation of a helper or an intercessor besides God, does not negate the help and the intercession of the prophets with regard to their followers and the help and the intercession of the Last Prophet for the creation as a whole because their help and their intercession by God's…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And drive (Prophet addressed for the people.) not away those who call upon their Lord, in the morning and the evening, they seek His countenance (Face.) ; neither it is on thee to answer for anything on their account nor is it on them to answer for anything on thine account so that thou driveth them away and thus be of the unjust (Reference to the aristocratic view of the common man which Islam was to abolish and bring those who prided over the others to the level of the brotherhood. Refer to Verses 17:15; 35:18; 39:7; 49:13; 99:7; 99:8.) . It is commented upon this Verse that this Verse was revealed when some rich ones among the Quraish proud of their wealth and position refused to sit mixed up with the poor ones among the followers of the Holy…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus, did We try some of them by others so that they say: "Are these they upon whom God hath conferred (Obliged with blessings.) (His) favours, from among us? Doth (This is an answer to the question) not God know best the grateful?" It was a trial for the arrogant wealthy Quraish who valued and regarded only wealth and nothing else and never treated the poor even as human beings.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when come unto thee, those who believe in Our signs, say: "Salamun-alaikum" (Peace be on you) your Lord hath prescribed (Took upon Himself to be merciful.) mercy on Himself, (so that) if anyone of you doth evil in ignorance, then turneth (repentant) after that and amendeth (himself), then verily He (An answer to the repentance (The Sixth Holy Imam).) is the Most-Forgiving, The Most-Merciful. This Verse conveys a very great note of mercy of the Lord.The offering of 'Peace' to the believers is not the peace in the ordinary sense of the word. Peace of God means His mercy.God Himself making mercy incumbent upon Himself, i.e., His mercy Supreme and Absolute, and when anyone is blessed with the mercy from the Lord, it will naturally be sufficient to wipe out all the sins of the individual - for God…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thus We explain the signs in details so that the way of the sinners may be manifest (By comparing it with the way of the repentants.) . See 6:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say! (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "I am forbidden to worship those whom ye call besides God;" Say Thou: "I follow not your inclinations for then indeed I should have gone astray and I will not be of those who are guided (aright)." See 6:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Verily I have manifest proof from my Lord and you belied it; I have not with me that (chastisement) which ye hasten (Asked to be hastened.) for; the judgment belongeth (to none) but unto God; Who declareth the truth and He is the best decider." See 6:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou, "If it were with me (The Chastisement.) , what ye hasten for, certainly would have been decided the matter between me and you (But it is with God.) ; and God knoweth best the unjust." That which you desire to hasten, i.e., the chastisement from God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And with Him are the keys (of the treasures) of the unseen - knoweth it not anyone but He; and He (alone) knoweth what is in the land and the sea; and (there) falleth not (even) a leaf (of a tree) but He knoweth it, nor a grain in the darkness (in the deepest parts) of the earth, nor anything wet or dry but (it is) in a clear Book (Refers - that besides his knowledge, there is with God the record of everything Refer to Verse. on Book 'Lawh Al-Mahfooz' The Protected Tablet Qur'an as a microform representing it. Refer to Verses 15:21; 34:3; 36:12.) . 'Mafatih' is the plural for 'Miftuh', i.e., treasury or a repository as well as for 'Miftah' meaning a Key - i.e., God alone is the Master of everything unseen (as well as the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: See they not how many a generation before them We have destroyed, whom We had established in the earth (to the extent to) which We had not yet established you (till now), and We sent the clouds to rain abundantly upon them, and We made the rivers flow beneath (their dwellings) and yea We destroyed them for their sins and raised (The modern time excavations and the findings of the ancient cities buried - prove the truth in this statement.) up after them another generation. See 6:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-An'aam:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:103 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Shall grieve them not the great terror and the angels shall meet them (saying): "This is your Day, which ye were promised" See 21:101

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:104 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On that day will We roll up the heaven, as is rolled up the written scroll; As we caused the first creation, (Creature.) so will We get it return. (It is) a promise binding Us, Verily We were doing (Indicates the process to be continuous.) it. Like a scroll of parchment, the Universe will be folded up. For those who doubt about the whole Universe being brought to an end, another phase of life being created by the Almighty Lord, there can not be a better answer than the following verse of the Holy Qur'an:"Is not He Who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Aye, He is, for He is the All-Wise Creator." (36:81)'Khalqin' may be used as an infinitive, i.e., 'Creation'. 'Khilqat' may also be used as a noun meaning a creature…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:105 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We did write in the Psalms (Zabur) (given to David) after the Reminder (at-Tawrat given to Moses), that the earth, shall inherit it My servants righteous. (The Righteous ones.) About the righteous ones inheriting the earth mentioned in the scriptures given to the apostles of God gone before the Holy Prophet - Psalms 25/11, 37/29; and Math. 5/3 and Exod. 32/13."His soul shall dwell at ease; and his seed shall inherit the earth." Ps. 25/13."But the men shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace."Ps. 36/11."The righteous shall inherit the land, and dwell therein forever." Ps. 37/29."Blessed are the poor in spirit; for theirs is the kingdom of heaven." Math. 5/3."Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, thy servants, to whom thou sincerest by thine own self, and saist unto them, I will multiply your…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:106 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily in this is a conveyance for a people who worship (Us). See 21:105

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:107 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We sent thee not (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) but a Mercy unto (all) the worlds. Sages had come to India for the local need of the guidance of the people of the place and the age. Similarly, apostles of God had visited all parts of the earth, some for a particular community and some for a larger group of the tribes and the people put together. Jesus had come for the lost house of Israel. Now the Holy Prophet had brought a message - the Book and the religion perfected by God Himself having in itself all the good that was endowed in the various previous messages, with the truth to its maximum fullness. This Universal Message and its Holy Messenger was nothing but the Mercy of the Lord, and the Mercy of the Lord in its fullness could…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:108 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "It hath only been revealed unto me that your God is One God: Will ye then submit (unto Him i.e. be Muslims)" It means that God is not the Lord Master of any particular people but of the Universe as a whole. This verse speaks of the Universal Authority and Lordship of God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:109 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they turn back say: "I have warned you all alike; and I know not whether nigh or far, is that which ye are (Threatened.) promised." The knowledge of the Day of Judgment and the decision about effecting the requital which the people were warned with, rests, wholly with God and not the concern of the Holy Prophet, to say when it would actually come to pass. Similarly did Jesus say: that none, not even the angels and neither he, but God alone knows about the Hour.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: How many a town (the people of) which were iniquitous, We did (Break.) destroy, and raised We up after it another (Nation – folk.) people? See 21:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:110 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, He knoweth what is spoken aloud, and He knoweth (too) what ye hide See 21:109

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:111 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And I know not (also) happly this (respite) may be a trial for you and a provision until a time.
