The good of the world enjoyed by the disbelievers need not worry the believers or grieve them for that it is only a tempting passing show, only a fleeting pleasure or enjoyment destined to end but that which is in store for the faithful, in the hereafter is the real and the everlasting.The Second Holy Imam Hasan quoted this verse in his sermon at the eve of giving up the reigns of the rule of the Caliphate to Muawiyah. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:112 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (the Apostle Muhammad praying): "O' my Lord! Judge Thou with truth; And Our Lord is the Beneficent, Whose help is sought against what ye (Unto God or to His apostles.) ascribe (unto Him)" See 21:111

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So when they felt (the coming of) Our torment, lo! they began (trying) to fly from it. People do not avail of the respite given to them and when the Wrath of God comes, they try to flee from it; but where would they go?

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Said We (God.) ): "Flee not ye but return unto that wherein ye revelled, (Lived easy – extravagantly.) and unto your dwellings, happly ye will be questioned." It is an ironical statement asking them why they do not return to the life of the luxuries on earth, which they were engrossed in and thought the life on earth to be permanent, and they did not believe in the Day of Reckoning.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "Oh! Woe unto us! Verily, we were unjust!" This would be the repentant lamentations of the disbelievers.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And ceased not this their cry till We made them like reaped (Cut off.) corn, extinct. The two similes refer to the fate with which the disbelievers are warned, as to what their end would be.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We created not the heavens and the earth and what is between them for (Refer to verse 44:38.) sport. Nothing in the universe has been created without any object behind its existence. People are warned not to take life lightly. To consider every factor of life seriously.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Had We intended that We should take amusement, We could certainly have taken it from (the things) with Us, if We had been doing (it) We had willed to do it. If at all God had desired anything like a mere sport, the things of real excellence with Him, would have sufficed the purpose and not the lowly creation of the earthly beings.Asserts that the creation of the heavens and the earth is not purposeless, and the purpose is something serious - and not playful and not for mere amusement. The analogical tendency in man makes him always to conceive about God after his own image. As man's action is sometimes motivated by fun or amusement, he attributes the same to God - that the purpose of creation is just for amusement in the same manner as the authorities amuse…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! We hurl truth upon falsehood, that it crusheth its head, and lo! it vanisheth; and woe unto you for what ye describe (of God). 'Describe' refers to the false belief of God having partners1 and God having begotten a son2 or His having daughters3 or any other polytheistic belief about God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And His is whosoever is in the heavens and the earth; and those who are (Present with God.) with Him are not proud to worship Him, nor do they get weary. The heavenly beings which are also the created ones of God unceasingly adore the Majesty of the Glory of the Lord.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (There) Cometh not unto them a reminder from their Lord, anew, save they hear it and they get busy in sport. Even with the repeated reminder from the Lord, instead of getting awakened to be guided aright, the people only listen to the admonition only to ridicule and laugh at them. They waste their life and wealth in wasteful fooleries forgetting totally the life Hereafter.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They glorify (Him) by night and day, they (even) intermit (Relax not.) not. See 21:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or have they taken gods from the earth who can raise (the dead)? It is made clear that the false gods or the imaginary deities can never give life to anything which God has destined to die. This does not mean that any of the apostles of God also who show miracles manifesting the Omnipotence of God, cannot raise the dead which they can do by God's will. Thus, the raising of the dead caused by Jesus as a miracle can never be brought under this statement.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Had there been in (the heavens and the earth) (other) gods except God, they both had been in disorder; So glorified is God, the Lord of the 'Arsh' (The Throne of Supreme Authority.) (High above) from what they attribute (unto Him). This is the simplest and the greatest and the self-proved argument about the Unity of God. The unity and the perfect harmony with which the universe is going on since its birth, itself is the proof positive that there is only One single authority which is governing the working of the universe with the laws regulated in perfect harmony with each other.If there be two or more beings holding equal authorities over the ownership or the working of the universe, the dual or the multiple personalities of the authority will be meaningless and unnecessary for when they work together…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He is not questioned about what He doeth, but they shall be questioned. There can be no argument against any Act of God. God is never questionable, whereas it is man who would be questioned.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Have they taken beside Him other gods? Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Bring ye your proof: (that they are gods). This (Qur'an) is the Reminder unto those with me, and the Reminder unto those before (Indicates the unity of God and the universal aspect of Islam.) me; Nay! most of them know not the truth, so they turn aside." This is the declaration that the Unity of God advocated by the Holy Qur'an is the truth which is found in the scriptures given to every other apostle of God who visited the earth, preceding the Holy Prophet (i.e., it is a universal truth or the basic fundamental of every religion which was preached to man by the men of God). The one without any external education under any mortal on earth, shut up in the land where heathenism and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And sent We not before thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) any apostle but revealed We unto him that "Verily there is no god but I; so worship ye Me (alone)" See 21:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "The Beneficent (God) hath taken unto Him a (Taken to - or adopted - has begun - beget – issuing.) son; Glory be to Him! Nay! They (The prophets and the angels whom they worshipped as gods or the sons or the daughters of God.) are (His) honoured servants." This verse refutes the false belief not only of the Christian trinity but also of the angels being worshipped as the daughters of God. The trinitarian belief is an innovation of the people of the church founded in the name of Christ. There is nothing there in the Bible to support any such phenomenon which is only the product of the over enthusiasm of the converts to the creed of the church from the pagan Romans. Trinity was innovated by Constantine the Pagan King of Rome as the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They speak not ere He speaketh, and they on His bidding (only) act. This verse clearly states that the apostles of God neither spoke nor acted at any time, of their own accord. It was only the Divine Will which they translated into their words and deeds. Hence they never sinned. Since always acting under the Divine Will they were naturally infallible. Jesus is reported to have said:"For I have not spoken of myself but the Father which sent me; he gave me a commandment, what I should say, and what I should speak."And I know that his commandment is life everlasting; whatsoever I speak therefore, even as the Father said unto me, so I speak." John 12/49-50.This is one of the unique characteristics of the Holy Qur'an as the Final Word of God and the clear testimony of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Knoweth He what is before them and what is behind them, and they can not intercede but for him whom He approveth, and they, of His fear, tremble. The fear mentioned here is not dread but the regard for the Majesty of the Glory of the Lord. And as for the question of the right of redemption or intercession allowed to the chosen ones of God.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whosoever of them sayeth; Verily I am god besides Him, such a one will We recompense with hell; Thus do We recompense the iniquitous. This refers to the priests and the kings who claimed godhead for themselves besides God - i.e., claimed Divinity. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Pre-occupied at their hearts with trifles; and discoursed in secret (Refer to verse 20:62.) ; those who did wrong (saying) "Is this (man) (The Holy Prophet.) other (Not more than an ordinary man.) than a human being like unto yourselves; What! will ye then yield unto sorcery while ye see (it)?" The reference is to the attitude of the disbelievers towards the recital of the Holy Qur'an. They listened with a trifling heart and when struck with the miraculous impression of the Word of God they secretly counselled to each other saying that the Holy Prophet was merely a man like them and what he recited was only a sorcery, hence they should not yield to the enchantment. When the people get helpless against the wonderful knowledge and the amazing excellences of the sublime and the superb qualities in the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or see not those who disbelieve that the heavens and the earth were one piece, (One solid mass.) and that We clave them asunder; and made We of water everything alive; Will they not then believe? A man asked the Fifth Holy Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir the explanation of 'Closed up' in this verse. The holy Imam asked the man, "Do thou thinkest that the heavens and the earth were combined or joined together and they were separated." The man answered, 'Yes, my Lord!' The holy Imam said:"Seek thou the pardon of God, for it means that the heavens were neither showering any water on the earth nor was the earth vegetating or growing anything on it. Both the heavens and the earth were closed for anything coming out of them. When God created life on earth, he made…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We have made in the earth, (lofty) mountains (standing firm) lest it should shake with them, and We have made therein broad highways that they may be guided aright. The position of mountains on earth is a factor of guidance. Those who have travelled through the barren plains of Sahara without any mountains in them, know the task of finding out the correct direction for the routes to the different places. If taking the figurative use of the word mountain, as some commentators have taken, it will mean that God by His infinite mercy has sent His apostles and His chosen guides for the guidance of man towards the correct route he has to take in his life-journey. The mountains will mean the holy apostles and the holy Imams.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We have made the heavens a canopy, (Roof or vault.) well guarded; and yet they, from its signs turn aside. None can ever even imagine passing through the heavens. Though man is trying to travel through space, even if he succeeds, the journey will be only with its own limitation. None can ever know the exact extent of the space and the existence of the millions and millions of the solar systems, one after the other being continuously discovered more and ever more by every stronger telescope that man could make. It clearly indicates the impossibility of any travel by any one all through the whole of space. Besides the professors of witchcraft falsely claim of their journeys into the heavens. This verse negates all such false claims of such bogus spiritualists getting into heaven or getting anything from…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He it is Who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon; all in their (respective) orbits move (in a swim). Until yesterday, the world of science believed the sun to be stationary and all the other planets revolving around it. As early as about fourteen hundred years, the Holy Qur'an informed man that the Sun also is on its march towards a fixed destination.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We granted not unto any man before thee life eternal, What! then if thou diest, will they live for ever? No man on earth has ever been granted to live for ever, altogether exempted from tasting death. Certain chosen ones of God are granted extraordinary long life, but even they have one day to taste death.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Every soul shall taste of death; We try you with evil and (with) good (by way of) a test (Refer to note on verses 8:185, 29:57 & 67:2.) ; and unto Us shall ye (all) be returned. In the preceding verse, reference is made to 'Bashar,' i.e., man, but here 'Nafs,' i.e., soul, is used for self. It obviously means that death or extinction of life is destined even for the non-human souls like the spirits like the angels. It is said that before the day of Final Judgment the whole universe along with the angels and the spirits will be ordered by God to go out of existence and then again everything will be brought to exist for the Final Judgment.Men are tested through afflictions and also through prosperity to prove the reactions from the individuals, as regards their…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When behold thee those who disbelieve, they take thee not but for a ridicule; (saying) "Is this he who speaketh of your gods?" and (while) they, at the mention of the Beneficent (God), are themselves disbelievers. The sceptic minds of the disbelievers used to take the warning against their infidelity and evils, as a joke and ridiculed the Holy Prophet. They did not even like the name of God to be taken even by the others.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Man is made of haste; I shall show you My signs, so ask Me not to hasten (on) A man named Harith bin Nasr, by way of taunting, used to frequently ask the Holy Prophet as to when the threatened wrath of God would come. This verse is in reply to it.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "When will this threat come to pass, if ye be truthful?" See 21:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If only know those who disbelieve, (of the time) when they shall not be able to keep off from their faces and the backs the (Hell) fire nor shall they be helped. See 21:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He (The Holy Prophet who brought the Reminder anew.) said: "My Lord (well) knoweth (every) word (spoken) in the heaven and the earth; and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." See 21:3

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! but it shall come on them suddenly, and make them confounded, so they shall neither be able to repel it, nor will they (then) be respited. See 21:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed were (also) ridiculed (some) of the apostles before thee, but surrounded those who ridiculed that (very torment) which they had been ridiculing. All those of the disbelievers who were punished in the previous generations did similarly ridicule but they were made to realise what their ridicule actually meant.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): Who can protect you by night and by day from the Beneficent (God)? Nay! they from the remembrance of their Lord turn aside. There is none who could save the disbelievers against the wrath of God. None of the gods whom they worshipped, would be of any avail to them. It is the mercy of the Lord that is delaying their punishment to give them the respite.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or have they gods who can protect them from Us; They have no power to help their own selves, and nor shall they from Us (From our punishment.) be protected. See 21:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! Provided We (enjoyment) unto these and their fathers until lasted their life; What! See they not that We come unto the land, shortening (Refer to verse 13:41.) its borders; Shall they then be the prevailing ones? In spite of the terrible resistance from the heathen world around Mecca, Islam flourished and gradually the lands in the hands of those openly opposed to Islam, were snatched away from the hands of the disbelievers and the land around was subjected to the Muslim rule. The disbelievers could not prevail over Islam which began its course amidst heartless persecution, brutal tyrannies, and unprovoked monstrous aggressions and terrible onslaughts, when the believers were only a few, unarmed and unprotected, who could be counted on fingers.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "Verily I do but warn you by the revelation (from God):" But the deaf will hear not whenever they are warned. See 21:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And yet if toucheth them a blast (Lit. Breath.) of thy Lord's punishment, certainly will they say, "Woe unto us! Verily we had been unjust!" See 21:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We shall set up the balances of justice on the Day of Judgment, so no soul shall be dealt with unjustly in the least; (Refer to verses 7:8, 57:25 & 55:7.) and even if there be the weight of a grain of mustard seed, (even that) will We bring it (into account); And sufficient are We (as) reckoners. The First Holy Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib answering a question said that: "The thoughts and the deeds have no body to be weighed in any physical balance which could weigh only things material. Nothing is hidden or unknown to God. The balance means justice, and the greatness in weight means the greatness of the number of the good deeds with the essential sincerity in them. And the weighing or the reckoning would be to prove to men themselves the actual…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We did grant unto Moses and Aaron the (Book of) Criterion (Distinguishing measure - The same was given to the Holy Prophet and Ali ibn Abi Talib, the First Holy Imam.) (between the right and wrong), and Light and a Reminder (Refer to verses 2:2, 2:177, 3:137 & 45:20.) for the pious ones. 'Furqan', i.e., the Criterion of judgment or the Means to distinguish falsehood from the truth or to sift or separate truth from falsehood, i.e., the heavenly scripture and the knowledge contained in the scriptures.The god-fearing are those who are always mindful of God and guard against evil with the correct belief in Him and the hereafter, the reckoning and the Final Requital.Whatever was proved for Moses was proved for Muhammad and whatever was proved for Aaron was proved for Ali with exception of apostleship -…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who fear their Lord unseen, and of the Hour (of doom) they are frightened. This is the continuation of the description of the qualities of the god-fearing ones, though they do not see God and yet they fear His wrath and His reckoning.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! say they: (these are) medleys of dreams (Refer to verse 12:44.) ! Nay! he hath forged it; Nay! he is a poet; let him then bring unto us a sign like unto the ones that were sent unto the former ones (of the apostles). They were struck with the miraculous effect the Holy Qur'an created and notwithstanding the natural and the irresistible impression the Word of God created on them, which they helplessly called it sorcery, or the wonders of a dream or the marvel of poetry. They demanded a miracle although the Holy Qur'an is by itself a challenging miracle.This was the actual position of the pagans who used to hear the Holy Prophet reciting Qur'an. They were undoubtedly influenced or would remain confused as to what to say - confused dreams, forgery, poetry - and when they…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And this (Qur'an) is a Reminder (Qur'an.) full of blessings which We have sent it down (Unto Our Apostle Muhammad) Do ye then deny it? See 21:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed gave We unto Abraham his rectitude (Refer to verse 6:75. The power of discerning between the right and the wrong.) before, and We did know him well. Abraham is the one who has been the most repeatedly mentioned in the Holy Qur'an and on each occasion with reference to a different aspect of his personal excellence.1Abraham was given 'Rushd', i.e., guidance, i.e., apostleship before Moses and Aaron.These verses assert that Abraham got his discerning power before he started preaching to Aazar in verse 6:75 - Abraham's preaching to Aazar is before his argument with the people about the divinity of the stars.2 This clearly proves that Abraham never accepted the divinity of the stars. It was just for the sake of argument he had said it. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Recollect thou O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) when (Abraham) said unto his father (Godfather - paternal uncle.) and his people: "What are these images unto which ye (as devotees) cleave" See verses 6:75 - 6:83. 'Aazar' was the paternal uncle of Abraham who had brought up Abraham. Hence Aazar is addressed as the father. Abraham asked Aazar and his people, about the idols which they worshipped.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "Found we our fathers, (Parents as well as ancestors.) worshippers unto them" They (the people) replied saying that they only followed their ancestors - to which Abraham though young and in the clutches of the idolaters opposed the very Sire, who was to him a father for he had brought him up and boldly condemned idolatry, declaring that the people and their fathers both had gone astray.This part of the life-history of Abraham informs some important guiding factors for mankind, i.e., how the duty to God should be the first concern of man when it is in conflict with the duty even to his parents, how boldly truth should be advocated and upheld against falsehood and be overcome and the fight against evil be carried to the last even if it needs to undergo the worst persecution and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Abraham.) he: "Indeed ye and your fathers had been in error (Clear.) manifest." See 21:53

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "Hast thou brought unto us the truth, or art thou of the jesters?" See 21:53

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: "Nay! Your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who hath created them; and I am unto this, (This Truth.) one of the witnesses." See 21:53

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And by God, I will scheme (This is what Abraham determines to do.) against your idols after ye go away, turning back Abraham determines to make the idolaters realize the fallacy of their creed by breaking the idols when they had gone from the place. The next day was the festival of the idolaters. They all went out to rejoice and Abraham with the excuse of sickness remained behind. The people had arranged all their idols adorned.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So he broke them (The idols.) into pieces, except the chief of them, that happly they may unto him return. It is said that Abraham's breaking of the idols is mentioned in the Jewish Rabbinical literature Gen. R. 38, and Tauna Debe Eliyahu 2:35 (Jewish Edition). Abraham broke all the idols save the biggest or chief one of them to convince the people of their gods being nothing but a senseless stock of stones, i.e., a helpless material.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "Who hath done this to our gods? Verily he is of the unjust ones" See 21:58

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Believed not before them (the people of) any of the towns which We did destroy: what! will these (now) believe? What happened to the miracles already shown heretofore by the previous apostles of God? Were they not sufficient? Should God and His apostles be ever ready to go on showing miracles as and when they are demanded by men stubborn, in their disbelief with a determination never to believe at all? Persistence in disbelief and wickedness in spite of the miracles had always been punished. Hence the mercy of the Lord demands belief through the use of reasoning. If miracles accompany the admonishing, surely the next step as the natural consequence would be destruction. And if the people resist even the clearest arguments, they would meet the consequence which their predecessors suffered.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Some others) said: "We heard a youth speak of them, he is called Abraham" See 21:58

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They said: "Then bring him before the eyes of the people, that they may bear witness." See 21:58

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Asked.) they: "Hast thou done this to our gods, O' Abraham?" See 21:58

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Abraham) said: "Nay! Hath done it he, the chief of them is this (idol) so ye ask them, if they can speak" When Abraham was asked if it was he who broke the idols - Abraham replied, 'Why do ye not ask the chief (of the idols) who is standing there safe. Perhaps he has done it, i.e., if your idol-gods can speak, ask them as to who broke them. When they were unable to ask their idol-gods, nothing but the confession of their own folly, was the alternative left to them.Note that Abraham did not utter any lie denying what he had done. He only wanted the people to first ask their own idols as to who had done it.It must be noted that what Abraham did with the idols, needed a godly courage, for Nimrod the powerful king…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then they turned unto them selves and said, "Verily, ye are yourselves the unjust ones," The idolaters being ashamed of the well-proved fallacy of their creed and getting convinced of the truth preached by Abraham condemned themselves. Similarly, after the great event of Karbala, Yazid and the Yazidians stood self-condemned and condemned forever also by the human world for all times.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then they were confounded (Figuratively their heads turned upside down - in shame.) in their heads, (and they helplessly said): "Thou knowest fully well that these (idols) speak not!" See 21:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said: (Abraham) "What! worship ye then besides God what profiteth you not, nor do any harm unto you?" This is what Abraham told addressing the ashamed idolaters. Compare this to Husayn's sermon at Karbala. 'O' people! I say unto you! guard ye against evil! Fear the wrath of the Lord!'.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Fie on you and on what ye worship besides God. What! Do ye not understand? See 21:66

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "Burn him (Abraham.) and help your gods, if ye can do (anything at all);" Having been totally defeated by the arguments of Abraham, and recovering from the shame against their inability to talk to the idols and ask them as to who it was that had broken them to pieces, the people shouted in their anger to one another to burn Abraham in defence of their gods who had already been destroyed by Abraham. This is what the enemies of the Holy Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt did when they could not face the truth from these holy ones. They killed the holy ones one after another and persecuted their devotees and also killed them.It is said that a huge furnace was specially constructed and an enormously huge quantity of firewood was lit and Abraham in chains and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (When Abraham was put into the fire.) We; (God.) "O' fire! Be thou cold, and a safety unto Abraham," When Abraham was being actually thrown into the fire through the sling, God willed the fire to get cooled to the degree of becoming a comfort to Abraham. And if the command from God had not been qualified by "Salaman", i.e., Comfort or Safety - the fire would have frozen Abraham to death had not been as it would have otherwise burnt him to ashes.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We sent not before thee, but men unto whom We did reveal, so ask ye the people of the (The Ahl al-Bayt with whom the Reminder (the Qur'an) was left see 'Hadith al-Thaqlayn'. See note to verse 21:7.) Reminder (Refer to note on verse 16:43.) if ye know not. 'Dhikr' - literally meaning a 'Reminder.' It is one of the names of the Holy Qur'an. 'Ahl al-Dhikr' means here the people of the Holy Qur'an, i.e., the Holy Prophet and the Holy Ahl al-Bayt whom God Himself purified1 and sent into the world for the guidance of humanity. It has repeatedly been pointed out as to who the 'Ahl al-Dhikr' are, i.e., who are the ones with whom God has endowed the fullest meaning of His Final Word, the Holy Qur'an.2 All these verses clearly say that the Holy…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they intended a device against him, but We made them the greatest losers, Thus those who desired to be cruel to Abraham, their plans were frustrated and they were the losers and the sufferers too far, a host of mosquitoes was sent down and they ate away the flesh and drank the blood and the people suffered a very painful death and a mosquito entered the nostrils of Nimrod and passed on to his brain and the heathen despot met a miserable end.1 Compare this to the miserable end the devilish despot of Damascus met after enacting the gruesome massacre of Husayn and his holy band at Karbala.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We delivered him and (also) Lot, (and took them safely) to the land which We have blessed for all worlds. See 21:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We gave him (To Abraham.) Isaac, and Jacob, as a further gift, and made We all of them righteous ones. See 21:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We made them (Imams.) leaders, guiding (the people) by Our command, and revealed We unto them the doing of good, and the establishing of prayer, and the giving of alms, and (only) unto Us did they worship, See 21:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And Lot, We gave him wisdom, the knowledge; and We delivered him from the town which were doing filthiness; for they were people evil, perverse, See 21:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We admitted him into Our mercy; verily he was of the righteous ones. See 21:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (remember) Noah, when he cried aforetime, then We responded unto him and delivered him and his companions from the great calamity. See 21:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We helped him against his people who belied Our signs; verily they were an evil people, so We drowned them all. See 21:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And David and Solomon when they were judging about the corn-field when the sheep of the people pastured in it by night, and We unto their judgment were among the witnesses, (We were witnessing.) Two men quarrelled and approached the holy Apostle David for judgment; one was Elia the cultivator and the other was Yohanna (John) the herdsman. Elia complained that John, his neighbour, had grazed his sheep in his cornfield or the vineyard in the night and the sheep had eaten away the plants causing him a great loss. David asked John, and John submitted that it happened when he was asleep, and he confessed himself to be guilty. The estimate of the loss was found to be equal to the value of the herd of John, and David ordered John to compensate the loss. Solomon, son of David…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then We made Solomon to understand it; and unto each one gave We wisdom and knowledge, and We made subservient with (Subservient to David.) David the mountains and the birds; to sing hymns of (Our praise) And We were the doers. This verse refers to the revelation which Solomon got about the better judgment he suggested in the case, for the apostles of God neither speak nor act but according to the revelation they receive from the Lord; but what David had decreed was also the revelation which was given before to David which was only superseded by the one now given to Solomon. Both the apostles had acted only upon the revelation that was given to them obviously it was a plan to prove the wisdom granted to apostles even in young age. It is said that when the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We made them not (such) bodies not eating the food, and they were not to abide (in this world) for ever. Meaning that all the other apostles of God were also men with a mortal body which is sustained only by some material food. Jesus, though born without a male parent had also a mortal body, and God who raised him in his body, to heaven is not a helpless and a resourceless being like any one of us; He is the Almighty Lord who created Jesus as the Sign or the Token of His independent Will, Authority and Omnipotence and He can sustain Jesus similarly with, in some way unknown to we mortals or even providing him with the needs of his sustenance in heaven. A body on earth is controlled by the various physical factors causing fatigue and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We taught him (David.) the art of making the coat of mail for you that ye might protect yourselves in your wars; Will ye then be grateful? As a return for the piety and the righteousness of David iron was made soft like wax, in his hand. David did not take from the public treasury, anything for his sustenance. He used to make articles like the weapons of defence by moulding iron with his hands and David was taught by God to make coats of mail for his men.1The teaching of the art of making the means of protection and not the means of destruction such as sword. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And unto Solomon (We subjected) the wind blowing violent, blowing at his command unto the land wherein We had blessed; And We are, of all things the Knowers. Solomon was endowed with an authority over the winds which carried his throne to distant lands in the shortest time. There is no reason to wonder if the forces of nature are made by God to serve His chosen servants as and when they need in their services. Those who believed in the Omnipotence of God can by no means doubt anything done by God's Will, and to those who know only of nature and do not know the absolute powers of the Omnipotent Author of nature, no amount of argument can be of any avail.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of the satans there were those who used to dive for him and to do other work besides that; and We were guardians over them, Solomon was given to rule over the devilish forces of evil and tame the supernatural beings to serve him in the cause of righteousness.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (Remember) Job (Ayyub), when he cried unto his Lord (saying); "Verily hath touched me distress, and Thou art the Most Merciful of the merciful ones!" The Holy Prophet is reminded of the apostle Ayyub, i.e., Job's life. Job used most of his time in prayer and meditation. Job's patience has passed into a proverb. Job's mother is said to be a descendant of the apostle Lot, and his father was in the line from Ishmael and he was endowed with enormous wealth. He was tested with the loss of all his wealth, his children and his health to a very miserable extent and yet Ayyub did not falter in his patience and his prayers to the Lord. Job was tempted by Satan and yet Job could not be conquered by him. Job became a pattern of humility, patient and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So We responded unto him and We removed what he was distressed with, and We gave him and his family and the like of them with them, a mercy from unto Us, and a reminder unto the worshippers (of Ours). Job was at last relieved of all the miseries that were inflicted on him which was only a test.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (remember) Ishmael and Idris and Dhul-Kifl; all were of the patient ones. For Idris - See 19:56 and for Dhu 'l-Kifl literary meaning, the possessor of Double Requital. He is also known for his patience.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:86 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We admitted them into Our Mercy; Verily they were of the righteous. See 21:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:87 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (remember) Yunus i.e. Zunnun when went he in anger, (Refer to verse 37:139 for the people not responding.) and imagined he that never would We (Put him into hardship.) straiten him; Then he cried out from the darkness: "There is no god but "Thou (O' my Lord!), Glory be to Thee, verily I was of (Belonged to.) the unjust ones!" The statement that Jonah was wrath with God is a blasphemy for it is far from any apostle of God at any time to disagree with the Will of the Lord.1When he faced hardships in three stages - the darkness of the night, the darkness of the and sea and the darkness inside the whale - then he cried - in the situations.It does not mean that he really had committed any wrong or any injustice. It means that…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:88 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then responded We unto him and delivered him from the grief, thus do We deliver the believers. See 21:87

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:89 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (remember) Zachariah, when he cried unto his Lord: "O' my Lord! Leave me not alone (without an issue) though Thou art the Best of heirs!" See verse 19:5. 'Khayr al-Warithin', i.e., The Best Inheritors, i.e., the one who would remain even after every one else is perished - The Everlasting One.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then fulfilled We unto them Our promise (of punishment), then We delivered them, and those whom We willed, and We destroyed the extravagant (Those who exceeded the limits.) ones. The reference is to the promise of the triumph of the apostles over their enemies - the destruction of all those who disbelieved in the Word of God and defied His apostles.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:90 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then responded We unto him and gifted unto him John (Yahya), and adjusted (Cured.) his wife (of her barrenness) for him; verily, they did vie in goodness and did call unto Us, with love and reverence, and were unto Us humbled The wife of Zachariah who was proved barren her whole life and had crossed the age of bearing a child, who herself thought it impossible for her at any time in the future to be a mother1 was made fit to bear John the Baptist.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:91 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (O' Our Apostle Muhammad! remember) her (Mary) who guarded her chastity We breathed into her Our Spirit, and We made her and her son a sign unto all peoples. The reference is to Virgin Mary being made to bear Jesus, without any male partner in the parentage.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:92 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, this (Islam) is your group, one group (Single one.) and I am your Lord! therefore worship ye Me (alone)! 'Ummah' stands for nation, community, religion, brotherhood and also religion, here to mean that Islam revealed through the Holy Prophet was one Universal Religion demanding faith in the Perfect Unity of God.'Ummah' has been interpreted by some commentators as 'Religion' which is only figurative with no clear evidence to support it. The proper meaning of the word, i.e., 'Group' is the appropriate meaning. This is your group - i.e., the group for the faithful to follow - The group distinguished with the unity of purpose and ideology as the group of the apostles mentioned afore.There is full justification for interpreting 'Ummah' here as 'Imams' - For a collective devotion to God it needs a guide or 'Imam'. But the unfortunate…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:93 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But they have rent asunder (this) their concern among them selves (into sects), (and yet) unto Us shall all of them return. The people later started their own divisions and got themselves divided into several sects and sub-sects. However much they might follow the different ways in thought and deeds, all of them are marching towards one and the same destination, i.e., their return to their Lord.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:94 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So whosoever shall do of good deeds and he be a believer, there shall not be any rejection (Denial.) of his endeavour, and verily, We will write it down for him. Mere righteousness without the correct faith in God, is of no value for the prerequisite for the acceptance of the good deeds of any one is the correct faith in God with which no virtue of anyone will go unrewarded. Every deed committed by man is then and there recorded.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:95 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And is forbidden (Binding.) unto (the people of) the towns which We did destroy that they shall not return. It is forbidden for the people of the town which has been destroyed by the wrath of God to return to this life again with any more chance of amending their faith and deeds. It means that the people of those places which were not destroyed by any wrath from God will have a return, and this is the doctrine of 'Raj'ah' when the Last Holy Imam Muhammad Ibn al-Hasan al-Mahdi would reappear. (MS and UB)1 give a long and detailed statement explaining what is actually meant by this verse and the question of 'Raj'ah', i.e., the return of the dead to this world before the final end of it.This does not refer to the Total Resurrection Day when one and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:96 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Until are let loose the Gog and the Magog and they shall from every elevation hasten forth. See verse 18:94. Among the prognostic signs of the approach of the Day of Judgment, will be that Dajjal, the Antichrist, the Imposter, will appear and then the barrier withholding Gog and Magog will be broken and they would be freed to roam playing havoc all-round the earth following the coming out of the Monstrous Beast called 'Dabbat al-Arḍ'. Then will appear the Last Imam Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mahdi - who will rule for a long time, when Jesus also will return to earth. The Holy Prophet said that: "If there be left even a single day for the end of the world before the day of the Final Judgment, there will appear one whose name will be my name and whose epithet…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:97 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the true promise shall draw nigh, then lo! stare amazedly, the eyes of those who disbelieve; (and they shall say): "Woe unto us! Indeed were we in heedlessness as to this; Nay! we were unjust ones." This refers to what the disbelievers would repent and say, having seen the wrath of God ready to overtake them.The signs of total resurrection given in Qur'an do not necessarily mean that after the appearance of the signs the Resurrection Day will follow immediately. The timing of the events in relation to the ultimate resurrection is beyond the human grasp. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:98 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, ye and what ye worship beside God, shall be the fuel for hell; unto ye shall arrive. (To go therein.) One day while talking to the Holy Prophet about their 360 idol-gods, the chieftains of the idolatrous Quraysh who were totally defeated, and inspite of their helplessness out of their adamance and arrogance said "O' Muhammad! We are firm in following our ancestors in their belief, (i.e., idolatry) and we shall remain steadfast to it and never change our thoughts and the ways of life." Nasr bin Harith who was one among the people began to quarrel with the Holy Prophet. Then the Holy Prophet read out this verse which was revealed to him.The infidels fired with anger were returning from the Holy Prophet when Abdullah Zub'air met them on the way and knowing the cause of their dismay…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anbiyaa:99 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Were these been gods they would not have come unto it and all shall abide therein. See 21:98

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They ask thee about 'Anfaal' (Accessions) (Spoils of war.) Say (O' Our Apostle)! "The 'Anfaal' (Accessions) are for God and the Apostle; So ye fear God and set aright (This indicates that there was some dispute about owning the accessions. The people thought that it was theirs and the result was a quarrel and a dispute - Its application is valid for ever and it is a part of Divine Sovereignty. The believers were asked to accept without any hitch.) matters between yourselves and obey God and His Apostle (The Holy Prophet.) if ye be believers." 'Al-Anfaal', a plural drawn from 'Nafl', literally meaning addition or accession as a due.This verse must have been revealed at Badr. A few people were guarding the tent of the Holy Prophet. 'Ali Ibn Abi Talib was busy in active defence fighting the enemy…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And caused it (Help with the angels.) not God but as good tidings (unto you) and that your hearts thereby be convinced; and no (Emphasises the fact that blessings in any form is God's and the other agencies - angelical or non-angelical are only the means.) help is there save from God; Verily God is Ever-Triumphant, Wise. God blessed the believers with a conviction of their victory and cast a dreadful fright in the hearts of the enemy.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Recollect ye) When He caused upon you a slumber as a security from Him and sent down water from heaven that He might purify (A physical purification by means of water but the purification in 33:33 is direct and universal - thorough. Internal and External- i.e. of Body and Soul.) you with it and take away from you the uncleanliness of Satan and that He might fortify your hearts and plant firmly with it your feet. Abu Jahl had cunningly encamped his forces on a hard soil, and the desert before the Muslims was of very soft sand in which the feet of the Muslims was getting sunk, disabling them even to walk properly against the enemy. God sent rain by which the hard soil on which the enemy was stationed was turned marshy and slippery whereas the rain water…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When thy Lord revealed unto the angels saying: "Verily, I am with you, make ye firm then those who believe. Soon will I cast dread into the hearts of those who disbelieve, therefore strike ye off their necks; and strike off then every fingertip of them." This verse clearly explains how God helped the Muslims through the Angels - by Himself casting fright in the hearts of the enemy and the Angels fighting the foe on behalf of the Muslims.The Holy Qur'an clearly indicates how helpless were the Muslims against the unprovoked huge onslaught of the invading formidable forces of the enemy. The question of the Holy Prophet taking any initiative against any unprovoked aggression does not at all arise but no amount of clarity of the matter seems to have been of any avail to the enemies of Islam…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This because they opposed (Waged war.) God and His Apostle (Muhammad), and whosoever opposeth God and His Apostle (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) then verily God is severe in punishment. The concluding words of this verse, clearly lays down the punishment for acting against God and the Holy Prophet. This law has to be remembered against the conduct of the people with the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt immediately as the Holy Prophet departed from this world. How they behaved with 'Ali Ibn Abi Talib, the first Holy Imam about whom the Holy Prophet had declared on the memorable historic day at Ghadir Khumm on his way returning from the 'Hajjat al-Wida'."Of whomsoever I am the Lord, this 'Ali is his Lord''"O' Lord be friend to him who is a friend to him ('Ali). Be an enemy to him who is an enemy…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This, (The cause of the punishment.) then ye taste it, and (Beware!) that for the infidels is the torment of the (Hell) fire. See 8:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! When ye meet those who disbelieve (to attack) in battle, turn ye not to them your backs. When the battle at Badr was being fought, some people sat quiet in the shade, merely witnessing and watching the trend of the events to join the triumphant party. And consider the position of those who turned their backs against the enemies at Uhud and ran away deserting the Holy Prophet in the midst of the overwhelming forces of the enemy, and disappeared for days together - Read authorities like, Tabari, Tarikh al-Khamis, Tafsir al-Kabir, Minhaj al-Nubuwwat, Early History of Islam by S. Husayn, which say, that the companions like Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Abu Ubayda were also among those who took to flight at Uhud and Hunayn.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whoever turneth his back to them on that day except if he turneth aside (in a stratagem) for the fighting or in joining (another) contingent then he deserveth himself the wrath from God, and his abode is Hell; and what an evil destination shall it be. See note on Verse 8:15 and decide about those who had deserted the Holy Prophet at Uhud and the other battle-fields (Hunayn).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So ye slew them not but God slew them, and thou (The Holy Prophet.) threw not when you threw it (the dust) but God threw it, that He might test (By the order to fight.) the believers by a gracious trial from Him; Verily God is All Hearing, All-Knowing. This verse clearly indicates that in the battles which the Holy Prophet fought for Islam, the hand of God was actually at work.The word 'Yubla' means gifting or conferring. Here it means that God willed to gift the Muslims with a good gift, i.e., the unexpectable victory over the enemy. It is said at Badr only nine from the ranks of the Muslims were martyred whereas the enemy lost seventy of their renowned warriors, and 'Ali alone dealt with thirty-seven of the infidels and slew them. It was in Badr that…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This (This is one cause and the other is that God weakens the crafty plans of the infidels.) (is the cause) and that God weakeneth the crafty plans of the infidels. See 8:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Know ye O' Infidels!) If ye demanded a victory then indeed hath come unto you (But not for you.) the victory, and if ye desist (from attacking the faithful) it will be better for you; and if ye return (to attack), We also shall return (to assist the believers), and never shall your forces avail you of anything, though they may be many, and (know ye) that God is with the believers. It is reported when the infidels left Mecca to attack the Muslims in Madina, it was Abu Jehl who held the 'Curtain of the 'Ka'ba' and prayed for 'the best of the sides to be assisted and the side which might be on the wrong to be destroyed,' and God had justly disposed of the matter as it was prayed to be by the infidels themselves.The Christian writers,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily believers are only those who when God is mentioned their hearts get thrilled (Refer to verse 39:23. All these qualities are found to the maximum limits possible besides the Holy Prophet in his Ahl Al-Bayt.) , and when unto them are recited His signs they increase them in faith, and on God (alone) do they rely, See 8:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' Ye who believe! Obey God and His Apostle (Muhammad!), and turn ye not away from him while ye hear (him) (This discredits the tradition which gives license to the participants of the battle of Badr among the Muslims to do whatever they like for God has already forgiven their sins. (A.P.).) . See 8:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And be not like those who said: "We heard" while they listen not. See 8:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the vilest of animals (The infidels. Lit. anything that walks, creeps, or crawls on earth.) in God's view are the deaf and the dumb who understand not. See 8:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if God had found in them any good, indeed He would have made them listen, and (even) if He makes them listen (With the absence of goodness in them.) , they would turn back while they swerve aside. See 8:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! Respond ye to God and to His Apostle (Muhammad) when He calleth you to that which giveth you life; and know ye that God getteth (always there) in between man and his heart (Intentions.) , and that it is unto Him ye shall (all) be (ultimately) gathered. By this verse the response to the call of the Holy Prophet is the same as the response to the call from God, thus the immediate response to the call of the Holy Prophet becomes compulsory. It is said that by the call of the Holy Prophet, is meant the Imamat, i.e., the Divine Guidance through the Twelve divinely commissioned Holy Imams. It also means that whenever the Holy Prophet calls the believers to Jihad to defend the faith, it is compulsory upon every believer to respond to it…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And guard ye (yourselves) against an affliction (A troublesome trial.) which may smite not (only) those who committed injustice among you in particular (but all of you); and know ye that God is severe in the requital (of evil); It is related from the Second Holy Imam Hasan Ibn 'Ali that he said that this verse was revealed as a prophecy about the Battle of Jamal, which was fought by Talha, Zubayr and Ammar, under A'isha, one of the wives of the Holy Prophet. This battle was fought at Basra. Tafsir al-Kashaf says that once Zubayr was going along with the Holy Prophet and 'Ali was coming in front of them. Zubayr pointing to 'Ali, asked the Holy Prophet as to how much the Holy Prophet loved 'Ali? To which the Holy Prophet replied, 'I love him more than as…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And remember ye, when ye were few and deemed weak in the earth, fearing that people may carry you away by force but He strengthened (This is a heartening warning to the believers not to be afraid of being a minority and thus to join the wrong-doers.) you with His aid and provided you of the good things (of sustenance) that ye may give thanks. See 8:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! Be ye not unfaithful to God and the Apostle (Muhammad), nor be ye unfaithful to (the) trusts (The Book of God (Qur'an) and the Ahl Al-Bayt, with which the Muslims were trusted.) with you while ye know, Unfaithfulness or treachery here relates to disclosing the secrets of God, of the Holy Prophet and also of the people themselves. It is reported by Jabir Ibn Abdullah al-Ansari that the Messenger Angel Gabriel appeared before the Holy Prophet and informed him that Abu Sufyan, the arch enemy of Islam, had secretly camped, and counselled to prepare to forestall the enemy and keep this a secret. When the Holy Prophet informed his closest lieutenants to prepare for the task ahead, one of the hypocrites got this secret and wrote a secret letter to Abu Sufyan and informed him of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And know ye! that your wealth and your children, are a temptation (Ar. 'Fitna' Refer to note on verse 64:14 & 64:15.) , and that, God, with Him is a mighty reward. See 8:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! If ye fear God He will grant you a distinctive (standard) (To enable distinguishing the right from the wrong.) and remove from you (all) your evils, (sins) and forgive you; and God is the Lord of Mighty grace. This verse speaks of the quite reasonable and practical way Islam wants mankind to be kept warned against sinning, as well as encouraging piety and with the promise of the pardon for the evils already committed, if duly repented with amendment.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who establish prayer and of what God hath provided them with, they spend (Benevolently in the way of their Lord.) See 8:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when planned they against thee, those who disbelieved, that they might imprison thee, or slay thee or drive thee away; and they devise plans and God (too) hath a plan; and God is the Best of the planners. When some people from Yathrib (later known as Madina) came to Mecca and invited the Holy Prophet to their place and promised faithfulness to him, the heathens of Mecca got alerted and apprehended that the Holy Prophet would soon be out of their hold. An urgent meeting of the elders of the tribes was hurriedly summoned at the Dar al-Nadwah, where the Meccans used to meet whenever they needed to take any important decisions about their civic as well as the other matters or to celebrate any great social events.The elders of all the tribes were gathered together, and Satan appeared…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (remember) when are recited unto them Our signs, say they: "Indeed we have heard" if we please we could say the like of this (Qur'an), It is nothing but the tales of the ancients. It is a reference to the empty boastings of the infidels. There is already the challenge of the Holy Qur'an to produce at least a chapter of its kind. Yet the world till now could not respond to this everlasting and ever-current challenge.The people sometimes used to say that they, if they only like it, can bring the like of this, (Qur'an) and they resorted to all means against the movement, but utterly failed. Their failure and their frustration is obvious from the next Verse 8:32. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (remember) when said they: (The infidels.) "O' God! If this (Qur'an) be the truth from Thee, then rain Thou upon us stones from heaven or inflict on us a painful chastisement." Nu'man Ibn al-Harith had been to Iran for the purpose of trade. He purchased the stories of Rustom and Sohrab and translating them into Arabic, said, that like the Qur'an he had also fabricated some stories of the eminent people. Uthman Ibn Math said, "O' Nu'man! fear God for Muhammad is the true Apostle of God and what he says is truth. He says, There is no God but (the One True) God. Nu'man replied, saying, 'I also say, There is no God but One God but I only add that these (angels) are the daughters of God.' Nu'man was brought before the Holy Prophet who rebuked him…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God is not to chastise them while thou (The Holy Prophet.) art among them (Refers to the people mentioned in the previous two verses: 8:31& 8:32 which shows that the people referred to were only professing Islam.) , nor is God to chastise them while yet they seek forgiveness. Allamah Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani al-Makki, a revered Sunni scholar in his well-known book 'Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa' says that this verse is also about the superiority and excellence of the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt. There are many traditions of the Holy Prophet saying, "as I am the source of peace and protection for mankind on earth, my Ahl Al-Bayt are also the same for them. (M.F.A.).This verse gives the reason for the postponement of the punishment as the Holy Prophet Muhammad is the 'Rahmatun li 'l-Alameen', the Mercy unto the worlds.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what plea have they that God should not chastise them while they obstruct (men) from the Sacred Mosque, and they are not (also) its guardians; Its guardians are not but only those who guard themselves (against evil) (The pious) but most of them know not. Guardians of the Mosque can be interpreted as the guardians of the faith, Islam, and according to this verse the guardians of Islam, i.e., the Imams, could be only those who were themselves the strictest observers of it and in this regard, none could even be equalised to the Twelve Holy Imams after the Holy Prophet. This unique superiority and the excellence of the Holy ones is universally acknowledged by all schools of thought among the Muslims.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And their prayer near the (Sacred) House (of God) is nothing but whistling and clasping of hands; Taste ye then the chastisement for what ye were disbelieving. There can never be any Islamic prayer acceptable to God and the Holy Prophet, with music.The innovation of the institution of 'Sama' which is conducted with music by some who call themselves Sufis (the mystics) could reasonably be termed as the legacy or the copy of some non-Muslim creeds.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily those who disbelieve spend of their wealth to obstruct (men) from the way of God, so will they spend it, then (in the end) it shall be against them (a matter of) regret; and those who disbelieve, unto the Hell shall they be driven. See 8:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That God might distinguish the impure (Refer to verse 3:178. Shows that the distinction referred to in this Verse is the object of the apostolic mission of every prophet - its application extending even to the disbelievers. (A.P.).) from the pure, and put the impure, some of it upon the other, and pile it up together, then cast it into the Hell; These are they the losers. See 8:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) to those who disbelieve: If they desist (from their disbelief and the enmity of the Apostle), will be forgiven for them (their sins) what hath past, (This is explained by the Holy Prophet who said: "Islam cuts off man from his past" (A.P.).) and if they return (to their disbelief) then indeed shall pass against them what hath already passed (against) the ancients. Note the mercifulness of Islam and the Holy Prophet that in spite of what has been done to torture the Holy Prophet and the faithful ones, the only condition for forgiveness, is the return from evil and embracing the truth, i.e., amending of one's conduct and character and disciplining the human self with the faith in God. And the desisting mentioned in this verse refers to the infidels desisting from opposing Islam…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And fight ye with them until (So that.) there be no mischief (Mischief - Object of the fight to stop mischief and to defend against unprovoked aggression.) and the religion be wholly for God; but if they desist, then Verily seest God what (all) they do. See 8:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These, (and) they (only) are the believers in truth; for them are (exalted) grades with their Lord, and forgiveness and a graceful sustenance. See 8:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they turn back, then know ye! that God is your Lord; (Protector – Master.) The Most Excellent Lord and the Most Excellent Helper. And if in spite of the amnesty and forgiveness offered, the heathens return to enmity and fight, then God promises the believers His protection and help. It is a prophecy that the infidels would never thereafter be able to succeed against Islam or the Holy Prophet.This proves 'Jihad'1 is valid on all parts of the earth until God fills the world with justice, peace, and no trouble or injustice is practised anywhere in the world, i.e., the day of the re-appearance of the Last Imam of the Ahl Al-Bayt - Muhammad al-Mahdi. For details See 'Fiqh.' (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And know ye (O' believers) that whatever of a thing ye acquire a fifth of it is for God, and for the Apostle and for the (Apostle's) near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, if ye believe in God and that which We sent down unto Our servant (Muhammad), on the Day of distinction, on the day when met the two parties; And verily God hath power over all things. 'Ghanimat' actually means 'Profit obtained' which includes the property surrendered by the enemies of Islam, in any battle (i.e., booty). But 'Ghanimat' mentioned here comprises of the profit obtained for instance through any of the following sources:Booty obtained in a war with the enemies of God, His Holy Prophet, i.e., the enemies of the religion Islam.Things like gold and silver obtained from mines.That which obtained from…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Remember) When ye were on the near side (of the valley) and they were on the farthest side (of it), while the caravan (of the enemy) was in a lower ground than you; and had you mutually made an appointment (To assume the described position.) certainly had you broken away (failed) in the fulfilment, but (ye were made to meet) in order that God might enact a matter which was destined to be done, that he who perisheth may perish after a clear proof and he who liveth may live after a clear proof; and Verily God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. This verse speaks of the various positions and the conflicting forces of the believers, and the disbelievers had been stationed at on the day of Badr when the Muslims were on a soft, sandy soil and the enemy was on…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Remember) When God showed them to thee in thy dream as few; and had He shown them to thee as many (then) certainly would ye have become disheartened and certainly ye would have disputed in the matter, but God did save you; verily He is the All-Knower of what is in your breasts. (Hearts.) See 8:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (remember) when He showed them to you when ye met, as few in your eyes and He reduced you to appear as few in their eyes in order God may enact the matter which had been destined to be done; and unto God (alone) will return all matters. If the believers had been shown to the infidels in the hugeness in the beginning itself as they were done later on, the heathens would have fled and the victory which was decreed by God would not have been achieved as it was made quite obvious to the infidels that God was with the believers and thus they with their overwhelming numbers and preparedness could not defeat the handful of the ill-equipped ones of the Muslims and on the other hand were hopelessly routed.1As already pointed out the holy souls of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! when ye meet a party (the contingent of the infidels) then be firm, and remember God much (This indicates that (jehad) is one of the devotional rites which needs the ('Neeyat al-Qurbat'). Refer to note to verses 8:45 3:12, 8:66.) , that ye be successful. See 8:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And obey ye God and His Apostle (Muhammad) and quarrel (Outcome of the disobedience to God and the Holy Prophet.) ye not, for then ye will be weakened in heart, and will depart your power and be patient; Verily God is with the patient ones. See 8:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (The Holy Prophet said: I am not afraid of my followers becoming open polytheists (Shirk al-jali), but I am afraid of their becoming victims of the Shirk al-Khafi i.e. the hidden polytheism of 'Ria' - i.e. doing good for show and not for God. Another tradition says, 'Shirk' in my followers is more concealed than the movement of the black ant on a black rock in a dark night.) be ye not like those who got out from their homes boastfully to be seen of men and (yet) who obstruct others from the way of God; and verily God encompasseth what they do. On the day of Badr, Satan appeared in the garb of Suraqah Ibn Harith and shook hands with Harith Ibn Hisham and had instigated and encouraged the infidels towards the battle and when Satan saw the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (remember) when made Satan seem alluring to them their (sinful) deeds and said (unto them) "None among men shall triumph over you today, while I am a protector for you," but when the two parties came in sight of each other, he turned upon his heels and said: "Verily I disassociate (myself) from you; Verily, I see what ye see not; and Verily God is severe in punishment." Some Meccans had embraced Islam in Mecca but for want of proper conviction in their faith, they had not migrated to Madina, and when the Meccans marched for the Battle of Badr, they accompanied the heathens saying that they would join the party which might seem to them as larger. The Muslims numbered only 313. Hence, they stayed away with the infidels. This verse refers to the people's conduct.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When say the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease: "Their religion hath beguiled these (Muslims)" And whoever relieth upon God, then God is All-Mighty, All-Wise. See 8:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Even as thy Lord caused thee out of thy house with the truth, though a party of the believers were certainly averse, The reference is to the Battle of Badr - when the Muslims numbering only 313 had to defend themselves against the onslaught of the huge army of thousands fully armed and equipped men of the heathens of Mecca headed by Abu Sufyan, the Arch-enemy of the Holy Prophet and Islam, the father of Mu'awiyah and the grandfather of Yazid. When the Holy Prophet asked the opinion of some of his companions, Umar and Abu Bakr objected to going out of Madina to meet the enemy outside the city, but Sa'd Ibn Ma'az and Miqdad said, 'We would do as we are commanded by the Apostle of God!'On one side Abu Sufyan was proceeding at the head of a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And hadst thou seen when the angels take away the souls (Refers to the heavenly help given to the Muslims) of those who disbelieve, smiting their faces and their backs, (and saying)-. "Taste ye the torment of burning (Hell-fire)." See 8:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This is for what sent forth your own hands, and that God is not unjust unto the servants. See 8:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Because they acted) like the people of Pharaoh and those before them; disbelieved they in the signs of God, so did God seize them for their sins; Verily God is Strong, severe in punishment. The comparison (of the disbelievers of Mecca to those of the people of Pharaoh is an indication to the likeness of the Holy Prophet to Moses. It is also a prophecy of the total destruction of the infidels as was done to the people of Pharaoh.'Aal', i.e., the nearest relation is a wide term which includes any person who is connected with the person in some way or other.
