Hence 'Aali-Fir'awn' means anyone who followed Fir'awn, but in the case of 'Aali-Ibrahim' mentioned in 3:32, the term is restricted to one descendant issued from the other. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This because God changeth not any favour (which) He bestoweth upon a people until they (themselves) change their own selves (This indicates that people's choice and deeds are responsible for their misfortunes) , and that God is All- Seeing, All-Hearing. See 8:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Because they acted) like the people of Pharaoh and those before them; they belied the signs of their Lord, so did We destroy them for their sins, and We did drown the people of Pharaoh; and all (of them) were unjust (tyrants). See 8:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the vilest of animals (Disbelievers compared to vilest animals, and in 25:44 said to be worse than the animals. Refer to verses 25:44, 47:12 .) in God's view are those who disbelieve, for they would not believe. See Verses 25:44, 8:55, 47:12.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those (O' Our Apostle!) with whom thou didst make a covenant (Indicates what a severe crime is the violation of the covenant made with God - Compare with the Covenant made with the Muslims at 'Ghadir Khumm'.) then they break their covenant every time, and they guard not themselves (against evil). The Jewish tribe Bani Quraiza had entered into a treaty with the Muslims that they would not assist the infidels, but in Badr they helped the heathens with arms. When brought to account for their treacherous conduct, they said that they had forgotten but they again allied themselves with the heathens at Khandaq. The reference here is to their conduct.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So, when thou taketh them in fighting, scatter (by punishing) them (making them an example) for those who come after them, that they may remember (Be mindful – warned. To stop the enemy front any further treachery or mischief and bloodshed - with an exemplary punishment.) . See 8:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if thou fearest treachery from a people, then throw (Justly i.e. to inform them of the giving up of the Covenant so that they may not accuse him of treachery. (A.P.).) back unto them (their covenant) on equal terms; Verily God loveth not the treacherous ones. Even repudiation to unfaithfulness on the part of the enemy has to be only in equal measure.Note, it is only a defensive measure and not offensive. Islam under the Holy Prophet has never inflicted on any one any unprovoked aggression at any time.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And let not those who disbelieve think that they have excelled (Or they are ahead of.) (the Muslims): verily they shall not weaken (God). See 8:58

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They dispute (This suggests the existence of a party which was not wholeheartedly submissive to the divine orders. Indicates the hopelessness with which the Muslims had to defend against the huge onslaught of the formidably strong enemy.) with thee about the truth after it had been made manifest, as if they were (helplessly) being driven unto death while they see it. See 8:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And prepare ye against them whatever (force) ye can (To your utmost ability in any form or manner - economically, physically, spiritually.) and steeds of war at the garrison to frighten the enemy of God thereby and your enemy and others besides them, whom ye know not, (but) God knoweth them; and whatever things ye spend (This indicates that any effort or wealth subscribed for the defence forces with pure intention is counted as 'Ibadat' i.e. serving God or worshipping Him. (A.P.).) in God's way, will be repaid unto you, and ye shall not be dealt with unjustly (Refer to verses 2:190, 2:217.) . 'Quwwat' in this verse implies everything which could be the source of strength at the time of need including all implements of war to meet both the defensive as well as the offensive exigencies as it…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they lean to peace, then leaneth thou too to it, and trust in God; Verily He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing (Refer to verse 4:90.) . If the enemy be inclined to peace, to grant them peace depending upon (God's help). This verse clears the position of Islam and the Holy Prophet to show whether they were defensive or offensive in their attitude towards the non-Muslims.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Anfaal:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they intend to deceive thee, then verily God sufficeth for thee (Refer to verse 33:25.) ; He it is Who strengthened thee with His help and with the believers (Those who never deserted him - like 'Ali Ibn Abi Talib.) . Mullah Jalahuddin Suyuti in his renowned commentary on the Holy Qur'an 'al-Durr al-Manthur' relates that Ibn Asakir reported that the Holy Prophet said that the following words were written on the Arsh or the Central Seat of the Divinity of God: "God, I am alone, there is no partner with Me, Muhammad My servant and Apostle, I helped him with 'Ali." item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thou didst not recite any book before it (the Qur'an) and thou didst not transcribe one with that right hand of thine, for then would have doubted those who utter falsehood. Before the revelation of the Holy Qur'an the Holy Prophet could neither write with his own hand nor could he read anything written by the others and this is a fact vouched by one and all of the age of the Holy Prophet. With this fact in view it would be sheer absurdity to say that what he delivered as the Holy Qur'an was not the revelation from God but a reproduction of what he read in the other scriptures and what he wrote, i.e., composed of and memorized. The Holy Qur'an contained all the good together only parts of which were contained in the various other scriptures.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! it (Qur'an) is the clear signs in the breast of those who have been granted the knowledge; (Said the Holy Prophet 'I am the City of Knowledge and Ali is its Gate.') and dispute not against Our signs except the unjust (ones) The Holy Ahl al-Bayt who were the heavenly depositories of the knowledge of the Word of God which was revealed through the Holy Qur'an as well as through the previous scriptures. The famous announcement of the Holy Prophet 'I am the City of Knowledge and Ali is its Gate' proves the above statement.1 Besides, there is the unique distinction gifted to the Holy Qur'an, i.e., no previously revealed scripture was ever made to be preserved in the memory of the people. It is one of the unique and wonderful distinguishing factors that the Holy Qur'an has been…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whoever hopeth to meet God and then verily the doom decreed by God shall certainly come (to pass); and He is the All Hearing, the All-Knowing. The meeting of God does not mean seeing Him. It means whosoever is sure of being resurrected for the Final Judgment of the Lord, which decree of the Lord is certain to come to pass.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "Why have not been sent down upon him the signs from the Lord?" Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "The signs are with God (alone); And I am only a plain warner" Signs i.e., miracles the people demanded, but what about the signs previously shown to them, and yet they believed not, and now the Holy Prophet was sent not to repeat the signs or the wonders of any physical world but to present the Word of God itself as said in verse 29:48 above which by itself is a great sign, and to warn that God is not there to go on working out wonders just to satisfy the playful demand of the people who in spite of the miracles already shown continued to disbelieve in the truth. Hence it is said miracles are wrought only…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Is it not enough for them that We have sent down unto thee the Book which is recited unto them? Verily in this there is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe. This verse answers the demand for miracles in the previous one.Now it is God who has granted a merciful respite to allow time for the people to repent and amend their faith and their practical life.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you; He knoweth what is in the heavens and the earth; and those who believe in the falsehood and disbelieve in God; these it is who are the losers." See 29:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they challenge (Seek – ask.) thee to hasten on the chastisement; and had not the term been decreed, the chastisement would certainly have come unto them; and certainly, it will come unto them suddenly while they perceive not. God's Plan is worked by God Himself. It could neither be hastened by anyone nor could it be deferred at anybody's fancy. It will come to pass exactly when God wills it without any previous notice1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they challenge (Lit. seek – ask.) thee to hasten on the chastisement, and verily the Hell will encompass the disbelievers, The respite for repentance is granted and when at the end of it the doom comes to pass, it will surely overtake the disbelievers from all around them.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the day when shall cover them the chastisement, from above them, and from beneath their feet; and shall say He; "Taste ye what ye were doing." See 29:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' My servants who believe! verily My earth is (If persecuted at one place for their faith the Muslim may take shelter in some other part of the earth - and be worshipful to God.) vast, therefore Me alone should ye worship! A group of the believers who stayed at Mecca passed their life in a miserable state of persecution. This verse was revealed to say that if they were persecuted at Mecca they might migrate away from it to a place like Medina where they would be safe and free. One cannot have the false excuse of one's inability to be true to his faith in God, owing to his unfavourable environment. One must share danger and evil and seek safety and good. If necessary, one should change the place. Duty to God should have every importance and priority…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Every soul shall taste of death; Then unto Us (only) ye shall (all) be returned. See 29:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who believe and do good, certainly will We lodge them in the exalted places in the gardens beneath which flow rivers, they shall abide therein; How excellent is the recompense of those who act (aright), See 29:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who are steadfast and, on their Lord, do they rely, See 29:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whoever striveth hard, he striveth only for his own self; verily (As otherwise.) God is Self- Sufficient (Independent of the needs) of (all) the worlds. Jihad does not mean only fight with sword against any enemy. It actually means striving. 'Jihad' against one's own self is the greatest 'Jihad', while 'Jihad' with sword against any enemy is only the lesser crusade. Here it means he who fights against the desires of his own self.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And how many a moving creature that doth not carry (along with it or does not own.) its sustenance; God sustaineth it and yourselves; And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Among the moving beings there are few or none which carry its sustenance. God provides all the sustenance, so it is sheer lack of faith that man started to control the reproduction on the basis of family planning for economical consideration.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if thou ask them: "Who created the heavens and the earth and made subservient the sun and the moon?" Certainly will they say: "God!" Whence are they then turned away? In order to remove man's economical apprehensions, Qur'an draws man's attention to the fact that the creation of the heavens, the earth and the other terrestrial and heavenly bodies including man himself and their destruction and death, all are beyond the human will and choice. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God (it is Who) maketh abundant the sustenance for whomsoever He willeth of His servants, and (similarly) He causeth it to be straitened for him (whomsoever He willeth); Verily God is Well-Cognizant of all things. See 29:61

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if thou ask them, "Who sendeth down from heaven the water, and giveth life with it unto the earth after its death?" Certainly, will they say: "God!" Say, "all praise is His;" Nay! most of them understand not. See 29:61

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And nothing is this life of the world but a vain sport and play; and verily the abode of the hereafter, is certainly the life: if they but know. This reduces the importance and the value of this worldly life and its comforts and miseries. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when embark they on ships, call they upon God sincerely vowing worship (only) unto Him, and when He bringeth them safe to land, behold! they associate (others with Him), See 29:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Then) let them thank not for what We have given them, and let them enjoy; (as they chose.) but soon shall they know. See 29:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! See they not that We have established a Sacred Precinct Secure, while people are ravaged all around them? Will they yet believe in the falsehood and in the bounty of God disbelieve? See 29:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And who is more unjust than he who forgeth a lie against God, or belieth the truth when it hath come unto him? Is not in the Hell the abode for the disbelievers? See 29:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who strive hard in (About – or to serve or to know.) Us, certainly will We guide them in Our ways; And verily God is (always) with those who do good. God is always with those who do good to others.This is the most promising assurance for those who sincerely strive in the Way of the Lord. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (as to) those who believe and do good, certainly will We blot out from them their evil deeds and certainly will We recompense them the best of what they were doing. Here is the greatest incentive and encouragement for the sinners to amend themselves and become righteous. Compare this offer of the infinite mercy of the All-Merciful Lord to the belief in the vicarious atonement by merely believing in a prophet or a saint by which one, getting sure of being saved by his hero even though he commits the gravest acts of sin and crimes, might remain a habitual sinner. The Christian doctrine of the vicarious atonement through the blood of Jesus means God the Lord of the Universe losing His Authority over the sinners.According to the Christian doctrine of atonement, Jesus has purchased the authority by paying…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We have enjoined on man goodness unto his parents; and if they (either of them) strive (to force) thee to (In authority.) associate (others) with Me (in worship) of which thou hast no knowledge, (This includes any order by parents which is against the Command of God.) then thou obey them not; Unto Me is the return of ye (all) and then will I inform you of what ye were doing. While Islam makes obedience to parents incumbent upon the children, it also says that in case the parents demand obedience against the truth (i.e., against God), the children need not obey their parents. But in everything else which is not forbidden by God, children must obey them. Both the parents and children must know and remember that they have to return to their Lord. The Holy Prophet said…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ankaboot:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who believe and do good, certainly We will admit them among the righteous, See 29:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Alif, Laam, Meem, Saad. Alif, Lam, Meem, Saad - (A, I., M, S).The first three letters are the same which appeared in the beginning of the Second Chapter.The fourth letter, Saad, is supposed by the commentators to stand for 'Sadiq'- the truthful. According to (M.F.A.)- 'An Allah ul-Muqtadir us-Sadiq', i.e., I am God the Omnipotent True One.The truth about the symbolic letters with which certain chapters of the Holy Qur'an start, which are divinely sealed secrets confided only with the Holy Prophet and his Divinely commissioned Deputies the Holy Imams. All the various explanations given by the various commentators are only conjectures1. However, when God Himself destined it to be a secret, there is no use or there can be no point in any one unnecessarily endeavouring to manifest His genius in perplexing the public mind with any conjectures.Once when…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, We have made you inhabit in the earth, and have made We, the means of livelihood for you in it; little it is that ye give thanks. Ma-ayish means the means for the fulfilment of life. In addition to all the material things necessary to sustain life, it also refers to all those powers and faculties which help man to rise to a higher plane to prepare for his spiritual destiny, on account of which the angels were asked to prostrate themselves before Adam. Iblis refused to be of those who bowed down, because he arrogantly despised the angels who bowed down as well as man to whom they bowed down. Arrogance, envy and rebellion were his crimes.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:100 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is it not (a lesson) guiding (enough) for those who inherit the earth after its former people that if We please We would afflict (too) for their sins, and set a seal on their hearts that they would not hearken? Setting of seal, is the natural consequence of the sinners being adamant and rejecting the guidance from God and being persistent in their misdeeds in spite of the guidance afforded and the repeated or the continuous warnings issued to them. The matter is further clarified by the subsequent verses.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:101 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These towns - We relate unto thee (some) of their events (Stories.) , and (that) indeed did come unto them their apostles with clear evidences (miracles), but they would believe not in what they belied (Reference to the similarity of the attitude in the other people.) from before; Thus doth setteth God a seal on the hearts of the infidels. See 7:100

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:102 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We found not in most of them any (faithfulness to the) covenant, and only found We most of them to be transgressors. See 7:100

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:103 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then raised (Sent.) We, after them Moses with Our signs unto Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they were aggressive with it, see (Consider.) then what was the end of the mischief-makers. The instances and the examples of Moses' mission and the conduct of the Israelites are very often given in the Holy Qur'an; it is mainly because of the fact that the Holy Prophet had more in common with Moses than with any other apostle of God and it was destined to be so.1 The events about Moses and his experiences with the Israelites are given in these following Verses.2Fir'awn or Pharaoh's name was Walid, son of Mus'ab son of Riyan. Like the title of Czar was given to every king of Russia, the title of 'Sultan' for the kings of Turkey, 'Shah' for the kings of Persia, 'Amir' for…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:104 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said Moses: "O' Pharaoh! Verily I am an apostle from the Lord of the worlds," See 7:103

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:105 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It is) incumbent upon (me) that I say not anything about God save the truth; indeed I have brought unto you with clear signs (miracles) from your Lord, so send Thou (Pharaoh.) with me the children of Israel. See 7:103

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:106 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He said: "If thou hast come with a sign, then bring it, if thou art of the truthful ones." See 7:103

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:107 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So he (Moses) threw (down) his rod, and lo! It was a serpent clearly seen. See 7:103

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:108 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then drew he (Moses) forth his hand (out of his bosom) and lo! it was white (shining bright) to (all) beholders. Moses had been gifted by God with two miraculous signs, one the staff which used to become a serpent and the other his hand shining white when it was put into his bosom and brought out. When Moses threw his staff before Pharaoh, he showed to him his hand shining bright.The Old Testament also says that Moses was given the two great signs vide:1. And Moses answered and said, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice: for they will say. The Lord hath not appeared unto thee.2. "And the Lord said unto him, what is that in thine hand? and he said, A rod.3. "And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:109 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said the chiefs of the people of Pharaoh: "Verily this indeed is an enchanter (most) learned." See 7:108

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We did create (Start creating and fashioning - not a simultaneous action - but under a gradual process mentioned (A.P.).) you, then We did fashion you, then said We unto the angels; "Prostrate yourselves unto Adam;" so they all did prostrate themselves except Iblees; he was not of the prostrating ones (Refer to Verses 2:30; 2:34; 15:28; 38:73; 18:50; 40:67.) . As said above under Verse 10, the spiritual destiny of man put him above the angels and jinn, so the refusal of Shaytan (Iblis) to accept man's superiority was unreasonable. It was egotism which prompted him to impertinent rebellion.Allah created man with His own hands from clay and gave him His own spirit (ruh)). The essential quality of clay is softness which makes it adaptable to any form or shape-obedience and submission, and total submission to Allah's…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:110 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He intendeth to turn you (Pharaoh addressing his chiefs.) out of your land; What is it then ye counsel? See 7:108

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:111 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: (The chiefs.) "Put him off and his brother, and send thou into the cities, collectors," See 7:108

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:112 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That they may (collect and) bring unto thee every enchanter (who is most) learned. See 7:108

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:113 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And came the enchanters unto Pharaoh and said they: "Verily for us must be a reward if we be the triumphants." It is reported that about twelve thousand magicians had assembled. There were four master magicians among them, named: Sadoor, Khadoor, Khatat and Musafi and there was a master of these four named Sham'oon. Soon after their arrival in Egypt the magicians had come to know that the staff of Moses remained a serpent and guarded Moses while he was asleep.The magicians got despaired; for a magical effect did not remain to act when the magician was asleep. It is said that this contest of the magic and the miracle took place in Alexandria and there was a very huge crowd of the public including the armies of Pharaoh and Pharaoh seated on a throne was witnessing the contests. (M.F.A.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:114 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: (Pharaoh.) "Yea! (even more) and Verily ye shall certainly be of those nearest (to me)." See 7:113

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:115 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They (Pharaoh's enchanters.) (the enchanters) said: "O' Moses! Wilt thou cast (thy rod first) or shall We be the (first) casters." See 7:113

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:116 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: (Moses) "Cast ye (first)! So when they did cast they bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them, and produced they a great enchantment." See 7:113

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:117 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And revealed We unto Moses saying: "Cast thou thy rod!" then (When Moses did cast the Rod.) lo! it swallowed (one after another all), that they falsely demonstrated. See 7:113

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:118 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So was established the truth and was made vain what (all) they were doing See 7:113

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:119 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So (Pharaoh and his enchanters) were defeated on the spot, and returned humbled (Abased.) down. See 7:113

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said He (God.) : "What preventeth thee that thou didst not prostrate when I did command thee?" said he (Iblees.) "I am better than him, me hast thou created of fire while thou didst create him (Adam.) (Adam) of clay (Refer to Verses: 28:76; 40:67; 55:15.) ." See 7:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:120 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the enchanters threw (themselves) down prostrating (in adoration) See 7:113

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:121 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "We believe in the Lord of the worlds," See 7:113

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:122 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Lord of Moses and Aaron. See 7:113

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:123 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said Pharaoh (Addressing the enchanters.) : "What? Believe ye in Him ere - I give permission unto you? Verily, this is a plot ye have plotted in the city, that ye may turn out of it its people, but soon ye shall know (the consequences)." See 7:113

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:124 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Surely will I cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, then will I crucify you all together. See 7:113

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:125 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "Verily unto Our Lord we return." The reply given by the believers to Pharaoh was the same which the faithful companions of the Holy Imam Husayn gave at Karbala saying that they preferred death and destruction rather than desert Husayn in the hour of the trial.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:126 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thou dost not wreak vengeance on us except because believed we in the signs of our Lord when they came unto us: O' Our Lord! pour (Grant us.) out upon us patience and cause us to die submitting (unto Thee, i.e., as Muslims). See 7:125

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:127 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said the chiefs of the people of Pharaoh: What! leavest thou Moses and his people to make mischief in the earth and to desert thee and thy gods? Said He: (Pharaoh.) "Soon will we slay their sons and suffer their women alive; Verily we, over them have hold (Ar. 'Qahir'- Here means Conqueror – Triumphant - One having supreme mastery or hold.) ." See 7:125

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:128 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Moses said unto his people: "Seek ye help from God and be patient: Verily the earth is God's, granteth He as heritage (in Vicissitude.) unto whomsoever He pleaseth among His servants." And the end is (only) for those who guard against evil. See 7:125

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:129 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "We have been persecuted before camest thou unto us and since thou hath come unto us;" Said he (Moses); "Maybe that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make ye the inheritors in the earth so that He may see how ye act (therein)." See 7:125

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said He (Means degradation in the state, Loss of rank rather than the change of place. (A.P.).) : Get thee down hence for it doth not befit thee to behave proudly therein. Get thee out; verily thou art of the despised ones. See 7:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:130 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed seized We the people of Pharaoh with (years long) droughts and diminution of fruits that they may be admonished. (to be mindful.) See 7:125

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:131 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But when reached them any good said they "This is due to us;" and when any evil did smite them, they ascribed it to ill-luck due to Moses and those with him; Be it known! Verily their ill-luck (Man's own misbehaviour is explained in 4:78, but every one's misfortune is with God i.e., in His Knowledge.) is only with God; but most of them know not. (Ar. 'Ta'ir' - Lit., bird - here Omen, Augury. The people of Pharaoh used to draw Omens from the flight of the birds into a particular direction - As some in our days draw similar Omens from Cats and other animals, even men crossing the way.) See 7:125

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:132 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said they: "Whatever thou mayest bring unto us of any sign to enchant us with it, we will not believe in thee." See 7:125

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:133 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So We sent upon them widespread calamities, (of wholesale death), and the locust and the lice, and the frogs and the blood, clear signs (miracles.) , yet they behaved proudly (arrogantly.) and so they were a guilty people. There is a mention also in the Bible, of these pestilences sent on the people.Visitation of Pestilence on Egypt.The river turned into blood – Exodus 7/19, 20Frogs sent – Exodus 8/2-6Dust turned into lice – Exodus 8/16-17Swarms of flies – Exodus 8/21-24The murrain of beasts – Exodus 9/3-6The plague of boils and blains – Exodus 9/9-11The plague of hail – Exodus 9/22-24Locusts – Exodus 10/12-14Darkness – Exodus 10/22.The calamity which smote both men and the cattle – Exodus 12/29

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:134 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whenever fell upon them the torment (The shocking and the shaking torment making them shiver.) said they: "O' Moses! pray unto thy Lord as He covenanted with thee, if thou removeth from us the torment, surely will we believe in thee, and surely will we send with thee the children of Israel." See 7:133

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:135 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But whenever removed We the torment from them till a fixed term which they should reach, lo! they broke (their promise). There is a mention of Pharaoh's people breaking promises to Moses.Pharaoh and his people breaking promises:Exodus 8/29Exodus 8/8, 28, 32Exodus 9/8, 27, 28, 34 and 25Exodus 10/27.When the magicians were turned into believers a great number of the Egyptians also embraced the faith in the True God but Pharaoh at the instigation of his Vizier Haman imprisoned all such believers. item.description: And (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) ask them about the town which was beside the sea; when they did exceed (the limits) in the Sabbath when their fish did come unto them on the day of their Sabbath, appearing on the surface of the water; and on the day they observed not the Sabbath, they (the fish) did not come unto them; Thus did We try them for they were transgressing. The prohibition of fishing on the Sabath night has been based on economical consideration to give respite to the animals at least a day in a week so that it may be better fishing the day after. This is similar to the law of cutting in the forest and hunting land animals, but the Jews violated the law of Sabath and suffered economically and also spiritually for their disobedience.
