(A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:185 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or look (Consider the instability of the transitory state and infer their terms coming nigh to the end.) they not into the kingdoms of the heavens and the earth and whatever things (God) created, and maybe that their term (End.) hath drawn nigh; then in what other words after this would they believe? See 7:184

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:186 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whomsoever God suffereth to stray (One who is not benefited or availed of the guidance of the Word of God.) there is no guide for him, and He leaveth them alone in their transgression, blindly wandering (bewildered). See 7:184

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:187 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They ask thee about the Hour (of Resurrection) when will be its fixed time; Say: "The knowledge of it is only with my Lord (Refer to Mark 13/32. But that day and that hour knoweth no man no, not the angels, which are in heaven, neither the Son but the Father. N. T. Math 13/32. But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven but my Father only. Math. 24/36.) , None shall manifest it at its time (Time here is only a figurative expression for there is no other term for the conditions of the timeless realm.) but He; Heavy (The stage is so difficult to be grasped as it is within the limitations of the heavens and the earth.) shall it be in the heavens and the earth; it will not come…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:188 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: 'neither I (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) own for myself any benefit nor harm except what willeth God; and had I known the unseen (Refer to note on verse 6:50.) indeed I would have had much of good and evil had touched me not, and I am not but a Warner and the bearer of good news for a people who believe? This verse exemplifies the Holy Prophet with the matchless simplicity and charity of the declaration about his personality as an Apostle of God against any ambiguity of a statement but the people might deify him as they have done in the case of the leaders of the other faiths (Jesus etc.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:189 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He it is who created you from a single self (Being.) and from it did He make his mate that he may dwell resting unto her, when he covereth her, she beareth a light burden and carrieth it, when it groweth more heavy they both pray to their Lord; ''If Thou givest us a good child, certainly we shall be of the grateful ones. See also Verses: 4:1 and 16:72 for the creation of mankind of one self or soul. By his calling himself a 'Nazir', warner, he alerts the sinners against the punishment and by his titling himself as a 'Bashir' i.e., the Giver of glad tidings to all the virtuous ones of the reward for their goodness.The verses are clear in their elaboration that there is no need for a particular story to be connected with the matter.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And O' Adam! Dwell thou and thy wife in the garden (State of enjoyment and bliss without any want or endeavour.) , so eat ye two from wherever ye two desire, but go (As already pointed out, this order to Adam was not imperative but explanatory to the requirement of the State in which Adam then was stationed (A.P.). Refer to Verse 2:35.) not ye two nigh into this tree for then ye two will be of the unjust (In relation to the state and not any disobedience to any definite order of God - In short Adam was informed that he will lose the state of comfort he was in, and not the final state he should be in. (A.P.).) . For the story of Adam and Eve being placed in the Garden and their being beguiled by Satan…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:190 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But when He giveth them a good child they ascribe unto Him partners in what He hath given them; but most exalted is God above what they associate (with Him). See 7:189

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:191 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Do they associate (with Him) that which createth not anything, and while they are themselves the created (ones)? See 7:189

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:192 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they cannot help them, nor themselves can they help. See 7:189

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:193 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If ye invite them unto guidance they will not follow you; it is the same to you if ye invite them or ye be quiet. The reference is to those adamant ones in infidelity that they would neither care for the warnings against their infidelity nor would they ever consider at all the promises of the heavenly reward for goodness1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:194 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those whom ye call upon other than God are subservient (to God) like unto your own selves, so call ye on them, then let them answer (Grant your prayers.) if ye be truthful. See 7:193

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:195 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! are there for them feet which they walk with, Or for them are hands which they hold with, Or for them are eyes which they see with, or for them are ears which they hear with? Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Call (The reference may seem to be to the idols but with profound reflections proves that it is applicable to the living entities other than God.) ye all your associates and then scheme ye (your worst) against me (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) and give me no respite." When the idolaters were admonished by the Holy Prophet against their associating others with the Only True God, they said that if their gods are in any way abused, they will send a chastisement. It is against this challenging threat of the idolaters that this verse was revealed.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:196 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily my Protector is God Who sent down the Book (Qur'an) and He guardeth the virtuous ones. It is clear prophecy of the helplessness of the idolaters against the onward march of Islam. This verse clearly warns the polytheists that none of their idol-gods will ever be of any help to them at all. It is a prophecy as well to say that all their power and authority would be frustrated.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:197 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those whom ye call upon other than Him are not able to help you, nor can they help themselves. See 7:196

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:198 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if ye invite them unto guidance, they hear not; and thou seest them looking towards thee, while they see not. See 7:196

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:199 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Adopt thou moderation (In all respects.) , and enjoin (To do good.) virtue and turn (Give up arguing with them.) thou away from the ignorant (Those adamant in disbelief.) ones. See 7:196

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (The) Book (The Holy Qur'an.) (the Qur'an) hath been sent down unto thee so that there be no (Should not be.) straintendness or narrowness in thy (The Prophet addressed for the people.) breast about it, that thou mayest warn thereby (and it be) a reminder to the believers. See 7:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then whispered Satan evil suggestions unto the two (Adam and Eve) that he might display unto them what hath been kept hidden from them of their shame, and said he (Satan.) : "Forbade not ye two, your Lord from this tree save lest ye two may become angels or lest ye two may become (Remain or live forever.) the immortals." See 7:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:200 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if an incitement from the Satan inciteth thee (The Prophet addressed for the people.) , then seek thou refuge in God; Verily He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. See 7:196

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:201 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily those who guard (themselves against evil) when an evil thought from the Satan (Including Impious one - the evil doers.) afflicteth them, they become mindful (of God and get awakened) then lo! they see (aright). See 7:196

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:202 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And their brethren (Of Satan - i.e. the impious ones.) drag them deeper into the error, so they cease not their efforts. See 7:196

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:203 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when thou bringest not unto them a sign say they: "Why not thou forge it?" Say: "Verily I only follow what is revealed unto me from my Lord; these are clear proofs (An eye opener.) from your Lord, and a guidance, and a mercy for a people who believe." See 7:196

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:204 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when the Qur'an is recited; then ye listen to it and be attentive, that mercy be done unto you. Listening to the recital of Qur'an is no doubt highly commendable but it becomes imperative only when the recital is by the Imam of the Jam'at in congregational prayer or in the 'Khutba' (Sermon) of the Friday Prayer. This is almost unanimous among the various Schools Refer to 'Fiqh' (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:205 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And remember thy Lord within thy self in humility and awe, and not (Less aloud.) aloud a voice, in the morning and the evening; and be thou not of the negligent (The Prophet addressed for the people.) ones. It is related that this order to recite the Holy Qur'an silently is an instruction as to what the 'Ma'mum', i.e., the guided one in prayer in the congregational prayers (Salat al-jama' at) has to do, i.e., to recite the passage along with the Imam but not aloud.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:206 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily those who are with (In direct Communion 'Sajdah', prostration. According to the Ahl Al-Bayt – 'Sajdah' i.e., prostration at the recital of certain Verses is 'Wajib' Compulsory - in four Chapters of the Qur'an: Surah As-Sajdah (32:15) Surah Fussilat (41:37) Surah An-Najm (53:62) Surah Al-Alaq (96:19) In rest of the chapters 'Sunnat' Optional. Refer to verses 13:15, 22:77, 32:15.) thy Lord, pride not to worship Him; they glorify Him and (in worship) unto Him they prostrate. The recital of this is as a Sunnat traditional, to be followed by a 'Sajdah' (i.e., a prostration).According to the 'Shi'a Ithna-'Ashari' school which is Islam-Original, i.e., according to the Holy Prophet and the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt 'Sajdah' the prostration is 'Wajib', i.e., compulsory only in four chapters of the Holy Qur'an:(1) 'Alif Lam Meem Sajdah.'(2) 'Ha-Meem'1 Sajdah(3)'Wan-Najm,'2(4) 'Iqra.'3In the rest of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And he (Satan.) swore unto them both: "Verily I am unto you a sincere adviser." See 7:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then he (Satan.) instigated them both by deceit (Aiming something and telling something else Refer to Verse 7:20. i.e. aiming at the first sentence of the Verse 7:20 and telling the concluding words of Verse 7:20.) so when they (Adam and Eve.) tasted (of) the tree their shameful things got displayed unto them, and they both began covering themselves with the leaves of the Garden; and called out unto them their Lord (saying): "Did I not forbid ye two that tree, and (did I not) say unto you both that Satan is of ye both a declared enemy?" See 7:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Prayed Saying.) they (Adam and Eve.) "O' Our Lord! Unjust (In losing the state which was given - This is not the actual loss - The actual loss will be only if Thou forgive not. (A.P.).) have we been unto ourselves, and if Thou forgive us not and deal (not) with mercy unto us (then), We will certainly be of the losers." See 7:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He (God.) said: "Get ye (Adam and Eve.) down (In State. This again establishes the present life as a state of conflict. Refer to Verse 7:17.) , some of you (being) the enemies of the others; and for you there is in the earth an abode and a provision (of sustenance) for a (fixed) time (Term.) ." See 7:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (And) said He (God.) : "Therein ye shall live, and therein shall ye die, and from it ye shall be brought (Resurrected.) out." See 7:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' children of Adam! Indeed We have sent down unto you raiment to cover your shame and (for) adornment (Including all means of comfort.) and the raiment of piety, that is the best; this (Refers to the provision of the means of the physical and the spiritual development.) is of the signs of God that ye may be mindful (In using the said mean; healthily and harmoniously and constructively.) . See 7:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' children of Adam! Let (A warning to mankind against the mischievous aim of Satan in the field of the conflicts, though his activities might result in some physical progress for man. Refer to Verses 7:14 - 7:17.) not Satan involve you into affliction as he got your parents out, from the garden (of the blissful life) stripping off their raiment, that he may expose unto them their shame; He watcheth you, he and (also) his tribe, from whence ye see (This proves the existence of beings invisible to man - Satan always attacks only from unexpected and unnoticed sources.) them not; Verily We have made the devils to be the guardians (The devil's activities will be affective only in those who have the affinity of the devilish characters.) of those who believe not. See 7:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when they act lewdness say they: "We found (This is a common excuse with all the wrong doers.) our fathers (acting) upon this, and God hath enjoined it on us," Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Verily God enjoineth not lewdness ('Fawahish' indecencies including nakedness - while circuiting round the 'Ka'ba'- as the pagans did while worshipping the idols- Other sins and crimes.) ; Do ye say against God what ye know not?" See 7:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "My Lord hath enjoined justice and set (Wherever ye be and stand for prayer-to turn to the 'Ka'ba' as the 'Qiblah'.) ye upright your faces at (each time and place) of prostration, and call (With full concentration and the presence of mind- Beseech.) upon Him, being sincere (With devout submission.) exclusively unto Him in religion; even as He brought (In accordance with the tendency with which life began, they will go back.) you forth (in the beginning) so unto Him shall ye also return." See 7:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (O' people!) Follow ye what hath been sent down unto you from your Lord, and follow ye not (any) other than Him (Any one, or anything else. This discredits 'Ijtihad' against any revelation.) , as (Your) guardians (or friends)', How little do ye mind. See 7:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: A party He hath guided aright, and (the other) party entitled themselves to error; (for) verily they took the devils for their guardians other than God, and think they, that they are the ones guided aright. (Refer to Verse 17:16, 36:7.) A part of them owing to their getting astray has earned perdition.This Verse clearly says that the friends of the devils thought themselves to be guided aright. Hence the mere imagination of any people without the truth in it, to be on the right, is also a satanic delusion.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' children of Adam! Be ye adorned at every time of prostration and eat ye and drink ye and commit ye not excesses; Verily He (God) loveth not the extravagants (This encourages the devotees to be well dressed and adorned as if they are going in festivity to meet the Lord. Condemns austerity, asceticism and luxury of extravagance in life.) . 'Zeenat' or embellishment refers to the cleanliness and decency of apparel specially against the pagan practice of going naked round the Ka'ba but the order is not restricted against any particular practice, but it has a wider significance. The second Holy Imam Hasan Ibn Ali al-Mujtaba used to put on very decent dress whenever he went to pray. When asked the reason of the special embellishment, he used to recite this Verse, and said, 'God is All-Beauty and loves…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Who hath prohibited (Rn. Or. the economical and the prohibitory problems in Islam. Every-thing on the earth is made for mankind provided it is acquired and used within the prescribed way and the limit.) the adornment (granted) of God, which He hath brought forth for His servants and the good things of the provisions?" Say: "These are for those who believe, in the (short) life of this world (to he) exclusively theirs on the Day of Judgment;" Thus do We explain in details the signs for a people who know (Who can understand.) . 'Zeenatullah', i.e., the embellishment of God-meaning the embellishment made lawful by God for men.And the external embellishment and the seeming enjoyments in this life, is there for both the believers in God and the disbelievers as well, but in the life…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "Verily did prohibit my Lord only shameful (Includes all kinds of indecencies.) deeds, those apparent of them and those concealed, and sin and rebellion without (any) right, and that ye associate (not) with God for which hath not been sent down any authority, and that ye say (This is a clear warning against the unwarranted conjectures of the modern irreligious ones, against the ordinances of the Qur'an and the Holy Prophet.) (not) against God what ye know not (Refer to Verse 7:3.) ." See 7:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And for every people (Community.) is (an appointed) term, so when cometh their (appointed) term, they shall not remain (Tarry.) behind an hour (even for the least while) nor can they go before (Refer to Verse 63:11.) . See 7:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' children of Adam! When come unto you apostles from among you, relating unto you My signs, then whosoever guardeth himself against evil and amendeth (The criterion of piety and amending is to follow the revealed guidance and the divinely appointed guide be that an Apostle or an Imam.) (himself), then no fear shall come upon them, nor shall they be grieved (Refer to Verse 2:38.) . See 7:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who belie our signs (the divinely appointed guides and their guidance.) and in pride turn away from them, these are the inmates of the (Hell) fire, and they shall abide therein. 'Wa 'stakbaru' declaring proudly against the signs, indicates the behaviour of the people with the Holy Prophet and the Holy Imams who are the greatest and the direct signs of God. The punishment which the people who misbehaved and annoyed the holy ones, is also mentioned as their being in the Hell for ever.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Who is then more unjust than he who orget (Accepting unauthorised opinions as the divine ones or actually belying the divine authorities like those of apostles or the Imams.) a lie against God or belieth His signs? Those (are they) unto whom shall reach their share (as decreed) in the Book; until come unto them Our messengers (The appearance of the angels may be to the individuals at the time of their death and at the first blow on the resurrection day or on any fatal occasion causing death for the individuals or collectively for the people as a whole.) , cause them to die, they (The angels.) (would) say: "Where is that which ye did call upon besides God?" They (The people.) would say "They have left us away in the lurch," and they shall bear witness against themselves…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He will say: "Enter ye among the people who indeed have passed away before you, of jinn and men into the (Hell) fire; Every time a (new) (A fresh batch of the Sinners.) people entereth (it) it shall curse its sister (Fellows in faith- Companions.) (people); until they have all come together into it, the later of them shall say about the former of them; "O' Our Lord! These are they who led us astray, therefore give them a double chastisement of the fire;" He (God.) will say: "For everyone (of you) double, but ye know." See 7:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the former of them will say to the later of them "So (now) there is not for you any advantage over us, therefore taste ye the chastisement for what ye earned." See 7:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And how many a town have We destroyed, Our wrath came unto them by night or while they reposed themselves at noonday (Refer to Verse 7:159.) . A living instance to prove the truth in this statement are the findings of the recent excavations in the various parts of the world where even flourishing cities have been found to be buried under hundreds of feet of earth covering them, from ages unknown to human history on earth.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily those who belie Our signs and in pride turn away from them, shall not open for them the gates of heaven nor shall they enter the Garden (of Paradise) until the camel passeth through the eye of the needle; thus do We recompense the guilty. The example of the passing of a camel through the eye of the needle stands for the impossibility of the action. A similar example is given in the Bible. Math. 19/24."And again, I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God."Mark the Biblical declaration-the doors of heaven closed to the rich-irrespective of their being good or bad, but Islam declares the closure against a vice be that in the rich or poor. According…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For them shall be the bed of the (Hell) fire and from above them the covering (of it); Thus do We recompense the unjust (Refer to Verses 15:41 - 15:53.) . See 7:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who believe and do good deeds, task We not any soul but to its ability, they are the dwellers of the Garden of (Bliss); They, in it shall abide. See 7:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We will remove whatever rancour be in their breast, there shall flow beneath their abodes rivers, and they will say: "All praise be (only) to God who guided us to this and We would not have been guided had not God guided us; Indeed, did come the apostles of Our Lord with the truth;" and it shall be cried out unto them that: "(Behold!) This is the Garden of which ye are made heirs (Getting with a right of heritage.) for what ye did (This is in Contrast to the discourse in Verses 7:37 & 7:38. Refer to Verse 59:10.) ." One of the greatest or the highly intellectual pleasures of the life hereafter is the inter communion of the souls of the believers in the purest feelings of real brotherhood. Having the social pleasure of life in the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And will call out of the inmates of the Garden (of Paradise) unto the inmates of the (Hell) fire (saying); "Indeed we have found what promised us Our Lord to be true; have ye too found what promised your Lord, to be true?" They will say: "Yes." Then a crier (The first Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abu Talib (See Kashf al-Ghumma) of Mardwaih.) will cry out between them that "The curse of God is on the unjust (This is a very brief description of a 'Zaalim' i.e. unjust.) (Refer to Verses 57:12, 57:13.) ." 'A crier will cry'-According to Ibn Mardwaih - a prominent Sunni Scholar (vide his Kashf al-Ghumma) the crier will be the first Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abu Talib. (M.F.A.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who hinder (Misinterpreting the Holy Qur'an and the sayings of the Holy Prophet, thus hinder others from the right course of faith and its practice.) (People) from the path of God and seek to make it crooked (Misinterpreting the Holy Qur'an and the sayings of the Holy Prophet, thus hinder others from the right course of faith and its practice. Refer to Verses 18:1, 39:28.) , and they in the hereafter (Applicable to those who would do this will call them-selves as believers (Muslims) in this life.) disbelieve. See 7:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And between the two shall be a veil (a curtain.) and on the heights (Overlooking both sides of the curtain.) shall be men who know all (Everyone.) by their marks, and they (Those on the heights.) shall call out to the inmates of the Garden (Paradise) "Peace be on you," They (Those addressed by those on the heights.) shall not have yet entered it, though they do hope (thereof). See 7:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when (they) (Those not yet entered the Garden.) will turn their eyes towards the inmates of the (Hell) fire, they shall say: "O' Our Lord! cause us not to be with the unjust people." See 7:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And will call the occupants of the heights (Ar. 'Araaf' A middle place between Hell and Paradise.) unto the inmates of the Hell who can recognise them by their marks; They will say: "Of (A clear warning to those who get puffed up because of their wealth and their worldly position. The first Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abu Talib says: 'What ye give birth is for dust. What ye amass is to go away. What ye build to be demolished. But what ye act is recorded and stored for the day of accounting or the Final judgment'. Though this is a description of the future-Quran gives us the past for the future, for the future to us is past for God, rather there is no past, present or a future for Him. Everything to Him or to whom He reveals…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Behold ye!) "Are these they whom ye swear that God will bestow not His mercy on them? (whom God now sayeth) Enter ye into the Garden (Paradise)! No fear shall be on you nor shall ye grieve." The people of 'A'raaf will ask the infidels in the Hell pointing to people like Bilal, Ammar, Salman, Sohail, Habab and the similar others, are these the people you used to say that God will not bestow mercy on them, look they have been admitted to Paradise without any fear or grief enjoying the heavenly bliss.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So their cry, when Our wrath came unto them, was not but said they; "Verily we were unjust." See 7:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall call the inmates of the (Hell) fire unto the inmates of the Garden (of bliss) saying: "Pour on us of the water or of what God hath provided you with; "They shall say: "Verily God hath forbidden both to the infidels." See 7:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Those) Who made their religion a past time and play and whom the life of the world hath deceived. So today We neglect (Ar. 'Nisyan' used in the case of God-means neglecting & not forgetting. This is a caution to all those who neglect the life hereafter and take religion lightly or even ridicule religiousness and scoff at the devout religionists.) them as they did neglect this day of theirs, and as they did deny Our signs. See 7:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, We have brought unto them a Book (The Qur'an.) , which We have explained it with know-ledge a guidance (Refer to Verses 2:2, 2:23, 3:177, 10:37, 45:20.) and a mercy for people who believe. See 7:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Do they wait (The Book is Complete so far as guidance and the blessing for the believers is concerned. Nothing has been left to be awaited except the final actuation. And when it comes, those who have neglected the Book before, will say this. Refer to Verse 35:37.) for anything but the final fulfilment (the resurrection)? On the day the final fulfilment cometh, those who neglected it before will say: "Indeed came the apostles of Our Lord with the truth; are there for us (now) any intercessors that they may intercede for us? Or could we be sent back so that we might act other than what we did act?" Indeed, they have lost (Put their souls in loss.) their souls, and what they forged hath gone away from them. See 7:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily your Lord is God who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Arsh (throne) (Of Power, Knowledge and Authority.) . He throweth the veil of night over the day, which pursueth it incessantly, and the sun and the moon and the stars, made (absolutely) subservient to His command; Be it known! (that) His is the creation and the command; Blessed is God, the Lord of the worlds (Refer to Verses 10:3, 11:7, 25:59, 31:3, 40:8, 50:38.) . 'Arsh'-From the primitive matter, the lowest realm of the finite beings up to the highest sphere of the intellectual and the angelical realm, there are finite beings, the higher ones encompassing and penetrating the ones lower to it Arsh of the finite being the highest one which penetrates and encompasses all the finite beings.'Istawa' means…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Call ye on your Lord, humbly and secretly; Verily loveth not God the transgressors (Those who remain aloof from supplication or disturb the peace and harmony of the others.) . See 7:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And make ye not mischief in the earth after its reformation, and call ye on Him (God.) fearing (His wrath) and Hoping (for His mercy), verily the mercy ('Rahimiat'.) of God is well-nigh unto those who do good. See 7:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He it is Who sendeth forth the (heralding) winds bearing good tidings before His mercy (The rain.) ; until they bring up laden clouds, We drive it to a land which is dead, then We send down water thereon, then bring forth with it of fruits of all kinds; Thus will we bring forth the dead (Example of the process which God's grace and blessings assume till the last stage of the fruit coming forth. The same process is applicable to all the dead coming to life. Refer to Verse 6:95. Persian: 'Baaran Ke dar Latafate Tab'ash Khilaf neest Dar Baagh lala rooyad-o-dar Shoora boom Khas (Sadi) The rain, the purity of which is doubtless, Raises flowers in a garden and in the saltish soil (rubbish or thorns). Refer to Verse 13:17.) that ye may be mindful. The revelation…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the good land, springeth forth its vegetation (in abundance) at the will of its Lord; and that which is bad cometh not forth (from it), (herbage); but scantily Thus do we display (In Varieties.) Our signs to people who give thanks (React thankfully.) . See 7:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed, We did send Noah unto his people, so said he: "O' my people! Worship ye God (alone)', ye have no god other than Him; Verily I fear for you the chastisement of a dreadful day (Refer to Verse 11:25, 23:23.) ." The reference to what took place with the other apostles, is only to remind the people of what happened to the disbelievers in the previous ages. The following Verses refer to the people of Noah 3:33; 6:84; 7:59; 7:64; 10:71 - 10:73; 11:25 - 11:48; 14:9; 17:3; 21:76; 21:77; 23:23 - 23:29; 25:37; 26:105 - 26:122; 29:14; 29:15; 37:75 - 37:82; 51:46; 53:52; 54:9 - 54:16; 57:26; 66:10; 69:11; 69:12; 71:1 - 71:28.Verses from 7:59 - 7:102 give the account of the preaching of the various prophets of God, indicates the units of the purpose of their mission…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then certainly will We question those unto whom (Our apostles) were sent, and certainly will We also question the sent (i.e., The Apostles.) ones. The people concerned in this Verse are those to whom apostles were sent. They will be questioned as to how they treated the apostles from God-and their messages.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said the chiefs of his people, "Verily we do see thee in obvious error." See 7:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: "O' my people! No error is in me, but I am an apostle from the Lord of the worlds." See 7:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: I deliver unto you the messages from my Lord and advise unto you and know from God what ye know not. See 7:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or (Or is it that you wonder.) wonder ye that an admonition hath come unto you from your Lord through a man from among you, that he might warn you and that ye guard (yourselves against evil) and that mercy be done unto you? See 7:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But they belied him, so We delivered him and those with him in the Ark (This denotes the reaction and the consequences to the reaction. Said the Holy Prophet: 'The likeness of my Ahl Al-Bayt is that of the Ark of Noah. He who got into it was saved and he who turned away from it, was drowned and lost'.) , and drowned those who belied Our signs; "Verily they were a blind (Blind at heart.) people (Refer to Verses 11:37 - 11:48 23:27 - 23:29 29:40, 37:76.) ." For a detailed reference to the Deluge Refer to Verse 11:37 - 11:48 and 23:27 - 23:29.It is reported that the original name of Noah was Abdul Ghaffar or Abdul Malik or Abdul- A'la, since he wept for fear of God for centuries together (viz. five hundred years) since then he…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And unto (the people of) Ad (we did send) their brother Hud. He said: "O' my people Serve ye God (alone), ye have no god other than Him; What! will ye not then guard (yourselves against evil (Refer to Verses 11:60, 38:12, 53:50, 89:6, 46:21.) ?" There is the mention of the tribe of 'Ad' with the apostle of God, Hud, in the following places in the Holy Qur'an: 7:65 - 15:72, 11:50 - 15:60, 14:9, 26:123 - 15:139, 29:38, 38:12, 40:31, 41:13 - 15:16, 46:21 - 15:26, 50:13, 51:41 - 15:42, 53:50, 54:18 - 15:21, 69:6 - 15:8, 89:6 - 15:8.The Holy Apostle Hud is of the children of Sam in the generation from Noah. Hud, son of Abdullah, son of Riah, son of Noah. He was sent to correct the people of Ad who were very flourishing and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said the chiefs (The rich or the Leaders Refer to Verse 7:75, the mischief mongers.) of those who disbelieved among his people: "Verily we do see thee in folly; and verily we do think thee to be of the liars." See 7:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: "O' my people! There is no folly in me, but I am an apostle of the Lord of the worlds." See 7:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: I deliver unto you the messages of my Lord and I unto you, am a trusted adviser. See 7:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Do ye wonder that an admonition hath come unto you from your Lord through a man from among you, that he might warn you? And remember ye when He made you successors after Noah's people, and increased you in stature (In strength.) , so remember ye the bounties of God that ye may be successful. See 7:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then certainly will We relate to them with knowledge for We were not absent. To know how the conduct of the people will be related to them refer to 36:65. The mouths of the people will be sealed, and the various organs of their body will be caused to relate what all they did.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "Come (Must thou come?) thou unto us that we may serve God alone and we give up what used our fathers to serve? Then bring that down unto us what thou doth threaten (Clearly indicate that the sign demanded by that adamant to the preaching of the apostles, was not the sign to prove the truth in the preachings but the destruction with which the Prophet bad warned and threatened them-The demand was only in mockery.) us with, if thou be of the truthful ones." See 7:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: "Indeed hath fallen upon you, from your Lord (His punishment and wrath); what! Dispute ye with me about the names which ye have named (Refer to Verses 12:40; 53:23.) them (your idols), ye and your fathers? For which hath not been sent any authority from God; Wait then, and verily I too, with you be of those who wait." See 7:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So We delivered him and those with him by mercy from us, and We did cut away the roots (Destroyed even the last one of them stopping even their progeny.) of those who belied Our signs, and (they) were not believers. See 7:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And unto (the people of) Thamud (We did send) their brother Saleh, He said: "O' my people! Worship ye God (alone) Ye have no god other than Him; Indeed came unto you a clear proof from your Lord; This is the She-camel (Refer to Verses 11:61, 91:11 - 91:15. Even today there are people who, if not the 'She-Camel' the miracle wrought by Saleh, mock the other signs, the miracles by the Holy Prophet and the Holy Imams of the Ahl Al-Bayt.) of God (which) unto you is a Sign, so leave it (free) to pasture in God's earth and touch her not with any harm, or ye shall be seized with a painful chastisement." Thamood has been often mentioned along with Ad. It is mentioned in the following Verses: 7:73 - 15:79; 9:70; 11:61; 11:68; 14:9; 15:80 - 15:84;…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And remember when He made you successors after the (people) 'Ad' and settled you in the earth, ye build mansions on its plain and hew the mountains into dwellings; So remember ye the bounties of God, and seek ye not evil in the earth, making mischief (Mischief invites perdition.) . See 7:73

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said the chiefs (The rich ones or the leaders, who had always been the mischief-mongers.) of those who were puffed up with pride among his people to those who were reckoned weak, to those who believed from among them; "Know ye that Saleh is sent by his Lord?" Said they (The weak or the poor.) : "Verily, in what he hath been sent with, we are believers." See 7:73

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said those who were puffed up with pride; "Verily we, in that which ye believe are disbelievers." See 7:73

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They ham-strung the She-Camel and rebelled against the command of their Lord, and they said (A challenge from the people to prophet Saleh to bring down the chastisement they were threatened with.) : "O' Saleh! Bring us what thou didst threaten us with, if thou art of the apostles." See 7:73

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then seized them (unawares) the earthquake, so became they in their dwellings, motionless (dead) (Refer to Verse 51:44.) . See 7:73

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then he turned away from them and said: "O' my people! Indeed I did deliver unto you the message of my Lord, and did admonish you, but ye love not the admonishers." This is what Saleh after the destruction of the people, returning to the place and addressing the dead said: It is not that the address was to any survivors as some commentator says-A similar event had taken place in the start of Islam. The Holy Prophet addressing the dead at Badr had likewise addressed saying: 'Did ye see that what the Lord had said was true?'It is reported in the Tafsir of Tha'alabi that the Holy Prophet once asked Ali if he knew as to who was the worst of men in the past ages? Ali replied: 'God and the Holy Prophet know it.' Then the Holy Prophet…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the measuring (Of the deeds of every individual. Stands for the effectivity of the actions in the order of the Universe. (A.P.). Refer to Verses 18:105; 21:47.) (of the deeds) that day will be just; so whomsoever's weight be heavy those are they who shall be successful. 'Wazan', literally meaning weight or weightage, means justice-or the means of knowing or valuing the correct weightage or measure or worth of a thing. Weighing by God means that every matter will be dealt with, with perfect justice.It was asked of the Seventh Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq whether the deeds of the people will be weighed on the Day of Judgment. He replied, "deeds are not material things to be measured through any balance. Besides the necessity- to weigh, falls only to those who lack in the knowledge of anything.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (We did send) Lot, when said he to his people: "What! Commit ye a lewdness, which did not commit before you, anyone in the worlds (Refer to Verses 11:77, 15:61 - 15:74, 21:71 - 21:74, 38:13.) ?" Lot was Abraham's cousin. Lot has been referred to in the following Verses in the Holy Qur'an 7:80 - 15:84; 11:77 - 15:83; 15:61 - 15:74; 21:74; 21:75; 26:160 - 15:173; 27:54 - 15:58; 29:32 - 15:35; 37:133 - 15:136; 38:13; 50:13; 51:31 - 15:32; 51:33 - 15:37; 53:53; 54:33 - 15:39; 66:10.Even according to Gen. 18/23 Lot has been regarded an apostle of God, a righteous man but in the same book Genesis in the very next Chapter 19/30-38, the worst blasphemy has been coined against Lot being in incestuous intercourse with his own daughters which is a manifest horrible lie…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily ye come to men in lust instead of women; nay, ye are a transgressor people. See 7:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (there) was not any answer of his people except that they said: "Turn ye them out of your town, verily they are a people who seek to purify (themselves)." See 7:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So did We deliver him and his family, except his wife, she was of those who remained behind (Refer to Verse 26:171.) . See 7:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We rained down on them a shower (of stones); Behold (Consider.) ! then, what had been the end of the criminals (The last word of this Verse clearly titles the shameful act not as a sin but as a crime. Refer to Verse 29:40.) . See 7:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And unto (the people of) Madyan (We did send) their brother Shu'aib; said he: "O' my people! worship ye God (alone), ye have no god other than Him; Indeed hath come unto you from your Lord a clear proof, so give ye full measure and weight, and diminish ye not to men their things, and make ye no mischief in the earth, after its reform; This is better for you, if ye be believers." Madyan was the name of one of the sons of Abraham. Madyan was married to one of the daughters of Lot and God blessed this union with abundance of male issues and wealth. The place where the children of Madyan had settled was named after Madyan. It is reported that the habitation consisted of only forty houses.Shu'aib who was among the descendants of Abraham, was deputed…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:86 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And sit ye not in every path, threatening and hindering (Refer to note to verse 7:45.) from the path of God, him who believeth in Him, and seeking to make it crooked; And remember ye, when ye were few He multiplied you, and behold (Observe - Consider - ponder over – Remember - be mindful.) ye what had been the end of the mischief-makers. See 7:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:87 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if there be a party of you who believe in what I am sent with, and another party who believe not, then wait ye with patience until judgeth God between us; and He is the Best of the judges. See 7:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:88 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said the chief of those puffed with pride from among his people: "Certainly we will turn thee out O' Shu'aib, and those who believe with thee, from our town, or ye shall return into our faith" Said he: "What! Even though we be those who detest (The faith of the people i.e., polytheism.) (it)?" See 7:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:89 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed we shall have forged a lie against God if we return in your faith after when delivered us God from it; it fitteth us not that we return into it, save if it willeth (Willeth – Compulsion.) God our Lord; our Lord comprehendeth everything in His knowledge; on God (alone) do we rely; O' Our Lord! Decide (To give verdict on.) between us and between our people with truth, and Thou art the Best of Deciders." (Judges.) See 7:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those whose measure (of the deeds) is light, those are they whose souls suffer loss for what they, with Our signs, did behave unjustly (Indicates that the actions will be weighed with the attitude of the mind towards the signs and not according to the quantity of the actions. The 6th Holy Imam Ja'far as-Sadiq says that even if a man stands the whole night in prayer and fasted the whole of his life, it will avail him of nothing if his deeds are not duly guided by the authority appointed by God. (A.P.).) . The meaning of this Verse is made clear by the previous Verse, i.e., those whose evils will be more than their virtues, 'Yazlimoon' meaning here 'Yakfuroon' and also behaving with 'Zulm', i.e., with aggression. By 'Yazlimoon' also may mean those who had dealt with…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:90 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said the chiefs of those who disbelieved from among his people: "(Beware!) If ye follow Shu'aib, certainly then ye shall surely be losers." See 7:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:91 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then seized them (unawares) the earthquake, so became they in their dwellings, motionless bodies (dead). See 7:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:92 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who belied Shu'aib became as if they never dwelt therein; Those who belied Shu'aib (it is) they (who) were the losers. See 7:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:93 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So turned he away from them and said he: "O' Ye people! Indeed I delivered unto you the messages of my Lord, and did admonish unto you; so how then shall I be sorry for a disbelieving people?" See 7:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:94 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We sent not in a town an apostle, but seized We its people, with distress and adversity, that they might humble themselves. As regards the outlook of the other Apostles of God towards the adamant offenders, the Holy Prophet greatly differs and definitely distinguishes himself in his mercy to the sinners. While all the previous apostles, after playing their role as best as they could, left the people to their fate and in some cases like Noah, even prayed for the people to be chastised, the Holy Prophet notwithstanding a much severer and a more terrible opposition from his people, was so much mercifully disposed towards them that he felt for them to the extent of torturing his own soul with the grief for the sinners, which fact is acknowledged by the Holy Qur'an - 'Perhaps thou wilt kill thyself'…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:95 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then changed We, in the place of evil, good (Evil and good i.e., distress and ease.) , until they grew multiplied (To the extent that they were left to themselves – in the sense of having been given the respite.) and said they: "Indeed did touch (befall) our fathers (also) adversity and happiness; "We seized them suddenly (by surprise) while they were not aware." See 7:94

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:96 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if the people of the towns had believed and guarded (practiced piety.) (themselves against evil) We would have opened up for them blessings from the heavens and the earth, but they belied, so We seized them for what they did earn. See 7:94

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:97 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Do the people of the towns then feel secure from coming unto them Our torment by night, while they are asleep? See 7:94

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:98 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or feel secure the people of the towns from coming unto them Our torment in the morning, while they are disporting? See 7:94

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-A'raaf:99 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Do they then feel (Feeling secure against God's planning is considered in Islam as one of the major sins and the same is to feel despaired of the mercy of God.) secure against the plan of God? But feeleth not secure any one save the people (who are the) losers. See 7:94

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Asr:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the Time (Lit. Squeezing.) ! 'Asr', i.e., Age, which is the continuity of time. The word 'Asr' meaning age or time is used in a mystic use. Commentators say it is a reference to the Age of the Holy Prophet, i.e., a period when the Lord's Promised Last Reformer and Final Law-giver was sent into the world and stayed preaching the truth and taught men the correct ways and means by which man can rise from the ignoble and the loathsome depth of the material world into the glorious heights of spiritual bliss. Some commentators take the word 'Asr' to mean the ceremonial afternoon prayer and the Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq says it is a reference to the age when the Last one of the promised Guide or Imam, in the seed of the Holy Prophet…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Asr:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, man is in loss! It is needless to go into the details that man amidst innumerable temptations, is always caught in the lust for the satisfaction of his carnal desires, thus under the risk of being easily beguiled by the innumerable and the most powerful and irresistible attractions. And if man, is not on his guard against all the formidable forces of Satan who is ever active to lead man astray, man suffers the loss, the loss of the pleasure of his Lord which is the loss of his own salvation, the loss real.It is said that this is, as well a reference to the taunt of Abu Jahl and Walid Ibn Moghaira who said that the Holy Prophet and his followers are the losers, for they have abandoned the worship of their ancestral gods and have given up…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Asr:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Save those who believe, and do good deeds, and exhort each other to truth and exhort each other to endurance (Refer to: 90:17.) 'Those who believe' may include every believer to the extent or the degree of the strength of his conviction or faith and those who will be meant here with the fullest application of the term, will be only those who satisfy to the fullest extent the owning of the several great qualities of a believer mentioned by God1.The believers are those from whom God has purchased their wealth and their lives in exchange for His pleasure with them 9:111. Those who hold the Holy Prophet in preference to their own souls 33:6.The perfection or the purity in the faith can never be found in any other than those whom God Himself has purified (33:33) to be the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! Swear I by this City (Mecca)! City, i.e., Mecca - The people were already aware of the sanctity of the place which was chosen by the great prophet Abraham where at the command of the Lord he left his wife Hagar and his son Ishmael. For the connection of Ishmael's name with Arabia is historic fact through Kedar, son of Bhima. This is vouched by the Old Testament: Gen. 25/13, 18 ps. 120/5, Isa. 42/11, 60/7. Abraham and Ishmael had built the Holy Ka'ba which they raised, dedicating it exclusively for the remembrance of the Lord1 and Abraham in his prayers to the Lord wanted a Prophet to be raised in his seed and to raise some holy one2 who would uphold the sanctity of the House and maintain it in purity and glorification3.The sanctity of the Ka'ba was…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And we showed him the two high-ways (Refer to: 76:3, 91:8.) (of good and evil) Refer to 76:3 and 91:8 and this verse clearly assert that man has been gifted with the power of discrimination and discretion between right and wrong, i.e., one should depend on this native endowment to some extent, independent of the guidance from without, through the apostles - or rather it can be said that without the inborn guidance, i.e., the power of reason, there would be no use of the external guidance. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But he strove not unto (crossing over) the Ascent steep (To ascend the steep.) The path of righteousness is well-known to be an uphill task for it needs to conquer one's self, fighting one's own passion of the carnal desires which go on forging luxuries which are forbidden, and thus lead a restrained life in this world. See Math. 7/14, and man is least inclined to adopt it. This has been referred to also by the Holy Prophet Jesus:''Because straight is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it" Math 7/14.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What would make thee know what is the Ascent steep? See 90:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It is) the freeing a slave or a captive Note the setting free of the slave has been so highly commended. Islam controlled slavery in such a graceful and practical way that it made the maintaining of a slave, a great responsibility for the Master and at the same it enjoined so much care and kindness to the slaves that when they were duly maintained, the slaves themselves, in many cases when they were freed did not like to have the freedom and to leave their masters. For the facilities to be given to the slaves to earn their freedom - See 'Fiqh.'

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or feeding in the day of hunger Note the care of the orphans, the needy, the destitute prescribed in all the acts of charity, as the test of the degree of the sincerity of the one in the faith.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: To an Orphan (Refer to: 4:2, 4:127, 2:220.) , being near of kin See 90:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or to the poor one lying in the dust See 90:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Besides this, to be of those who believe, and enjoin (Recommend (A.P.).) steadfastness on each other, and enjoin mercy on each other (Refer to: 103:3.) Here, patience and compassion is stressed upon whereas in 103:3 endurance and adherence to the Truth. Taking both together, indicated that man's perfection in theory and practice is intended. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These are the people of the Right Hand (Refer to: 56:8.) Those who achieve their cherished goal of salvation1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who disbelieve in Our signs, they are the people of the Left Hand (Refer to: 56:9.) Those who would lose the game of life and thus be committed to the hell-fire which will encompass them from all sides1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: While thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) hath been settler (Unfettered - (A.P.).) in this City! It is given as an exclusive privilege to the Holy Prophet to act freely in the city irrespective of the conventional observance of the sanctity of the place, i.e., to use force, arrest the disbelievers, punish them, deal with them as he deems necessary in the execution of his duties as the Apostle of God, which freedom none else had or would ever have, till the end of the world.This refers to the freedom that God gave the Holy Prophet when he had to enter Mecca by force to free the Holy Place from the control of the pagans who had desecrated the Holy House by turning it into the centre of idol worship and all kinds of barbaric customs and rituals and restored it…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On them shall be the fire closed over See 90:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the Begetter (Refers to Adam as a chosen one and what he begot of chosen ones of God. (A.P.). Refer to: 3:32; 3:33.) (Adam) and whom he begat (mankind) The Begetter, i.e., the First begetter of man, i.e., Adam, and the begotten, the human race as a whole or Abraham the Begetter of Ishmael who assisted Abraham in building the Holy Ka'ba, the House of God, and in whose seed is the Holy Prophet.Refers to Adam as a Chosen one and what he begot, of the chosen ones of God. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed We have created man (to dwell) amidst hardship It is a well-known fact that man has been mysteriously created with distress and difficulties, pangs and pains connected with his birth and is placed in the world to face distress, difficulties and miseries to live in toil and labour and also in mental worries of which not a single human soul, could be free since the birth of the first man on earth till the end of the world, and with the burden of the responsibility of his accountability in the ultimate1.''For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief, yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity" Eccles. 2/23.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Thinketh he (Man.) that over him none, ever hath (any) power? Let no man even for a while imagine that there is none over him to control or to take an account of his motives and deeds - verse 89:14 clearly warns man to beware saying ''Thy Lord is watchful"

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Saith he (Man.) : ''I have wasted, wealth enormous! This is what the disbelievers said when they saw Islam progressing in spite of all their wealth which they exhausted to obstruct its march1. They at last felt their spending away the wealth to stop the Holy Prophet from preaching the Truth, (i.e., Islam from spreading) was all a waste, being of no avail at all. And what some hypocrites felt and said that at their embracing Islam they had been made to spend in dispensing the prescribed poor-rate and the other charities which they deemed as a waste of their wealth.It is clearly indicated here that wealth is given to man as a trial to test his disposition with it.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Balad:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Thinketh he that no one seeth him (Refer to: 8:36.) ? The way of righteousness has been shown and explained by Islam and the way of evil has been pointed out and warned against, informing man of the evil consequences if it - Both the ways have been shown and man has been given eyes and mouths - With the eyes man can see the facts and differentiate between the right and the wrong and the mouth is given to speak, i.e., to enquire about the truth and also to speak it out, tongue to taste the right food and the wrong one, before he devours anything and everything. The eye and the mouth are the two highways shown to man A proper pondering over this will disclose the significance of this reference to the great gifts of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Baqara:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Alif, Lam, Mim Bismi-Llah. - Bismi-Llah, Al-Rahman, Al-RahimBismi-Llah, Al-Rahmani, Al-Rahim is a part of the Surah al-Fatiha and all the other Surahs save the 9th. It has been used obviously for the following important purposes:To condition the mind of the reader with the sanctity of the purpose i.e. the Divine Guidance for which the Holy Word of God is recited.By the meaning of the words 'I begin in the Holy name of God, the Beneficent, the Merciful', means to invoke the Beneficence and the Mercy of the Lord to bestow upon the reciter, the guidance he needs.By using Bismi-Llah before the very commencement of any good work, also means that the individual does it, not for any selfish motives of his own, but he does it on behalf of, and as commanded by the Lord. By this is meant that…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Baqara:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In their heart is a disease, and God increaseth their disease, for them is a painful chastisement, because of the lie they were saying The disease referred to, is the envy and jealousy which burnt those who had not sincerely believed and had envied the Holy Prophet's ever increasing supreme power and authority. The more and evermore increased the glory of the Holy Prophet, the more did increase also the envy and the jealousy of the hypocrites. The disbelief, the envy and the jealousy of the hypocrites is termed as disease, and since it was God's Will that caused the increase of the Holy Prophet's supreme power and authority over the peoples, the increase in the consequent disbelief, envy, and jealousy of hypocrites, is said to have been caused by God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Baqara:100 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And is it not (true) that every time they make a covenant, a party of them cast. it aside? Nay, most of them believe not This verse condemns the people who were given scriptures breaking the covenant they had made with God through His apostles who were sent towards the people. The same condemnation would naturally be drawn against those who break the Covenant made with the Holy Prophet Muhammad at 'Ghadir Khumm' (i.e. those who defy the apostle's teachings and those who displease him by going against his expressed will and his given commandments). All those who acted with selfish motives to usurp the political power or to gain material benefits after the departure of the Holy Prophet, logically come under this verse.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Baqara:101 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when there came unto them an apostle from God confirming what was (already) with them, some of those to whom the scripture was given cast the Book of God behind their backs as if they knew (it) not In the previous verse reference is made to the Isra'ilites casting aside the covenant and their throwing the Book behind their backs. Both the charges refer to the Jews paying no heed to the prophecy made in Deuteronomy. 18/18 about the advent of the one like Moses."I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him" Deuteronomy. 18/18.The truth in this prophecy was proved in the advent of the Holy Prophet Muhammad. The prophecy in Deuteronomy. 18/18…
