Thus, seek protection for thy followers. The Holy Prophet was one of those already protected. Refer to note on verse 33:33 & 55:2.) , and celebrate the praise of thy Lord in the evening and the morning. This verse needs to be studied intelligently. Taking the words 'Wa'staghfir li-dhanbika' isolated, torn away from its context and interpreting them under the influence of wishful thinking and their preconceived antagonistic complex, the Christian commentators in their missionary zeal, to keep away the just and unprejudiced minds in their folds, from embracing the Truth, present the divine personality of the Holy Prophet Muhammad as one not free from sins. This, they do to say that a sinful being can not purify…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who dispute about the signs of God without any authority having come unto them, naught is there in their breast but (a vain desire (Ambition.) ) to become great, which they shall attain not; therefore seek (thou) refuge in God, verily He is the All Hearing, the All-Seeing. See 40:55

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Surely, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of the people, but most people know not. This is another figurative verse of guidance towards the right persons one has to follow. The blind here is the blind at heart and seeing stands for those endowed with knowledge. For similar guiding factors in the Holy Qur'an, see verses 10:35, 39:9, 67:22 & 11:24.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Not equal are the blind and the seeing, nor those who believe and do good and the doers of evil (are equal); little is it that ye reflect. See 40:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, the Hour (The ultimate end.) (of Reckoning) is to come, there is no doubt therein, but most people believe not. See 40:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thus did prove true the sentence (The word.) of thy Lord against those who did disbelieve that they are the inmates of the fire. See 40:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And sayeth your Lord: "Call (Pray.) ye unto Me, I will answer (Response.) you;" Verily those who are arrogant to serve Me, shall soon enter Hell, disgraced. This indicates that no prayer from man is without the response from God. The response may be in complete accord to what man has prayed for or it may be a blessing in other shape and form depending upon, and in God's knowledge what is advantageous to the supplicant. On this basis, the Fifth Holy Imam's 'Du'a' itself is one of the best forms of devotion to God and no devotion will be left without reward. And he said that there is nothing more loved by God than man's asking and beseeching Him for His bounties and there is nothing which is disliked by God more than the one who refrains front such…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God is He who hath made for you the night that ye may rest in it and the day to give you light; Verily God is gracious unto the people, but most people thank not. See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That is God, your Lord, the Creator of everything; there is no god but He; why then are ye turned away? See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus were turned away those who denied the signs of God. See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God is He Who made for you the earth to stay and the heaven a canopy, and shapened you, and made goodly your forms, and provided you with sustenance with goodly things; that is God your Lord; Hallowed (Blessed.) is then God the Lord of the worlds. See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He is the (Ever) Living, (Arabic 'Hai'.) there is no god but He so call ye upon Him, devoting (The faith and the practice of it being exclusively for God's sake.) unto Him the religion; All praise is God's, the Lord of the worlds. See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "Verily I am forbidden to worship those whom ye call upon besides God when clear proofs have come unto me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit myself unto the Lord of the worlds." See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He it is Who created you from dust, then from a life-germ, then from a clot, then He bringeth you forth as a babe, then that ye may reach your full strength, then that ye may be old, and of you are those who are caused to die early and that ye may reach the appointed term, and (all this is related) that happly ye may understand. See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He it is Who giveth life and causeth death, and when He decreeth an affair, He only sayeth unto it 'BE' and it IS. See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Seest thou not those who dispute about the signs of God; how they are turned away? See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who bear the 'Arsh' (The Throne of Supreme Authority.) and those around it celebrate (Hallow.) the praise of their Lord and believe in Him and seek forgiveness for those who believe in Him (saying): "O' Our Lord! Thou comprehendeth all things in (Thy) mercy and knowledge, therefore forgive Thou those who turn (unto Thee) and follow Thy way, and save them from the torment of the Hell:" 'Arsh' i.e., The Throne or the Seat or the Centre of God's Supreme Authority. The throne of a king is the seat of his royal authority from where he enforces his royal will. The word throne is a figurative expression as well as the act of the throne being sustained by the angels.The 'Arsh' or The Throne of Supreme Divine Authority could be conceived as the State of Absolute Divinity which is…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who belie the Book and what We sent Our Apostles with; then soon shall they know, See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When the fetters shall be in their necks and the chains; they will be dragged, See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Into the boiling water, then in the fire shall they be burned; See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then it shall be said unto them; "Where are those whom ye used to associate (as gods)," See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Besides God?" They shall say: "They have gone away from us, nay, we used not to call upon anything before;" Thus doth God leave the disbelievers to stray. (In their confusion.) See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It will be said unto them) "This because ye exulted in the land without any right, and because ye were insolent." See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Enter ye the gates of Hell to abide therein." Wretched then shall be the abode of the arrogant (Haughty.) ones. See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So be patient thou, verily the promise of God is true; And whether We let thee see of what We threaten them with, or We cause thee to die (before that), unto Us shall they be returned. See 40:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily sent We apostles before thee, of them there are those whom We have mentioned unto thee; and of them are those whom We have mentioned (Note the wide range of the recognition of the apostles sent to the other people in the different parts of the earth, though their names might not be found in the Qur'an. No other religion has done this.) not unto thee; and it was not given to any apostle to bring a sign (miracle) save with the leave of God, but when came the behest of God, (it) was executed with truth, and those who stood on falsehood were then the losers. The passage refers to destructive signs - meaning when the order of God comes, wherever it may be, it is executed with full truth. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God is He Who made for you the cattle that ye may ride on some of them, and of them ye may eat. See 40:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' Our Lord! Admit them into the ever-blissful gardens which Thou hast promised unto them and those who do good from their fathers, and, their wives, and their children; for Thou art the Almighty, the All-Wise! See 40:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And for you in them are other benefits, and that ye may realize thereon the need ye cherish in your breasts; and upon them and upon the ships ye are borne. See 40:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He showeth you His Signs; which, then, of the Signs of God will ye deny (See verse 55:13 and its repetition in the surah.) ? See 40:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! have they not travelled in the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were more (in number) than those and mightier in strength, and greater are their relics (of their power) in the earth, but availed them not what they were earning. See 40:78

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when came unto them their apostles with clear proofs (of their truthfulness), exulted they in what they had with them of knowledge, but encompassed (Surrounded them.) them that which they were wont to scoff. This applies to those who exult in their own knowledge of science, mocking at whatever is beyond their experimental sphere. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But when they beheld Our punishment said they: "We believe in God alone and we deny what we used to associate with Him." See 40:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But shall not benefit them their faith when they had beheld Our punishment; (Getting into the grip of the divine order - creative or legislative. (A.P.).) (such is) the procedure of God which hath indeed been in use concerning His servants; and then (When they get with the grip. (A.P.).) the disbelievers have lost. See 40:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaafir:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And keep (Protect.) them from evil: and whomsoever keepest thou from evil, this day indeed Thou hast bestowed mercy on him, and that, it is a Mighty Achievement. See 40:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hath not come unto thee the tidings of the Overwhelming Event? (Refer to: 12:107, The Total Resurrection.) 'Ghashiyah', i.e., that which covers or overshadows or overwhelms, i.e., a terrible thing or event which confounds the people and sends them off their senses. The Day of Judgment will be a state of such reality that what we think and see in this life will have been lost in our realisation of the reality which will be laid bare before us1. The Day of Judgment.The enjoyments referred to in this Surah are all figurative presentations of the heavenly entertainment in the heavenly assemblies of the souls. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In a grand garden See 88:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They shall hear not therein any vain talk See 88:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therein a spring flowing See 88:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therein are couches (Exalted - joyful seats raised.) exalted See 88:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And goblets ready placed See 88:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And cushions ranged in order See 88:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And carpets spread forth See 88:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! See they not unto the camels, how they are created? Man's attention is invited to the four things which he sees every day.The Camel, the ship of the desert. The usefulness of the animal, its build and its peculiar traits.The Skies, with their unlimited heights, their wonderful bodies and their mystic functioning with the tremendous control over their regulated activities.The Mountains, their huge sizes, their fixed immovable stand, the usefulness of its material, the stone.The Earth with its extent, being a globe yet serving a wide plane, and its amenability to the growth of the essential produce out of it, and the great store of minerals, metals and the liquids treasured in it.M.A. translates (Ibil) to mean 'clouds' - and in his notes refers to - Tajul Arus and some Arabic Lexicon - saying it is the view of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And Unto the heaven, how it is raised See 88:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And unto the mountains, how they are set up? See 88:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Some) faces on that day shall be downcast The feeling of humiliation in a man is manifested only on his face. On the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers and the wicked will be humiliated for their arrogance and pride. Their faces will be awful and terror-stricken and downcast.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And unto the earth, how it is spread out? See 88:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So, thou (The Holy Prophet.) (go on) reminding; Thou art only a Reminder (Refer to: 87:9.) The duty of an apostle of God is only to preach the faith and teach the people its practice and show them the right ways of life. It is not for the apostle of God to watch the people against their wickedness or to punish them.'Musaitir' here is used in sense of compelling one to any action, i.e., Compeller1, as otherwise the Prophet and his successors represent God as His Vicegerent to execute the divine legislative will and it is in absolute conformity with it. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thou art not, over them, a compeller (Refer to: 2:256, 10:99.) See 88:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But whosoever turneth back and disbelieveth Chastising those who turn back and disbelieve in the truth rests only with God.Here and elsewhere God refers to Himself in plural, the totality of His Authority is implied. Thus, all the entities functioning in the machinery of His authority are included1. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then will chastise him God with the greatest chastisement See 88:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily unto Us is their return See 88:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then verily, upon Us is to reckon with them See 88:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Toiling, weary Those who were striving in the life here in hostility against the godly ones. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Entering into the fire, blazing See 88:3

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Made to drink from a spring (fiercely) boiling (Or a humiliating stuff.) See 88:3

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For them there shall not be (any) food but of the bitter-thorny fruit 'Zaree' 'Zaree' a kind of dry thorny shrub, so bitter in taste that none of the animals even go near it, it is also loathsome in appearance. This tree will be the food of the fellows in hell.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Which will neither fatten nor give any relief (Sufficing – satisfying.) from hunger See 88:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Other) faces on that day shall be happy The state of bliss which the righteous will be placed in.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ghaashiya:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: With their efforts past, well pleased See 88:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Reality (That which is sure to come) ! The Inevitable: - That which shall surely come to pass without fail - when all falsehood shall vanish, only the absolute truth shall be laid bare - The word 'Alhaqa' is derived from 'Haq' or 'Haqiqah', i.e., the truth.That which is sure to come - the inevitable, i.e., The Resurrection. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they disobeyed the Apostle of their Lord, so He seized (Gripped) them with an increasing seizure (Vehement – intense. Refer to Verse 11:42.) See 69:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, We, when rose the water (of Noah's flood) surpassed the (ordinary) limits, bore you up (O' mankind) in the Ark made to float Reference is to the rescue that Noah along with his sincere followers being saved by through Ark1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That We may make it unto you a Reminder, and that retaining ears might retain it According to the Holyat al-aulia, and Kashshaf Ms., etc. This Verse was revealed about Ali Ibn Abu Talib. The above authorities report that the Holy Prophet said: "O' Ali! God hath commanded me, to always keep thee near me and not away from me - and I prayed to God to make thy ear such that whatever thou hearest of the Word of God and receiveth the knowledge from me, thou forgetteth not but preserve it always. I have been commanded by God to convey to you whatever knowledge I receive from Him" It was based on the strength of this divine gift that Ali on the day of his departure from this world, though mortally wounded in the head, by a strongly poisoned…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when is blown by the Trumpet (Refer to Verse 6:73.) , a single blast This refers to the inevitable event, the day of the Final Judgment. The whole creation will first pass through the destruction, to be raised once again to account for each one's faith and conduct. For the first blast1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the earth and the mountains shall be borne away and crushed with a single crushing (Refer to Verses 89:21, 56:1 - 56:6, Chapter – 101.) The whole physical world will pass away and a new one will be brought into being1. The mountains which stand on the earth since its creation, with their hardness, will be rendered into powder and blown into the atmosphere. For what will happen on that day, to the earth and the mountains2.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On that Day shall come to pass the Great Event (of Reckoning) (Refer to Verse 89:21, 59:1 - 59:6, Chap. 101, 56:1.) See 69:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall cleave asunder the heaven (Refer to Verse 84:1 - 84:5.) , so that on that Day it shall be (mere) frail (Nebular State.) See 69:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the angels shall be on the sides of it; and above them shall bear that Day 'Arsh' (the Throne of Authority) of thy Lord, eight (The divine attributes of God.) (of them) The 'Arsh' i.e., the seat of the Might, Wisdom and Authority of God, will be borne by eight angels. Angels representing the various aspects of the divine attributes of God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the Day ye shall be exposed, (and) shall remain not hidden any secret of yours See 69:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then he, who is given the (Record) Book (of his deeds) in his right hand (Refer to Verses 17:71, 84:7.) , will say: 'Lo! read ye my book! (Refer to Verse 35:11 - 35:14.) ' The righteous are called the Companions of the Right Hand1.Righteous are said to receive the record of their deeds in their Right Hand2.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What is the Reality? The Resurrection, i.e., passing into new life or the coming into life after death, everyone individually and collectively, according to Qur'an is such a reality and so certain to happen that in many places has been termed as 'Haqq al-Yaqin' - the Certain Truth, as otherwise Qur'an considers the creation as meaningless. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, I did feel (Think – realise.) that I shall meet my account (See Verse 2:46.) See 69:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So shall he be in a life (of bliss), pleased (with it) See 69:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In the Garden Exalted (See Verses 88:10; 56:12; 52:17; 55:46.) See 69:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The fruits of it being low and near at hand There will not be the least difficulty or hindrance in the enjoyment of the bounties in the heaven. Fruits in bunches will be hanging low within the reach of everyone. All the descriptions of the heavenly bliss, given in the Qur'an, are figurative.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It will be said unto them): "Eat ye and drink ye for health and pleasure, for what goodness ye sent before (Refer to Verse 77:20.) you, in the days past (Refer to Verse 2:110.) !" Everybody will be justly repaid for his deeds in this life1.The days gone by are referred to the life in this world for then the world be wholly new. This earth and the heaven would have been changed2. There would not be the present conception or the realisation of even the time and the space.The address 'Eat and drink' will be particularly to those righteous ones, who in this life, in the way of the Lord, suffered hunger and thirst and fasted to please the Lord.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But he, who is given the (Record) Book (of deeds) in his left (Refer to Verses 84:10 - 84:12.) hand, will say: "O' that the Book had not been given me! (Refer to Verse 35:11 - 35:14.)" In contrast to the righteous ones, the wicked ones, will be given the records of their deeds in their left hand who would remember their past life with agony and repentance which would be of no avail to them causing them a mental torture. They would like to have not been given any records at all1.Right always means the direction towards God and the left, i.e., to the material world. In this sense it is correct to term the direction 'left' as 'Backward'. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And I had not known what my account was See 69:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' would that it had made an end (of me)! They would wish death to have been an end of the world and their life in it, but to their disappointment death was only a transition to a new world, in a new state of reality and actual realization.This has always been the tendency of the evil doers when they face the consequence of their own misdeeds, they wished that they had not been in the know of it. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Availed me naught my wealth! See 69:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And hath gone from me (all) my power! Every soul would have lost hold on itself and the power and authority, as a whole, would be only of God and none else. He would be the only King, the Master, the Lord of the Day1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what did thou (O' Man) comprehend what the Reality is? See 69:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It will he said unto him)'. "Seize him ye (angels)" and fetter him! See 69:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then into the blazing fire burn him! See 69:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then into a chain, of the length of cubits, tie him into! 'Seventy Cubits' represent the enormity of the size and the weight and grievous nature of it.Qur'an has a special reference to the number seven and its multiples, particularly in reference to the several stages or the aspects of hell as it is said. The justification for that is the five external and two internal senses through which the devilish temptations are affected1. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily he used not to believe in God, the Great! See 69:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And he urged not the feeding of the poor The expression includes obstructing or preventing the dispensation of the poor-rate 'Zakat' and 'Khums' and the aims to the poor.Not felt as necessary - Indicates the sympathy of the needy and service to them here, is of no avail in the hereafter. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So for him here today there is not a friend See 69:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And no food is for him save the refuse of the wash of wounds! See 69:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Which shall eat none but the sinners! See 69:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So, I swear (Refer to Verses 56:75, 90:1.) by what ye see! Falsehood always yields and gets vanished, giving place to Truth. Though one might deny God or call His word a lie or doubt the Truth and term it as poetry or folklore, but the nature, even that which is seen by man, the visible world itself is quite sufficient to prove the truth and establish it. This refers to the Holy Qur'an being the Word of God and not the fabrication of the Holy Prophet.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what ye see (All-Enveloping - nothing left over.) not! See 69:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Belied Thamood and 'Ad' the striking (Horrible) calamity (Resurrection. Refer to Verses 7:73 - 7:78, 11:61, 51:44.) 'Qariyah' derived from 'Qar' i.e., striking of one thing over the other - here meaning calamity striking terror by the events causing horror and awe in the hearts of the people - The Day of Doom which the people 'Ad' and 'Thamood' disbelieved and called it to be a lie. Qariah is another name for the terrible day of the Final Judgment1.Thamood, the people who defied the apostle 'Saleh' who hamstrung the 'She-Camel' which appeared by God's command - A Mighty Calamity consisting of earthquake and a terrible Thunderstorm overtook them and they were destroyed2.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, it is the word of the most honoured Apostle! The Holy Qur'an is the utterance of the Word of God by the Holy Prophet, who is God's Honoured one.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And it is not the word of a poet; (How) little it is what ye believe? See 69:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nor the word of a soothsayer; (How) little it is what ye reflect? See 69:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is a despatch descended from the Lord of the worlds See 69:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if (Our Apostle Muhammad) had fabricated against Us any of the sayings This divine undertaking is to assert that those who have been commissioned by God, cannot but deliver whatever they are charged with, and God never allows them to forge anything of their own on His behalf. It does not mean that the imposters or the false prophets who forge lies and falsely claim to have been commissioned by God, need not be exposed - in this manner, the lack of evidence is itself sufficient to expose them. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Certainly, would We have seized him by the right hand See 69:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then certainly would We have cut off his aorta See 69:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of you not one could have withheld (Us) against him See 69:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily, it is a reminder unto the pious (Those who guard themselves against evil) ones. (Refer to Verse 2:142 for the part of the Verse related to the Holy Qur'an as a source of guidance, and to 3:137 for the part of the Verse related to the Holy Qur'an as a reminder.) See 69:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily know We that some of you are the beliers See 69:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So as to Thamood, they were destroyed by an exceedingly terrible thunder See 69:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily it is a great grief unto the disbelievers See 69:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily, it is the very Truth, fully assured (Refer to Verses 102:5, 102:7.) Certainty could be in variant degrees:(1) The knowledge acquired through external evidence, which is to a degree of certainty, is called the ''Ilm al-Yaqin' i.e., the knowledge of the certainty1;(2) Seeing something with one's eye also, leads to a kind of certainty which also sometimes proves to be a deception or the limitation of our vision. It is called 'Ain al-Yaqin', i.e., the vision of the certainty2;(3) 'Haqq al-Yaqin' the Certainty Proper Doubtless which could never be disproved. It is that degree of certainty referred to here.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So Hallow by the name of thy Lord, The Great! See 69:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And as to 'Ad, they were destroyed by a roaring violent blast 'Ad' the people who defied the apostle Hud, who were destroyed by a terrible violent blast of the wind1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He made it rage against them for seven nights and eight days uprooting, that thou mightest see the people therein prostrate as if they were the trunks of the hollow palms See 69:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Seest thou then, of them any surviving? Not one left alive - Even those who took shelter under the underground cells, were blown out and killed.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Haaqqa:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And came Pharaoh and those before him and the cities over-thrown, with evil Pharaoh whose inordinate pride and being puffed up with power, has passed into a proverb. He defied the apostle Moses and was destroyed1.The cities overthrown are Sodom and Gomorrah which defied the preachings of the apostle Lot - They were overturned2.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Celebrateth the praise of God, whatever is in the heavens and the earth; and He is the Ever-Prevalent, the All-Wise (Refer to Verse 17:44.) The praise or the glorification of the creatures of the Almighty Creator of the Universe is their serving Him, governed by His laws, the laws of nature which none could ever go against. Surrender is of two kinds, the helplessness under which an individual or a group of individuals cannot but act in a given pattern, and while acting realise the Wisdom and the Grace endowed in the behaviour or the pattern and then glorifying the Authority controlling the affairs.The second kind of surrender is, the voluntary submission adopting a pattern or a mode of thought or action, of one's own accord, at one's own choice and discretion, knowing the beauties, the wisdom and the grace…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what reasons have ye that ye spend not in the way of God, and God's is the heritage of the heavens and the earth; alike are not among you those who spent before the victory and fought and (those who did not), they are more exalted in rank than those who spent and fought afterwards; and unto all hath promised God goodness; And verily God, of whatever ye do, is All-Aware Before the capture of Mecca, the Muslims who yet were a small minority, were very poor – those who spent before the victory of Mecca which opened the road to ease the economic tension and paved the way to prosperity - could not be equal to those who spent when there was not so much need for it. It was 'Ali and exclusively 'Ali among the companions of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Who is he who would loan unto God a goodly loan? so that He may double it for him, and for him shall be a noble recompense (Refer to Verses 2:245; 5:12.) The goodly loan to God is charity, i.e., spending of the wealth in God's way. It is hound by the following conditions for its acceptance:That which is given away or spent in the way of the Lord must have been well-earned, i.e., through lawful means.The thing given must be defectless.That which is given, must be needed by the giver for himself and not the stuff not needed by the giver.Not that which is given away at the point of death when the giver would not need it any longer.It must be given without any publicity.It must be given to the one who needs it, the most.When given away…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Day thou shalt see the faithful men and faithful women, with their light (The Light of faith and righteousness.) running before them, and on their right hand (shall be given) glad tidings for you of that Day! Gardens 'neath which flow rivers, to abide therein; That is the great achievement (Refer to Verse 7:44.) Ibn Mas'ood says that on the Day of Judgment everybody will have the light of his own righteousness to the extent of the degree of his or her own individual faith and goodness in his life. When the righteous ones - helped by the light of their own goodness would be admitted to the heavens, they would be welcomed at the entrance1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the Day will say the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women unto those who believe: "Tarry ('Look ye' unto us.) ye for us, that we may borrow (To have a share from.) light from your light;" It shall be said: "Turn (Turn to - or reflect on what you have done and borrow from your own deeds what you left behind you.) ye back and seek ye (some other) light!" So there will be set between them a wall (a harrier) with a door therein; the inside thereof shall be mercy in it, and outside it, before it shall be chastisement (Refer to Verses 7:44; 59:18; 66:8.) The illustration goes to mean that on the Day of Judgment none would have the least relief from the others' faith. It would be a day of 'Everybody fur himself'1. Only those…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They will cry out unto them: 'Were we not with you?' They shall say: 'Yea! but ye cast yourself into temptation, and ye waited (for us to be beguiled) and ye doubted (in God's warning), and deceived you your vain desires till came the decree of God (to pass) and deceived you about God the (Arch) Deceiver (Satan.) ' By the word 'amr' meant the command for their death.The Deceiver, i.e., Satan.This shows the mere physical companionship in this life is that, even with the Holy Prophet - be of no avail (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So this day shall not be accepted from you any ransom nor from those who disbelieved; your abode shall be the fire; it is your guardian (Has a right over you.) , and what a wretched resort it shall be! (Refer to Verses 2:48; 2:54; 2:123; 6:165; 17:15; 17:38; 17:52; 35:18.) See 57:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hath not the time yet come, for those who believe that their hearts become humble for the remembrance of God and what hath come down of the Truth? And (that) they should not be like unto those who were given the Book before, but (when) lengthened the ages passed over them (In arrogance and disobedience.) , so it hardened their hearts; and many of them are transgressors According to Ibn Abbas, 13 years, and according to Ibn Mas'ood 14 years after the revelation of the Holy Qur'an had started his mission, this verse was revealed about the companions of the Holy Prophet. It could be easily judged how deep had faith gone into the hearts of the people. The hearts were not humbled and the declaration of the faith was only verbal. The reference is to the Jews who became…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Know ye! that God enliveneth the earth after its death (To show how the dead will be resurrected.) . Indeed, have We made the signs clear unto you, that ye may understand See 57:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily charitable men and charitable women and those who offer a goodly loan unto God, doubled shall it be unto them, and for them shall be a noble recompense (Refer to Verses 2:245; 5:12; 64:17; 73:20 and 57:11.) See 57:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who believe in God and His Apostle, these it is who are the truthful ones (Those who doubted the bonafide of the Holy Prophet at Hudaibiyya and those who deserted him in the battles can never be the 'Siddiqun' – i.e., the truthful ones.) , and the witnesses with their Lord. For them shall be their recompense and their light; And those who disbelieve and belie Our signs, these are the inmates of hell The people are divided into groups - the one consisting of those who believe in God and the Holy Prophet - and the others who disbelieve and belie the signs from God. The division though very brief but very comprehensive. None is a believer, if he believes only in God - Since his faith is completed only by the belief in the truthfulness of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: His is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth; He causeth life and causeth death; and He, over all hath power Compare this Verse with:"Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven." (Math 6/10).The manner in which the Bible of the Church, founded in the name of Jesus which suggests that somebody else rules on earth and the will of someone else other than God, is done on it and man is yet praying for the kingdom of God to come and God's will to be done. The Holy Qur'an refutes such a belief and declares that to God, to none else, belongs the kingdom both of the heavens as well as of the earth. The following verses up to verse 8, give further illustration of the declaration of God's exclusive ownership of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Know ye! That the life of this world (The instability of which is like vegetation) is only a sport and play, a gaiety and a boasting and the lustful-vying (Rivalry.) in the multi-plication of wealth and children, is like unto the rain therewith springeth up the vegetation, it pleaseth the husbandmen (May refer to ungodly peasants.) ; then it is withered away, and thou seest it becometh yellow, then becometh it stubble crumbleth down; And in the hereafter is a severe chastisement and (also) forgiveness from God, and (His) pleasures; and naught is the life of this world but means of illusion (Refer to Verses 6:32; 29:64; 47:36.) There is in this terse the manifest truth about this world. People not only spend their life in it, but they mostly indulge in showing off and boasting and piling up riches…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Vie ye in hastening unto forgiveness from your Lord and unto a garden whose extent is like the extent of the heaven and the earth, prepared for those who believe in God and His Apostles; that is the grace of God, He bestoweth it upon whomsoever He willeth; and God is the Lord of Mighty Grace (Refer to Verse 3:132.) It is said that his deputy from Heracles asked the Holy Prophet, "If Paradise is to be extensive in the heavens and the earth, where would then be the hell?" The Holy Prophet replied "Glory he to God! Where remains the night when day comes."1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Befalleth not any disaster in the earth or in your own selves save it is in a Book, ere We cause it to be, verily that is easy for God 'Kitab' referred to in this verse is the secured Tablet. 'Lawh al-Mahfooz' which is the record of everything that is willed by God to be enacted. When it has been said that nothing takes effect without God's Will, i.e., everything is done when it is willed by God, man should resign himself to the will of the Lord both in pain and pleasure in loss and gain. In loss because it is the unavoidable decree of the Lord and in prosperity because the man would die leaving everything behind.The recording, is the necessary consequence of His Infinite Knowledge but informing man of the predestined record to avoid distress to man…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Lest distress ye yourselves for what escapeth you, and be over- joyous for what He hath granted you; and God lovcth not an arrogant boaster See 57:22

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who are niggardly and enjoin upon people niggardliness; and whosoever turneth away (from charity) then verily God is He who is Self-Sufficient (In Arabic, Ghani.) , the Most Praise-Worthy (In Arabic, Hameed.) See 57:22

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed, sent We Our apostles with clear proofs, and sent We down (Revealed, through the Messenger Angel.) with them the Book and the scale that people may establish themselves in justice; and sent We down iron wherein is latent (in its use) mighty power (Violence - Strength.) and also benefits for mankind (It is worth imagining for a while as to what will happen to human life on earth if God only commands the iron to become soft instead of being hard.) and that God may prove who helpeth Him and His apostles in secret; Verily God is All-Strong the Ever-Prevalent (Refer to Verses 16:35; 55:7 - 55:9.) 'Mizan', i.e., The Balance or Measure or the laws governing justice.'Hadeed', i.e., Iron. According to the holy Ahl Al-Bayt the iron in this verse refers to Zul Fiqar the sword which was…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed sent We Noah and Abraham, and endowed We in their seed the Prophethood and the Book, so among them are some who are guided aright; and most of them are transgressors This passage asserts the 'Nubuwah' and the Book will not go out of the issues of Noah and Abraham but it does not mean that all issues will be righteous and on the contrary most of them will be wicked1. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We made Our apostles to follow in their footsteps, and sent We after them Jesus, son of Mary, and We gave him the Evangel; and We put into the hearts of those who followed him kindness and compassion; but (as to) the monastic life, they invented (The Christian monasticism is only an innovation. There is no monasticism in Islam.) it themselves. We prescribed not on them save seeking the pleasure of God, and this they observed not as they ought to have observed it; and gave We unto those of them who believed their (due) recompense; but many of them are transgressors See 57:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! Fear ye (the wrath of) God and believe in His Apostle; He will give you a twofold ('Rabtnaniyat', 'Rahemiyat'. See Note on 'Rahman' & 'Rahim' under S.I.) of His Mercy, He will appoint (Make.) for you a light wherein ye shall walk (straight on the Right Path) and He will forgive you; and God is Oft- Forgiving, the Most Merciful (Refer to Verse 7:156.) See 57:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So that may know the people of the Book that they control not aught of the grace of God, and that grace is in God's hand, He bestoweth it upon whosoever He willeth; and God is the Lord of Mighty Grace See 57:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Hidden: and He is the Knower of all things (The All-Knowing.) Note how brief is the statement, within only four of the divine attributes of the Absolute viz., the External, the Manifest and the Hidden Existence of the Reality of the All-Divine Being is presented.These attributes in their true sense cannot be applicable but to an Absolute and Unlimited and All-embracing One about Whom nothing can be said actually except negation of the ideas and the concepts which are applicable to beings of composite nature (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He it is who created the heavens and the earth in six periods, then firmly established (Himself) over the 'Arsh' (Refer to the note on the process of creation and the absolute hold on the Arsh) (the Seat of supreme authority)', knoweth He whatever entereth the earth, and whatever goeth forth from it, and whatever descendeth from the heaven, and whatever goeth up into it; and He is with you wherever ye be; and God, is the Seer (All seeing.) of whatever ye do (Refer to Verse 58:7.) This state of the Creator, being with His creatures, in all circumstances, is another state which indicates His only presence of All-embracing nature and is a blow to all anthropomorphic conception of the godhead (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: His is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth; and unto God (alone) arc returned (all) affairs (Refer to Verse 57:2.) See 57:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He causeth the night to enter in upon the day, and causeth (He) the day to enter in upon the night, and He (alone) is the Knower of whatever is in the breasts (Hearts.) See 57:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Believe ye in God and His Apostle (Muhammad)! and spend ye (in charity) of whatever He hath made you the successors thereof; for whosoever among you believe and spend (in charity), for them is a recompense very great (Includes every kind of gift - intellectual as well as physical (A.P.).) Any intelligent student of the Holy Qur'an would not fail to note and appreciate Islam associating alms or charity with the faith. In fact, the sincerity of the believer in Islam, is proved by his attitude to his possessions in the material world. One who loves God, would surrender himself with all his interest, to Him.The verse means - "admonish the believer to remember that the wealth you have inherited was earned by the previous owners with toilsome efforts, they did not use it for themselves, nor did they spend…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what reasons have ye that ye believe not in God? And the Apostle (The Holy Prophet.) inviteth you to believe in your Lord, and hath indeed taken a covenant from you if ye are believers Some commentator says that the 'Covenant' stands for the promise taken by God from each soul in the pregenital spiritual state, that the souls would serve God and none else.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hadid:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He it is Who sendeth down unto His Servant (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) signs manifest, so that He may bring you out of the darkness (of infidelity) into the light (of faith)' (Refer to Verse 2:257.) , and verily God unto you is the Most Kind and the Most Merciful! See 57:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye People! Fear ye your Lord! Verily, the quake of the Hour (of Doom) is a thing tremendous! (Grievous.) The reference here is to the end of the world. The address is to every man and woman as a warning against infidelity and wickedness. Inviting them to the faith in God and to lead a righteous life - The terrible happening of the convulsion or the quaking of the earth marking the beginning of the Hour of Judgment will be a terror only to the disbelievers and to those who have rebelled against the authority of the Lord by disobeying the prescribed laws (Shariah) and not for the faithful. The righteous ones are told of the bliss they would enjoy. The matter in this and the next verse is to warn mankind against infidelity and wickedness and to invite…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (And unto him will be said): "This is for (what thou worked in your life.) what sent before thy two hands, and that (verily) God is not unjust to His servants." Man's sufferings could be what he had himself earned by his own sinful deeds. God is never unjust to anyone.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of the people is he who worshippeth God (standing) on the verge, so if befalleth unto him good he is satisfied, and if afflicteth him a trial, he turneth back his face; loses (He has lost.) he both this world and (also) the here after; That is a loss (which is) manifest. (Clear.) 'Ala Harfin', on the verge - Being with fluctuating faith - Who has entered the ranks of believers with doubt and suspense with a wavering mind, ready to quit the faith if any mishap befalls him or to the believers. "Like him who is in the outskirts of the army, who remains there if sure of victory and spoils, otherwise flees away. People who are not firm in faith. They are believers as long as everything goes on well with them, but as soon as they…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He calleth besides God, that which harmeth him not nor doth it profit him; that is straying far off. The apostate calls or prays to the one besides God, who cannot hurt him even if he does not pray to him and who cannot profit him in the least even if he is prayerful to him.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He calleth upon him whose hurt is nearer than his profit: verily evil is the lord, and evil certainly is the associate. See 22:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily God will admit those who believe and do good deeds, into gardens 'neath which flow rivers; Verily God doeth what He intendeth. See 22:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whoever thinketh that never will God help him (the Apostle Muhammad) in this life nor in the hereafter, let him stretch a cord unto the heaven (Ceiling.) (to raise himself) and hang himself, then let him cut it off, (Stop the heavenly help.) then see if his device taketh away what he is enraged at. (The divine help which the Holy Prophet received.) Meaning that he who thinks that God would never grant the Holy Prophet victory over his enemies - or if the enemies of the Holy Prophet do not want the Holy Prophet to be helped and they are enraged at the Holy Prophet getting God's help, let them in their rage and disappointment hang themselves with a rope hung from the ceiling of their houses. And taking the meaning of the word 'Sama' as the heaven, it…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thus have We sent it down, as signs manifest, and that verily God guideth whomsoever He intendeth. Indeed, availing of the guidance from God is also God's grace which is granted to whomsoever He pleases.The prophecy about the continuance of the Divine help to the Holy Prophet against the infidels is itself a clear sign by which many were guided. (A.P).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who believe and those who are Jews and the Sabaeans and the Christians and the (Magians. Refer to note on verse 9:29.) Magians (Zoroastrians) those who associate (The polytheists.) (other gods with God), verily, God will decide between them on the Day of Judgment; Verily God is witness over all things. The judgment about the Jews, the Sabians1, the Christians, the Magians and the polytheists who associate their fanciful gods, (i.e., their deities) with God, rests with God to be decided on the Day of Judgment. The believers in this life have only to be tolerant as long as there is no initiative of oppression or injustice or persecution against them. When there is unprovoked aggression it has to be duly met and the believers should not shirk their duty of defending the faith and the faithful, but…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Seest thou not that God (is He), unto Him prostrateth ('Sijdah' i.e. Prostration here means obedience – subservience. Pays obeisance – Adores.) whosoever is in the heavens and whosoever is in the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and animals, and many of the people; and many there are unto whom hath become due the chastisement; and whomsoever God abaseth, then there is none for him to honour; Verily God doeth whatever He willeth. (Sijdah (Prostration) Sunnah.) See 22:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These are the two disputants who dispute about their Lord; but for those who disbelieved, shall be cut off for them garments of fire; (and) shall be poured over their heads boiling water. Sahih Bukhari relates that Abu Dharr al-Ghifari related with an oath that this verse was revealed in the matter of the six persons, three of whom were disbelievers (1) Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, (2) Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, (3) al-Walid ibn Utbah, and the other three faithful ones (1) Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, (2) Ali ibn Abi Talib, (3) Ubaydah ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib. The three faithful ones were those who were the foremost in meeting the enemy defending the cause of truth.Of the three abovementioned enemies of Islam who had come to destroy Islam and the Holy Prophet, Hamzah aided by Ali killed Utbah, Ali single-handed killed…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the day ye shall behold it, every suckling mother shall forsake (Will be so much perplexed.) her suckling babe; and every pregnant female shall drop her load, (The child in the womb.) and thou shalt behold the people (as) intoxicated; But the wrath of God will be (so) terrible. The matter pictures the terror and awe the hour will create in the minds of the disbelievers and the sinners.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: With it shall be melted what is in their bellies and (their) skins (as well). See 22:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And for them are (Hooked rods of iron.) maces of iron. See 22:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Every time they will intend to go forth from (Grief.) it, from the very anguish, back shall they be turned into it: and (it will be said unto them) "Taste ye the torment of the burning (fire)." See 22:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, God will admit those who believe and do good deeds, into gardens 'neath which flow rivers, adorned shall they be therein with bracelets of gold and with pearls; and their raiment therein shall be of silk. See 22:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For they (in this life) are guided unto goodly words, and they are guided unto the path of the Praised One. See 22:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who disbelieve and obstruct (people) from the way of God and from the Sacred Mosque (Masjid-al-Haram) which We have made alike; for the dweller therein as well as the stranger; and whoever doth intend to wrong (Compare this to the plot against the Holy Imam Husayn on account of which he had to leave the place without performing Hajj.) therein unjustly, We will make him taste of a grievous chastisement. The Mosque around Ka'ba is hereby declared the Sanctuary. None shall even annoy anyone therein. It is said entry into Mecca, not clad in the pilgrim's robes, is also an act of injustice. In all other places, the mere intention of committing any evil until the evil is not actually committed, is not recorded, but in Mecca, even an evil intention is a sin and it is recorded.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (remember O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) when We fixed for Abraham the place for the House, (saying): "Associate thou not with Me aught, and cleanse My House for those who make the circuits and stand in prayer, and bow and prostrate themselves (unto Me)" A particular site was pointed to Abraham through the revelation from God and he was commanded to raise the edifice of a House of Worship, exclusively to the Only True God. By the address to Abraham not to associate any one with God, is meant the people. The instruction to clean it is the declaration of the place already being the Sanctuary dedicated for the adoration of the All-Pure Lord of the Universe.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And proclaim thou unto the people the Pilgrimage (Hajj)! They will come unto thee on foot and on lean camel, coming from every remote (high) way. When Abraham and his son Ishmael had completed the erection of the Ka'ba, Abraham was commanded by God to sound a Call to the people to come over to the House of God for Pilgrimage. Abraham submitted that how could his voice from the solitary place in the wilderness in the desert reach the ears of all men of the world? Abraham was informed that the question of his call being heard by the people of the world was God's concern. It is said that Abraham got over the mountain Abu Qubayis and gave the Call and the sound of it reached all those who were destined to make the pilgrimage, including those who…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That they may witness the advantages unto them, and mention the name of God during the appointed days over what He hath provided them of the cattle quadrupeds (as sustenance) then eat of them and feed the needy the poor. Advantages connected with Hajj referred to here are of various kinds - the Secular or the Material as well as the Religious or the Spiritual. By the mutual contact with the other members of the brotherhood in faith, from the different parts of the world, one can improve his trade as well as his knowledge of the men and matters in the other countries and climes, and also improve the strength of his faith in God and imbibe further godliness by his presenting himself at the place and taking part in the acts of special devotion to the Lord and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then let them get cleansed and smarten themselves and fulfil their vows, and let them circuit the Ancient House (the Ka'ba). Then clean the body of the superfluous growth of the unnecessary hair and nails (which is not allowed during the state 'Ihram' or the dedication to pilgrimage) and clean the body thoroughly of the dirt.The Ka'ba is called the Oldest or the most Ancient House. It was known as such throughout the land with this name indicating its established antiquity.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And among the people there is he who disputeth about God without knowledge, and followeth every rebellious Satan, The word 'Shaytan', i.e., Devil, need not always refer to any spirit. 'Shayatin', i.e., devils are of two kinds - 'Shayatin al-Ins', i.e., devils among men and the 'Shayatin al-Jinn', i.e., the devils among the spirits. Here in this verse men are warned against two things: (1) Disputing about God without the necessary knowledge, (2) Blindly following those who have rebelled against God and godliness. This is the case with most people that they dispute about the truth without its knowledge and they, blindly follow their ancestral belief and traditions, and they identify themselves with the leaders of their fanciful belief and defend them however wicked they may be in their conduct and false in their claims. Those who annoy and hurt…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That (shall be so); and whoever respecteth the sacred ordinances of God, it is best for him with his Lord; And the cattle are made lawful unto you, save that which is (already) specified unto you, (Go not near it.) shun ye therefore, the pollution of the idols; and shun (According to the Holy Ahl al-Bayt 'Vain Words' includes any utterances disapproved by God.) vain words. 'Hurmat' stands for the sacred laws, i.e., the rites prescribed by God - Shunning the abomination or the uncleanliness or the pollution of the idols, i.e., of polytheism. The word 'Zawr' has several meanings which include falsehood and false utterances like the musical expression of vain ideas and false emotions. To defend their passion for the entertainment by music, people go into unnecessary debates saying that music has not been forbidden in the Holy…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Being upright for God, not associating (anything) with Him; whosoever associateth with God, is like that which hath fallen from heaven and (a vulture) bird snatched it away or the wind wafted it to a distant abyss. The one who falls or deviates from the correct faith in the Only True God, has been aptly compared to the one who falls from heaven and is attracted by the false objects of worship, (i.e., the false deities) such a man is compared to his being picked up in the air by the birds of prey. The belief in false gods has no permanence, hence the faith of the man gets gradually adulterated, i.e., shattered like the victim in the clutches of a bird of prey is torn to pieces and the gush of some violent wind, (i.e., a further temptation of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That (shall be so); And whoever respecteth the signs of God verily it is (the reflection) of the piety of the hearts. 'Sha'a'ir', i.e., symbols or signs which indicate a thing to belong to a person or a nation, like the banner of a king or the flag of a nation. Even the mounds of Safa and Marwa have been called as the Signs of God1 and in verse 22:36 even the camels of sacrifice are called 'Sha'a'ir Allah', i.e., the Signs of God. It is clearly given that honouring or holding in respect and regard anything which helps the remembrance of God, with the purity of heart and without any idea or intention of worshipping it, is termed as the sincere piety. The particular reference here is to the rites connected with Pilgrimage.The Shiah, hold the symbol or the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For you therein are benefits till a fixed time, and the place of their sacrifice is the Ancient House, (The Ka'ba). The Old or the Ancient House refers to the Ka'ba.1The most appropriate opinion about 'Fiha' therein - is that it refers to the Divine Signs and Rites concerning the pilgrimage - which includes sacrifice also. These advantages continue to a limited time and the end of them is the Ancient House and it is wrong to think that the pronoun in 'Fiha' and 'Mahalluha' refers to sacrifice only. Because the place of sacrifice for Hajj is not the House but Mina. But it is true that all the rites of pilgrimage end with the last circuit round the Ka'ba. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Unto every people We have prescribed a rite (of devotion) that they may mention the name of God on what He hath provided them of the cattle quadrupeds, (as their sustenance) so your God is One God, so unto Him submit ye (all) yourselves; and thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) give glad tidings unto the humble ones, Sacrifice in some form or other existed in the various other religions of old, but the sacrifice prescribed in Islam has a deeper meaning with a higher object applicable to the practical life of the believer in God. Sacrifices in the other creeds are only means to appease the anger of some imaginary deity and to escape the wrath or the dread of some gods. The sacrifice prescribed in Islam carries quite a different significance, i.e., the dedication of the self of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Who, when God is mentioned, get thrilled their hearts (with awe for His Glory); and the steadfast on what befalleth them, and the establishers of prayer and of what We have provided them with they spend (benevolently). This verse describes the qualities of the 'Mukhbitin' (i.e., the humble ones). They are not those who make mere verbal profession of the faith but translate it into their daily life. They are the ones that the mention of God makes their heart filled with the awe for His Glory and their hearts get further steeled with the strength of their faith in the guardianship or the Authority of God and that nothing but His Will prevails. Hence, they are always patient under every kind of trying circumstances.1 They are always mindful of the Lord and prayerful to Him. And whatever God has…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the camels (of sacrifice) We have made them for you among the signs of God, for you in them is good; so mention the name of God on them (when they are drawn) in rows (to be sacrificed); and when fall they down (sacrificed), on their sides, eat of them and feed the contented (poor ones) and the beggar; thus have We subjugated them unto you that happly ye may give thanks. About 'Sha'a'ir Allah' - See verses 2:158, 5:2.In charity, preference is commanded to be given to the contented and to those who, though being in need, do not beg but receive gifts with grace and gratitude. Thus Islam does not appreciate open begging forfeiting one's self-respect and personal dignity.1The Sixth Holy Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq interprets 'Qani'' as one satisfied with what he is given, and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Never doth reach God their flesh nor their blood, but reacheth God the piety on your part; Thus hath He subjugated them unto you that ye might pronounce the greatness of God for what He hath guided you aright; and thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) give glad tidings unto the doers of good. See note on verse 22:34 above. The opening words of this verse lay bare the spirit in which the sacrifice of the animal prescribed by Islam, should be offered. It must be in the spirit explained in verse 6:163. Good news is given to those who do good in this life to benefit the others.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, God doth ward off (the mischief of infidels) from those who believe; Verily, God loveth not any of the unfaithful, ungrateful (ones). This is a guarantee from God to defend the faithful against the evil from their enemies. When the heathens of Mecca, inflicted upon the early converts to Islam in Mecca, all sorts of unbearable miseries and tortures, the people sought the permission of the Holy Prophet to fight their enemies. The permission was deferred until the Muslims were settled in Medina when the next verse was revealed - to fight only in defence against the unprovoked attacks from the enemies.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Permission (To the believers.) (to fight) is given unto those upon whom war is made for they have been op pressed, and verily, to help them, God is Most Potent, Note the reason given in this verse for the permission granted to fight the enemy.This is the first instruction revealed concerning 'Jihad' and the reference to the believers being driven out of their homes, may refer to the migration to Abyssinia or to Medina. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Against him is decreed that whosoever taketh him as his friend, then verily shall he beguile him and lead him unto the torment of the burning fire. Refers to the fate of those who follow the Devil, i.e., the devilish instigations and the devilish characters - i.e., the satans among men and the devilish spirits.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who have been expelled from their homes unjustly save that they say: "Our Lord is God!" And had repelled not God some people by others, verily had been pulled down the cloisters (Monasteries.) and the churches and the synagogues and the mosques in which is God's name is much mentioned; and verily God will help him who helpeth Him (His cause); for verily God is Strong, Mighty. Note see verse 2:251. David was asked to fight against the Philistines to suppress mischief and to defend the people against their mischievous and aggressive enemy. Here the question involved was the very life and death of the Muslims and the total destruction of their faith and their being unjustly driven out of their homes in their very native town. What would have happened if God had not permitted the fight as…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those, if We establish them in the earth, will establish prayer and pay the poor-rate and enjoin good and forbid evil; and unto God (alone) is the sequel of (all) affairs, This verse is said to refer to the Last Holy Imam being given the authority and dominion over the earth - For establishing prayer, dispensing charity - enjoining good and forbidding evil.1Indicates that the Divine help is for the ultimate success of the truth against falsehood - as otherwise the temporary success mostly is of the other side as indicated in verse 22:44. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they belie thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) then indeed have belied (Belied the prophets who were sent to them.) before thee the people of Noah and 'Ad and Thamud (the prophets sent unto them), If the Holy Prophet was accused of imposture, it was nothing new, for the other apostles of God in the past, also were held as such and were similarly ridiculed. For the references to what happened to the different people of the other apostles of God See: Noah - 7:64, Hud - 7:66, The Apostle of the Thamud - 7:76, Abraham - 21:55, Lot - 7:82, Shu'ayb - 7:85, The Companions of the Wood - 15:78 and Moses - 2:49 - 2:61.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot See 22:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the dwellers of Midian, and was (also) belied Moses, but gave I respite unto the disbelievers, then I did seize them, and how (severe) was My (wrathful) rejection. See 22:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So how many of towns We did destroy while they (Verb in Plural is used here referring to many towns - in Arabic for plural verb in sing. fem. gen. is used.) were un just, and (their walls) have fallen down over their roofs, and (how many a) well abandoned and (even) lofty castles (ruined) See 22:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Have not they travelled in the earth that they should have hearts to understand them with, or ears to hear them with? for verily blind are not the eyes but blind are the hearts which are in the breasts. So that by seeing the fate of those who disbelieved in God and disobeyed His Apostles, the people might realise the truth at their heart and their ears might hear the admonition through the miserable and the pathetic sight of the ruins present there. It is said that every individual has got two kinds of eyes, ears, tongue and hands (i.e., touch) i.e., the external and internal. When God wants to guide a man or a woman, his or her heart is opened to the insight to probe through the manifest or the apparent, to the hidden or the latent,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Hajj:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
