item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ikhlaas:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: ''He, God, is ONE (alone) The Jews asked the Holy Prophet to describe the identity or to relate the genealogy of God and the Messenger Angel brought this Surah.There is a vast difference between the two Arabic words ''Ahad' and 'Wahid' both commonly thought to mean Oneness. To indicate the Unity of God, it is said in this verse that God is 'Ahad' i.e., One, One in the sense of the Absolute Oneness of His Essential Existence, not in the numerical sense of the numeral which has its second and third but the One which has no second of it. The expression one, is in the sense of being the ONLY in conceiving Whose existence all the faculties of the human intellect are helpless. He is such a one that even His attributes are His Essence and not separate…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ikhlaas:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God, the Needless (Perfect - the compact - independent- on Whom all depend. See the note.) 'Samad', i.e., independent of any one - All perfect - The One to Whom recourse is made by everything Eternal for its needs, both for existence and for perfection. The One who needs no subsistence of any kind – Self existing to understand Whose existence every mind is drowned in marvel and wonder. Nothing is hidden from His all-enveloping Knowledge - Is not accommodable in anything not even in intellect, Infinite in all aspects of the existence and attributes.In fact, the names or the attributes mentioned to describe His existence or its nature, are unconveyable in their fullness hence cannot be translated to give the correct or the fullest sense or the meaning of the terms.All the meanings attached to this term 'Samad' are…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ikhlaas:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He begetteth not, nor is He Begotten Nothing has come out of Him, i.e., He has not begotten any issue. There is no son or daughter born of Him. To assign a son or a daughter to Him, is the greatest blasphemy. Nor is He born of any other being. There is no match or equal to Him in any aspect, in any meaning or in any sense of any of the divine qualities. To assign any wife or mate to Him is a gross blasphemy against His All-Divine Being.Since man is a limited being and he with his inherent limitations cannot correctly conceive of things unknown to him but through some examples in the terms used for the things physical, certain terms have to be helplessly used, otherwise the essence or the qualities of God are beyond any description…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Ikhlaas:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And there is none like unto Him See 112:3

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When the heavens cleave asunder (Refer to: 84:1.) Here is another Surah about the happening of the Day of Judgment. It can be easily imagined how important and essential is for man, the belief in the Day of Judgment and how much he must fear the Day of Requital and how much he must be concerned about his getting ready for the day before the respite given to him in this life comes to an end or before death, which comes and often times overtakes unawares.The first four verses relate the events of the dawn of the Day of Judgment1. The collective meaning of all these events will be that the Day of the Final Judgment will begin with the total destruction of the present physical world which we See and its disappearance, giving place to a new state of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: While verily over you are posted the Watchers (Refer to: 50:18.) See 82:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Recorders Honourable (Refer to: 50:18.) See 82:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Know they whatever ye do (Refer to: 50:18.) See 82:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, the righteous shall be amidst bounteous bliss See 82:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily the wicked shall be in the flaming fire See 82:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They shall be committed to it on the Day of Judgment See 82:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nor they shall themselves be absent from it See 82:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what will make thee know what the Day of Judgment shall be? See 82:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then what maketh thee know what the Day of Judgment is? See 82:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It is) The day on which soul shall own not anything (helpful) for another soul; and the Command Supreme that day shall be God's (alone) No soul has the least power to anything for or against the other. The law of strict equity, i.e., of cause and effect for the individual or the personal responsibility, will be fully enforced as the decreed order of the day1. The whole mastery of the day will rest in God's will Who at His own independent choice, would grant anyone of His own chosen beloved ones to intercede on behalf of anyone they please and this will be in recompense to their perfect surrender to the Lord's will during their life on earth and their suffering persecution, death, and destruction in God's way - viz. the Apostles of God, their divinely chosen deputies, the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And When the stars (Refer to: 81:1 - 81:14.) disperse (Scatter.) Note that in 81:2 for the stars the name 'Nojoom' is used, and verb used there is 'Inkadu' i.e., getting covered with darkness, i.e., losing their lustre and here for stars the name 'Kawakib' is used, and the verb used is 'Intasarat', i.e., getting scattered. The state of the change meant there, was as to what will have happened to the native property or the function of the stars and here is meant the disturbance which their usual position will suffer, i.e., in the symmetry, i.e., the arrangement in the great constellations.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And When the seas (Refer to: 81:6.) be comingled When all kinds of the barriers withholding the rivers and the seas1, natural as well as artificial, preventing the great waters from overflowing, will go. The rivers and seas will burst forth and boil. The fresh and the saltish waters will be mixed, and the flood will cover the whole globe.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when the graves be overturned (to be vacated) See 82:3

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then shall every soul know (Refer to: 81:14.) what it hath sent forth and left behind (Refer to: 81:1 - 81:14, 99:6.) Note, in 81:14 is said that man will know what he has put forward, i.e., what provision of good and evil deeds he has done and what a recompense for his own deeds are in store for him and here there are two verbs used, i.e., what he has sent before and what he left over behind him, i.e., what good or evil he himself committed during his life time and what arrangements or what consequences his life created for good and evil to be done after him on his behalf. It might mean also what spiritual prospects he earned and what physical things he prided over he left behind.This clearly indicates that it is man's individual responsibility…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' thou man! What hath beguiled thee from thy Lord, the Most Gracious One Note that God has referred to Himself with His attribute 'Kareem', i.e., the Most Charitable, the Most Noble, the Most Gracious. It is this divine attribute of God that Satan uses to instigate man to sin, encouraging him saying that God is 'Kareem'. He will surely pardon hence why not enjoy life even with the evils in it. Man is warned not to be beguiled by such rebellious belief or confidence in God's grace and mercy.Some say that it is an indirect guidance to man, i.e., man is taught that when he fails in his duties, i.e., if he involved in sins and if he is questioned by God ''What made thee rebel against My authority?" Then man may say ''Thy great charitable disposition my Lord"…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (He) Who created thee, and fashioned (Gave shape.) thee and (gave thee a body) justly proportioned (Symmetrical.) Reference to God's creative authority over man and His grace in giving man the well-formed perfect body with harmoniously active organism which He did as a grace, of His own accord and not in return for any obligation from anyone. It will be quite sufficient if man only reflects on the great gifts he has received from the Great Author of his very existence with the wonderful native endowments, physical, mental and spiritual1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In whatsoever form He willeth He casteth (Refer to: 6:2, 87:2.) thee 'Surat', i.e., shape personality with the gifts of the physical strength and the mental faculties.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Infitaar:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! but ye belie the Reckoning See 82:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Surely did come over Man to pass an occasion of time when he was nothing, mentioned of? The literal meaning of this Verse is that surely there was a time for man when he was not mentioned by anyone, i.e., when he was only a drop of a life-germ.According to the holy Ahl Al-Bayt, the one referred to here, is Ali Ibn Abu Talib and the question is an assertion to say that there was no time when Ali was not in existence in the knowledge of God, or his name was not mentioned in the heavens. The Holy Prophet says that when he visited heavens during the Ascension (Mi'raj) he found on the gate of the heaven written in clear letters - "There is no God but God, Muhammad is His Apostle and Ali the brother of the Apostle…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, we dread from our Lord, a stern day of distress See 76:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So will God guard them from the evil of that day and cause them to meet freshness and pleasure (Refer to Verses 75:22; 75:23. Note: All the references to the heavenly pleasures wherever mentioned i.e. in this sura and elsewhere in the Qur'an all are figurative. (AP).) The godly ones for whom this grace of the Lord is meant are the holy Ahl Al-Bayt and the others would naturally earn it according to the degree of their success in following their footsteps. Verse 11 refers to their being safe from dreadful events of the judgment1.Verse 11 refers to the reward they will receive from the Lord for their patience and endurance in the face of persecution, as well as for their willing surrender of all they have, offering their lives as martyrs in the service of the Lord2.About the blissful…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall recompense them, for what they endured with patience, with garden (to abide) and silk (to wear) All the references to the heavenly pleasures mentioned in this Sura and elsewhere are figurative. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Reclining therein on exalted couches (Refer to Verses 18:31, 56:15.) , they shall find not therein (the excessive heat of) the sun, nor any (intense) cold See 76:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And close low over them (shall be) its shades, and the clustered fruits (Refer to Verses 56:20; 56:21.) thereof (shall be) bowing down (in easy reach) When there will be neither the sun nor the moon the question of the need for any shade does not at all arise, but the illustration is just to give an understanding of the state there in heaven in terms of our life in this world, which is only figurative1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall pass round among them vessels of silver and goblets (Refer to Verses 43:71; 56:18.) of crystal (glass) About the enjoyment, they will have, refer to Verse 43:71. The ideal accommodation in the mention of the metal and the stuff of which the vessels will be, is a figurative indication of the rarity and the preciousness and the splendour of the things.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Bright as glass, made of silver; measure they to a well-measure (As desired.) See note on Verse 15 above. About the kind of drink they will have, refer to Verses 5 and 6 above. Zanjabil or Ginger is an ingredient which gives warmth to the body and zest to the taste. It may be a new kind of drink of a taste and flavour unknown to us in this life. 'Zanjabil' also is a figurative expression.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they shall be supplied with the drink therein of a cup tempered with 'Zanjabil' (ginger) (Flavour or strength.) See 76:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It is the water of) a spring therein named 'Salsabeel' (The Soft Flowing) It is the name of a spring in heaven specially promised to the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt who are praised in this Sura.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And around them in their service shall be boys (graced) with eternal youth (Refer to Verses 56:17; 52:24.) ; when thou seest them thou wilt deem them as pearls scattered about See 76:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily We created man from a (small insignificant) life drop (Refer to Verses 80:19, 86:6.) of inter-mingled life germ (of both sexes); in order that We put him to trial, so We endowed him with hearing, seeing (Made hearer & seen.) ! It is known that a human child starts its response first to sounds and then to light or vision.Ibtila - Lit. trial and wherever in Qur'an it has been used in connection with God it means to give chance to the development of the latent aptitude. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when thou seest there, thou shalt see bounties (abundant) and a kingdom magnificent The Holy Ahl Al-Bayt have been given a kingdom which in the words of the Almighty is called 'Great.' Thus the kingdom or the authority given to them in the heavens cannot be fully assessed or imagined by the mortals in this physical life.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Upon them shall be robes of fine green silk and rich brocade, and they shall be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord give them to drink a drink, pure (and wholesome) (Refer to Verse 18:31.) Regarding adornments in store for the holy ones, refer to Verse 18:31. The idea is of the rarity and the preciousness of the articles. A figure in terms of the things in this world.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Saying unto them) "Verily this is unto you a recompense, and your endeavour is accepted (with appreciation)" The address is in clear words to the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt, a reward for their endeavour in the way of the Lord, i.e., for their piety and their selfless life.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, We ourselves have sent down unto thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) the Qur'an, in a proper descension The Holy Qur'an was revealed in parts, i.e., in Verses and chapters one after another to facilitate the gradual development of the faith and the study of its articles of belief and practice by the people.This Verse hints that the presentation of the facts of the heavenly and the spiritual spheres to a human being will always be in revealed terms graspable by mankind. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Await then with patience the command of thy Lord, and obey not from among them a sinner or an ungrateful one See 76:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And remember (Glorify or hallow.) thou the name of thy Lord at morn and at even See 76:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And during a part of the night prostrate thou in obeisance unto Him and celebrate His praise long night through Prayer in the dead of the night has its own facility for concentration and meditation and is also of special spiritual effect on the mind. To be in communion with the Lord when the world around is enjoying rest and when the quiet of the night helps the mind to concentrate, the prayer in such hours is of special value and worth, and gets easily effective.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, these (people) love the fleeting present (The immediate gain of this world. Refer to Verses 21:37; 75:20; 75:21.) , and (neglect) putting away behind them the Day (which shall be) hard People, particularly the disbelievers, are always inclined to avail of the immediate enjoyment in this life which are only passing shows and neglect the hereafter though it is of a permanent duration1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We Ourselves created them and made them strong in their parts, and when We will, with the like of them, will We replace them (Refer to Verses 47:38; 56:61; 56:62.) This may mean also the change of form in conformity with Verses 56:61; 56:62 or it may mean to replace you with some other generation in conformity with 47:38. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily this is a Reminder, so whosoever pleaseth, taketh unto his Lord the (Right) way See 76:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, have We shown him (Man.) the (Right) way, be he grateful or ungrateful (Refer to Verse 90:10.) ! The Divine guidance is there for all. The choice of availing it thankfully or not availing it thanklessly, is left to each individual human being.This asserts man's responsibility for his destiny. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And ye desire not save what God desireth; Verily God is All-Knowing, the All-Wise This is the exclusive quality of the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt which God wants to please them with His acknowledgement of it in open words.The whole of this chapter is an open acknowledgment of the Lord, of the unique excellence of the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt whom He Himself had purified to the limits of purification.This confirms what is said in Verse 74:55 and Verse 74:56. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He admitteth whosoever He willeth into His mercy; and (as for) the unjust ones, He hath prepared for them a painful chastisement See 76:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily have We prepared for the disbelievers chains, and shackles and a flaming fire! See 76:3

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, the righteous ones shall drink of a cup tempered at the fountain 'Kafoor' (Camphor)! 'Kaafoor', i.e., Camphor - either it is the name of a spring in the heaven, or it means a special taste. Some commentators interpret the word 'Kafoor' taking the root word 'Kafr' to cover meaning one who drinks of that water, his thirst for the fulfilment of all sorts of carnal passions is quenched for ever as all poisonous matter is antidoted by Camphor.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The fountain whereof shall wherever drink the servants (Sincere devotee – the pious.) of God, they shall cause it to flow a desirable (Whenever they desire to have it.) flow The scholars of both the Shia and Sunni schools are unanimous in their statement that these Verses and even the whole of the chapter was revealed in praise of the holy Ahl Al-Bayt. The occasion for the revelation of this Sura is said to be that once Hasan and Husayn the two grandsons of the Holy Prophet were ill, and the Holy Prophet went to his daughter's house to enquire about the health of the children - and suggested to Ali to make a vow of fast for three days at the recovery of the children. Accordingly, as the children recovered, Ali, Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn, fasted. Fatimah prepared five…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They who (The Ahl Al-Bayt.) fulfil their vows, and fear the day the woe of which stretcheth far and wide See 76:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (while needing it for themselves) they give away food, out of love for Him, to the poor and the orphan and the captive The inseparable pronoun 'Ha' in 'Hubbihi', i.e., Out of love - may refer to God when the phrase would be adverbial modifying Verse 'Yot'imoona' meaning out of love for him and it may refer to 'Ta'aam', i.e., food - then the phrase would be adjectival qualifying food meaning in spite of its being wanted for their own selves. This gets into conformity with Verse 3:92. However, both the interpretations are valid and convey the same significance. This Verse encourages the well treatment of a captive in the manner that a poor - an orphan is treated. Hence the killing, ill-treatment of captives cannot be said desirable in Islam1 (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Insaan:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Saying): "We feed you only for God's sake, we intend (Expect.) not of you any recompense, nor (even) thanks (thereof)!" This is what the godly ones mean and say when they feed anyone for, they do it just to please the Lord and never in the least with the least expectation of any return or to earn any praise or obligation from any one save God.It is a guidance for mankind as a whole as to what extent those who sincerely love God, should sacrifice their personal interest and how selfless any service in the way of the Lord should be. Charity should always be motivated by piety and righteousness and should be unpretentious.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When the heaven shall rend asunder (Refer to: 82:1.) Refers to what will happen to the sky at the dawn of the Day of Judgment, i.e., when the sky will be rent asunder - to manifest the state of reality.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And he who is given his Book (from) behind (Left Side, Refer to: 69:25.) his back The disbelievers and the wicked will have their hands tied at their back and hence they will be given their records from behind them. He would wish that he had not been given any record at all1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He shall invoke destruction The wicked would wish for death and annihilation once for all but they will be in a state which will be neither life nor death1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall be committed to the flaming fire See 84:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily he was joyous (In his life in the world before death.) among his people While in this life the wicked one was happy rejoicing and enjoying the pleasures of the world among his people, i.e., relatives and friends, without any regard to the pleasure or the displeasure of the Lord.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily he thought that never will he return (unto God) Man is led into the evil ways of life mostly of his self-complacence and self-conceit and getting himself intoxicated of the enjoyment of his carnal desires in his lower life, forgetting his personal responsibility and his accountability on his return to the Lord in the ultimate. He must remember the inevitability of his return to Him.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Yea! Verily his Lord was always vigilant of him Man forgets that the Lord is ever watchful of him for his motives as well as his deeds.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And I swear by the Glow of the sunset" (84:61) The beautiful and wonderful show of the radiance of the sun in the evening which is the work of nature.The note on this verse by a commentator1 is another example of a wishful distortion of the Qur'an narrowing its original significance to the rise and the fall of the Arabs in power. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (by) the night and what it enshroudeth Man's attention is drawn to the mystic functioning of the great and the wonderful phenomena of nature in the daily life in this world, the functioning of the wonderful organization of the universe being before man's eyes all the while he takes these great events of the life, to be so common and so easy that he does not think of ever pondering over the secret of the genetic factors in the functions of nature which every moment passes from one stage or state into another or regulated and controlled that the daily repetition is maintained with perfect success without the least failure.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (by) the moon when at her full See 84:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That ye shall certainly march (Ride.) from state to state See 84:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And it shall hearken unto its Lord, and (as) it ought to do! The heavens with their greatness, and limitless extent, only await the command of the Lord which shall be carried out.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But what then hath happened unto them that they believe not? With so much of the guidance from heaven through the wonderful manifestation of the Might, and the Wisdom and the Existence of God and so much of the exertion to bring home to man the Truth, through a long line of God's inspired men, His apostles, if man still fails to believe in the reality, it is naturally a matter of wonder and surprise.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when is recited unto them the Qur'an, they prostrate not in obeisance (Refer to: 7:206, 13:15, 22:77, 32:15.) ? The Prostration means respect, reverence and the humble submission to God1 - Prostration on the part of the reciters of this verse is only 'Sunnat', traditional, and not 'Wajib', i.e., compulsory.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! those who disbelieve belie (the Truth) It is said that when above verse 21 was revealed, the Holy Prophet went into prostration and the believers present there followed his example. The disbelievers got over the backs of the believers lying in prostration and standing on the heads began clapping their hands. It was then these verses were revealed.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And Verily God knoweth best what they hide (in their hearts) See 84:22

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So announce thou unto them the tidings of a painful chastisement! See 84:22

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Save those who believe and do good deeds, for them shall be a recompense unending (Refer to: 41:8.) See 84:22

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when the earth shall be stretched out (flattened) (Refer to: 71:26 or disintegrated.) The earth will be changed from its global form to a flat levelled plain.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall cast forth whatever is in it and becometh empty (Refer to: 99:1 - 99:2.) All the things - minerals, metals and the bodies of the innumerable generations buried in it, i.e., all its contents, will be thrown out, i.e., the earth will vanish with all its contents destroyed, and reduced to nothing.In this verse and 99:2 points out the time for the disintegration, i.e., when the earth's productive capacity gets exhausted, and this principle is applicable to all growing and evolutionary movement in every part and particle of the Universe. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And it shall hearken unto its Lord, and as it aught to do! See 84:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' man! Verily thou art in strive unto thy Lord, (with) a striving, and thus thou art meeting Him! The path of righteousness, i.e., the path of those who earnestly wish to get nearer to the Lord, is full of toil and misery. It is the godly ones that scorn and forego the pleasures of this life and choose the life of want and difficulties. Those who toil in the sincere hope of meeting the Lord, are assured of their success so that they may not fall victims to dejection and give up their quest for Him.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And he who is given his Book in his right hand. (Refer to: 17:71, 69:19.) Those who suffered, and yet led pure lives of faith and righteousness and suffered miseries in the way of the Lord 1and yet toiled continuously to earn His pleasure for which they avoided the pleasures of this life and chose for themselves and remained contented with the miseries and sufferings. They avoided evil in spite of its strong attractions and earned goodness at all costs.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Soon shall he be reckoned (with) an easy reckoning The reckoning will be affected without the least difficulty. The Holy Prophet said that he who has these three qualities shall meet a very easy accounting at the judgment. He said: -To provide the one who hath deprived thee of the legitimate due.Meet the one who shuns you.Pardon him who has been unkind to you.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Inshiqaaq:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And he shall return unto his people delighted To his people, i.e., to his kith and kin and the others spiritually on the same level with him without the restriction of the age, i.e., preceding or succeeding him in time.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Glory be to Him Who carried (Caused the journey.) His servant (Apostle Muhammad) by night from the Holy Mosque (of the Ka'ba) to the Farthest Mosque, which We have blessed its environment (Precincts – Neighbourhood.) that We may show unto him, of Our signs; Verily He, is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. Read verses 53:8 & 53:9.This verse relates about the Holy Prophet's Mi'raj, i.e., Ascension to meet God at His Very Seat (the Arsh) the Centre of His authority.'Masjid al-Haram,' i.e., the Mosque built around the Ka'ba and 'Masjid al-Aqsa,' i.e., the Farthest Mosque - The Mosque in heaven. This verse refers to the Holy Prophet's Ascension (Mi'raj). One night when the Holy Prophet was in one of the chambers of the Masjid al-Haram, i.e., Holy Mosque at Madina or in the house of Umm Hani - the Messenger Angel…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who believe not in the hereafter, We have prepared for them a painful torment. See 17:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:100 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: If ye own the treasures of the mercy of my Lord, (even) then will ye certainly withhold them for fear of spending; and man is ever (Owing to the lack of the power of reproduction of what is spent away.) niggardly. See 17:94

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:101 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We gave Moses nine clear signs (miracles); so ask the children of Israel when he came unto them, Pharaoh said unto him; "Verily I deem thee O' Moses one (Lost sense of reasoning.) bewitched" The following nine signs are given in the Old Testament:(1) Turning of water into blood, (2) Frogs, (3) Lice, (4) Flies, (5) The plague, (6) Hail, (7) Locusts, (8) Darkness, (9) Plague on the first born.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:102 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he (Moses.) Indeed, thou knowest that none hath sent these down save the Lord of the heavens and the earth (as) eye opening proofs; and I think thou O' Pharaoh is doomed to perdition. See 17:101

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:103 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And resolved he (Pharaoh.) to tare them away out of the land, so We drowned him and those with him, all together, See 17:101

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:104 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said We after that, unto the children of Israel: "Abide ye in peace in the land, but when cometh the later (Refer to verses 17:101 & 17:4 - 17:8.) promise, We shall bring you all rolled up (collected together)" See 17:101

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:105 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And with truth have We sent it down and with truth it hath come down; and We sent not thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) but as a Giver of glad tidings and as a Warner. See 17:101

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:106 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And it is Qur'an which We have apportioned it (Or made distinct.) so that thou mayest recite it unto the people with deliberation (by degrees), and We have sent it down, gradually in portions. See 17:101

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:107 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "Believe ye in it or believe ye not; Verily those who are (already) given (Refer to verse 29:46.) the knowledge from before it, when it is recited unto them they fall down on their faces prostrating in obeisance," See 17:101

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:108 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "Glorious is our Lord! verily the promise of our Lord was (a certainty) to be fulfilled." See 17:101

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:109 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they fall down on their faces weeping and it (the listening to the Qur'an) increaseth their humility. (Devotional humility.) After exposing the adamance of the contemporary infidels and comparing them to the repulsive attitude of Pharaoh and his people towards Moses and their ultimate destiny, God gives the utmost assurance of the truth of the Qur'an and the success of the Holy Prophet and thus gives the confidence to the Holy Prophet that whether they accept the truth or not, the people gifted with the knowledge1 will submit with utmost devotional humility to it. In support of this refer to verses 29:47 - 29:52. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And prayeth man for evil as he prayeth (As sincerely as he ought to pray in the manner for good.) for good; and man in ever hasty. This verse applies to the following occasions:When one is worried or angry against himself or his people in disgust, the individual starts cursing himself and his people in the same earnestness as he prays for good. If God only grants such prayers the individual will meet only perdition, which. But God by His mercy does not do it.Praying for immediate gains, neglecting the ultimate consequences.Praying for things not allowed in the same way that he prays for things allowed. This depicts the common aspects of these three tendencies in man. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:110 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "Call upon 'Allah' (God) or call upon (Refer to verses 25:60 & 20:8.) 'Rahman' (the Beneficent); whichever ye call upon, for Him (alone) are all the best names; and say thou not thy prayer too aloud, nor say it in too low a voice, but seek between these (extremes) a middle course." The Holy Prophet told Ali Ibn Abi Talib that the recitation of the last two verses of this chapter are a guarantee for my people against theft.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:111 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say thou: "(All) Praise is God's, Who hath not taken unto Him a son and Who hath not a partner in the kingdom, and there is not for Him any helper against any humility, and proclaim thou His Greatness magnifying (His Glory)." See 17:110

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We have made the night and the day two (of Our) signs, then cause We the sign of the night to pass away and have made We the sign of the day sight-giving that ye may seek grace from your Lord, and that ye may know the number and the count of the years; and every thing have We explained in detail. The mental tendency of haste in man is in resemblance with the sign of the night which passes away and the ultimate as the sign of the day.The sign of night is the moon which is not real in its radiation and whose phases are not constant, whereas the sign of day is sun the source of real light of its own - the phases of which are not changeable - and through which we regulate our…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And every man's destiny (Arabic 'Taa'ir' i.e., deeds wrought by the individual.) We have caused to cling to his neck; and We will bring forth unto him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find wide open. See 17:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It will be said unto him) "Read thou thy book; Sufficeth thine own self today, as a reckoner against thee." Every individual will have the record of his own deeds clung to his neck and they will be weighed in the balance of equity which never mistakes in the least1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whosoever getteth guided aright, verily he getteth guided aright for his ownself; and he who goeth astray, verily he goeth astray against his ownself; nor shall the bearer of a burden bear the burden of another; And We chastise not (any people) until We raise an apostle (among them) See 17:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when intend We to destroy a town, (first) send We Our commandment to its people who lead easy lives (to obey Us), and yet (when) they transgress (Disobey the Commands. Refer to verse 18:50.) in it, then proveth true against it, the (Then the decree of punishment is passed.) word so We destroy it to a complete destruction. See 17:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And how many have We destroyed of the peoples after Noah! and thy Lord is (Himself) sufficient (Sufficient Knower and Seer of the Sins, the hidden and manifest alike.) with regard to the sins of his servants, (for He is) the All-Aware, (Sufficient Knower and Seer of the Sins, the hidden and manifest alike.) the All-Seeing (Sufficient Knower and Seer of the Sins, the hidden and manifest alike.) . See 17:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whosoever intendeth this (fast hastening) immediate (life) We hasten unto him in it what We please for whomsoever We intend, then assign We unto him the hell; he shall enter it despised, driven away. See 17:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whosoever intendeth the hereafter and striveth for it a (sincere) striving and he is a believer, these, their striving shall be (recompensed fully) appreciated. See 17:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And gave We unto Moses the Book (Torah) and made it a guidance for the children of Israel, (saying) that "Take ye not other than Me (any one as) a guardian." After stating the Ascension, Qur'an makes a comparison with Moses, the way he received the Book from God on the mountain and the receiving of the highest knowledge including all that was given to all the previous Prophets at the highest level and both events are miracles if one is possible the other is also possible, i.e., the power which brings the Book to the mountain can take a person up into heaven. The object of both the events of the Revelation and the Ascension is the same - to make it known to the people that God is the Sole Authority to be depended on. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: All We do aid, these and (also) those out of the bounty of thy Lord; and the bounty of thy Lord is not confined. See 17:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Behold (thou) how We caused some of them excel the others; and surely the hereafter is much greater in respect of degrees and greater still in respect of excellence. See 17:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Associate not with God any other gods, lest thou sittest despised, neglected. See 17:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And commanded thy Lord hath that thou shalt worship not (any one) but Him, and goodness to parents; if either or both of them reach old age with thee, utter not unto them (even so much as) "Fie" nor chide them, and speak unto them a generous word. Note the rank Islam has given to obedience to parents, which is next only to God. The extent to which one has to regard his parents and obey them is peculiar only to Islam. None should even raise his voice higher than the voice of his parents - nor look towards them even eye to eye - nor walk in advance of them - nor address them with their names. Nothing shall be done to bring disrepute or blame on them from the people and if they be believers, the children should…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And lower unto them the wing of humility out of compassion, and say (Praying to God.) thou: "O' My Lord! Have mercy on them as they cherished me when I was little." See 17:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Your Lord knoweth best what is in yourselves (Your hearts.) ; if ye be righteous, then verily He is for the repentants Oft-Forgiving. See 17:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And give to the near of kin his due and to the needy and the wayfarer, and squander not (thy earnings) wastefully. See verses 8:41, 16:90, 17:26, 30:38, 59:7. Ibn Jarir reports that the Fourth Holy Imam Ali Ibn Husayn al-Zain al-Abidin asked a Syrian, "Hast thou read in the Chapter Bani-Israel in the Holy Qur'an. Give the near of kin his due?" He said, 'Yes'. Then the Holy Imam said: "We are the near of kin meant by the verse." Bazaz Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh relate on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that immediately as this verse was revealed the Holy Prophet called his daughter Fatimah and gifted the garden of Fadak. (D.M., M.F.A.).Besides the confirmation of the Ahl al-Bayt that this verse refers to the event of the Holy Prophet being ordered by…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the squanderers are the brethren of the satans; and Satan to his Lord is ever an ingrate. See 17:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If thou (helplessly) turn away from them (The kindred, the needy, the wayfarers.) seeking mercy from thy Lord which thou hopest for, then speak unto them (The kindred, the needy, the wayfarers.) (at- least) a kindly (Gentle - a word of ease.) word. See 17:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And cause thou not to shackle thy hand unto thy neck, nor stretch it forth to the maximum (limits of) stretching forth, lest thou shouldst (thereafter) sit down blamed, destituted. Neither be niggardly nor be wasting but be moderate in even charity, neither abstain from giving any thing at all to any one, nor give away everything and put thyself in need and misery.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (O' ye!) The offspring of those (The faithful issues of Noah and the righteous members of his family.) whom We bore with Noah (in the Ark); Verily, he (Noah) was a grateful servant. See 17:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily thy Lord extendeth (Maketh plenty.) the sustenance for whomsoever He willeth and measureth (Restricteth.) it He (to a just measure); Verily He is, of His servants ever Fully- Aware, All-Seeing. See 17:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And kill ye not your children for fear of want; (Compare this to the modern un-natural Family Planning.) We sustain them and yourselves (too); Verily killing them is a great sin. The people used to kill their children. Particularly a female issue was considered to be a disgraceful encumbrance to the parents. People feared their inability to provide themselves with the necessary subsistence. This admonition was required not only in the days of the ignorance of the Arabs but even today its need is more than it had ever been, for the tendency to decrease the birth-rate by all unnatural devices of birth-control is ever on the increase under the modern civilization with highly deceptive technical terms viz. Family Planning etc.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And approach ye not adultery, (Refer to verse 6:151. Refer to note on verse 17:23.) Verily, it is a shameful act, and an evil way (opening to many other evils) This is an evil which is ever on the increase under the modern civilization. Islam not only forbids adultery but forbids even going near it, i.e., to avoid all opportunities for it, like co-education, clubs, associations of mixed gathering of the sexes, conducting of dances and such demoralising activities as dancing and singing in the name of Social and Benefit Performances etc.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And kill ye not any one whom God hath forbidden but for a just cause; and whoever is slain unjustly, then indeed have We given his heir the authority, but he shall not be extravagant (Exceed the limits of justice.) in slaying; Verily he is aided (by God). The administrators of the Islamic law should help the heir of the murdered one in bringing the murderer to account for the crime. None, not even the heir should take the law in his own hands nor the punishment should exceed the limits of the crime. When Abdur Rahman Ibn Muljim the assassin of Amirul-Momineen Ali Ibn Abi Talib was brought before the Holy Imam whom Abdur Rahman had struck with his poisoned sword, the Holy Imam lying mortally wounded commanded that none should even tease Abdur Rahman. The Holy Imam commanded…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And approach ye not the property of an orphan save in a way which is good until he attaineth his maturity and fulfil ye the promise; Verily (every) promise shall be questioned about. See 17:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And give ye full measure when ye measure out (anything) and weigh ye with a correct balance; This is good and the fairest in the end. See 17:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And pursue thou not that which thou hast not the know ledge of; Verily, the hearing and the sight and the heart, all these shall be questioned about it. If people only abide by this injunction, much of the evils of vain talk among men about the affairs of the others would end and consequently many of the mutual ill-feelings created by idle gossip and uninformed or ill-informed narratives about the character and the conduct of the others, would be wiped out and instead of the evils of the ill-feelings thus created, goodness and harmony would reign among the people.On the Day of Judgment every organ or every part of the body of every man and woman would be questioned as to how it was used during the life on earth. A man reported to the Sixth Holy Imam Jafar…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And walk thou not on the earth exultingly; for thou (by thy insolence) canst not rend the earth nor reach (the heights of) the mountains in stretching (thyself). Note what minute details of ethics and good behaviour and gentle conduct on the part of the believers in God are stressed upon. How unpardonable a crime and a blasphemy it would be to call Islam which is the religion of peace, love and etiquette, as the faith of aggression and cruelty. The learned non-Muslims who come across the details of the ethical values to which Islam binds the Muslims and what it has actually prescribed, automatically curse the falsehood uttered against God's prescribed faith and readily embrace it.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: All this, the evil of it, with thy Lord is hateful. See 17:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This of what thy Lord hath revealed unto thee of wisdom; and set not with God any other god lest thou be cast into the hell, blamed and cast away. See 17:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (Refer to verse 5:78.) We had (expressly) declared unto the children of Israel (a warning) in the Book (Torah saying): "Certainly ye will make mischief in the land twice, (Refer to verse 5:78.) and certainly will ye be elated with great arrogance." Twice, i.e., Once slaying the Apostle Usha and disobeying the Apostle Ermia. Again, slaying the Apostle Yahya (John) and plotting to kill Jesus.1Those of the Israelites who disbelieved their apostles were cursed by David and Jesus and owing to the transgression of the Israelites, Jerusalem was destroyed once by the Babylonians and again by the Romans. For warnings from Jesus see Math. 23/38 and Luke 21/24 and the Psalms are also full of the warnings. Regarding the repeated destruction which Jerusalem suffered.2

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! has then your Lord preferred giving you sons, and taken (for Himself) (This refers to the peoples holding angels as the daughters of God and worshipping them as deities.) daughters, from (among) the angels? Verily, ye utter an awful saying. See 17:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed have We displayed (the warnings) in this Qur'an that they might take heed; but it addeth not to them save aversion (against the truth). The more the truth was preached to the disbelievers, the more did they become adamant in their disbelief and wickedness1.This is in sequence to the previous verses. The purpose of the display and the repetition of the signs and the arguments of the Qur'an is to make people display their reaction to the signs, either to be mindful or be averse to them. But greater are in numbers those who are averse than those who are benefited by them. In any case the purpose of display is achieved as pointed out in verse 17:20. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) If there were with Him (any) other gods (also) as they say, then certainly they would have been able to seek against the Lord of the 'Arsh' (The Throne of Supreme Power and Authority.) a way. If the idols had really been gods as they are falsely taken and worshipped, they would have found their way to heaven.Seeking the way to the 'Arsh' may be in the endeavour to get nearer to the god of the gods as some section of the pagans would believe; or it may mean that sharing in godhead they would seek to compete God in authority. In both cases it means that the concept of another god or gods being with the One True God makes all of them limited in power and subject to conflict. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Glory be to Him and Exalted is He far above from what they say (The concepts about Him. Refer to previous verse, 17:42.) He is the High, and the Great. See 17:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Celebrate His glory the seven heavens and the earth, and (all) those in them; and there is not any thing but it glorifieth Him, but ye understand not their glorification; Verily, He is the Forbearing, the Oft-Forgiving. The declaration of God's glory need not be in words uttered by any tongue. The greater and the fuller declaration of God's glory is in the undisturbed continuous working of His will, with perfect harmony.1 Only the people do not ponder over the mysteries of the creation and the wonderful working of the Universe in perfect harmony in obedience to the Law of the Lord which is itself the most eloquent declaration of the Lord Creator of the whole organism of the Universe, being free from every imperfection.Most commentators generally interpret this passage as to refer to the absolute submissiveness of every part…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) recitest the Qur'an We set between thee and those who believe not in the hereafter a hidden veil, This is a reference to the adamant aversion on the part of the disbelievers against the repeated preachings, inviting them to the truth. Once the Holy Prophet was in the house of Abu Bakr when the wife of Abu Lahab went there in search of him with a stick in her hand to strike him with it. She entered the house and though the Holy Prophet was just in front of her, she could not see him and she went on enquiring about him. The Holy Prophet told Abu Bakr to say that he was in the house and to herself find him out. The woman in angry mood told Abu Bakr not to cut jokes…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We have set on their hearts coverings lest they should understand it (the Qur'an) and in their ears a heaviness and when thou mentionest thy Lord alone, in (reciting) the Qur'an, turn they their backs in aversion. See 17:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We know best what they hearken, when they hearken unto thee, and when they are (Talking secretly to each other.) whispering secretly apart, when say the unjust (unto the believers): "Ye follow none but a man bewitched." See 17:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Behold thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) what similitudes they coin for thee! for they have gone (so far) astray (that) they can not find the way (to truth). Realising the fascinating force of his behaviour, Qur'an explains it in terms which may justify their aversion to it. Sometimes they used to say that the Holy Prophet was mad and an enchanter and sometimes an enchanted one. All these terms would not stand before the lofty and the sublime teachings and the force of Qur'an or the excellence of the character of the Holy Prophet. A mad enchanter, or an enchanted one, could not bring such a work. They themselves felt helpless - to which the verse refers.The opponents talking of such nonsense is not surprising. The surprise is that some who professed to be Muslims should fabricate traditions that the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "What! when we become (mere) bones and a decayed dust, shall we (even) then in fact be raised up into a new creation?" See 17:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So when came the first of the two (promises), raised We upon you Our servants, with terrible prowess, so they invaded (They treaded every nook and corner.) the innermost parts of your abodes; and it was a warning (completely) fulfilled. Jalut tortured the Israelites and plundered their habitations and there he was defeated by Talut and was killed by David. Some commentators say that the reference is to the punishment which was inflicted through violent winds and dreadful thunderous sounds.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) (Even if) become ye stones or iron, See 17:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or any other creature which seem yet harder to you (to receive life)", But they will say "Who will cause us to return?" Say thou: "He Who created you first!" Then will they wag their heads unto thee and say: "When will that be?" Say thou "Maybe it is nigh. See 17:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the day when He will call you forth, and ye will respond with His praise and ye will think that ye tarried (Refer to verses 20:102 - 20:104.) (in your graves) but a little (while). For the disbelievers witnessing the miserable life which they would get during 'Barzakh', i.e., the purgatory, would deem their life in the world to be very little. Some commentators say that those referred to in this verse are the believers, for owing to the blissful life they would have enjoyed in the purgatory, they would think the duration of the bliss to be very little, for it is but natural that the period of enjoyment passes away very quickly.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) unto My servants that they should utter (only) that which is best; Verily Satan soweth dissensions among them; Verily Satan unto man is an open enemy. See 17:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Your Lord knoweth you best; If He willeth He will have mercy on you, and if He willeth He will chastise you; and We sent not thee to be a guardian (Be in charge.) over them (against the evils they do). The Holy Prophet who was mercifully worried about the fate of the disbelievers, is said to have been sent not to guard the people against disbelief but only to invite them to the Right Path. Hence he need not worry much about the adamant disbelievers who inspite of the repeated admonitions and warnings, still persist in their infidelity. It is God's concern to be merciful to any or to chastise them.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thy Lord knoweth best (all) those who are in the heavens and the earth; and indeed We have exalted (Refer to verse 2:253.) some apostles to some (other apostles): and gave We unto David, 'Zabur' (the Psalter). The Sixth Holy Imam Jafar Ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq said that there were five chiefs among the apostles of God: (1) Noah, (2) Abraham, (3) Moses, (4) Jesus, and (5) the Holy Prophet Muhammad. The Holy Prophet said that "God has granted superiority to all his apostles over the angels and He has made me 'Superior to all His apostles and after me O' Ali thou and thy divinely chosen issues, and the angels are the servants of ours and if not friends".1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Call ye those whom ye fancy (The false gods, the deities - the idols or the angels who were worshipped as the daughters of God.) (to be gods) other than Him: they shall neither have the power of removing the distress from you nor (even) to alter (Transfer.) it." Those asserted besides God - are the angels whom the people worshipped as the daughters of God, Jesus whom the Christians worshipped as the son of God, and Uzair.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those (The apostles, and the angels held and worshipped as deities.) whom they call, to seek (As the medium.) the access unto their Lord (to know) which of them is the nearest (to Him) and hope they for His mercy, and fear they His chastisement; Verily, the chastisement of thy Lord is to be dreaded of. 'Wasila', i.e., means of approach to God - recommended in verse 5:35 - and here also asserts that all the deities, angels and the prophets which the pagans or the Christians or the Jews were calling, they themselves pray and seek the means of approach to God, the nearest one confirms the commendability of seeking 'Wasila', means of approach to God. The question is about the identification of the correct 'Wasila'. Some schools of thought hold the view that obedience is itself the means…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And there is not a town but We shall destroy it before the Day of Judgment or chastise it with a severe chastisement; that is written in the Book (of Our Will). See 17:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And nothing hindereth Us that We should send signs (Miracles.) save that belied them the ancients; and gave We unto Thamud the She-Camel, an open sign (Miracles.) but unto her they did injustice; and We send not signs (Miracles.) but to warn (the people). The 'Signs' referred to here and in several verses of Chapter 6 and Chapter 25 are the Signs proposed by the infidels not with the intention of removing their doubts in their search of the truth, but to show their averting challenge to the Holy Prophet. In the same way that the ancient people showed their aversion in a challenging manner and deserved severe punishment or a total destruction because the Holy Prophet's mission was universal and not confined to any particular race, community, place or time - the destruction of which would have some justification,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then returned We unto you the turn (to prevail) against them and aided you with wealth and offspring and made you a numerous host. The return of fortune referred to is the return of the Israelites to Jerusalem and their building the temple under Zurubbabel and their once again being prosperous.This is the second promise, i.e., The Roman onslaught and the destruction of Jerusalem when the Jews could not establish any dominion of their own anywhere until the recent Israelite republic - to which verse 17:8 refers to, with a warning that should they repeat the mischief, God will repeat the punishment after which there will be no more respite - excepting conviction to Hell. This is a prophecy. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (recollect thou O' Our Apostle Muhammad) when said We unto thee: "Verily, thy Lord encompasseth the people;" and We caused not the vision (Refer to verses 48:27 & 8:43.) which We shewed thee save as a trial for the people, and (similarly) the (Refer to verses 14:26, 5:78 & 5:79.) Accursed Tree in the Qur'an; and We cause them to fear, (To warn.) but it addeth not to them but their grievous transgression. The opening words of this verse is a recollective reference to what God promised the Holy Prophet about His help in the Battle of Badr.About the vision mentioned here there are three visions: the one is that the Holy Prophet's dreaming about the conquest of Mecca - when in the first attempt a Treaty was achieved at Hudaybiyyah which was a great victory to the Holy…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (remember O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) when said We unto the angels: "Prostrate ye (in obeisance) to Adam!" Prostrated all (of them) but 'Iblis' (who did it not) said he: "(What!) Am I to prostrate unto him whom Thou hast created of clay?" See 17:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He (Iblis) said: "Seest Thou, (This) is (the creature) whom Thou hath honoured (Refer to note on verse 17:70.) above me? If thou respiteth me until the Day of Judgment, I will sever (Arabic 'Ehtanuca' Lit. Severing from the root.) his posterity (Issues.) (under my sway) from its origin save a few." This clear directive proves that man in Origin is pure from all defects as asserted in verse 95:4, to have been created and best balanced. The defect and the deviation crept into the lineage of Adam by Satanic factor, is a subsequent matter. Hence the concept of the Original Sin of the Christian Church is unfounded. This fact is supported by several verses of Qur'an asserting that those who deviate from the Right Path tending towards the temporal life and its enjoyment are not real human beings -…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said He (God.) : "Begone! But whosoever of them followeth thee, then verily Hell is your recompense, a recompense in full!" See 17:62

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And tear thou away whomsoever of them thou canst with thy voice, and collect (against) them thy cavalry and infantry, and partake with them in (their) riches and (their) children, and make promises unto them;" and promiseth not unto them the Satan but a deceit. Devil's sharing in the wealth of his followers - his instigating them to earn wealth unlawfully and to spend it also extravagantly in all evil ways1.Showing in the issues, means for instigation towards adultery and thus causing the questionable birth of illegitimate children. The Devil's promise is his making the evil fair-seeming and his inviting towards disobeying God's commands.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily (as for) My (own) servants, (Refer to verse 33:33. Those purified by God Himself - The Holy Ahl al Bayt - and also the apostles of God.) thou shalt not have over them any authority, and sufficeth thy Lord (as their) Guardian. My servants - those who never in their lives yielded to the Devil, i.e., the divinely purified ones.1 They are duly protected by God.2

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Your Lord is He who saileth the ships for you in the sea that ye may seek of His grace; Verily He is ever unto you the Most Merciful. See 17:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When toucheth you any distress in the sea, away go those (The false gods whom they worshipped.) whom ye invoke, save He (God.) (alone) yet when He bringeth you safe unto the land ye turn away (from Him); and man hath ever been ungrateful. The native tendency in man is pictured in this verse. Any loss or calamity afflicts him, man resorts to seek God's help and prays and implores for mercy and relief, and once the Lord's mercy relieves him of the affliction, he forgets the Lord.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! feel ye then secure (feel secure against.) that He will (not) cause the slope of the earth for you (to be swallowed up) I or that He will (not) send against you a violent wind showering stones (Also sand storm.) (on you), then ye shall find not for you any protector. God is able to make you sink in the earth as He could drown you in the sea. Thus, man having been saved from a calamity should not think that he is safe for all times against the chastisement from God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or feel ye secure that He will (not) take you back into it (the sea) another time, and then send on you a fierce gale and drown you for what ye disbelieved, then ye shall find not against Us any pleader (To question why – Avenger.) As said in the previous verse though people might be safe for a while, but the chastisement from the Lord, if He wills, will overtake them whenever they earn it, by man's return to disbelief or evil ways.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If ye do good, ye do it for your own selves; and if ye do evil it is (in like manner) for your ownselves; So when came the second promise (warning to be fulfilled) (We roused your enemies to) sadden (with grief & sorrow.) your faces, and that they may enter the Mosque (The Mosque at Jerusalem.) as they entered it the first time, and to destroy whatever they conquered (with) total destruction. The opening words of the verse clearly declare the personal responsibility of each and every individual regarding his or her deeds. None shall carry the burden of the other. This fact is repeatedly stressed in the Holy Qur'an.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We have honoured the children of Adam, and We carry them in the land and on the sea and We provided them with sustenance of good things, and We have exalted them over most of those whom We have created, by (high) decree of exaltation. This verse confirms what Satan said in verse 17:62 - God has honoured the children of Adam by giving them authority and domination over many creatures. This is only a test. Ref. - preceding verses from verse 17:60 - and to the result of which will be announced as given in the following verse (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Remember the Day (of Judgment) when We will summon every people with their Imam (There are two kinds of Imams - Imam guiding at God's Command. Refer to verses 11:73 & 32:24 and imams inviting to Hell. Refer to verse 28:41.) (Leader); then whosoever is given his book in his right (Refer to verse 69:19.) hand, these shall read their books (with pleasure), and they shall not be dealt with (even) a shred unjustly. The Book mentioned here is the record of one's own deeds accompanying every individual which shall be manifested in a visible form on the Day of Judgment1.'Imam', i.e., Guide. It is said that whosoever, an individual follows in his life, on the Day of Judgment with him only the individual will be called to account for his faith and deeds. Blessed are they who follow the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whosoever is blind (Read this with verse 13:19 - 13:22, 46:20, 20:124, 20:125 - The blindness referred to here is not the physical blindness but the blindness of heart - the lack of attention towards God's Commands and His Signs.) in this (life), he shall in the hereafter (also) be blind and gone further astray from the (right) way. The blindness mentioned here is not the blindness of the physical eye but the blindness of heart. He whose heart did not get the benefit of the correct belief in God, shall also be deprived of seeing the light of salvation or the bliss in the life Hereafter.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily they had well-nigh purposed to turn thee (The Prophet addressed for the people.) away from that which We have revealed unto thee, that thou shouldst forge against Us other than that, and then they would surely have taken thee as a friend. The people of Banu Thaqif demanded a concession to them, i.e., to allow them to worship the idols for one more year and thereafter they would give up idolatry and embrace Islam.1 Another version says the reference is to the heathens offering the Holy Prophet some very tempting offers like making him the ruler of the whole of Arabia and giving in wedlock the most beautiful of the women of the land etc. The Holy Prophet's reply was: "If they place the sun in my right hand and the moon in the left in return for…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if it was not that We had firmly established thee, (The people.) thou wouldst surely had been nigh to incline unto them a little, See 17:73

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In that case We would surely have caused thee (The people.) taste a double (torment) in this life and a double (torment) after death, (and) then thou wouldst not have found for thee against Us any helper. See 17:73

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily well-nigh they purposed to tare (by Boycotting.) these away from the land, that they might drive thee out from it, but then, they would not have tarried (This may refer to the Interdict of the 'Shi'b Abi Talib' and the Non-Co-operation of the heathens forcing the Holy Prophet to leave Mecca. Qur'an prophecies that after that, they themselves would not stay there long.) (therein) after thee, but a little. Refers to the plot of the Quraysh to expel the Holy Prophet from Mecca. The latter part of the verse is a prophecy about Mecca being captured shortly after the Holy Prophet migrated from it.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This was Our way with those of Our apostles whom We did send before thee, and thou shalt find not in Our way any change. See 17:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Establish prayer (regularly) from the declension of the sun till the darkness of the night, and the recital at the morn; verily the recital at the morn is witnessed. This verse comprehends all five daily prayers prescribed by Islam.From the declining of the Sun to Sunset - there are two prayers. (1) 'Zuhr' - the noon prayer. (2) 'Asr' - the afternoon prayer.And from the Sunset to the full darkness there are two prayers. (1) 'Maghrib' - the evening prayer (2) 'Isha' - the night prayer.At the break of the dawn one prayer (1) 'Fajr' - the morning prayer.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Israa:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (in a part) of the night, forsake sleep for prayer, in addition to (what is incumbent on) thee; Maybe that exalteth thee thy Lord unto a position praised. (All-Glorious.) 'Tahajjud' or getting wakeful in the night. This prayer is to be offered after midnight but before dawn. This is not compulsory but very strongly commended. The glorious position mentioned is the highest exaltation to which a mortal could rise. The Holy Prophet said that on the Day of Judgment he would be in the 'Maqam al-Maḥmud' (the position of the great Praise and Glory) and from there he would seek intercession for the sinners and the Lord will grant whatever he would command.'Asa' means 'May' or 'Might' but when the nominative of this verb is God, it means certainty.
