item.description: Unto the disbelievers (it shall be) anything other than ease! See 74:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Leave Me (to deal with) him whom I created (bare and) alone! When the beginning Verses of the Sura Ha-Meem (H. M.) i.e., chapter 40 were revealed, the Holy Prophet recited them in the Mosque and seeing Waleed Ibn Mughaira seated near the Mosque, he recited the Verses repeatedly. Waleed got up and returned to his people and told them: "I tell you the truth that I have heard from Muhammad (the Holy Prophet) words which could he neither of any man nor of any jinn. It has the melody which the words of none in the world possess. It is glorious and very high, and it triumphs over the words of all the mortals" Having said this, Waleed returned home. The pagans felt sad, thinking that Waleed has been converted to Islam as Waleed was their leader. Abu Jehal…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And unto whom I granted wealth in abundance! God had given Waleed abundant wealth and a large number of sons, none of them he possessed before, and he was very proud of his prosperity.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And sons abiding in his presence! See 74:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And unto whom I made (life) adjustably smooth! See 74:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And yet desireth he that I should further add! See 74:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Never (it shall be)! for unto Our signs he was a foe! See 74:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Soon will I make him afflicted of a severe punishment (Refer to Verse 72:17.) 'Sa'ood' also refers to a particularly distressing kind of punishment in the hereafter. And some commentators say that Waleed had the taste of the wrath of God even in this life. Before his death, i.e., three of his sons deserted him and joined the ranks of the Muslims and the rest perished and he was deprived of his wealth and ultimately died in utter misery, disgrace and poverty.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, he thought and determined This refers as to how Waleed acted in the presence of his people and what he uttered taunting against the Holy Prophet and the Holy Qur'an.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But may he be ruined how he determined See 74:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Arise (thou) and warn (mankind) (The Prophet addressed for his followers. Otherwise he was already doing it 78:2. He was the leader of those who were purified by God Himself Refer to Verse 33:33.) ! See 74:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Again may be he ruined how he determined! See 74:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then looked he around! See 74:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then frowned he and scowled! See 74:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then turned he his back and swelled in pride! See 74:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then said he: "This is naught but sorcery from of old (Fascinating or the people fascinated of.) !" See 74:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This is naught but the word of a human being! See 74:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Soon will I cast him into hell! See 74:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what will make him realize what hell is? See 74:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It leaveth not nor it spareth (aught) See 74:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It shrivelleth (Alter.) a human body! See 74:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thy Lord, magnify! Magnifying in both ways - by the repetition of the Clause "Allahu Akbar' in prayer and elsewhere and by explaining His Absolute Authority and Hold over the entire Universe and His infinite Might and knowledge. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Above it (guardians) are nineteen! The number nineteen refers to the nineteen angels active for hell. Some commentators say that they refer to nineteen kinds of faculties endowed in man which if misused will drag the individual to the hell-fire.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We have made not the guardians of the fire other than angels, and We have made not the number save as a trial for those who disbelieve, that certain may be those who have been given the book, and may increase those who believe in (their) faith, and may doubt not those who have been given the book and the believers, and that say those in whose hearts is a distress and the disbelievers: "What meaneth God by this similitude?" Thus doth God alloweth to stray whomsoever He willeth, and guideth He whom He willeth, And knoweth not (any one) the hosts of God save He Himself; And this is naught but a reminder unto mankind (Refer to Verse 2:26.) Regarding the guardian angels of hell, refer to Verse 66:6. And there is the mention of the angel connected with…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! By the moon! An oath is generally taken by things solemn and great. Next to the sun, the moon is supposed by the general public of mankind as a great luminary. Besides, for the people of the earth, the Moon is one of the great signs of God which gives the world cool and pleasant light and its reflected light with its daily well- regulated diminishing and increase, is a sign of the divine control of the reflection of the Sun's light for the seasonal benefit for the working of the natural phenomenon concerning the vegetable world. To the poets and the mystics, the moon and its light are of special effect. Even to this day, to the pagans, the moon is a mystery, and it is worshipped as a deity. The Hindus (in India) even to this day…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And by the night when it retreateth! To an actively and correctly thinking mind the regular alternation of day and night, is not a small sign of the supreme authority of the Almighty Author of the Universe. Hence the constant changing in the nature of the day as well as the night are mentioned in solemn declarations.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And by the morn when it brighteneth! The dawn after the darkness of the night is practically the renewal of the life in the world.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily it (the Hell) is one of the grievous woes (Refer to Verse 74:31.) ! There is no limit to the number of the signs of God and the day of the Final Requital is the greatest of God's signs.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: A warning (it is) unto mankind! The message of Islam is for the human world as a whole and not for any particular community, clan, tribe, or nation.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Unto him among you who desireth to go forward (in goodness) or to remain behind Again, asserts that man is responsible for the re-action - by the choice given. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Every soul (Again asserts that man is responsible for the reaction by the choice given. (AP). Refer to Verse 52:21.) , for what it earned, is held in pledge! Every soul1 is under a commitment to goodness and is pledged with responsibilities.Man can redeem himself by his own good deeds in this life. There is no shifting of the responsibility2.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Save the people of the Right hand (Refer to Verses 56:8; 56:27; 56:38.) It is expressly said that the people of the Right hand in the life hereafter, are not fettered by their deeds in this life - 'Raheen' means each one reaped the result of his action. Hence the people of the Right hand there are not an exception. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thy raiment, purify (Refer to Verse 2:187.) ! The commands contained in this Verse have a deeper meaning- than mere literal interpretation. It did not mean that the Holy Prophet was ever unclean in his dress. Commentators say that here the word 'Thiyab' clothes mean his wives. For a similar reference to women see 2:187.Some commentators say that this Verse and the next, i.e., the 5th mentioning the cleaning of the clothes and shunning the uncleanliness refer to cleaning and shunning the dirt and the filth which the disbelievers used to throw upon him.'Thiyab' Lit., a cloth which covers the body but here as interpreted by the Ahl Al-Bayt is used in a very wide sense, meaning anything that surrounds human inner self which includes the character surrounding it and the body surrounding the character and garments surrounding the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In gardens shall they be, asking each other See 74:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: About the guilty ones See 74:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What hath brought you into the hell! See 74:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They shall say: "We were not of those who offered the regular prayers (to God)" See 74:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And we used not to feed the poor! See 74:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And used we to talk vanities with the vain talkers! See 74:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And used we to belie the Day of Judgment! See 74:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Till came upon us the Certainty (death) (The one thing which is certain & never fails, is death. Refer to Verse 15:99.) See 74:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So, shall avail them not the intercession (Refer to Verses 2:255; 4:85; 10:3; 19:87; 20:109; 21:28; 34:23.) of the intercessors! By 'Shafiyeen', i.e., intercessors, mean only those false deities and the bogus leaders of any faith in whom the people might rest their hopes of intercession on their behalf. But the great ones in the true faith who have endeared themselves to God to the extent of earning the right of intercession for the unintentional sinners among the faithful, are quite different and they are there to help those who err in their practical life owing to the natural weakness in them without any intention of rebelling against the authority of the Lord or without any wilful violation of the prescribed laws1.This Verse indicates and implies that there are intercessors whose intercession will be of avail to some groups but…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What hath happened then (unto them) that they turn aside from the warning See 74:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And every kind of abomination, Shun it! The injunctions addressed to the Holy Prophet, i.e., the representative of his followers. Orders meant for the people are given to their leader. The commands are meant for the believers to discipline them to qualify themselves for the higher regions of the state of spiritual bliss. The dirt or anything that diverts man from God such as idols, etc., should be avoided. Both these ideas are presented in Qur'an in different ways1. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: As if they were asses affrighted See 74:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Fleeing from a lion ('Qaswara' is used to mean also – archers.) See 74:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! But willeth every one of them that he may be given (the heavenly book) in open pages spread out (Refer to Verses 2:118; 17:93.) The pagans wanted that to every one of them God should send through his angels a separate book in open scrolls addressed to the name of the individual, commanding each one separately to obey the Holy Prophet and follow him1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! But they fear not the hereafter! See 74:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! Verily it is a Reminder! The Holy Qur'an is a reminder of the truth already revealed through the Apostles of old containing admonition and glad tidings to the devotees of truth and the doers of good deeds.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So whosoever willeth may mind it See 74:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They will mind it not unless God willeth; Worthy is He to be feared. And worthy is He to seek refuge to For 'Taqwa' or for the 'Muttaqeen' see 2:2; 2:177. Note that the truth having been revealed, there is no compulsion in faith. To adopt the right or the wrong course, is left to the individual choice. See 2:256; 76:3.'Willeth' here points out that man's action is the outcome of his own personal will, but man's will is subordinate to God's will but on the phenomenon of re-action - Refer to note on action and re-action in Sura 1. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And bestow not favours (expecting) that thou mayest receive them back increased Do not oblige considering your contribution to be great. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And for (the sake of) thy Lord (endure every hardship) in patience! See 74:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For when the Trumpet is beaten (Blown Refers to Resurrection.) Reference is to dawn of the Day of Judgment and what man will then experience particularly the evil fate of the disbelievers who reject the faith and ridicule the believers for their belief in the day of requital.It is said that Zararah Ibn Adna recited these Verses thrice and gave out a loud cry and died fearing the Day of Judgment.It indicates the nature of the punishment connected with the unsuccessful, strive to go up and this applies to those who are unduly ambitious in their life. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muddaththir:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That, that shall be the Day of distress (for those who disbelieve) See 74:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed, hath God heard the statement of her who pleadeth with thee about her husband and petitioneth unto God; and verily God heareth the contention of you two; Verily God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing (Refer to Verse 33:4.) . Khaula Binte Tha'laba, wife of Aus son of Samit, one day when Khaula had just finished her prayers, her husband wanted her for sexual enjoyment which she resented. Aus pronounced 'Zihar', a pre-Islamic social custom that if a husband says to his wife 'Thou art to me as the back of my mother', thereafter the husband was relieved of the conjugal obligation, not bound to support either his wife or his children. It was practically a divorce, besides the woman was also not free to contract a second marriage. Khaula disappointed at the conduct of her husband reported herself to the Holy…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Secret counsels are (Simulated) only by satan (i.e. this is a satanic act.) , that he may cause grief unto those who believe, but he shall harm them not in any way but with the permission of God; and upon God alone depend those who believe. Secret counselling on evil has been condemned as the act of the devil. If any one sees any dreadful dream, the recital of this verse is recommended soon after he awakes and says in continuation of it: - "Allahumma Bi Haqqi Muhammadin wa Aali-Muhammad. Allahumma Salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad waqeni Sharra ma ra'aitu fi manami" i.e., O' God! In the name of the Holy Prophet Muhammad and his Descendants, Send Thy blessings O' Lord! 'on Muhammad and the Descendants of Muhammad and save me from the evil effects of what I saw…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: 'O' ye who believe! when it is said unto you, 'Make ye room in (your) assemblies! then make ye room, God will make room for you; and when it is said unto you, 'Rise (Get up.) ye up! then rise ye up, God will exalt (you in) ranks (Refer to Verses 4:95; 6:165.) (unto Him), those who believe among you, and those who have been granted knowledge; and God is All-Aware of whatsoever ye do (Refer to Verses 3:7; 3:18; 4:162; 29:49.) . Most of the companions, while sitting before the Holy Prophet used to cover all the space for themselves and when they saw any one intending to sit along with them, they would not give room to him. Once when the Holy Prophet was sitting in a corner of the Mosque and the companions had covered the whole…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: 'O' ye who believe! When ye (wish to) consult in private with the Apostle, then offer some alms before your consultation, that is better for you and purer; but ye find not any means (to do so), then verily God is Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful (Refer to Verse 47:38. See note - Since only ''Ali acted on this and none else - this Ordinance was abrogated by the next verse.) . The restriction on the consultation with the Holy Prophet might sound unreasonable to an ordinary lay mind but the serious ones among the intellectuals, in every school of thought know that the time of an Apostle of God, could never reasonable be monopolized by a few rich ones or those well-placed in the society or those who merely claimed to be his companions, shutting the audience to the poor…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What Restrained (This is practically the condemnation of the niggardliness of the people for to avoid the giving of alms they had stopped consulting the Holy Prophet - the order was withdrawn.) ye that ye give alms before your consultation? Then since ye did it not and God turned (merciful) unto you, then keep ye up (the regular) prayer, and pay ye (the prescribed) poor-rate and obey ye God and His Apostle; and God is All-Aware of what (all) ye do. It was evidently a providential plan to issue the ordinance controlling vain private counselling with the Holy Prophet just to prove that among the companions of the Holy Prophet, there was only 'Ali who would always readily comply with God's commands and none else.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hast thou not seen those who befriend a people on whom hath been the wrath of God? Thy are neither of your party nor are they of theirs, and swear they for falsehood while they know (what they do) (Refer to Verse 60:13.) . The hypocrites had friendship with the Jews and conveyed the secrets of the believers to them.Among the hypocrites was one Abdullah Ibn Naheel who often used to sit before the Holy Prophet and used to convey to the Jews all the talk which took place with the Holy Prophet. Once the Holy Prophet was seated with his companions in his apartment. The Holy Prophet said, "Now mil come the one those pride is that of the rebellious ones and whose sight is that of Satan." Abdullah Ibn Nabeel entered the room. The Holy Prophet asked him…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For them hath prepared God a severe chastisement; Verily, evil is what they do. See 58:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Make they their oaths a shield (A cover, Refer to Verse 63:2. Refer to the conducts of the hypocrites.) , and obstruct they (others) from the way of God, so for them shall be a shameful chastisement. See 58:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Never shall avail them aught against God, their wealth nor their children; they are fellows of the fire; they shall abide therein. The hypocrites boasted saying that their abundant wealth and the large number of their issues would be of avail to them on the Day of Judgment. This verse was revealed against their false notion.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the day when God will raise them all, then will swear they unto Him as they swear unto you, and deem they that it will avail them. Nay! verily they, they are the liars! On the Day of Judgment, the hypocrites would swear upon their being the sincere believers as they did to deceive the Holy Prophet and the believers in their life, but it will be in vain1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Satan hath gained hold on them, so he maketh them forget (Those who neglect the daily prayers to note - lest they be listed as the Satan's party.) the remembrance of God; They are Satan's Party; Beware! verily, the party of Satan are the losers. See 58:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those of you who abandon any of their wives through 'Zihar' (i.e. a husband in anger declaring as a vow that his wife would thereafter be to him as his mother to deprive her of the sexual enjoyment, as a punishment to her (See 'Fiqh').) (by saying "Be thou unto me as my mother's back"); they are not their mothers; their mothers are only those who gave them birth! and certainly they utter a word hateful and false; and verily God is Pardoning, Oft-Forgiving (Refer to Verse 33:4.) . See 58:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily those who are opposed to God, and His Apostle (Refer to Verse 6:34.) , they shall be of the most humiliated. The reference in this verse to those who opposed God and the Holy Prophet, applies equally to those who go against the Islamic laws and opposed the Holy Prophet, until the end of the world. Apply this verse to those who acted blindly to satisfy their selfish desires in depriving 'Ali and Fatimah and the other members of the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt which act was diametrically opposed to what God had conveyed to His comrades1 through the Holy Prophet and what the Holy Prophet himself had repeatedly told the people about his Ahl Al-Bayt. It is a well-known historic fact that Othman owing to his own relationship with Hakm the father of Marwan, brought him into Madina from…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God hath decreed: "I shall prevail (Dominate.) , I and My apostles!" Verily God is the All-Strong, the Ever-Prevalent. When after their triumph over the surrounding habitations the Muslims said that very soon God would help us to bring Rome under the sway of Truth (Islam) and the hypocrites said, "Perhaps you imagine Rome and the other countries like those of your environment." Here is the prophecy about the triumph of the Muslims over the other great countries.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thou shalt find not a people who believe in God and the hereafter befriending those who oppose God and His Apostle, be they even their own fathers, or their sons, or their own brothers, or their kinsmen, they are those God hath inscribed faith in their hearts and hath strengthened them with a Spirit (Refer to Verse 41:30.) from Himself; and He will admit them into gardens 'neath which flow rivers, they shall abide therein; with God well pleased (These cannot be save those whom God Himself purified - Refer to Verse 33:33 Compare this to what the Holy Prophet said at Khaybar before giving the Standard of Islam to fight the enemy.) with them, and they will be well-pleased with God; They are the party of God; Be it known, verily the party of God alone shall be the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who abandon any of their wives through 'Zihar' and then would recall what they have uttered, they may free (Note how far Islam prescribes charity to expatiate sins.) a captive ere they touch each other; that ye are admonished (to conform); and Verily God, of whatever ye do, is Well-Aware. See 58:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But whosoever findeth not the means (to free a captive), he may fast for two months consecutively ere they touch each other; and whosoever is not able to do (so) shall feed sixty needy ones; that is in order that ye may believe in God and His Apostle; And these are the bounds set of God; And for the disbeliever there shall be a painful chastisement. See 58:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who oppose (Compare this to the defiance against the demand for pen and paper, by the Holy Prophet on the eve of his departure.) God and His Apostle, shall be humiliated as were humiliated those before them; and indeed We have sent down signs clear; and for the disbelievers there shall be a humiliating chastisement. The humiliation or the frustration of the enemies of the Holy Prophet referred to here, is that which the enemy suffered at the battle of 'Khandaq' (the Ditch) - (Ahzab) - (M.S.). It refers also to the bigger and the graver penalty in the hereafter and on the Day of Judgment.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the day when God will raise them all to life and inform them of what they did; God hath encompassed (everything) in (His) record; while they (might) have forgotten it; and God is over all things a Witness. Everyone will see the true value and the inward aspects of all his deeds which were not manifest ever before1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Seest thou not that God knoweth whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth? nowhere taketh place any secret counsel between three (persons) but He is fourth of them, nor between five, but He is the sixth, nor (between) less than that, nor (between) more but He is with them wheresoever they may be; then will He inform them of whatever they did, on the Day of Judgment - Verily God Well Knoweth all things (See Verse 57:4.) . This contains a warning to the hypocrites who were busy plotting against the Holy Prophet and the believers thinking their secrets to be secrets for God and the Holy Prophet also, whereas God knows everything, and the Holy Prophet was continuously' in communion with the Lord, having the revelations from Him, and thus had the knowledge of every…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Seest thou not those who have been forbidden secret counsels, yet return they unto what hath been forbidden and hold they secret counsels to sin and revolt and towards disobedience to the Apostle, and when come they unto thee, they greet thee, not as greeteth thee God; and say they in their selves "Why doth God chastise not for what we say?" Enough for them is hell, they shall enter it, and what a wretched destination it is! As the believers in Madina gained strength after strength in their number as well as in their influence and power. The disruptive forces of the Jews resorted to duplicity and secret intrigues and plots. Here is the reference to the machinations of the Jews as well as the hypocrites1.. Whenever the Muslims go out on any defensive expedition against the enemy's assaults,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mujaadila:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: 'O' ye who believe! When ye counsel among yourselves in secret, then counsel ye not to sin and revolt and disobedience to the Apostle, but counsel ye among yourselves for goodness and restrain (of yourselves against evil)', and fear ye (the wrath of) God unto Whom ye shall all be gathered! Note how far Islam controls the personal morals of the believers even in the private lives.Muslims are forbidden against participating in any secret movement with any evil intent and to be constantly counselling each other on goodness and piety.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hallowed is He in Whose hand is the kingdom (of the heaven and the earth), and He, over all things is All-Powerful (Qadeer.) The word i.e., 'Hand' stands for authority, power or might and 'Mulk' means the Kingdom or the Dominion, both visible and invisible to us that which is within the limits of the conception of space and even beyond it. The word 'Mulk' is a very wide and a comprehensive expression which covers anything and everything of matter or energy in the conceptive limits of human intellect and beyond it. This truth about the universal authority of the Lord Creator and the Owner of the Universe is given to educate the human minds against the imaginary or the conjectural dogmas about the existence of multiple or the manifold number of deities or gods, wielding authority over the destinies…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they shall say: "Had we but hearkened (unto them) or pondered (over what they said), we would not have been amidst the fellows in the flaming fire" This Verse refers to the failure of man in using his conscience and the discretionary powers, which failure draws the individual to the blazing fire.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So shall they confess their sins, but far will be (from mercy) the fellows in blazing fire When passing through the punishment, the disbelievers in the apostles of God and the Holy Imams would not help confessing their folly and their wickedness but that would not be of any avail to them at all for repentance must be with the necessary amendment and then the time or respite for the amendment would have been long over and thus the chance will have long been lost.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who fear their Lord in secret, for them shall be forgiveness and a great recompense (Refers to the last clause of Verses 35:18, 31:16, 36:11, 50:33.) The fear of God means not only dreading His displeasure and the consequent wrath of His, but also loving Him so heartily and so intensely at heart though He is not seen by the physical eyes or perceived through any of the bodily senses1.Indicates that what is valued with God, is the sincerity in faith and the purity of intention whether declared or not. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And conceal ye your word or declare it; Verily, He is the Knower of whatsoever is in the breasts (hearts) See 67:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Knoweth not He that created? and He is the Subtle (Lateef.), the All-Aware (Refer to Verses 6:18; 6:103; 11:1; 17:30; 22:59; 24:18; 31:16; 33:34; 35:14; 67:14.) 'Man', i.e., who, or whom - here may be in nominative case meaning who - i.e., What! He Who created - and may also be an objective case meaning - What, whom He has created - and the nominative understood - the latter seems to be more appropriate as a proof in the favour of the statement made in Verse 13.'Lateef' may be used to mean ''kind' - and also as 'Subtle' - Penetrating - the latter is more appropriate here. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He it is Who made for you the earth subservient (Yielding.) , traVerse ye then its broad sides, and eat ye of His provision; and unto Him (alone) is the return (After death.) The earth has been made usable for the intelligence of man to manage his life affairs concerning his stay in it - 'Zulal' meaning manageable and serviceable, has been used relating to the animals subjected to usage by man1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! deem ye yourself secure of He Who (ruleth) in the heaven (as well) (As well as in the earth.) , that He will cause not the earth to swallow you up (Refer to Verses 17:68, 28:76 - 28:82.) ? Then lo! it shall quake Man has been warned against any false feeling of security in the earthly life against the wrath of God - If God wills the earth on which we live, feeling ourselves safe and secure, would swallow up habitation together through typhoons, earthquakes and tornadoes1. -Heaven is not the physical one - but the spiritual sphere dominating the spheres. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or deem ye yourself secure of He Who (ruleth) in the heaven (as well), will send not down upon you a stone-charged violent storm; Then shall ye know how (terrible) My warning is (Refer to Verses 17:68, 29:40.) For the fate of the cities which rebelled against the authority of the Lord and the fate of the people of Lot see 17:68, 29:40.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed belied those before them (My signs): how (terrible) then was My wrath (Refer to Verses 22:42 - 22:44.) See 67:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Behold they not the birds above them, outstretching (their wings), and contracting (them) (Refer to Verse 24:41.) ? upholdeth them not save the Beneficent (God); for verily He well seeth everything Note how Islam invites man to use his intellect in understanding the glorious existence of the Creator of the Universe, His Power, His Might, His Wisdom by reflecting on the marvels of the various units of His creation. If intelligently viewed the beautiful appearances of the birds, their marvellous flights and their wonderful formations during their flight into the sky, is the most beautiful and the most wonderful manifestation of nature.Their structure, their shapes, their colourful beauty, their sweet melodious musical voices and the various adaptations in their structure to suit their aerial life - their stretching their wings in the air and their darting about in the space…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Who created death and life that he may try you (to prove) which of you is best in deeds (Refer to Verses 10:14, 11:7, 18:7, 21:35, 29:3, 38:27, 51:56, 2:28, 40:11.) ; He is the Ever-Prevalent, the Oft-Forgiving Note - Death is mentioned before life, and it is said to be created. If death is to mean the cessation of existence, how could it take effect before the existence itself taking its effect. In 2:28, mankind is told:"How disbelieve ye in God when ye mere dead and He gave life to you! Then He will give you death, then life again, and then unto Him ye will return" (2:28)Thus death would mean not the cessation of the existence but a turning point in it. The word 'Kuntum', (i.e., you were) in the Verse 2:28 means that we did exist though…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or who is that who can be a host for you to succour you besides the Beneficent (God)? the disbelievers are but in mere delusion There is no power besides God's and none can ever defy His will - Hence let man be mindful of his helplessness and the supreme authority of the Lord.Here Qur'an has used the demonstrative pronoun - 'Haaza1', i.e., this - for which we have used 'that' to maintain the English language otherwise the use of this is more justified to indicate the nearness similar to the nearness of God required for the helper to help. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or who is that who can provide you with sustenance should He withhold His sustenance? Yet persist they in disdain and aversion (against the Truth) (Refer to Verse 16:73) The word 'sustenance' is a comprehensive term which includes even thing that an individual needs for the various phases of existence, physical, mental, and spiritual, etc. If anyone obstinately pursues the rebellious impulses of his corrupted passions, imagining them as the necessities of life, the individual is vainly pursuing a mirage which would ultimately end in his own perdition. The sustenance being from heaven as well as in the earth1. A soul receives its sustenance even after its death, particularly the one who surrenders his self in the way of the Lord2. Life after death is only a continuation of this life and those who surrender their lives in this world…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! is he who goeth along grovelling on his face, better guided or he who walketh upright upon the straight path (Refer to Verses 32:19, 10:35, 5:100, 13:16, 39:7) ? Everyone in this life, except those who have been purified and guided by God Himself1 () needs a guide or a model to follow.This Verse and Verse 10:35 give the clearest guiding formula for a sincere seeker of the right course. The use of the clue given in this Verse, one needs nothing but an unclouded common sense to enquire and find out the beings whose purity is divine and whose conduct and character is flawless and ideal and whose life from the beginning to the end, had been pure and godly - whose practical life had always been on the path of truth and righteousness, who had never in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "He it is Who brought (Raised.) you (into being) and made for you the ears and the eyes and the hearts (As the centre of cognition.) ; yet how little is it that ye thank (Refer to Verse 6:98.) !" See 67:22

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "He it is Who hath spread you in the earth and unto Him (alone) shall ye all be gathered" See 67:22

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "When shall this appointment (Of the threat or promise.) come to pass, if ye be truthful?" See 67:22

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Verily the knowledge (of it) is only with God, and verily I am only an open Warner" See Math. 24/36, Mark. 13/32."But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but thy Father only" Math. 24/36."But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father" Mark. 13/32.Jesus also gives the same reply.The Final Judgment is certain to come but the hour is known to none but God. For the counting of the time with God1."And they will bid thee hasten on the Doom, and Allah faileth not His promise, but lol a Day with Allah is as a thousand years of what ye reckon" (22:47).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But when they shall see it nigh, grieved shall be the faces of those who disbelieve, and it shall be said (unto them): "This is what ye have been calling for" See 67:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "See ye? If God were to destroy me and those with me or He bestoweth mercy on us, yet who can protect the disbelievers from the painful chastisement?" The tone here is identical with 5:20 pointing out that God is the Absolute Authority over the entire Universe. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "He is the Beneficent (God)! believe we in Him and on Him (alone) do we rely; so ye shall come to know who it is that is in manifest straying" Here points out that God's authority always manifests through His all-pervading grace. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Who created the seven heavens layer above layer (Refer to Verses 65:12, 71:15.) : thou seest not in the creation of the Beneficent (God) any defect or incongruity. Then look thou again; Seest thou any gap (To prove the unity, Qur'an advises to refer to the experimental method of repeated observations.) ? The heaven has been created into seven regions and the regions are said to have been arranged as layers one above another1.The arrangement of the heavenly regions and everything in each region is in such perfect order and harmony with one another and the motions of each body in the space is so marvellously regulated by the Universal law that nowhere in the Kingdom of God, i.e., in the Universe, there is the least flaw of any irregularity or failure or a gap. There is neither any incongruity…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "See ye? if your water should go down (If water totally disappears - getting absorbed in the earth.) (into the earth), who then can bring you flowing water?" The Verse may be taken as a proverb expressing that if you lose even one benefit for some reason who is going to substitute it with another one. It implies that nothing advantageous to man's progress disappears without a successive substitution. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then repeat thou (thy) gaze again and again, thy gaze shall return unto thee dulled, being Wearied (Refers to the impossibility of the sight passing through the heavens.) It is almost a challenge to man to see, scrutinise or examine not once but repeatedly, for the eye in its travel to examine this fact would only exhaust itself to return dejected. Note, that Islam does not impose any dictated faith but invites every individual to study minutely as might be possible to each one individually, again and again. Even the region which could be seen, are so vast and stretching so far beyond our ken that even with the aid of the most powerful of the implements, our eyes would not help acknowledging their defeat or failure to penetrate even the space to its nearest extent.To prove the unity, Qur'an…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed, have We adorned the lower heaven nearest to the world with lamps (i.e., the stars), and We have made them (as) missiles to repulse away the Satans, and We have prepared for them the chastisement of the flaming fire The physical world is divided into seven regions called the seven heavens and the heaven in which is situated the earth, is said to be the lowest heaven which is lighted with the stars1. All these stars, the nearest and the farthest of them and this earth, the sun the moon and the galaxies put together are accommodated in the lowest of the heavens or the regions, the knowledge about the vastness, i.e., the extent of each of these heavens and the beings in them, is beyond the conception of the human intellect.The stars are sometimes used as missiles to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the chastisement of the hell, and evil is the destination See 67:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When they shall be flung into it, they shall hear its roaring as it boileth up (Refer to Verse 11:106.) See 67:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: As it would burst with rage; Whenever a group is flung into it, its keepers shall ask them; "Came not there unto you a warner (Refer to Verse 39:71.) ?" See 67:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mulk:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They shall say: "Yea! Indeed, a warner did come unto us, but we belied (him) and said we: "God hath sent not down aught, ye are in naught but a vast delusion (Refer to Verse 36:30.) !"'" Here the signs of God, mean the apostles as well as their divinely commissioned deputies the Holy Imams who were also not only rejected but also equally persecuted, mocked and martyred1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed successful are the believers, The faithful ones surely succeed in reaching their destined goal of life.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These, they are the heirs, Such perfection in the above qualities would naturally inherit the abode of the heavenly bliss for ever, and no doubt, the others also, to the extent to which they qualify themselves for it by their acquiring the above excellence for themselves.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:100 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That I may do (the) good which I have left undone." By no means! it is but a word he sayeth; and after them shall be a barrier (Any distance in between.) until the day they shall be raised (Resurrected for the final judgment.) (again). 'Barzakh' here means the interval between the death of the individual and the state of total or collective resurrection. Regarding the condition and the state of that interval or the intermediary state the passage is silent - all that is said about this state is derived from authentic sayings of the holy Prophet and the Imams of his House, supported by sound reasoning. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:101 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when the trumpet is blown, there shall be no ties of kindred between them on that day, nor shall they ask of one another. The word 'Sur' here and elsewhere may be the plural 'Surat', (i.e., Form) - and it may may the time or the also mean the Trumpet. However, the time or the state of the Blow, is when the whole universe along with all its components, animate and inanimate, beings angelic and human, assume the final form and shape to which they are destined. Before reaching that state the relations of the parts and the components to each other and to the whole is subject to change - for instance a seed contains parts and the components of the tree and each is co-relative of the other but when the seed is sound and the process…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:102 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then (those) whose scales (of good deeds) are heavy, they shall be the successful ones; (In getting salvation.) 'Mawazin' here and elsewhere indicate that every aspect or act of human life will be weighed and for each aspect there will be a different scale. But the Scale of scales is the Imam. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:103 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those whose scales (of good deeds) are light, they are those who shall lose their souls, abiding in Hell. See 23:102

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:104 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The fire shall scorch their faces and they therein shall be grinning (of the affliction). See 23:102

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:105 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Then will God ask them) "Were not My signs rehearsed unto you? then ye used to belie them" See 23:102

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:106 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They shall say: "O' Our Lord! overcame us our ill-luck and we were people gone astray" See 23:102

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:107 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' our Lord! Take us out of it; if we return (to evil) then verily we shall be unjust, See 23:102

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:108 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (God will) say: "Be ye driven down into it, and speak ye not unto Me!" See 23:102

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:109 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, there was a party of My servants who said: "O' our Lord! we believe, so forgive us and have mercy on us, and Thou art the Best of the Merciful ones!" See 23:102

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (These are) those who inherit the Paradise; they shall abide therein. See 23:10

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:110 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But ye took them with ridicule that (until they) made you to neglect My remembrance, while ye did laugh at them. Actually, their mockery was the cause of their negligence and not the believers but they were at the bottom of the mischief. The act attributed to them. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:111 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, I have recompensed them this day for they were patient; (that), they are the achievers. See 23:110

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:112 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He will say: "How many years did ye tarry in the earth?" See 23:110

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:113 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They will say: "Tarried we a day or part of a day, ask thou those who keep account" However long may be the stay on the earth, it is nothing in comparison to Eternity but however one should realise that this short stay here is not vain and purposeless.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:114 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (God will) say: "You did tarry but a little if ye only knew (it)" See 23:113

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:115 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! think ye then that We created you in vain and that unto Us ye shall not be returned? Man is informed that the whole working of the Universe is not a vain or an aimless game but a predetermined plan of the All-Wise Author of Creation. Man being one of the constituent beings of the organism of the universe, has also his own individual responsibility - for which one day he would have to account for.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:116 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then (behold) the most exalted is God, the True King; No god is there but He, the Lord (Lord Cherisher.) of 'Arsh' (Which comprehends the whole universe.) (the Throne) of Grace. See 23:115

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:117 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whoever invoketh with God another god - he hath no proof therefore - his reckoning is only with his Lord; Verily, the disbelievers shall not be successful. Though there are many proofs for the Unity of God but there is not a single piece of evidence of anyone being besides Him. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:118 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "O' my Lord! For give and have mercy, and Thou art the Best of the merciful ones!" See 23:117

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We, (God.) created man, from an extract of clay, In the opening verses of this chapter, is dealt with the moral or the spiritual growth of the human being marching on the Right Path of the guidance from God. In these verses, is recapitulated the physical growth of man as it was referred to in verse 22:5. This is to make man realize his origin from dust and his return to it once again. The various evolutionary stages of the creative artistry of the Almighty Author of the Universe, is to impress upon man, how the Omnipotent One could convert the inorganic matter into a living organism and deposit it into the ovum, convert it into a clot of thickly congealed blood and cause the cells to grow through segmentation and then grant it the growth into a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then We made him sperm, in a firm resting place, Refers to the beginning of the development of the life from the extract of an inanimate matter. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then made We the sperm a clot, then made We the clot a lump of flesh, then made We in the lump of flesh bones, then clothed We the bones with flesh; then We did grow it into another (Refers to beginning or the development of the human Psyche in the newly born child.) creation; so Blessed be God, the Best of the creators. Refers to the substitution of the original matter of the primary stages, with the newly-evolved generation.(Another Creation) Refers to the beginning of the human psyche in the newly-born child. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then verily after that ye shall die, Man is caused to suffer the death of his physical body. But death by no means is the end of his life. It is not the extinction of the life but the transfer or the conveyance of the soul from the physical to the spiritual realm, from the sensual consciousness to the spiritual realisation, from the false to the real or from the sleep to the awakening.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then verily on the Day of Judgment ye shall be raised. As light alone is shone out from light, only wisdom issues from the wise. God is the All Wise. Nothing but wisdom could ever manifest from God. Could all these creative faculties in man be only to be made extinct or perish altogether at death without any plan for the future? It is said here that every one is accountable and shall be resurrected for the Final Judgment.May refer to the physical spheres which are above us or to the spiritual spheres above the primary human psychical stage up to the ultimate stage of communion with the Absolute - stages which are termed by the mystics as 'Taba' Instinct, 'Nafs', i.e., Desire, 'Qalb' i.e., the state of inter-relation and Emotion, 'Aql' Intellect - conception, 'Ruh' Spirit, i.e., Intuition or…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed made We above (Refer to verse 78:13.) you seven paths (heavens); and neither, of the creation, We are heedless 'Tara'iq' is the plural of 'Tariq', i.e. way, road, tract. The seven roads referred to are the seven orbits of the planets. This statement indicates God's ownership of the world of nature, His Absolute authority and His independent management of the affairs of the whole working of the Universe - and His sustained purposeful - interest in it.The proper system and order including the various stages - and it is not any heedless or aimless action.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And send We down water from the heaven according to a measure, and We cause it to settle in the earth; and verily to take it away We are able. The few words of this verse, have volumes of meaning referring to the Divine wisdom with which the earth is given the ceaseless water supply. The rain comes, not for the whole year but in the fixed seasons. The water from the sky is not dropped in big logs collectively; for, had it been so, the creation on earth below would have been destroyed. The water rains in small drops and flows away to sea, washing the surface of the earth and the surface of everything on it viz. the buildings, the trees and the mountains and all the dirt is taken through the flow of the water into the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then with it We grow for you gardens of date-palms and grapes; for you therein are fruits in plenty and from them ye do eat, See 23:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who in their prayers are humble, This verse gives the description or the identification of the true believers in God - In prayers they are filled with awe for God's Glory - Humility on the part of the individual presented in prayer manifests the individual's estimation and the acknowledgment of his own self, being nothing in the presence of the Almighty power of God's glory and the individual's consciousness of the Absolute Omnipotent Authority of the Lord. Once a man was seen, while in prayer playing with his beard. The Holy Prophet said: "Had the man been conscious of his insignificance in the presence of the Supreme Majesty of the Lord's Authority, he would surely have manifested in his physical existence, and his presenting it before Him."It is said that in the battle of Uhud, the steel-point of an…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And a tree that groweth out of Mount Sinai which produceth oil and a condiment for those who eat. It is said that the Olive was first grown on the Mount Sinai through which Moses saw the fire and God spoke to him. There are some mystic meanings of the names; the 'Fig' the 'Olive', 'Mount Sinai' and the Holy City of the 'Ameen', i.e., the trusted one (i.e., Muhammad), i.e., Mecca.1 The Olive is called the Blessed Tree.2

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily for you there is, in the cattle a lesson; We Provide you to drink of what is in their bellies, and for you there are in them benefits in plenty, and of them ye do eat, See 23:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on them and on ships are ye borne. See 23:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed sent We Noah unto his people, and he said: "O' My people! worship ye God (alone) ye have no (Jesus also said the same and not Trinity 'Hear O' Israel; the Lord our God is one Lord' New Testament. Mark 12/29, Corinthians 8/4, Ephesians 4/5-6.) god other than Him; Will ye not then guard (yourselves against evil)?" God after giving the examples of the creative order, refers to His legislative system of guidance1. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But said the chiefs of those who disbelieved, among from his people: "This is a man like unto yourselves who intendeth to exalt himself above you; but had God will (to send any apostle) He would certainly have sent angels. We have heard (People believed that an angel only could be a prophet from God and not a human being -They wondered at a human being claiming to be a prophet.) not of this among our fathers of old;" See 23:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily (This is what the people said.) he is not but a man maniac (One with the touch of madness.) so bear ye with him for some time. Noah was considered by his people to be mad, otherwise, in their opinion no man could ever think himself to be an apostle of God and yet condemn their deities. Hence, they suggested him to be left to himself for by the segregation, the madness might run out or he would perish.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He (Noah) said: "O' my Lord! help me against what they belie." See 23:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So revealed We unto him that: "Make thou (O' Our Apostle Noah!) the Ark before Our eyes and (as per) Our revelation (Direction.) and when cometh (unto thee) Our command, and gusheth forth water from the oven, take into it two of every species a pair and thy people except those among them about whom had already been issued the word; and address (Pray not – wish not.) Me not in respect of those who are unjust; for verily they shall be drowned." See 23:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when thou art settled (in the Ark), thou and those with thee, then say thou: "All praise be unto God Who delivered us from the unjust people!" And when thou and those with thee on the Ark, are settled, then say thou - (The Praise of the Lord) (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say thou: "O' my Lord! disembark me with a blessed landing, for Thou art the Best of all who cause to land!" See 23:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who, from what is vain, (Word or action.) keep (themselves) aloof, 'Laghw' i.e., Vain, the First Holy Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib says that all that is void of the remembrance of God is meant by this term - With the Ahl al-Bayt this term includes all useless entertainments wasteful of time including musical enjoyments, and vain games played just to while away the time, are also covered by this term.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily in this are signs (Of the Omnipotent.) and We do only try (the people). See 23:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then We raised up after them another generation (Hud). See 23:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then sent We among them an apostle (Saleh) from among themselves saying "Worship ye God (alone), there is not (This is what Jesus preached and not Trinity. "Hear, O' Israel; the Lord our God is one Lord." Refer to New Testament Mark 12/29, Corin 8/4, Ephes 4/5-6.) for you any god other than Him: What! Will ye not therefore guard (against evil)?" See 23:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the chiefs of his people who disbelieved and belied the meeting of the hereafter, and whom We had richly (Given the provision to indulge.) provided in the life of this world said: "This is not but a man like yourselves, eateth he of what ye eat from, and drinketh he of what ye drink," See 23:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Far, (This is what the disbelievers said to the people obstructing them from believing in the Apostle.) Far (from sense) is what ye are promised! See 23:28

item.description: There (This is what the disbelievers said to the people obstructing them from believing in the Apostle.) is nothing but our life in this world: We die and we live and we shall not be raised again. See 23:28

item.description: He (This is what the disbelievers said to the people obstructing them from believing in the Apostle.) is nothing but a man who hath forged a lie about God, and we are not going to believe in him. These1 are common statements of the disbelievers. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He (Saleh) said: "O' my Lord! help me against what they belie!" See 23:38

item.description: And those who act (Acting by the payment of the dues from their well-earned wealth and in whatever purifies one's heart.) for purification, The Sixth Holy Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq says that whosoever stops himself or anybody else from giving away even a grain in dispensing 'Zakat', i.e., the prescribed poor-rate, is not a 'Mu'min', i.e., a True Believer.Purification by payment of the dues from their wealth or in what purifies the heart.1 (Refer to 'Fiqh') (A.P.).

item.description: And those who guard their private parts, This brief verse of only a very few words comprehends all the aspects of a chaste life both of the male and the female members of the human family. It enjoins guarding the self against the abuse of the sex urge in both the sexes. The refinement of a human personality can be measured and assessed according to the manifest activity as well as hidden, or the latent ideology. It is in the universal acknowledgment of the dangers of this urge in a man as well as woman getting out of bounds and rebellious that even the average or the minimum activity of this urge is strictly restricted to the bonds of wedlock in which the rights or the liberties of both the sexes in this regard are duly regulated and controlled.A true…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And made We the Son of Mary and his Mother a (Of the Ever-fulfilled Omnipotent will.) Sign, and We gave them a refuge for both on a high land, quiet, secure and watered with springs This is a reference to the situation when the Virgin Mary having conceived the Holy Spirit in her womb (Jesus) being afraid of the condemnation of her people about her bearing a child without a husband, did not know what to do and where to go to take shelter. She was directed by God to take refuge in Bethlehem, where there was for her the fruit tree to eat of and also a spring of water to drink from. The place is on the heights of Palestine nearby Jerusalem, surrounded by vineyards and fruit gardens and meadows with herds of cattle grazing in them. History…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (And the apostles were commanded by God) "O' (My) apostles! eat ye of the good things and do good; Verily I know what ye do." See 23:50

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily this your group is one group, and I am your Lord therefore fear ye (Only Me). This verse declares the natural unity of mankind and the divisions effected in it, into communities, sects, tribes and nations. The message, the source of guidance and the perfect identity of the messengers bring the messages, all being perfectly identical, obviously proves the Unity of God. All the messengers of the apostles naturally constitute one Brotherhood. Hence all men should naturally be united with mutual love as the creatures of one and the same Lord and worship Him and Him alone and none else1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But they have (Islam is a sectless - rather anti-sectarian religion. Sects were started in opposition to the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt Islam-Original is only identified as 'Shiaism') rent the unity among themselves into sects; each party rejoiceth in that which is with them. See 23:52

item.description: And Verily they who are thrilled for fear of their Lord, The address shifts from the ungrateful disbelievers in the truth to the grateful believers in it and the following verses identify such infallible ones who should be followed in faith and its practice. The verse also enumerates the basic qualities of godliness and goodness which identifies them.The maximum of each and every one of the qualities mentioned in these verses could be found with the maximum possible perfection, only in the Holy Ahl al-Bayt who alone could naturally own them in the degree and the perfection desired by God for they and none else are those purified by God.1 The description in these verses would reflect upon the others in mankind according to the degree in which the people would own the described qualities.

It is pitiable that without the proper knowledge of the amount of regard and protection woman gets under this proviso, much of calumnious matter is talked of by people without which only betrays their ignorance of their knowledge of the…

After giving the possible reasons for their disbelief here is given the actual reason in their being adamant against the truth because it does not agree with their inclinations. (A. P.).

A thoughtless or unintelligent recital of the Word of God is quite different from a serious study of it, to earn the guidance it provides, one has to apply its knowledge to the men and the matters in the world.Let us find out who in Islam has all the qualities enumerated in the above verses of this Surah and who has guarded the prayers to serve as models for us. Taking the observance of the prayers as laid down in this verse, the Muslim world as a whole would unanimously vouch for the fact that the Holy Prophet, Ali,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:90 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:91 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Never did God take unto Him a son and never was there with Him any god - else would each god have certainly taken away what he had created, and some of them would certainly have overpowered others; Far from the glory of God, be what they attribute (unto Him), The conception of other deities has no logical justification unless it is postulated that each is totally differentiated from the other without any aspect common between them. On this postulation the result would be as said here. Hence from the unity and the continuity of the system, the unity of the Author is inferred. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:96 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Repel evil by what is best; We know best what they attribute (against thee). The highest point of Islamic ethics has been given in this verse. To speak of the doctrine of an unconditional and a total surrender against any unprovoked aggression is very easy. What is in the Bible 'Turn the other cheek also if the one is smitten and to give away thy shirt also if the cloak is taken by force' is very easy to be praised and to pride over but the impracticability of the ideal has already been proved by the inability of the Christian authorities themselves to act upon the doctrine. The world can never forget the Edict of Milan against the Jews and the war on Abyssinia which Christendom waged. Mark the wording of the doctrine of goodly return against evil which Islam…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:97 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say thou: "O' my Lord! I seek refuge unto Thee from the (evil) (Suggestion.) promptings of the satans!" The evil suggestions of the Devil are such common experiences of every one of us that the matter needs no elaborate dealing. The maximum amount of faith in man is to seek refuge in the Lord Himself which suggests the conviction of the individual about, God alone being worthy of granting the refuge and the inner-most aspiration of the soul to return to All-goodness, (i.e., God) against the attack from the evil one.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muminoon:98 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: I seek refuge unto Thee O' my Lord! from their (Their presence with me.) access to me With the announcement of the end of the world and the dawn of the Day of Judgment, all family relationship between the members of the human family will be dissolved and every soul will be a separate individual standing upon the merits and the demerits it has earned in its life on earth.

The verses begin with the injunction to the believers not to have any friendly relations with the enemies of God, i.e., with ungodly elements, who would naturally be the enemies of the believers, (who are the godly ones.) item.description: And if any of your wives passeth away from you unto the disbelievers and thereafter ye have your turn (of triumph over the disbelievers) then give unto those whose wives have gone away the like of what they have spent; and fear ye (the wrath of) God in Whom ye believe (Note: the strict justice maintained favouring the legal right of even the disbelievers.) . item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mumtahana:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: 'O' ye those who believe! Those who do not believe in having any sign of the graves at all or opposed to honouring the graves of holy men by reciting the Word of God to invoke the mercy of God on the dead, may note this. Visiting the grave yards and standing at graves and remembering the dead with the recital of the Holy Qur'an and doing some good on behalf of the dead, can never be compared to worshipping the graves, for worship, it will…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mumtahana:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Never shall profit you your relations, nor your children, on the Day of Reckoning; He (alone) will decide between you, and God Seeth All whatsoever ye do (Refer to Verses 2:48; 6:164; 17:15; 35:18; 39:7; 53:38.) . Faith and faithfulness should never be allowed to be corrupted by prejudice for the sake of even the nearest relatives - for none, no member of the family, would be of any avail to anyone on the Day of Judgment - as none would bear the burden of the other1.Any infidel resorting to violence, however close a relative he might be, should be disassociated, similar to what has been done by Abraham. (A.P.)

His real father was Tarakh - Azar was only a patron. Refer to Verse 14:41.) "I shall certainly seek forgiveness for thee, and I own not for thee aught from God; "O' Our Lord! On thee (alone) do we rely; and unto Thee (only) do we turn! and unto Thee (alone) is (our) final return (Refer to Verses 6:74; 19:45.) ." As…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mumtahana:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: 'O' Our Lord! make us not a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us O' Our Lord! Verily Thou art the Ever-Prevalent, the All-Wise. Do not give the disbelievers a triumph over them so that they might be subjected to their cruelties to try them with their patience and on their, (i.e., believers) failures, they are punished by the chastisement from the Lord.The Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq said: "In the days gone by a believer was always a poor man and a disbeliever was always rich - until Abraham came into the world as an Apostle of God who offered this prayer after which poverty and riches were left to each individual's earning, be he a believer or a disbeliever.1"

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mumtahana:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Maybe that God will cause friendship between you and those whom ye take to be your enemies (The enmity being not personal they may change their view.) among them, and God is All- Powerful; and God is Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful. item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Munaafiqoon:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That is because they believe, then (again) disbelieve they, so a seal hath been set upon their hearts, so they understand not (Refer to Verses 2:7; 7:101; 10:74; 16:108; 17:46; 45:23.) .
