item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Munaafiqoon:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When thou seest them, marvel thee (Personalities.) their bodies; and if they speak (The Prophet addressed for the people.) , thou listeneth unto their speech; (they are) as if they were blocks of wood propped up in garments, deem they that every cry is against them, They are the enemy (of yours), so beware thou of them! may God annihilate them, whence do they deviate! Note how aptly the hypocrites are compared to how bits of timber propped up against other things, i.e., they are useless to serve as a reliable support, i.e., they are without faith or any firmness of character. They are unsafe and unreliable props. Their guilty conscience so constantly pricks them that whenever any cry is raised, they think it to be against them, and they get alarmed and whenever there happens any incursion of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Munaafiqoon:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when it is said unto them: "Come ye! the Apostle of God will seek forgiveness for you," they turn back their heads, and thou seest them turning away while they are the arrogant ones. The adamance of the rejectors of the truth has deprived them of God's mercy for the intercession of the Apostle of God, would be available for the unintentional sinners among the believers who owing to their personal weakness and not for those who have adamantly rebelled against God and His Apostle.It does not mean that God refrains, or the Holy Prophet's intervention is of no use, it means that the blessing of God through the intervention of the Holy Prophet would not avail those whose heart is perverted as explained in the verse itself. (A.P.)

The hypocrites did not relish the Madinites helping the believer refugees from Mecca, and went to the extent of dissuading them from doing any good to them.Note how the truth has been presented that God does not leave His devotees to the mercy of the charity of the disbelievers or the hypocrites. item.description: Say they: "If we return to Madina, the honourable ones will certainly drive out the meaner ones; "but for God is all honour and for His Apostle and for the believers, but the hypocrites know (it) not." This is what the Arch-Hypocrite Abdullah Ibn Obai had said - which was reported by Zaid Ibn Arqam1.This is an encouragement for the advocates of the right cause to be sure that they are honoured by God with blessing in spite of the hypocrites and the infidels looking down on them. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Munaafiqoon:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! let not your wealth, nor your children divert you from the remembrance of God; and who-soever doeth that, these are then the losers Any amount of wealth and any number of the issues a man might have, all these sources of the enjoyment of this life are only fleeting fortunes combined with miseries and toils. Nothing of these should be allowed to lead men astray from remembering God actively, i.e., from doing as much good as possible. This verse exposes the truth that it is mostly the wealth and the prosperity of a man that makes man forget God and one's duties to Him. One should be specially guarded against being beguiled by his riches and the other family prosperity.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mursalaat:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By those sent forth with goodness, one after another 'The Sent Forth', i.e., the winds which blow to the profit of everyone in the world.The letter 'Waw' stands to mean swearing.The benefits which the winds give in their flow are so many that they cannot be enumerated here. Everyone knows that they are the powerful factors which serve in innumerable ways. Air is the cause of life on earth. It is the winds that scatter the clouds and distribute the rainfall. It is the wind that gives life to the vegetable world by its cooling effect1. It scatters seeds, it separates the chaff from grains. It cleanses the air of the poisonous and contagious matter in it. It carries the sound from one place to the other. It helps boats and ships to sail in the rivers and the high…

item.description: Then by those that give forth the Reminder See 77:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mursalaat:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In what other word after this will they believe? When such a clear message, the people reject, which is the other message they would accept to believe in? (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mursalaat:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Either justify (the punishment), or to warn See 77:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mursalaat:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, what hath been promised (The Day of Judgement.) unto you shall come to pass (Refer to Verses 51:1 - 51:6.) See 77:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mursalaat:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So, when the stars shall be caused to cease radiating (As the consequence of the cessation of the radiation. Refer to Verses 81:2, 82:2.) See 77:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mursalaat:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when the heaven shall be rent asunder (Refer to Verses 82:1, 73:18.) As the consequence of the radiation, causing gaps in the space. (A.P.)As a consequence of the cessation of the radiation. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Woe unto the defrauders in measuring! Note the perfect justice & fair play Islam stresses in matters of dealing with men. What is meant here by 'Mutaffifeen' are those who exact their dues in full but when they pay their dues to the others, they commit fraud and disburse less. One must give in full what is due from him even if the other side returns the same in full or not.Commentators have given the root of the word and its meaning in details, but Qur'an itselfdefines what it means by this term. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Woe on that day unto the beliers See 83:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who belie the Day of Judgment See 83:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And belieth it not (any one) save every transgressor, a sinner Those who were lost in sinning would only deny such an inevitable event.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When, are recited unto him Our signs (Refer to: 6:25, 68:15.) , sayeth he: (These are only) the stories of yore! They ridicule the Word of God, the Holy Qur'an - and attribute it to the narration of tales of the ancients borrowed from the folklore1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! rather, has rusted their hearts, what they used to do The Holy Prophet said that when a man commits any sin a black dot is created on the heart of the individual and if the man does not repent and continues to sin, the dot covers the whole heart and the whole heart is blackened. The Fifth Holy Imam Muhammad Ibn-Ali Al-Baqir said: ''On the heart of every believer there is a white dot and when he commits any sin, a black dot is created and when the individual repents the black dot disappears and if the individual does not repent and continues to sin, the black dot spreads and gradually covers the whole heart and the white dot disappears and then the individual is totally lost to the evils and gets un-amenable to any amount of admonition".The Sixth…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! verily that day they shall be shut (As a result of their deeds.) out away from the mercy of their Lord It never means that God will hide Himself behind any veil, for such a conception would mean God being confined to a place. He is the Omnipresent. He is the Universally Manifest One. None can hide Him or His glory save the stain of one's own disbelief and evil deeds which sully the heart and destroys its reflectivity so that the heart fails to receive the light and it is the stain on the heart of the individual that disables it to realise the existence of God and enjoy the view of His glory.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, they shall be committed to the flaming fire See 83:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then shall it be said (unto them): ''This is that which ye belied (Refer to: 36:63.) !" See 83:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! The record of the righteous shall be in the 'Illiyun (Refer to: 56:10.) ' i.e., The highest places and most exalted in grades, the nearest approach to divinity. It is in contrast to 'Sijjiyeen' in verse 7 above. It is the place where the records of the righteous ones are preserved.The high stage or state or the right side of the Universe towards the Absolute as appeared to the left side tending towards the material realm and whatever is recorded there is witnessed by conscious entities termed as 'Moqarraboon', here the Near Ones and as 'Aaleen' in 38:75 and as Qur'an expressively asserts the prophets and their Vicegerents - who attain the same purification are also included in the witnesses of 'Illiyeen' and this witnessing is not confined to the beings of the angelical order as some commentators think.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what will make thee know what the 'Illiyun' is (Refer to: 85:21 - 85:22.) ? i.e., None can even imagine correctly what those high places of greatest exaltation could be. They are inconceivable for the intellect of any mortal.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Who, when take they by measure from the people, demand (Considering what has been given to them as less. i.e. holding other's measure as less.) it full (Refer to: 74:6.) Considering what has been given to them is less, i.e., holding others' measure as less. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It is) a book written As in the case of the recording of the evils of the disbelievers and the sinners, mentioned in verse 9 above. The record of the deeds of the ones righteous are perfect in every detail of every motive, words and the deeds of every individual one of the doers of good1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: See it those who are the near ones unto God The Nearest Ones to God witness these records of the righteous ones. Witnessing the records can be interpreted into being present at the recording itself.The nearest to God is said to be the angels highest in purity and excellence but it does preclude to mean the highest spiritual dignitaries who can encourage and help goodness intended to be done by the righteous ones. Who could be nearer to God than the Holy Prophet, the most loved one of God in His whole creation, the Holy Imams whom the Holy Prophet had said to be of the Divine Light of which he himself is. This verse testifies to the truth in the statement that on the Day of Judgment a witness will be called for each people and the Holy Prophet…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the righteous ones shall be in bounteous bliss See 83:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On exalted couches will they view (Refer to: 36:56.) (the delightful sights) See 83:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!') wilt recognise in their faces, the (delightful) radiance of the bliss (Refer to: 75:22, 76:11.) ! See 83:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They shall be provided to quaff of pure drink (which shall be) sealed (Exclusively reserved for them, not allowed to the others, or with sealed purity.) (to others) Could be interpreted as of the maximum purity, and the most delicious in taste.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The seal (being) of musk; For that may aspire (all) those who (wish to) aspire (for bliss) Refers to the extraordinary and special aspect of the value and the flavour.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Mixed therewith shall be the water of 'Tasnim' 'Tasneem' - The name of a spring in heaven whose drink is of super excellence in purity, flavour and taste, purer than the purest of the drinks in this world.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Which is) a spring from which drink the Near Ones (Refer to: 56:11,88, 3:45, 96:19, 19:52.) This verse speaks of the water of the spring being used for the drink of the Nearest Ones to God. It indicates that among the nearest ones are also the human souls like those of the Holy Prophet and the Holy Imams, otherwise, the conception of the need for food and drink for the angels nearest to God does not agree with the nature of the angels who are spirits and energies who need no food or water, and nowhere in the Holy Qur'an is there any statement about the angels eating and drinking. It must be remembered that when the angels appeared to Abraham on the way to Sodom to punish the people of Lot, and when Abraham taking them to be mortals…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily they who are the guilty ones, used to laugh (During their life in the world.) at those who believe According to the well-known commentator Kashshaf, once the First Holy Imam Ali-Ibn Abu Talib along with a group of some poor men of the believers, while going to the Holy Prophet passed a party of the hypocrites who seeing Ali and those with him winked to each other mocking at them. Those hypocrites said: ''We saw today the bald-headed one (Ali was bald in the front portion of his head)''' and mocked at him. Ali had not even reached the Holy Prophet; the Messenger Angel Gabriel revealed these verses condemning the conduct of the hypocrites and praising Ali. (M.S.)According to Ibn-Abbas - by 'Those who are sinful', the reference is to the hypocrites and by 'those who believe' is…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But when they measure unto them, or (when) they weigh unto them, minish (Diminish - reduce - give less.) they (i.e. deceive) When this Surah was revealed, the Holy Prophet went to the open market and amidst the merchants there, read it out and said that the following five evils in the conduct of men, invite the calamities mentioned against each of them:Breaking a promise or any solemn undertaking - Invites the triumph of the enemy.Enjoining on people that which God has not enjoined - Brings poverty and need.Immorality - Brings abundant death.Fraud in measure and weight - Famine, drought and restraint on the produce of foodgrains.Failure to pay the poor-rate and uncharitability - Brings deprivation of the grace and the mercy of God.The First Holy Imam Ali-Ibn Abu Talib, after his official work as the Kalif or the Ruler…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when they pass by them, wink (While in the world.) they at one another See 83:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when return they unto their people, return they jesting See 83:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when they see them, say (While in the world.) they: ''Verily these are the straying ones" See 83:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: While they are sent not over them to be the watchers The reference is to those who mocked at Ali and also those who mocked at the other believers - that they had no business to behave as they did for, they were not posted by God to watch the movements of those righteous ones.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So, today, those who believe shall be at the disbelievers laugh Those who mocked at the righteous ones among the believers - will be made to be mocked at on the Day of Judgment by the believers.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On couches (exalted they shall be) seeing (the delightful sights) The righteous ones or believers will be seen on exalted position enjoying the bliss in heaven seated on the exalted thrones of dignity and excellence.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Shall not the disbelievers be (also) recompensed for what they used to do? The evil return for the conduct of the disbelievers is sure and certain. The arrogant braggarts will certainly he brought low - a recompense for their own disbelief and wickedness.This is an expression in terms of the feelings of an opponent for the adversity of the other just for the sake of warning the disbelievers, that on the Day of Judgment their position will be such that if the believers would be in a retaliative state they would be justified to laugh at them, but in fact it is far above the believers to enjoy the sufferings of the others. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Think they not that they shall (Bound to be raised.) be raised Men are admonished to know and remember that there is the All-Knowing One above all, who knows everything even though people may know it or not - and there is a Day of Judgment when each one has to account for one's own thoughts, words and deeds. Those who think or speak or act wrongly will be disgraced openly on that day and suffer the grievous punishment even for the least evil done by him.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For a Mighty Day (The Day of the Final Judgment.) See 83:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the day when mankind shall stand before the Lord of the worlds? It is said that men will be made to stand in the sun brought over their heads perspiring profusely according to the degree of their individual position in their sins. The heat will be so scorching and strong that it will be melting the elements in the body of the wicked.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! the record of the wicked (Destiny.) hast been preserved in the 'Sajjin' 'Kalla', i.e., No! Never. Will they, the people be able to deny any of the evils they had committed? Hence, they should not commit any fraud in the measure or in the weight.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what will make thee know what 'Sajjin' is? 'Sijjin' is from Sijn, i.e., a prison. It is a place in heaven where the reports or the records of the deeds of men are stored.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Mutaffifin:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is a Book Written It is a written record. It should not be imagined to be a record written by any pen and ink on any paper of the kind we have in our use. It means it is perfect in every detail with regard to the motive, words, needs, attitudes and everything connected with the good and evil of each and every individual sinner and his sins without any exception whatsoever. For example, the tap al-recording of speeches may be taken. Everything spoken is recorded in all its details with regard to words as well as the sound, but nothing is written in the tape. If we mortals could affect such a wonderful implement, what is the thing that the Almighty and All-Wise Lord could not do?

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' thou the Wrapped (The Holy Prophet Muhanmad.) up in thy mantle! 'The Wrapped up' is the address to the Holy Prophet. In the early days, i.e., in the beginning of his ministry, the Holy Prophet used to pray covering his whole body with a big piece of cloth and when this Verse was revealed he was preparing to start his prayers and was wrapped up.It is said whenever the Holy Prophet got into the state of receiving any revelation, he used to feel a shivering in his body and felt the necessity of getting himself covered with some cloth. God liked His most loved Apostle in the state of being covered that He addressed him as the 'Muzzammil', i.e., the Wrapped up one. 'Muzzammil' is also interpreted as the one burdened or charged with (the ministry)1.The term 'Muzzammil' here…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And be thou patient against whatever they say and avoid them with a decorous avoidance The disbelievers and the ungrateful ones among the men who forget the bounties of God bestowed on them and speak nonsense and ridicule the faith and the faithful. These must be ignored and left to themselves in a noble and a respectable way making them realise that the real believer in God does not care for them at all for all his hopes rest only in God and in none else.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And leave Me (to deal), and the beliers, the possessors of the bounties, and respite them a little Those who enjoy the abundance of the bounties of God must be more and more grateful to Him and if they are not, it is God's concern to deal with them duly.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily with Us are strong fetters and the flaming fire When a tooth pain made one restless, the First Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abu Talib said 'When a small lot of bone could make man feel so much and make him restless, what would the chastisement on the Day of Judgment do to man and how would he bear it.'

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The food that choketh, and a painful chastisement See 73:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the day when the earth and mountains shall be shaken and mountains shall become heaps of sand, rendered loose The dawn of the Day of Judgment would cause such a violent commotion that it would change the whole face of the physical world affecting violently the laws of nature working in them. The hard rocks of the mountains would suffer the loss of cohesion within their matter and the mountains will be turned into heaps of loose sand.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, we have sent unto you an Apostle, a witness against you, as sent We an Apostle unto Pharaoh (Refer to Verses 10:75 - 10:92.) See 73:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But Pharaoh disobeyed the Apostle, whereupon We seized him with a severe (a violent seizure.) seizure Pharaoh disobeyed God's laws and defied God's authority - what happened to him? God's laws must stand and shall be fulfilled and all else shall be swept away and vanish - The wisdom, authority, power and the might of the forces of Pharaoh had been of no avail to him by one surprise from the Divine will, all vanished away for ever.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: How, then, will ye guard yourselves, if ye disbelieve, against the day which shall turn children greyheaded? If man defies the authority of the Lord in this life which is only a period of probation, what will he do on the day of the Final Requital which will be a day of the terrible manifestation of the reality. The transformation of the present into the hereafter will be so terrible and violent that even young children would be shocked so much that they will look like hoary-headed old men and the skies will be cleft asunder 82:1. The state of affairs will undergo a violent change manifesting the true value of everything in the uniVerse.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The heaven shall be rent asunder by it; His promise is always made to be fulfilled God's promise of justice being meted out to every individual being and everyone being duly recompensed for one's own good and evil, shall be fulfilled.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily this is a reminder, let him, whoso will, adopt unto his Lord, the (Right) way! The Holy Qur'an is a reminder to those who sincerely wish to know the right course to earn the grace and the mercy of the Lord. Repentance with the due amendment in the practical life is highway to obtain the forgiveness and the mercy of the Lord and getting nearer to Him.From Verse 1-19 the Verses themselves speak of themselves to belong to the early period of the Holy Prophet's ministry. From the 10th to 19th the Verses show that they belong to the period when the opposition had started - The Verse 20 with its length is obvious that it belongs to the period when 'jehad' was enforced and there is no single tradition to show that this Chapter had a different arrangement…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Rise thou in the night to pray (Reference to 'Tahajjud' prayer.) but a little! (and not for the whole night) (Refer to Verse 17:79.) In the beginning, the believers had to offer the midnight 'Tahajjud' prayers. The people did not know the exact hour when they had to pray and hence, they used to keep awake the whole night in prayers. The merciful Lord had to reveal His will that they had to stand in prayers only for a small part of the night and not for the whole of it.This prayer, i.e., 'Tahajjud' is optional with the highest recommendation to offer it to achieve spiritual progress.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, thy Lord knowest that thou standest up (in the Night- Prayer) nigh (About) two-thirds of the night, and (sometimes) half of it, and (sometimes) a third (As ordered in Verses 73:2 and 73:3.) of it, and a group (Ali, Abu Dharr, have been particularly mentioned in the tradition about this Verse) of those with thee; and God measureth (well) the night and the day; Knoweth He that never can ye take (correct) account of it, so turneth He unto you (mercifully), so recite ye whatever be easy (As the Verse deals with the facilities given in the night prayer the recitation of Qur'an refers to the portions to be recited in prayers.) (in the prayers) to be read of the Qur'an; Knoweth He that there may be among you sick, and others travelling in the earth seeking of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Half of it or curtail of it a little! See 73:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or add to it, and intone the Qur'an in a regulated tone! The choice to increase the duration of prayer is left to the individuals.The recital of the Holy Qur'an is not to be in a hurry or hasty, just for the purpose of covering the passage. It has to be recited slowly in studious way and the beauty of the Word of God has to be manifested in an attractive tone observing duly the punctuation.This indicates that the Holy Prophet already knew the Qur'an and he was only ordered to recite it in a well-measured way. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily soon will We send down upon thee (some) weighty words (Refer to Verses 94:2; 94:3.) The 'Weighty word' is the Holy Qur'an - The Holy Prophet has addressed the Holy Qur'an and his Ahl Al-Bayt as 'Thaqalayn' the two weighty things. (Tafsir al-Kabir, D.M., etc.) Thus the Ahl Al-Bayt and the Holy Qur'an are of equal weight or importance to mankind, the Holy Qur'an being the Word of God and the Ahl Al-Bayt the godly means to understand it duly i. e., The responsibility of guiding mankind which is termed here as weighty words but in 94:2 and 94:3 as a burden for which he required an assistant in the manner that Moses required Aaron to assist him - as hinted in Verse 15. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the rising at night when impression is intense and straightest in words Note how Islam wants man to avail of the best time in the nature of the day and night for concentration, meditation, supplication and for disciplining the soul to get into communion with the All-Divine. Night is the time when the world seeking the material profit in the earth gets practically all still, silent and when there is the cessation of voices of the day time, which distract and even destroy contemplation, concentration and meditation it is the best and most suitable time for a human soul to get mindful of its Creator Lord. Only those who get up at midnight and engage themselves in prayers would know the realisation of the communion with their Lord and how the soul gets tranquilled.In the night prayer the attitude…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily thou hast in the day long occupation (For serving the Lord and for the legitimate purpose of self - For propagating the truth - for doing as much good as possible before death - none knows, when) See 73:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And remember thou, the name of thy Lord, and devote thyself unto Him with an exclusive devotion 'Tabattul' to cut away one's self and get communion exclusive, with the Lord - The Holy Lady Fatimah, the daughter of the Holy Prophet is called 'Batool' for she used to turn to God in prayers, disconnecting herself from everything in the world, or for her life as a whole being dedicated exclusively to God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Muzzammil:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Lord of the East and the West, there is no god but He, take Him then as the Protector! This is also to be a counter to the false and the imaginary belief of the heathens about the existence of regional gods and the local and the other deities. It is to say that God is the Lord of the whole uniVerse, and no part of the world is out of His control and authority. Hence the believers need not fear anyone besides God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Striking Calamity! 'Qariah', i.e., a tremendously clamorous striking noise which will accompany the inauguration of the great calamity, the earth will suffer at the dawn of the Day of Judgment when the whole of the present order of the world will undergo a thorough change giving place to a totally new atmosphere of a new state of the existence of a new world of a new order of realities with total wiping out of all false appearances and false values.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What maketh thee know what 'Haviah' is? As man in this life cannot rightly imagine the like of what the 'Qariah' mentioned in the verse 1 above, will be, he cannot correctly visualise the likeness of the abyss called 'Haviah' which will be the abode of the wicked.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is a Raging Fire The simplest note of description of the abyss 'Haviah' is that it is a blazing fire and the rest of it to be experienced and known when it is given to the wicked on the Day of Judgment.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What is the Striking Calamity? Since anything similar to the terrible experience of the clamorous noise mentioned here, has never been experienced by anyone in the world, it is an impossibility even to correctly imagine what the noise would be like.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What maketh thee know what the Striking Calamity is? See 101:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The day when people shall be like moths scattered Out of the terror, the clamorous voice will create in the minds of the people they will be running bewildered on all sides in tumultuous multitude - out of the fear and the tumult each falling over the other, like the tiny insignificant being, the moths scattered by a violent stormy wind. This is to give an imaginable view of the confusion and distress and helplessness man will be thrown into, all of a sudden.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the mountains shall become like wool carded (Loosened. Refer to: 70:9.) When even the solid and immovably and unshakably fixed huge mountains will be scattered in the atmosphere, like the insignificant flakes of the carder's wool1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then as for him whose scales (Refer to: 57:25, 55:8, 42:17, 77:20 - 77:21.) (with good deeds) are heavy On that day nothing but the deeds, good and bad will be counted. The appraisement, valuation measuring or the weighing, will be strictly to the real value of each deed and deed means any deed of the physical body given to man and as well as the activity of the mind, i.e., the various faculties he has been endowed with. Every action physical and mental will be weighed viz., the motives, passions, thoughts, imagination, feelings, aspirations, love, hatred, the degree of faith in God anil the extent of the disbelief in Him, and the attitudes etc. And whosoever's measure of his good deeds will exceed the measure of his evils, will receive the blissful life with which he will naturally be…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He shall be in a life, well pleased with See 101:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And as for him whose scales (with good, deeds) are light And whosoever's evils will exceed his good deeds will be thrown into the abyss -and 'Haviah' is interpreted to be the abyss or the depth the bottom being immeasurably low in an unfathomable depth.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qaari'a:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: His home shall be 'Haviah' (a burning abyss (It may also mean tending towards the abyss.) ) See 101:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qadr:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, We sent it (The Qur'an) down in the Night of 'Qadr' (Grandeur. Refer to: 2:185, 44:3.) ! The word 'Qadr' may mean - Power, Grandeur, Majesty.'Lailat al-Qadr', i.e., the Night of Grandeur of the Lord - is kept a secret. The verse 2 below clearly means that none knows, what the night is, i.e., which night in the year it is and the special value of it, to its fullest extent.The various statements of the commentators are:Some say it is concealed in the whole month of Shahan.Some say it is the 14th of Shaban.Some say it is one of the nights of Ramadhan.But the majority of the commentators agree on its being one of the odd nights in the latter half of the month of Ramadhan - commonly agreed to be 19th, 21st, 23rd, 25th, 27th and the 29th…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qadr:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What can make thee know what the Night of 'Qadr' is? The question put in this verse, is a clear indication of the mystic nature and value of the Night of Grandeur which none else but the Lord knows. The succeeding verses only defined the night with its value and do not say which night in the year it is.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qadr:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Night of 'Qadr' is better than a thousand month! The announcement here in this verse about the night, refers to the greatness of the Night.The Second Holy Imam Hasan Ibn-Ali says that he heard from his grandfather, the Holy Prophet, that once he dreamt of monkeys getting upon his pulpit, and the Messenger Angel Gabriel informed him of the significance of the dream saying that ''Those whom thou dost see get upon thy pulpit are the Bani-Umayyah who would rule the Muslim Empire after thee for a thousand months" And revealed this verse.Quoting 32:4 - 32:5 and 70:4, a commentator says that the term "A Thousand, must be taken in an indefinite sense, i.e., a timeless time - and interprets it to mean that one moment if enlightenment under God's light is better than thousands of months or the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qadr:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Angels and the Spirit descend therein by the permission of their Lord, with (decrees) of all affairs (Refer to: 16:2, 78:38.) It is said that angels and holy spirits descend on earth with the special blessings from God and peace for those who seek them through prayers, supplications to the Lord1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qadr:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Peace is (the whole Nighty)! till the breaking of the dawn! Taking the mystic word 'Night of Grandeur' as one of the sacred nights, in any of the months mentioned above, this verse would mean that the shower of the special boon and the great blessings of God, promised to the sincere devotees that night, continues until the dawn of the succeeding day.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: 'Nun' and (N) by the Pen and by what they write The letter with which this Sura begins is supposed to mean the Inkpot from which the pen gets the matter (the ink) with which is the writing is affected to spread knowledge and learning into this world. The pen represents the written form of the Will of the Lord about the creation and the events to be affected in the countless generations from the beginning of the world to its end. The inkpot and the pen mentioned here have a mystic expression of the source of the knowledge through the ret elation front God. When a thing gets common or abundant in quantity, however much it may be invaluable in its worth, man does not note its original value. Take for instance air and water which are essential for…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And yield thou not unto any despicable swearer (Refer to Verse 2:224.) See 68:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Defamer, going about with slander See 68:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Vehement hinderer of good, uncontrolled transgressor, sunk deep in sin See 68:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Cruelly violent, besides all that, baseborn (Ar. 'Zaneem', He whose father is not known, and whose mother is unchaste. He is a base born.) 'Zaneen' a product of adultery. Walid who was a Qoreishite chief, did not know that he owned the quality. When this Verse was revealed, Walid said to himself. "I am the Qoreishite Chief and Mughaira is known to be my father, I am also sure that Muhammad never utters a falsehood" He got wild, drew his sword and with a drawn sword went to his mother and asked her to tell him the truth about his parentage. She had to helplessly disclose saying "Look! Thy father Mughaira was unfit for any woman. Since I had no issues from him, his brother's sons coveted to inherit the enormous wealth of thy father Mughaira. I did not like…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Just because possesses he wealth and sons Abundance of wealth and male issues was a matter of pride. It is not uncommon among the people even today. People who are puffed up with wealth and the largeness of the number of their family members, are in the view of the Lord branded as rebellious. A believer is not to heed to such worldly possessions and positions.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When unto him are recited Our signs, sayeth he: (they are the) "Stories of yore" (legends of the ancients) (Refer to Verses 6:25, 83:13.) Nose being the most prominent or the raised part of the face, is always used to indicate the proud part of it and it is a popular proverb to rub the nose of one on the ground or to cut or disfigure it, is to degrade or humiliate the individual. Walid Ibn Mughaira was branded with a wound in the Battle of Badr, the mark of which remained to his shame and disgrace until his death. (Bd., Rz., MS)(Kartoom) literally means the proboscis, the most sensitive part of elephant's body by which he could very easily be controlled, the rebellious one against God is compared to have been degenerated to a beast.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We will brand him (Walid Ibn Moghaira.) on the snout! The story of the sons of the charitable man related in these Verses serves a double purpose. It gives the state of the conduct of the enemies of the Holy Prophet and the hypocrites, and it also illustrates how the unlimited mercy of the Lord allows wickedness to flourish for some time, allowing the respite for the individuals to turn to the right course. This also refers to the long patience which the infinite mercy of the Lord allowing the individual to behave as they please and then effecting the punishment in gradual stages, allowing chance after chance for the sinner at every stage to repent and rectify, his conduct. The story illustrates how greed and selfishness and the love of wealth, take a man away from the right course…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily We will try them as We did try the owners of the garden, when they vowed that they would certainly pluck the fruits at morn See 68:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And made no (room for) exception (for the will of God) (saying 'If God willeth it') (In complete conformity with Verses 18:23; 18:24.) See 68:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So encircled it a visitation from thy Lord, (rendering the garden desolate) while they were asleep See 68:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thou (O' Our Prophet!) by the grace of thy Lord, art not mad The reference is to what the heathens of Mecca in the beginning of his ministry called the Holy Prophet as 'Majnun' (i.e., mad). The people said: what the Holy Prophet preached was the raving of a mad man - whereas it was the Word of God which was recorded in writing by the angels.Being always under God's special guidance as Ali says that 'Ever since his (the Holy Prophet) birth was tinder the care of the greatest of angels, guiding him to all aspects of life. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And it became like black barren soil (Or reaped land.) See 68:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they cried out one unto each other at morn See 68:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Be ye early at your tilth if ye would pluck (the fruits) (Refer to Verse 3:117.) See 68:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And went they whispering unto each other See 68:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Saying: "No poor man shall enter it today upon you" See 68:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And at morn went they, strong in their resolve (to prevent the poor) See 68:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But when they beheld it, said they: "Verily we have strayed!" See 68:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! we are (the) deprived ones (of the fruits of our labour).'' Ibn Abbas says that the sons thereafter repented, and God of His infinite mercy accepted their repentance and granted them a better garden of a greater, i.e., of a more profuse yield. This indicates also that sincere repentance on the part of sinners, earns the pardon from the Lord and the Lord rewards the sincerely repentant ones with greater blessings and bestows more bounties.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said the most balanced one of them: "Said I not unto you, 'Why should ye not glorify (God)'?" See 68:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "Hallowed be Our Lord! Verily we have been unjust!" See 68:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily there is for thee a recompense unending (unobliging) The return or the recompense for the Holy Prophet being a continuous and an unending flow of the Grace and the Mercy of the Lord. The reward which unlike any earthly bounty, would never cease or never fail him.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then some of them proceeded against the others, reproaching each other See 68:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "O' woe unto us! Verily we have been arrogant! (Inordinate – Transgressing. Refer to Verses. 34:18, 34:19.) " See 68:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Happly, our Lord will give us in exchange a better one than it; Verily unto our Lord do we turn (in repentance) See 68:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Such hath been Our chastisement, and certainly the chastisement of the hereafter is greater still; Did they but know (it)! (Refer to Verse 39:26.) The punishment in this life might be gradual with the respite for repentance and amendment but in the hereafter, the time for the repentance would have passed and thus the punishment, meted out would naturally be in full.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, for the pious ones (Those who guard themselves against evil.) with their Lord are the Gardens of bliss Those who guard themselves against evil. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! shall We then make the 'Muslims' (Those who submit themselves to God.) like unto the guilty ones (Refer to Verses 6:50, 45:21.) ? See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What is the matter with you? How judge ye (An appeal to Commonsense, Refer to Verses 52:32 - 52:34.) See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or have ye a scripture wherein ye read? See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, therein is for you what ye choose? See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or have ye a sworn covenant from Us tending to the Day of Judgment that ye shall surely have whatever ye judge? See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And most certainly thou standest on sublime morality (Character. See Verses 2:143, 33:45, 33:21.) The character which the Holy Prophet was endowed with was so matchless that none could reach its limits. The Holy Prophet's is a historic personality. Every detail of his character, even the minutest aspect of it, has been noted and recorded both by his friends and his foes. It was the sword of the ideal heavenly character and godly conduct that subdued the man like Omar to join the ranks of the Muslims. To cite even a very few instances of his marvellous behaviour would need separate volume. It is said that one can visualise his personality in the mirror of the tenets of the Holy Qur'an. But I would say that one can visualise Qur'an in the personality of the Qur'an. It is not merely…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ask them (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) which of them will guarantee that! See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or have they any 'Partners' (to Us)? Then let them bring their partners (associate gods) if they be truthful! See 68:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the Day that the shin (When befalleth the affliction.) shall be laid bare, (i.e. befalleth an affliction), and they shall be called upon to prostrate in obeisance, but they shall not be able (to do it) When the anklets shall he disclosed stands for the vanishing of all pretences and mysteries and the reality about each individuals faith and conduct being laid bare, i.e., fully manifested. Some commentators interpret it as 'the day when the affair shall become hard and formidable and say that the origin of the expression is in the fright and the flight and the tucking up of the garments to facilitate fleeing from any dreadful situation. When all the secrets of every individual will be laid bare (MS).Ibn Abbas says that the Holy Prophet said that: of all the situations on the Day of Judgment,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Casting down their looks, shall cover them abasement, and indeed they had been called upon to prostrate in obeisance, while yet they were whole (Healthy Ones.) (healthy) 'Saalimoon' whole - with the sense of judgment and the strength of executing their will in tact - not constrained and yet they did not act as commanded by God - Their mind and body in a wholesome state and yet they abstained from adoring the Lord in their mind, on earth.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So leave Me and him who belieth this announcement, We will lead them on (to ruin) by steps (Taking them by degrees. Refer to Verse 7:182.) from whence they know not Since the conduct of the people worried the Holy Prophet much, to console him, God told him to leave the matter of those who reject His Word to Himself to deal with them.When anyone in spite of wickedness seems to us to flourish it may be, that the punishment is evolutionary and gradual. The ways of the Lord are mysterious and His plans none can ever know or understand beforehand1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And yet respite (Refer to Verses 3:178, 7:183.) them; for verily My device (Scheme – plan.) is firm Respite is given to the sinners and the disbelievers but if it is not availed of, then, the punishment is enforced.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or askest (Neither dost thou ask any recompense for them to feel burdened of the demand.) thou from them a recompense that they are burdened with a load of debt (Refer to Verse 52:40.) ? See 68:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or with them is the knowledge of the unseen, that they write (it) down (Refer to Verse 52:41.) ? See 68:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So wait thou patiently for the judgment of thy Lord! Be not thou like unto the Companion (Zun-Noon – Jonah. Refer to Verses 3:134, 12:84, 40:18, 6:87, 10:98, 21:87, 37:139.) of the fish! when cried he when he was confined (Despair - imprisoned – isolated.) 'Companion of the fish', i.e., 'Zun-Noon' or Jonah1 - There is a mention of Jonah and his people in 6:87 and 10:98. Who thought that he would not be put into hardship by God. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Had not a bounty from his Lord reached him, he would certainly have been cast forth on the naked shore while in disgrace The use of 'Lau la' had not - acquits the apostle Yunus of all possible blame and makes him worthy of being chosen. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So thou wilt see and they (too) wilt see When the Qoreish (the Meccans) found the Holy Prophet always speaking high of Ali, assigning to him a unique position next only to himself, they taunted saying that the Holy Prophet has gone mad in his love for Ali - 'Muhammad Ibn Sama' reports of Ka'b Ibn Alzah and Abdullah Ibn Masood that once when they were in the presence of the Holy Prophet a man asked him about the personal excellence of Ali to which the Holy Prophet replied: -Ali Ibn Abi Taleb is Foremost in Islam among you and none else before him, mas blessed with this degree in faith.The degree of faith of Ali, is greater than that of all of you.His patience is always triumphant against you all.His anger in the matters of faith is more justified…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then chose him his Lord and made him of the righteous ones (Refer to Verse 21:87.) See 68:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who disbelieve would almost smite thee with their eyes (Angry looks.) when they hear the Reminder, and say they: "Verily he is mad" 'Smiting with eye', i.e., the disbelievers having become helpless against the irresistible truth in the message of the Holy Qur'an, now gaze at the Holy Prophet as if they would smite him, if not with any other weapon, at least with their sight, their evil eye, which was in vain.The Verse apparently depicts the attitude of the angry looks of the disbelievers whenever they heard the recitation of Qur'an and their remarks against the Holy Prophet, but most of the commentators have given a different account for the revelation of this passage, i.e., the disbelievers' attempts to do harm to the Holy Prophet through the stroke of the evil eye. That may be true but…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And it is naught but a Reminder unto the worlds (the whole Mankind) See 68:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Which of you is demented (Fascinated – crazy.) The appeal is to reasoning in view of the factual position of the enemies of the Holy Prophet who were ultimately befooled by their disbelief what was the ultimate position of Walid-Ibn Mughaira, Abu Jehl and Abu Lahab.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily thy Lord! He knoweth best of him who is astray from His way, and He knoweth best of those guided aright This Verse warns man against the false standards and the wrong and the mistaken standpoints of judgment about men and matters. The correct viewpoint is always that of God Whose knowledge of every being in the Universe is complete and all-comprehending. To Him alone are known the hidden motives and the open conduct of men. It is He and He alone Who knows the past in which are embedded the roots of the present and also the future of everyone, which is always generated from the present. Hence the value which man assesses to anyone is not always the true or the correct one. The praise of the Ahl Al-Bayt is by God1 and the praise of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So yield (The Prophet addressed for the people.) thou not to the beliers! Though the address is to the Holy Prophet - which means a consolation to him against the offending remarks of the hypocrites, but it means a command to the Ummat (the Muslims) not to be deluded by the false estimation about anyone if they have to earn the approval and the pleasure of God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qalam:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Wish they that thou shouldst be pliant so they (too) would be pliant (Compromising.) The hateful qualities mentioned in this Verse refer to the personal qualities of the enemies of the Holy Prophet, particularly the hypocrites who doubted about the bonafide of the statement of the Holy Prophet about the unique excellence of the holy personality of Ali.As the guided ones shall never be compromising with their opponents (the unguided ones). (A.P.)There, such people depicted in the Verses above, cannot be guided. Therefore they should not be followed. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nigh hath come the Hour (of Reckoning) and hath been rent asunder the Moon (The Sign demanded has been given and there is no excuse for disbelief.) The miraculous event of moon getting rent asunder as mentioned in this verse has been vouched by many reliable authorities from among the companions of the Holy Prophet viz., Ibn Mas'ood, Anas Ibn Malik, Huzaifa al-Yamani, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Jabir Ibn Mat'am. The evidence vouching the incident is strong and so abundant that even the Ahmadi commentator (M.A.) who habitually interprets every miracle into a metaphorical expression has accepted the incident to have taken place (M.A.).Besides the large number of the witnesses to the incident, there are the holy Ahl Al-Bayt whose evidence is always unquestionable.Since commentators say that the prophetic past tense used is to mean the incident to happen in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So he called upon his Lord (saying): 'Verily, I am overcome (by these people), so give help' See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So opened We the gates of heaven with water pouring down See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We caused the earth to break forth like springs and water from the heavens and the earth met together for the purpose verily destined See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We bore him on a thing (The Ark of Noah.) made of planks and nails See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It floated on, before Our eyes, a recompense for those who had been rejected (The Apostles.) (by the infidels) See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, We have left it (the Ark) as a sign, but is there one to remember (it) (The Warning. For the different Signs left for mankind refer to the following Verses: 15:77; 25:37; 26:121, 29:35; 51:37; 54:15.) ? See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: How (great) was then My chastisement and My warning! See 54:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, have We made Qur'an easy (for remembrance (For men to be mindful and get admonished.) ), but is there one to remember (it)? Unlike any other sacred scripture, the Holy Qur'an is not only abundant with the highestphilosophy governing the life secular as well as spiritual, but also full of illustration of the fate of the disbelievers and those who rebelled against the laws prescribed by the Lord. It contains warnings against disbelief, and the evil ways of life and is a perfect code of the laws essential, to discipline the human life in this world.With all these beautiful and wonderful qualities, it is simple, plain and easy to understand. Thus, there remains no excuse for any one with the com non sense, not to avail of the admonition.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Belied (the truth) (the people of) 'Ad, then how (great) was My chastisement and My warning! (Refer to Verse 69:7.) The reference is to the violent stormy wind which lasted for seven nights and eight days1.For the people of Ad see Verses 7:65 to 7:72; 11:50 to 11:60; 44:15 and 44:16.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Lo!) Verily sent We on them a violent wind, on a Day of constant ill-luck (Constant calamity.) See 54:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they see a sign, turn they away and say (that it is) sorcery continued (Constant.) In spite of the people witnessing the great incident they turned away and did not embrace the truth. Ibn Abbas solemnly affirms that he saw the Mount Hira interposing between the two parts of the split Moon.The second verse clearly asserts that the Splitting of the Moon, had taken place as a Sign which the disbelievers interpreted as continued sorcery. For the denial of this and the apostleship they will be punished as said in Verses 9-15. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Flinging the people away, as if they were palm-trunks uprooted See 54:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: How (great) was then My chastisement and My warning! (Refer to Verses 54:30; 54:32; 54:39.) See 54:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, have We made Qur'an easy (to remember), but is there one to remember (To receive the warning.) (it)? (Refer to the note on 'Tahrif' in the introduction.) See 54:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (The people of) Thamood belied the warners (Every warning. Refer to Verse 41:17.) For the people of Thamud see 7:73 to 7:79; 11:61 to 11:68; 44:17 and 44:18.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said they: 'What! A single man, from among us! and we to follow him? Verily then (In that case.) we shall be astray and in distress (People believed that a warner or an apostle from God cannot be a man. Either God Himself should come or He should send at least some angel. Besides, they thought a single lonely man could not be a warner & could not be followed.) ' This is the mental altitude against God's Vicegerency of a single, and a representative character of a single man as an Absolute authority to be followed, common to all the opponents of the absolute theocracy. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: 'Is it that (the duty of) reminding hath been bestowed on him (alone), of all the (people) among us? Nay! He is a great liar, an insolent one!' See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Soon they shall know on the morrow, (as to) who is the liar, the Insolent One! (Refer to Verses 26:141 - 26:158.) See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (O' Our Apostle Saleh!) verily We are going to send the she- camel as a trial for them; so watch them and be patient See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (thou O' Saleh!) make them aware (beforehand) that the water is (to be) divided (Shared.) between them (The She Camel and the people.) ; and every drinking share shall be witnessed (Be present there.) (on it) (Refer to Verses 26:155; 26:156.) See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But they called their companion, then he pursued (her) and hamstrung (her) (The She Camel.) See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they belie (it), and follow they their vain inclinations (Lust, desires.) and every affair is unalterably fixed (Refer to Verse 33:62.) Everything has an end, similarly the rule of evil, and the persecution of the truthful shall also one day end, and the matter against the evil shall be settled for ever,

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: How (great) was My chastisement and My warning? See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily sent We upon them a single (violent) blast, and they were (all) like the dry stubble used by a fencer in a fence (Refer to Verses 7:78; 36:53.) See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, have We made Qur'an easy (to remember) but is there any rememberer? See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The people of Lot belied the warners (Refer to Verses 11:74 - 11:83.) See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily sent We upon them a stone-storm, (which destroyed them all) save the followers of Lot; We saved them by early dawn (Refer to Verses 11:82; 17:68; 29:40; 67:17.) See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (As) a bounty from unto Us; Thus do We recompense him who giveth thanks See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, he did warn them of Our severe seizure, but they did dispute about the warner (Refer to Verses 11:78; 11:79.) See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, they did demand him (Lot.) of his guests (for their evil desert), so did We blind their eyes (saying)'. 'Taste ye then My chastisement and My warning!' See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, dawned on them in the morn a lasting chastisement See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Now taste ye My chastisement and My warning! (Refer to Verse 36:63.) See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, hath come unto them some of the tidings wherein is restraint (from evil) The warning given in the past through the preceding apostles of God is hinted.The recounting of the sins of past generations, having been punished with exemplary punishments, when they belied the messengers sent to them with the message of Allah, should open the eyes of the disbelievers and check them in their obstinate belying and sinning. For a time, godlessness seems to triumph, but this triumph is short-lived.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, have We made Qur'an easy (to he remembered) (For men to be mindful and get admonished.) but is there any one to remember (it) (To receive the warning.) ? See 54:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, came unto the people of Pharaoh the warners (Or the warnings, Moses and Aaron.) For Musa and Firawn refer to Surah Ta Ha, 20:9 to 20:98.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They belied all Our signs so did We seize them after the manner of the one the Ever Prevalent (Aziz in Arabic.) , the All-Mighty One See 54:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Are your disbelievers (O' ye Meccans!) better people than these? Or is there an exemption (Immunity.) for you in the sacred Scriptures? A reference to the fate of the disbelievers at the Battle of Badr. It was the triumph of the truth against falsehood.These verses refer to the battle of Badr. Refer to Surah 'Ali Imran, 3:10 to 3:13; Anfal, 8:5 to 8:19 and 8:42 to 8:48.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or say they: "We are a host joined together to help each other? (Refer to Verse 8:7. This is a prophecy made before the Muslims coming into power and the fate of the disbelievers (A.P.).)" See 54:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Soon shall the host be routed, and they shall turn their backs This is a prophecy long before the Muslims coming into power. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! The Hour (of Reckoning) is their promised time, and the Hour shall be most grievous and bitter The Day of Judgment will be the most grievous and most bitter experience for the disbelievers.The unjust men are puffed up with pride on account of their numbers and their resources, but more often they are punished in this world, and certainly in the hereafter. Their punishment is for ever. The unjust think that the godly are straying, and mad, particularly when they are in power and in the enjoyment of all the good things of this life. Refer to Sura Ya Sin 36:63 to 36:67.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the guilty ones are straying and mad (in distress) (Refer to Verse 54:24.) The disbelievers would then, i.e., on the Day of Judgment, realise that it was they, who had gone astray1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On that Day they shall be dragged upon their faces into the fire (and it will be said unto them)'. 'Taste ye (now) the touch of Hell! (Refer to Verse 36:63.) ' See 54:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily every thing have We created to a determined measure Everything and every event happen strictly according to God's plan.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Consummate wisdom, but (they) availed not (of) the warnings (Or of the warners.) See 54:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And Our command is but one (word 'Be'! And it becometh) like the twinkling of an eye (Refer to Verses 2:117; 16:40; 19:35; 36:82; 40:68.) Refer to Verses 2:117; 16:40; 19:35; 36:82; 40:68.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, have We destroyed the like unto you, but is there any one to receive the warning? (To get admonished, or warned) Refer to the references mentioned in the commentary of verses 54:9 to 54:16; 54:18 to 54:21; 54:23 to 54:32; 54:33 to 54:39; 54:41 and 54:42 of this surah for the destruction of the disbelievers.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And everything they have done is in the books (of deeds) (Refer to Verse 36:12.) See 54:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Every matter small and big, is (correctly) recorded in writing (Refer to Verse 25:29.) See 54:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, the pious ones shall be in gardens and rivers (Blissful life.) See 54:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In the seat of Truth, with the Sovereign Omnipotent One (In direct communion. Refer to Verse 3:167.) See 54:51

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So withdraw from them thyself (O Our Apostle Muhammad!) On the day when the Caller shall call them unto the hard task (of Reckoning) (Refer to Verse 20:108.) The call for the great Day of Reckoning which will be a terrible affair for the disbelievers and the evil doers. For the caller to the Day of Judgment1.for the callers who will summon all created beings on the day of reckoning and direct them to the presence of the Lord of the worlds. It will be terrible day for the disbelievers.Five of the stories of the sins of past generations are referred to in the verses 9 to 42 of this surah.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: With their eyes cast down, they shall go forth from their graves as if they were locusts scattered (Refer to Verses 6:73; 36:51; 36:52; 39:68; 50:20.) It is the most appropriate illustration of the people stunned, rising up in swarms from their graves and getting scattered saying 'Woe unto us'.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hastening unto the Caller; Shall say the disbelievers: 'This is a hard day!' See 54:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qamar:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Belied before them the people of Noah (their apostles), so they belied Our servant and said they (he was) "Mad (Called him mad.) " and he was driven out (Refer to Verses 11:25 - 11:48.)" Who has raised us, why have we been resurrected1. They shall hasten on to the Lord. See also Verses 6:74, 78:18, 39:68, 50:20.For the people of Nuh refer to Verses 7:59 to 7:64; 11:25 to 11:48; 23:23 to 23:25 to 23:48; 26:105 to 26:122.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ta Seen Meem (T. S. M.) See 28:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the heart of the mother of Moses became tranquilled; she was about to disclose it had We not strengthened her heart so that she might be of the believers (in Our promise) See 28:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said she unto his (Moses'.) sister, "Follow him!" And she watched him from afar: while they (Pharaoh & bis people.) perceived it not, See 28:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And already forbade We on him all fostermothers ere (his sister cometh there) and said: "Shall (This is what Moses' sister told Pharaoh's wife & the others there with her.) I guide you unto the people (Refer to verses 33:33 & 66:5.) of a house who will take care of him for you, and they will (also) wish well of him." Moses was forbidden to suck any milk except that of his mother. This was a Divine Plan to restore the baby to the restless mother and at the same time to give Moses the sustenance pure and holy viz., his own mother's milk, for his body to be erected with the sustenance containing the excellence of character and conduct as the spiritual heritage of his ancestry. It is worth mentioning that it is a historic event that when Ali…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So We did restore him unto his mother that her eye might be refreshed (Rejoiced.) and that she might not grieve, and that she might know that the promise of God is (always) true, but most of them know not. See 28:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when he reached the (age of) strength and was full-grown, (State of perfect equity.) We granted him wisdom and knowledge; Thus do We recompense those who do good. Hukm - authority, i.e., Apostleship.The stage of 'Istawa' - Equity in the course of rise to the status of apostleship is so important without which the attainments are impossible, i.e., the state of complete balance in viewing both aspects of the creation - manifest and hidden. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
