item.description: And he entered the city at a time when unvigilant were its people, and found he therein two men fighting: the (Lit. This.) one, of his own party; and the other (Lit. This.) of his enemies; And the one of his own party sought his help against the one who was of his enemies, and Moses smote him with his fist and (Killed him. Refer to verse 28:33.) passed (death) on him; Said (Moses): "This (The man who was killed.) is of the Satan's doing; verily, he is an enemy, an open misleader." Moses found an Egyptian who was Pharaoh's cook, beating a poor helpless Israelite who sought help from Moses. Moses asked the Egyptian to leave away the poor Israelite and when he did not cease beating the poor man, Moses rendered a blow by his fist just to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Moses): "O' my Lord! Verily I have hurt mine own self, so grant Thou refuge to me!" So granted He refuge to him, (against his enemies); Verily, He is Oft-Forgiving, the All-Merciful. Fearing the Egyptians would wreak vengeance on him for the death of the Egyptian, Moses prayed to God to keep his deed hidden from the Israelites. 'Faghfirli', meaning protect me, i.e., keep me covered from the sight of the men of Pharaoh.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Moses): "O' My Lord! because (Due to.) of the grace Thou hast bestowed on me, never shall I be a supporter of the guilty." This dearly indicates that Moses killed the criminal one, helping the helpless oppressed one.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And in the morn he, in the city, passed full of fear apprehending when lo! he who sought his help the day before, (again) crying out unto him for help. Said unto him Moses: "Verily thou art an open hot-head." The two events between the man of Moses and Pharaoh's party were before Moses' being permitted to declare war against the infidels. In this stage 'Taqiyya', 'Hiding the faith', is commendable though the defence is not prohibited. Therefore, in the first quarrel Moses also put aside 'Taqiyya' and killed the infidel. That action encouraged his man to pick up quarrels with another of the kind. Thus, Moses blamed him for being hot-headed and not being able to observe 'Taqiyya', forcing Moses also to take his side. However, nothing was legally against Moses' action on both occasions. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when he intended to seize him who was the enemy of them both, said he: "O' Moses! Dost thou intend to kill me as didst thou kill one the day before? Intendeth thou nothing but thou shouldst be a tyrant in the land, and intendeth not thou to be of those who compromise." The compromising attitude was expected of the infidels of Mecca from the Holy Prophet for they approached Abu Talib to ask the Holy Prophet not to abuse their gods and be satisfied with his own way of worship. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These are the verses of the Book which is manifest. (Manifesting.) See 28:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And there came a man (Hizqil - i.e. the 'Mu'min-e-Al-e-Firaun' - The Believer among the people of Pharaoh - The man who concealed his Faith - practised 'Taqiyya' as did Abu Talib to save the Holy Prophet.) from the remotest part of the city, running, (and) said he: "O' Moses! verily the chiefs are consulting to slay thee, Begone (from here at once)! Verily unto thee I am of the sincere advisers." The man was Hizqil, the Believer in God among the people of Pharaoh as was Abu Taleb protecting the cause of Islam and the Holy Prophet, against the Pharaohs in Mecca.This man was the same person1 who belonged to the people of Pharaohs who concealed his faith - similar to the attitude of Abu Talib in his effort to protect the Holy Prophet. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So, forth he went in fear, apprehending, (and) said he "O' my Lord! Deliver me from the unjust people!" See 28:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when he turned his face towards (the land of) Midian said (Moses): "Maybe my Lord will guide me in the right path." See 28:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when arrived he at the water (A watering place, a well.) of Midian, he found on it a group of men (watering their flocks) and found he besides them two women keeping back (their flocks); Said (To the women.) (Moses): "What aileth you?" Said the two (women): "We cannot water until the shepherds take away (their sheep from the water), and our father is very old." Moses while escaping from Egypt turned towards Midian and was only a wanderer in the desert and when he arrived at an oasis, weary, hungry for the last about a week, sat under the shade of a tree and saw at the well nearby, shepherds giving water to their flocks but two girls waiting there with their flocks. The shepherds were one after another drawing water for their own sheep but there was…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So he watered (their flocks) for them, then retired he unto the shade, (and) then said he: "O' my Lord! Verily of what Thou hast sent down unto me of the good, I stand in need" Moses could not resist the spirit of sincere and selfless chivalry in him and went to the helpless girls who stood quiet, and asked them how about watering their flocks. They expressed their helplessness and the un-avoidability of their waiting until the shepherds finish giving water to their flocks and leave the water for their flocks. Moses asked the shepherds to help the poor young ladies but they told Moses himself to draw the water for the flocks of the girls. Seeing the robust figure and the strong arms of Moses the shepherds stood aloof. Moses threw the huge bowl into the well and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then came unto him one of the two women walking bash fully; Said she: "Verily my father calleth thee so that he may recompense (Reward.) thee for what thou hath watered for us: So when came he unto him and narrated unto him his story, Said (the old man): "Fear thou not, thou art (now) secure from the unjust people" Invited by Shu'ayb through one of his daughters, Moses went to him."And he said unto his daughters, And where is he? Why is it that ye have left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread." Exodus 2/20."And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter." Exodus 2/21.While walking he told the girl to come behind him and if he needed any guidance on the right track to her place, she might…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said one of the two (women): "O' my father! Employ him, verily the best of those who thou canst employ is the strong (man) the trusted (This is the quality required for leadership i.e, Imamat (A.P.).) (one)." One of his daughters recommended to Shu'ayb to take Moses in his employ saying that he was strong and trustworthy. The Seventh Holy Imam Musa ibn Jafar al-Kadhim says that Shu'ayb told his daughter "From his (i.e., Moses') removing the rock from the mouth of the long-covered well, I understood he was a strong man but 'O' daughter of mine how dost thou know that he is trustworthy also?" "The girl related to her father (Shu'ayb) how Moses had asked her to walk behind him and be pointing the right way by throwing a small stone before him, for he said that he…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: "Verily, I intend to wed to thee one of these two daughters of mine on condition that thou servest me for eight years, and if thou didst complete ten (years) that will be a goodness of thine own accord; and I intend not to place any hardship on thee; Thou wilt find me, if God willeth, (one) of the righteous ones." See 28:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Moses) "Be it so between me and thee: whichever of the two terms I fulfil, there shall be no injustice unto me: And God, on what we say, is a witness." And Moses accepted the condition - and held it as an agreement to be fulfilled by him and Shu'ayb.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when Moses had fulfilled the term and was travelling with his family, perceived he on the side of the mount 'Tur' a fire; Said he unto his family: "Wait ye! Verily perceive I a fire, maybe I bring unto you from it some tidings or a brand (lighted) of the fire, so that ye may warm your selves." See 28:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We recite unto thee from the accounts of Moses and Pharaoh, with truth, for a people who believe. See 28:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When came he unto it, (he) was called (by a voice) from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the Tree, saying: "O' Moses! Verily I, am God, The Lord of the worlds" This was the place where Moses came in direct communion with God and the stage of 'Aw Adna' mentioned in verse 53:9 which is beyond - 'Sidrat al-Muntaha' in 53:14 was the place where the Holy Prophet, was invited in direct communion with God as mentioned in verse 53:10. (A. P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And saying: "Cast thou down thy staff;" And when he saw it moving as if (it were) a serpent, he turned back retreating and returned not: (then it was said unto him): "O' Moses! Come thou forward and fear thou not! for verily thou art of those who are secure!" See 28:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (And now) pass thou thy hand in thy bosom, it shall come forth white (radiant) without evil: and close nearer thy sides against fear, and these be two proofs from thy Lord unto Pharaoh and his chiefs, verily they are a transgressing people. See 28:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Moses): "O' my Lord! Verily have I killed (Refer to verse 28:15.) one of them, so fear I that they would slay me;" See 28:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And my brother Aaron, he is more eloquent than me in speech, so Thou send him with me as an assistant, to testify (Similarly Ali was given to the Holy Prophet to testify him. Refer to verse 13:43.) me; for fear I that they would belie me See 28:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (God) said: "We will strengthen thy arm with thy brother, and We will give ye two an authority so that they reach not unto ye two, (go ye) with Our signs, ye two and those who follow ye two shall be the triumphants." The Fifth Holy Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir said that when Moses returned to his wife from the Mount Sinai, she asked him where he was returning from. Moses replied that he was returning from God, Who is the Creator of the fire. He then left towards Pharaoh. The First Holy Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib said: "Upon God I say that even now I see Moses with his large arms, clad in the woollen long shirt, with the staff in his hand his waist tied tight with the woollen rope, his shoes made of ass's skin…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So when came unto them Moses with Our clear signs, said they: "This is nothing but a sorcery forged, and we heard not of it amongst our fathers of old." Pharaoh termed the miracles as sorcery and Moses as a sorcerer but acknowledged that he had never before seen such an enchantment though the heathens called the Holy Prophet a sorcerer but dared not to call him a liar.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said Moses: "My Lord knoweth best who cometh with guidance from unto Him, and for whom shall be the good end of the abode; Verily, succeed not the unjust ones." See 28:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said Pharaoh: "O' Chiefs! I know not any god for you other than me, so burn for me O' Haman, bricks of clay, and build for me a tower that I may mount up to the God of Moses, and verily I deem him to be one of the liars" The difference between the Pharaohs of the modern times and the ancient ones, is only that Pharaoh of Moses' time wanted to build a lofty tower by use of a brick industry to go into the outer space and the modern ones are doing the same by means of atom industry in rising up as the ancient ones who attempted at the same. Qur'an does not deny the possibility of such movement to penetrate the dimensions of the heavens and the earth but it says this would not be…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And prided (Considered themselves big.) he and his hosts in the land, without any right (Lit. Justice.) * and deemed they that they will not be returned unto Us. The same is the vanity of man of today and they will be caught one day and thrown into destruction - as the last clause of the verse indicates. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and divided its people into parties, weakening a group among them, he slaughtered their sons and spared alive their women; Verily he was of the mischief-makers. See 28:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We seized him and his hosts and We cast them into the sea; Behold then how (bad) was the end of the unjust ones. See 28:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We made them Imams (leaders) who invite unto the (Hell) fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they shall not be helped. See 28:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We caused them to be followed in this world, by a curse; and on the Day of Resurrection they shall be of the loathed (ones). The reference, to the encounters of Moses and Aaron with Pharaoh and the perdition suffered by Pharaoh with complete success to Moses and Aaron, was to warn the people that all those who would defy the Holy Prophet and Ali, would be walking in the footsteps of Pharaoh and will suffer perdition and the wrath of God, both will be on them, in this world and in the hereafter.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We gave Moses the Book after We had destroyed the generations of yore, (containing) clear arguments for man kind and a guidance and mercy, that happly they might reflect. See 28:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thou wert not on the western (Refer to verse 19:16 and the notes on the commentary (the east and the West).) side (of Mount Sinai) when passed We unto Moses the commandment, nor wert thou one of the (eye) witnesses, The valley of 'Tur' - Sinai, where Moses received his apostolic commission is situated in the North Western comer of the Arabian Peninsula. The address here is to the Holy Prophet, saying:"O' Our Apostle Muhammad! Thou wast not physically present at the place when Moses was called to the apostolic office to have witnessed the event to have it related to the people as you do it." (28:46) not the same wording as above translationThis could never have been possible for anyone who had not been an apostle inspired by God.It may mean the Western side of the order…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But We raised up generations (after Moses), and a long time passed upon them, and nor wast thou a dweller among the people of Midian, rehearsing unto them Our signs, but We were that sent (One after another. Refer to verse 23:44.) thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad); (with the knowledge) (of the past). Several generations had passed between Moses and the Holy Prophet. The rehearsing of the heavenly signs was to guide the people to the fact that he who had been sent to admonish the people and guide them aright was none else other than the apostle from God with the inspired knowledge of the events even of the distant and obscure past.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thou wert not on the side of the Mount 'Tur' when called We (unto Moses), but it is the mercy of thy Lord that thou warneth a people, unto whom no warner hath come before thee, that they may reflect. Though the Holy Prophet was not on the Mount 'Tur' where Moses was addressed and yet it is by the mercy of God towards mankind that instead of chastising the people for their persistent disbelief in the Apostle (the Holy Prophet) who was sent as a reminder inviting them to the truth. The next verse further explains the meaning of this verse.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And were it not so and should there befall unto them a calamity for what their (own) hands have sent before (them), then they would say: "O' Our Lord! why didst Thou not send unto us an apostle then we would have followed Thy signs and had been of the believers" See 28:46

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But (now) when hath come unto them the truth from Us, say they: "Why is he not given the like of what was given unto Moses?" What! did not they disbelieve in what was given unto Moses before? They said: "(these are) Two sorcerers (Enchantments.) backing up each other;" and they said: "Verily we, in everything do disbelieve." It may mean the same miracles given to Moses or the same form of Book, all at once.1 The answer to them is that coming all at once or gradually makes no difference. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Bring ye then some (other) book from God which is a better guide than both of them, Torah and Qur'an), that I may follow it, if ye be truthful." The two books referred to in comparison here in this verse once. are Torah, i.e., the Pentateuch (the scriptures given to Moses) and the Holy Qur'an.Refers to Torah which was brought by Moses and not to the version hailed by the Jews as the genuine Torah. However, the passage indicates that one should always follow the best in guidance, which is the basis of the argument in the question of 'Imamah' as well as the doctrine of the 'Ijtihad' following of the most learned one. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And intend We to bestow (Our) favour upon those who were considered weak in the land, and to make them the Imams (guides in faith), and to make them the heirs, The First Holy Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (in Nahj al-Balaghah) says that by 'those who were weak' are the holy Ahl al-Bayt, i.e., the Holy Imams, and one day, i.e., when the Twelfth and the Last Holy Imam Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mahdi would appear, and the Kingdom of God on earth will be established in the world, i.e., in the whole of the earth, there will not remain a single disbeliever, i.e., the earth will be ruled by the believers having True Faith in God. The earth as a whole would be ruled by the Holy Imam Muhammad al-Mahdi - A total vanquishment of all the disbelievers would…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then if they answer (Respond not to the challenge. Refer to verse 28:49.) thee not, then know thou that they follow their own caprices; And who is more astray than he who followeth his own caprices without any guidance from God? Verily God guideth not the unjust people. This verse stems out the permissibility of using one's discretion without being supported by the divine ret elation and the divine guidance is not given to the unjust ones. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We caused the Word (of guidance) to come unto them continuously, that they may be admonished. Meaning either 'We sent down verse after verse connecting each other with the knowledge, i.e., the necessary guidance', or it means that "We effected the revelation of Our Word of the Reminder (Qur'an) and Guidance, to be continuous." This is a reference also to the decree of the Lord for the 'Imamah', i.e., the series of the Twelve Holy Imams to immediately follow the conclusion of the apostleship of the Holy Prophet Muhammad, the last Apostle of God.This confirms the continuity of the divine work through the apostles without break.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those whom We gave the Book before it, they are believers in it. This and the following verses are said to have been revealed in praise of the Christians who had believed in Islam and they were forty in number - thirty-two had come from Abyssinia along with the Holy Prophet's uncle Ja'far-e-Tayyar and eight from Syria, including 'Buheira'.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when it is recited unto them say they: "We believe in it, verily it is the truth from Our Lord, verily we were Muslims - (Submitters) (even from) before it (came)" Note that these converts even before their open declaration of their formally embracing the faith 'Islam' are called Muslims, i.e., those who had submitted themselves to God's Will - in which sense it will be true if all the apostles of God preceding the Holy Prophet are called 'Muslim' for there could not be any apostle of God who would not have submitted himself to God's Will. When those who had not declared openly and yet adopted for themselves the title of 'Muslim', (i.e., faithful believers, or true muslims), where could there be any doubt of Abu Talib under whose patronage and protection Islam and the Prophet of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These shall be granted their reward twice for what they were steadfast, (The patience they exercised.) and they repel evil with good, and of the sustenance We have provided them with, they spend (in Our Way) See verse 33:31 about a double reward promised by God. The believers are described to be those who return good for evil. The Sixth Holy Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad says that by 'good' means 'Taqiyya', i.e., bearing the persecution and the torturous treatment with patience, hiding the faith in their hearts and returning the evil done to them with good. It is noteworthy that the Islam was started by one lonely helpless Holy Soul the Holy Prophet assisted by another similar one, i.e., Ali ibn Abi Talib in the teeth of the declared inimical opposition from the world all around.The new converts to this…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when hear (Note - How much vain talk without proper knowledge of the matter is abhorred.) they any vain talk, they withdraw from it, and say they: "For us shall be our deeds, and for you shall be your deeds, peace be on you, we desire not the (society of the) ignorants." This is a further description of the ideal excellence of the believers which establishes the fact that Islam was always for peace and harmony among the members of the human family. Even when taunted, scoffed, and jeered at, the believers used only to wish their persecutors peace and love.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, thou canst not guide whomsoever thou likest; but God guideth (Enlightens according to the sincerity of the quest.) whomsoever He pleaseth, and He knoweth best those who follow aright. Some misinformed commentators have heaped the blasphemy on Abu Talib (Ali's father) being a disbeliever - in spite of the clear evidence of Abu Talib being the foremost believer in the truth. Refer to what the great Sunni scholar Obaidullah Amritsari1 says in his famous work 'The name of Abu Taleb, Ali's father was Abd Manaf his 'Kunyah' Epithet was Abu Talib. He was the own brother of Abdullah the father of the Holy Prophet. With the death of his father Abdullah, the Holy Prophet remained in the loving care of his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib who before breathing his last passed on the care of the Holy Prophet, to his…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they say: "If we follow the guidance with thee, we shall be driven out from our land" What! have We not established them in a sacred (and) safe precinct, unto which are drawn fruits of every thing? - a sustenance provided from unto Us; but most of them know not. See 28:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And how many a town We did destroy, which exulted in its means of subsistence; So these their dwellings have not been inhabited after them save a little, and We are their (Ever the Owner of every thing - even after these who possess them pass away.) heirs! See 28:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thy Lord destroyeth not the towns until He raiseth in their Mother-(Town) (Metropolis or the chief or the central place.) (metropolis) an apostle, rehearsing unto them Our signs, and We destroyed not the towns except while their people were unjust. See 28:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And to establish them with power in the earth; and to show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts to see from them what they did dread. It is said that Pharaoh was informed and warned by the scholars of the ancient scriptures, that a son born to the Israelites, would bring perdition to his kingdom. He appointed informers to find out the children born to the Israelites. The midwives were under orders of Pharaoh to kill the male children born to the Israelites and to spare the female ones. When the wife of Imran conceived Moses, no midwife could make out the pregnancy and when the time for the birth of Moses approached the midwife had determined either to kill the child or to inform Pharaoh if the issue be a male one. But when Moses was born, the midwife…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of whatever things ye have been given are only a (Enjoyments.) provision of the life of this world and its adornment; and whatever is with God, is better and more lasting; What! do ye not then understand? See 28:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Is he then unto whom We have promised (What is with God. Refer to verse 28:60.) a goodly promise which he shall meet it, similar to him whom We have provided with the (Enjoyment Refer to verse 28:60.) provision of the life of this world, then on the Day of Resurrection he shall be of those arraigned? (For the requital.) See 28:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On that day will call (God) unto them and say: "Where are My partners whom ye were asserting?" See 28:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those against whom the sentence hath been confirmed will say: "O' Our Lord! These are they whom we led astray: we led them astray even as we had been led astray ourselves: we declare unto Thee to be free (of them): They were not unto us worshipping." i.e., Those who worship or submit to the authority of beings other than God. In reality they are worshipping or submitting to their own inclinations.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And it will be said (unto them): "Call ye your associate (gods)" so they called upon them, but they answered them not, and they shall see the chastisement, and would wish that they had been guided aright. See 28:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on that day shall (God) call unto them and say: "What was it that ye answered the apostles (from Me)?" See 28:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But the (Events.) tidings shall that day be so confusing that they shall (even) ask not each other. See 28:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Yet as to him who turned repentant unto God and believed and did good, maybe (Refer to verses 9:102 & 17:79.) he will be among the successful (ones) God's giving hopes is as good an assurance and wherever 'Asa', i.e., maybe, is used in the sense of giving hope, should be for giving assurance.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thy Lord createth whatever He willeth and (also) chooseth too; it is not theirs to choose; Hallowed is God and Exalted High is He (far) above what they join (with Him). It means that both creation and legislation is by God's Will and choice - man has no choice in either field. Therefore, it is surprising that some schools of thought, who call themselves the determinists claim that the question of the supreme authority in Islam (Khilafah) is to be decided by human choice. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thy Lord knoweth what concealeth their breasts and what they declare. See 28:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And revealed We unto the mother of Moses, saying: "Give him suck; and if thou fearest for him, launch him on the River; and fear thou not, nor grieve thou; for We will return him unto thee, and make him one of the apostles." See 28:6

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He is God, there is no god but He! His is all praise, in first and (in) the last, and His is the authority, and unto Him (only) ye shall be returned. See 28:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "See ye? Had God made the night to continue on you until the Day of Resurrection, who is the god other than God that could bring light unto you; What! Do ye not then hear?" See 28:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "See ye?" Had God made the day to continue on you until the Day of Resurrection, who is the god other than God that could bring, night unto you, that ye rest therein? What! Do ye not then see? See 28:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of His mercy He hath made for you the night and the day, that ye may rest therein, and that ye may seek of His grace, and that ye may give thanks. See 28:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on that day when He shall call unto them and say: "Where are My partners whom ye used to (Imagined - as gods or equal to God or imagined to exist.) assert?" See 28:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We will draw forth from every people a witness, and We will say: "Bring ye your proof; then shall they know that the truth is God's, and shall depart from them what they used to forge." See 28:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, Korah (Qarun) was of the people of Moses, but he rebelled against them, and We had given him of the treasures so much that its keys would have been a burden to a company of men of strength. When his people said unto him, "Exalt thou not, for God loveth not those who exult." 'Qarun', i.e., Korah - was the cousin of Moses. He was one of those who had believed in the ministry of Moses, but when God tested him with the abundance of wealth, he was proved to be a disbeliever. He was exceedingly beautiful, hence people called him 'Munawwar', i.e., the lighted one.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And seek, by means of what God hath given thee, the abode in hereafter, and forget not thy share in this world, and be good to others even as God hath been good unto thee, and seek thou not to mischief in the earth, Verily, God loveth not the mischief-makers. This is the fundamental principle on which every one should base and modify his life. The aim of life should be the comfort of the hereafter but one should not give up his worldly enjoyment totally. To this effect the Holy Prophet said: "The good among you is not those who give up the life here for the life hereafter nor the one who gives up the life hereafter for the life here, but of you the good one is he who tries through his moderation and harmonises both the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Korah): "It (The wrath he possessed.) hath been given unto me only for the knowledge I possess;" What! knew he not that God hath indeed destroyed before him of the generations that were mightier in strength than he and greater in hoarding (of wealth)? And the guilty (at the time of punishment) shall not be questioned (respited to explain.) against their faults. See 28:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So went forth he (Korah.) unto his people in his pomp; (And) Said those who aspired for the life of this world: "Oh! would that we had the like of what hath been given unto Korah, verily he owneth a great fortune" This example of Korah is given here to confirm the statement in verse 28:60 and the subsequent verses (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And took him up Pharaoh's people, that he might be unto them an enemy and a (cause of their) grief; (for) verily Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts were sinners. The 'Lam' means that it was not the motive of the action but the result or the consequence of it. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who were given the knowledge said: "Woe unto you! The reward of God is better for him who believeth and doeth good, but none shall attain it save the steadfast ones" After Pharaoh and his hosts had been drowned, Moses delegated the authority to Aaron. Qarun (i.e., Korah) became envious and inimical towards Moses and Aaron and had determined to somehow put Moses to some degradation in the eyes of the people. Korah was extremely stingy and never paid the poor-rate. Korah employed a public woman bribing her with two purses of gold (sealed by him) and told her to get into the crowd in which Moses would be preaching the next day and declare to the gathering that Moses had committed adultery with her. The next day when Moses was preaching to the crowd against adultery, Korah…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then We caused the earth to swallow him up and his abode; then for him there was no group to help him against God; nor was he of those who can defend themselves. See 28:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who coveted his position only the day before began saying: "Ah! that God amplifieth the sustenance for whomsoever He pleaseth, of his servants and straiteneth it; had not God been gracious unto us, He would certainly have abased us; Ah! the ungrateful (ones) succeed not." See 28:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That abode in the hereafter, We assign it for those who intend not to exult themselves in the earth, nor (to make) mischief (therein) and the end is (best) for the pious (Those who guard themselves against evil.) ones. See 28:80

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whosoever bringeth good, for him shall be better than it, and whosoever bringeth evil, then shall not be recompensed those who wrought evil, (with) aught save what they had been working. This is an assurance that whatever may be the vicissitude of fortune here, for individuals and nations, at the end, the success is only for the pious ones, and this assurance has been frequently repeated in Qur'an, and this discards all arguments in favour of pessimism forwarded by pessimistic doctrines of Buddha, Mazdak, Mani, etc. With this assurance however hard and miserable may be life here, the pious one, would only be happy and without this conviction, however comfortable may be the person's life, he will be miserable and can never be happy. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily He Who hath (Note - reciting the first clause of this Verse into ear of one starting on any journey is very effective for safe return - 'Inna alladhi farada 'alayka al-Qur'ana la-radduka ila ma'ad'.) ordained the Qur'an unto thee certainly bringeth thee back {to thy) home; Say thou: "My Lord knoweth best him who hath brought the guidance and him who is in manifest error." See 28:84

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:86 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thou (The Prophet addressed for the people.) didst not expect that the Book would be inspired unto thee, but it is a mercy from thy Lord, therefore be not a supporter of the disbelievers. This verse indicates that whatever one has been given of the revelation and the blessings, it is of God's Will, not due to one's activities. Therefore, God alone should be trusted, and no attempt should be made to make any compromise with the infidels. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:87 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And let them not turn (The Prophet addressed for the people.) thee aside from the signs of God after they have been sent down unto thee, and call (mankind) unto thy Lord, and be not of the polytheists. (Those who worship or depend upon authorities other than God.) See 28:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:88 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And call not with God any other god; There is no god but He: All things are perishable but He: His is the Authority, and unto Him shall ye be returned. See 28:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qasas:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said Pharaoh's wife: "(Here is) a joy (Refreshing the eye.) of the eye unto me and unto thee: slay him not: maybe he will be useful to us, or we will adopt him as a son;" But they knew (What would be the consequence.) not (what would Moses he to them). It is said that one of the daughters of Pharaoh suffered from leukoderma. The scholars of the ancient scriptures had predicted that an animal like a human child would come floating in the river, if the saliva of that child is applied to the patches, the patches would disappear. The girl was stationed on the bank of the river waiting for the animal to come floating. When the baby Moses came floating in the box, Pharaoh and his wife Asiyah daughter of Muzaḥim were there with their daughter.…

item.description: Nay! I swear by the Day of Resurrection! 'La' the prefix to the oath is a term used to give emphasis to the oath.'Qiyamah', i.e., Rising, meaning the resurrection of the dead for the Final Judgment.The justification for swearing with the resurrection is the contents of the Chapter which deals with resurrection, individual and collective. (A.P.)

(A.P.)Applicable to man's life here and in the hereafter - meaning there is no use of forwarding excuses when he himself knows. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) Move not thy tongue with it (the Qur'an) in haste (Refer to Verse 20:114.) ! An intelligent study of this Verse and also Verse 20:114 indicates a very great factor along the personality of the Holy Prophet. It indicates that the whole matter of the Holy Qur'an was there already in the heart of the Holy Prophet, and he was commissioned to release only the portion or the part of it which was conveyed to him through the Messenger Angel Gabriel and nothing more. The revelation of the Verses through Gabriel was not repeatedly recited to the Holy Prophet. It was revealed only once and unless the matter had already been there in the heart of the Holy Prophet it could not have been remembered to be recited by him to the people.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, on Us is the collection of it (The Qur'an. This is a clear indicative that the Qur'an was duly compiled in a divinely willed arrangement before the Holy Prophet left this world - This is the under-taking of God by Himself. Refer to Verse 15:9. See note on 'Tahrif' in the introduction.) and the recital of it! This Verse clearly indicates that under the Divine undertaking about the security of the Holy Qur'an, in its originality and completeness1; the Holy Qur'an as it was revealed, was collected duly under the guidance of the Holy Prophet and there was a complete version of it during his life-time for this Verse clearly indicates the compilation of the Holy Book and to have been done under the Divine guidance and the collection implies the arrangement of the different Verses in their appropriate…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So, when We have recited it, then follow thou the recital! See 75:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Again, it is on Us the explaining of it! This is another undertaking from God about the correct explanation of the Word of God.This promise was fulfilled in the institution of the Imamate to continue until the end of the world.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! I swear by the Self- Accusing (Self-censuring, Self-reproaching.) self! 'Nafs al-Lawwama' i.e., The self-accusing self or sense, (the conscience)There are the three senses or spirits or the aspects of the human self-active in each human individual. The first is 'Nafs al-Ammara'1 on account of which the human soul is prone to evil. This tendency, if not controlled, will lead the individual to be totally lost in evil. To check this tendency towards evil the grace of the All-Merciful God provided man with the self-accusing self-called 'Nafs al-Lawwama' which makes the individual feel conscious of the wrong way he treads and to resist it and to seek forgiveness of the Lord. The third sense is called the 'Nafs al-Mutmainnah', i.e., the attainment of perfect satisfaction for the soul to rest in peace which is achieved after a complete surrender of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! But ye love the fleeing (Refer to Verses 26:128; 21:37.) life! Man by nature is hasty1. Thus, man is after immediate enjoyment of the present life which is temporary and does not care for the hereafter which is permanent.The Verse 'Tohibboona' in plural indicates that the actual addressee in the Verse 16 was not the Holy Prophet but the people - pointing out to man's nature in general that in every matter, the immediate gain is always preferred to the remote one and this tendency manifests itself in every walk of life unless man is controlled by strong intellectual faculties or submits himself to the divine guidance2. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And neglect ye the hereafter! To avail of the enjoyment at hand in this life, which are only a passing show, man forfeits the hereafter which is an enduring reality.

item.description: (Some?) faces (Refer to Verses 76:11; 83:24.) on that day shall be resplendent! This never means that God will appear to anyone in any physical form. The seeing here means realisation of the glory of God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Qiyaama:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then went he unto his people in haughtiness The Eighth Holy Imam Ali Ibn Musa Ar-Ridha' says that when these Verses were revealed the Holy Prophet held Abu Jehal by his garments and dragging him recited Verses 34 and 35. "O' Muhammad! Neither thou nor thy God can ever do any harm to me! I am the chief of Mecca!"On the day of the Battle of Badr, seeing the Muslims in a small number against his huge army, Abu Jehal got sure of his success and taunted the Holy Prophet saying that God had brought humiliation to Islam and the Muslims. At last Abu Jehal fell in that battle and was killed by Abdullah Ibn Mas'ood.

Thus, his sensual desires influence his reasoning. (A.P.)

Some say, that the reference is to those who were the foremost to belief in the Truth, viz. all the apostles of God and those who accepted the Truth, the Unity of God, when it was first declared by the Holy Prophet, those who were the foremost to offer the prayers along with the Holy Prophet like 'Ali and Lady Khadija were with the Holy Prophet, in offering the prayers to God, those who were foremost in all the fights for God, those who from the…

item.description: (A group of the) numerous from among the first ones (The followers of the previous prophets preceding the Holy Prophet.) The number of the Foremost ones, from Adam to the Holy Prophet, is great, i.e., those who believed in God and suffered the most for God and godliness.The reason from the first (verse 13) group being many and from the later (verse 14) - is obvious as in term 'Sabiqoon' and 'Muqurraboon' all the prophets and their divinely commissioned successors (Ausiya) are included - and it is clear that the number of the prophets preceding the Hoy Prophet is greater than the number of 'Sabiqoon' and the 'Muqarraboon' the divinely 'Ausiya' or the successors who are limited to only Twelve as the Holy Prophet has declared 'Al-Ainimato Ba'di Ithna-Ashar' - The leaders or the guides after me are only Twelve…

Among the later generations the foremost ones will be few for among- the ancient ones there is the huge number of apostles of God and larger still is the number of their deputies and besides this huge number, are those of the believers who sacrificed themselves for the truth. Though, every sincere follower of the Holy Prophet, i.e., a True Muslim, is surely among those who would enter Paradise but the number of the 'Sadiqoon in Islam could he of the holy Ahl Al-Bayt and the very few of their faithful devotees, who will be rarely found with the degree of the faith and wholehearted devotion to it.This is the reason re: the people of right below the rank of the 'Muqarraboon' there is no question of the…

item.description: This shall be their repast on the Day of Reckoning (Day of the Final Judgement.) The presentation of the reward and the punishment in the life hereafter and the terms of enjoyments and the tortures of a physical life, as it has already been pointed out in the previous notes on the topics, are figurative expressions and in the sense of presenting the unknown in the terms of the known but taking the non-material and metaphysical world as real and the material and the physical one as a mere phenomenon and the manifestation of the real one, it should be said that the enjoyments and the tortures of this life, are figurative expression of the real one1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is We Who created you, why then do ye not admit the Truth? To prove the evolutionary process of the development of life from physical to the transcendental one Qur'an forwards the process of creation which is known to everyone, i.e., the development of a most complicated and perfect living being out of the most insignificant frivolous emitted life germ and the various forms it assumes in the embryo and after its birth till its death, the power which administered these processes, shall not fail to take this continuous change of germs into a further realm of creation unknown to us (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Have ye seen what ye emit (the life germ)? See 56:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is it ye that create it or are We the Creators? See 56:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they shall become scattered dust (Refer to Verse 51:1.) See 56:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is We Who have decreed death among you, and We are not to be frustrated (Prevented.) The decreed respite, given to man in this world until his death which none can ever change or avoid.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: To Our changing (Or substituting others like unto you in your place.) your forms and raising you in that ye know not (In a form or a state not known to you now.) If God wills, He can replace any people with any other. Or our soul and put into new forms not known to us - But this is not the transmigration in this world itself.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, know ye the first growth, why then ye reflect not? It is asserted that the process in the unknown realm is comparable to the process known.Moreover, this verse proves that the life of man is capable of being remembered in the first development known to man. There is no such a thing as a previous development and previous birth, in other words this birth known to man, is the first birth1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Have ye seen what ye sow Note the arguments from verse 58 above to verse 73 below, proving the supreme and the exclusive authority of God over the universe, enumerating a few of the innumerable obvious bounties of nature which also are great marvels if studied intelligently - viz, the growing of the seed, the rain-water, coming down from heaven, the combustion or the quality of the fire etc.,There are the other examples of growth, development and changes. In each case, it is to bring home to man that in both cases, though the action is attributed to man but the effect is always due to God's administration (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Is it ye (Causers of the growth.) that grow it or are We the growers (Cause it to grow.) ? We only sow the seed. Who is it that makes it grow and yield in manifold quantities. Is it not a wonder, and none else but God does it.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Had We willed, We could crumble it to dry bits, and ye would be left only to lament See 56:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Saying): 'Verily we have been burdened with loss! (We have wasted the money, effort and time and we are deprived of the result.) ' See 56:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: 'Nay! We are deprived (Suffered the loss.) (of the benefits!)' Can anyone else, except God, cause the life-giving water to rain from heaven. It is not a proof positive of the existence of the One who does it?

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Have ye seen the water which ye drink? See 56:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Is it ye that send it down from the heaven or are We the Senders ? This refers to the change of the clouds into fresh drinking water without any mixture (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And ye shall be (sorted into) three kinds (People will be sorted into three main groups.) See 56:4

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Had We willed, We would have made it saltish (Unfit to drink. Without which there can't be life on earth.) , why then ye thank not? What could we have done, if the water we get from heaven upon which depends the life on earth, had been turned saltish. Is it not God's grace for which we should remain grateful to Him?

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Have ye seen the fire which ye kindle (by friction)?' Is not the burning quality endowed in fire, a great bounty of God? Could" we have caused it without His will? Or could we have lived without the heat it provides us with? Does it not, prove the existence of the One who does it and should we not remain grateful and obedient to Him?Example of bringing out a deadening and destructive element (fire) from a living and growing being (tree) (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Is it ye who produce its tree? Or are We the producers (Produce – grew. Refer to Verse 36:80.) (of) it? Though fire as an essential provision for the human life on earth has many uses, the burning of it, serves also as the signal to the travellers in the desert at night, who make out the human habitation from a distance and they could direct their move on the right track, guided by it. Only those who have an experience of the travel through an extensive desert, particularly at night, know the aptness of this illustration."Reminder" may refer to the tree or to the fire. Refers two aspects - as a Reminder as well as a provision intellectual as well as physical advantages (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is We Who have made it a reminder (It may refer to the tree or to the fire.) and a provision (of comfort) for the needy ones (Or the wayfarers.) See 56:72

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So hallow thou the name of thy Lord, the Great See 56:72

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But nay! I swear by the setting of the stars (Or the position of the Qur'an.) 'Maqam an-Nujum' i.e., the time or the occasion of the setting of the stars - the time between midnight and the approach of the dawn. It is true when the pious ones or the staunch devotees of God are busy in their supplications or adoration to the Lord. Some commentators say that it refers to the revelation of the Qur'an. However, it is the time when the Mercy of the Lord unfolds itself specially for those who are busy seeking it, by their supplications.It is the best time for concentration, meditation, and thus for communion with the All-Divine. This is the time availed of, by the sincere devotees of God to elevate their souls from the limitations of the depth of the material sphere…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily it is a great oath if ye only knew it See 56:75

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily it is Qur'an honourable (Refer to Verses 43:4; 50:4.) To get the full meaning, this verse has to be read along with the other following two, i.e., 78 and 79 below. These three verses deserve a serious and intelligent study. Note the Holy Qur'an is called 'Kareem' which may mean Honourable as well as Charitable, Beneficent, Liberal, Kind. All the various meanings of the word 'Kareem' are equally applicable to the Holy Qur'an. Taking the meaning Gracious, Beneficent, it has the quality in perfect consonance with the fact that it is the Word of the Gracious and the Beneficent Lord of the Universe. Beneficence or Grace, is always given to anyone and everyone who seeks it. Similarly, the Holy Qur'an is there, ever ready to benefit or profit whosoever approaches it duly as the guidance of God is promised…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In a Book hidden (Refer to Verses 85:21 - 85:22; 80:13 - 80:16.) It is clearly said, that it (the Holy Qur'an) is treasured in a Concealed or a Hidden Book, which means that the Holy Qur'an is an object contained in a Book which is Concealed or Hidden, i.e., duly protected - in which case the thing in our bands is only a Recital form of the Holy Qur'an and not the actual Book itself, for it is clearly said here that, it is in the 'Kitab al-Maknoon' 'Hidden Book.' Supporting this is verse 43:3, which says, that this is the only Arabic version of the Holy Qur'an, and 43:4 says that the actual Holy Qur'an is in the 'Umm al-Kitab' the 'Mother Book.'The Holy Qur'an was revealed through the Messenger Angel Gabriel descending on the heart of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Toucheth it not save the purified ones (Refer to Verse 33:33.) The ordinary rendering of translation of this verse, is that it shall be held in all honour and purity. It shall not even be touched but by the clean at least in body with the prescribed ablution without which none shall even touch its written form. The wording means also that none but the purified one would understand it duly. Here the mental or the intellectual touch is meant.Even the Ahmadi commentator (M.A.) acknowledges this to be one of the meanings of this verse saying: "This also shows that the understanding of the Qur'an is granted only to those who are pure in heart." One should know as to who could be the purified ones who could have the external as well as internal purity to have the perfect…

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then (will be) the people of the Right hand; Oh! What (a happy state shall) the people of the Right hand (be in)! (Refer to Verses 74:38; 74:39.) The Companions or the Fellows of the Right side - i.e., those who in the beginning of their lives were sinful but subsequently repented and got themselves amended and ended their lives in righteousness.The Sides - 'Right,' (in verse 8) 'Left' in verse 9: and 'Foremost' in verse 10 - are relative terms which are used in Qur'an to indicate the sides inclined towards the Absolute One, the side inclined towards the material are, Many and the Foremost in the order of the beings in submission to the Absolute respectively1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Sent down by the Lord of the worlds See 56:79

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Hold ye then in scorn (Hypocritically.) this statement? Reference to the disbelievers, ridiculing the Holy Qur'an, calling it a compilation of old stories and not being a revelation from God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And make ye your sustenance (Habit similar to the habit of eating (A.P.).) that ye should belie it Once while the Holy Prophet was travelling there happened the dearth of water and the people needed water immediately to quench their killing thirst. The Holy Prophet said if I pray to God and get the water from heaven, you will ascribe it to the effect of some star. They said that they would not. The Holy Prophet prayed and instantaneously it rained very heavily. A man while taking water for him, said that the rain was due to some star's movement. The Holy Prophet heard it and said that I am afraid of three forbidden things in my people:(1) Cruelty to my Ahl Al-Bayt,(2) Disbelief in the Holy Qur'an,(3) Belief in the stars.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Why then do ye not (help) when (the soul of the dying man) cometh up to the throat (Refer to Verse 56:82.) ? See 56:82

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And ye then (remain) only gazing (Helplessly.) (at him) See 56:82

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We are nearer to him than ye, but ye see (Us) not (Refer to Verses 34:50; 50:16.) See 56:82

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:86 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Why not then, if ye are not in bondage (If you are not held under any authority (A.P.).) (unto Us) See 56:82

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:87 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ye send it (the soul) back, if ye be truthful The gist of this challenge is that if you think that life and death is not controlled by any Supreme Conscious Agency - then you, the Conscious independent being should be able to bring it under your hold (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:88 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then if he be of those drawn nigh (unto God) This is a re-assertion of the statement and the classification in the beginning of the chapter (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:89 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (For him is) rest and happiness and a garden (Paradise.) delightful See 56:88

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the people of the Left hand; Ah! What (a wretched state shall) the people of the Left hand be (in it) The companions or the fellows of the Left-side, i.e., those who from the beginning to the end of their lives were indulged in sinning and ended their lives in sins.

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:90 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if he be of the people of the Right Hand See 56:88

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:91 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then Peace unto you from the people of the Right Hand See 56:88

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:92 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if he be of those who have belied, gone astray See 56:88

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:93 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He shall have an entertainment of a boiling water See 56:88

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:94 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the boiling of the hell-fire See 56:88

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:95 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, this is truth in certainty This is not a mere fanciful or a wishful thinking but the Truth in its certainty (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Al-Waaqia:96 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hallow therefore the Name of thy Lord, the Great See 56:95

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naas:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: ''I seek refuge in the Lord of the people! This Surah is identical with the previous one, Surah 113. The matter is supplementary to that of the previous Surah.Man is asked to seek refuge in God with His name as "Rabb", i.e., the Lord of Men - i.e., the Cherisher and Sustainer. Invoking this great attribute, man can expect an especially paternal treatment.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naas:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The King of the people! To seek refuge in God, invoking His authority over the affairs of men, as their King, i.e., He is the One Who can independently act over His creation.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naas:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The God of the people! To seek the protection invoking the divinity of the Lord as the God of mankind - for it is God's authority which must necessarily be obeyed, i.e., it is His command or His will which is always done.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naas:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: From the evil of the Satan (slinking whisperer,) 'Khannas', i.e., the one who gets back or withdraws. This is a reference to Satan who withdraws himself, the moment he hears the name of the Lord mentioned.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naas:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Who whispereth into the breasts (hearts) of the people Satan Who whispers evil into the minds of men and leaves them to suffer the consequences of obeying his instigations to evil.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naas:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: From among the Jinn and the Men Be the evil doers, the Jinns or human beings. It is a well-known fact that among the forces hidden from the human eye, which are active in the world, there are good and also bad ones among them. Jinns, like Satan are spiritual beings1.The End

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''By those (Angels.) who drag forth violently (Refer to: 51:1 - 51:4, 77:1 - 77:5, 37:1 - 37:3.) The Arabic alphabet is used to indicate the swearing, i.e., by the angels who tear out the souls of the disbelievers from their bodies. The beginning of this Surah is like that of Surah 77.The swearing by the angels and the other forces and the elements in nature, might not give the true sense of the gravity of the act to those ignorant of the greatness of the things or the phenomenon but those who know how great and mysterious are the things and the functioning of the natural phenomena would realise the seriousness or the importance of the occasion for God to do it - and how great and vital the thing must be to mankind that the Gracious God announces…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''They shall say (then): ''What (Parenthetical sentence referring to what people would say.) ! Shall we indeed be restored to as (we were) at first? This refers to the deniers denying such a sure event which shall take place.A parenthetical sentence referring to what people sat now in this life - doubting about resurrection. (A. P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''They said: ''That then will be a return in vain (Losing - With lose.) See 79:10

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''Verily (Refer to: 36:29, 49, 53, 37:19.) , it shall be but a single (violent) blast (Or a cry - or a shaking.) See 79:10

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''When lo! they shall (all) be in the awakened state (Refer to: 50:22, 78:40, 75:22.) Said the Holy Prophet: - ''Annas Niyammon Fai'za Maatoo intabaho", i.e., People are asleep, they will awake when they die. To which reference is made in 50:22. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''Hath not come unto thee the story (Story of Moses is recollected. Refer to: 20:9 - 20:73.) of Moses? See 79:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''When called him his Lord in the Holy Valley (called) 'Tuva' (Refer to: 20:12, In a sudden change.) See 79:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''(Saying)-. ''Go thou (O' Moses!) unto Pharaoh (Refer to: 20:24.) ! verily, he hath transgressed the bounds! See 79:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''And say (unto him)'. ''Hast thou (Pharaoh.) (a desire) to cleanse thyself (of thy disbelief)? See 79:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''And I will guide thee unto thy Lord so that thou mayest fear him See 79:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''And those (Angels.) who untie (the knot) briskly By the angels who gently cause the soul of the righteous ones to get released of their confinement of their bodies. In contrast to the disbelievers and the wicked ones, the souls of the believers and the righteous ones, only await their release from the material bodies and its commitments. Hence the souls themselves pass out of their bodies willingly and the angel makes the task easy and pleasant.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''And he showed him the greatest sign (miracle) (Refer to: 20:20, 22:23, 17:101, 7:133, 20:70, 20:73.) See 79:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''But belied he and disobeyed See 79:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''Then turned he his back hastily See 79:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''And gathered (the people) and proclaimed See 79:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''And said ''I am your Lord, the most High! See 79:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''So seized him God (Refer to: 20:78, 20:79, 7:135 – 137.) , with the chastisement in the hereafter, and the life before (it) See 79:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''Verily in this there is a lesson unto him who feareth (God). (Refer to: 24:44.) See 79:14

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''Are ye the harder to be created, or the heaven which built He (Refer to: 2:29, 41:9 - 41:12.) ? Man is reminded of his insignificant physical position in the universe. When the heavens with all their heavenly bodies will succumb to the will of the Lord and vanish at His will - of what consideration could be man who is nothing more than an insignificant germ in the set-up of the universe.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''Raised He its heights and established (Put in an established position.) it The mystery of the existence of the heavens and the wonderful heavenly bodies in them, with the perfection in their form and the perfect harmony, with which each one works with the other, was brought into existence by God, and is worked at His will.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''And He darkened its night, and brought forth its noon light See 79:28

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''And those who glide on (Swiftly) By the angels who are busy moving about briskly in executing their duties in the management or the administration of the universe.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''And the earth, afterwards he stretched forth 'Dab.' here means further expansion1 of its surface long after the creation of the earth and the heavenly bodies. It may refer to the last layer of the earth which produces food for men and the animals. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''He brought forth from it, its waters and its pasteurage The ready supply of water through the underground springs and wells and the wonderful arrangement of rain from heaven and the evaporation of the water from seas; all these are the unquestionable proofs of the Wisdom and Might of the Creator.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''And the mountains, He set them firm See 79:31

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''A provision (Refer to: 80:32.) for you and your cattle See 79:31

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''When cometh the Great Calamity. (The day of final Judgment.) See 79:31

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The day when man shall recollect (This confirms the awakening slate mentioned in Verse 79:14.) (all) that he strove for Every act and motive of evert one, will be laid bare to each individual to account for.This confirms the awakening state referred to in in Verse 79:14 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the hell shall be displayed unto him who seeth See 79:35

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then, as for him who hath transgressed the bounds Those who wilfully persisted in transgressing the prescribed limits, will have the abiding chastisement and those who were the victims of the common weakness in the human being and who yielded to the human frailty, will have to face the balancing of their evil with their goodness1.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And preferreth the life of this world See 79:37

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then, verily, Hell, that shall be his abode See 79:37

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ''Then those who go ahead with a foremost speed By the angels which race with each other in executing the will of the Lord to His satisfaction and pleasure.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And as for him who feareth the standing (The justice.) of his Lord, and forbiddeth (his) self from (following) his inclinations (Submitting to God's will.) Note the key to heaven and the blissful life therein, has been shown and that is the control of the self and refraining from low desires, abstaining from the forbidden.

item.description: Wherein art thou of its notion (You are far away from grasping its ultimate significance. Refer to: 11:107, 11:108.) ? God alone knows the extent or its duration. The whole matter lies in the will of the Lord1.You are far away from grasping its ultimate significance. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naazi'aat:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Unto thy Lord (alone) is its termination! The duty of an apostle of God ends with warning those who want to avail of the message and the admonition. No apostle of God is responsible for the conduct and character of the people.It indicates that the whole system of universe is in motion and in the state of ever becoming. It is He to Whom the motion terminates. There is nothing in the whole system of the Universe to be termed eternal. Hence 'Hudoose Zamani al-Aalam', i.e., The universe being as a whole and past being created from naught. (A.P.)

item.description: It shall seem unto them, on the day when they see it, as though they tarried not in (their graves) but a (single) evening, or the following morning (Refer to: 10:45.) Refers to the last state of the awakening when the conscious self gets out of the bounds, time and space, the whole system of the four-dimensional state will appear to him and even less than a part of an ordinary day - to which Eqbal says: Referring to the stars addressing man - saying ''Thy century unto Us is only a moment and thine Ocean unto Us is only a drop. We are seeing and passing".Qur'an says the day shall come - man will be in a position to say the same to the whole heavenly bodies. (A.P.)
