item.description: ''To abide therein for ages ('Ahqab' See note.) 'Ahqab' is the plural of 'Huqub', and the Holy Prophet said that a 'Huqub' is the duration of Eighty and more years and each year of an especially long duration of thousands of years in the terms of our present calculations. The First Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abu Talib was asked by Bilal as to the length of a ''Huqub' which is ordinarily taken and he replied, ''that a Huqub is of Eighty years and each year of twelve months and each month of thirty days and each day of thousand years!" Then Ali said that 'Huqub' which will continue one after the other before those committed to hell are taken out of it.About the duration of the stay in hell and heaven see 11:107 and 11:108.The continuous chain of the 'Ahqab'…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Decree of God hath come, therefore ye hasten it not: Glory be to Him and Exalted is He above what they associate with Him. 'Amrullah', i.e., God's Command - Here meaning the punishment from God with which the people were threatened.'Amrullah - The commentators have given various interpretations of 'Ata-Amrullah'. Whether it means in future, though the verb is in the form of past or it means perfect, 'Amr' undoubtedly is the decree of punishment. If this verse is read with verse 10:47 it gets clear that with the advent of the Holy Prophet the faith of the people, the believers and the disbelievers, had been decided. All that remains is, its execution to which the people are warned here, not to hasten. Hence the interpretation should be taken as present perfect. (A.P.).

(A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:120 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily Abraham was an Imam (The Leader of the faith or the religion.) (leader in religion) (for the) people, devoutly obedient to God, upright, and he was not of the polytheists, Here Abraham is asserted to be an 'Ummat' which cannot mean but 'Imam', (i.e., a distinctive leading personality), because the word 'Ummat' is used in Qur'an to mean any distinctly distinguished group, person, point of time, point of space, to which attention is drawn. This is the justification of the interpretation of the word 'Ummat' as 'Imam' here and in the other verses of Qur'an which asserts the leading duties for 'Ummat' (A.P.).

item.description: Verily the sabbath (Refer to verses 2:65, 4:154 & 7:163.) was ordain ed only for those who differed about it; and verily thy Lord will judge between them on the Day of Judgment in what they used to differ about. See 16:120

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:125 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And call thou unto the way of thy Lord with wisdom (Refer to verses 2:231 - 2:269, 3:48, 3:81, 3:164, 4:54, 4:113, 5:113, 33:34, 31:12, 38:20, 42:63 & 62:2.) and kindly exhortation and dispute (Argue.) with them in the manner which is the best; Verily thy Lord knoweth better of him who hath gone astray from His path; and He knoweth best of those guided aright. Note the most polite way in which Islam wants a Muslim to spread the truth against such clear and the most civilized and human method of the propagation of the truth, a heavy attack on Islam and the Holy Prophet is made with the greatest blasphemy that Islam was propagated by sword which is nothing but either the betrayal of the conscience or the betrayal of the ignorance of the facts.This verse restricts preaching…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:126 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if ye punish then punish ye as ye were afflicted; But if ye be patient, certainly it will be best for the patient (Note the patience enjoined by Islam even against unprovided aggression.) ones. This verse gives one the right of retaliation or punishment to one who has done him wrong but Qur'an recommends patience as the best course, and further emphasises on the same in the next verse, 16:127, and explains that this tolerance should be for the sake of God, and in God's way. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:127 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And be thou patient (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) and thy patience is not but by (the help of) God, and grieve not for them; and distress not thyself at what they devise. See 16:126

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:128 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily God is with those who guard (themselves against evil), and those who do good (to others). See 16:126

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what He hath produced in the earth of varied hues (and qualities) Verily there is in this a sign for a people who are mindful (with gratitude). See 16:12

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He it is Who made subservient the sea that ye might eat from it fresh meat and take out from it ornaments which ye wear, and thou seest the ships cleaving through it, and that ye might seek of His grace, and that ye might give thanks. See 16:12

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He hath cast great mountains (standing firm) in the earth lest it may shake with you, and rivers and the roads that ye be guided aright, This expression which has been repeated in the Qur'an may refer to the geological fact that the surface of the earth is subject to shaking due to the internal heat of the earth, which had not been covered with a rocky layer. Referring to this Ali says: 'He bolted with rocks due to the shaking of the surface of the earth'. And in another place he says, 'He has balanced the movement of the earth with the bolting granites or rocks' (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And landmarks (too), and by the star they are guided (to the right way) The First Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abi Talib said that by 'Najm' meaning, Star, i.e., the Pole-Star which is stationary and by which the travellers in the wilderness and on the sea determine their routes. The inner meaning of this statement is that by 'Alaamaat', i.e., the signs, are meant the holy Ahl al-Bayt and by 'Najm' i.e., the Star, means the Holy Prophet Muhammad.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Is He then who createth like unto him who createth not? Will ye not then consider? See 16:16

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If ye would count God's bounties, ye can not compute (Count.) them; Verily God is Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful (Refer to verse 14:34.) . See 16:16

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God knoweth what ye hide and what ye manifest (Show – publish.) See 16:16

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He sendeth down the angels with the spirit (revelation) by His own decree on whomsoever He willeth of His servants saying: "Warn ye (the mankind) that there (Refers to the source and the course of the receipt of the revelations by the apostles of God, and the object of the revelations.) is no god but I therefore fear (Obey - Be dutiful.) Me." The 'Ruh', i.e., Spirit or Soul - Here 'Ruh' stands for the Holy Qur'an, i.e., guidance which enlivens the dead souls, quickening the ignorant ones with knowledge. 'Ruh' is stated to stand for 'Gabriel', i.e., the Angels always accompany _Gabrie_l1.'By His Command', i.e., to execute God's Command.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those whom they call on besides God create not aught while they are themselves created. See 16:16

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Dead (they are), not living, and they perceive not when they will be raised. See 16:16

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Your God is One God; and those who believe not in the hereafter, their hearts are repulsive (against the truth (Perverse.) ), and they are men of pride. (Arrogant.) See 16:16

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Certainly it is that God knoweth what they hide and what they express; Verily He loveth not the proud ones. See 16:16

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when it is said unto them: "What is it that your Lord hath sent down?" Say they (Nothing but the) legends of the ancients, See 16:16

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That they may bear their burden entirely on the Day of Judgment and also of the burdens of those whom they led astray without knowledge; Behold! Evil is it what they bear! Those who mislead others shall bear not only the burden of their own sins but also the sins of all those misled by them without diminishing anything from the punishment of the followers. Similarly, those who guide others aright shall have the reward not only for their own goodness but also for the goodness spread by them among those who follow them, without prejudice or any detriment to the rights of the followers for their own rewards.The Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq commanded 'Associate ye not yourselves with the wicked and even sit ye not with them, for with God, ye may be counted as one…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed did plot those before them, and then (the wrath of) God came (attacked or commanded.) (and destroyed) their structure (from) the foundations, and fell on them the roof from above them, and came on them the torment whence they perceived not. God gives the rope of the length of the respite to the disbelievers and the wicked to hang themselves, by frustrating their plans at the end. The disbelievers are allowed to complete their plans and then when they have exerted themselves to the maximum limits possible for them and exhaust all their resources, then all that they have wrought is made null and void.1Some say the reference is also to the building of extraordinary height which Nimrod had erected at Babel which at its completion was simply pulled down by the gush of a wind, and suddenly the…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then on the Day of Resurrection He will bring them to disgrace and say: "Where are My partners (which ye ascribed unto Me), about whom ye have been disputing; (Opposed or turned hostile.) Those who have been given the knowledge will say: "Verily the disgrace this day and evil is upon the infidels," 'Utu al-'Ilm', i.e., those gifted with knowledge. This clearly indicates that there are some, whom God has Himself gifted them with knowledge and they could not be other than the Apostles of God, and the Holy Imams who are Divinely commissioned to preserve and maintain the truth preached, in its original purity and fulness.1 The term is applicable in the first place to those whom God has Himself purified, i.e., the Holy Ahl al-Bayt.2

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those whom the angels terminate their life while they are unjust (Sinners.) unto themselves, then they would offer submission (saying): "We used not to do any evil," (the angels will reply): "Aye! Verily knoweth God well what ye were doing." See 16:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therefore enter ye the gates of Hell, to abide in it; Woeful indeed will be the abode of the haughty (Arrogant ones.) ones! See 16:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Created He (God.) the heavens and the earth with the truth; Exalted is He above what they associate (with Him). See 16:2

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And it is said unto those who guard themselves against evil: "What is that hath sent down your Lord?" Say they: "Good; For those who do good in this world is good; and indeed the abode of the hereafter is better; and excellent indeed is the abode of the pious ones," See 16:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Gardens of eternity, they shall enter therein, beneath them flow rivers; they shall have in them whatever they desire for; Thus doth God reward the pious ones, See 16:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those whom the angels take away in a good state, (the angels) while receiving them will say: "Peace be on you; Enter ye the Garden, for what ye were doing." See 16:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Await they aught save that come (The coming of the angels to execute the decree of the punishment to them.) unto them the angels or cometh (to pass) the decree of thy Lord? Thus did those before them; And God was not unjust unto them, but they were unto their own selves unjust. See 16:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So afflicted them the evils what they did; and encompassed them that which they were scoffing at. See 16:27

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they who associated (other gods with God) "If God had willed, we had worshipped not aught besides Him, (neither) we nor our fathers (Fathers and fore-fathers.) ; nor had we (forbidden) aught without a (decree from) Him;" Even so did (say) those before them; Is then (aught) incumbent upon (Our) apostles save a clear delivery (plain preaching of the message)? This is a common plea of all evil doers to throw the responsibility of their actions on God and the answer to that also is only one, i.e., it is the duty of God and His Messenger to show the path, the right one from the wrong one, and the rest is left to the choice of man.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed raised We in every nation an apostle (of Ours) (preaching) that "Worship ye God (only), and (Avoid.) shun ye (the worship of every kind of) idol," so of them were some whom God guided, and of them were others on whom error was confirmed; Therefore travel ye in the earth, then see what hath been the end of the beliers. See 16:35

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If covetest (Strives – Tries – Endeavours.) thou (The Prophet addressed for the people - O' man!) for their guidance, yet verily God guideth not those whom He leaveth to stray, and neither for them shall be any of the helpers. See 16:35

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And swear they by God, with the strongest of their oaths that God will raise not one who dieth; Nay, but it is a promise binding on Him in truth, but most people know it not, A disbeliever owed a debt to a Muslim. While demanding the repayment of the loan the Muslim took an oath saying, 'I swear in the name of God who would raise one after death,' at which the disbeliever asked the Muslim: 'Art thou sure that thou wouldst be raised from death?' in a tone asserting that there is no return to life after death. The Muslim replied saying, 'Yes', by all means. The reference here is to the belief of the disbeliever. The resurrection of the dead for the Final Judgment is reiterated here as the promise of the Lord to do it.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (They will be raised up) so that He might manifest unto them that which they differed about, and (that) those who disbelieved might know that they were liars. See 16:38

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He created man from life sperm or germ (Sperm.) and behold! (that same drop now a man) he is an open disputer. (Refer to verses 36:77 - 36:79.) 'Nutfah' which literally means also a small quantity of liquid - Here stands for the small drops containing the life-germs or the spermatozoon in the seminal fluid.Ibne Ubai brought a few bits of some rotten bones and asked the Holy Prophet with ridicule saying: "Who could raise these bits to life again?" This verse was revealed.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily only Our word for a thing when We will it is that We say unto it, 'Be' and it exists. See 16:38

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who migrate in (the cause of) God (A wider implication means the travel towards God.) after they are oppressed, certainly We will give them good (recompense) in this world; and certainly the reward in the hereafter is much greater, if they only know (this), Those who, for the sake of the faith suffered the worst persecution at the hands of the pagans of Mecca and at last fled their home in utter helplessness, first to Abyssinia and later to Madina.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who endured patiently (Persecution.) and on their Lord (only) do they rely. See 16:41

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We sent not before thee but men (as Our apostles), We revealed unto them; So ask ye the people of 'Dhikr' (The Ahl al-Bayt with whom the Holy Prophet left the Qur'an i.e. Dhikr, refer to verses 21:7, 16:44, 43:43 - 15:44.) (the Qur'an) if ye know not, The general interpretation of this is, if you do not know ask your own scholars and priests, who know the history of the ancient people, whether the Apostles of God who visited this earth in the past, were men only, and they were not angels, and they were only men and none of them was a woman.'Dhikr' is one of the names of the Holy Qur'an as well the Holy Prophet Muhammad.1 According to the interpretation of the Holy Ahl al-Bayt 'Dhikr' here means the Holy Prophet and by 'Ahl al-Dhikr'…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: With (Every apostle was sent with clear proofs. Signs to prove his bonafide to the people.) clear proofs (miracles) and scriptures; and We sent down unto thee the 'Dhikr' (Qur'an.) (The Reminder i.e., Qur'an) that thou mayest make clear unto mankind what hath been sent down unto them, that they may reflect (The development of intellect & thought in man is one of the objects of the revelation of the Holy Qur'an.) See 16:43

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! then feel they secure, who plan evil devices, (against) God causing them swallowed up by the earth, or cometh unto them the wrath from whence they perceive not? See 16:43

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or that He seizeth them during their movement, they shall not frustrate (Escape.) (God's decree), See 16:43

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or He seizeth them by a gradual (In their fear) loss, for verily your Lord is Pitiful and All-Merciful. See 16:43

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or see they not towards what God hath created that everything turneth its shadow to the right and to the left, prostrating in obeisance unto God, while they lie abased. Obeisance is of two kinds - the one with one's own will and the other by nature. The one done at one's own will is that which the believers offer, freely acknowledging the authority of the Lord and the other is that which everything in the universe is subjected to yield to the function of their native peculiarities like the cold and the flow in the water, the heat and the glow in the fire, the blowing in the wind, the solidity and the dryness of the earth, the pull of the gravity in the earth, the fixed rotation of the celestial bodies, the dark ness in the shadow and…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And prostrateth in obeisance unto God (only) whatever (Nothing in the Universe dare exercise pride against the authority of the Lord.) is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, (and) of the (moving) creatures, and the angels (too), and they pride (Neither arrogant nor proud.) not. See 16:48

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the cattle (He) created them for you, therein is warmth (In their hide and wool.) and many (Advantages.) gains, and of them ye eat. See 16:4

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They fear (Actually they are afraid or conscious or mindful of their own short coming in their obedience due to God.) their Lord (Supreme) above them and do what they are commanded. (Every thing in the Universe acts implicitly as destined by God, to do.) See 16:48

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God hath said: "Take ye not two (Reference may be to the 'Dualism' the doctrine of 'Yazdan'. The goodness and 'Ahriman' the source of evil - the source of both is one - Man's hopes should be in God and he should fear only Him.) gods, Verily, Verily, He is only One God; So of Me (alone) should ye be afraid." See 16:48

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And His it is whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and unto Him (only) should obedience constantly (Without any break.) be; Do ye then fear (any one else) other than God? See 16:48

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whatever of the bounty is with you, it is from God, then when any distress toucheth you, unto Him do ye cry for help. When afflicted by any misfortune then the nature in the individual urges him to helplessly turn to the Lord for help.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Yet when removeth He the distress from you, lo! some of you associate others with their Lord, When fortune favours man he forgets the Lord from Whom he received the grace and the blessings.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That they may deny what We have given them; (Say O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "then enjoy your selves (for a time); for soon will ye know." See 16:54

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they assign for what they know not, a portion of what We have provided them with; By God! Certainly ye shall be questioned about what ye have been forging. See 16:54

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they ascribe daughters (People worshipped the angels as the daughters of God.) to God Glory be to Him; And for themselves (they ascribe sons) what they desire! (As they would like to have for themselves.) See 16:54

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when is announced unto (any) one of them a daughter, black becometh his face and he is filled with wrath. (People hated to get a female issue and if they got it, they used to bury it alive.) See 16:54

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He hideth himself from the people, of the evil for the tidings given to him, (he pondereth whether) he shall keep her with disgrace or bury her (alive) in the dust? Behold, (how) evil it is what they decide. See 16:54

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And for you they beseem well when ye drive them (home) and when ye drive them forth (to pasture.) See 16:4

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For those who believe not in the hereafter is an evil similitude, and God's is the highest similitude; for He is the Mighty, the All-Wise. This verse read with verses 53:27 - 53:31 refers to the common belief of the pagans about the angels that they were step-daughters of God or goddesses. It is true of those who cannot see any reality beyond the material realm. Therefore, to them should be in the similitude, of the material beings - thus they are either male or female and the same was applied to the angels - considering God as a male (father) termed the angels as female (i.e., goddesses). (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If God had to take to task the people for their inequity, He would not leave on it (the earth) a single moving being but He respiteth them until an appointed term; so when cometh their doom, they shall delay it not (even) an hour, nor shall they bring it on before (its appointed time). See 16:60

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they assign unto God what they (themselves) (Worshipping angels as the daughters of God.) hate (Daughters.) and attribute their tongues falsely that for them are (all) (Sons – or – good rewards.) good things; Inevitably there shall be for them the (Hell) fire and they shall be the foremost to it. (Hell fire.) See 16:60

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By God! indeed sent We (Our) Apostles unto people before thee, but Satan made unto them their deeds fair-seeming, so he is their guardian today, and for them shall be a grievous chastisement. See 16:60

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We sent not down unto thee (O' Our Apostle Muham mad!) the Book (the Qur'an) but that thou mayest explain unto them that which they differ (Such a polytheism, Dualism, Trinity, crucification of Jesus - his resurrection - heresy of Aaron and Solomon, about what is permissible & what is forbidden etc.) about, and (as) a guidance and a mercy for the people who believe. See 16:60

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God hath sent down from the heavens water, then enliveneth He with it the earth after its death; Verily, in this is a sign for people who listen. Some commentators interpret the mention of the life-giving water being raised from heaven and quickening the dead earth as the revelation of the Holy Qur'an and the world getting enlightened by the knowledge of the truth revealed through Islam.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily for you there in the cattle is a lesson; We give you to drink what is in their bellies, from betwixt the (Sediment - excrement of the beasts.) faeces and the blood, milk pure, easy and palatable for those who drink (it). It is a Divine Law working in nature that milk is sorted out of the food after the creation of blood and before the actual excretion of the bowels. The 'Betwixt' refers to the middle of the functioning of the process and does not refer to the quality concerned. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of the fruits of the date-palms, and the grapes - obtain ye from them (drinks of) intoxication and goodly sustenance; Verily in this is a sign for people who understand. Some commentators thought that this passage was revealed before the prohibition of intoxicating liquor but the passage has nothing to do with the permissibility or the prohibition of liquor. It states the various usages of the product of the fruits. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (Inspired through instincts.) revealed thy Lord unto the bee saying: "Make thou hives in the mountains and in the trees and in what they (men) (Buildings.) build," 'Wahi' mentioned here is not through the same source as it was effected for the revelation of the Holy Qur'an or conveying any matter from God to the Holy Prophet or any other apostles Here the 'Wahi' stands for the instinct endowed in the Bee. Instincts and inspirations are also a kind of 'Wahi' or a Divine Guidance. Even the inanimate objects are inspired with the Will of the Lord.1 The disciples of Jesus were inspired to believe in Jesus.2 The mother of Moses was also inspired to act in a particular way.3 It is clear that every one who gets such an inspiration or endowed with such special instinct is not…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then eat thou of all the fruits and walk thou in the ways of thy Lord submissively." There cometh out from within it a drink of divers colours, in it is healing for men; Verily in this is a sign for the people who reflect. See 16:68

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And bear they your burdens to lands which ye could not else reach but with distress unto (your) self; Verily thy Lord is Pitiful, All-Merciful, See 16:4

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God hath created you, then He taketh you away, and of you is he who is reverted to the lowest state of the age, so that he knoweth not aught after (once) having knowledge: Verily God is All-Knowing, All-Powerful. See 16:68

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God hath favoured some of you above the others in the provision of sustenance, now those who have been more favoured give not their sustenance to those whom their right hands possess, (the slaves) so that they may be equal therein; What! Is it then the bounty of God they deny? See 16:68

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God hath given you wives of your own selves, and hath given you from your wives sons and grandchildren, (To continue posterity.) and sustained you of good things; What! Is it then in the falsehood they believe, and (While.) (a) in the bounty of God (that) they disbelieve? See 16:68

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they worship other than God that which owneth not for them any sustenance (aught) from the heavens and the earth, nor have they (whom they worship) any power? See 16:68

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So coin ye not any similitudes to God; Verily God knoweth (everything) and ye know not. See 16:68

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Setteth forth God the similitude (of two men: one) a slave, a property of another, who hath no power over aught, and (the one) whom We sustained from unto Ourselves a goodly sustenance, and he spendeth from it secretly and openly; Are the two equal? All praise is God's! But most of them know it not. See 16:68

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Setteth forth God the similitude of two men; one of them is dumb, unable to do anything, he is a burden to his master; wherever he (the master) sendeth him, he bringeth no good; can he be equal to him who enjoineth justice and he (himself) is on the straight (Right.) path? Compare the purity of character, conduct and the inimitable personal excellence of the First Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abi Talib and his identity with the Holy Prophet, and what yeoman services he lent in the establishment of the faith, Islam, in the worst of the situations, to those whose character and conduct had to be remoulded and whose personal weaknesses, lack of faith and cowardice made them run away from the situations deserting the Holy Prophet and leaving him amidst the worst of his blood-thirsty enemies.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God's is the unseen (worlds) of the heavens and the earth; and the matter of the Hour (of Judgment) is but like a twinkling (Refer to verse 54:50.) of the eye, or nigher still; Verily God over all things hath power. See 16:76

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God hath brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers - ye knew not anything, and He gave you hearing and the sight and the hearts, that ye may give thanks. See 16:76

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! See they not towards the birds held poised in the air in the sky? Nothing holdeth them but God; (By giving them the balancing faculty.) Verily in this are signs for a people who believe See 16:76

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (He made) horses and mules and asses that ye might ride upon them and as adornment; and createth He what ye know not. See 16:4

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God hath made for you of your houses, a place of rest (and the quiet) and hath made for you of the skins of the cattle houses (Tents.) which ye find so light to carry on the day of your march and on the day of your camping, and of their wool and their fur and their hair (he hath provided for you) (useful) goods of convenience and a provision for a time. See 16:76

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God hath made for you, of what He hath created shelters, and hath made for you (some) of the mountains (as) places of refuge, and He hath made for you garments to guard you against the heat (and cold), and the garments (Armour.) to protect you in your fighting; Thus completed! He, His bounties on you so that ye may submit (unto Him thankfully). See 16:76

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But if turn they away, then on thee is incumbent only the clear delivery (of Our message). See 16:76

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They recognise the bounties of God, and yet they deny them, and most of them are infidels (Ungrateful ones – Deniers.) By 'Na'mah', i.e., the bounty or the favour, is meant the Holy Prophet. The Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq said: 'the grace or the bounties of God were perfected with the appointment of Ali Ibn Abi Talib as the Maula or the Master in the place of the Holy Prophet on the day of Ghadir Khumm.'1The huge gathering of the thousands of the people like the pilgrims witnessed it and Omar Ibn Khattab was the first to felicitate by his homage or 'Bay'ah' to Ali on his appointment as the 'Maula' or the Master of every believer-man and believer-woman and yet the people denied it and acted not as decreed or commanded by the Holy Prophet through…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on the day We will raise up from among every people a witness, then shall be no permission for those who disbelieve (to make any excuses) nor shall they be allowed (Since after that no further amendment could be expected in the life hereafter.) to solicit any amends. See 16:83

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when those who act unjustly shall see the torment, it shall not be lightened for them, nor shall they be respited. See 16:83

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:86 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when those who associate (others with God) will see their associates, (The false gods i.e., the deities associated with God.) they shall say: "O' Our Lord! These are our associates whom we called besides Thee!" But they will throw (back) unto them (their) word, (and say) "Verily ye are liars!" See 16:83

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:87 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they shall tender submission unto God on that day; And shall depart from them (leaving them in lurch) what they were forging. See 16:83

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:88 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (For) those who disbelieved and hinder people from the way of God: And We unto them will increase torment over torment for they were making mischief. See 16:83

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:89 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on the day when We will raise up in every people from among themselves, a witness (upon them) and bring thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) as a witness upon (all) these; and We have sent down upon thee the Book (The Qur'an) explaining everything, and a guidance, and mercy, and glad tidings unto those who submit themselves (To God). As in verse 16:84.This verse makes obvious the unique spiritual existence of the Holy Prophet from the very beginning of the world to its end. Evidence could be acceptably taken only when the individual giving the evidence has witnessed the object under question. The witness to give evidence about a people would naturally be the apostle who ministered to them the truth and the one to be a witness over all such witnesses could be only he who must have…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And upon God rests the guidance unto the right way, and of them (the ways) are the deviating ones; and if He willeth He would certainly guide you all aright. Referring to the means of communication, it is asserted that God will add something besides what is already known, (i.e., what is unknown) and the purpose of it is to straighten or shorten the way and facilitate the conveyance towards reaching its destination. Asserting that providing this facility is His duty, it indicates that along with the straight ways there are crooked ways also, and God does not force anything on any one. By these examples of the means of communication in the physical life, man is reminded of the means of communication between man and God. It is God's duty to show man the right path and the crooked…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:90 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, God enjoineth justice and benevolence (to others) and giving (Benevolently.) unto the kindred, and forbiddeth lewdness, and evil, and rebellion; He exhorteth you that ye may take heed. The Fifth Holy Imam Muhammad Ibn Ali al-Baqir said that 'Giving to the relatives' stands for the relatives of the Holy Prophet, i.e., Ahl al-Bayt, as in the case of verses 8:41; 17:26; 30:38; 59:7. It is left for every student of the Holy Qur'an to consider that God's command is to deliver to the relatives their due. How could the Holy Prophet himself go against such an explicit ordinance of the Lord and deny his only issue Fatema her due to inherit from her father. But history records the violation of this ordinance in denying Fatema her right over Fadak, the legacy left behind by the Holy Prophet.It is narrated…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:91 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And fulfil ye the covenant of God when ye have covenanted, and break ye not the oaths after ratification (Solemnizing them.) thereof while indeed ye have appointed God over you a surety (for it); Verily God knoweth (everything) what ye do. Was not the 'Bay'ah' taken by the Holy Prophet from the Muslim for Ali Ibn Abi Talib at Ghadir Khumm on 18-12-10 A.H. with a covenant and should it not be honoured and do not those who break that covenant violate this ordinance.The Verse emphatically enjoins the fulfilment of any promise, undertaking, pact or covenant provided it is not ungodly or illegal as it is implied in the phrase 'Ahdillah' particularly such pacts and promises in which God has been pledged as the guarantee for the fulfilment of it. For details refer to 'Fiqh' (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:92 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And be not like unto her who unraveleth her yarn, dis joining it into thin filaments, after she hath made it spun strong, ye take your oaths as means of deceit between you for one nation is more flourishing than (other) nation. Verily God only trieth you by this; And most assuredly He will make it clear unto you on the Day of Judgment about what ye were differing. To appreciate the exact significance of this Verse one should refer to the sermon by Lady Zainab, the daughter of Ali and Fatema and the sister of Husayn, in the Bazaar of Kufa when she was taken as a captive after the martyrdom of Husayn at Karbala. She addressed the Muslims and reminded them of their covenants with God and the Holy Prophet and quoted this passage pointing out and saying,…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:93 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if God willeth He would surely make you all a single nation, but He leaveth to err whomsoever He willeth (This does not mean compulsion.) and guideth whomsoever He willeth; And certainly will ye be question ed of what ye were doing. See 16:92

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:94 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And take ye not your oaths a means of deceit between you, lest slippeth a foot after it hath been firmly fixed, and ye taste the evil for ye hindered (others) from God's way; and for you be a great torment. See 16:92

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:95 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Sell ye not the covenant of God for a mean (Worldly gain.) price; for verily with God is that which is better for you, if ye only knew. See 16:92

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:96 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What (ever) is with you passeth away and what is with God is everlasting; and certainly We will give those who exercise patience, their return, with (For Punishment or reward in this life is given for the sake of the act but in the hereafter the same evil or goodness done here, the worst or the best of it will be returned.) the best of what they were doing. See 16:92

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:97 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whosoever did good, whether male or female, and he be a believer, then We will certainly make him live a life good and pure, and certainly We will give them their return with (Refer to note on verse 16:96.) the best of what they were doing. See 16:92

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:98 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when recitest thou the Qur'an seek thou refuge with God from Satan the accursed. See 16:92

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nahl:99 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily there is no authority for him over those who believe and rely on their Lord. See 16:92

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the star when it goeth down Verses 1 to 8 assert the infallibility of the Holy Prophet in his movements between the Creator and the creation, similar to the movement of the star in its orbit. It negates any mistake or deviation in action or uttering anything other than what is revealed. It refers to his attaining the realisation and the stage of the realisation he had reached.The first stage of realisation he reached, is the stage of 'Istawa' in the highest horizon which is the highest stage of the angelical force, at which appear the two arcs, the arc of godhead and the arc of creation to meet. Then moving further beyond the dualistic view, assuming the state of pending between the finite and the infinite as the joining point between the two arcs, there comes the state…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then revealed He unto His Servant what He did reveal The tone of the statement clearly says that which transpired between God and the Select Servant and the Chosen One of His Apostles, i.e., the Holy Prophet, during the State of the maximum communion with the Lord, none could ever know it.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Belied not (his) heart what he saw (In his state of Ascension (A.P.).) What the Holy Prophet said about his seeing the angel Gabriel in his full stature of Strength and power, was not a lie. This does not at all indicate his seeing God with his physical eyes, for the physical eyes can see only physical matter or material things and God is not matter but the Creator of matter. God being only the Absolute Truth that is active in everything, everywhere, an infinite existence, no finite being can ever view the infinite One. What the Holy Prophet saw in the heaven, he saw only the manifestation of His glory and power.No doubt the things of greater glory of God, in His Kingdom in the heavens would naturally be quite different than those on the earth and as such…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Dispute ye then with him as to what he saw? It is an interrogatory address to those who disbelieved in what the Holy Prophet related about his experiences in the heavens, during his Ascension - Journey.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed he (The Holy Prophet.) did see him (Archangel Gabriel.) at another descent (The last but one height in Heaven) The Holy Prophet saw Gabriel for a second time.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: At the 'Sidra' (Overshadowing.) (the Lotetree) 'Muntaha' (the all-Comprehensive Terminus) (Refer to Verses 34:16; 56:28.) The second time the Holy Prophet saw Gabriel, was at the 'Sidratul-Muntaha' the point where ends or stops all knowledge of every one - and no one's knowledge crosses the limit. It is said that when the Holy Prophet reached the point of 'Sidrat ul-Muntaha', Gabriel said "I shall not step an inch further from this." The Holy Prophet passed that point also and what is mentioned in verse 8, 9 & 10 above is what happened after crossing this point when Gabriel had stopped away.There is the mention of the Lote-tree in verses 34:16 and 56:28 as symbolic of the heavenly bliss. But the mention of it here, is a symbol marking the extreme bounds or the last limit of heavenly knowledge beyond which…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nigh unto it is the Garden-Abode (Paradise, Heavenly adobe of Bliss.) The garden or Paradise or the blissful region near the Sidra is the abode of the pious ones - and some say, it is the place of the highest resort for all angels also.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When covereth (over) the 'Sidra' (Tree) that which covereth it After reaching the point of Sidra, the realities of the Kingdom of God beyond the point unveiled, i.e., the Holy Prophet was made to visualise the kingdom beyond Sidra which none else besides God has the knowledge of it.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Neither his eye did dazzle nor did it rebel (There was no visual delusion nor any nor any intellectual or emotional disturbance.) In spite of the things around made manifest, being full of marvel and wonder, the Holy Prophet's gaze was only towards the manifest Glory of the Lord and never even cast his glance on anything around him, nor did his eye or his sight or attention was so much engrossed in view the glory of the Lord that it did not care to turn towards anything of his environment though everything was full of marvels and wonder. This is only the skeleton of the great event each expression here has its mystic meaning see note by (A.P.) below.There was no visual delusion nor any physical disturbance. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed he did see of the greatest signs of his Lord Let not any misleading idea pollute our faith that it is in the highest heaven that God lives or His existence is found only there, for it is not in the sense of any physical space but it is to denote the excellence or the degree of the special manifestation of His Higher glory, otherwise His 'Arsh' or the Throne of lbs authority and glory extends over the heavens and the earth1.Of all the Apostles of God, it was only Moses whom only the prefigurement of the divine effulgence on earth took place. See 20:10 - 20:14, 20:28 - 20:30 and Exodus here below:"Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian, 'and he led the flock behind the desert, and came to the mountain…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: See ye then (the idols) Lat and the Uzza ? When the Holy Prophet was reciting this Sura, a voice was heard reciting "There are the lofty idols, verily their intercession is sought", to disturb the recital of the Sura and to put the audience into confusion but the whole context goes against this insertion1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Erreth not your Companion (Our Apostle Muhammad) nor is he led astray (Refer to Verses 4:113; 93:7.) 'Sahib' meaning companion, i.e., The Holy Prophet - he is addressed as such for his living among the people along with them in the same place.The negation about his going astray or deviating from the right path or uttering anything of his own inclination and the assertion of his being directly under the revelation, is not restricted to any particular age or period or any particular aspect of his life but starts from his very pregenetal state to which fact bears testimony and evidence the statement of Abu Talib, the uncle of the Holy Prophet and the father of 'Ali in one of his eulogical verses addressed to the Holy Prophet while he was still very young: "Certainly do I bear testimony to…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And Manat, the third (idol) besides? (This and the following Verses are in immediate refutation of the confusing satanic insertion (A.P.).) See 53:19

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! for you the males and for Him (God) the females? (Refer to Verses 16:57; 16:58; 43:16; 52:39.) See 53:19

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This indeed is a division unjust See 53:19

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They are nothing but (mere) names, which have named ye and your fathers (The false gods or the deities which the idolators worship they are mere names of unreal imaginary beings- - hence they are mere names - and nothing more.) , sent not God for them any authority; They follow nothing but a conjecture what their selves are inclined to; and indeed, hath come unto them from their Lord the right guidance (Refer to Verses 7:71; 12:40.) What the idolaters worship as gods, are merely names without any reality or anything which at all existed1. It was only their conjectures2.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Shall man have whatever he wisheth? It is not for man to have anything he covets for, i.e., no man has the power or the authority to provide himself with whatever he wants.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! God's is the (life) hereafter and the former (life) (God's is the ultimate as is the Start, the Lord of all.) The Kingdom, i.e., the Authority, from the beginning to the end is exclusively God's and of no one else.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And how many an angel in heavens are whose intercession is of no avail at all save after that permitteth God whomsoever willeth He and chooseth (This clears the position of the angels regarding intercession.) The disbelievers hoped for the intercession of the angels, for them. It shall be of no avail to them for there could be no intercession without God's permission1.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who believe not in the hereafter (The life beyond the physical one.) name the angels (The heathens believed the angels to be the daughters of God.) with female names See 53:26

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But they have not of it anything of knowledge; they follow nothing but a conjecture; verily a conjecture availeth naught the truth at all (This applies to all materialistic schools.) See 53:26

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therefore, turn thou (The Prophet addressed for the people.) aside from him who turneth his back against Our reminder, and desireth not anything but the life of this world (This indicates that the materialists see everything in the term of material life.) See 53:26

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And nor he speaketh of (his own) inclination (The Holy Prophet.) This unique quality of the godly truthfulness. Everything of the utterance of the Holy Prophet has been referred to while Moses was told by God about the advent of his Apostle (Muhammad)1, and a similar prophecy did Jesus make to his followers, before his departure from the informing of the advent of the Comforter, the Spirit of Truth and the Holy Ghost."I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth: and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him." Deut. 18/18."Howbeit when he, the Spirit of Truth, is come, he null guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself, but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That is the (last) reach of their knowledge; Verily, thy Lord knoweth best of him who is astray from His path and He knoweth best of him who is guided aright See 53:26

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God's is whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, that He may recompense those who do evil for what they did, and that He may recompense those who do good, with what is best See 53:26

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who do avoid the great ones of the sin and shameful (Indecencies.) deeds save accidentally (Provided followed immediately.) verily, thy Lord is (the Lord of) vast forgiveness: He knoweth best about you when He raised you from the earth (Dust.) and when ye are embryos in the wombs of your mothers; so assert ye not the purity of your selves; He knoweth best of him who guardeth (himself against evil) Among 'Kaba'ir', i.e., the great sins, is adultery and theft which are very vehemently condemned in Islam and severely punished.'Lamam', i.e., stands for the desire or the intention not enacted and also the sins committed before embracing Islam, i.e., while the individual was ignorant of the laws against the evils, but subsequently repented for and amended."God is liberal in forgiving" - As His existence is infinite, every attribute of…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hast thou then seen him who hath turned his back "He who turns back" refers to those who forsake the faith like those who left the Holy Prophet in the midst of danger and ran away from the battles of Uhud and Hunayn.According to Minhaj us-Sadiqin Uthman bargained with Abdullah Ibn Ubay for a camel load of merchandise if Abdullah would take upon himself the sins of Uthman. After giving the merchandise Uthman put a stop to alms giving relying upon Abdullah's undertaking. Then these verses were revealed. If we accept Islam, we must accept it whole-heartedly and not look back to pagan superstitions. No man can bargain about spiritual matters, for he cannot see what his end will be in the hereafter. It is the unchangeable law of Allah in every age that no bearer of burden can bear…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And giveth he a little and withholdeth (his hand) See 53:33

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Is with him the know-ledge of the unseen that he seeth The question is to say that the one who believed in Abdullah's undertaking the responsibility of his sins and stopped his charity did not have the knowledge of the hidden, i.e., whether what Abdullah claimed to hold himself responsible for the other man's sins, had any truth in it or not.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or hath he not been told of what is in the scriptures of Moses? See 53:35

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of Abraham who fully discharged (his mission)? See 53:35

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That no bearer of a burden shall bear the burden of another (No one shall bear the burden of another. Refer to Verses 2:48; 2:123; 2:254; 17:15; 35:18.) The verse 38 answers the question asked in Verse 35.For further details, see the commentary of 2:48; 2:123; 2:254; 6:165; 17:15; 35:18.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And that there is not for man (aught) save what he striveth for (Refer to Verse 52:21.) Note the individual responsibility every man and woman is charged with to work goodness and shun evil as much as one could do it and thus make this world itself a blissful place to live in.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It (the wording) (His speech.) is naught but a revelation revealed (unto him) (Refer to Verse 10:15.) See 53:3

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And that his striving shall soon be seen (Refer to Verse 52:21.) See 53:39

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then shall he be recompensed to the fullest measure See 53:39

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And that unto thy Lord is the end (of all) (Refer to Verses 79:42 - 79:44.) See 53:39

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily He it is Who causeth (one) to laugh and causeth (him) to weep See 53:39

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And that He it is Who causeth death and causeth life See 53:39

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament

The constellation beyond the Zodiac line which was the object of some star worshippers. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Taught him the (No one else.) one Intense in power (Refer to Verse 81:20.) 'Allamaho', i.e., 'Taught him', i.e., he revealed to him who is endowed with mighty' power by God, i.e., the Angel Gabriel - meaning the Holy Qur'an is no poetry composed - no stories compiled by the Holy Prophet but the Word of God which has been conveyed to him by the Angel being the nearest of God, 'Mighty in Power' compared to the others of his kind1.Shadid al-Quwa, "the supreme in power", is Allah. To translate and interpret it as the angel Jibrail is to belie the verses 30 to 38 of Baqarah2 and verse 75 of Sad, because Jibrail was one of the angels who prostrated themselves before Adam when Adam taught them "the names" they did not know. As mentioned in the commentary of…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The one endued with wisdom; (and) hence he (The Holy Prophet.) took an overviewing position This verse refers to the 'Mi'raj,' i.e., Ascension of the Holy Prophet into the heavens and him meeting the Angel Gabriel in his full form of his wonderful strength.For all the details of the Ascension, Mi'raj, see the commentary of Bani Israil 17:1.The Holy Prophet held in view the entire universe from the highest position, where he found Jibrail. Then the Holy Prophet drew near to Allah "till a distance of two bows or still nearer"The nearness described by "still nearer" cannot be imagined by human mind. It is the nearest nearness possible between the finite and the infinite. Arabic idiom qaba qawsayn indicate extreme nearness. "The drawn bows, with their chords touching," make a circle of union, yet the Holy Prophet is not to…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Prostration is compulsory at the recitation of this verse for there is the command of the Lord to do it and it must immediately be obeyed then and there and the later part of the Verse is to obey them, i. e., to serve Him, which means to mould the life as a whole as desired by the Lord and actuate it accordingly and not as forced by one's passions.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: While he was in the highest horizon Gabriel was found in the highest part of the heavens and power. At this place the Holy Prophet heard a Voice - he asked the Angel Gabriel who was with him as what the Voice was - the Angel replied that it is Lord's prayer or blessing which was - 'Subboohun Quddoos Ana Rabbul-Malaikato War Rooh-Sabaqat-Ramati Ghazabi' - Hallowed and Holy - 'I am the Lord of the 'Malaika' and the Spirit. My Merry dominates My Wrath.' (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then he drew nigh, and became pending (Refer to Verse 17:1.) The Holy Prophet drew nearer and nearer to Him - a reference to the 'Mi'raj' (Ascension) of the Holy Prophet and his reaching the nearest point of approach possible for any mortal. The Holy Prophet was drawn nearer and still nearer to the All-Divine Lord.In between the creation and the Creator, i.e., the finite and the infinite (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Najm:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus was (he) the measure between two bows (facing each other) or nigher still (In between the creation and the Creator i.e. between the finite and the infinite (A.P.). Refer to Verse 17:1.) A reference to the highest state of communion with God granted to the Holy Prophet. Note the beautiful illustration given to the maximum communion with God which the Holy Prophet was granted. The measure or the distance of two bows, to mean that when the two bows meet, they meet at their ends but still they are away from each other on all points of their body. It could never mean' that the Holy Prophet was totally absorbed into divinity and yet bodily as is mortal, he was separate from God.It must be remembered that the expression of getting nearer used in this verse and in the…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ta (Refer to note on verse 2:1.) Seen (Refer to note on verse 2:1.) These are the verses of the Qur'an, and the Book maketh the truth manifesting, See 27:2

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And cast thou down thy staff! "So when he saw it moving as if (it was) a serpent, he turned back retreating and returned not: (then it was said unto him): "O' Moses' (Fear befits not the apostles of God. Refer to verse 20:21.) Fear not! for shall not fear (My) apostles in My presence." See verses 27:10 & 20:21. Note, God says that no apostle shall have any fright in His presence. How could the Prince of Apostles, the Holy Prophet Muhammad, have any fright when he was first commissioned by God through the Messenger Angel Gabriel. The blasphemy against the Holy Prophet is proved. This is a proof also of the fact that all apostles of God are sinless and infallible.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Save he who hath been unjust, then in its place he doeth good after the evil, for verily I am the Oft-Forgiving, the All- Merciful. See 27:10

item.description: Now put thy hand into thy bosom, it shall come forth white, shining, without evil: (this is) along with the nine signs (thou wilt take) unto Pharaoh and his people; Verily, they are a transgressing people See 27:10

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
