item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They denied them in iniquity and arrogance while their hearts (Lit. Selves – souls.) were convinced; See then how was the end of the mischief makers. See 27:10

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed gave We knowledge to David and Solomon, and (both the apostles) said: "All praise is God's, Who hath made us to excel many of the believing servants," This verse proves that knowledge to the apostles of God is gifted by God Himself and not acquired by them from anyone in the world. The same was true with the Twelve Holy Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt who learnt nothing from any one on earth and yet were the fountainheads of wonderful knowledge and wisdom.1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And Solomon (Compare with this the false tradition "We the apostles neither inherit nor leave any thing to be inherited" which was advanced just to deprive Fatima of her right.) inherited David, and he said "O' people! We have been taught the language of the birds, and We have been granted (plenty) of every thing; Verily this is a manifest grace." It is said that David had 19 sons and each contested to inherit his father's (David) throne. God informed David of a few questions with their answers and commanded David to put the questions to each of his sons and whosoever answers correctly, shall be David's heir. David called all his sons in the presence of the scholars and the chiefs of the tribes and put the following questions:What is the nearest thing?What is the farthest thing?What is the…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And gathered together unto Solomon his hosts of jinn and men and birds, then they were arrayed in ranks. The hosts at the disposal of Solomon consisted of all varieties of God's creation viz., birds, animals, beasts, men, the spiritual beings like jinn etc. It is said that the hosts occupied a very extensive space on earth.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Until they came to the valley of the Ants, said an Ant (addressing the other ants of the valley): "O' ye ants! enter ye into your dwellings, so that Solomon and his hosts may not crush ye (all) while they know (Unintentionally - without knowledge.) it not." As usual with him, a commentator has put up his own construction upon the word 'Naml' and draws his own interpretation using the obscure meaning of the word 'Naml'. The motive behind such interpretation is to deny the extraordinary significance of Solomon being recognised even by the small beings in God's creation on earth viz. the ants. The meaning of the matter in this verse is the same as the simplest rendering of it gives out, i.e., it was the valley of the Ants. The Sixth Holy Imam Jafar Ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq says…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then smiled (Solomon) laughing at her word, and said: "O' My Lord! (Make me to.) arouse me to be thankful for thy bounty which thou hast bestowed on me and my parents, and that I do good such as Thou wouldst be pleased with, and admit me by Thy mercy, among Thy righteous servants." Solomon smiled at the caution taken by the ants and ordered his hosts to await the ants getting into their holes and to be careful against causing any hurt to the ants in their passing over the land. It is said that Solomon addressing the chief of the ants said: "How could my hosts hurt thee and thy kind as they are passing in air and dost thou not know that I am the apostle of God and would never act inequitably?" The chief replied "O'…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: A guidance and glad tidings unto the believers, The Holy Qur'an does not mention names of persons but refers to their qualities so that the verse could be applied to any situation or individual, appropriate for the purpose. Here only the believers are mentioned and when any quality is indefinitely mentioned, it would naturally mean its perfection, wherever it might be found.The verse in the first place would mean those who possess the qualities in their perfection. It is the universally acknowledged truth that these qualities and also the others mentioned elsewhere in the Qur'an, are found in their perfection only in the Holy Ahl al-Bayt who were purified by God Himself.1 Hence the guidance and the glad tidings will first be meant to these holy ones and in the case of the others, only to the extent of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And reviewed the birds, then said: "How is it, I see not Hud-hud (Hoopoe) or is that he is among the absentees?" 'Hudhud', i.e., Hoopoe - It is reported that whenever Solomon went on a journey and fell in want of water for ablution for prayers, this bird used to show the place of water, for it is an instinct in the bird that it could see water underground as one sees a liquid through a bottle. This could not be doubted in the days when by passing the rays of light through opaque bodies things beyond them are pictured (the Xray implement). If man can do it through his own device, there is no room to doubt God's endowing the power in one of his creations. There are many more wonders which as yet man has not dreamt of.'Tafaqqada',…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Certainly will I chastise him with a severe chastisement, or will I certainly slaughter him, or he shall bring unto me a (Excuse.) warrant clear, See 27:20

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And he tarried not long, then (he came up in the air and) said: "I comprehend what thou comprehendeth not, and I have brought unto thee from Sheba tidings sure." When 'Hudhud' was flying to report himself to Solomon, he met another of its kind and asked him to which place he belonged. 'Hudhud' replied 'To Solomon's kingdom', and gave the details of Solomon's glory and asked the other bird about his native place and he gave the details of the vast realm of 'Saba' (Sheba) which was ruled by Bilqis the Queen. Hudhud flew along with him to the land of Bilqis and having witnessed the greatness and the glory of the royal court of the Queen returned to Solomon and reported to Solomon about the vast realm which Bilqis the Queen ruled, the greatness of her wealth and…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily found I a woman ruling over them, and she hath been given plenty of every thing, and she hath a throne magnificent. Hudhud related all that he saw in Sheba about the Queen and the people who worshipped the sun. It is commended that the reciter of this verse offers 'Sajdah' or prostration.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And I found her and her people prostrating (in obeisance) unto the sun, besides God, and unto them Satan hath made their deeds fair-seeming, and thus hath turned them from the (right) way, so they are not guided aright. See 27:23

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That (why) they make not obeisance unto God. Who bringeth forth to light what is hid den in the heavens and the earth and what ye hide and what ye manifest, See 27:23

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God! There is no God but He! He is the Lord of 'Arsh', the Mighty (Throne of Supreme Authority) See 27:23

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Solomon): "We will see if thou hast uttered the truth or thou art of the liars" To test the statement of Hudhud, Solomon wrote an epistle to the Queen of Sheba.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Go thou with this letter of mine and convey it unto them, and turn away from them and see what (answer) they return Hudhud is given the epistle to the Queen of Sheba and to get a reply to it.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (On receipt of the epistle from Solomon.) (the Queen of Sheba) "O' ye Chiefs! Verily, has been delivered unto me a letter honourable!" The Queen receiving the epistle consulted her courtiers about the graceful communication she had received from Solomon.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Who establish prayer and give the poor-rate, and of the hereafter, they are sure. See 27:2

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, it is from Solomon; And it is: "In (The text of the epistle.) the name of God the Beneficent, the Most Merciful" The matter of these two verses was the contents of the communication from Solomon. Solomon had invited the Queen and her people to Islam, i.e., submission to God, against their submitting themselves to anything else.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That "exalt not yourselves against me, and come ye unto me submitting (yourselves to God)" See 27:30

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said she: "O' ye chiefs! advise me in (this) my affair; (To reply to Solomon's epistle.) (ye know) that I decide not any affair but in your view" (In consultation.) See 27:30

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They said: "We are endued with strength and possess mighty prowess, and (But.) to command is thine: so think (well before) what thou wilt command" See 27:30

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (the Queen): "Verily kings, when they enter a town (victorious), ruin it and make the noblest of its people the meanest; and thus will they (also) do." See 27:30

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily I will send unto him a present, and (wait to) see with what (answer) return the messengers The Queen decided to send some valuable presents to Solomon and something to test his wisdom. If Solomon was only a king, he would accept the presents and would not know the solution of the things of test and if he be an apostle of God, he would reject the gifts and declare the matter hidden in the problematic things. She sent many invaluable gifts and along with them some slaves in the guise of women and some female attendants of her in garb of men.When the messenger from the Queen arrived in the Land of Solomon and found the greatness and glory of Solomon's possessions and his court, compared to which the gifts he had brought for Solomon were worthless…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when came (the messenger of the Queen) unto Solomon, said (Solomon): "Aid ye me with riches? But what God hath given unto me is better than what He hath given unto you, Aye! it is ye, of your present, exultant." It indicates that Solomon was proud of the divine blessings and the power bestowed in him and not of the temporal power and worldly possessions. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Return thou unto them: for we will surely come unto them with (such) hosts which they shall not be able to meet, and certainly will we expel them out therefrom abased, while they shall be contemptible. Solomon ordered the Messenger to return to his Queen and informed him of his decision to march to Sheba with his unconquerable hosts.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Solomon): "O' ye chiefs! which of you can bring unto me her throne, ere they come unto me submitting?" (Bold.) See 27:37

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said an audacious one among the jinn; "I will bring it unto thee ere thou risest up from thy place; for verily I am strong (enough to do it) and I am (also thy) trusted one" The task which Solomon wanted to achieve was something which ordinarily seemed to be impossible, i.e., the bringing of the Queen single-handed arresting her and presenting her with her throne itself. The offer to do it was from a jinn who said he would do it before Solomon rises from his seat, i.e., Solomon disperses his court and gets up but even with that, Solomon was not satisfied. The Ahmadi Commentator just to establish his own peculiar interpretation of the word of Jinn that was an Amalekite who was of a large stature. It will be ridiculous to imagine that however huge a man…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who believe not in the hereafter, We have made their deeds fair-seeming unto them, so they wander bewildered. God Himself making the deeds of the disbelievers, fair-seeming to them, means that the disbelievers being endowed with the means to enjoy His bounties in this world, but the people intoxicated with the abundance of the bounties of God, instead of being grateful, meek and submitting to God take undue advantage of their position with the means given to them and get attracted by the evil ways of using the bounties conferred on them. This is what usually happens in the case of the wealthy ones particularly those who have been given by God to rule the States. Instead of their being gratefully obedient to God, they get maddened and blinded by their means and spend their wealth and time…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he with whom was some knowledge (of a part) of the Book: "I will bring it unto thee ere thy eye (When the one with the Knowledge of a part of the Book could do this, imagine what the one (Ali) with the Knowledge of the whole of the Book could do, about whom the Holy Prophet said: 'I am the City of Knowledge & Ali is its Gate.') twinkleth," and when saw (Solomon) the throne settled besides him, he said: "This is by the grace of my Lord that He may try (Prove.) me if I am grateful or am ungrateful; and he who is grateful, verily he is grateful for his own self, and whoever is ungrateful, then verily my Lord is Self-Sufficient, (Ar. Ghani.) Bounteous." This verse is of special importance and special significance to guide…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Solomon): "Transform (Alter it to look otherwise.) her throne for her; we will see if she followeth the way aright, or (she is) of those who go not aright?" See 27:40

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So when came (the queen), it was said (unto her): "Is thy throne (also) like this?" Said she: "as it were the same, and we were (already) given the knowledge (of thy apostleship) before it, and we were submitting." See 27:40

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But prevented her what she worshipped besides God, verily she was of the disbelieving people. See 27:40

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It was said unto her: "Enter thou the palace", but when she saw it she deemed it to be a pool of water and bared her legs; (Solomon) said: "Verily this is but a place smoothed with (slabs of) glass;" said (the Queen): "My Lord! verily I have been unjust to myself, and I submit (along) with Solomon unto God, the Lord of the worlds." While receiving the Queen, Solomon had made arrangements to disillusion her mind by an unbreakable argument and undeniable fact. He had built a palace of glass with a floor of glass and under the sheet of the glass, flowed water with fishes of various kinds. The floor seemed to be one tank of water since the glass sheet covering the water was made indistinguishable. When the Queen arrived, she had to pass through the courtyard…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed sent We unto (the tribe of) Thamud their brother Salih, saying: "Worship ye God (alone)!" but lo! they became two parties, wrangling (with each other). See 27:44

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Salih): O' my people! Why seek ye to hasten on the evil ere the good? Why seek ye not pardon of God? that ye may be shewn mercy. Since the people always waited for the fulfilment of the threat against the wrath of God, it is said, why do they hasten it, and not seek God's pardon and his protection against the chastisement.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "We augur ill from thee and those with thee." Said (Salih): "Your ill augury (Omen.) is with God; Nay! ye are a people who are being (Put to trial.) tried." See 27:46

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And there were in the town nine men who made mischief in the land and they would not amend (Reform – rectify.) (themselves) There were nine ringleaders of the mischief-mongers in the town of Salih who were always behind every mischief. The Holy Prophet said the most cursed one of the people would be the assassin of Ali Ibn Abi Talib.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They said: "Swear ye to one another by God that surely we will suddenly attack by night, him and his family, and then surely we would say unto his heir we witnessed not the murder of his family, and verily we are truthful." Conspiracy was made against the Holy Prophet by the tribes of the Quraysh after the demise of Abu Talib, and this became the cause of the 'Hijrah', i.e., migration of the Holy Prophet from Mecca to Medina. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These are those for whom shall be a grievous chastisement, and (these are) they in the hereafter, who shall be the greatest losers, See 27:4

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And plotted they and We (too) plotted a plot, and they perceived not. Similar plotting was done against the Holy Prophet also - Ali's taking the place of the Holy Prophet in his couch at the night of his Migration to Medina which led to their destruction later on in the battles of Badr, Uhud and till the conquest of Mecca. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: See then what was the end of their plot, that We, destroyed them and their people as a whole. See 27:50

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So those are their houses in empty ruins for they were unjust; Verily there is in this a sign for people who understand. See 27:50

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And delivered We those who believed and guarded (themselves) against evil. See 27:50

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (sent We) Lut, when said he unto his people "What! Commit ye filthiness while ye see." See 27:50

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! come ye unto men with lust rather than (unto) women? Verily ye are ignorant people? See 27:50

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But the answer of his people was naught save that said they: "Turn ye the people of Lut out of your town; Verily they are people (who seek to be) Pure." See 27:50

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So We delivered him and his followers, except his wife (Note: a wife of an apostle is wicked to be chastised by God. This is a clear proof that a woman because of her being the wife of a prophet can not also be his Ahl al-Bayt.) ; We had decreed her to be of those who remained behind. See 27:50

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And showered We on them a shower, and evil was the shower of those who had been warned. See 27:50

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "All praise be (only) to God, and peace be on His servants whom He hath chosen: What! Is God better, or what they join (within?)" According to the interpretation of the Holy Ahl al-Bayt, the servants of God referred to herein this verse are the Holy Prophet and the Holy Imams. (M.S., U.B.)1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) receivest the Qur'an from unto the All-Wise, All-Knowing. See 27:4

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is not He Who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down for you water from heaven; then caused We to grow by it gardens beautiful; it was not in your power that ye grow the trees thereof; What! Is there any god with God? Nay! they are a people who (yet) find equals (unto Him)? See 27:59

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is not He Who made the earth a resting place, and made in it rivers, and made on it mountains, and caused between two seas a barrier; Is there any god with God? Nay! most of them know not. See 27:59

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is (Note: The recital of the first clause from: "Amman yujibu al-mudhtarra idha da'ahu wa yakshifu us-su'u" is an often found surely effective prayer for relief from any unavoidable difficulty 12,000 times at a stretch - but with the constancy of the 'Wajib' or compulsory daily prayers. Beginning and ending with 'Salawaat'.) not He Who answereth the distressed one when he calleth Him, and removeth the distress and maketh you the successors in the earth; Is there any god with God? (Nay!) Little it is what ye reflect. This verse forms an unfailing prayer, if recited 12,000 times at the time of any insurmountable difficulty or need.It is true that man in general is the Vicegerent of God on earth but all are not on equal footing in the vicegerency. In accordance to verse 6:166, some are made superior in…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is not He Who guideth you in the darkness of the land and the sea, and Who sendeth the winds as the bearers of the good news of His Mercy? Is there any god with God? Exalted High is God above what they associate (with Him). See 27:62

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is not He Who originateth the creation, then reproduceth it, and Who provideth for you sustenance from the heaven and the earth? Is there any god with God? Say: "Bring ye your proof, if ye be truthful." See 27:62

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "None (either) in the heavens or in the earth knoweth the unseen save God; And they perceive not when they shall be raised" See 27:62

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! hath reached them the knowledge about the hereafter; Nay! they are in doubt about it; Nay! they are blind unto it. See 27:62

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say those who disbelieve: "What! when we have become dust, and our fathers (too), shall we certainly be brought forth (again)?" See 27:62

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed we had been promised this, we and our fathers before (too); (But) these are naught but stories of yore 'Travel' here does not actually mean travelling throughout the earth, it means a proper study of the life of the nations which proves beyond doubt that their actions were not without the consequences and is evidence that the movement of the whole system of creation is not without consequences. This is in answer to the doubts which the short-sighted materialist expressed. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Travel ye in the earth and see how was the end of the guilty (ones)" See 27:68

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When said Moses unto his family, "Verily I (Refer to verses 28:29 & 20:10.) perceive fire; soon will I bring unto you of it some tiding or bring I unto you a brand lighted, that ye may warm yourselves." See 27:4

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And grieve thou not for them and be not distressed of what they devise. See 27:68

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "When shall this promise (of chastisement) come to pass, if ye be truthful?" See 27:68

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Maybe that it is after you, a part of what ye seek to hasten." See 27:68

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily thy Lord is the Lord of grace unto the people but most of them thank not. The grace of God referred to here, will be clear if this verse is read with the verse 27:10. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily thy Lord well-knoweth what do enshroud their breasts and what they declare. See 27:73

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nothing is there hidden in the heavens and the earth but it is in the manifest Book. The Book manifest is the 'Lauh al-Mahfuz', i.e., the secured Tablet - it is called 'Mahfuz', i.e., secured because none else other than God has any hold on it. There is one point worth consideration, i.e., in the following verse God says that,'Everything We have accommodated in the Imam' (36:12)(i.e., Guide) 'Manifest' in which case it could be said the Imam or the divinely commissioned guide is also endowed by God with the knowledge as a whole. This fact is proved by the Holy Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, though not having any education under any mortal in this world and yet every one of them was the fountainhead of knowledge.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily this Qur'an relateth unto the children of Israel most of what they therein disagree. See 27:75

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily it is a (sure) guidance and mercy unto the believers. See 27:75

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, thy Lord will judge between them by His (Own) decree, and He is the All- Mighty, All-Knowing. See 27:75

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then rely thou on God; verily thou art on the manifest truth. See 27:75

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So when he came unto it, he was called unto saying, "Blessed is whosoever is in the fire and whosoever is about it; and hallowed is God, the Lord of the worlds!" The fire appeared to Moses, being actually the divine manifestation, obviously was blessed itself and whoever surrounded it, (i.e., the angels and Moses) - and to discard the possible conception identification or the of God with the Light or considering it as His incarnation. The last clause has been used to say that God is above being identified or incarnated even in light. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily thou canst not make the dead to listen nor canst thou make the deaf to hear the call when they turn away backward. The dead, the deaf and the blind mentioned here are the disbelievers who never wanted to see the right way or to know the truth for they are so deeply sunk in falsehood.Refer to verse 35:22. God can make whomsoever He pleases to hear - but the Holy Prophet limits it just to make the living and the man of understanding to hear as stated here. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And nor canst thou be a guide unto the Blind against their straying; thou canst make none hear save those who believe in Our signs, so they have submitted themselves. See 27:80

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when the word shall come to pass on them, We shall bring forth unto them, a walking one from the earth who shall speak unto them, that the people believed not (with certainty') in Our signs. This verse should be read in the light of verse 3:109: to guide people and make them do good and prevent them from doing mischief - God brought forth the best living being - at the end when the final judgment is going to pass against them. The living being which will be brought out from the earth to speak to people must be of the same category, i.e., he should he a human being of utmost accomplishment capable of addressing man of both the types good and bad. And this coincides with the day prescribed in the next Verse - the day…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on the day when We will collect from every people a party from those who belied our signs, then will they be formed into groups. This verse indicates the 'Raj'ah' that when the Last Holy Imam Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mehdi would appear s some of the staunch believers in God and those faithfully attached to the truth and those worst among the wicked ones would be resurrected to see their return for their own goodness and vices in this world itself before they meet the chastisement that awaits them after the Final Judgment.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Till they come before God (who will) say "Belied ye My signs while ye comprehended them not in your knowledge? or what is it ye were doing?" See 27:83

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the word shall come to pass on them for they were unjust, and they shall speak not. See 27:83

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:86 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! See they not that We have made the night that they may rest therein, and the day with light (to see); Verily, in this are signs for the people who believe? The change of the day and the night and the purpose they serve, bear clear testimony to the purposefulness of the plan of the Creator. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:87 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the day when there shall be blown the Trumpet, and those in the heavens and those in the earth shall be terrorized, save him whom God willeth, and all shall come unto Him abased. Refers to the day of the Total Resurrection as it is clear from the verse. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:88 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thou wilt see the mountains which thinkest thou firm, solid, pass away the pas sing of the (As pass the clouds in air.) clouds. It is the work of God Who hath made everything firm; Verily He is All-Aware of what (all) ye do. At the dawn of the Day of Judgment people would see the mountains blasted up into the skies and moving in the air as a cloud of dust.Refers to the continuous change in the material substance or substantial change in the matter which is the basis of evolution and the evidence of the purposefulness of the creation in the sense that motion means change of the past into present and present into future. Each following event is the total and the summing up of the preceding ones. Thus, the ultimate end is a sum total…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:89 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whosoever bringeth good, for him shall be better than it and they, of the terror of the day, be secure. See 27:88

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' Moses! Verily it is, I am God the All-Mighty, the All-Wise, The Voice came from the direction of the fire and not from the fire itself or the direction of the right side of the Valley - or from the Tree.1 There is no room for any conception of form or incarnation or God being a physical substance. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:90 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whosoever bringeth evil, these shall be cast down on their faces, in the (Hell) fire; Ye shall be recompensed for aught save what ye were doing. See 27:88

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:91 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Say thou unto them O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "I commanded only that I should serve the Lord of this city, Who am hath made it sacred, and His are all things, and commanded I am that I should be of the Muslims (those who have submitted themselves to God)," See 27:88

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:92 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And that I should recite the Qur'an: so whosoever is guided aright, he is guided aright for his (own self), and whosoever goeth astray, then say thou: "I am only of the warners." See 27:88

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Naml:93 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say thou, "All praise is God's. Soon will He show you His signs that ye shall recognise them;" and thy Lord is not heed less of what all ye do. See 27:88

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nasr:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When cometh the help of God and the Victory The great prophecy was wonderfully fulfilled in the bloodless conquest of Mecca, and the other Arab tribes sent their deputations to the Holy Prophet and entered the folds of the faith, Islam, one after another.The world knows that the one, the Holy Prophet who was persecuted and hunted out of his birth-place Mecca, and who took refuge in Madina, could not be defeated or stopped from having his godly way, even by the most formidable forces of the Meccans and their confederates. His mission gradually made its way and all the wickedness and the treachery of the enemy, recoiled on the enemies themselves. Now this prophecy and the promise came from the Lord with which all the outlying parts of Arabia ranged themselves under the banner of Islam. This was the…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nasr:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thou seest people entering the religion of God in multitudes See 110:1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nasr:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Celebrate then the praise of thy Lord and seek thou His protection (Refer to: 48:2 - Refer to note on 'Istighfar'.) , (for) verily He is Oft-Turning (merciful)! It is indirectly an ordinance for mankind to celebrate God's grace and glory, at each event of success in life and seek His grace through prayer and earn the protection through God's forgiveness of the shortcomings.'Istighfar' in the case of a sinful being, means seeking the pardon of God and the same 'Istighfar' on the part of a sinless infallible one like the Holy Prophet and His Ahl Al-Bayt who have already been purified by the Lord Himself (33:33) will mean seeking further grace and the greater blessings or the further protection of the Lord against the Satanic forces. Here 'Istighfar' means the Holy Prophet's asking for the protection of the Lord…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' men! take shelter in your Lord Who hath created you from a single self (Ar. 'Nafs' – Soul.) and created from it, its pair, and spread from these two, men manifold (Innumerable.) and women, and fear God, in Whose name ye importune one another, and (be mindful') of kinship; Verily God is vigilant over you. When it has to be addressed to the people (mankind) in general, the address has been as 'Ya ayyuha an-nas', i.e., 'O' people! And when the Jews or the Christians or those given the scriptures are meant, the address has been 'Ya ayyuha al-Kitab', i.e., O' people of the Book. And when are meant the Muslims, they have been addressed as 'Ya ayyuha al-Mu'minoon', i.e., 'O' believers'. Here the address is to mankind in general, saying: 'Ya ayyuha an-nas', i.e., 'O' People'. The contents…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who eat away the properties of the orphans unjustly, they swallow (only) fire into their bellies; and anon shall they (Meet – embrace.) enter the blazing Hell-fire. The example given here indicates the grave nature of the crime. It is related by the Holy Prophet that on the Day of Resurrection some people will rise with fire blazing out from their mouths. The crowd witnessing them will ask who are they. The reply to the query will be: 'These are the people who devoured the properties of the orphans' (M.S.)

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:100 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whosoever migrateth in the way of God, findeth in the earth refuge abundant and spacious; and whoever goeth forth from his house migrating unto God and His Apostle (Muhammad), and then (before he reacheth the destination) death overtaketh him, indeed hath become his recompense incumbent upon God; and God is Oft-Forgiving, Merciful. (a) The significance of this and the previous passage has been extended by the Holy Imams, as to mean not only a physical migration from a place to place but to mean the migration of one from the actual sense of the cognitive self to his own ego, i.e., 'I', towards the universal self, through his representative the Holy Prophet or the Imam.(b) This does not mean any material comfort for an immigrant may gain in it or not, it means the detachment from the particular land…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:101 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When ye travel in the earth, it shall be no blame (Sin. Refer to Verse 2:158.) on you if ye shorten the prayers if ye fear that those who disbelieve will cause you distress. Verily, the infidels to you are open enemies. Shortening the prayer means cutting short the Four 'Rakat' prayers viz. Zuhr, Asr and Isha by two rakats. This has to be done when facing an enemy in a battle as well as during travel. It must also be remembered that if anyone, during travel, intentionally offers the full prayer, the prayer is null and void. It is a matter of discipline which must never be molested. In the matter of 'Salaat-ul-Qasr' i.e., Namaz or prayer during travel, the journey must not be less than about 27 miles, nor is the concession available if a man halts at…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:102 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) art among them (when a battle rages) and thou establishest (Lead.) prayer for them, then let a party of them stand up with thee and let them take their arms; then when they have prostrated (Completing one 'Rak'at' (unit) and complete the other 'Rak'at' individually.) (themselves) let them take their position in your rear, and let the other party come up, which hath not prayed, then let them pray with thee, but let them take their precautions and their arms; for, desire those who disbelieve that if ye be negligent of your arms and your baggages, that they may turn upon you all at once; But it shall be no blame on you, if ye be inconvenienced by rain or be ill that ye put away your arms; but take your precaution; Verily God…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:103 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when ye have finished the prayer remember God standing, and sitting, and reclining, and when ye are secure (from danger), establish (As usual.) prayer; Verily Prayer is, (imposed) upon the believers as (a) timed Ordinance. 'Kitaban Mauqoota', i.e., an ordinance to be punctually executed at the prescribed times. This indicates how careful a Muslim has to be about the prescribed communion with the Lord strictly at the regulated times. It speaks of the prescribed prayers being unavoidably compulsory until consciousness lasts in a man or a woman.Some commentators take the expression signifying prayer being obligatory on all times and in all circumstances with different regulations implying the saying of the Holy Prophet.'Prayer is not to be given up under any circumstances.'This is an assurance which demands every believer not to be discouraged in the worst of circumstances. For details…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:104 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And slacken not in pursuit of the (enemy) people; If ye suffer pain, assuredly they also suffer as ye suffer; but ye hope from God what they hope not (This is the assurance which made every believer not to be dejected.) ; And God is All-Knowing and All-Wise. The warning refers to the conduct of the hypocrites at Uhud when they had left the battle field giving a false excuse saying that the enemy would not return to attack again1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:105 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily We have sent down unto thee the Book (The Qur'an) with the Truth that thou mayest judge between people by what God showeth thee (Refer to Verse 4:109. To be always just according to God's decree and not at any individual's opinion.) ; and be not thou a pleader for the treacherous (A Muslim or a non-Muslim.) . Commentators relate that this verse was revealed on the occasion of a dispute between a Muslim tribe and a Jew. Three brothers Busheer, Mubashir and Bashr, sons of Ta'ma of the Ubairaq tribe stole some property from the house of the uncle of Qatada and concealed it in the house of a Jew and when the theft was revealed, they threw the whole blame on the Jew. Notwithstanding the open enmity of the Jews the Holy Prophet gave the verdict against…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:106 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And pray for the Pardon of God (for thy followers), Verily, God is Oft-Forgiving, Merciful (Refer to Verse 2:255.) . In many places when the people are to be enjoined upon about any good deed or to be warned against, the address had been to the Holy Prophet. For instance:The injunction to seek protection of God-addressed to the Holy Prophet is to every Muslim who is to act as a judge. The injunction to seek pardon or the protection of God against the consequences plead on behalf of the unjust ones. And Verse 63:6 clarifies the position once for all declaring it in clear cut words that even if the Holy Prophet with his natural mercifulness prays for any hypocrites or he prays not, never, never will God forgive them. Thus, to imagine about tyrants and the unjust one's ever…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:107 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And plead not on behalf of those who deceive their own selves; Verily God loveth not any who is treacherous, sinful. See 4:106

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:108 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They hide (Their Crimes for shame.) from people but they hide not from God and He is with them when they hold nightly discourses which He is not pleased with; And God doth compass round what all they do. The reference is to the secret consultations that were held by the hypocrites of the tribe of Ubairaq and Asid Ibn Urwah who went to the Holy Prophet pleading for the three culprits hiding their crime.1

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:109 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Behold! ye pleaded for these (The Criminals.) in this worldly life; hut who shall plead (For the Criminals.) with God for them on the Day of Resurrection? or who shall be their defender? People may defend any unjust one or a criminal in this world but on the Day of Judgment they shall have no pleaders on their behalf.Here Qur'an aims at developing an inner preventive force against all individual and social crimes by diverting the attention of man towards God, in all circumstances of shame, fear, hope etc., so that the individual should feel ashamed, be hopeful, be afraid of God and of none eke and be mindful of the eternal pleasure and pain, not that of this transitory life. With this force developed, man is safe from all vices and if this is absent, nothing in the world…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God enjoineth (Regarding inheritance.) you about your issues! the male shall have the equal of the shares of two females and if they be females (only two and) more than two, then they shall have two thirds of that which (the deceased) hath left; but if she be an only daughter, she shall have the half; and the father and the mother of the deceased shall each of them have a sixth part of what he hath left if he hath an issue but if he hath no issue and his parents be his heirs then his mother shall have the third; and if he (The deceased.) hath brethren his mother shall have the sixth, after paying the bequest he shall have bequeathed and his debt; As to your father or your issues, ye know not which of them is…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:110 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whoever doth evil, or wrongeth his own self and thereafter seeketh pardon of God, shall find God Oft-Forgiving, Merciful (This merciful assurance is after the severe warning given above) . The door of pardon is always open for those who commit sins affecting their own self, i.e., not affecting the interest of the others.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:111 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whoever comitteth a sin (Refer to Verses 4:109; 4:110.) , verily, he committeth it against his own self; And God is All Knowing, All-Wise. Everyone, man or woman, is personally responsible for his or her sins and none else shall bear the burden of the others.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:112 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whoever committeth a fault or a sin and throweth it on one innocent he indeed burdeneth (himself) with the calumny and a manifest sin. False accusation against any innocent person is calumny and is a declared punishable sin.This is the unique and an exclusive characteristic of Islam. No other religion lays so much stress upon an unbiased and strict administration of justice.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:113 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Had it not been God's grace upon thee and His mercy, a party among them had certainly resolved to lead thee astray; but they shall not (Refer to Verses 53:2; 95:7.) lead thee astray but their own selves, and they shall, not harm thee of aught; and God hath sent down unto thee the Book (The Qur'an.) and Wisdom, and hath taught thee what thou didst not know; and God's grace on thee is very great (Infinite.) . The reference about a group trying to mislead the Holy Prophet is to Asid-Ibn Urwah's pleading on behalf of the culprits1.In Verse 93:7 the conjunctive 'fa' there is no interval or lapse of time between God's finding and guiding and there is no interval or lapse of time in His giving existence to a being and Himself finding it. Hence the guidance…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:114 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: There is nothing good in most of their whisperings (Secret talk.) except (in his) who bideth charity or goodness or peace among the people; And whoever doth this seeking the pleasure of God, anon We will give him a great recompense. The reference here is also to the event mentioned in the note on Verse 4:105. The Holy Prophet was in fact, conversant with the conduct and the character of the people he was surrounded with.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:115 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whosoever opposeth (get hostile.) the Apostle (Muhammad) after that guidance hath been manifest to him and followeth a way other than that of the believers, We will turn him to that to which he hath (himself) turned and will cast him into Hell; and Oh! what a bad destination it is (Refer to Verses 8:13, 33:57.) ! The return or the punishment for acting hostilely against the Holy Prophet and following a path other than that of the believer, is clearly given in this verse.Acting hostilely against the Holy Prophet does not restrict the conduct to the life-time of the Holy Prophet. The hostility against the Holy Prophet means acting in any manner which displeases him. The question arises whether the Holy Prophet would have been pleased at the brutal conduct of the tyrants who teased, tortured and massacred…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:116 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily God forgiveth not that (anything) be associated with Him, and forgiveth anything besides this to whomsoever He pleaseth; and whoso associated! (aught) with God, hath indeed strayed far, far away (from the right path) (Refer to Verse 4:48.) . Polytheism or associating anybody or anything with God, i.e., 'Shirk' is unpardonable1. It is not because polytheism in any way effects the Glory of God, but because it Jowers the dignity of the human nature. It is such an impossibility that it can never be entertained without stultifying reason and thus, rendering man inherently incapable of any spiritual progress. Thus, a polytheist can never hope to rise to the heavenly bliss.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:117 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They (The Pagans) invoke not besides Him but the female deities (the Idols) and they invoke not but Satan the persistent rebel (void of all good). 'Inas' refers to the idols, inanimate objects like trees, stones, wood etc. The infidels named their idol deities as females for they held them as the daughters of their god. For instance, 'Lat' 'Uzza' and 'Manat.' Every Arabian tribe had an idol as its own favourite deity, and they called it 'Inas' the female.Since Satan was the misleading force, the infidelity is referred to him.The reference is to what was prevailing among the ancient pagans in Arabia and elsewhere to present their deities and the angels mostly as females or to invoke the devilish forces. The idolaters used to hold the idols as the daughters of God and the extent that the term female…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:118 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whom God hath cursed him and he (the Satan) said "Most certainly will I take of Thy bondsmen an allotted share." Satan being cursed by God, gets all the more resolved to exert his most to mislead mankind and take them to perdition. The share appointed for him is in the nature of things, nature of man and the forces around him.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:119 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And assuredly will I lead them astray and certainly stir (vain) desires in them, and certainly bid them that they slit the ears of cattle, and will I certainly command them that they shall change (the faces) of God's creation;" And whoever taketh Satan as a guardian besides God, indeed suffereth he a manifest loss (Refer to Verse 5:108.) . The heathen Arabs used to slit the ears of a she camel and had exempted it from being used or slaughtered, i.e., devoted to their idol gods. It was a prevalent form of polytheism in Arabia.The animal, be it a she-camel or a goat was called 'Bahira' viz., she camel having her ear slit-there is a mention of this in Verse 5:103.Changing of God's creation means using of God's created things for an object other than that for which they…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For you, shall be half of what leave your wives if they have no issue, but if they have an issue, then for you shall be a fourth of what they leave after paying the bequest they had bequeathed and the debt; And for them (Wives.) shall be a fourth of what ye leave if ye have no issue, and if ye have an issue then for them (shall be) the eighth of what ye leave after paying the bequest ye had bequeathed and the debt (Ye incurred.) ; and if a man or woman leaveth (his property) to be inherited by (not the lineage (His parents or his issues.) but) any side relation (Ar. 'Kalalah see Verse 4:176.) and he (The deceased.) or she (The deceased.) hath a brother or a sister each of these two shall have the…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:120 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He (Satan) giveth them (false) promises and (he) stirreth (vain) desires in them; but Satan promiseth not (aught) but (it is sheer) deception. See 4:119

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:121 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These, (Satan's dupes), their abode shall be Hell, and they shall not find from it any escape. See 4:119

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:122 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But they who believe and do righteous deeds, shortly We will admit them into gardens 'neath which flow rivers, for ever shall they abide therein; (It is) a promise of God. (It is) true indeed; And who can be more true than God in utterance. See 4:119

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:123 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It shall) not be according to your desires nor the desires of the people of the Book; (but) whoever doeth evil shall be recompensed for it, nor will he find for himself, besides God, any guardian or a helper. Islam is the religion of nature. Every action must have its re-action. According to the law of nature evil and good shall have their respective return. Islam always warns man and woman, to be always mindful of the natural consequences of Vice and Virtue. Muslims are warned against imagining themselves as the favourites of God, as do the Christians and the lews.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:124 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whoso doeth deeds of righteousness, whether male or female, and be a believer, then these shall enter Heaven and they shall not be wronged (even) to the husk of a date-stone. This verse clearly says that in the rewarding of good and the punishing of any evil, there shall not be any distinction between man and woman.There is one factor notable in this Verse-doing of good deeds need true belief, to be accepted.Good deeds are acceptable only from those who believe and not from the disbelievers.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:125 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And who is better in religion than he who resigneth himself (His Cognitive self.) entirely unto God? and is righteous, and followeth the creed (Milla al-Ebrahim' is repeatedly used in Qur'an indicates the Universality of his mission - while the mission of Moses and Jesus was circumstantial) of Abraham, the Upright One, And God took Abraham for a Friend (Refer to Verses 2:112, 3:18, 3:84.) . The best religion is submission to God - (i.e., Islam.)'Hanif', i.e., wholly devoted to one object-attached exclusively to the Right Path-always avoiding the wrong one.'Vajh', literally face. In Qur'an mostly used, signifying the distinctive aspects of a being by which the being is recognised-Man is distinguished by his cognitive self-God is distinguished by His Absolute Universal Excellence which is manifest throughout 2:112. (A.P.)'Millat lbrahim' repeatedly used in Qur'an indicating the universality of his mission…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:126 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: To God belongeth whatever is in the heavens and all that is in the earth; and God encompasseth all things. The ownership of the universe belongs to none but God. Hence there can never be any other owner or the master for man to worship, besides the One and the only God Lord of everything in the heavens and the earth.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:127 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They ask thee for a decision (Fatwa.) about women Say! (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "God doth decision for you about them; and that which is recited unto you in the book concerning orphan girls, whom ye give not what is assigned (Their right to inheritance and the freedom of choice given to them by the law Refer to Verse 4:3.) to them, while (yet) ye desire to wed them, and also (concerning) the Weak among the children, that (God's decision.) ye stand firm tor the orphans, with justice; and whatever of good ye do. Verily God knoweth it." The right of women referred to here are those mentioned in Verse 4:3 at the commencement of this chapter.'Yateeman-nisa' means the girl orphans. There is a reference about the dealings with orphans in Verses 2:220; 4:2; and 90:15.No religion other than Islam…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:128 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if a woman feareth ill-treatment desertion (Ar. 'Nushooz' Refer to Verse 4:34.) from her husband, then shall it be no fault on the twain if they effect compromise (peace) between them two amicably; for compromise (peace) is good; and Avarice (Self-interest always influences man and woman which is the root of all disputes.) is made to be present in (people's) minds; and if ye do good and guard yourselves (against evil (Ar. 'Shoh' Avarice.) ), then verily God is All-Aware of what ye do. When Khuwailad, Salma-Ibn Nafe's wife, got old, Salma wanted to divorce her and marry another woman. Khuwailad told her husband that he may marry another woman but not to divorce her and she would forego her turn, and he may have it whenever he pleased. But Salma did not agree. Khuwailad reported herself to the…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:129 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ye will never be able to do justice (Equity in Love. Refer to Verse 4:3.) between women, (wives), even though ye may covet (Justice.) (it), so incline not with a total inclination (to one) so that ye leave her as it were in suspense; and if ye effect a reconciliation and guard yourselves (against) (evil), Verily, then, God is Oft-Forgiving, Merciful. Justice between the wives means equal treatment to every one of them as regards feeding, clothing and giving them the other conjugal rights that not one of them should have the least grievance of partiality. If one night is spent with one wife the other night must be spent with the other, by regular turns. Verse 4:3. If such a perfect equity is not practicable, then the husband should at least be mindful not to be totally inclined towards…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These are the limits set by God; and whoso obeyeth God and His Apostle (Muhammad), him will God admit into gardens beneath which flow rivers to abide therein for ever; and this is a Great Achievement. These two verses give out the reward for abiding by the laws as well as the punishment for transgressing them.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:130 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they separate, God will render (e)each free from want out of His abundance; and God is Omniscient, Wise. Note the highly consoling promise of God's grace and bounty to the parties separated justly, with goodness and piety.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:131 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God's is whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth; and indeed We enjoined (Ar. 'Wassaina', instructed.) those who were given the Book before you, and unto you (too) that ye should take shelter in God; and if ye disbelieve, then, verily, God's is whatever is m the heavens and whatever is in the earth; God is Self-Sufficient, Praise-worthy. Piety is once again repeated in this verse as the object of the human life on earth.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:132 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God's is whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth; and God is sufficient as a Protector. Here Qur'an has repeated the Absolute Sovereignty of God over the entire universe to emphasise that man in his individual domestic, social and personal attitude, should have in mind that he is not free to decide as he likes, disregarding the fact that he is only subservient and a part of the whole which is administered by the Absolute who needs nothing and everything is sustained by Him. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:133 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If He pleaseth, He can cause you pass away, O' people! and bring others (in your stead); and for this God hath power. Note the warning against being totally wiped out of existence and being substituted with some other people, faithful and obedient to the Lord. This warning clearly indicates that a nation will Ire allowed by God to exist until it is not totally rebellious and disobedient. Many rebellious people Viz. the 'Ad' & 'Thamad' had met such a fate1.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:134 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whoever desireth the reward of this world, then with God is the reward of this world and the hereafter; and God is All-Hearing and All-Seeing. See 4:133

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:135 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! do stand (Maintain Justice.) firmly with justice, Witnesses for God's sake, though it be against your own selves or your parents or your kindred, be he rich or poor, for God is closer (Ar. 'Aula' in all respects in ancestry and affection.) (than you) to them both; Therefore follow not your inclination (Ar- 'Hawa' desire.) , lest ye deviate, (from the truth) and if ye swerve (Twist the argument.) (from the truth) or turn aside, then Verily God is All-A ware of what ye do (Refer to Verse 34:46.) . There shall not be any partiality expecting in favour from the rich or fearing any harm from them, nor a witness be given for any undue compassion to anyone. Neither the ties of blood or of love, nor the consideration of any fear or favour or…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:136 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! Believe in God, and His Apostle (The Holy Prophet.) and the Book which He hath sent down unto His Apostle (Muhammad) and the Book which He hath sent down before (him); and whoever denieth God, and His Angels, and His Books, and His Apostles and the Last Day (of judgment) hath indeed strayed off, far away (from the right path). The address in this Verse is to the believers, to believe in God, His Apostles, His Books.It clearly indicates that a mere hereditary belief will not be of any avail to anyone. One should earn the correct belief for one's own self by a careful study, with compare and contrast. This Verse invites every man and woman to know the truth by himself or herself for his or her own salvation. This is a clear warning…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:137 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who believed and thereafter disbelieved (Refer to Verses 3:89; 3:90.) , again believed, and again disbelieved, thereafter increased they in disbelief, It is not for God to pardon them, nor will He guide them to the (right) way. The reference here is to the people who first believed in Moses and then disbelieved in him and worshipped the Calf and then again believed in Uzair and again returned to disbelief and they believed in the Holy Prophet and then disbelieved in him and their disbelief was continuous and on the increase. Ibn e-Abbas says that every hypocrite who lived in the time of the Holy Prophet, in land or on sea, comes under this and this statement is proved to be true by the immediately succeeding Verse which relates about punishment to the hypocrites. (M.S.)Refers to the hypocrites…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:138 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Announce (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) to the hypocrites that for them there shall be a painful torment. 'Basharat' is generally used for announcement or giving of a glad tiding, a news which produces joy in those whom it is meant for. But it is also used ironically while announcing a punishment to a people who arc persistently on the wrong path and yet hold themselves to be on the right one.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:139 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who take the disbelievers for (their) friends (Helpers.) rather than believers; Do they seek honour from them? Then, Verily, All honour (as a whole) belongeth (only) to God. It is a warning against seeking protection of the disbelievers instead of that of the believers (the Muslims) while every believer should know that glory, grace and triumph belongs to none but God. Believers in God should always be with God and depend upon none but on Him-and seek everything from Him. Every Muslim has to declare his faith in this fact every day through the prescribed daily prayers (Salat, i.e., Namaz), through the opening chapter of the Holy Qur'an saying:"To Thee alone do me worship (serve) and of Thee only do we seek (every) help". (1:4)

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whoso disobeyeth God and His Apostle (Muhammad) and transgresseth His limits, him shall God admit in Hell-fire, to abide therein and for him shall be a shameful torment. See 4:13

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:140 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed hath He sent down unto you (O' Believers!) in the Book (The Holy Qur'an.) (Qur'an) that when ye hear the signs of God disbelieved in, and mocked at, then sit ye not with them until they enter into some other discourse, otherwise, ye would become like them; Verily, God will gather the hypocrites and the infidels in Hell all together. In Verse 6:68, also it has been enjoined upon the believers to leave the assembly where truth is mocked at. Some Christian critics draw a peculiar inference from this injunction and say that the Muslims have been asked by their faith to shun criticism. Any intelligent one would only ridicule at such an inference for it needs nothing more than common sense to differentiate between ridicule or mockery and criticism.This is applicable to anyone who associates himself with…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:141 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who (keep) watch upon you; then if there be for you a victory from God say they "Are we not with you?" and if the infidels have a share (in the victory), say they "Did we not acquire mastery over you and defend you from the believers?" Therefore God shall judge between you on the Dry of Resurrection; And never will God make for the infidels a way (to triumph) against the believers. The reference here is to the hypocrites who always joined the triumphant side to have their share in the gains.The last portion of the verse has been incorporated as a principal legislation governing all social, political, economic, rules and regulations restricting their validities to (non-Muslims) to the extent not giving chance of the superiority to the disbelievers over the believers (the Muslims). (A.P.)In the concluding words…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:142 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the hypocrites strive to deceive God while He is deceiving them; and when they stand up for prayer, they stand up sluggishly (without earnestness) they do it only to be seen of men, and they remember not God save a little. For a similar warning see 2:9.It is obvious that none with common sense will think of deceiving God. It means the attempt to deceive the believers-believers standing for God. Similarly, God is above the evil of deceiving anyone. His giving the disbelievers and the hypocrites and not exposing them which results in their fall, is termed as God's deceiving them. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:143 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Wavering between that (and this); Neither towards these (believers) nor towards those (infidels); And whoever God leaveth to go astray, never then shall thou find for him a way. Wavering between truth and falsehood, faith and disbelief.Refers to the psychological state of some of the new converts who had embraced Islam fascinated by the force of the new faith and not yet freed from their traditional traits. 'Ali was the only one whose cognitive self 'Wajh' was honoured by God, in not turning to anything save to Him. Which fact the Muslim world even to this day acknowledges by titling him as 'Karrama Allaho Wajhaho', i.e., He whose cognitive-self God has honoured, whereas all the others the Muslims wish them as 'Radhi Allaho Ta'ala' i.e., May God be pleased with him. The same condition is true of those whose minds…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:144 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! take not the disbelievers for friends rather than the believers; Desire ye to furnish unto God against yourselves a manifest authority (proof) (to punish you)? See Verse 4:139.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:145 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the hypocrites shall be in the lowest stage of the (Hell) fire, and never shalt thou find for them a helper. The hypocrites are the hidden enemies of the faith and the Holy Prophet. A hidden enemy is worse than an open enemy. Hence the hypocrites shall have the worst punishment.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:146 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Except those who repent, and Amend (themselves) and hold fast to God and purify their religion (Faith in practice - Submit purely, sincerely.) (wholly) for God, these then shall be with the (true) believers; and anon will God give the believers a great reward. The condition of repentance being accepted, is laid in clearcut words that the repentant should amend their conduct and character and must sincerely hold fast to God with purest faith and devotion. Mere verbal declaration is of no avail. Holding fast to God is not possible without a 'Wasila' or a medium mentioned in 5:35.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:147 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What hath God to do to torment you, if ye be grateful and ye believe? While God is the (greatest) Appreciator (of worth) and the All-Knowing. 'Shakir' literally means one who gives thanks for any good done to him.But when this quality is attributed to God it means one who recognise: and appreciates goodness and rewards it in multiple degrees more than the act increasing it in His estimation.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:148 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Loveth not God, open utterance of evil (Hurtful.) in speech except by one who hath been wronged; And God is the Hearer, the Knower. Islam strictly forbids every kind of defamation either by speech or in action. But open defamatory speech by an aggressed one against the aggressor is a natural expression of the aggressed's feelings of pain for the injury suffered by the individual. Islam being a natural and a practical religion tolerates such exposition of the human feelings in an open utterance. Thus, the cursing of a tyrant by those who feel for the tyranny has been exempted. The devoted Muslims who identify themselves with the Holy Prophet and his Holy Ahl Al-Bayt naturally feel for their sufferings and openly invoke the curse of God upon the tyrants. Such an open cursing is alluded under this verse. It…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:149 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If ye do good openly or conceal (Unobserved) it, or pardon an evil, then Verily, God is Pardoning, Powerful. See 4:148

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And as to such of those who are guilty of lewdness (Ar. 'Fahishatun' adultery.) from among your women, then bring four witnesses against them from among yourselves; and if they bear witness (to the fact), Confine them to the houses till death taketh them away or God maketh some way (or by the punishment prescribed later.) for them. This Verse was revealed to correct a practice prevalent among the early Arabs. They used to confine their women in their houses-for life-whenever they found them guilty of adultery. The Verse says that they may do so, but they should not do it on their own allegations unless their guilt is duly proved by witnesses of four men. Failing this they can divorce their wives if they please, and can take no further action against them."Or God opens some way for them."…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:150 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily those who deny God and His apostles and desire that they differentiate (About the authority of. Refer to Verse 152) between God and His apostles and say, "We believe in some and we deny some", intend they to take between (this and) that a (midway). Distinguishing between God and His apostles means believing in God and not believing in any one of His apostles. The Jews believed in Moses and disbelieved in Jesus. The Christians believed in Jesus and disbelieved in the other apostles of God. The Jews and the Christians believe in Moses and Jesus but disbelieve in the Holy Prophet. Islam demands belief in God and in all the apostles of God. Disbelief in any one of God's apostles, takes the individual out of the fold or the category of believers and places him among the disbelievers.…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:151 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These are they the infidels truly, and We have prepared for the infidels a disgraceful torment. See 4:150

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:152 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they who believe in God and His apostles and differentiate not between anyone of them, they, (are those whom) He will grant them their recompense; And God is Oft-Forgiving, Merciful. It is noteworthy for every student of comparative study of religions that Islam and no other religion demands its adherents to believe in all the apostles of God without any distinction about their being Truthful and being from God.(Differentiate) See also the subsequent: verse. Qur'an asserts a complete representative status of every apostle during his mission to the people to whom they had been sent. Any attempt to differentiate between the authority of God and the prophets, and between the prophets with regard to the representative status of each one of them within the prescribed and the declared limits of time and place, is infidelity.The attempt of some schools…

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:153 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The people of the Book ask thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) to get descended upon them a book from heaven; so indeed they had demanded of Moses (a) greater (thing) than that, for they said "Show us God manifestly" whereupon seized them a rumbling for their wickedness; Then they took a calf (for a god) even after what clear signs had come unto them, but (even then) We pardoned them (for) this; and We gave Moses a clear authority. See 4:152

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:154 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We lifted up the Mountain over them at their covenant and said We unto them "Enter the door prostrating" and said We unto them "Exceed not (Our limits) in the Sabath (Some may argue about the importance of the 'Sabath' while days are God's. The answer is the same as would be given about the importance attached to the 'Qiblah' while in all directions is God's - It is only a Test.) (day)" and We took from them a firm Covenant. See 4:152

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:155 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So for their breaking their covenant and their denial of the signs of God, and their slaying the apostles unjustly and their saying "Our hearts are covered;" Nay! God hath set a seal upon them for their disbelief, so they believe not but a little (A very few.) . See 4:152

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:156 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And for their disbelief and for their utterance against Mary a grievous calumny. The calumny referred to here is the Jewish accusation of Mary, of fornication. According to 'the Jewish Life of Jesus' the man about whom the Jews accused Mary, was a Jew named Panther.

item.title: bil-Quran: An-Nisaa:157 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
