item.description: And on that Day shall not be asked (None need say or testify for the very bodies of the men and the jinn will say out every thing.) man nor jinn of his sin (Refer to Verses 24:24; 36:65.) The deeds good and bad, of every individual will be so much self-proved, that there would not be any necessity of asking anyone, whether he accepts the report about his conduct and character or not, nor would the convicts be asked for any explanation as to why he did it. Every case will be self-proved and the ultimate state of every individual self-evident. The very organs of the body of every individual would bear witness1.It indicates that this does not refer to the Final Resurrection, but to a different stage of the resurrection other than referred to in verse 7:6 -…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Rahmaan:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He taught him expression (The power of speech and expression. Refer to Verses 2:31; 3:138.) 'Biyan', i.e., the means of expressing one's mind - 'Biyan' has also been used for the Holy Qur'an1.Taking the word for the art of verbal expression of the ideas, the Holy Qur'an which is the only record of what spoke out the Holy Prophet, is such a wonderful verbal expression which, in spite of its open challenge2, the world would never till now produce an equal even to the smallest chapter of it. It is further said that even if mankind as a whole and jinns joining with them, try to produce an equal to the Holy Qur'an they shall never be able to do it at all3.As regards the daily discourses, the utterance of the Holy Prophet was suspected by the disbelievers as a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Rahmaan:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The sun and the moon follow the (prescribed) timings (Refer to Verses 13:2; 21:33; 36:38.) The astronomical constitution of the universe is bound by such strict, universal and fixed mathematical laws and calculations and are continuously going on with its work, in such an unchanging manner, that men could depend upon the knowledge of the heavenly bodies without any fear of any change or alteration in the original laws.This verse refers to two of the major heavenly bodies, the sun and the moon, following the computed courses in the prescribed order. This announcement of the natural phenomenon active in the heavens, was made at a time when the world was indulged only in mere conjectures about the astronomical world1.

item.description: In both of them are two fountains flowing The Two Springs are called 'Tasneem' and 'Salsaheel' They could be of clean, clear and refreshing waters and of the delicious and pleasing drinks. The dual springs, here also, as in the case of the gardens might mean variety.

Ibn Abbas says there shall be no fruit of this world the like of which would not be in the heavens, besides there would be such other delicious fruits which would neither have had been seen nor tasted before.All sorts of fruits in pairs, corresponding to various aspects of true faith and good deeds. (A.P.)

item.description: And the herbs and the trees do obeisance (unto Him) (Refer to Verses 13:4; 16:48; 16:49; 22:18.) Prostration here means submitting to the law of the Lord, i.e., serving them - never going against their respective native endowments. It is in this sense that all nature adores God, its Creator Lord1.Everything in the heavens and in the earth adores God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Rahmaan:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is the recompense for good aught but good? (Refer to Verses 99:7; 99:8.) Note the simplest, shortest and the best expression given to the phenomenon of equity:The return for service to God, increase in the status.The thanksgiving, further increases the grant of the bounties.The piety brings enjoyment.The repentance earns forgiveness.The Holy Prophet said that he who declared God's unity saying: 'La ilaha illa Allah', shall have Paradise. The Holy Prophet said: "If you do any goodness in return for any goodness already done then the one who did it first shall he entitled to a greater reward for the good was one not in return, and if you want your goodness to earn a greater reward, then do more than the goodness what has been done to you."As there is a sure reward for every goodness1, every evil will also…

item.description: And besides these (two) are two other gardens Heavens (Paradise), will not be of any one single fixed nature or kind. There will be gardens or the places of eternal bliss of various kinds and degrees, even the sight of which would be giving pleasure and amusement - These places would be the environment of the blissful abode granted to the pious.Abu Basir asked the Sixth Holy Imam, Ja'far Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq: "Master! would the believer-pious wife of a believer-pious man be the wife of the man also in the heaven?" The Holy Imam replied, "O' Abu-Muhammad! God is All-Just, if the husband be of a greater faith and piety than his wife, he will have the choice of having his wife as his mate and if the wife be greater than her husband in faith and piety, she will…

item.description: And the heaven, He did raise it high, and placed the scale (within reach) (Refer to Verses 42:17; 52:25.) The perfect man as the microcosm is the infallible scale with which the truth of the Universe and the right and wrong, of human action should be measured and viewing the Holy Prophet as such Abu Talib says: 'The Scale of Truth which defaults not even Io an atom - and weigher of the justice his weighing falleth not short' (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Rahmaan:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In them are virtuous women, beautiful ones (Refer to Verses 44:54; 52:20; 55:66; 55:72; 56:22.) Since God asks to which of His bounties or grace man can deny, it is desirable that the reciter of this Sura, whenever he recites the questioning clause, says 'La bi shayin min alayka Rabbi na kazzib', i.e., nothing of any of Thy bounties "O' Our Lord! do we deny?"1

item.description: Alif, Lam, Mim (A. L. M.) See 30:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then evil was the end of those who wrought evil, for belied they the signs of God, and at them they used to mock. This is a strong warning to the sinners that it may result in the total disbelief in God and the denial of the truth. The same passage was quoted by Zaynab, Husayn's sister, in the court of Yazid son of Muawiyah when she was brought as a captive, in answer to Yazid's reciting the verses of Abdullah ibn al-Ziba'ra meaning:Played Hashemites with the kingdom as otherwise neither came any news nor did descend any revelation from heaven. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God (it is Who) originateth the creation, then causeth it to return again, then unto Him shall ye all be returned. As already pointed out, this verse and the verses of the similar tone, confirm the fact that everything returns to the point from where its existence commenced - and it has been passed into a proverb. 'Everything returns to its origin' - and this has been attested by the NT1. This shows that the process of creation though evolutionary, yet it is circular. See introduction. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on the day when shall come the Hour (of judgment), in despair shall be the guilty (ones) See 30:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And there shall not be for them any intercessors from among their (The false deities they associated with God, and worshipped.) partner gods, and they shall be the deniers of their partners. (The false deities they associated with God, and worshipped.) The false deities they associated with God - whom they worshipped as gods, instead of God. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the day when arriveth the Hour (of Judgment), on that day shall (they) be separated (Sorted.) from one another. Here and elsewhere the Resurrection Day is presented as the day when people will be separated and in other verses 11:103, 64:9, the day is said to be a day of gathering together. It is clear from the verses that there is no contradiction between the two statements as the reference is to two different aspects of the Resurrection. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And as to those who believed and did good deeds, they shall be in the garden, made happy. See 30:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And as to those who disbelieved and belied Our signs and the meeting of the hereafter, these shall be brought over to the chastisement. See 30:14

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So glory (Glorify God with prayers to Him.) be to God when ye enter the evening and when ye enter the morning. The praise to God referred to here, stands for the prescribed five times daily prayers:Tumsun: Evening, i.e., the evening and night prayers, i.e., Maghrib and Isha.Tusbihun: Morning, i.e., for the morning prayers - Fajr.Ashiyyan: Afternoon, i.e., for the afternoon prayer - Asr.Tuzhirun: Mid-day, for the Noon prayer - Zuhr.Asserting all these changes are the manifestations of His glory. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And His (alone) is all praise in the heavens and the earth, at the sun's decline and when ye enter the noon. See 30:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He bringeth forth the living from the dead and bringeth forth dead from the living, and giveth life to the earth after its death, and thus shall ye (too) be brought forth (after ye are dead). Nothing in this world has been a perpetual existence. The process of extinction and revival is a mysterious purposeful working of nature. The creative process is in its constant course and the cycle of appearance and the disappearance of the things in this world is continuously at its work. The Seventh Holy Imam Musa ibn Jafer al-Kadhim said that by a 'being' given life after its death, means God sending His chosen men to enliven the hearts of men by His guidance to the right way to the life eternal. The concluding words of this verse'Thus ye shall be brought forth' (30:19)gives the assurance…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Romans have been defeated, (By the Persians.) In 614-616 A.D. the Romans under Heraclius were defeated by the Persians and the Roman Empire lost many of its territories. The pagans of Mecca rejoiced at the defeat of the Romans who were Christians, i.e., the people of the Book. The Muslims were grieved at the defeat of the Romans because Persians, the victors, were only fire-worshippers.1 The pagans of Mecca began taunting the Muslims saying that the fate of the Muslims would also be the same for they deemed it as an omen of their triumph upon the Muslims.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of His signs is that He created you from dust, then lo I ye are human beings scattering (in the world). See 30:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves, mates that ye may dwell (inclined) unto them, and caused between you love and compassion: Verily in this are signs for a people who reflect. The wonderful love between (man and woman), i.e., (husband and wife) is the grace of God.1This is the fundamental object of the alliance between the couples - of the same origin, and love and compassion is the only means to achieve that aim. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the variety of your languages and your complexions; verily in this are signs for the learned (who can ponder on matters serious.) (ones). Refers to the development of the various languages and clauses which are of the most complicated subjects of the human strides. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of His signs is your sleeping by night and day and your seeking of His grace; verily in this are signs for a people who would (who interestedly listen.) hear. See 30:22

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of His signs is that He sheweth you the lightning causing awe and hope, and sendeth down from the heavens water and giveth life with it to the earth after its death; verily in this are signs for a people who (who have the intelligence with the insight to understand things beyond the apparent or the immediate.) understand. See 30:22

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of His signs is that the heavens and the earth stand firm by His command; then (after your death) when He summoneth you with a (single) summons from out of the earth, lo! ye come (Resurrected.) forth It refers to the fact that the cohesive force holding the dimensional realms cannot be but the non-material one, which cannot be explained in any term but as His will. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And His is whosoever is in the heavens and the earth: all are subservient unto Him. See 30:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He it is Who originateth the creation, then causeth it to return again, and to Him it is most easy; His are the most exalted similitudes (The attributes beyond our imagination.) in the heavens and the earth; and He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise. See 30:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He setteth forth unto you a parable of yourselves. Have ye of those whom your right hands possess partners in what We have provided you for sustenance, so that in regard to it, ye are alike, Fear ye them as ye fear each other? Thus We make clear Our signs for a people who understand. It compares all the physical and spiritual forces dominating and working in the system of the Universe as the activities of a slave, i.e., one whose power and actions are subservient and subordinate to the will of the master. Therefore, none should give them the similar status which is given to the master himself. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! those who are unjust follow their vain desires without any knowledge: Who can guide him whom God hath allowed to err? There shall not be for them any of the helpers. See 30:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In a nearer land, (Near East.) but they after being defeated will soon be victorious, To console the grieved Muslims this verse was revealed prophesying the triumph of the Romans upon the Persians within a short period which is interpreted as seven to nine years, meaning that the enemies of Islam, i.e., the pagans of Mecca who rejoiced at the defeat of the Romans, would very soon be disillusioned both about the fate of the fire-worshippers of Persia and their own fate against the Muslims. The prophecy of the Holy Qur'an was fulfilled, i.e., in 624 A.D., Heraclius defeated Persia and at Badr (2 A.H.) the heathens of Mecca were beaten by the Muslims and this served also as a proof of the Holy Qur'an being the revealed Word of God.The Fifth Holy Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir said that…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then set thou thy face uprightly (The nature on which God made man.) for (the right) religion, in natural devotion to the truth (following) the nature caused by God in which He hath made the people; No change can there be (by any one else) in the creation of God; This (uprightness) is the established (See verse 9:36.) religion; but most people know not, Religion here stands for Islam, i.e., to be steadfast on Islam is to be ever submitting to God's will by living according to His law 'Shariah.'It is a death blow to the doctrine of Original Sin - in support of this, is the well-known saying of the Holy Prophet: "Every child is born on nature and it is his parents that make him a Jew, or Christian or a Majus."1 Thus the Jewish and the Christian…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Turning unto Him and fear His wrath and establish prayer and be not of the polytheists, See 30:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Of those who split up their religion, and have become sects, every party rejoiceth in what is with them. The groups who rejoice here in this life, will be cursing each other at the end.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when afflicteth the people any harm call they upon their Lord turning unto Him, then when He causeth them taste of mercy from unto Him, lo! some of them associate partners with their Lord, See 30:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Let them be ungrateful for what We have given them; But enjoy ye (only for a while) for soon shall ye (the consequence or the end.) know. See 30:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or, have We sent down upon them any authority that it speaketh of what they associate with Him? See 30:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when We make people taste of mercy they rejoice in it, and if befalleth them an evil for what have already wrought their (own) hands, lo! they are in despair. See 30:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! See they not that God amplifieth the provision for whomsoever He willeth and straiteneth? (For whomsoever He willeth.) Verily in this are signs for a people who believe. See 30:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then give thou to the near of kin his due, and to the needy, and the wayfarer; this is best for those who desire the pleasure of God, and these it is who are the successful ones. It is noteworthy that how could the Holy Prophet have ever ignored this definite ordinance about his own duty in this regard, to his issues and relatives. When this verse was revealed, the Holy Prophet called his daughter Lady Fatima and conveyed to her the right over the possession of the garden of Fadak which was confiscated immediately as the Holy Prophet departed from this world. (See the note on this)1.This payment to the nearest relatives of the Holy Prophet and to one's own relatives of their dues have been presented here as a good deed for those who seek the pleasure of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what ye give out at interest, (Your money.) so that it (Simple or Compound.) may increase in the wealth of the people, but it increaseth (In the view of God.) not with God, and whatever ye give in charity desiring the pleasure of God, it is these that shall get (Grow.) manifold. 'Riba' is usury - Lending money on a condition to be repaid with an increase in the amount lent and collecting such an increase is forbidden. One has to show his active love and practical sympathy to his fellow being, by lending the monetary help which he needs, without any condition of exploiting the miserable position of the individual. Profiteering at the expense of others is forbidden. The reward from God for such a selfless service will be manifold - multiplied many times the amount lent.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Within a (Ar. 'Bidh'i' i.e. a short period from 3 to 9 years 614 A.D. - to 622 A.D.) few years; God's is the authority before and after; and on that day the believers shall rejoice, See 30:3

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God is He who created you then provided you with sustenance, then He causeth you to die, then bringeth you to life; Is there any of your associate gods who doeth aught of these things? Glory be to Him, and Exalted High is He far above what they associate (with Him). See 30:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Mischief hath appeared in the land and the sea on account of what the hands of men have wrought, that He may make them taste a part of what they have done, so that they may turn (away from evil). The corruption which ruled the various parts of the earth prior to the advent of Islam, is a matter of history, Hinduism, Budhism, Judaism, Christianity and Zoroastrianism had lost their hold upon their votaries. Vices of all kinds were freely practised in the name of religious orders of the ages. Since Jesus, six centuries had passed away without any heavenly guidance. Christianity, though the most modern and the youngest of the religions had sunk deep in idolatry and pagan practices.The holy Prophet Jesus was deified and the saints among his believers, were worshipped. Islam came with the torch of knowledge…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Travel ye in the earth, then see ye how was the end of those who were before (you); most of them were polytheists." The world had become polytheist. How even Christianity had lost the doctrine of the Divine Unity preached by Jesus and was lost in the belief in the fanciful trinity, is a fact too obvious and well-known to be repeated here.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then set thy face upright unto the established religion ere cometh from God the day, (Death or Resurrection for the Final Judgment.) there is no averting for it, on that day they shall be separated. See 30:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whoever disbelieveth. on Him shall be (the charge of) the disbelief, and whoever doeth good deeds, for their own self they are preparing, See 30:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So that He may recompense those who believe and do good out of His Grace; Verily He loveth not the disbelievers. See 30:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of His signs is that He sendeth forth the winds bearing good tidings, and that He may make you taste of His mercy, and that ships may sail by His Command, and that ye should seek of His grace, and that ye be grateful. See 30:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed sent We before thee apostles unto their people, and came they unto them with clear proofs, then took We vengeance upon those who were guilty; and was incumbent on Us the succour of the believers. See 30:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God it is Who sendeth forth the winds, so raise they the clouds, then He spreadeth it forth in the skies as He willeth, and causeth it to break up so that ye see the rays coming forth from inside it; and when He causeth it to fall upon whomsoever He pleaseth of His servants, lo! they rejoice. See 30:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Even they who, before it was sent down upon them, were in mute despair. See 30:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: With the aid of God; Aideth He whomsoever He willeth; And He is the All-Mighty, the All-Merciful, See 30:3

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Look then at the traces (The phenomenon of the Divine mercy.) of God's mercy, how He giveth life to the earth after its death; verily He (This same God.) is the giver of life to the dead; and He hath power over all things. See 30:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if We send a wind (from which) they see (their tilth turned) yellow, they become, thereafter, disbelievers (ungrateful). See 30:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For verily thou canst not make the dead (at heart - adamant in their disbelief.) to hear and thou canst not make the deaf (at heart - adamant in their disbelief.) to hear the call, when they withdraw turning their backs. The statement made in these two verses means that the preachings and the guidance of the apostles will only avail those whose minds and hearts are inclined towards the truth, and for those who are adamant, it shall be of no use. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nor canst thou lead the blind out of their straying; Thou canst not make hear any but those who believe in Our signs for they are resigned (to Our will i.e. Muslims). See 30:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God (it is) Who created you out of weakness and then caused strength after weakness, then caused weakness after strength and grey hairs; Createth He what soever He willeth, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful. See 30:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the day whereon the Hour (of Judgment) arriveth, the guilty will swear that they tarried not but an hour; Even so they used to utter lies (on earth) See 30:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who have been given knowledge and faith will say: "Indeed tarried ye according to the decree of God till the Day of Resurrection, so this is the Day of Resurrection but ye were wont not to know." The tarrying refers to the intermediary stage as indicated in the following verses. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But on that day their plea shall not profit those who were unjust, nor will they be allowed to (By any repentance.) please (God). See 30:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed have We set forth for the people, in this Qur'an every kind of similitude; And if thou bringest unto them a sign, certainly will say those who disbelieve: "Ye are naught but a false (Who mislead others.) claimant." See 30:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus doth God set a seal on the hearts of those who know not. See 30:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (This is) the promise of God! Faileth not God His promise, but most people know not (this). See 30:3

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therefore be thou patient (for) Verily the promise of God is True, and let not those who have no certainty hold thee in light estimation. See 30:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They know (only) the appearance of the life of this world, while of the hereafter they are heedless. (Inattentive.) The use of the word 'Ghafilun', i.e., heedless, indicates that man is not totally ignorant or unaware of the life hereafter, but as he is fascinated and attracted by the apparent aspect of this life, he has become inattentive. Otherwise, the human cognitive self, itself bears more affinity to the life hereafter than to the sensual and material world - as hinted in the next verses. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Reflect they not with in themselves; (that) created not God the heavens and the earth and what is between them two but with truth, and for an appointed term? And verily most of the people in the meeting of their Lord, disbelieve. The grant of the worldly power in this life is controlled by the high purpose of the Creator Lord of the Universe. Hence let none be infatuated with the foolish belief of whatever given to him is for all times and will not be snatched away from him to fulfil God's Plan and let everyone know that for everything granted to him, he has to render account for it, as his personal responsibility1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ar-Room:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Have they travelled not in the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were stronger than them in strength; and they dug up the earth and built on it more than what did these build; and there came unto them their apostles with clear proofs (miracles); (for) it is not God Who should do them (any) injustice, but they did injustice unto their own selves. Let everyone have in view the perdition suffered by the people gone before and their kingdoms which flourished in number, strength and prosperity when they went astray and disobeyed the Word of God.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By those who range themselves in ranks, 'Wa' as a prefix, ordinarily meaning conjunction 'And' has been used in the Holy Qur'an for several obvious purposes:(1) When any fact has to be presented not as a mere allegation or statement but to assert with special emphasis, i.e., to assert some truth against any expected or apprehended rejection of it. Sometimes it is used to prophecy an event. A very reasonable question could arise, whether the persons mentioned in the three different consecutive verses are one and the same or different ones, and who they are. Commentators say that the persons meant are the angels and the men of God, as both of these two kinds of beings, possess the qualities mentioned and function as described in the verses. The angels and the men of God, both range themselves to serve…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Except, he who stealeth (a word) by stealth then pursueth him a glistening (Piercing.) flame. Even if any devilish spirit dared to rise to approach the region of the assembly of the angels, it is repulsed and pursued by flames by means of the shooting stars.1This passage indicates also that the devilish beings fascinated with the phenomena of the lower sphere are unable to come in communion with the angelical beings of the higher sphere but some may attempt to get stealthily the news of the higher sphere but will be driven back. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:100 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' my Lord! Grant me a righteous (son)! Abraham receiving Hajira as a gift from his good-hearted wife Sara who could not till then bear any issue for him, prayed to God for an issue at least from the newly acquired wife (Hajira).To have a companion from his own lineage to assist him in his movement towards God. The same was the prayer of Moses, Zachariah and the Holy Prophet. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:101 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So We gave him the glad tidings of a son (Ishmael.) extremely forbearing (Also gentle.) 'Halim' Forbearing - Extremely Patient - Never being hasty in any serious action. This quality of 'Hilm' has been mentioned particularly of Abraham and his son Ishmael, the ancestor of the Holy Prophet, who had inherited this quality specially commended by God.1It was asked of the Sixth Holy Imam Jafar Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq as to what was the interval between the two glad tidings given to Abraham of Ishmael and Isaac. He said 'Five years', the first about the birth of Ishmael and that of the subsequent one of Isaac. Though Sara had herself presented Hajira to her husband Abraham, but after Hajira bearing an issue (Ishmael) to Abraham, which she had not by then been blessed to do, she could not tolerate Hajira with…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:102 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when (the son) reached (the age of) working with him, said he: (Abraham.) "O' my son! verily I saw in a dream that I sacrifice thee: now what is thy view?" Said (the son)! "O' father! Do thou what thou art bidden; (Commanded.) If God willeth, thou wilt find me of the steadfast ones" When Abraham visited Hajira, Ishmael his son had reached the age of thirteen. Once Abraham dreamt to be sacrificing his son Ishmael. It was on the 8th of the lunar month of Dhu al-Hijjah. But Abraham thought it to be some fantasy. Again on the 9th, i.e., the next night, he saw the dream repeated and Abraham got convinced of it to be the command of God and decided to act as he was bidden by the Lord. Since on the 8th Dhu al-Hijjah Abraham…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:103 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when they both had surrendered (themselves) to the will of God and he (Abraham) threw him (the son) upon his forehead, Before laying his son on the ground to fulfil what he had been commanded in the vision to do, Ishmael asked his father to tie his hands and legs tight, and blindfold himself by a bandage on his eyes and to girdle his cloak. Abraham asked Ishmael the reason for the suggestion and if he was afraid and unwilling. Ishmael said that when his throat would be cut, though wholly resigned Ishmael said that when his throat would be cut, though wholly resigned to the will of the Lord, he might naturally feel the pains and get restless and struggle, which sight might naturally disturb Abraham while acting to fulfil only the will of the Lord, hence he…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:104 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We called out unto him: "O' Abraham!" Any other father would have only rejoiced at the escape of his son from death but Abraham stood disappointed and dismayed apprehending if his sacrifice had been rejected by God. A voice from above cried out to Abraham saying, "O' Abraham! Worry thyself not (37:104), for indeed thou hast been true to Our command given to thee in the vision and thus it is, We recompense those who do good (37:105)".

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:105 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed hast thou proved true the dream; Verily thus (In this way.) do We recompense the doers of good! See 37:104

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:106 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, this is an open trial. The command was only an open trial to prove the pure calibre of Abraham and Ishmael, the true servants of God, were made of, and the high degree of faith in God they possessed and to what an extreme extent they actually submitted themselves to the will of their Lord.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:107 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We ransomed him with a Great Sacrifice. 'Fadayna' means, ransoming - which demands a similar thing in the place of the one spared. The quality of the sacrifice with which the sacrifice of Ishmael was spared, is termed by God Himself as 'Azeem', i.e., Great. What God the Greatest Being Himself terms as Great must naturally be something Great in an absolute or in an extraordinary degree. In the first place an ordinary sheep can by no means and in no sense whatsoever be sensibly termed to be Great. Secondly, to term a sheep as great, in comparison to the godly son of the great apostle of God, who was also God's apostle, would be nothing but illogical but also degrading Ishmael.A ransom should essentially be of a preferably greater value, otherwise the offer for substitution would never be…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:108 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We shifted (this blessing) on him (who is from) among the generations (to come) in later times; Five years after he had received the glad tidings about the birth of Ishmael, Abraham was given the glad tidings about the birth of Isaac when he was about 100 years of age.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:109 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Peace be on Abraham. See 37:108

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ask them then (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Are they stronger in creation or (the others) whom We have made?" Verily We created them of a sticky clay. The Holy Prophet was commanded by God to ask the disbelievers whether they were stronger than the former generation who were created with a firm clay, i.e., of strong power of resistance who in spite of their being stronger in build, were destroyed, when they disbelieved and defied the Divine Laws.1The beings of the higher, i.e., the angelical sphere. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:110 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus do We recompense the doers of good. See 37:108

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:111 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily he was (one) of Our faithful servants. See 37:108

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:112 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We gave him the glad tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous ones. The keynote is that the tidings of the birth of Isaac is mentioned here after giving the detailed story of Abraham starting his movements, his young son Ishmael and the story of his sacrifice - indicate clearly that the whole story belongs to Ishmael and the history of Isaac being the subject of sacrifice is unfounded according to Qur'an. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:113 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And bestowed We Our blessings on him and on Isaac: and on their progeny are the doers of good, and those (too) who are openly unjust (Of the Children of Israel (Jacob) son of Isaac, there were good and also bad ones.) to their own selves. The other name of Isaac was Israel, hence the children of Isaac are referred to as the children of Israel who enjoyed the promised blessings of God as long as they deserved it and when they got corrupted in faith and in their practical life, they themselves earned the fall from God's grace and harmed none but themselves. When the offerings of Abraham are referred to it need not necessarily or exclusively be the children of Isaac only but Abraham's progeny in general, i.e., the issues from both of his sons Ishmael and Isaac.…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:114 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed conferred We Our favour on Moses and Aaron. The events relating to the life-history of Moses are very frequent and many in the Holy Qur'an. But for the events specially concerned with reference to this verse.1

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:115 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We delivered them both and their people from the great distress See 37:114

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:116 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We succoured them, so they were the triumphants. See 37:114

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:117 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We gave them both the Book making things clear. See 37:114

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:118 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We guided them both on the right way. See 37:114

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:119 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We perpetuated (Lit. left to stay.) their praise in the later generations, See 37:114

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! Wonderest thou (at their disbelief) while they mock (at thee) See 37:11

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:120 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Peace be on Moses and Aaron. Whenever Moses and Aaron are mentioned jointly as the blessed and the chosen ones of God, the saying of the Holy Prophet should be remembered - Ana wa Ali min Noorin Waahid. I and Ali are of one and the same Light - 'O' Ali thou art to me as Aaron was to Moses.' (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:121 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, thus (In this way.) do We recompense the doers of good. See 37:120

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:122 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, they were both Our faithful servants, See 37:120

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:123 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily, Elias was (one) of the apostles. See verse 6:85. Yaseen was the name of Ilyas' father, and that of the Holy Prophet Muhammad, hence in the Qur'anic address the name of the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt are also known as Aali Yaseen.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:124 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When said he unto his people; "What! Guard ye (Why do ye not practice piety.) not yourselves (against evil)?" Refers to Ilyas admonishing the people who had turned idolaters after the death of Moses. The people worshipped a huge idol called Ba'l and the place was called after the name of the idol Ba'l Bak – Bak - i.e., the city Ba'l-Bak i.e., Baal's city.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:125 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Call ye upon Ba'l (The idol whom the people worshipped as God.) and forsake the Best of the creators? See 37:124

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:126 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God, is your Lord and the Lord of your fathers of (Ancestors.) yore? See 37:124

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:127 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But they belied him, so they shall certainly be brought (to account), See 37:124

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:128 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Save the servants of God, the freed ones (from sinning) See 37:124

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:129 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We perpetuated his praise in the later generations, The clause 'We perpetuated' has been mentioned with Noah, Abraham, Moses, Aaron and Elias and stopped. Which means that in the later generation they were persons who represented these personalities - Refer 'Ziarat' (Salutation) of Warith. All these apostles were represented in the Ahl Al-Bayt. Since Lot and Jonah are not reported to have had any offsprings and do not come in the lineage of Noah and Abraham, Elias being alive still, is represented by Ali. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when they are warned, (Reminded.) they mind not, See 37:11

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:130 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Peace be on 'Ilyasin' (Elias). Whether the recitation of 'Ilyaseen' or 'Aale-Yaseen' the evidence of the context leaves no doubt that it means the same 'Ilyas' mentioned in verse 37:123 - who is identified in the Bible as 'Elia' or 'Elyah'. There is a narration from Ibn Abbas which asserts that the word here is 'Aale-Yaseen' refers to 'Aale-Muhammad' because 'Yaseen' is the title of the Holy Prophet. If the tradition is authentic, most possibly Ibn Abbas mentioned 'Aale-Yaseen' not as the word of the title of the Holy Prophet but on the ground of the association of the ideas he might have mentioned, 'Aale-Yaseen' also to be the subject of the 'Peace from God' similar to 'Ilyaseen' and there are many biblical evidences which show the reappearance of Elijah as identified with Ali. However, this has nothing to do…

item.description: And when they see a sign they incite mocking (at it) See 37:11

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:140 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When he fled unto a ship fully laden, See 37:130

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:141 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they drew lots, and he was of those who were cast off. When the lot was cast as to who in the boat should be cast off into the sea, it is said that forty times consecutively the lot fell to the name of Jonah and ultimately, he was cast out from the boat into the sea.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:142 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the fish swallowed him while he was blamed. Jonah was swallowed by a fish – and it is said that Jonah felt miserable in the belly of the fish and was caused to remain there for three days and when he prayed to God reciting:"La ilaha illa Anta, Subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin"(21:87), i.e., There is no God save Thee, Thou art the Pure and verily I am of the unjust ones.Jonah was caused to be cast out from the belly of the fish and was restored to ordinary life on earth. Hence the times every day after any recital of this sentence for 121 times every day after any one of the daily prayers regularly for 40 days is very effective to get relief from any calamity or sorrow (This is a tried prayer).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:143 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So if it were not that he was of those who glorify Us, See 37:142

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:144 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He would certainly have been detained in its belly to the Day (of Resurrection) when they shall be raised; See 37:142

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:145 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We cast him forth on the naked shore and he was sick. The fish was commanded by God to cast out Jonah from its stomach - upon a barren plain.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:146 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And caused We to grow (to give shade) over him, a plant of gourd. When Jonah was cast out of the fish's belly, he was very ill - with his skin worn out. God caused gourd plant to grow which provided Jonah with its wide leaves with which he protected his body against the sun and prevented flies troubling his wounded body. A wild goat at the command of God, used to come and feed Jonah. When he got better and could move about and had been out somewhere and returned to his place, he found the gourd plant dried away. Jonah felt for losing the useful plant.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:147 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We sent him unto a hundred thousand (people) or (even) more were they. God addressing Jonah said: "O' Jonah! thou didst not feel for a hundred and several thousands of thy fellow men having been made to perish for rebellion against thee and now thou feelest for merely losing a gourd tree which thou needest no more. Now go thou to thy people for a hundred thousand and even more of them have turned faithful and eagerly await to meet thee."

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:148 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And believed they, so We gave them provision till a time. When Jonah reached the outskirts of the town of Nainavah, he met a shepherd who did not believe him to be Jonah, for the people knew him to be drowned. Jonah prayed to God and a sheep cried out in clear words bearing testimony to Jonah's identification. The shepherd went to his people and announced to them about Jonah's return but the people first disbelieved, but when they heard the sheep bearing testimony to his claim they believed in him.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:149 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then ask them (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) Is it that thy Lord hath daughters, (The angels worshipped by the heathens as the daughters of God.) and they have sons? After giving a brief account of the prophets who preached against idolatry in general and the Star-worship in particular, Qur'an turns back addressing the pagans of the time of the Holy Prophet attacking the paganic idea of the time. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "this is but an open sorcery" See 37:11

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:150 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or have We created the angels, females? and did they witness it? See 37:149

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:151 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Beware! Verily it is of their own falsehood that they say: See 37:149

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:152 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (that) God hath begotten: (Jesus worshipped as the begotten Son of God.) And verily they utter a lie. See 37:149

item.description: Hath he preferred daughters to sons? See 37:149

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:154 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:155 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! will ye not then reflect? See 37:149

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:156 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or have ye any clear authority? See 37:149

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:157 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then bring ye your book if ye be truthful. Most probably the reference is to the star-worshippers who claimed to have their own scripture from one of the ancient prophets. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:158 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And assign they between Him and the jinn a kinship, and indeed the jinn to know that they shall surely be brought up (to account on the Day of Judgment) Some of the infidels believed that the angels are the issues of God, through His alliance with the selected women of the Jinns. And the fire-worshippers thought that God and Satan are two brothers, one works goodness and creates light and the other works evils and causes darkness.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:159 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hallowed is God far above from what they (people in general.) ascribe (unto Him), See 37:158

item.description: What! when we are dead and are dust and bones, shall we (even then) indeed be raised? See 37:11

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:160 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But (not so are) the servants, freed (from sinning) The conception about God, forwarded by the others, to the purified servants of God, has no value. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:161 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So verily ye and what ye worship, See 37:160

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:162 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ye can excite not (any one) against Him, See 37:160

item.description: Except him who goes to Hell. See 37:160

item.description: And there is not (any one) of us, but for him is an assigned place, Ref. to what the angels state about their own position, against the wrong description of them the pagans - from verse 149. (A.P.).

item.description: And verily we are they who range ourselves in order. (Explanation to the beginning Verses of the Chapter.) See 37:164

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:171 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed Our word hath already gone forth about (in favour of.) Our servants, the apostles: See 37:164

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:172 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily they shall be the succoured ones. See 37:164

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:173 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily Our hosts, (only) they shall be the victorious. This implies that there should be a state before the Resurrection Day of complete triumph of the mission of the divine guidance on earth which would mean, the triumph of everyone who played his part in the promotion of the divine mission. This is what the reappearance of the last Imam of the Ahl Al-Bayt, The Mahdi, implies - and this refers to the doctrine of 'Raj'at'. In the sense that man by spiritual accomplishment succeeds, to establish communication with all those who took part with all the personalities of the past who played prominent parts in this final triumph of the Truth.This is not the final resurrection day - in support of this refer to verses 39:67 - 39:75. This is a reference to the day of the manifestation…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:174 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So turn thou away from them for a time, (Until the Final Triumph.) See 37:173

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:175 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (then) behold thou: for they too shall soon behold (their doom). See 37:173

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:176 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! would they then hasten on Our chastisement? See 37:173

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:177 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But when it shall descend in their court, (face to face just before them.) evil shall then be the morning of the warned ones. Refer 175This is what the tradition of the Ahl Al-Bayt asserts, that during the final trial not only those who played a prominent part in favour of the triumph will enjoy, but the chief opponents also wherever they be, will realise the triumph and will suffer. All this shall take place before the Total Resurrection. (A.P.).It is wrong to confine the application of this verse only to those Meccans who were defeated by the Muslims until the conquest of Mecca, as it would mean limitation of the jurisdiction of the Holy Prophet against what is declared at the beginning.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:178 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And turn thou away from them for a time, Indicates that before the final triumph, there will be setbacks as the past of the Muslims and the believers should not become loose-hearted or get dejected. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:179 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (then) behold thou, for they too shall soon see (their doom). See 37:178

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And stop them, for verily they have to be questioned: See 37:22

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Saying) "How now, that ye (The disbelievers.) help not one another?" See 37:22

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! on that day they shall be submitting themselves. The arrogance they used in the life before death would have totally disappeared and they would become very submissive.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And some of them shall advance unto the others questioning each other. See 37:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They shall say: "Nay! ye (yourselves) (Mutual accusation.) were not the believers:" See 37:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And by the reciters of Qur'an, See 37:1

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And there was not for us over you any authority. Nay! ye were a people rebellious! See 37:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So now hath been proved true against us the sentence of Our Lord that verily we shall (have to) taste (the doom) See 37:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And we led you astray, for verily we ourselves were astray. See 37:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily they on that day shall be the sharers in the punishment. See 37:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, thus do We deal with the guilty ones. See 37:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily they, when it was said unto them that there is no god but God, used to behave (Turn away.) proudly, See 37:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (used) to say "What! Are we to indeed give up our gods for a poet (who is) crazed?" See 37:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! he hath come with the truth and did testify (Also - are testified the preceding apostles by him.) the (preceding) apostles. His advent also was testified by the apostles of old. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, ye will taste the painful chastisement. See 37:37

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And ye shall be recompensed not but what ye were doing, If this and the next verse are read together it indicates that the evil doers will only suffer for their own misdeeds but the purified servants of the Lord will enjoy the grace and blessings more and ever more. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily your God is (only) One. The Unity of God is the important message or the Greatest Truth, to convey which, so much emphasis has been used through such a solemn and emphatic assertion, for the correct faith in the Unity of the Creator of the Universe, is directly and most vitally connected with the life and the destiny of the human race. Man has to necessarily know that he has not been created by a mere accident or as a sport of any vain creative power or by any contending forces or by any purposeless mechanical process. Man should essentially know as to who actually is his creator and master and what are his qualities and powers and his rights over his creation. Man must know the correct source or authority from whom he gets all that he needs…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Save the servants of God, the freed ones (Refer to note on verses 37:39, 15:39 - 15:42, 14:22 & 17:65.) (from evil inclinations). See 37:39

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Fruits, and they shall be highly honoured, See 37:39

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In the gardens bountiful, (Of delight and bliss.) See 37:39

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Upon couches facing each other See 37:39

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Round will go unto them a cup from a clear spring, See 37:39

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Limpid white, delicious unto those who, drink. See 37:39

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nothing therein to oppress (Affect, spoil.) the sense, nor shall they be exhausted therewith The spiritual world is one abstract unit and the bliss of it is universal and enduring but the physical world is a composite organisation with opposites of contrasting demerits. Trouble or fatigue is the state of exertion of the physical body. The life in Paradise being free from all physical dependence and needs, there naturally can be no trouble or exhaustion in any aspect of the blissful life which would naturally be of continued or sustained state of realisation. Such a unique state of existence would be the award from the identical attributes of God who owns it, in its absolute or infinite degree.1 Neither slumber nor sleep could ever approach Him, and in the conclusion of the verse is said that the preservation of His…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And with them shall be chaste women with modest gaze, with big (beautiful) eyes, The qualities of chaste, modest and pure womanhood have been presented in this verse. The description of the women in Paradise, no doubt refers to the kind of the mates, the righteous ones would have, in heaven, but the qualities figuratively imply as a model or ideal, worthy to be adopted by every believer woman in her life on earth. It is given here that the most valuable quality in a woman, worthy of belonging to Paradise, is the quality of chastity which is said to possess eyes free from lust.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: As if they were eggs (secured) hidden The eyes are described as eggs which are always kept safe, closely guarded against the least effect detrimental to its external and the internal security, i.e., from breakage as well as from getting rotten. It is said the Ostrich secures its eggs by keeping them concealed in its feathers against the dust and the sun. The comparison to eggs, is the most apt and in another place women are compared to rubies and pearls which another place women are always found treasured deep in the earth in the mines or in the strong safes in the secured places of the owners.1 Every verse of the Holy Qur'an has an outer and several inner meanings applicable to individuals and people in various states and different walks of life.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and the Lord of the places of the rising (Literally, Easts. Refer to verse 7:137.) of (the sun and the moon). 'Mashariq' (the plural of 'Mashriq,' i.e., East). There is not the only one East in the whole universe. The sun rises not only for this earth of our habitation but its rise is for the other globes swimming in the immeasurable space called the heavens and the rotation of each such globe around the sun manifests the rising of the sun and its setting and wherever manifests its rising and setting, is a Mashriq East and a Maghrib West.1 The astronomical discoveries have declared that there is not one solar system but many others. Thus there are as many Easts and Wests as the revolutionary activity…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall advance some of them unto the others questioning each other. See verse 27 above. The righteous ones in the heavens discussing with each other.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Shall say a speaker (among them) who shall speak: "Verily, there was of mine an intimate one," One in the heaven would say that he had an intimate one in his earthly life.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He used to say: "What! art thou (too, indeed) of the testifying (a believer.) ones (of the Resurrection)?" He wondered at the believer in truth.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! when we are dead and are dust and bones, shall we (even) then in fact be brought to account (Requital – judgment.) ? And doubted about the resurrection after death.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He shall say (unto those around him): "Will ye look?" He shall tell them to see the fate of the disbelievers in Hell.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then he looked down and saw him in the midst of Hell. See 37:54

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He shall say: "By God! thou hast almost caused me to (an exclamation or expression of surprise.) perish!" See 37:54

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And had it not been the bounty of my Lord, certainly would I (too) have been (with thee) brought into (the Hell) See 37:54

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is it then we die not (hereafter)? Having seen the fate of the disbeliever and feeling the joy for being safe, the individual gets conscious of the danger of once again being returned to the earthly life and asks if there is in future any other life of temptation and. the risk of suffering any consequent perdition. Death stands for the turning point from the one state of life to another.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Save our first death; And we shall not be ('Which we have already had before we are granted this bliss.') chastised? See 37:58

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily We have adorned the heaven nearest to this world (earth) with an adornment, the stars, 'Sama'ad Dunya', i.e., the Lower heavens.1The nearest heaven to the earth is the Lower heaven, lower than the heavens, which could be called to be the seat of the Exalted Assembly of the Angels.The heavens surrounding the earth are said to be the lowest or the nearest to the earth.The beauty of the starry skies is proverbial. Here is implied the marvellous beauty and the well-planned grouping and the perfectly harmonious working of everything in the heavens manifesting the Unity, the Power and the Wisdom of the One All-Perfect Designer, Creator and the Supreme Master of the Universe.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily this is a great (feeling of realisation.) achievement. See 37:58

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For the like of this should act every active one! See 37:58

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is this the better entertainment or the tree of Zaqqum? The tree of 'Zaqqum' according to some, is a tree having small leaves, stinging and bitter. 'Zaqqum' is a dust-coloured tree, having small round thorny leaves. It has a pungent odour with a bitter taste, and has knots in its stem - the heads of its leaves are very foul.1

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, We have made it a trial for the unjust. See 37:62

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, it is a tree that groweth in the bottom of the hell, See 37:62

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Its produce is (ugly) as the heads of the satans. See 37:62

item.description: And verily they shall eat from it and fill (their) bellies with it. See 37:62

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then verily for them shall be to drink over it, a mixture in boiling water. See 37:62

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then verily their return shall be unto the hell See 37:62

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily they found their fathers (Also ancestors.) going astray, See 37:62

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (which is also) a guard against every rebellious Satan; The perfect, the harmonious, the undisturbed and the continuous movement of everything in the heavens, is itself obvious and sufficiently eloquent in its declaration that the Kingdom of God is perfectly planned and entirely guarded against any rebellious elements, material or spiritual, venturing to disturb it. The functioning of the heavens manifest not only the inimitable divine beauty but also the glory of the power and the authority of the Omnipotent Creator. Goodness is always protected by the All-Good, against evil. Similarly, the men of God who are the goodness personified or the reflection or the manifestation of the goodness of the Lord, are also duly protected, hence they are called 'Masooms', i.e., 'the Divinely Protected ones.' The protection of such absolutely godly ones, has been effected from the very…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So they in their footsteps did hasten (running after.) on. See 37:62

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed went astray most of the ancients before them, See 37:62

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We did send among them warners. See 37:62

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: See then how had been the end of those (already) warned, See 37:62

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Save the servants of God, the freed (See verses 15:39 - 15:42, 14:22 & 17:65.) ones (from sinning). See 37:62

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed did call on Us Noah, and (We are) the Most Excellent answerers (of prayer) See 37:62

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We, delivered him and his followers from the great distress. Noah and his posterity saved through the Ark and the rest made to perish.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We made his progeny the survivors. Noah's offsprings have been presented here as the sole survivors after the Deluge though from verses 10:73, 11:36 and 11:40, it is clear that there were others also, though very few - who followed Noah and survived the Deluge. The passage here should be interpreted as of his survivors who carried the torch of guidance to the present day. In other words the spiritual leadership continued unabated and from Abraham through the branches of the Ishmaelites and of Isaac.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We did perpetuate for him (his praise) in the later generations. See 37:77

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Peace be on Noah in all the worlds! See 37:77

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (So that) They may hear not (what passeth in) the assembly on high, and they are darted from every side. It is said that the evil spirits, perhaps as a respite, could approach the lower heavens and while they did so, they used to get some information from that region about the future and used to adulterate the knowledge with some falsehood on behalf of their own selves and inspire the matter to their devotees on earth but since the advent of the Last Apostle of God and the revelation of the Final Code of Guidance, the Holy Qur'an, even this approach to the first or the lowest regions above, has been stopped, and since then no evil one could have any knowledge from the higher regions where the Grand Assembly of the holy and the heavenly beings, is said…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily thus do We recompense the doers of good. See 37:77

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily he was (one) of Our faithful servants. See 37:77

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then We drowned the others. See 37:77

item.description: And verily of his persuasion (i.e., Party – group.) was Abraham. (Compare with verse 3:67.) Persons of the same ideology are called 'Shias'.1 This has become a distinguishing term for those who followed Ali, as the Holy Prophet said: 'O' Ali thou and thy Shias, on the Day of Resurrection will be on the pulpits of light and be successful.' (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When came he unto his Lord with a submissive heart, See 37:83

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When said he unto his father (Godfather who adopted. Refer to note on verse 14:41.) and his people: "What is it that ye worship?" See 37:83

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:86 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is it a falsehood - gods other than (the One True) God, desire ye? See 37:83

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:87 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What then think ye about the Lord of the worlds? See 37:83

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:88 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then glanced (Looked up.) he, casting glance at the stars, See 37:83

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:89 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then said he: "Verily, sick I am (of your worshipping these)" i.e., I am sick of your worshipping false gods, (i.e., idols). As if he was pained by the people's idolatrous belief in the influence of the stars for which they had made their temples with the idols of the stars. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (To be) Driven off, and for them being a perpetual chastisement, It is said that after the advent of the Holy Prophet, the doors of even the lower heavens got closed to the devils or the evil spirits. No soothsayer could cheat the people with false prophecies about the future of persons etc.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:90 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So they turned away turning (As the result of the disgust.) their backs. See 37:89

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:91 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then he (Abraham) turned unto their gods secretly and said: "What! eat ye not?" See 37:89

item.description: What aileth you that ye speak not? See 37:89

item.description: Then he attacked them in secret, striking with his right hand See 37:89

item.description: Said he: (Abraham.) "What! worship ye what ye (yourselves) hew out?" See 37:89

item.description: And God hath created you and (also) what ye make (the idols) See 37:89
