item.description: Said they: "Erect for him (Abraham.) a building (Manjaniq) (furnace) and fling him in the flaming fire!" See 37:89

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:98 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So they desired a plot against him, but We brought them low. They plotted against Abraham but Abraham was helped to escape from their clutches and to prosper and, it was his enemies that were defeated in their plans and were themselves humiliated.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saaffaat:99 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said he: (Abraham.) "Verily, I am going unto my Lord, He will guide me;" When Abraham found the people to be immune to every kind of admonition and guidance, and were getting further astray and ever more persecutive, he decided to leave the place and that was Abraham's Hijrat from his native place, the place of his ancestors which was naturally dear to him but dearer still was truth to him, for which he chose to fly away from the people, being sick of their incorrigible and unyielding nature and their adhering only to falsehood and living a rebellious life, Abraham trusted himself to God and left the place.It may be noted that this same thing was repeated by the Holy Prophet Muhammad, in his migrating from Mecca to Madina, trusting himself to God. But when Abraham was providentially…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Halloweth (Refer to Verses 17:44; 62:1; 64:1.) God whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth; and He is the Ever-Prevalent, the All-Wise. This verse is similar to 59:1 and 62:1. The glorification of God by everything of His creations means the implicit obedience with which the beings known as animate and the inanimate in our classification, both in the heavens and in the earth, working out God' plan without the least diversion from the course given to them by their Lord.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! shall I show you a merchandise which will deliver you from a painful chastisement? Truly it is a very profitable business towards which God guides mankind, for the very little investment, there is an ever-recurring or an everlasting gain, with an eternal bliss1.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (That) ye should believe in God and His Apostle, and strive in the way of God with your possessions and your selves; that is better for you, if ye but knew! See 61:10

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He will forgive you your sins and admit you into gardens, neath which flow rivers and excellent abodes in the gardens (Paradise.) of eternity; that is the supreme achievement. See 61:10

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And another (blessing will He bestow) which ye love, (that is) the help from God, and a victory at hand; So give thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) the glad tidings unto the believers. May refer to the conquest of Mecca as well as to the ultimate triumph of Islam at the re-appearance of Imam. There the use of 'Qareeb', Near - will be in the same sense as used for the Resurrection Day1. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! Be ye the helpers (in the cause) of God as said Jesus, son of Mary unto (his) disciples: "Who (among you) wall be my helpers unto (the work of) God?" Said the disciples (of Jesus) "We are the helpers (in the cause) of God! "Then believed a party of the children of Israel and disbelieved a party (among them), Then We aided those who believed against their enemy, so they became victorious (Refer to Verses 3:52, 5:54.)" "Now the names of the Twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother""Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Mathew the publican; James the son of Alphacus, and Lebhaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus',"Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him." Math. 10/2-4.1An identical incident…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: 'O' ye who believe! Why say ye what (That which.) ye (yourselves) do (it) not? This refers to the tall talks of most of the companions of the Holy Prophet. People had talked a lot about their devotion to God and His Holy Prophet, about the great sacrifices they were ready to offer, and about their verbal determination to do or to die in the fight for the Truth but when the occasions arose against the enemy, they miserably failed to maintain their verbal resolution with any firmness in action. At Uhud most of the weak in faith and the fickle-minded ones among the converts to Islam took to flight and according to Tabari, Tarikh al-Khamis, Tafsir al-Kabir, Minhaj an-Nubuwwah etc. many of the prominent companions were also among those who ran away from the field deserting the Holy Prophet…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Most hateful is it unto God that ye say what ye (yourselves) do (it) not (Reformer reform thyself first.) . The Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq said: "The promise of a faithful to his brother in faith is a solemn pledge, the failure to fulfil it or acting against it, earns the displeasure and invites the wrath of God. This includes the scholars, the priests and the Preachers of Islam who preach a goodness and godliness to the people but they themselves never act in accordance to what they preach to the others to do." There is a reference to such a character in 2:44.Those who do not themselves act on goodness, are not entitled to preach it. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily God loveth (He hates those who run away from the battlefield.) those who fight in His way in ranks as if they were an unbreakable metalled wall (Refer to Verse 37:1. Believers to be well organised and disciplined acting in coordination with each other.) . Note the degree of Firmness, Steadfastness, Courage and Fortitude which God wants in a true believer in Him, at the time when He tries him against the disbelievers. A believer on such occasions of trials, has to stand by the truth like a compact wall immovable by any attack from falsehood. This is quality which those who ran away from the battle-field miserably lacked, which was exposed at Uhud, Khaybar and Honain1. These are the qualities which distinguished 'Ali from the rest, on all occasions without any exception. There were a few others also…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when said Moses unto his people: "O' ye my people! Why do ye pain me? while indeed ye know that verily I am an apostle of God unto you;" but when (yet) went they astray, God (too) allowed their hearts (to astray)', and God guideth not the people who transgress (Refer to Verse 33:69.) . The people of Moses were characteristically rebellious, they used to vex him with all sorts of ridiculous desires, and insulted him with irritating criticisms. They called him a sorcerer, a madman, and sometimes they wanted him to fix up a god for them to worship as the others had it. They began worshipping the calf - They once told him that they would not believe in God unless he showed Him to them. They had been frequently shown miracle after miracle. It was their…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when said Jesus, son of Mary: "O' ye the children of Israel! Verily I am an apostle of God unto you, confirming what is before you of the Torah and bearing (unto you) the glad tidings of an Apostle who shall come after me, his name being Ahmed (The Title of The Holy Prophet Muhammad - i.e. 'Ahmad al- Mujtaba' i.e. the Parcele to John. Which has been anglicised as the Comforter - the Spirit of Truth. N.T. John. 16/7-14) (i.e. Muhammad) and when came he (Ahmed) unto them said they: "This is a manifest Sorcery!" This is one of the verses which have to be studied along with the reference in the Old and the New Testaments. Jesus invites the attention of the Israelites to their sacred scripture the Torah in their own hands, the scripture given to…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And who is more unjust than he who forgeth a lie against God while he is invited unto Islam? and God guideth not the unjust people (Refer to Verses 3:94; 3:192.) . Nasr Ibn Harith said that on the Day of Judgment his idol gods Lat and Uzza would intercede on his behalf and God would accept the intercession - This verse was revealed - meaning of the idol.Like the light of the sun, which is shone upon all, irrespective of anyone being faithful to God or unfaithful to Him and on those who do not want to avail of it, the sun docs not cease to shine.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Intend they to put out the Light (Refer to Verses 9:32; 24:35 - 24:37; 64:8.) of God with their mouths! but God will perfect His Light, though averse may be the dis-believers. The foolish ones think that they can extinguish (defeat) the truth by false arguments. But God has decided to fulfil it1.Once a Jew, Ka'b Ibn Ashroff saw the Holy Prophet in the state of the trance while he was receiving a revelation from God, and said: "Rejoice ye O' Israelites for God hath extinguished the Light of Muhammad and thank God his mission has been left incomplete." This verse was revealed.Regarding the light of God the method and the place of its manifestation2This asserts that the Divine Light of Guidance is a continuous process to be completed. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Saff:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He it is who hath sent His Apostle (Muhammad) with the Guidance (Qur'an) and the Religion of Truth (Islam), that He may make it triumph over all the (other) religions, though averse may be the polytheists (Refer to Verses 48:28; 9:33.) . The verse prophesies that Islam would be the most dominant religion of the world – which prophecy is yet to be fulfilled. Commentators say that the predominance would be established in time. It would take effect when the Last of the Apostolic successors, the Twelfth Holy Imam. Muhammad Ibnul Hasan Al-Mahdi would re-appear. Though the complete dominance of Islam over all the other religions of the world is destined to take effect in its own time - but the triumph of its doctrines has already started and is gaining hold over the religious ideology of the various schools…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Alif, Lam, Meem. (A. L. M.) See 32:3

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said they: "What! when we become lost in the earth, shall (Is it - Are we going to be in a new creation?) we even then be (returned) into a new creation?" Nay! in the meeting of their Lord they are disbelievers. See verses 13:5, 17:49, 19:66, 36:78.This is said referring to what the Holy Prophet used to assert that man is created to last for ever and not to be destroyed after a while. The only thing is that man is shifted from one abode to another one which may be happy or miserable as per his own doings 'khuliqa al-nasu li-l-baqa' la li-l-fana'' - Man has been created to last and not to perish. 'innama yunqaluna min dari al-a'mali ila dari al-shaqawati aw al-sa'adati' They are only shifted from the abode of action to the abode of…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Shall cause you to die the angel of death who is put in charge of you, then unto your Lord ye shall be brought back." Here asserts that it is the angel of death who causes death. In verse 6:61 - it attributes death to the angels and in verse 39:42 attributes to God Himself - just to indicate that whatever is done, God is the real cause of it. The others are only the agencies subservient to His will. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And couldst thou but see when the guilty ones shall droop their heads before their Lord (saying): "O' our Lord! we have seen and we have heard, now then send us back, we will do good; verily (now) we are certain" See 32:11

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Had We pleased certainly We would have given every soul its guidance, but true (Just.) is the word which hath gone forth from Me, certainly will I fill hell with jinn and men together. As an explanation to this verse refer to the portion of Ali's prayer 'Dua Kumayl'.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So (they will be told) "Taste ye (the recompense) for what ye had forsaken (Neglected.) the meeting of this your day Verily We too forsake you: and taste ye the abiding chastisement for what ye were doing." See 32:13

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily believed in Our signs only those who when they are reminded of them, fall down prostrating in obeisance and celebrate (Expose His glorification by praising Him.) the praise of their Lord, and they exalt not (with pride). See verses 7:206, 13:15, 22:77. Those who recite this verse and also those who hear it recited, must offer a prostration to the Lord. The prostration here is Wajib, i.e., Compulsory.Exposes His glorification by praising Him.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Their sides (For 'Tahajjud' prayers.) forsake their beds (getting way from their beds overnight), praying unto their Lord in fear and (in) hope, and (of what We provide them with) spend they (benevolently in the Way of their Lord) This verse was revealed about the Holy Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib and those of his followers (his Shias) who following his example, sleep only the first two-thirds of the night and in the last one-third they are awake with the eagerness and sincerity to pray to God. The Holy Prophet said: "Shall I inform you of the entrance of righteousness - Remember ye that fasting is a shield against the fire of Hell - Giving of alms wipes out sins - and waking up in the night in prayer takes one nearer to God. The Holy Prophet said that he…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And knoweth not any soul what is hidden for them (the righteous ones) of the joy of the eyes, in recompense for what (good) they were doing. What God has in store to reward his faithful servants with, no eye has seen, nor any ear has heard it and no heart of any man can ever conceive it.This verse proves that all the description of the sensual pleasures of the life hereafter is a mere figurative expression as otherwise the pleasure is hidden far beyond the human grasp. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is he then who is a believer like the one who is a transgressor? (What about breaking the Covenant of Ghadir Khumm?) They shall not be held (Not equal.) alike. It is recorded alike by both the Sunni and the Shia commentators that al-Walid ibn 'Utbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt who was a step-brother of Uthman, once by way of priding over Ali said "O Ali, thou art only a boy and the strength of my youth is superior to thine, I am more than thee in the sharpness of the tongue, my lance is sharper than thine and in the army I am more steadfast than thee." Ali in reply to the infidel said "Be quiet O' rebellious one! Though art no comparison to me." This verse was revealed (U.B.)1.This same Walid was appointed by Uthman, as the Governor of…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: As for those who believe and do good, for them, the gardens (of bliss) shall be the (heavenly) abode; as an entertainment for what (good) they were doing. See 32:18

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The revelation of the Book (the Qur'an) there is no doubt in it, (it is) from the Lord of the worlds. See 32:3

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But as for those who transgress, their abode shall be the (hell) fire; so oft as they shall desire to get out of it they shall be brought back into it, and it shall be said unto them: "Taste ye the chastisement of the fire which ye used to belie." See 32:18

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (here) certainly will We make them taste of a minimum chastisement instead of the maximum chastisement, that happly they may turn (unto Us, repentant). This could be a reference to the drought of seven years which took place during the lifetime of the Holy Prophet or to the battle of Badr when most of the leading chiefs of the disbelievers were killed.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the signs of his Lord, then he turneth away from them? Verily We, from the guilty ones, shall exact (the due) retribution. See 32:21

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed gave We unto Moses the Book, so be thou (The Prophet addressed for the people.) not in doubt of receiving this from Him (God), and it (Torah) made We a guidance unto the children of Israel, The life-history of Moses is identical with that of the Holy Prophet:Moses was given the Torah and the Holy Prophet, the Holy Qur'an.Moses was under the command to fight his enemies, the Holy Prophet was also ordered to do the same.Moses had prayed to God to assist him with Aaron as his Deputy, the Holy Prophet was given Ali as his Deputy.Moses was victorious against Pharaoh's forces and the Holy Prophet was granted triumph over his enemies.Moses's wife Safoora fought with Usha ibn Nun, and A'isha the wife of the Holy Prophet, at the head of the army, fought Ali at Jamal…

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of them made We Leaders (Imams) (Note: Like the apostles and prophets, Imams or leaders also are made or appointed by God and not by man through election or nomination.) to guide (the people) by (In accordance to.) Our command as they were steadfast (in the calamities); and they of Our signs were quite certain. This is a reference to the twelve holy Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, the divinely commissioned guides to mankind on the path of Islam and the custodians of the Final Word of God (the Holy Imams) - with whom the Holy Prophet left the Holy Book to secure it intact, against any corruption or Tahrif and to give to mankind its correct interpretations as the authorised deputies of the Last Apostle of God.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily thy Lord Himself will decide between them on the Day of Judgment concerning what they therein were disputing. See 32:24

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Doth it not guide them aright (to see) how many of the generations We did destroy before them, they walk (They pass through or pass by.) (today) in (the ruins of) their abodes; verily in this are signs; Will they not then hear? The very fact of the vicissitude of fortune or the natural changes which are daily taking place here are the proof that, in this life, all are in transitory state which undoubtedly has an end and that whatever one should do to secure a good end it should be done here. Otherwise at the end nothing can be done. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! See they not that We drive the water unto the parched earth and We bring forth with it crops of which eat the cattle and they themselves? Will they not then see? See 32:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "When will this judgment take place? (tell us) if ye be truthful," See 32:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "On the Day of Judgment, will not profit those who disbelieve, their faith, nor will they be respited." See 32:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or say they "He (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) hath forged (Qur'an.) it?" Nay! it is the truth from thy Lord, that thou mayest warn a people unto whom came not any warner before (Since the immediately preceding apostle Jesus.) thee, that happly they may be guided aright. Since the departure of Jesus until the advent of the Holy Prophet Muhammad, there had not come to the people any Warner, i.e., an apostle from God, to prevent their going astray from the right path which was already shown to them through Jesus and the apostles preceding him.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So turn thou away from them and wait, verily they too do wait. See 32:26

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God (it is) Who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days (stages) and got firm on His Throne (of authority), for you there is none besides Him of a guardian, nor any intercessor; What! will ye not then reflect? See verses 7:54, 10:3, 11:7, 25:59, 41:12, 70:4.About the conception of time beyond this life, i.e., on the Day of Judgment - see verse 70:4 and the next verse.

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Regulateth He (all) the affairs from the heaven to the earth, then shall it ascend unto Him in a day the measure of which is a thousand years of what ye reckon. In view of the extent of the time which to us, now is unimaginable, the restoration of all values on the Day of Judgment will be in so short a time that it will be the twinkling of an eye and yet to our calculation it will be thousands of years.1This clearly indicates the circular process of the divine administration - descending from the highest to the lowest and ascending from the lowest to the highest, not in the ordinary days of twenty-four hours. Refer to note on verse. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This (Such.) is the Knower of the hidden and the manifest, the All-Mighty, the All-Merciful, This 'al-Ghayb' and 'al-Shahadah' in correspondence with the 'al-Sama' and the 'al-Ard' mentioned in the previous verse 5 in the sense that by 'al-Sama' means the unseen world and 'al-Ard' the seen world which appeals to the external senses. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He Who made best every thing which He hath created and began the creation of man from clay. Refer to verse 23:12 - 23:16.His planning of everything is the Best. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then He made his progeny of an extract of despised water (Sperm. Refer to note on verses 36:77, 16:4 & 86:6.) (liquid) See 32:7

item.title: bil-Quran: As-Sajda:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then (Refer to verse 15:29.) shaped him and breathed into him of His spirit (Into a harmonious whole.) and made for you the ears, and the eyes and the hearts; (yet how) Little is it that ye give thanks. See 32:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the sun and his radiation! In the verses 1-7 the solemn appeal is made to the reflective faculty mankind has been endowed with. Each one of the objects in whose name the swearing is done, if studied intelligently is one of the manifestations of God's might and wisdom which none else besides Him could ever be imagined to effect.The sun even to this day with the boasting of the human intellect about the progress it has made, is a mystery. None could ever even presume definitely what the matter is that burns so continuously for all the unknown millions of years of its age. The sun with its natural properties and the influence it has over the other heavenly bodies and the blessing it is, to the earth, is nothing but a mystery which has proved itself insolvable for…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, faileth he who polluted it! Corruption in the faith in the True God, the Lord, and the failure of the control over the self against its rebellious passions towards the realisation of the carnal desires, leads the soul in the march of life, to perdition.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Belied (the truth the Tribe), Thamood, due to their rebellious impiety! The Prophet was Saleh. The above verses invite the attention of man, to the fate of the people1 who acted rebellious to the instructions of apostle Saleh and hamstrung the She camel, which was sent as a trial, which conduct of the people brought perdition to them.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When rose up the worst wretch among them (with mischief) (Refer to: 7:73 - 7:79, 11:61.) ! See 91:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then said unto them (Saleh) the Apostle of God: ''It is the She Camel of God, (leave her) and its drink! See 91:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But they belied him (Saleh.) and hamstrung her, so crushed them their Lord for their sins, and levelled them (all with the ground) Hamstrung with no reason, save the rebellious nature which made them commit the heinous act. The Holy Prophet of Islam said: ''The wicked person among the ancients, is the murderer of the harmless She Camel of Saleh which was endowed to the service of God and the most wicked person of the latter age is the murderer of Ali Ibn Ahi Talib as there is no justification for the heinous crimes but the rebellious spirit against a person who has devoted his life from his birth to death to the service of God"This Tradition has been narrated by Usman son of Suhail from his father and from Ammar Ibn Yasir - that the Holy Prophet said this…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He feareth not (any one against) the consequences (they met) When the decree of the Lord comes, it cares not for the consequence which the people might meet.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the moon when she followeth after it! The moon following the sun, and its native reflective property, its acting as the substitute of the sun in illuminating the world as the sun's vicegerent - the contrast in its effect of the coolness, in its light quite different from the heat producing light of the sun, though the light reflected by the moon is nothing else other than the light of the sun, and what makes the same light of the sun to become the opposite in effect and nature, to its original properties it possesses before the reflection, is another mystery left till now for the scientist to only speculate and imagine and to go on revising their own theories, one after another.'Tala' meaning - following of a thing as a consequence of another one as antecedent, i.e., the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the Day when it unfoldeth its (Sun's.) light! The day - its duration with fully regulated working of the phenomenon of the dawn and the dusk - the revealing aspect of the sun's glory and effect on earth and all the earthly beings and their activities in it - its end and its fully regulated repetition of the renewals and its closure, is a mystery to any intelligently active mind. It is a proof positive to tell man that as the day is renewed and the sleeping world is once again resurrected, the Lord will one day effect the Final Death and the Final Resurrection for the Final Judgment.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the Night when it enshroudeth it! The disappearance of the sun concealing the light, making man and animal to rest, restore once again the quietude to make man thoughtful that as the day has disappeared and the world ceases to be active, there is one day for the world to sleep in its getting extinct at the will of its Almighty Author. The inimitable beauty that the skies manifest in their glorious exhibition of the heavenly bodies, each one of whom is a wonder by itself. The changing phases, the appearance of the starry show in the skies and the gradual increase of the darkness and the cool atmosphere and the return to the dawn - all in a fully regulated cycle, almighty system, even to this day is nothing but a wonder to the human intellect.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the heaven as it is built! The firmament above the skies with the rain-giving clouds - and the wonderful harmony with which the heavenly bodies work, in a wonderfully organised teamwork with the mighty control of the Omnipotent Will, the raising of the water to be stored in the clouds - the distribution of the rain to the various parts of the earth according to mysteriously planned allotment of the fixed annual quota and thousands of the other marvels, are too great and unapproachable for the human intellect to assess the correct value or worth of even a single one of them.The three passages - verses 5-7, the reference is to the mechanism of heavenly bodies and their functioning harmoniously and the earth: its expansion in a harmonious way and to the soul and the harmonious functioning of its…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the earth as it is expanded forth! The earth, with the invaluable stores of minerals, metals, liquids and gasses treasured in it and its usefulness to life on it, its rivers and springs, the wide, deep and mighty oceans, its fixed and immovable mountains, the various kinds of climate in the different parts of it, with the variety of its soil in its appearance and its properties, it being in global form and yet serving as a plain to the habitations and the innumerable other wonderful properties and its unlimited usefulness, all these are the great marvels which only an intelligent study can disclose.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the soul as it is perfected (Well-harmonised (A.P.). Refer to: 32:9.) ! The soul, particularly the human, is one of the greatest mysteries of the universe. The different faculties endowed in it, its gradual development or progress in consciousness, the zenith of the same soul which at its birth could not utter even a single syllable and which could not help its body to take a turn of its own accord, becomes the best gymnast, best scholar and the best sage, every soul by itself is a separate wonder.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And inspired unto it (against) its vices and (about) its piety (Refer to: 76:3, 90:10.) ! The soul was inspired by God, its Almighty and All-wise Author - the consciousness and the faculty of discretion to distinguish impiety and piety, the right conduct and the wrong ways of life. This is the most invaluable gift granted exclusively to man.Make it known to it what is Vice and what is Virtue. Vices are termed as 'Fujoor' meaning bursts, and Virtue as 'Taqwa' guarding, to indicate that Vices are the outcome of loose conduct and Virtue is the outcome of self-control and will power. The example is given in verse 12. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shams:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed, succeedeth he who purifieth (Through abstinence from the forbidden and adopting only the course prescribed by the Lord) it! The success of every human individual male and female, as achieved the right goal of this life, the salvation, depends upon preserving the soul in its original purity against its getting soiled, polluted and clouded by the carnal desires, by submitting it to the will and the pleasure of the Lord1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) What! Have We not expanded for thee thy breast (Refer to: 20:25.) ? In spite of the simple and clear words, this Surah, as a whole, has been most erroneously misinterpreted by some commentators. The misinterpretations mislead the common people who blindly follow their pet religious leaders without any scrutiny or verification, readily accepting whatever is told to them. 'Sharh al-sadr' means expansion of the breast, i.e., heart. It is an acknowledged term, to mean the broadening or the extending of the faculty of conscience, reasoning and understanding for the accommodation of wider, greater or higher knowledge. The verse means an assertion from God that He has given the heart of the Holy Prophet, the greatest expanse for knowledge. When Moses was commanded by God to proceed to Pharaoh, to preach to him the truth and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We took off from thee thy burden (Ar. 'Vizr, the burden of apostleship - The ministry.) ? The 'Vizr' means the burden of the apostleship, i.e., ministry1. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Which weighed down thy back (Refer to: 73:5.) ? See 94:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And exalted we for thee, thy fame (Eminence Remembrance.) ? This is a prophetic announcement of the mention, or the eminence of the Holy Prophet being raised to glorious heights both in this world and in the hereafter, high above the mention of any one in the world. Bringing into account the 'Salawat' or the salutation, every Muslim is obliged to recite it at least in each of the five times daily prayer. There is none in the world to be compared to the Holy Prophet in this regard for the name of no other apostle of God, is mentioned in such abundance. This prophecy was made when the Prophet was a solitary figure, not much recognised even by the people of his own place and when most of the people in his environment were hostile to him.None can correctly…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily with (every) difficulty (there) is ease The whole life of the Holy Prophet was of persecution, difficulties and toil, dangers and worries. The repeated statement here is to give emphasis to the promise and its assurance of the ultimate triumph of the cause even though in the earlier stages the situation was utterly hopeless and the survival of the Holy Prophet, the Muslims and the very name of the faith, Islam, seemed to be an impossibility.By making his name to be mentioned in the 'Azan' the Call for prayer - in the 'Tashah'hud' in the prayer itself and in the form of 'Salawat', i.e., the Salutation - on him and his Ahl Al-Bayt wherever his name is mentioned1. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily with (every) difficulty (there) is ease (Refer to: 5:3, 5:67.) This is in conformity with the first and second verses of the previous chapter. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when thou hast finished (While concluding the task of the apostleship establish or perpetuate.) (the duties of thy ministry), then thou establish it (Refer to: 28:51.) ! This refers to the instruction to the Holy Prophet, to fix up the one already notified by him at the 'Dawat al-Asheera', (i.e., Ali Ibn Abu Talib). See note on verse 2 above and 5:67, in his place. By the time and wording of the verse 5:67 it gets evident that it was the instruction through this verse, i.e., about appointing Ali as his successor that the Holy Prophet was waiting to execute. The verse 5:67 clearly states ''Convey that which has already been sent down to thee", i.e., appointment of Ali the instructions for which had already been received.The concluding words and the tone of the same verse 5:67 show that…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Sharh:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And unto thy Lord, return with fervour (The guidance to mankind by appointing the successor 'Imam' (guide) and the Maula (guardian) of the people in thy place - which the Holy Prophet did at Ghadir Khumm. Refer to: 5:3, 5:67.) 'Farghab', i.e., get inclined - This was the instruction to the Holy Prophet - When he had finished his work as God's apostle, i.e., completed the duties of his ministry, to fix up Ali in his place and then get ready to return. Note the sublime words in which God expresses His will that the Holy Prophet should retire from this world. There is no mention of death. The instructions are to incline himself, i.e., to return to Him at his own choice and pleasure for it is quite evident from this, that death to the Holy Prophet is not…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ta Seen Meem (T. S. M.) Ta, Seen, Meem, (T. S. M.).Regarding the correct interpretations of these symbol letters refer to note on verse 2:1. Various meanings are said to have been given on various occasions which would be only to suit the individual capacity of the enquirers. Let us be content with what Qummi the famous commentator says that the letters stand for the 'Ism-e-A'zam', i.e., the Greatest Name of God which has been kept a close secret.

item.description: And when called out thy Lord unto Moses saying: "Go thou unto the unjust people (to guide them)?" See 26:7

item.description: The people of Pharaoh; Will they not ward off evil? See 26:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:111 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "What! Shall we believe in thee, while follow thee the meanest (ones)?" This is the common argument of the aristocratic class against the prophets that their followers are commoners. The common answer to their argument is that it is only the deeds of man which make him great or low and not the worldly possession, the account of which is with none but God. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:112 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Noah); "No knowledge have I of what they were doing;" See 26:111

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they have (a charge) against me (of) a crime, and fear I that they may slay me. Moses was brought up in the very palace of Pharaoh.1 Once when Moses saw an Egyptian beating an Israelite, he rendered a blow by his fist to the Egyptian who succumbed to it. Moses escaped into the Midianite country but the charge of slaying the Egyptian was there against him. Moses remembered the charge and feared the vengeance against him. The statement of Moses about the difficulties in his way to proceed against Pharaoh, was not to avoid the commission but only a prayer seeking the aid by Aaron. Note that the Holy Prophet had also to wait for forty years until (an Aaron to him) was given in Ali Ibn Abi Talib. Compare this to the incident how Ali stood and…

item.description: So go unto Pharaoh and say ye both (unto him): "Verily we two are the apostles of the Lord of the worlds!" It is said that for about 400 years the Israelites were subjected to the tyrannies of the Egyptians - Moses and Aaron came to Egypt and stayed there for a year. People taking them to be mad men did not make any mention of them to Pharaoh. Once a jester told Pharaoh that there were two men more foolish than him for they claimed to be the apostles of God. Pharaoh ordered the two men (Moses and Aaron) to be presented to him to ridicule them. Pharaoh recognised Moses.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:195 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: In the language, (Chaste and Eloquent.) plain Arabic. The Holy Qur'an was revealed in the most eloquent language of the Arabic tongue so that those who embraced it immediately might understand it easily and fully and spread it all over the world. The matchless eloquence of the Qur'anic language is a challenging sublimity of the Arabic tongue.1

John 16/14 is the best evidence of this. (A.P.).

It does not mean that Moses was in any way ignorant of the truth for an Apostle is born with the wisdom, duly enlightened with the knowledge of the truth.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So I fled from you when I feared you, then granted unto me my Lord, command, and made me (one) of (His) apostles. 'Hakm' i.e., Wisdom or authority stands for the apostleship and the commission of it.(a) 'You' indicates that Moses did not consider the act against the will of God but against the will of the unjust ruler.(b) God gifted Moses with command and power of judgment, in return for the golden deed of helping the oppressed against the aggressor the man of Pharaoh otherwise all the apostles have the status of prophethood, i.e., being under Divine Guidance from their very birth. (A.P.)

item.description: And warn thou thy relatives of nearest kin. The command to warn the nearest kinsmen was with the idea that when the admonition is given to the very nearest relations of the Holy Prophet, the others in mankind automatically come under the warning. On receipt of this command from God what the Holy Prophet did is recorded in all the basic books of Sunni commentary on the Holy Qur'an and books on the biography of the Holy Prophet and Islam viz. Ma'alim al-Tanzil, Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur, Musnad Ahmad Ibn Hanbal and Riyaḍ al-Naḍra etc. When this verse was revealed, the Holy Prophet called Ali and ordered making a few loaves, with some meat on them and a cup of milk and to invite the sons of Abdul Muttalib. Ali acted as he was commanded and there assembled forty men from…

God's seeing anyone standing or prostrating was no secret for the Holy Prophet to be informed of it. It is a disclosure of the hidden truth for the enlightenment of the people about the divine personal excellence of the soul of the Holy Prophet as well as the purity of his physical body that in its journey from the seed of Adam, the soul of the Holy Prophet passed on only through the channels of the purified loins of godly souls who spent their lives in obedience and devotion to the Lord and never the partnership in his ancestral parentage was polluted by the impurity of polytheism or any fallacy in the worship to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shu'araa:223 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Lend they their ears (eagerly), and most of them are liars. The disbelievers had their own conjectures about the Holy Qur'an. Sometimes they said that it was mere stories of old, sometimes they called it the work of the Devil and sometimes they called it the work of a poet having the enchanting appeal of a poetic melody without much seriousness of the meaning or any reality of the thoughts contained in it. The reference here is to some particular class of poets who indulge in vain and exaggerative expressions misleading and rousing unhealthy passions and not against the art of poetry. The particular persons or the kind of the poets referred to here were - Abdullah Ibn al-Ziba'ra, Abu Sufyan bin al-Harith, Zuhayr Ibn Abi Sulma al-Muzani, and Samir Ibn 'Abd Manaf al-Jumahi.These poets used to compose poetic praise…

See the position and relationship of Ali with…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hasten it on (in challenge) they who believe not in it, and those who believe are afraid of it, and know they that it is the truth; Beware! Verily those who dispute about the Hour (of Reckoning) are far astray. Refer to verse 13:6. Not believing in the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers in their arrogance openly say: "If it has to come let it come" whereas those who believe know that it is a truth and hold it in awe. The disbelievers shall one day come to know how far they had strayed from the right path. A reply to the similar attitude of the disbelievers is given in verse 13:6.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God is Benign unto His servants; Provideth He sustenance to whomsoever He willeth; and He is the All-Strong, the All-Mighty. See 42:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ain. Seen. Qaf. (Y. S. Q.) Ha, Meem (H.M.)Ain, Seen, Qaf (A. S. Q.)These three letters are also a divine mystery known to none but the Holy Prophet and the custodians of his knowledge the holy Imams. What all the others have said about these letters are personal conjectures. The conjectures are the unwarranted interpretations of the mysteries treasured in the Holy Qur'an the knowledge of which has been secured only with the chosen ones, the purified ones of the Lord.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whosoever intendeth the tilth (The life in the hereafter is compared to tilth – As one would sow here so will he reap there. This life as a whole is a sowing season given to every man & woman.) of the hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; whosoever intended the tilth of this world, We give him of (A little.) it, and for him in the hereafter shall not be any share. It is said that those who had joined the battles to earn the reward in the life hereafter, shall have the material benefit, (i.e., the booty) as well as the reward from God, and those who joined the fighting for the truth merely for the material gain, (i.e., the booty) shall have only to be profited by the booty and shall not have anything in the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or for them are any partners (of God) who have prescribed for them any religion which God doth not sanction? And had it not been for the word of decision (to wait until the Day of Reckoning), the decision would certainly have been made between them; and verily the unjust, for them shall be a painful chastisement. If the decree of the Lord had not been passed for a respite to the disbelievers, they would have a painful chastisement.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (On that Day) thou wilt see the unjust alarmed for what they have earned, and (the chastisement for) it shall befall them; And those who believe and do good deeds shall be in the meadows of the Garden (of Paradise); For them shall be whatever they please with their Lord; that is the greatest grace. See 42:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That is of which giveth God the glad tidings unto His servants who believe and do good deeds; Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "I demand not of you (the only believers - Refer to note on verse 25:57.) any recompense for it (the toils of the apostleship) save the love of (my) relatives; (The holy Ahl Al-Bayt, if one loves the holy ones, he will follow them for by following the divines only, man will get himself divined and reach the All-Divine Lord.) and whosoever earneth good, We increase for him good therein, verily God is Oft-Forgiving, the Most Grateful (One)." The 'Ansars' the helpers, i.e., the people of Madina who accommodated the Holy Prophet in his migration from Mecca to their place, used to pride over the 'Muhajirs,' i.e., the emigrants who left their homes at Mecca and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or do they say: "He hath forged a lie against God?" But if God hath willed, He would have sealed thy heart (and quiet thee) and (yet) He would blot out the falsehood and prove (Confirm.) the truth with His words; Verily He knoweth best whatever is in the breasts (hearts) If God only wills it, He could cause the Holy Prophet to be quiet and He could Himself wipe out the falsehood.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He it is Who accepteth repentance from His servants, and forgiveth the sins, and knoweth He whatever ye do, Note the encouragement the sinners in Islam are offered not towards unconditional redemption saying just believe in any one as the son of God who has paid the price of the sins of the world and you are saved, but assuring of the repentance from sinning, being accepted and pardon granted so that a sinner need not be dejected and get hopeless of his being pardoned and thus go on sinning and not amending his conduct. This verse is another assurance that God is He Who is not interested in only punishing His offenders but more than His wrath His mercy always awaits the sinners to turn to Him repentant asking His pardon which He is ready to grant.1Jabir Ibn Abdullah…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He respondeth to those who believe and do good deeds, and increaseth unto them of His grace; And the disbelievers, for them shall be a severe chastisement. To those who amend their character and conduct and do good deeds, and never go near evil, there is the encouragement through the promise of not only the reward of an equal value but more than that, through the infinite mercy and the grace of the All-Merciful Lord.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And should God amplify the sustenance unto His servants, they would certainly rebel in the earth, but He sendeth it down by measure as He willeth; Verily of His servants, He is All-Aware, All-Seeing. It is the every day experience of the world since the advent of mankind in it, that it is only the rich and the wealthy ones and those endowed with power and authority that revolted against God. Hence it is more a warning to those entrusted with wealth and power to be careful against getting astray, 'As He pleases' meaning, as one pleases Him by one's goodness and entitles one's self to His grace.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He it is Who sendeth down the rain after what they have despaired, and spreadeth His Mercy; And He is the (Greatest) Guardian, the (Most) Praised One. God's mercy, grace and bounties come to His creation beyond all calculations of human intellect.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and (the creation of) what He hath spread out in both of them of the animate beings and for their gathering together when He willeth, He is All-Powerful. See 42:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus doth reveal unto thee as (did He) unto those before thee, God, the Almighty, The All Wise. See 42:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whatever befalleth you of a misfortune, it is what your (own) hands have wrought, and (yet) He pardoneth the most of your sins. This refers only to what befalls the sinners as the natural consequence of their own doings. This does not refer to the calamities and the miseries which the apostles and the Imams and the other holy ones meet at the hands of the people while discharging their sacred duties in the world.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ye can not frustrate (God's) will in the earth, and for you (there) is none other than God, Guardian or a Helper. Pardon or punishment to man or to any being, can come only from God and from none else and when it comes, it comes in any measure or without any restriction and none can defeat God in executing His will.This sura is Makki but these four verses are Madani, i.e., revealed at Madina when Hasan and Husayn were born. This fact is proved by the great number of 'Riwayat' detailed narratives from the most reliable authorities on the Islamic history. Even if these verses also are imagined to be Makki there could not be any argument to say that since Hasan and Husayn had not yet been born, the verses could not relate to them, for it is…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And among His signs are the ships in the sea like mountains. Those who can reflect upon the working of the forces of nature in the world, and how much man depends upon God's mercy, can easily appreciate the example given in these verses, for it is one of the most can easily appreciate the example given in these verses, for it is one of the obvious instances of man's helplessness that one experiences in deep waters and in the midst of the high seas when a ship sails safe amidst the mountainlike waves and through the stormy gales and how helplessly it depends upon the favourable winds and tides.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If He willeth, He lulleth the wind that they (the ships) lie motionless on the back of it (the sea); Verily in this are signs for every steadfast grateful one, See 42:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or He may cause them to perish (To sink.) for what they have wrought, and (yet) He pardoneth the most, See 42:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (that) may know those who dispute about Our signs; For them (there) is no refuge. See 42:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whatever ye are given (here) is but a provision for the life of this world, and what is with God is better and more lasting for those who believe and on their Lord they rely; See 42:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who shun the great sins and filthiness, and when they are angry, they forgive; 'Kaba'ir' - Greater or Graver sins viz. Polytheism, Adultery, Drunkenness, Theft etc. The Fifth Holy Imam Muhammad Ibn Ali Al-Baqir says that one who, with the power, authority and means to retaliate, still suppresses his own anger against any one - on the Day of Judgment God would fill his heart with peace and security and he will be safe from the Hell-fire.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who respond to their Lord, and establish prayer, and (conduct) their (Note mutual consultation commended only in the people's own private affairs and not in the affairs of the public and not of the nation as a whole.) affairs with counsel among themselves, what We have provided them with their sustenance they spend, This verse refers to the good-hearted Muslims who while under persecution from the heartless pagans of Mecca, prior to the 'Hijrat', i.e., the emigration to Madina, used to act after consulting each other. The people had assembled in the house of Abu Ayub Ansari and had discussed about their receiving the Holy Prophet on his 'Hijrat', (i.e., emigration from Mecca) - God praises these good-hearted believers who acted after consulting each other. This was when the conversion to Islam had just begun and they were…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (those) who when afflicteth them any great wrong, they get helped by themselves. There are two kinds of people among the believers: Those who overlook and forgive the excesses and aggression against them and the others who take the revenge for the wrongs done to them. The command is that the revenge should never exceed the limits of the wrong done and under no circumstances the retaliation should cross the extent of the offence, and, if any wrong is forgiven and pardoned, it has its own reward with God - for the compensation for it, God has taken it on Himself, which means the reward would be extraordinarily great.The critics of Islam may note the control that Islam imposes even on those who suffer wrongs, i.e., unprovoked aggression against them, far, far away from allowing any one to commit…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: His is whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and He is the Highest, the Greatest. See 42:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the recompense for an evil shall be an ill-return like unto it, but (if) one pardoneth and amendeth, his reward is incumbent on God; Verily He loveth not the unjust. See 42:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whosoever defendeth himself (in avenging) after being oppressed, then against these there is no way (to blame) See 42:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The way (to blame) is against those who do injustice unto the people and transgress (Cross the limits.) in the earth unjustly; these, for them shall be a painful chastisement. Note - Islam's attitude towards unprovoked aggression. None can ever prove that the Holy Prophet, ever in his life-term, conducted or permitted any unprovoked aggression even upon any of his enemy tribes. Every battle fought, was in defence of the faith and the faithful or to frustrate the enemy's plans and plots which were to take the Muslims unawares.This is in case the transgressor being overpowered but by no means the transgressor should be encouraged – as the verse indicates that God loves not the unjust or the transgressors. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed whosoever remaineth patient and forgiveth, verily this is an act of great resolution. See 42:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whomsoever God alloweth to stray, for him (there) shall not be any guardian after it; and thou shalt behold the unjust when they see the chastisement, saying: "Is there any way (to help us) to return" See 42:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thou shalt see them brought unto it humbled of disgrace, looking with a stealthy glance; And shall say those who believe: "Verily the losers are those who lost their selves and their people on the Day of Reckoning." Beware! verily the unjust shall be in a lasting chastisement. See 42:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And there shall not be for them any of the guardians to help them besides God; and whomsoever God alloweth to stray, for him shall not be any (other) way (way out.) (of being guided aright) See 42:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Respond ye unto your Lord ere cometh the Day from God for which there is no averting; for you shall not be any refuge on the Day, and nor for you will it be to make any denial. See 42:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they turn away, then We have not sent thee over them as a watcher; On thee is naught but only to convey ('Balaagh' i.e. To deliver – It may be to deliver the message which is only the apostolic duty and it means also taking one to the end, which is the function of 'Vilayat' Refer to verse 3:67 & 33:6 (A.P.).) (Our Word unto mankind); And verily when We make man taste mercy from Us, rejoiceth he thereby, and if afflicteth them any ill for what have done their (own) hands, then verily man (forgetteth all Our grace and) turneth ingrate. 'Balaagh', i.e., to deliver - it means to deliver the message which is only the apostolic duty and means also taking one to the end, which is apt – which is the function of 'Vilayat'1 Refer…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God's is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth; Createth He whatever He willeth; Granteth He unto whomsoever He willeth females (Only daughters.) and granteth He whomsoever He willeth males, (Only sons.) See 42:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nigh it is (that) the heavens cleave asunder from above (Refers to the relative pronoun 'Whatever' in the previous verse 42:4.) (for the very awe of His glory), while the angels are (there) celebrating (Refer to verse 40:7.) the praise of their Lord and seeking forgiveness for those in the earth; Be it known that verily, God, He (alone) is the Oft- Forgiving, the Most Merciful. The rending asunder of the heavens, signifies God's displeasure and wrath at man's associating any one with Him.The noblest and the purest spiritual beings, which we men can conceive outside the human ranks of God's creation, are the angels, and among the angels, the nearer ones to the 'Arsh' or the Central Seat of the Divine Authority, are those with greater or superior excellence. The pure, noble and venerable abstract beings function one side…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or mingleth (grants both sons and also daughters.) them of both males (i.e., sons) and females (i.e., daughters), and maketh whomsoever He willeth barren; Verily He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful. This may hint to the outstanding examples of Abraham being given only males – Ishmael and Isaac and Zaccharias also having only a son, i.e., Yahya.1Imran having only a daughter – Virgin Mary.2 The Holy Prophet having both sons and a daughter, Lady Fatimah - and Ayesha and the other wives of the prophet's being made barren – and Ali and Fatimah getting both sons and daughters. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And it is not for any man that God should speak unto him save by revelation or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger and to reveal by His permission what He willeth; Verily He is the Most High, the All-Wise. This verse explains the verse 42:4, meaning that even the discourse with Moses was through a medium and not in person, i.e., in the manner mentioned here. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus did We reveal (Thus, in the same manner.) unto thee Our guidance by Our command; Thou didst know (Whatever the Holy Prophet possessed was not his own but that which was only gifted by God. Refer to verse 34:50.) not what the Book (Qur'an) was, nor the faith, but We made it a light, guide We thereby whomsoever We will of Our servants; and verily guideth thou unto the Right Path; 'Rooh', i.e., spirit i.e., the Holy Qur'an which is the Spirit of Truth or the Spirit of the Faith. 'Thou didst not know - what the Book (the Holy Qur'an) was and the Faith was' - meaning that the Holy Prophet knew the contents of the Holy Qur'an in their external and internal meaning but had not yet received the verbal form of it and he did not…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The path of God, Whose is whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth; Be it known! Unto God (alone) shall be referred all affairs. See 42:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who take aught besides God as their guardians, God watcheth over them, and thou art not over them a guardian. (A watcher.) See 42:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thus have We revealed unto thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) an Arabic Qur'an, that thou mayest warn the Mother City (Mecca) and those around (To begin with those around - not to be confined to the particular people or restricted to the area, but the whole around with Mecca as the Centre.) it, and (that) thou warn of the Day of Gathering (The Total Resurrection.) together (the Resurrection), wherein (there) is no doubt; (when) a party shall be in the garden (of Paradise) and a party (shall be) in the burning (Hell) fire. 'Ummul-Qura', i.e., The Mother City in Mecca and 'All around it' i.e., the whole world.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And had God (so) pleased certainly would He have made them a single people, but admitteth He whosoever He willeth into His mercy; and the unjust, for them shall not be any guardian or a helper. See 42:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Ash-Shura:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or have they taken besides Him, guardians? But God, He is the Guardian, and He giveth life unto the dead, and He is, over all things powerful. See 42:7

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the heaven and the Nightly Visitant The mention of the Night-visitant is a mystic expression. There are various interpretations of the word 'Tariq'. Some take it to be a particular star, some say it is the Morning Star, some say Sirius, and some take it to be the star in general for the stars shine in the nights, all through the year.'Tariq' lit. Hammering - figuratively has been used for a visitor at night who knocks at the door by a hammer hanging at it. Furthermore, it has been used for a constant traveller who hammers or tramples the ground at the time. Here as expressed in Verse 3, is used to mean a piercing or shining star. According to a tradition from the Ahl Al-Bayt it refers to a star which traverses all the seven spheres above, one…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then for him shall not be any power, and nor any helper On the Day of Judgment, which will be the day of reality and truth, none shall have any help from anyone else. Everybody for himself. None shall bear the burden of the other1.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the heaven endued with rotation 'Raj', i.e., return. Here the return of the same action or function again and again in a prescribed order or cycle - the return of the monsoonic functions and their relevant changes in the working of the heavenly bodies and the consequent effects on the earth. Though the Firmament above, is always the same yet the change in its function takes place quietly, secretly, smoothly and regularly without any voice of anyone else in the matter save the will of the Almighty Author of the Universe. The revolving and the change in the activities of the heavenly bodies, goes on constantly and it is ever true to its Centre.It indicates the rotational and revolutionary nature of the heavenly bodies. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And by the earth endued splitting (With power or the capacity of recipiency and productivity.) The earth is made amenable to opening itself or yielding to the gushing out of the springs and the sprouting of the vegetation, necessary for every kind of life on earth.Refers to the recipiency and the productivity of the earth. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, it (the Qur'an) is a decisive word The Holy Qur'an is the Final Word of God, complete and perfect to be current for all times until the end of the world for the human race as a whole.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And it is not a jest It is not a collection of mere tales of the ancient people as imagined by the disbelievers1.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily scheme they (against the truth), a scheme It is a reference to the scheming activities among the disbelievers and the hypocrites. The immediate reference is said to be to what the pagans of Mecca did, in their preparation for the battle of Badr. But the reference has the common application also that the disbelievers will always exert to the utmost, plotting to thwart the spread of the truth or to make it totally extinct.God undertakes to Himself to fight the disbelievers and hypocrites, i.e., the enemies of the truth. This indicates the continuous effort against Islam and the perpetual help from God, to save and spread it1.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And I too do scheme (against them), a scheme See 86:15

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So respite thou the disbelievers; let them alone a while Thus, the disbelievers and the wicked ones, are granted a respite. It is the mercy of the Lord that has given a chance for those who reject the truth to reconsider their decision and amend it. At the end, their doom shall overtake them and bring everyone to account individually for each, of the good and the evil, even the motives as well as the deeds.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What will let thee know what the Nightly Visitant is? The query itself suggests the mystic nature of the reference and meaning of it having been kept a secret, and all interpretations being mere conjectures.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It is) the Star of piercing radiance See 86:2

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: There is not a soul is set a Watcher (Refer to: 2:143, 22:78, 16:89, 33:45.) It is only said that it is the star of piercing brightness. It is not said which star - for it is a figurative reference to the great personality. Some commentators take the reference to the First Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abu Talib, for he used to get in communion with the Lord in getting himself absorbed in the All-Divine, in his prayers that Salman and the others had more than once taken him even to be dead. Besides, Ali used to get out in the night enquiring about the needs of the poor and the helpless and help them. It is said that even soul has been preserved or guarded or protected by a number of angels, but for this grace of the Lord…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Let man then reflect, of what he is created See 86:4

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He is created a water (drop) ejected The sperm issued from between the back and the ribs1.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Coming forth from between the backbone and the ribs (Refer to: 36:77, 76:2, 80:19.) The stimulant for the discharge of the matter is generated in the brain and is conveyed through the spinal cord, continued with the Medulla Oblongata. The kidneys thus pissing from the back from between the ribs and the hip bones.The ejected water referred to here, with a mention of backbone (the Spinal Cord) and ribs evidently refers to the part which the breast and the spinal cord play a joint role in the process of the meeting of the sperm and the ovum which result in the formation of the embryo. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, He is Well-Able to resurrect him (Man. Refer to: 85:13.) See 85:12, 36:77 - 36:82, particularly 36:81 wherein is given the greatest argument ''What! Is not He who created the heavens and earth, able to create the like of them? Yes, He, is the Creator (of all) the Knower.'He who created the physical body with all its Psychic forces with the wonderful harmony in the working of the various kinds of forces, can bring back the same at His will.God who caused the union of the sperm and the ovum out of which the most complicated form of an organic being comes into evidence, is naturally able to make a higher complicated soul to proceed towards its Maker by undergoing trial after trial to unfold the possibilities endowed in it. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taariq:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the day when all things hidden shall be tried When asked what are the secrets that will be disclosed, the Holy Prophet said ''All your deeds good and bad, open and hidden" (MS.)

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taghaabun:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Halloweth the Glory of God whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth; His (exclusively) is the Kingdom and unto Him (only) is due (all) praise, and He (alone) is over all things All-Powerful (Refer to Verse 17:44, 61:1, 62:1.) . All praise and gratitude are due only to God and to none else-for it is He and He alone Who has power over all things. This is to inform man that there is none besides God who has any power over the destiny of any one in the universe. Hence every praise or adoration or gratitude should be only to Him and to none else1.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taghaabun:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who disbelieved and belied Our signs, they are the fellows of the fire, to abide therein; and wretched is the destination. See 64:9

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taghaabun:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Afflicteth not any affliction (One who has faith in God is guided by Him as to what to do when facing hardships.) save by the leave of God; and whosoever believeth in God, He guideth aright his heart; and verily God well-knoweth all things. One who has faith in God, is guided as what to do when facing hardships. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taghaabun:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And obey ye God, and obey ye the Apostle! And if ye turn away, then upon Our Apostle is only the clear delivery (of Our Message) (And the warnings.) . See 64:11

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taghaabun:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God, there is no god but He; and upon God (alone) should rely the believers. See 64:11

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taghaabun:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye who believe! Verily of your wives and your children (some are) enemy unto you; wherefore beware (Lest they may deviate you from the right path. Meanwhile you may not adopt a harsh course against them.) of them, and if ye forgive, overlook and cover up (their ills) then verily God is Oft-Forgiving, The Most Merciful. Lest they may deviate you from the right path - Meanwhile you may not adopt a harsh course with them. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taghaabun:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily (ye should know that.) your possessions and your children are only a trial (not the end.) and verily God it is (He) with Whom is a great recompense (Refer to Verse 8:28.) . See 64:14

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taghaabun:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So fear ye (the wrath of) God as much as ye can, and listen ye (unto His word), obey ye (only Him), and spend ye (in His way), it is better for yourselves; and whosoever is saved from the greed of his (own) self, these it is who are the successful ones (Refer to Verse 59:9.) . Some early commentators thought that this passage abrogates the contents of 3:102. While a proper study of both shows that one supports the other. That passage means to be careful of the duty to God as it ought to be and here it says - as much as you can - and nothing ought to be done beyond one's individual ability. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taghaabun:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If ye lend God a goodly loan, He will double it unto you and will forgive you; And God is Most Appreciating, the Most Forbearing (Refer to Verses 2:245; 5:12; 57:18; 73:20; 35:30.) . Re 'Shakoor' thankfulness, but on the part of God it means His appreciating the indebtedness on the part of the receivers of His bounties1.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taghaabun:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Knower of (all things) the unseen and the seen, the Ever-Prevalent, the All-Wise. See 64:17

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Taghaabun:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
