Why didst thou give them leave (to stay behind) until it was manifest unto thee those who spake the truth (Refer to verses 24:62, 8:68, 66:1.) , and thou hadst known the liars. The tone here is the same as that of 66:1. The Holy Prophet is addressed but actually the blame is directed to the third party concerned. And 'Afallahu ank' - God forgive you - is the same expression as 8:68 and it shows that the Holy Prophet had the option of giving the permission. Refer to verse 24:62 and there had not been any prohibitory order prior to the Holy Prophet's action. It indicates the Holy Prophet's anxiety for not exposing the hypocrites, but God in a correct tone condemns them. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They ask not leave of thee, who believe in God and the Last Day (of Judgment) (to be exempt) from striving with their wealth and their selves (Lives.) ; Verily God is the knower of the pious ones. See 9:43

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Only they ask leave of thee (to be exempt) who believe not in God and the Last Day (of Judgment), and their hearts are in doubt, hence in their doubt they are tossed to and fro. See 9:43

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And had they (really) intended to go forth, they would certainly have made preparations for it, but God was averse (Because of their evil intention and their wavering mind.) to their going forth, so He withheld (Left them in the desire for this life.) them and it was said (unto them) "Sit ye (still) with those who sit (idle)." See 9:43

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Had they gone forth with you they would not have added to you aught save mischief (Disturbance - as the others caused the trouble and the loss by running away from the battle fields.) , and they would have certainly hurried about (to and fro) amidst (This indicates that all hypocrites had not remained behind and there were some with the Holy Prophet and their number was considerably great even until 9 A.H. God knows how they disappeared or went underground immediately as the Holy Prophet left this world.) you, to sow dissensions amidst you and among you there are those who hearken for their sake; And God knoweth the unjust. This verse was revealed during the journey to Tabuk when most of the hypocrites had stayed away at Madina with false excuses, but they had sent some of them…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Certainly, did they seek (to sow) dissension before they upset matters for thee, until came the truth and did prevail the decree of God, though they were averse (from it). In Uhud they ran away and in Khandaq they wanted to create chaos and confusion among the Muslims' ranks shouting 'O' people of Yathrib there is no concern for you with them (the Muslims)'. To know as to who were those who ran away at Uhud and the other battle-fields one may refer to any detailed Muslim history.It may refer to the hypocrites lagging behind, not proceeding to the battle of Uhud or the conspiracy of the hypocrites to kill the Holy Prophet on the various occasions after Hunayn, and at the eve of his leaving for Tabuk while he was passing the valley at night and there were Twelve…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Among them there is (many) a man who says, exempt (Permit to stay behind.) me, and try me not; Surely into trial have they already fallen; and verily hell encompasseth the infidels. See 9:48

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So when the sacred months are past then slay the idolaters wherever ye find them, and seize them and besiege them and lie in wait for them in every ambush, then if they repent and establish prayer, and give the poor-rate, then leave their way free to them; Verily God is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful. The fight enjoined here is only against the repeated violation of the treaties by the infidels and the condition to grant amnesty is their repentance for their past conduct and their sincere yielding to God and godliness. This condition was laid against the continuous violation of the treaties by the people and their repeatedly disturbing the public peace and security. The infidels used to attack the Muslims whenever they found an opportunity to do it, and whenever they got overpowered by the Muslims, they…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If befalleth thee (any) good (Success.) , it grieveth them, and if afflicteth thee (any) hardship (Defeat.) , say they "indeed we had taken care of our affair before," and turn they away and they rejoice. See 9:48

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Never shall afflict us (anything) save what God hath decreed for us; He is our (Liege) Lord; and on God should the believers rely." This verse gives that a true believer will always reconcile himself with whatever befalls him as he always depends upon God as his Guardian and helper and none else. The best example of the superb strength of faith and total dependence upon God, can be seen in Karbala.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "What! await ye for us aught but one of the two excellent things (either victory or Martyrdom)? and we await for you that God afflicteth you with chastisement from Himself or from our hands; Then wait ye, Verily we too with you will wait." See 9:51

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "Spend ye willingly or reluctantly never shall it be accepted (Note that charity to any extent without piety and righteousness can be of no avail.) from you; (for) verily ye are (a) transgressing people." This clearly indicates that quantity in charity has no value in view of God. What is counted is the purity of motive and intention. Willingly, here does not mean the willingness for the sake of God, it means, those who are ready to spend but in ungodly manner and the others do not like to spend at all. See next Verse (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And nothing hindereth the acceptance from them of their offerings save that they reject God and His Apostle (Muhammad) and they come not to prayer but sluggishly and spend not (in goodness) but reluctantly. See 9:53

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Let not therefore amaze thee (The Prophet addressed for the people.) , their wealth nor their issues; Indeed, intendeth God (only) to torment them with these (things) in the life of (this) world and that their souls depart while they are disbelievers (Refer to verse 9:85.) . The torture the hypocrites felt about their wealth would be about its hoarding and getting punished for it vide verses 9:34 and 9:35 and about their children they will have to die leaving them behind either to undergo the same miseries as their parents suffered or to join the faithful and strengthen the faith which the hypocrites did not like to do.The very audacity for the accumulation of wealth and the upbringing of their issues with no idea of securing eternal happiness and the spiritual attainments, is a torture and source of worries…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they swear by God that they are surely of you; While they are not of you but they are people afraid (Actually meaning separate - detach - avoid - the reason may be fear.) (of you). See 9:55

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If they could find a refuge, or caves or a place to enter (conceal themselves) therein, certainly would they have turned themselves unto it, rushing thereto (in haste). See 9:55

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of them are those who blame thee with regard to the (distribution of) alms; if they are given from it they are pleased, and if not given to them from it, Behold! they are enraged. This verse was revealed at an incident which Bokhari, Nisai, Ibn Munzir Ibn Jarir Ibn Abi Hatim Abu Sh-shaik and Mardwaih have related from Abu-Sayeed Khidi who said that one day the Holy Prophet was distributing the booty, a man named Hargoos Ibn Zuhair Zulkhoisar at-Tameemi came before the Holy Prophet and criticized the Holy Prophet saying, 'O' Apostle of God - please do justice!' The Holy Prophet replied: 'O' man! if I do not justice who else would do it?' One of the Muslims standing by asked the Holy Prophet to permit him to slay the man. The Holy Prophet said: 'leave him,…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if only they were content with what God and His Apostle had given them and had said: "Sufficient for us is God! Soon will give us God of His grace and His Apostle too; verily unto God (alone) do we (all) turn (in our hopes)" See 9:58

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if anyone from the idolaters seeketh protection from thee, grant thou protection to him till he hears the Word of God (This indicates, how particular Islam is about making people hear the Word of God and giving respite to them to ponder over and understand it. The pagans had to be given security to have approach to it, in utter contrast to the other Scriptures. (A.P.).) , then convey him to his place of safety; This because they are a people who know not. Note the toleration exercised by Islam. It is said that at the proclamation of the verses by 'Ali Ibn Abi Talib, some people in the assembly asked Ali if they will be killed if they go over to the Holy Prophet and enquire about Islam. In reply to the enquiry, 'Ali recited this verse.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily alms are only for the poor and the needy and the workers (The one whose income is insufficient to meet the needs of the daily life. Those with no income at all - None of these terms are applicable to professional beggars (A.P.).) (in the administration of the poor-rate) and those (Those inclined to Truth.) whose heart's alliance is sought and (the ransoming of) the captives, and those in debt, and in the way of God and the way-farer; a duty ordained by God; And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise (Refer to verse 2:273.) . See 9:58

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Among them (Companions and followers. Refer to verses 3:158, 4:115, 8:13, 33:57.) are those who hurt the Apostle (Muhammad) and say they (that) "he is (all)-ear" (i.e., one who believes in everything he hears); say (he Muhammad,) is the Ear (Hearer.) of good for you; he believeth in God and hath faith in the believers and a mercy unto those of you who believe, and those who hurt (Consider here if the Holy Prophet was hurt or pleased with the treatment meted out to the members of his family after his departure from this world - and if those responsible for it come under this or not.) the Apostle of God (Muhammad) for them is a grievous chastisement. It is left to the reader of the Holy Qur'an to apply this verse about those who teased the Holy Prophet and…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Swear they by God unto you that they might please you (The believers.) ; and (whereas) God and His Apostle (Muhammad) hath a greater right that they should please Him, if they are believers. See 9:61

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Know they not that whoso opposeth (Compare this to the violation or acting against the covenant of 'Ghadir Khumm' and the refusal to give pen and paper to the Holy Prophet.) God and His Apostle (Muhammad) verily for him is the fire of Hell to abide therein? that is the grievous abasement. Apply this verse impartially to everyone who defined the Holy Prophet during his life-time as well as after his death. Particularly about those who disputed his command at the parting hours of his life on earth, consequent upon which the Holy Prophet had to turn them out from his presence saying, 'Qoomu-Anni,' Get up ye! and begone! A reference to the Islamic history will show as to who they were and then could be judged their position in the light of the verse.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The hypocrites fear lest a 'Sura (Chapter.) ' should be sent about them declaring openly unto them what is (there really) in their hearts; Say! (This was on the return from Tabuk. It seems that they used to utter such words in mockery. This is an open prophecy that the hypocritic tendency will be exposed by God through trial after trial. Refer to verse 29:2.) "Scoff ye! verily God bringeth forth what ye fear." It is said that this Verse was also revealed concerning these twelve hypocrites1. It is said that Ammar Ibn Yasir and Hudhayfa was then with the Holy Prophet and they repulsed the attack of the Hypocrites by the order of the Holy Prophet and that the Holy Prophet gave the names of all those persons who had disguised themselves as to be Hudhayfa and Ammar. Thereafter…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If ye question them, surely will say they "We were only discoursing and jesting;" Say! What at God, His signs and His Apostles, scoff ye? This indicates the conduct of the hypocrites.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Make ye not excuses, indeed ye have denied after ye had believed; If We pardon a party of you, we will chastise (another) party (of you) for surely, they are the guilty ones. Note - hypocrisy is declared as 'Kufr', i.e., infidelity.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The hypocrite men and the hypocrite women are one (Not by birth but by character as stated in the passage itself.) from another, they enjoin evil and forbid good and withhold their hands (from spending in the way of God); They have forsaken (bypassed forgot.) God, so He hath forsaken them; verily the hypocrites, they are the transgressors. See 9:66

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God hath promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell to abide therein; this sufficieth for them; and God hath cursed them, and for them is the chastisement (which shall be) lasting. See 9:66

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (O' Hypocrites! ye are) Like those (who flourished) before you; they were stronger than you in strength and more abundant in wealth and children; so they enjoyed their portion; thus have ye enjoyed your portion as those before you did enjoy their portion, and ye indulge in vain discourses as those (before you) (in vain) did indulge in; These are those whose works have come to naught in this world and the hereafter; and these are they the losers. See 9:66

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: How can there be a covenant for the idolaters with God and with His Apostle except (for) those with whom ye made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque? So long as they stand faithful to you, then be ye too faithful to them; Verily God loveth those who guard themselves (against evil). Note the regard Islam gives to promises and the covenants, be they with the polytheists – and the stress laid on piety.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! came not unto them the news of those before them; of the people of Noah and 'Ad and Thamud', the people of Abraham and the inhabitants of Midian and the cities over-thrown; came unto them their apostles with clear proofs (of their truthfulness) Thus it was not God to do injustice unto them, but they unto themselves were unjust. See 9:66

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the believer men and the believer women, they arc guardians (Close to one another in the character defined in the verse.) to one another; they enjoin (Make people do good.) good and forbid evil and they establish (the regular) prayer and pay the poor-rate and obey God and His Apostle (Muhammad), These, God will bestow on them His mercy; Verily God is All-Mighty, All-Wise (This is the opposite to verse 9:87.) . It is related in Tirmizi and Nisai that the Holy Prophet told 'Ali Ibn Abi Talib 'O' 'Ali! None will love thee save a 'Momin', i.e., a faithful and none will bear any ill against thee except a 'Munafiq', i.e., a hypocrite.' Some of the companions relate that during the life-time of the Holy Prophet a faithful and a hypocrite was distinguished through the love for 'Ali…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God hath promised to the believer men and the believer women gardens 'neath which flow the rivers, to abide in them, and the excellent mansions in the gardens of 'Adn (Of perpetual bliss.) ' But the good-will of God is the greatest; That is the grand achievement. See 9:71

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' (Our) Apostle (Muhammad)! strive (Fight, war against.) hard against the infidels and the hypocrites, and be severe unto them; and their abode shall be hell; and (what) an evil destination it is (Refer to verses 33:60 - 33:62, 66:9.) . The word 'fahada' means here, fighting with sword, and not striving - for it does not suit the contest at all. The Holy Prophet was already striving to the utmost possible limits. (M.S.).It is related that after the Battle of Tabuk some of the hypocrites had plotted to kill the Holy Prophet and stationed themselves at a particular place. The Angel Gabriel informed the Holy Prophet of this, and those hypocrites were brought arrested by Ammar Ibn Yasir - When produced before the Holy Prophet they said that they only joked. (M.F.A.).Here and in 66:9, the Holy Prophet has…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Swear they by God that they uttered (anything wrong.) not (what they are charged with) (although) they did utter the word of infidelity, and disbelieved after their (embracing) Islam, and they designed (Intended.) what they could not achieve, and they did not seek revenge but because (Not the actual cause of their finding fault but it is the cause of their forgetting themselves and the blessings they had from God and the Holy Prophet - It is a reproachful term.) God and His Apostle had enriched (made care-free.) them by His grace; If they repent it will be good for them, and if they turn back God will chastise them with a painful chastisement in this world and the hereafter; and there shall not be for them on earth any protector or a helper. Tha'laba Ibn Habiba-Ansari who was a…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of them are those who made a covenant with God; "If He giveth us out of His grace, we will certainly give alms and we will certainly be of the righteous ones." See 9:74

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But when He did give them out of His grace, they became niggardly with it and they turned back, averse (Refer to verses 58:12, 58:19.) . One example of the niggardliness in parting from their money was that they refrained to talk to the Holy Prophet privately for a few days when they were ordered to pay a small amount of charity before having interview with the Holy Prophet as mentioned in 58:12 & 58:13. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So in consequence hath He effected hypocrisy in their hearts till the day when they shall meet Him because they had failed to fulfil unto God what they had promised unto Him and because of what they used to lie (continuously). See 9:76

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! know not they that God knoweth their hidden thoughts and their secret whisperings, and that God is the Greatest Knower of (everything) unseen. See 9:76

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who traduce the free givers of charity among the believers and them who find not anything (to give) but their hard earnings, so they scoff at them; God will scoff' at them and for them shall be a painful chastisement. On the occasion of raising funds for the expedition of Tabuk the wealthy ones donated large sums, and the poor ones subscribed their mite. The hypocrites taunted both - in the case of the wealthy they said that they made a show of their wealth and about the poor ones they said that they only brought their small amounts just to be along with the wealthy ones. This verse was revealed to disclose what the hypocrites were doing.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: How (can there be any alliance!) while they overcome you they regard not in you any tie nor of any covenant; They allure you with (the sweet words of) their mouths while their hearts are averse (from you), and most of them are transgressors. See 9:7

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Seek thou (O' Our Apostle!) forgiveness for them or seekest thou not forgiveness for them, (the same will it be); if thou seeketh forgiveness for them seventy times, never will God forgive them; This because they disbelieved in God and in His Apostle (Muhammad!) and God guideth not the transgressing people (For a similar declaration see - 63:6) . This emphatically asserts the futility of the Holy Prophet's intercession and seeking forgiveness for the hypocrites and the infidels. And it is wrong to think that the Holy Prophet wanted to intercede or ask for forgiveness for the hypocrites and the infidels hut God prevented him. The Holy Prophet never does or says anything of his own accord1 . He follows nothing but the Divine Revelation. What is narrated from the Holy Prophet that he said he would increase the number…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Delighted were the ones left behind (in the expedition of 'Tabuk') for their sitting (in-active) behind (After the Holy Prophet had gone on the expedition.) God's apostle and they were averse (Disliked.) from striving (Fighting.) in God's way with their wealth and their selves (Lives.) , and said they (to the others) "Go ye not in the heat;" Say thou! "The fire of Hell is fiercer in heat;" If only they could understand. See 9:80

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therefore, they shall laugh little and weep much (as) a recompense (Consequence.) for what they used to earn. See 9:80

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If God bringeth thee back to a party of them, then they seek thy permission to go forth, say thou "ye shall never go forth with me and ye shall never fight an enemy with me; verily ye chose to sit (idle) the first time, then sit (now also idle) with those who stay behind (This is a prophecy that they shall never have any more chance to march with the Holy Prophet against the enemy, because it was the last battle in which the Holy Prophet himself took part.) ." See 9:80

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And pray (Literally stand not to pray over the body.) thou not at all on any one of them who dieth and nor stand thee ever at his grave; (for) verily they disbelieved in God and His Apostle and died they as wicked ones. Abdullah Ibn Obai was the chief of the hypocrites of Madina. When he fell ill, the Holy Prophet went to enquire about his health. Abdullah requested the Holy Prophet to present him with an old shirt of his for his shroud and desired the Holy Prophet to offer his funeral prayers. Abdullah died. The shirt had already been given away to him and when then the Holy Prophet was standing for his funeral prayers the Angel Gabriel appeared and conveyed this verse and the Holy Prophet stayed away from the prayers. When people criticized about the…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Let not their wealth and their children astonish thee (The people addressed through the Prophet.) ; Verily God only wisheth to chastise them with these (Their belongings.) in this world and that their soul should depart while they are infidels (Refer to verse 9:55.) . See 9:84

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:86 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whenever a 'sura' is revealed (enjoining) that (they should) believe in God and strive (Fight.) hard along with His Apostle; those with abundant means seek thy permission and say, "Leave us (behind) we may be with those who sit (at home)." See 9:84

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:87 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Prefer they to be with those (women children and the sick) who stay behind for a seal hath been set on their hearts there-fore they understand not. See 9:84

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:88 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But the Apostle and those who believe with him strive hard (fight) with their wealth and their selves (Lives.) ; And these, for them are (all) good things; And these, they are the successful ones. See 9:84

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:89 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God hath prepared for them gardens 'neath which flow rivers to abide therein; that is the great achievement. In view of the fact that this is the last Madinite chapter and these and the preceding and the succeeding verses regarding the hypocrites and their aversion to 'Jihad' and the political stand taken by the Holy Prophet, it becomes certain that the number of the hypocrites was on the increase towards the close of the Holy Prophet's ministry and that the day belonged mostly to the aristocratic class, and this attitude culminated after the Hajjjat al-Wida', the last pilgrimage and the covenant at Ghadir Khumm, with their refusal or hesitation to march under the command given to them by the Holy Prophet and when he asked for pen and paper. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They have bartered the signs of God for a small price, so they turn others away from His way; Verily evil is what they do. See 9:7

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:90 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And came with excuses (Seeking excuse.) from the dwellers of the desert that permission may be given to them, and sat (Reference to the hypocrites in Madina.) (at home) those who lied to God and His Apostle; unto those of them who disbelieved shall shortly reach a grievous chastisement (Refers to the people of the tribe of Bani Ghaffar who belong to the major tribe of Asad and Ghatfan who pleaded false excuses for not joining the expedition to Tabuk. Refer to verse 9:86.) . The word 'A'raab' has been used for the dwellers of the deserts, but in the Islamic law it has been extended to include any uncultured, uncivilised person, even a dweller of a city. By culture and civilisation here is meant the Islamic culture and civilisation. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:91 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It) shall not be on (Blame.) the weak nor on the sick nor on those who find not what they should spend, a task when (Provided.) they are sincere to God and His Apostle; And against the doers of good there is no way (to claim); and God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful (The unreasonable excuse of the hypocrites necessitated the regulation as what excuses be accepted & what should not be and who be exempted & who should not be.) . See 9:90

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:92 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nor (is the task) (Jihad.) on those unto whom when they came unto thee to provide them with mounts, thou didst say, "I find not means to carry you;" They went hack with their eyes overflowed with tears sorrowful that they find not means to spend (in the cause). When the expedition of Tabuk was proclaimed seven men of the Ansars came to the Holy Prophet weeping and saying 'O' Apostle of God! We have neither the provisions for the long journey nor any conveyances. Otherwise, we are here to accompany you.' The Holy Prophet replied, 'There is nothing left with me now to provide you with.' He provided only Ibn-Hamir who was one of the seven and he joined the expedition. (M.S.).

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:93 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the way (to charge) is only against those who seek thy permission (to stay behind) while they are rich; prefer they to be with those who remain behind (Women, Children and the sick) and (it is as if) God hath set seal upon their hearts, thus they know not (what they miss). See 9:92

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:94 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They will make excuses unto you when ye return unto them (after the expedition)', Say thou (O' Our Apostle) "Make ye no excuses (now), by no means will we believe you, Indeed God hath informed (Given the tidings about.) us of the matter of (the truth) about you; And now God will behold your doings and (also) His Apostle, then shall ye be returned unto the Knower of (everything) hidden and the manifest, then ye will be informed of (all) what ye were doing." The matter of the actions of men being referred in the ultimate, to God the Knower of the hidden and the manifest is mentioned in 62:8.This also is about the hypocrites who had stayed behind giving false excuses for their not joining the Tabuk expedition. When the Muslims returned from the expedition, they came with all…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:95 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They will swear unto you by God, when ye return unto them, that ye may turn aside from them; so turn ye aside from them; verily they are unclean and their abode is hell; a recompense for what they did earn. It is said in this verse that the oath was only false, and it was taken just to quiet the Holy Prophet and the Muslims against the conduct. The Holy Prophet said: 'He who seeketh the pleasure of God in the pleasure of man, is a true believer and has his reward, and he who seeks the pleasure of man at the east of the displeasure of God, is an outcast of the faith' (viz. conducting or attending entertainments with music, dance, taking false oaths and teasing men etc., which are forbidden by Islam). Imam Muhammad al-Baqir says the…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:96 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They will swear unto you that ye may be pleased with them, but (even) if ye be pleased with them, verily God is not pleased with people (who are) wicked. See 9:95

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:97 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The (rustic) Arabs (of the desert) are very hard in infidelity and hypocrisy, and more inclined not to know the limits what God hath sent (Revealed.) down unto His Apostle; And God is All Knowing, All-Wise. See 9:95

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:98 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of the (rustic) Arabs (of the desert (Bani Tameen, Bani Asad and Bani Ghatfan who did not pay Zakat & whatever they spent it was for mere show - who were stubborn and arrogant.) ) are those who take what they spend to be a fine (A loss.) , and they wait for calamities (Misfortunes.) (to befall) unto you; On them (shall be) the evil calamity; And God is All Hearing, All-Knowing. The tribes of the Sahara viz. Banu Tameem, Bani Asad and Bani Ghatfan who did not pay even the 'Zakat' or the poor-rate and whatever they gave away it was only for a show were very stubborn and arrogant in their infidelity. This is about those of the Sahara who believed and did good for the sake of good and to earn the pleasure of God.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tawba:99 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of the (rustic) Arabs (of the desert) are those who believe in God and the Last Day (of Judgment) and deem what they spend to be (the means of) approach unto God and the prayers (blessings) of the Apostle; Verily it shall be the means of approach for them; soon shall God admit them into His mercy; Verily God is Oft-Forgiving, All-Merciful. See 9:98

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tin:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the Fig and the Olive! The names of the things and the events which have been used in the solemn statements in the Holy Qur'an, are mostly symbols of some latent objects, the knowledge of which God has willed to keep it away from the common minds.'Teen', i.e., Fig, but commentators have given many alternate interpretations which are only conjectures. Ibn-Abbas says i.e., the Fig stands for the Mosque of Noah, and 'Zaitoon', i.e., the Olive, for Jerusalem. 'Balad al-Ameen', i.e., the City of Security, City of the Trusted One the Holy Prophet i.e., Mecca.Fig is known to be the finest, the most wholesome and also the most nutritious fruit used not only as food but a remedy for several bodily complaints. It is taken as a symbol for man's destiny. In its origin, i.e., in its existence, as…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tin:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the Mount Sinai (Refer to: 52:1.) ! 'Seneen', i.e., Sinai - where the Law was given to Moses - See 19:52 and on the Mount Sinai God manifested His glory to Moses and the men who came there asking for the manifestation of God's glory.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tin:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And by this City (declared) Inviolate (Refer to: 14:35, 3:97.) ! 'Balad al-Ameen' - The city of security - Mecca, where the Final Word of God, the Holy Qur'an, had the start of its revelation. But some say 'Ameen' stands for the Holy Prophet - then it will mean the city (Mecca) where the Holy Prophet, the Last Apostle of God, was born. The people themselves called the Holy Prophet as 'Ameen'.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tin:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed, We created man in the best structure 'Ahsan', i.e., the best. 'Taqweem', i.e., the make, the constitution, structure, form, pattern. One who knows the wonderful wisdom with which every part of the human body, with its form, its structure, its faculties and its constitution, which manages the function of each part in perfect harmony with every other and the marvellous faculties, the brain is endowed with, will know the significance of man being referred to in invoking the recognition of the existence of the One with the supreme Wisdom, Power and the Authority who has affected such marvels in the Universe. The make of everything in God's creation is so perfect that there is no room for any change or alternative in it1. Man has been made with such supreme endowments that with the maintenance of these gifts in…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tin:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then We reverted (Rendered.) him to the lowest of the low (Refer to: 25:44, 7:179.) When man, the same wonderful and the great work of the Almighty and All-Wise Providence, loses the equilibrium of his conscience and gets lost into the wrong tracks of low passions seeking the satisfaction of the carnal desires, is thrown in the abyss of degradation and ignominy, and fits himself only for the flames of the hell-fire.The same Almighty and All-Wise Author of the laws of nature, Who creates man with such marvellous and excellent gifts of the wonderful strength of mind and body, again manifests the function of His will on the reverse side of the existence that as man advances in age, after reaching the zenith of the development of the endowed faculties, he begins to deteriorate and is ultimately reduced to the…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tin:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Save those who believe and do good deeds, for them shall be a recompense incessant It is far from real charity to give a thing and take it back. When we give anything to the needy, we do not take it back from them. Would God, having given life to man, take it away from him? No! Man has been created for eternity. He has to work in this world, for the life eternal of his, in the hereafter, to be either in bliss and enjoyment or in misery and suffering. The life in this world is only the chance given to every individual man and woman to prepare or build his or her own heaven or hell. He who believes in the True Lord and does good to others in this life shall get the unending blissful life in…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tin:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (O' Man!) What then can make thee belie after this the Final Judgment? In spite of so much clear evidence given and the doubtless proofs presented, none can ever contradict what the Holy Prophet preached about the Day of Judgment.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tin:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Is not God the Judge of the judges (Refer to: 10:109; 6:57; 2:284; 4:40; 18:49; 21:47.) ? God is the Best of judges to know the truth about each individual being, be that open or concealed. Justice will be meted out to each one according to the individual's merits and demerits. None can ever escape the law of requital which will be strictly followed both in this life as well as in the hereafter.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By (I swear.) the Mountain 'Tur' (Refer to Verse 95:2.) The adjuration is by five things to assert the certainty of future events in the most emphatic terms in verse 7 to 28 - the coming of judgement and the passing away of this phenomenal world; the future ill consequences of ill deeds; and the future attainment of bliss and complete realisation of Allah's grace and mercy as recompense for good deeds.Tur, i.e., The Mount, The Mount Sinai, which stands for all that happened in the ministry of Moses. There is a mention of it in 95:2.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the mountains shall fly an (awful) flight (Refer to Verses 81:3; 77:10; 78:20.) See 52:7

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Woe then that day unto those who belie the Truth (Refer to Verses 70:6 - 70:10; 83:10.) The day of reckoning will be a day of woe to the unjust who belied the signs of Allah, just as it will be a day of joy and bliss to the righteous believers. Every evil thought or deed has its own retributive and punishable chain of consequences. Whatever is done in this life is a preparation for the hereafter, which the disbelievers will find a reality after the day of judgement, not a farce. They did not take notice of the signs of Allah nor paid attention to the warnings the messengers of Allah gave them, so there will be no time for repentance. They will roast in hell, whether they endure it or not.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who, in vain sport (In discourse.) do play The reference is to those who ridicule the warnings about the day of requital, and spend their time in sport and vain amusements, the time which everyone has to avail of, to prepare for himself for the life hereafter specially to give the account of his life, to the Lord.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Day on which they shall be driven unto the hell-fire with a violent drive See 52:12

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: [And it shall be said unto them]: 'This is the Fire (Refer to Verse 36:63.) which ye used to belie' See 52:12

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Is it sorcery then? Or ye see it not? The disbelievers would then be asked, if they now realise that the warnings that the apostles of God, gave them about the Day of Judgment, were not fake or false but truth which they see with their own eyes.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Enter ye into it then be ye patient, or be ye not patient, alike shall it be unto you; certainly, shall ye be recompensed what ye used to do In the worldly punishment one is punished for an act but in the natural punishment one receives, which one does here, i.e., the final shape of what the actions assume (A.P.).The righteous believers will be in the land of eternal bliss. By their own effort and striving they won Allah's grace and mercy.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the pious ones shall be in the gardens (Of Paradise.) amidst the bounties (therein) Everyone, as an individual, will have full satisfaction (in whatever he or she does) dignity and joy of companionship. Every one will be purified but will not be merged into one sameness.There will be a general social satisfaction shared with all whom they loved in this earthly life, all near and dear ones, provided they had believed and done good deeds, because each individual is responsible for his conduct and none shall bear another's burden, as stressed in 2:48, 2:123, 2:254; 6:164; 17:15; 35:18; 39:7 and 53:38.Relationship of this life has no value in the hereafter unless it is sanctioned by the ties of true faith.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Rejoicing in what gave them their Lord, and saved them their Lord from the chastisement of the Hell See 52:17

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It will be said unto them)'. "Eat ye and drink ye in health and delight for what ye used to do'" See 52:17

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the Book written The Book inscribed 'The Secured Tablet' called the Lawh al-Mahfooz., Some commentators mean the Holy Qur'an and some others mean Torah which was given to Moses on the Mount Sinai, inscribed on Tablets of Stone.With the exception Tur which clearly refers to Mount Sinai- The rest of the references are to things not terrestrial. The written Book in the lustrous sheet, refers neither to Torah nor to Qur'an nor either to other Scripture in its revealed form. Therefore, the Book will refer to whatever is inscribed on 'Lawh al-Mahfooz', on the Secured Tablet (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Reclining on thrones ranged; And We will unite (Make their offsprings follow them in their goodness thus multiply or add the reward of one with that of the other, for both of them.) them with Huries (maidens pure) with large (lovely) eyes (Refer to Verses 37:48 - 37:49; 44:54; 55:56; 55:72 56:22; 56:35 - 56:37.) Though the Hoor or the Ghilman, would not be the beings, same as the imperfect, impure and the mortal human beings of this life, they are beings, purity and beauty embodied who could not be aptly explained with comparison to anything in this world which could not be compared to that of the hereafter. Make their offspring follow them in their goodness1.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who believe and follow them their offspring in faith, We will unite (Make their offsprings follow them in their goodness thus multiply or add the reward of one with that of the other, for both of them.) with them their offspring and We will lessen not unto them aught of their (good) deeds; Every man shall for what he hath wrought, be responsible (Refer to Verses 53:39; 74:38.) Note the doctrine of the personal responsibility of every individual man or woman – None shall bear the burden of the other - This aspect of the individual responsibility, the realization of which is essential to make man live a strictly controlled and perfectly cautious life, is repeatedly stressed as in 2:48, 2:123, 2:254; 6:164; 17:15; 35:18; 39:7 and 53:38.Clearly asserts that mere relationship in this life is of no…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We will provide with fruits and flesh of what they desire (What they would be pleased to have. Refer to Verses 56:20; 56:21.) See 52:21

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They shall pass therein to one another a cup (Of drink which would not corrupt the mind or affect the health) wherein shall not be any vanity nor a sin (Refer to Verse 56:25.) See 52:21

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And there shall go around them (serving them) youths (handsome) as if they are imbedded pearls (Refer to Verses 56:17; 76:19.) See 52:21

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And some shall accost the others making mutual enquiries See 52:21

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They will say: 'Verily we feared ere (this) in regard to our families' See 52:21

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But God hath bestowed His grace on us, and He hath saved us from the chastisement of the scorching wind See 52:21

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, we used ere this to call upon Him; Verily, He is the Benign, the Most Merciful See 52:21

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So thou remind on (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) for thou, by the grace (Bounty.) of thy Lord (on thee), art neither a soothsayer, nor a mad man See 52:21

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On a lustrous Parchment outstretched The Scroll unfolded is The Holy Qur'an, which is unfolded by a revelation for the benefit of mankind as a whole and for all times.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or say they (about thee O' Our Apostle!) 'A poet (is he)! Let us wait (What the people said.) for him (The Holy Prophet.) some fatal adversity (Death.) (drawn) by time!' See 52:21

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!). "Wait ye, and verily I too with you am of those who wait' (Refer to Verses 9:15 and 9:52.)" See 52:21

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or is it that bid them their deliberations, to do this, or are they an inordinate (Rebels.) people? See 52:21

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or say they (that): 'He (The Holy Prophet.) hath forged it (the Qur'an)? Nay! they believe not (Refer to Verses 69:41 - 69:47.) ' See 52:21

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Let them then bring a dis-course like unto it, if they be truthful (Refer to Verses 2:23; 10:38; 11:13.) Of all the religious scriptures of the world which claim to be heavenly or sacred in any other way, the Holy Qur'an is the only Scripture which has repeatedly challenged its disbelievers to bring a part of its kind and about 1400 years have elapsed and yet none could reply to it. This is one of the living miracles of the Holy Qur'an that its text is inimitable, even from the literary aspect of its beauty and superiority and none could corrupt it nor effect any change in its arrangement1.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or were they created by nothing? Or are they themselves the creators? (See note on the Existence of God in the introduction.) The disbelievers are asked that if they believed, that they had been created without a Creator or without any purpose.This lays the fundamental axiom which is one of the and scientific propositions are based - that an effect of a phenomenon or by itself (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or created they the heavens and the earth? Nay! they have no certainty (Firmness of belief.) See 52:35

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or with them are the treasures of thy Lord, Or hold they the absolute authority? See 52:35

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or for them is a ladder by which they can (climb up into the heaven and) listen (to the angels)? Then let the listener of theirs bring a proof manifest Or is it that they have any ladder to get into basic foundations on which all philosophic cannot come into being out of nothing heaven to know the secrets1.This applies to those who claim that besides the logical method of the approach to the moral, social and theological problems, they have special ways of direct communion or direct touch with the divine sources. Claims of such nature have no value unless it is supported by clear and irrefutable evidence, such as miracles (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or for Him are daughters and for ye sons? (Refer to Verses 16:57; 43:16.) See 52:38

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And by the House (The Ka'bah.) populated (Visited by frequent worshippers.) Bayt al-Ma'mur (the much-frequented house), the Holy Ka'ba, which is always full of the visitors, the pilgrims, on all days of the year, the Ka'ba which was cleared of the idols in it by the Holy Prophet (S) and Imam ''Ali ('a) and re-dedicated to the worship of the One True God.Some commentators say that by the word 'Bayt', i.e., house, it means the 'Bayt al-Ma'mur' a place of adoration for the heavenly bodies.So, 'Bayt al-Ma'mur' does not refer to any terrestrial sacred place of worship none of which is ever filled with worshippers all the days of the year; but it refers to the heavenly place of worship as narrated by ''Ali Ibn Abi Talib ('a): "The heavenly place of worship which is visited every day by a…

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or thou asketh of them any recompense, that they are burdened with the weight of debt? (Refer to Verse 68:46.) See 52:38

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or with them is the unseen that they write it down? (Refer to Verse 68:47.) See 52:38

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or intend they to lay (Scheming.) snares for thee? But those who disbelieve are themselves the snared ones See 52:38

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or for them is a god other than God? Hallowed is God from what they associate (Creating equals to Him - False Gods - Worshipping angels as the daughters and Jesus as the Son of God.) (with Him) See 52:38

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they see a portion of the heaven coming down, they would say: '(they are) clouds piled up (Refer to Verse 26:187.) ' See 52:38

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Leave them then until they encounter the Day of theirs where-in they shall be smitten (With Thunderbolt.) (with terror) to swoon (Refer to Verse 39:68.) See 52:38

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: A day wherein their devices shall avail them not aught, nor shall they be helped See 52:38

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily for those who did injustice there shall be a chastisement besides that, but most of them know it not See 52:38

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And wait thou patiently for the command of thy Lord, for verily thou art before Our (Purview.) eyes, and celebrate thou the praise of thy Lord when thou risest (Thus, every act of the Holy Prophet will be the view of the Lord. Refer to Verses 50:39 - 50:40.) See 52:38

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And in the night too, celebrate thou His Glory and at the setting of the stars About spending a part of the night in prayer, see Verses 17:78 - 17:79. And at the setting of the stars, see Verse 113:1.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And by the Roof (Refer to Verses 16:26; 21:32.) elevated (Something beyond the physical expanse.) "The roof elevated" is the canopy of heaven, to whose height or sublimity no limit can be assigned by the mind of man. The nebular ocean refers to the beyond physical expanse. Except Tur, all above-noted signs or things are celestial.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And by the Sea (Refer to Verses 40:72; 81:6.) boiling The Nebular Oceans within the heart of the earth, within the suns - and the other heavenly bodies (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the chastisement of thy Lord shall indeed come to pass Verses 7 to 10 illustrate with the solemnity the reference to the above great things of wonder which are facts, the coming Doom from God also, is assured as a reality which shall come to pass.

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: There is none to repel (Refer to Verse 70:2.) it See 52:7

item.title: bil-Quran: At-Tur:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the Day (The happenings on the eve of the Resurrection for the Final Judgment.) when the heaven shall reel a (Terrible) reeling (Refer to Verses 82:1; 84:1.) See 52:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zalzala:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When the earth shall quake with her (terrible) quaking (See 70:7 - 70:9.) These verses 1-4 refer to the violent effects of destruction and disaster the earth will suffer on the Day of Judgment. See Chapter 88.The whole earth will be quaked and getting reduced to nothing bursting and throwing out all its contents, even the heaviest of them.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zalzala:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the earth bringeth forth her burdens See 99:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zalzala:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And man shall say: ''What hath happened to her (Earth.) ? Since the disaster will overtake the world all of a sudden, the sudden upheaval and the uprooting of the mountains and the strongest structures on earth and the convulsion of the earth as a whole will only confound man who will be plunged into a terrific surprise.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zalzala:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On that day she shall relate her news (about all that happened on her) The earth will declare aloud what all had happened on it.Tamim Ibn Hatim says ''Once we went to Basra and while we were about to camp, a quake of earth was felt. We were all panicky, but Ali got down from his camel and placing his hand on the ground addressing the earth, said, 'What hast happened to thee.' The quaking stopped.Lady Fatimah reports that once in Madina an earthquake was felt and the people got panicky and rushed to Abu-Bakr and Omar who took the whole multitude to the door of Ali and Ali came out with perfect peace of mind and took the people outside Madina and sitting on a mound, addressed the huge crowd and asked them, saying, ''Ye are panicky at this…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zalzala:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That thy Lord hath revealed unto her (Earth – See note.) The word of command from the Almighty Lord would have brought the dissolutive and disastrous effect and the deeds done openly or secretly will be laid bare in the full light of the day.'Wahi' or the revelation or instruction or command need not always be through an angel1.This verse indicates the extent of the divine revelation and that even the earth shall have some sort of receiving the revelation. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zalzala:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On that day shall come out people (from their graves) in (scattered) groups, to be shown their own deeds (Refer to: 82:4 - This is the first stage of the total resurrection.) Since the day of the Final Judgment will be the day of sorting out the good and the evil stuff in humanity - the dead will be divided into groups of good and bad according to the various levels of their merits and demerits, and rising from their graves, rush to see to know what is there for them by way of their own earning in this world, in the records of their own deeds1.This is the first stage of the Total Resurrection. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zalzala:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then he who hath done an atom-weight of good shall See it (Note: - What a great encouragement. Refer to: 55:60.) Note: how man is warned of the strictness with which he will he dealt with in the accounting for his deeds. Even the smallest deed, good or evil, will not escape the accounting and will be duly recompensed, and no one will be able to bear the burden of the other1.In this state every individual will realise his own deeds - good or bad - and the last stage of the resurrection is the judging of the actions, as a whole, i.e., the last stage of 'Shafa'at al-Kubra'.These verses have been taken as to signify that our action here, assumes concrete forms on the resurrection day, causing pleasure or pain. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zalzala:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And he who hath done an atom-weight of evil shall see it (Note: - What a great Warning - Refer to: 55:60.) See 99:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ha. Mim. (H. M.) See 43:2

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He Who made for you the earth (as) a cradle (Or a couch.) and hath made therein ways for you that ye might be guided aright. See 43:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He Who sendeth down water from the heavens in a measure; then raise We with it a country which is dead (dried), even so shall ye be brought forth (from your graves on the Day of Resurrection) See 43:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He who created pairs in all things and made for you of the ships and the cattle that ye may ride on, See 43:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That ye may mount (Settle – Take position.) on their backs, then remember ye the bounty of your Lord, and when ye mount (Settle – Take position.) on it and say ye: Hallowed is He Who subjected this unto us, and we (by ourselves) were not able to attain (Capable of Subjugating or Subduing them or making them yield to us.) this, Settle - take position - 'Istawa' means to dominate - to mount - to take an equidistant position, i.e., Central - In no place has been used in the sense of mere sitting.This is the actual sense of the 'Istawa', i.e., dominance.Capable of subjugating or subduing them. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily We, unto our Lord, shall return, (Are returning.) See 43:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (yet) they assign (Man generally ascribes some human aspects to the Absolute.) unto (some) of His servants a partnership with Him; Verily man is an open ingrate! Generally, asserts that some human aspects for the absolute. So it is anthropomorphism in some way or other, in crude or a refined way, it is very difficult for man to escape from that tendency - this is the reason that Qur'an insists that nothing should be attributed to God but that which has been revealed. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Hath He taken daughters (Refers to the heathens regarding the angels as the daughters of God and worshipping them.) (unto Himself) of what He hath (Himself) created, and chosen you to have the sons? Since the people held the female sex in contempt, they ascribed daughters to God saying that the angels were the daughters of God. To assign daughters or to imagine God having wives or any issues, is most abominable with God and a blasphemy most abhorred by Him.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when the news (Of the birth of a daughter to themselves - they hated to have daughters - used to bury them alive.) is given unto anyone of them of what he setteth up a similitude unto the Beneficent (God) his face becometh darkened (With sorrow.) and he is choked with rage. The disbelievers used to assign daughters to God but when they were informed of a daughter born to them, their complexion used to get turned black in their sorrow and disappointment and they were filled with rage.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! the one (Refers to the idols bedecked with ornaments – unable to speak.) which was brought up amidst ornaments and in disputes can make not itself plain (to be associated with God)? The reference to idols which when bedecked with ornaments and fixed for worship, could not answer any criticism against them - and yet they were adored as gods and goddesses.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And make they the angels who are the servants of the Beneficent (God) - females (deities); What! did they witness their creation? Their witness shall be written down and they shall be they questioned. See 43:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By the Book Manifesting, By the Book (the Holy Qur'an) which makes manifest and plain the truth and the laws of the human discipline on earth. This verse and the similar other verses clearly indicate what was revealed or given to the Holy Prophet was a Book in its fullness, not mere verses for the people to put it into a book form.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "If had willed the Beneficent (God) we should not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of this; they do but guess. See 43:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or have We given them a Book ere it that they hold fast (hold fast the Book in their arguments.) unto it? See 43:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! say they: "Verily we found our fathers on a creed (a way distinguished.) and verily by their footprints are we guided" See 43:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thus, We sent not ere thee in any town a warner, but the luxurious (Those who indulge in luxury and ease.) of it said: "Verily, we found our fathers on a creed, and verily, of their footprints we are the followers" See 43:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (that warner): "What! even if I bring you a guidance better than that on which found ye your fathers (will ye not believe)?" Said they: "Verily we are disbelievers in whatever ye (The apostles.) are sent with". See 43:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So We did retribute them, and behold thou how was the end of those who belied (Our apostles). See 43:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (remember thou) when said Abraham unto his father and his people: "Verily I am free (Arabic 'Bara'un'. This is 'Tabarra'.) of what ye worship," See 43:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (I worship) but (only) Him Who created me, for verily He will guide me. See 43:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And he (Abraham.) made it a word (doctrine) (The unity of God - in the sense of rejecting all deities and submitting only to God.) to continue (Lasting .) in his progeny that they may return (unto God). The 'Word', i.e., the knowledge about the Unity of God which he left behind him hoping his progeny to preserve the faith in it.(a) Indicates that the doctrine of the Unity of God shall remain in the seed of Abraham for ever. In the lineage of the Holy Prophet, all were monotheists.(b) Of the Unity of God - in the sense of rejecting all deities and submitting only to Him. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! I did provide these and their fathers to enjoy until there came unto them the truth (the Qur'an) and the Apostle (Muhammad) manifesting (the truth). See 43:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an that ye may understand. The Holy Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic language so that the people to whom it was first conveyed might understand the truth fully and then convey the same to mankind in the other parts of the world.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when came unto them the truth (the Qur'an) said they: "This is a sorcery, we are disbelievers in it" See 43:28

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "Why was not this Qur'an sent down unto a man in the two cities, (Mecca and Taif the two important cities of the land.) (who is) great ?" (Some prominent i.e. man of political or tribal position or importance. See verses 2:247 & 4:54.) This is what the people said that if the Holy Qur'an was in fact the Word of God, it ought to have been given to any one of the leading persons in wealth in Mecca or Taif and not to a poor man like the Holy Prophet who did not own any wealth and comforts. So degenerated had become the tastes of the people that moral greatness and spiritual excellence had no value at all with them.These passages show the amount of the importance attached to the worldly position by the majority of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! do they distribute the mercy of thy Lord? (It is) We Who did distribute among them (even) their livelihood in the life of this world, and We did raise some of them above the others in rank, so that some of them may take the others in subjection; (For the purpose of serving each other, to maintain discipline in the practical life.) and the mercy of thy Lord is better than whatever they hoard. (Wealth.) God does not commission any one with His apostleship on the merit of owning any material wealth in this world but according to the personal excellence He Himself grants to the individual Himself conditioning the person for the purpose. To the disbelievers, wealth is the criterion of greatness but with God, what value or worth any amount of wealth could ever have when the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And were it not that all people had been (Become.) of one (evil) way of life, We would certainly have provided those who disbelieve in the Beneficent God, (to make) for their houses, roofs of silver and the stairs on which they ascend, Had it not been misleading to the people, God would have granted so much of gold and silver to the disbelievers that they could have made their abodes with their roofs, of gold but then people would have thought the bestowal of the wealth, to be the reward for the wrong ways of the disbelievers and all of them would have joined the disbelief and had gone away with them from the right path.Here it is pointed that even the distribution of the worldly position and fortunes is done by God just to create ranks to test…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the doors of their houses, and the couches on which they recline, See 43:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And ornaments of gold; But all these are only the provision of the life of this world; And the hereafter (Spiritual position - Status – gain – bliss.) unto thy Lord is for the pious ones. And what is with God, as the reward for the pious and righteous, is more than what human imagination could conceive.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whosoever is blinded against the remembrance of the Beneficent (God), for him We appoint a satan and he shall be his close companion. (Associate. Refer to verse 41:25.) He who avoids remembering God, is naturally going on adding to his evils. The First Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abi Talib says 'He who goes on sinning gets blind at heart.' When one leaves the society of God Satan naturally gets free access to the individual. It is to keep man necessarily in communion with the Lord the minimum course prescribed for man is the regular offering of the five times daily prayers.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily (the satans) turn them away from the (right) path, and deem they that they are guided aright. The worst is that man maddened by evil, thinks that he is on the right path and there is no harm in whatever evil he commits, whereas every step of his, takes him farther away from the right course, and nearer to perdition.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Until when cometh he unto Us, he would say: "(O' Satan!) would that between me and thee there were the distance of two Easts!" (The relative value of the term - East and West.) (what) an evil companion is (Satan)! This is what on the Day of Judgment, the victims of Satan would say.The use of Two Easts – for east and west implies the relative value of the term east and west (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And never shall it profit you on this day, since ye did injustice, that ye be partners in the chastisement. See 43:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily it is in the Mother-Book (which is) with Us, Most Exalted (The same attribute. Refer to verse 42:51.) (it is), full of Wisdom. 'Ummul Kitab' the Mother Book, i.e., the Secured Tablet from which gets out all knowledge.1 The Opening Chapter is also called the 'Ummul Kitab' for it contains in essence, the whole matter of the Holy Qur'an in a nutshell, i.e., the Original Source of the Holy Qur'an. It also means that the original of this Holy Book is secured and none can ever make it extinct.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Canst thou then make the deaf hear or guide the blind (The arrogant ones who would neither listen to nor see the facts - thus deaf and blind at heart.) and him who is manifestly astray? Guidance is God's grace and mercy and it comes only from God and not at the will of even the apostles.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Even if We take thee away, then verily shall We extract retribution from them Ibn Mardwaih reports from Jabir Ibn Abdullah Ansari that the Holy Prophet said that this verse is about Ali who after the Holy Prophet would fight and punish the treacherous ones who violate the covenant of faith they had entered into.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or We shall show thee that which We have promised them for verily We are over them (fully) Powerful. See 43:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therefore, hold thou fast what hath been revealed unto thee, Verily, thou art on the Right Path. Jabir Ibn Abdullah Ansari reports that after returning from the 'Hajjat ul-wida' (i.e., the Last Haj) the Holy Prophet used very frequently to admonish and warn the people about holding fast to the command of Ali as set up at Ghadir Khumm where the Holy Prophet under the command from God had declared 'Of whomsoever I am the Lord, this Ali is his Lord'1 on the declaration of which, depended the completion of the mission of the apostleship of the Holy Prophet and the perfection of the faith as a duly regulated religion for mankind.2 The concluding words of the verse indicate that to acknowledge Ali in the place of the Holy Prophet and to follow him is the right path.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily, it is a reminder (Imminence.) for thee and for thy people, and ye shall soon be questioned (about it). The question would be as to how much the Holy Qur'an was honoured in practice, in the daily life. The Fifth Holy Imam Muhammad Ibn Ali Al-Baqir and also (the Sixth Holy Imam Jafar Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq said, "Zikr is the Holy Qur'an and we are those who would be questioned about." (MS.)According to 'Tha'alabi' one of the renowned Sunni Commentators, the Holy Prophet said that 'On the night of Mi'raj (Ascension) when I was in the heavens among the souls of the apostles of God, and angels, at the command of God desired me to ask the apostles with what basic object they had been sent into the world. When I asked them, they all unanimously declared, saying,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And ask thou those of Our apostles We sent before thee: Did We appoint besides the Beneficent God any gods to be worshipped? See 43:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed sent We Moses with Our signs, unto Pharaoh and his chiefs, and said he: "Verily I am the apostle of the Lord of the worlds" (Refer to verses 7:104, 7:130 - 7:136.) See 43:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when came he unto them with Our signs, lo! they laughed at them, See 43:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We showed them not a sign but it was greater than the other, and seized them with chastisement, that they may return. See 43:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said they: "O' sorcerer! Call on for us thy Lord, (to do) as he hath covenanted (to remove the destructive signs. Refer to verses 7:132 - 7:135.) with thee; verily we will be guided aright." See 43:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Shall We then turn away from you the Reminder wholly for ye are a people extravagant? 'Reminder', i.e., the Holy Qur'an.Since the people ridicule the apostles and reject their messages, should God also be unmerciful and refrain from revealing His word which, if a few of the people did not like it, others would surely be benefited, and if one generation does not avail of it duly, the other one might do it.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But when We relieved them from the chastisement, lo! they broke the pledge. See 43:44
