item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And proclaimed Pharaoh unto his people: "O' my people! is not the kingdom of Egypt mine? And these rivers flow below me; What! behold ye not?" See 43:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! I am better than this (fellow) who is contemptible, and who scarce can speak distinctly? (Make plain. Not that there was any defect in his vocal system. (A.P.).) See 43:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And why have not then bracelets of gold been put upon him? Or (why have not) come with him angels as (his) companions? See 43:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus, did he persuade his people to levity and they obeyed him; verily they were a transgressing people See 43:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when they had angered Us, We did retribute them, so did We drown them all together, See 43:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We made them a precedent and an example for the later generations. This is just to compare the similarity between the people of Pharaoh and the people of Mecca - attaching importance to temporal power and possession and ignoring the spiritual side of the life and the life hereafter.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when was set forth (Jesus) son of Mary as an instance (of Our power), lo! thy people laughed out (in ridicule). Power and righteousness - Pharaoh was the instance of wickedness - resulting in invoking wrath of God - Jesus an example of the divine blessings manifested in his ideal righteousness. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "Are our gods better or is He?" (God.) They do not set it forth unto thee but by way of disputation; nay! they are a contentious people. See 43:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: None was he but a servant (of Ours), bestowed We on him (Our) favour (In the same manner as in verse 4:69.) (giving him the miracles); and We made him an example (of Our power) unto the children of Israel. With the unusual mode of his birth and his miraculous disappearing, as in the case of the last saint in the seed of Ishmael, the Last Imam, Muhammad Ibn Hasan al-Mahdi shares his grace as they would resemble each other in their miraculous reappearances - the former following the lead of the latter.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And how many did We send of Our prophets among those gone before. (The ancients.) See 43:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And had We pleased, certainly We could have made from among you angels to be in the earth (your) successors. (To succeed their lands.) See 43:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily he shall be the sign of (approach of) the Hour (of Reckoning), doubt not then about it and follow Me: This is the Right Path. 'The Hour', i.e., the Day of the Final Judgment, Jesus shall be the sign for the dawn of the Day of Judgment. Just before the Day of the Final Judgment, Jesus shall descend from heaven and destroy the idols in the churches which people have established in his name and break the cross and abolish once for all the false doctrine of trinity and prepare the way for the universal acceptance of the doctrine of the Unity of God as founded by the Holy Qur'an. There are the other details about all that Jesus would do after his second advent into this world.According to most of the early commentators, the pronoun 'he' refers…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And let not satan prevent you, (The people.) verily he is your open (Refer to note on verse 36:60.) enemy. See 43:61

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when came Jesus with clear proofs (miracles), said he: "Indeed have I come unto you with wisdom, and that I may make clear for you some of those things of which ye differ in; so guard ye (yourselves against evil) and obey me." See 43:61

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily God (alone) is my Lord and your Lord, so serve ye (only) Him; This is the right path. "Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and Him only shalt thou serve."1

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But differed parties from among them, so woe unto those who were unjust, from the chastisement of a painful day. See 43:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Wait they for aught but the Hour (of Reckoning) to come on them suddenly while they perceive not? See 43:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The friends that day shall be enemies to one another, save the pious ones. The partners in the evil ways in this world who think themselves to be the friends of each other in this life, would on the Day of Judgement condemn each other whereas the pious would naturally feel increased in joy when they meet each other in the rejoicing.The Sixth Holy Imam Jafar Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq gathered his devotees the Shias and reciting this verse commanded them to seek the friendship of the pious even if they be found in the darkest part of the earth. But to know as to who the perfect ones of the 'Muttaqin' the pious ones are1 and for the position of the pious with God.2Refer to note on verse 23:101 & 15:45 - 15:48 and the saying of the Holy Prophet…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' My servants! No fear shall be on you this day, nor shall ye grieve. See 43:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who believed in Our signs and were Muslims (those submitting themselves unto God). See 43:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And there came not unto them a prophet but at him they used to mock. See 43:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Enter ye the Garden, ye and your mates; ye shall be made to be delighted. (Rejoicing.) See 43:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Shall be passed round unto them dishes of gold and cups (of drinks); and therein shall be whatever desire their souls, and (wherein) could delight the eyes; and ye shall abide therein. The purpose of Qur'an enumerating the details of the sensual pleasure, is to bring home and assert the fact that in the life hereafter, none of the senses of any individual, are lost but are developed and sharpened - so each will have the object desired by it the most, as the verse says and the weakest1 will suffer for being deprived of the realisation of the objects of their senses. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This is the Garden (Paradise) ye are made to receive as a heritage (in recompense) for what ye have been doing. See 43:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For you therein are fruits in abundance of which ye shall eat. See 43:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the guilty ones, in the torment of Hell, they shall abide. See 43:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It shall not be abated from them, and they therein shall be despairing. See 43:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We were not unjust unto them, but (it was) they (who) were unto themselves unjust. See 43:71

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they shall cry out: "O' Malik! would that thy Lord maketh an end of us!" He shall say: "Verily ye shall remain (here)." It is said that when the fellows of the Hell-fire would feel the torment therein as unbearable they would cry out to 'Malik' the angel in charge of Hell to pray to God to kill them once for all. But he would reply 'Ye have been convicted to remain thus in Hell.'1

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed have We brought unto you with the truth but most of you unto the truth, were hateful. See 43:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or (Either ye hated or did devise plots.) have they settled any device (among themselves)? then verily We too shall be the settlers (of Ours). See 43:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then We did destroy those mightier than these in strength, and hath gone (such) examples among those gone before. See 43:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or think (Or used to think Refer to verse 45:29.) they that We hear not their secret and their concealed discourses? Aye! (We do hear everything) and Our messengers (The angels.) unto them do write down (everything). See 43:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "If there be for the Beneficent God any son, I am (to be that (If God had to adopt any one as His son, it would have been the Holy Prophet Muhammad for he is the First and the foremost of God's creation and the first to worship Him. Refer to note to verse 43:81.) for I am) the first of the worshippers (to Him)" If there had been any son of God, the Holy Prophet being the greatest servant and the chosen one of God even among His apostles, would have been the first to serve that son. But far, far away is God's having any son for Him. As the verse 39:4 clearly says that if God had chosen to have any son for Him, the Holy Prophet Muhammad would have been chosen…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hallowed is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of 'Arsh', (The throne of Supreme authority.) far from what they attribute. See 43:81

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So leave them to plunge on, and sport (into vanities of falsehood) until meet they their day which they have been promised (warned with). See 43:81

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He it is Who is God in the heavens and God in the earth; and He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing. See 43:81

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Holiest is He Whose is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them two, and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour (of Reckoning), and unto Him shall ye all be returned. See 43:81

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:86 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those whom they call besides Him, own not any power of intercession, save he who beareth witness of the truth and they know (the truth). Those who deny the doctrine of intercession for the repentant sinners may note the condition laid down in this verse. He who Bears Witness by surrendering his own soul to the Lord, i.e., a martyr in His way shall own the right to intercede. And who else could be greater than Husayn the King of Martyrs, the Greatest Bearer of witness to the truth, whose severed head bore witness glorifying the Lord even from the point of the lance.This verse lays down the criteria for the right or the qualification to intercede. The readers should refer to all the references given here1. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:87 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if thou ask them who created them, they would certainly say: "God". Whence are they then deluded away (from the truth)? See 43:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:88 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (God hath the knowledge of) his cry (i.e. of the Prophet): "O' my Lord! verily these are people who will believe not!" See 43:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:89 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So turn thou (Address to the Holy Prophet.) away from them and say: "Peace (be unto you)"; for they shall soon know (the result). See 43:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zukhruf:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if thou shouldst ask them: "Who created the heavens and the earth?" certainly would they say: "Created them the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing," It is a challenging fact that even if it be asked of the disbelievers as to who created the heaven and the earth, they could not help declaring it with perfect conviction at their heart saying it is God Who has created them, i.e., the exclusive propriety of God as the Creator of the Universe is such an undeniable fact that every one in the world knows it, be he a believer in Him or a disbeliever even.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The descent of the Book (Qur'an) is from God, the Al-Mighty, The All-Wise. This indicates the Qur'an as a Book, was revealed as a whole to the Holy Prophet. Refer to verse 44:3. (A.P.).It is asserted that:(1) The Holy Qur'an is the Book from God.(2) God Who is exalted in Power, i.e., He could cause His will to be revealed to any one He chooses.(3) The Book being from the All-Wise One, contains guidance to the wisdom essential for mankind.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "O' my servants who believe! Fear ye (the wrath of) your Lord, for those who do good in this world (there) is good, and God's earth is extensive; Verily, only the patient (Are there any in the Islamic World as a whole who were tortured, persecuted more than the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt, particularly the martyrs of Karbala, and those taken captives thereafter? What could be the recompense of Lord? How great & unaccountable would be their recompense.) ones will be paid their recompense without any account." Regarding the value of piety in Islam see verses 49:13, 7:26, 2:188, 189, 9:108, 28:83, 39:33. Islam has fixed the superior most degree of excellence acceptable to God, entitling man to the nearness to Him. For Piety see 49:13. Only the Pious are the near and the dear…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "I have been bidden that I should worship God (alone) being sincere unto Him in religion," The pagans asked the Holy Prophet as to why he preached a new faith opposed to the idolatry already current, and put his followers and devotees to untold miseries and heartless persecution - This verse was revealed.Not in the order of the conversion of Meccans, but in the order of creation as a whole, mentioned in verse 3:183. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And Commanded I am, that I shall be the first (Of those who submit themselves to God.) Muslim See 39:11

item.description: Say: "Verily, fear I, if I disobey my Lord, the chastisement of a great day." See 39:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "God (It is Whom) worship I, being sincere unto Him in my religion," See 39:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Worship ye then whatsoever ye like other than Him." Say thou: "Verily, the losers are those who have lost their own selves and their families on the Day of Judgment; Beware! that is the clear loss This is not even a permission but a note of reproach meaning, if in spite of all the given admonitions and the clear guidance, any one chooses only to go astray, let him act as he pleases and entitle himself to the return for it. But later this verse is said to have been abrogated by the command for the fight for the cause of truth.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For them shall be from above them coverings of fire and from beneath them coverings; with that maketh God His servants to fear; (so) fear Me ye O' My servants. See 39:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who shun the worship of the idols and turn they unto God, for them is the glad tidings, so bear thou the glad tidings unto My servants. See 39:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who hearken unto the word (All words – all talks.) and follow the best of it; those are they whom God hath guided; and those it is who are the men of understanding. See 39:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Is he on whom the sentence of chastisement hath been justly passed (equal to one who deserveth a reward)? Canst thou rescue him who is in the fire? See 39:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, We have sent down unto thee the Book (Qur'an) with the truth; so worship thou God (alone), being sincere unto Him in religion Adoration, Gratitude and Service is due to none but God. Man should seek protection and succour from none but God and God alone can give protection or succour to every being in the Universe. Nearness or approach to God could be had through none but the men of God, i.e., man should seek the correct or the right medium or means to approach Him.The correct medium is that of the Holy Prophet and the Holy Imams, by following their ideals and the practical examples set by these holy souls in their life on earth. Islam stresses on practical life and not on any rituals. Islam is nothing but a prescribed correctness in faith and goodness in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But (for) those who fear (The pious ones.) the (wrath of) their Lord are lofty pavilions, above them (ever) lofty pavilions, built (for them), 'neath which flow rivers: (this is) the promise of God: Faileth not God (His) promise. Reference may be to the enjoyments awaiting the Pious in the life hereafter. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Seest thou not that God sendeth down water from heaven, then causeth it go into the earth in the springs, then bringeth forth with it herbage of various colours (Kinds.) then it withereth that thou seest it yellow, then He maketh it chaff (Crumbleth it down.) ? Verily in this is a reminder for men of understanding. See 39:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! is he whose breast (heart) God hath opened for Islam then he followeth the Light from God (like unto the hardhearted one)? Nay! Woe unto those whose hearts are hard against the remembrance of God; those are in a clear error. It is said that this verse was revealed referring to the First Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abi Talib who was endued with the light of Islam and whose personal purity and spiritual excellence and that of the Holy Prophet was one and the same. Besides the Holy Prophet, Ali was the only one who never in his life bowed to any save God. About Ali the Holy Prophet had said: 'I and Ali are of one and the same Light.' This being the direct application of the revelation but indirectly and generally it could be applied to the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God hath sent down the best recital, a Book Consistent (Consistent similarity in its parts.) (in its parts) with iteration, at which do shudder the skins of those who fear (The pious ones.) their Lord, then get softened their skins and their hearts unto the remembrance of God; This is God's guidance, guideth He with it whomsoever He willeth; and whomsoever alloweth God to stray, for him there is no guide. The Holy Qur'an was revealed in parts on various occasions during the wide span of 23 years. The greatest proof of the Holy Book being the revealed Word of God is in its uniformity in all its parts conforming to each other and constituting a perfect harmonious whole without the least contradiction or inconsistency anywhere in it, though the circumstances necessitating the revelations, were of varying nature and yet…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! is he then who hath to guard himself with his own face against the torment of the chastisement on the Day of Judgment (like unto him who is secure from it)? And it will be said unto the unjust: "Taste ye what ye were earning!" See 39:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those before them did belie (the apostles) so came there unto them the chastisement from whence they perceived (Expect.) not. Regarding the chastisement coming to the disbelievers and the evil doers from which they would not perceive.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then did God make them taste the disgrace in the life of this world and certainly the chastisement of the hereafter is greater: did they but know. See 39:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed have We set forth for the people in this Qur'an examples of every sort that happly they may reflect. Matters spiritual, things abstract in nature and the factors of higher wisdom, would be conceived or understood easily by means of parables, metaphors and similitudes which are aptly used in the Holy Qur'an. Figurative language is used not only to teach matters of wisdom and higher knowledge, but also to treasure greater or higher secrets for the minds qualified to own them, with the necessary search for them at any time until the day of judgment.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: An Arabic Qur'an without any crookedness, that happly they may guard (they may become pious.) themselves (against evil). See 39:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Setteth forth God the examples of the man in (the service of) associates quarrelling with each other, and of a man (devoted) wholly to a (single) man (Master). Can the two (such) ones be alike in condition? (No!) All Praise is God's; Nay! most of them know not. The impracticability of serving two masters opposed to each other, (i.e., the falsehood of Polytheism) and the harmony, the love and the happiness naturally found in the service of one single master, (i.e., Monotheism), is depicted here.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Beware! Unto God alone is due all (Religion exclusive.) obedience; and those who take guardians besides Him, (say) "we worship them not (The excuse the idolators give.) save (in order) that they may make us near unto God," verily God will judge between them about what they differ; Verily, God guideth him not who is a liar, an ingrate (ungrateful.) Worshipping anything or any power in the place of God, in any form whatsoever is strictly forbidden.(Take guardians) i.e., without His permission - This does not refer to those who have been ordered by God Himself to be taken as guardians1 and as the means of approach to Him.2 (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily thou shall (one day) die, and they (too) shall (one day) die. All men good or bad, even the apostles of God, must die. None is exempt from the bodily death. There is life after death and it is then, and there, that every one good or bad would have to render account of his faith and deeds.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then verily ye on the Day of Judgment before your Lord will wrangle one with another. On the Day of Judgment, the disputers about the truth would realise their folly and meet the consequence of it.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Who is then more unjust than he who lieth about God and belieth the truth when it cometh unto him; Is there not in the Hell an abode for the disbelievers? If man in spite of the continuous efforts for his guidance from the High above and in spite of the manifest signs drawing his attention towards the Truth, denies his own Creator, Sustainer and Protector, it would be an act of unpardonable ingratitude1. The Holy Prophet Jesus warns against blasphemy against the Holy Ghost:"Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men."And whosoever speaketh a word against the son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And he who bringeth the truth and he who testifieth it - These are they that are the pious ones. By 'He who brought the truth' is meant the Holy Prophet Muhammad and it is the most undeniable fact of Islamic history that the first to believe among the males was Ali Ibn Abi Talib the first cousin and the Vicegerent of the Holy Prophet.Ibn Abbas says, when on the of 'Mi'raj' (Ascension) the Holy Prophet visited the Kingdom of God in the heavens, God told the Holy Prophet "Go and inform thy people on the earth what thou hast seen in the Heavens," to which the Holy Prophet submitted "Who would vouch my statement O' Lord?" The reply came "Ali would do it."The Holy Prophet said, "There are three Truthful ones" - (1) Ezkhiel the 'Mu'min Aal Pharaoh', (2)…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For them is whatever they please with their Lord; that is the recompense of the doers of good; See 39:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That God may take away from them the worst of what they did, and recompense them with their reward for the best of what they used to do. See 39:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is not God sufficient for His servant? And they frighten thee with those besides Him, and whomsoever God alloweth to stray, for him there shall not be any guide. (No amount of guidance will be effective.) See 39:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whomsoever God guideth, then him none shall beguile; Is not God the Almighty Lord of Retribution? (Not against any wrong done to God but, the wrong done to each other - He is Self-Subsistent, Self- Sufficient. None can harm 'Him'.) See 39:33

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if thou ask them who created the heavens and the earth? They would certainly say: 'God'; Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "Bethink ye then of what ye call upon besides than God, if willeth God unto me a harm, could they be the removers of His harm, or if willeth (God) unto me His mercy, could they be the withholders of His mercy?" Say thou: "Sufficeth me God! On Him (alone) do rely the reliants." Even the disbelievers helplessly acknowledge God alone being the Creator of the earth and the heavens.1The believers depend only upon God.2

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "O' my people! Act ye (as ye like) in your place, verily I (too) do act, soon will ye come to know," See 39:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Had God intended to take a son unto Himself, certainly would He select those He willeth of what He hath created, Hallowed is He! He (alone) is God, the Almighty. See verse 112:4. Neither God begets nor is He begotten. Begetting needs two interdependent partners to be the joint-causative factors, - none of them alone do anything of its own accord, without the co-operative partnership of the other. Dependence is a shortcoming, an imperfection and a weakness and God is Omnipotent, All-Perfect and All-Powerful and independent. The act of begetting needs a husband and a wife and the functioning of animals passion in both, thus the act is an animal act.God being the Creator of every power in the Universe, Himself to depend upon any of His own creations, stands neither to reason nor to any necessity for Him to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Who it is unto whom cometh a chastisement which will disgrace him, and whom there falleth the everlasting doom. See 39:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily We sent down on thee the Book (Qur'an) for the sake of the people, with the truth; and whosoever is guided aright, it is for his own self, and whosoever goeth astray, strayeth he only to its own hurt, (detriment.) and thou art not over them a custodian. See 39:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God taketh the souls at death, and those that die not (He taketh) during their sleep; and He withholdeth those on whom He hath passed the decree of death (from returning unto their bodies); but sendeth He the others (to their bodies) till a time which is fixed; Verily, in this are signs for a people who reflect. Points out the affinity between sleep and death - to some extent1. There is no doubt that in the state of sleep, the cognitive self-disassociates its attention from the external senses but not from the body, totally. In that state it turns sometimes to the state of sub-conscious, unconscious and super-conscious. Each state is responsible for some sort of corresponding dreams. If the dreams which are prophetic belongs and correspond to the super-conscious state this state is a brief example of the…

item.description: Or, have they taken intercessors other than God? Say thou: "What! even though they have no power over anything, nor do they understand." See 39:42

item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "God's (alone) is intercession altogether; His is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth; then unto Him (only) ye shall all be returned." About the doctrine of 'Shafa'at', i.e., (Intercession).1

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When God alone is mentioned, shrink the hearts of those who believe not in the hereafter; and when those besides Him are mentioned, lo! they rejoice. This verse clearly says that a mere verbal declaration of the faith does not necessarily mean that every such declarer is also a genuine believer1. Such was the case with many of those who had merely professed Islam but were not believers in fact.2 Only such hypocrites were those who turned inimical to the House of the Holy Prophet (the holy Ahl Al-Bayt) for, immediately as the Holy Prophet departed from this world all such hypocrites who were actually mere opportunists, turned into fortune-hunters and thus they never liked these holy ones to gain any recognition at all, at the hands of the public for they would never be able to realise their selfish…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "O' God! the Originator of the heavens and the earth, the Knower of the unseen and the manifest! Thou (alone) shalt judge between Thy servants in the matter wherein they were differing." See 39:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And had it been for those who did injustice, whatever is in the earth and the like added to it, they verily will seek to ransom themselves with it from the pain of the chastisement on the Day of Judgment; and there shall appear unto them, from God, that which they had not been reckoning. See 39:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall appear unto them the evils of what they wrought, and shall surround them that which they used to mock at. See 39:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when toucheth (Afflicteth.) man a harm he crieth unto Us; then when We grant him a favour from Us, sayeth he; "I have been granted it only on account of (my) knowledge." Nay! it is only a trial, but most of them know not. See 39:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He hath created the heavens and the earth with the truth; causeth He the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night, and subjected the sun and the moon; each one speedeth on to an assigned term; Beware! He is the All-Mighty, the Oft- Forgiving. See verse 6:73.'Mighty and the Most Forgiving' God is the Mightiest and at the same time the Most Pardonful for those who turn repentant of their sins and amend thereafter.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed, the same did say those before them, but availed them not what they had been earning. See 39:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So befell unto them the evils what they did earn; and (for) those of these who did injustice, soon shall befall unto them the evils what they did earn, and they shall frustrate Us not (in Our Plans). See 39:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! know they not that (it is) God (alone Who) amplifieth the sustenance unto whomsoever He willeth, and straiteneth (it) (whosoever He willeth); Verily in this are signs for a people who believe. The provision of sustenance to His creation is a matter which is in the hands of God Himself. He provides every thing with its sustenance. Everything needs the sustenance necessary for its life and when sustenance is in the hands of God, the existence of everything would naturally depend upon Him, and everything should necessarily adore Him and none else. There is no need for any creature to fear or implore anyone else save God. Any act of worshipping anyone besides Him would not only be foolishness but an unpardonable act of ingratitude and thanklessness.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "O' My servants! who have been extravagant unto their own selves, despair ye not of the mercy of God; verily God forgiveth sins all together; verily He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful." The First Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abi Talib says that there is no greater verse of God's grace and His mercy than this verse in the whole of the Holy Qur'an. It is Islam and no other religion in the world which introduces God to His creation, not as a mere mercilessly just judge whose decisions are based only on law and the facts without any concern of any grace or mercy in it, but as the Independent the Beneficent, Oft-Pardoning, the Most Merciful Master of the Universe who deals with His creation as He pleases, and whose justice is ever…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And return ye unto your Lord, and resign ye yourselves unto Him, ere cometh unto you the chastisement, for then ye shall not be helped. This verse invites the sinners to turn to the Lord before their case comes up to Him for His final decision. Pardon could reasonably be had before being caught by the execution or the application of the law and before being held by justice to deal with the offence, and once the decree is passed there remains no room for any excuse for the one who never repented and went on committing the offence until caught and brought to account.Mercy would naturally be due to one who surrenders himself and repents for any offence before he is caught by justice and not for the one who continues committing the offence and when caught, wants to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And follow ye the most excellent thing what hath been sent down unto you from your Lord, ere cometh unto you the chastisement suddenly while ye even perceive it not, The best one sent down to man from God is the Holy Prophet with the Word of God, the Holy Qur'an. Before leaving this world, the Holy Prophet made it known to the people as to who should be their ideal or models in their practical life in this world in his absence from it. There are a great many of his declarations about the position of his Ahl Al-Bayt and the most prominent and directly speaking are the following announcements of his, which are universally acknowledged by the Muslim World as a whole1."Verily, I leave behind me among yon Two Great Things, The Book of God (The Holy Qur'an)…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Lest a soul should say: "Oh! Alas, Woe unto me! for what I failed (in my duty) unto God, and certainly was I of those who mocked," Thus, a disbeliever or a sinner who mocked at every admonition, would retrieve his position and all kinds of regrets would assail the individual with sighs of no avail.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or, it should say: "Had God guided me, I would certainly have been of the pious ones," See 39:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or, it should say when it seeth the chastisement: "Had there been only a return for me, I would be of the righteous (ones)" See 39:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! indeed did come unto thee My signs, then thou didst belie them, thou didst act proudly and thou wert of the disbelievers. See 39:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He created you from a single (Refer to verses 16:72 & 22:5.) being, then made He from it its mate, and sent down for you eight (Refer to verse 6:143.) in pairs, of the cattle, He createth you in the wombs of your mothers a creation after a creation, in triple darkness; that is God your Lord, His is the kingdom; there is no god but He; How then are ye turned away? About the creation of men from one same self.1 Sheep, goats, camels and oxen in pairs. Wild and domestic in each kind.2As regards the creation of man passing through stage after stage, and the evolutionary process he undergoes in the womb of his mosher.3The justification for the use of the word 'Anzala' - 'Sent down' is based upon the principle laid down in the verse 21:15. (A.P.).Three…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on the Day of Resurrection thou shalt see those who have uttered lies against God their faces shall be blackened; is there not in Hell an abode for the proud? 'Spotless White' has been taken as a sign of joy and honour1 and 'Darkness or Blackness' as the symbol of sorrow, grief, disgrace.2 With this sign of their given complexion, the blessed and the cursed ones on the day would be identified by the others.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall deliver God those who guard (themselves) against evil, with their success: evil shall touch them not, nor shall they grieve. See 39:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God (alone) is the Creator of everything, and He (alone) is over all things the Guardian. See 39:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: His are the keys of the heavens and the earth; and those who disbelieve in the signs of God, these are they who are the losers. See 39:60

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (Ask the people.) thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!)'. "What! Bid ye me to worship others than God? O' ye ignorant ones!" The Gospel of Unity, has been the message from God to mankind since the birth of the very First man.The passage itself indicates that it is a general statement, no particular person is meant. The people are addressed through the Holy Prophet. It indicates that not only associating with God destroys one's deeds but even if the motive of the deeds is not exclusively for God. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed hath it been revealed unto thee and unto those before thee: "Verily if thou (Prophet addressed for the people.) associatest (others with God), certainly would come to naught thy work, and certainly wouldst thou be of the losers." See 39:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! But God alone, worship thou and be of the thankful ones. See 39:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They have esteemed (Refer to verse 22:74.) not God, as it is His rightful due; While the whole earth shall be in His grip on the Day of Judgment and heavens rolled (Refer to verses 14:48, 21:104, 22:74 & 39:69.) up (shall be) in His right (An aspect of God's power.) hand; Hallowed is He, high above what they associate (with Him). If they have duly valued the Power, Might and the Authority of God, people would never have run after false gods and worshipped imaginary beings who have neither any power nor any authority with them, to rule the destiny of anything in the world and who are themselves helpless and lack an existence for them1.The heavens shall be rolled up in His right hand.2Those who associate others with God in authority or 'Esteem'. This expression has been used…

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (when) shall be blown the Trumpet, then shall swoon (die) whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth save those whom God hath willed (to keep alive); then (the Trumpet) shall be blown (Refer to the note on Trumpet.) again, then lo! they shall stand up awaiting. With the first Trumpet would all the beings on the earth be caused to die and with the second Trumpet all heavenly beings would cease to live. And there will come into existence a new earth and a new heaven with the people resurrected.1'Sayiqa' literally does not mean death but 'swoon'2 but the loss of the consciousness in that state is synonymous with death. However, there is an exception which according to Ahl Al-Bayt, are those who have attained the state of 'Shahadat.' (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the earth shall get radiant with the light of its Lord, and the Book (Book of the deeds of the people.) (of deeds) shall be set, and the prophets shall be brought up and the witnesses, (Refer to verses 36:65, 40:51, 41:20 - 41:23.) and (it shall) be judged between them, and they shall not be dealt with unjustly. 'Kitab' means the individual record of the deeds, i.e., deeds of every individual. (A.P.).This includes the witnesses of high order1 but even the very organs of the individual's body.2 (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If ungrateful ye be, then verily God is (Self-Sufficient) independent (above all needs. Refer to verse 3:96.) of you; and He liketh not ingratitude in His servants; and if ye be grateful; He liketh it in you; and no bearer of a burden shall bear the burden of another; then unto your Lord is your return, then will He inform you of what ye were doing; verily, He knoweth all what is in the breasts (hearts). On the Day of Judgment, none shall bear the burden of the other.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall be paid in full unto every soul what it hath wrought, and He knoweth best what they do. See 39:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall be driven those who disbelieved, unto the Hell, in flocks; Until, when come they to it, its doors shall be opened and shall say unto them the keepers (The angels.) of it; (The hell.) "Came not unto you apostles from among you reciting unto you the signs of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your day?" they shall say; "Yea! but just is the sentence of punishment on the disbelievers" See 39:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It shall be said (unto them): "Enter ye (Now) the gates of Hell, to abide therein, and wretched the abode of the arrogant." See 39:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall be conveyed those who feared (Take shelter against - or guard against.) (the wrath of) their Lord, in companies unto the garden; until when they come to it, and its doors shall be opened, and the keepers of it shall say unto them: "Peace be on you! ye shall be happy; Enter it then to abide." See 39:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they shall say: "All praise is God's, Who hath made good to us His promise, and He hath made us to inherit the earth, we may dwell in the gardens wherever we please, and goodly is the recompense of the workers (of good deeds)." The creation begins with 'Alhamdulillah' praising God and ends with the same. Thus, the Holy Imams recommend that man should begin with thanksgiving to God and end it with it.1Attributing this grace and the blessings of God to the early Muslim conquest of a strip of some fertile lands, is nothing but the profanation of the high ideals of Islam, into a mean and limited temporal gain. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thou shalt see the angels circling around the 'Arsh' (Refer to verse 40:7.) (The Throne of Absolute Authority), celebrating (Hallowing Him by His praise.) the Praise of their Lord; and it shall be judged between them with justice, and it shall be said, All praise is God's the Lord of the worlds! This is the presentation of the Absolute Divine Sovereignty and the Hold over the entire universe, in the terms of the Royal Majestic form of which the people are acquainted. Otherwise, the throne actually as the Holy Imams of the Ahl Al-Bayt interpret it, is His All-Embracing Knowledge wherein the angelical entities and the agencies, are at the verge of it.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when toucheth (Afflicteth.) man a distress he crieth unto his Lord, oft-turning unto Him; and when He bestowed upon him a favour from Him, forgetteth he that for which he did cry unto Him before, and (he) setteth up rivals unto God, that he may beguile (men) to stray away from His path; say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad! unto such a man) "Enjoy thyself in thy ingratitude a little; verily, thou art of the inmates of the (Hell) fire" See 10:12, 30:33, 16:53. While caught in adversity or any trouble or difficulty man turns to God imploring for relief or rescue and when God's favour is bestowed on him, he forgets Him from Whom came the succour and attributes his happiness and prosperity to his own self.

item.title: bil-Quran: Az-Zumar:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! (this or) he who is prayerful during the hours of the night, prostrating in obeisance and standing, and he taketh heed of the hereafter and hopeth he for the mercy of his Lord! Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "What! Can those who know be equal to those who know not? Verily only the men of understanding take the warning" This is one of the verses of the Holy Qur'an which gives clear and definite guidance to the right course following only certain men of God who are endowed with distinguished qualities of knowledge, wisdom, and goodness, and insight.1 It is a universally acknowledged fact that the holy Imams were divinely endowed with knowledge to a wonderful degree. This fact is vouched by the declaration of the Holy Prophet about Ali saying, 'I am the City of Knowledge and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (All) praise is God's, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, the Maker of the angels, messengers flying on wings, two, and three, and four: (A figurative expression to the graded flights.) He addeth to His creation whatever He willeth; Verily God, over all things hath power. All praise is God's and gratitude due only to Him.1To know God the Creator or the Originator of the Primeval cause which started the genetic process of the creation of the Universe and its ever-progressive functioning in the innumerable forms and in infinite ways which is beyond the power of reasoning by the finite endowment of the faculties of the human intellect. The matter of the origin of life and the causative factor of the spiritual forces, is unquestionably beyond the ken of any experimental experience to help man to comprehend the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whosoever desireth honour (let him seek it from God, for) God's (alone) (God alone gives honour to whomsoever He pleases. Refer to verse 58:8.) is all honour; Unto Him (only) ascend all good words; and as for those who plot evil deeds, for them shall be a severe chastisement; and their plot, it shall be vain. Those who wish for honour and reward even in this world as in the next should turn only to God Goodness in any degree, is never lost. Every good word and action, is certainly exalted. Every kind of goodness by its nature, rises up to achieve God's pleasure and grace and similarly every evil is marked for the punishment due to it.1It is God's plan that is always done and everything else other than that shall miserably fail and perish.(a) God alone is the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God created you of dust, then of the life-germ, then He made you pairs (of male and female); and a female beareth not, nor doth she deliver, save with His knowledge; and ageth not the aged, nor finisheth from any one's life, but it is all in a Book (decree ordained); Verily this, for God, is easy. This refers to the lowly origin of the physical existence of man whose body has been created of dust1 and who had his origin from a drop of sperm ejected, the matter which is considered dirty and its ejection considered as an act of shame to be hidden. The dependence of one sex upon the other, in bringing forth an issue proves that the very existence of man is dependant and every individual sex being by itself insufficient for a progressive life…

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And nor are the two seas alike, this one (is) sweet, quencheth thirst its sweetness, (and) pleasant to drink, and the other salt, and bitter; and yet from them both, eat ye flesh fresh (Fish.) and take forth ornaments which wear ye; and seest thou the ships cleave through it, that ye may seek of His grace, and that ye may be grateful. Man has to use his discretionary powers in differentiating good and evil as both can never be of one and the same value and worth. There is an indirect hint or even a taunt for those who profess to be believers and yet love the disbelievers. Under the guidance of this verse none could compare the Holy Ahl al-Bayt who have been purified by God Himself1 to the others who had been polluted by a sinful and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Causeth He the night to enter into the day, and the day to enter into the night, and hath made He subservient (unto you) the sun and the moon; each travelleth to an appointed time: This is God your Lord! His is the kingdom; and those whom ye call upon other than Him, own not (even) a straw. Compare with verses 13:2, 21:33, 22:61 & 36:38.Indicates that the act of creation is constant and the continuation has a beginning and an end. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If ye call on them they shall hear not your call; and even if they hear they shall answer you not; and on the Day of Judgment they will deny your associating them (with God), and none can (ever) inform thee as (the One Who is) the All-Aware. See 35:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye people! ye are the needy unto God; and God (alone) is He Who is the (Arabic Ghani.) Self-Sufficient, the Most Praised (Arabic Hameed.) One. Every man or woman undoubtedly depends upon God's provision even for his or her own sustenance.This is the permanent tie between the creature and the Creator. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If He willeth, He will take you off and bring a new creation. See 35:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And nor this is hard for God. See 35:15

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And no bearer (Refer to verses 2:48, 2:123, 2:254, 6:165, 17:15, 39:7 & 53:38.) shall bear the burden of another; and if the heavy laden one should cry for (another bearer to carry) its burden, (even) aught (Any thing.) of it shall not be carried, and even if he be near of kin; Thou canst but warn those who (Refer to verses 36:11, 50:33 & 67:12.) fear their Lord unseen and keep up regular prayer; And whosoever purifieth (himself), he only purifieth for his own (In his own interest.) self; And unto God (alone) is the destination (of all). There is no contradiction between this verse and verses 29:12 & 29:13. There, it is asserted that none shall shoulder the burden of the other; his own burden may increase on account of misleading others. Every wrong doer shall be responsible…

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And alike are not (both) the blind and the seeing, This is the refutation of the doctrine of the subjective value of good and bad which even now a section of the Indian School of Philosophy maintains. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whatever God layeth open of His mercy unto the people, there is none to hold it back, and whatever He holdeth back there is none to send it forth after that, and He is the All- Mighty, the All-Wise. God's will is always done. No power can ever stop or withhold any decrees of His, be that to grant any gift or to chastise any individual or people.

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nor the darkness and the light See 35:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nor the shade and the heat, See 35:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And neither are alike (both) the living and the dead; Verily God heareth whom He willeth, and thou canst not make those hear who are in the graves. See 35:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: None else art thou (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) but a Warner. This indicates that those who are dead, though their connection is severed from this world they are not totally perished. It is a figurative expression to say that those who are alive to the message, are not like those who are totally indifferent to it. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily We sent thee with truth, as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner: and there is not a people (This Verse indicates that the great Sages who visited the other parts of the world like India, China etc. could be the Warners to those respective people.) but a warner hath gone among them. See 35:23

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they belie thee, so indeed did belie those before them; their apostles had come unto them with clear proofs, and with scriptures, and with the enlightening Book. Refer to verses 3:185, 5:48, 10:47, 16:36.Regarding the previous apostles also having suffered rejection from the people. See verse 35:4 above.

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then did I seize those who disbelieved, so how (Severe) was the abhorrence (of Mine)? See 35:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Seest thou not that God sendeth down water from the heaven; then We bring forth with it fruits of various colours; and in the mountains are streaks white and red, of various colours, and (others) intensely black? Presents the universal grace which produces various effects in various receptacles. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of the people and beasts and cattle are of various colours likewise; verily fear God only those of His servants endued with knowledge: Verily, God is All-Mighty, Oft-Forgiving. See 35:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who recite the Book (Qur'an.) of God and establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided them with, secretly and openly, hope for a merchandise which will never perish, See 35:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye people! Remember ye God's bounty on you; Is there any creator other than God who provideth you with your sustenance from the heaven and the earth? There is no god but He; Whence then are ye turned away (from the truth)? The Primal Cause of the whole creation, is none else but God. By the question 'whether man finds any other creator besides the Only God' man is exhorted to turn only to God and not to get involved in the false fancies about imaginary deities.Sustenance is necessary for the soul as for the body - The sustenance from heaven is God's guidance which is necessary for the health as well as the progress of the soul, and the provision from the earth is the terrestrial food for the material body. Thus, it is God and God alone…

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That He may give them back their recompense (in full) and increase of His grace unto them; verily, He is Oft-Forgiving, the Greatest Appreciator (of Good) See 35:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And that which We have revealed unto thee of the (Qur'an.) Book, it is the truth testifying that which hath come before it; verily God, about His servants is All-Aware, All- Seeing. See 35:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then made We the inheritors (Before leaving this world, the Holy Prophet entrusted the Book of God, Qur'an, to the Ahl al-Bayt. Refer to the Hadith al-Thaqalayn - "I leave behind among you the Book of God & my Ahl al-Bayt etc., etc.") of the Book (Qur'an) those whom chose We from among Our servants: and of them is he who causeth himself to suffer a loss, and of them is he who followeth the middle course, and of them is he who is the foremost in goodness by God's permission: This is that which is the greatest excellence. This verse has to be intelligently studied. The opening words say that God has bequeathed the Holy Book, i.e., the Holy Qur'an to His chosen servants. The chosen ones of God could not be any other than those who are guided…

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Gardens of eternity they shall enter into, they shall be given to wear therein bracelets of gold and pearls, and their raiment therein be silk. (A figurative expression of the sublime bliss.) See 35:32

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they shall say: "All praise is God's (alone) Who hath taken away from us (all) (Caused by dirt. Refer to verse 33:33.) grief; Verily our Lord is Oft-Forgiving, the Greatest Appreciator (of goodness)" This is an indication to the state of perfect peace of mind and tranquillity that the people in it would enjoy, i.e., there shall be in Paradise, neither any fear any grief of any kind whatsoever for the inmates.

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He Who hath alighted (Figurative expression to the heavenly bliss.) us of His grace in an abode to abide (for ever); therein toucheth us not any toil, nor affecteth us therein any fatigue. Neither any toil nor any fatigue - Fatigue could be even of rejoicing. The Bliss in Paradise shall be universal, continuous, and perpetual.

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who disbelieve, for them shall be the fire of Hell, it shall not be decreed that they should die, nor shall be lightened unto them aught of its torment; Thus do We retribute every ungrateful one. See 35:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they shall cry aloud therein for help: "O' our Lord! Take us out (hence), we will do good deeds other than what we used to do (before)." (It shall be said unto them by the Lord): "Did not We keep you alive long enough for him who reflected to reflect therein? and came unto you the Warner (too); So (now) taste ye (the fruits of your deeds), then for the unjust there (shall be) no helper." Respite for repentance in the present life. No repentance could be of any avail, in the hereafter. Hence one should hasten to repent for his sins and amend his life duly, before death overtakes him.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, God (alone) is the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth; Verily He knoweth all that is in the breasts (hearts). The attributes of God are not any addition to His All-Perfect Self. Hence knowledge of any thing or action, hidden or manifest, even feelings, motives, and plans, is not to be acquired by God as in the case of any other being. God's knowledge pervades in and out of everything in the world.Whatever is of the heavens, in the earth and in between the two aspects, one which may appeal to human senses which may be termed as phenomenon and the other which is hidden from the reach of the human senses. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He is the One Who made you the successors (of those who preceded you) in the earth; so whosoever disbelieveth against him shall be his disbelief; And the disbelief of the infidels shall increase not with their Lord but (His) wrath, and increaseth not the disbelief of the infidels but loss. See 35:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they belie thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) indeed have been belied apostles before thee; and unto God (alone) are returned all affairs! No apostle of God was ever honoured in this world. Every one of the apostles had suffered rejection, ridicule and persecution at the hands of the people, but none of the apostles was discouraged for they were sure that the ultimate return of every one and all matters, is only to God and to none else.

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "See ye not your partners whom ye call upon other than God? Show me what part of the earth they have created, or have they any share in the heavens; or gave We unto them any scripture so that from (From the Book.) it they (may give) proof (be sure of the authority.) (of their claim) Nay! Promise (hold out a promise.) not the unjust unto one another of them but only to delude. (Deceive.)" See 35:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, God holdeth (Upholds.) the heavens and the earth lest they come to naught; and if they come to naught none besides Hirn can hold them back; Verily, He is the Most Forbearing, the Oft-Forgiving. This is the clear assertion that the dimensional being whether terrestrial or celestial, is nothing existing in itself as a substance. It is a mere phenomenon, the outcome of a cohesive power, unexplainable in dimensional terms. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And swore they by God with the strongest oaths that if came unto them a warner, they would certainly be guided aright better than any other people; but when came unto them a warner it increased not in them but their aversion, See 35:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (In) priding in the earth, and planning evil; and the evil plans {of theirs) shall beset not but the devisers themselves; Then wait they for aught save the course of the people gone before? For never shall thou find any change in the course of God; and never shalt thou find in the course of God any alteration. To all the ancient people who rebelled against the truth and lived beyond the control of faith were dealt with respite - first they were shown mercy and given the respite to correct their belief and amend the ways of their life, then apostles were sent to them to admonish them and exhort them to goodness in thought and deeds and lastly when they did not avail of any of the opportunities of the grace and the mercy shown to them and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Have they travelled not in the earth and seen how was the end of those before them though they were stronger than them in strength? And God is not such to frustrate Him aught in the heavens or in the earth; Verity He is the All-Knowing, All-Powerful See 35:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And were God to seize the people (to punish them) for what they wrought, He would leave not on the back of it (the earth) any moving being, (Any creature.) but He respiteth them till an appointed term; and when cometh their doom, then verily God, about His servants is All-Seeing. It is God's mercy that the sinners in the world are left to themselves with the respite to amend their deserts otherwise everyone on earth would long have perished if God had dealt every one with His strict justice. That is why the Holy Ahl al-Bayt have taught us to be ever prayerful saying, 'O Lord! Deal us with thy Mercy and deal Thou not with Thy Justice.'Respite given by God, does not mean that those given the respite could ever escape the ever vigilant and all-enveloping knowledge of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' ye people! verily the promise of God is true, so let not the life of this world beguile you; and let not the Arch-Beguiler (Satan) beguile you about God! Man is exhorted to remember that from God, he has come, and unto Him alone, is his return to render account of the life he spent in this world. One should remember that life does not end in this world, but there is the future for it, in which God promises man, mercy, i.e., the reward or the punishment he entitles himself to, by his goodness or badness in this life. Both the promises of God are certain to be fulfilled.Let not man be deluded by the deceptive instigation of the Satanic thoughts of committing sins, depending upon God's mercy or depending upon any durability of life, delaying repentance and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily Satan is your enemy, so ye (too) take him (as your) enemy; He (Satan.) only inviteth his party that they may be the fellows of the flaming fire. Satan is evil personified, hence every evil should be treated as our enemy. The snare of Satan is very vast and ever spread. He wants man to share his damnation. Hence man should always shun evil.

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who disbelieve, for them shall be a severe chastisement; And as for those who believe and do good, for them shall be forgiveness and a great recompense. To reject the belief in God is to reject everything good which He has created. Those who are not true or correct in their faith and righteous in their living, shall have the consequent evil return for it and those who are true and correct in their faith and are faithful in its practice, shall have God's grace and a great reward.

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Is he then whose evil deed is made alluring that he beholdeth it good (equal to the one guided aright)! (Nay! by no means!), for verily God leaveth to stray whomsoever He willeth and guideth He whomsoever He willeth, so let not thy self go (in vain) in grief (Worry about.) for them; Verily God knoweth all that they do. Man is exhorted to guard against his own rebellious self and should not allow it to get astray from the right path.

item.title: bil-Quran: Faatir:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God is He Who sendeth the winds and they raise the clouds, then We drive them on to a country (which is) dead, and give We life therewith to the earth after its death; Even so is the (rising of the dead in) Resurrection. To prove as to how the dead will be resurrected, the example of the dried, unpromising soil is given which to all intents and purposes, seems to be dead and which is once again quickened by rain and made productive.The same will be the process of the Resurrection. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ha. Mim. (H. M.) This Book is the manifestation of God's Grace and Mercy in the aspects of 'Rahmaniyat' and 'Rahimiyat'.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And hath made therein mountains high from above its surface; and He blessed therein, and planned therein its foods, in four (Including the first two days in the previous verse.) days (periods): alike for the seekers. (equal opportunity for all.) In verses 7:54, 10:3, 11:7, 25:59 & 32:4 it is said that God created the heavens and the earth in Six days. The above verse (verse 9) mentions the base of the two main groups of the beings, i.e., physical and the spiritual, (i.e., matter and spirit), and in this, the remaining four stages relating to the details of the beings from each base. The term 'days' in this verse and in the other verses referring to the creation of the heavens and the earth - means the several stages, the sequence of the order in which the various components…

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then He applied Himself unto the heaven, which was yet only a smoke, so said He unto it and unto the earth: "Come ye Two, willing or reluctant;" Said the two: "We do come willingly" About the mountains.1This may refer to the theory of Nebula (Nebular Theory) as the Original form of the heavenly bodies. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He made them seven heavens in two days (periods), and revealed in every heaven His Will; and adorned We the lower heavens with lights (of the brilliant stars), and made it guarded (with angels); That is the decree of the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing. This and the verses 67:5, 77:8, 15:16 - 15:17 indicate that all illuminating stars are arranged in the lower sky. Then the other six skies may be in the nebular state1. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they turn away, then say: "I warn you of thunderbolt (Scourge, affliction.) (of a destructive punishment) (which afflicted the people) of 'Ad and Thamud." 'Ṣa'iqah' - as used in the Holy Qur'an - any destructive heavenly phenomenon viz. lightning, thunderbolt, Meteor, etc. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when came unto them apostles from before them and from behind them, (Successively.) saying: "Worship ye not aught but God;" said they: "Had our Lord willed, He would certainly have sent down angels; so verily in what ye have been sent with, we disbelieve." See 41:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And as to the people of 'Ad, they prided (Became arrogant.) in the land without right, and said they: "Who is mightier than we in power?" What! Beheld they not that God Who created them is mightier than they in power? And Our signs they used to deny. (To gainsay.) See 41:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So sent We on them a violent wind in inauspicious days, that We may make them taste the chastisement of disgrace in the life of this world, and certainly the chastisement of the hereafter is more disgracing, and they shall not be helped. Jabir Ibn Abdullah Ansari says that Abu Jahl gathered the chiefs of the Quraysh and said that what Muhammad (the Holy Prophet) has, is nothing but sorcery, poetry and some black art of the soothsayers. We must send someone who knows these arts to him and get him examined. Utbah bin Rabi'a stood up and said "I know these arts, I shall go and try Muhammad." Utbah came over to the Holy Prophet and said "O' Muhammad, art thou better than thy elders Hashim, Abdul Muttalib and Abdullah who were thy father and thy grand-father who did…

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And as to (the people of) Thamud We did guide them aright, but they loved (Preferred.) error against the right guidance, so there seized them the thunder bolt of a disgracing chastisement for what they used to earn. See 41:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We rescued those who believed and guarded (themselves against evil). Those who believed in God and lived a righteous life were saved.

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on the day when shall be collected together the enemies of God, unto the fire, then they shall be ranked in groups. See 41:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: A descent (Revelation) from the Beneficent, the Most Merciful (God); See 41:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Until they come unto it (the Hell), shall bear witness against them, their ears and their eyes and their skins as to what they used to do. See 41:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they shall say unto their skins: "Why witness ye against us?" They shall say: "Caused us to speak God who maketh everything speak, and He it is Who created you for the first time, (Indicate this birth of man is the first birth - This refutes the theory of this birth being the re-incarnated one.) and unto Him ye shall (all) be returned." See 41:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And ye covered not yourselves (merely) lest that your ears and your eyes and your skins should bear witness against you, but (it was) that ye thought that God knoweth not most of what ye did.
