May refer to the doctrine that God's knowledge comprehends particular objects viz. deeds of the individuals. His knowledge is confined to general and universal objects and ideas. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And that your (evil) conjectures which ye did conject about your Lord hath tumbled you into ruin, so ye are become of the losers. The Sixth Holy Imam said that 'A believer should fear God's wrath so much that he must imagine himself being cast into the hell-fire and must be hopeful for God's mercy so much that he must be imagining himself to be of the fellows of Paradise.' And said that 'God is there with the thought of man and if the thought be good, He rewards the individual and if that be evil, the thinker is punished.' The Holy Prophet said that 'There is not one sent in humanity, who bears good thoughts and God is not with him, to remind him' and recited this verse.

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they be patient, yet the fire shall be their abode: or if they seek favour, yet then they shall not be of the favoured (ones). It is a sarcastic announcement. 'If they only wait, then they would surely find the hell-fire their abode and if they seek grace then it will be too late.'

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We have appointed for them intimate companions so for them have they made fair seeming what is before them and what is behind them, and the sentence (Literally, Word.) proved just against them, as it did among the peoples of the jinn and the human beings that have passed away before them; verily they were the losers. As the happiness increases in a congenial society of the partners in the joy, so also the regret, sorrow and grief is multiplied and deepened and gets more effective when the partners in evil are put together to multiply the feeling of grief and regret by not only the individual himself suffering the chastisement but also by being affected by witnessing the misery around.Regarding the jinns see verse 6:131.

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who disbelieve say: "Hearken ye not unto this Qur'an, make noise in it, happly ye may overcome." Refer to note on verses 22:52 - 22:54 verses on Taḥrif in the introduction. This was and still is the effort to create confusion about Qur'an but it had been in vain. Refer to note on verses 41:41 & 41:42. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So, We will certainly make those who disbelieve taste a severe chastisement, and certainly will We recompense them for the worst of what they used to do. See 41:26

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That shall be the recompense of the enemies of God, the fire! For them therein shall be the abode to abide; in recompense for what they, with Our signs used to deny. It clearly indicates that their misdeeds themselves will be paying them. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who disbelieve will say: "O' our Lord! show us those who led us astray of the jinn and the human beings; both of them will we trample under our feet so that they may be of the lowest (meanest.) ones." As goodness rejoices in helping the others to be good, so also evil tends to drag others into it and longs to see them disgraced and condemned. The forces of evil had been on their work ever since the advent of human life on earth.1 Those meeting the afflictions which their evil had earned for them, would like to see their leaders who misled them to the torturous destiny.

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: A Book, fully expounded (Made plain.) are its verses, a Qur'an (A collection, a recital. Refer to verse 24:49.) in Arabic, for people who know, The Holy Qur'an, is a Book not of any ambiguous and mystic sayings but with every verse of it, duly explained. It is in Arabic, the language of the people through whom it has been divinely willed to reach every nation in the various parts of the world, so that the people, the Arabs, to whom it was first introduced, might easily know the truth and spread it to others.Arabic here does not mean the Arabian language but is an adjective meaning the best, the most expressive, the most eloquent language. Opposed to this the Arabs called 'Ajam' meaning the reverse - Non-expressive, slang dialects. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who say: Our Lord is God! and persevere aright, descend upon them the angels, (saying): that "Fear ye not, nor be grieved, and receive the glad tidings of the Garden which ye were promised." This clearly indicates that the descension of the angels with glad tidings, is not only for the apostles but to whomsoever believe and persevere aright. But from some traditions of the Ahl Al-Bayt, it seems that it refers to the descension of angels to the true believers at the agony of death. That may be one of the instances of the descension of the angels. It is not impossible if they descend to the true believers even earlier with the glad tidings. The next verse confirms this. It is not what the tradition asserts that in the battlefield of Karbala the angels descended to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We are your guardians in the life of this world and in the hereafter, and for you shall be therein whatever desireth your selves and yours shall be therein whatever ye shall ask for. See 41:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: A hospitable welcome (Reception or entertainment.) from the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful (God). See 41:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And who is better in speech than he who calleth unto God and doeth good and sayeth "Verily I am of the Muslims (These who have submitted themselves to God.)" See 41:30

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And equals can not be the good (Thus those purified ones by God (see verse 33:33) i.e., the Ahl Al-Bayt and the others cannot be equal.) and the evil. Repel thou (evil) with what is the best, when lo! he between whom and thee was enmity, shall be as though he were a warm friend. Here again a note of guidance is given to help men to have a correct value and appreciation of goodness and not to equalise it with evil. The holy Ahl Al-Bayt were goodness personified. The believers are guided in various ways, through parables and figurative expressions to bring home to the seekers of Truth and goodness, the value of the genuine goodness against the deceptive nature of evil. It could be a warning too, against equalising goodness and evil, the holy Ahl Al-Bayt and their…

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And receive it not but those who are steadfast, and receive it not but those with the greatest good fortune. See 41:34

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if an enticement from satan enticeth thee, (The people addressed through the Prophet.) then seek thou refuge in God; Verily, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. In the verse above, the Muslims are admonished to fight evil in the best way possible and here the greatest and the best remedy against an open attack from the Satanic forces is given, i.e., to seek refuge with God and the promise of response from God is there for every one who seeks to have it.

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And among His signs are the night, and the day, the sun and the moon; Do not prostrate ye in obeisance (Worship.) unto the sun nor unto the moon; and prostrate ye in obeisance (Worship.) unto God (alone) Who created them, if Him it is ye worship. See 41:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But if they be arrogant (to do this), yet those with (The angels and the Holy ones.) thy Lord glorify Him during the night and the day, and they tire (Refer to note on verse 21:8.) not. From the use of the term ''inda rabbika' - with thy Lord - here and in verses 21:8 and in 3:169, 15:21, 13:39, 16:96 it is obvious that it refers to a particular state of being in the presence of God. The Mother Book is with Him, i.e., the source of everything is with Him. There are entities in His presence who are constantly praising and praying to God. This state is not a physical one - it is purely spiritual. This may be true of the person whose body is within the boundaries of Throne and the space. It is true of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And among His signs is this, that seest thou the earth barren, but when send We down on it water, it is stirred and swelleth; verily He Who giveth it life, will certainly give life unto the dead; (Refers to resurrection.) Verily, He hath power over all things. See 41:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: A Bearer of glad tidings and a Warner, but turn away most of them and hearken not. The qualities 'Bashir' and 'Nazir' mentioned in this verse refer to the believers and the righteous ones and as well as warning to the disbelievers and the evil doers.

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who distort (Cause distortion in the Signs.) (a) Our signs are not hidden from Us. What! is he then who is cast in the fire better or he who cometh safe on the Day of Judgment? Do ye what ye like; Verily seeth He what all ye do. See 41:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it cometh unto them, and verily it (Qur'an) is a Book Unassailable. (Mighty, Triumphant.) Qur'an depicted as unassailable in complete conformity with verse 15:9 and it refutes the possibility of being tampered by anyone. Lit. Descension1. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Shall come not nigh it falsehood from before it nor from behind it: a revelation from the All- Wise, the Most Praised One. See 41:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nothing is said unto thee save what indeed was said unto the apostles before thee; Verily, thy Lord is the Lord of forgiveness and the Lord of grievous retribution. See 41:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And had We made it a Qur'an (A recital.) in a slang (Inexpressive.) language, certainly had they said: "Why are not its verses been made plain? What! in a slang (tongue)? (This is what the people would have said if the Qur'an had not been in the plain eloquent language as it now is.) while the Prophet is Arabian" Say: "It is unto those who believe a guidance and a cure; but as to those who believe not, there is in their ears a heaviness and it is unto (such of) them a blindness; These are like unto those who are called to from a place far off. (Refer to verses 41:3 & 43:3.)" Other translators have translated – 'Ajami' as foreign but it is opposed to Arabic which is used as a quality of the Arabic tongue to depict…

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed, gave We Moses the Book, but disputes arose therein: and had not a word already gone forth from thy Lord, there would certainly have been judgment (Sentenced.) between them; and certainly they are about it in a disquieting doubt. See 41:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whosoever doeth good, it is for his own self, and whosoever doeth evil, it is against it; and 1 is not unjust unto the thy Lord servants. See 41:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Unto Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour (of Reckoning); And cometh not forth any of the fruits from its covering, and beareth not any of the females, and nor doth she delivereth, but with His (God's.) knowledge; and on the day when He shall call unto them (saying). "Where are (those whom ye made) My partners?" They shall say: "We declare unto Thee, there is not from us any witness," Since everything in the universe is only that which God made, nothing can ever be hidden from Him and nothing can ever act without God's will. Everything and every act, big or small, manifest or hidden, is only open in the knowledge of God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall pass away from them what they called upon before, and they shall know that for them there is no escape. See 41:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Tireth not man in praying for good, and if toucheth him any evil, then is he despaired, hopeless. See 41:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "Our hearts are under coverings from that unto which thou inviteth us, and in our ears is a heaviness, and between us and thee hangeth a veil, so act thou (as thou thinkest right): Verily we too act (as we do)" It was either to the superiority complex under which the people mostly laboured that the people sarcastically said that their hearts were not intelligent enough to understand the high ideals nor were their ears sufficiently acute to hear their exposition, as if the Holy Prophet and the people were quite different from each other and there could never possibly be any conciliation between them and hence why should he worry about them. They wanted him to have his own way and they would have their own.

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if We make him taste mercy from Us, after a distress hath toucheth him, certainly sayeth he: "This is my due; and I deem not the Hour (of Reckoning) would ever be established (Will ever come to happen. Refer to verses 18:35 - 18:36.) : and if I be returned unto my Lord, verily for me (is stored) with Him is (much of the) best;" but certainly will We inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and certainly will we make them taste of a hard chastisement. See 41:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when bestow We (Our) bounties on man, he turneth away, and withdraweth himself; and when toucheth him any distress, then aboundeth he in long prayers. See 41:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "See ye then? If it (i.e. this Book Qur'an) is from God, and yet disbelieve ye in it, who is farther astray than he who is in (such a great) opposition far away (from truth)?" See 41:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Soon will We show them Our signs in the horizons (of the world), and in their own selves until it becometh manifest unto them that He is the Truth. Is it not sufficient for thy Lord that He ('O' He, Who proves His existence with His Own Self.') is a witness over all things. Truth needs to be raised by anyone but it rises of its own accord, rises and spreads by itself. It is a heavenly challenge to the opposition from the people that signs of the triumph of Islam would be shown even among the very people in the place of its very start and also in the remote extremities of the world. Mecca which in the start had become a furnace of the fire of opposition and enmity and the seat or the headquarters of all hostilities…

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Be it known that) verily they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord! (Be it known that) verily He encompasseth (Penetrates.) every thing. See 41:53

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "I am only a man like you; it is revealed (The distinction of being in communion with God definitely separates him from ordinary men.) unto me that your God is One God, be ye then in attention straight unto Him, and seek ye His forgiveness; and woe unto those who associate others with God," 'I am a man like you.' This statement qualified by 'it has been revealed to me' - gives a unique and distinguishing position to the Holy Prophet among mankind as a whole. Though a man for all purposes of appearance and nature, is an animal but endued with the extraordinary and the unique excellence of conscience and reasoning qualifying him for the communion with the Lord, distinguishes him as a separate specie other than the ordinary animals.Similarly, the one among…

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who give not the poor-rate, (In Arabic, Zakat. This is a reference to the Muslims who avoid giving Zakat and are not mindful of the life hereafter.) and they in the hereafter too are disbelievers. 'Zakat' here may mean giving for the sake of God - though they may give in the form of charity for motives not godly, otherwise the disbelievers were not expected to pay the 'Zakat' prescribed by the faith of Islam. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who believe and do good, for them shall be a recompense ceaseless. See 41:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Fussilat:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "What! do ye indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days (periods), and set ye up unto Him equals? that is the Lord of (all) the worlds" The term 'days' used in this verse, and the next verses besides the others, in the Holy Qur'an, can never be in the sense or the measure we use it, in the ordinary meaning of the word. A day to us is a measure of the time calculated according to the movement of earth in relation to the sun. When the sun and the earth and nothing else exist, the term day would necessarily mean something other than what we mean with it on earth under the sun. The term 'day' here means stages or periods. Here the Two days would mean the Two main stages, i.e., physical…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: 'Alif Lam Ra. (A L. R.) (this is) a book whose verses are firmly arranged (together) then separated (in revelation) from the All-Wise, the All-A ware (Refer to verses 17:106, 25:32.) . 'Alif Lam Ra - A. L. R.This verse has been interpreted in several ways. All mean a separate description and quality applicable to Qur'an but the translation and interpretation here is more appropriate and it is in complete accord with the verse 17:106, which shows Qur'an had a pre-existence in a well-arranged and a perfectly collected form of a Complete Book. The separation of the Verses, Chapters took place in the course of the gradual revelation to make it easy for people to understand, remember and digest it. Refer to verses 17:106 & 28:321. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if We make him taste (Our) favours after distress hath afflicted him, he will surely say: "The evils have (all) gone away from me;" Verily he is joyous, boastful See 11:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:100 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This is of the account of (the fate of) the townships We relate unto thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) of them some are standing and some have been mown down (by the passage of time) See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:101 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We did no injustice unto them, but they were unjust unto themselves, so availed them not aught their gods whom they called upon besides God when came to pass the decree of thy Lord; they added not (aught to their lot) but perdition. See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:102 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Such is the grasp (of punishment) of thy Lord when graspeth (Punished.) He the townships while they are unjust; Verily His grasp (punishment) is painful, severe. See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:103 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, in this there is a sign for him who feareth the chastisement of the hereafter; This is a day for which mankind shall be gathered together, And this day shall be witnessed (by all) See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:104 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We delay it not but to an appointed (Numbered.) term. See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:105 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The day (when) it arriveth, no soul shall speak but by His leave; then (some) of them shall be wretched and (some) blessed. A) Ref. to the Resurrection Day. Here it is asserted that no soul shall speak without His permission. In 77:35 it is said on that day they will not be permitted to forward their excuses. In 55:39 it is said none neither men nor the jinn will be questioned. In 37:24 it is asserted they will question each other. In 41:21 it is said that they will ask their skins as to why they gave evidence against them. The answer from the skin will be that God made them speak. These and similar passages seem to be contradictory but we have already pointed out that the Resurrection Day has many stages - and stages each of which…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:106 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then as for those who shall be wretched, they shall be in the (Hell) fire, for them therein shall be sighing and groaning. The commentators have forwarded several views as to the exact meaning and significance of these Verses. The most appropriate one is to take these verses as referring to the conditions of the two classes of the wretched and blessed not after but before the Resurrection Day. It means people will be classified into two groups on the Resurrection Day prior to it. The groups of the wretched ones are kept in hell and torture as long as the heavens and earth endure subject to God's will which means there is the possibility of their being taken out even before the end of the heavens and the earth and similarly the blessed ones will be kept in Paradise…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:107 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They shall abide therein so long as the heavens and the earth endure, except (as) what willeth thy Lord; Verily thy Lord is the (Mighty) Doer of what soever He willeth. See 11:106

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:108 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And as for those who will be blessed, they shall be in the garden (of Paradise) abiding therein so long as the heavens and the earth endure, except (as) what thy Lord willeth; (it will be) A gift incessant. One of the commentators holds that the punishment after the Final Judgment will not be a permanent one. To establish this contention, he quotes this verse - interpreting 'As long as the heavens and the earth endure'. But this argument does not hold good for it will be a time when the heavens and the earth will also cease to be and it will be a time when this temporary earth and the temporary heavens would have been changed into another permanent earth and permanent heavens which will constitute Paradise. They will be real and everlasting. Thus, the suffering awarded after…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:109 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therefore be thou (The Prophet addressed for the people.) not in doubt concerning what worship these (people); they worship not but as their fathers did worship before (them); and verily We will certainly pay them back in full their (due) share without (any) rebate. See 11:108

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Except those who forbear and do good; these! for them is forgiveness and a recompense (very) great. See 11:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:110 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed gave We unto Moses the Book, (The Torah.) but variance was created in it; and had not a word (decree of respite) gone forth from thy Lord, the matter would surely have been decided between them; and verily they are in a doubt (about the Qur'an which is) disquieting (them). See 11:108

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:111 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily unto all will thy Lord pay back in full their recompense for all their deeds; verily He of what (all) they do is fully aware. See 11:108

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:112 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then stand thou fast (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) (on the Right Path) as thou art commanded (by thy Lord) and also he who hath turned (unto God) with thee, and (O' men) be ye not inordinate; Verily He (God.) (your Lord), what ever ye do, well-seeth. See 11:108

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:113 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (ye believers) incline ye not unto those who act unjustly lest toucheth you the (Hell) fire, for you besides God there is no protector, nor shall ye be helped. It is reported from the Holy Prophet that on the Day of Judgment an announcement will be made aloud. "Where are the iniquitous and the tyrants and those who assisted them, agreed with them, and those who used their pen and ink for them. Bring them all along with the iniquitous and the tyrants."

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:114 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And establish thou, prayer in the two ends of the day, and at the approaches of the night, Verily the good (Note the unique way Islam encourages man to good deeds with the promise to remove the evil ones in return.) deeds take away the evil deeds; This is a reminder for the (believers who are) mindful (of their Lord). This verse gives the ordinance about the five times of the prescribed daily prayers. This is another clear evidence against the fallacy in the claim of 'Hasbona kitabullah.' The Verse gives only the timings of the prayers and the details as to how they should be conducted and with what recitals of the passages of the Holy Qur'an, i.e., the wording of the prayers, which we have to get from the Holy Prophet. This fact clearly indicates that any heavenly…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:115 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And be thou patient, for verily God suffereth not to be lost the recompense of the righteous (ones). See 11:114

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:116 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But why were not there among the generations before you those endowed with understanding forbidding against mischief in the earth, except a few of those whom We delivered from among them? And pursued those who did injustice, what they were made to enjoy (of the plenty) and they were guilty. See 11:114

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:117 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nor was thy Lord (ever such) to destroy townships unjustly while its people were righteous. See 11:114

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:118 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And had thy Lord willed He would certainly have made men a single people, but they will cease not to differ, See 11:114

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:119 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Except he on whom thy Lord hath mercy; And for this did He create them; and the word (decree) of thy Lord is fulfilled; Certainly will I fill the hell with the jinn and the men, all together. This clearly indicates that God has left man to develop his native endowments at his own choice and did not force any particular way of life on man and asserts that there will always be differences save those who have submitted their limited will to God's universal will and has enjoined His blessings and mercy for which they had been created. That shows that those blessed with the mercy of God do not differ. That shows that those blessed with the mercy of God do not differ and those who differ are not blessed by His mercy. Hence the tradition justifies the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So perchance mayest thou (be inclined) to give up a part of what is revealed unto thee and becometh straitened thy breast by it lest they say: "Why hath not a treasure been sent down unto him or an angel come with him?" (Say thou that) Verily thou art only a warner; and God over all things is the Custodian! Ayashi in his commentary on the authority of Zaid Ibn Arqam, reports that the Messenger Angel Gabriel arrived on the eve of Arafat to convey the message of God's appointing Ali Ibn Abi Talib as the successor to the Holy Prophet. The Holy Prophet apprehending the opposition he was sure to encounter at announcing then the heavenly news to the men and recollecting the difficulties, tortures, persecutions and wars he had suffered at the announcement of his apostolic office and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:120 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And all that We relate unto thee of the accounts of the apostles is to confirm with it thy heart (The conviction of the people.) ; And hath come unto thee in this the truth, and an admonition and a reminder unto the believers. The Holy Qur'an is an admonition and a reminder for the true believers in God. In 2:2 there is a similar statement saying, that the Holy Qur'an is a Guidance for the Pious and in 3:137 is said that the Holy Qur'an is a mere statement for the ordinary people but an exhortation and a guidance for the pious.

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:121 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) unto those who believe not; "Act (ye) whatever ye can: and verily we (too) do act." See 11:120

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:122 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And wait ye! and verily we too do wait. See 11:120

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:123 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God's is the unseen (worlds) of the heavens and the earth, and unto Him (only) is returned the whole of the affair, so worship thou (Address to the people through the Prophet.) (only) Him and rely thou (Address to the people through the Prophet.) (only) on Him; and thy Lord is not heedless of whatever ye do. See 11:120

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or do they say: "He (Our apostle) hath forged it." Say thou! "Bring ye then ten suras (Chapters.) like unto it forged, and call ye (to your aid) whomsoever ye can besides God, if ye be truthful. (Refer to verses 2:23,10:38,17:88,52:34.)" For a similar challenge see 2:23, 10:38 and 17:88. It is noteworthy that all the other religious scriptures of the world are held holy and sacred simply because they relate to religious knowledge. There is nothing in any one of them to assert any of them being the Word of God with such a vehement and such a repeated challenge about its position. It is to say that the Holy Qur'an is not the work edited by the Holy Prophet or any mortal, but its author is none but God.It must be remembered that the challenge was in the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then if they answer ye not, then know ye that this (Qur'an) is revealed (only) by God's knowledge, and that there is no god but He! Will ye then submit (and be Muslims now?). See 11:13

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whosoever desireth the life of this world and its pomp, We shall pay them (the recompense for) their deeds therein, they shall suffer not any loss. Even the disbelievers if they do anything good will be duly recompensed then and there in this life as Qur'an repeatedly says that God never lets go any good unrewarded but they will have no share of it in the hereafter. Therefore, their deeds here will be of no value or avail to them in the life hereafter. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These are they for whom there is nothing in the hereafter but (the Hell) fire, and vain shall be (all) that they wrought in it, and vain shall be what they were doing. All that is acquired of the things of the enjoyment of this world will be made of no avail and every such act of seeming goodness done, not to earn the pleasure of God but only to make a show of godliness, will be made null and void on the Day of Judgment.Some commentators say that it is also a prophecy to say that whatever plot that will be devised against the Holy Prophet would be frustrated.The Sixth Holy Imam Jafar Ibn Muhammad as Sadiq says that the Holy Prophet said, "that seeking the enjoyment of this life which is only temporary and nothing but a passing…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is he then (like unto him) who hath a clear proof from his Lord and followeth him a witness from Him, and preceded by the Book of Moses, a guide (Lit. 'Imam'.) and a mercy (testifying it)? These believe in it (Qur'an.) ; and whosoever of the parties (of the idolaters) disbelieveth in it, the (Hell) fire is the promised place; so be thou (The Prophet addressed for the people.) not in doubt about it; verily it (Qur'an) is the truth from thy Lord; but most of the people believe not. The following renowned and celebrated Sunni authorities on the faith1 report: that once the Holy Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib said from the pulpit that there is not a single person from the Quraish about whom something or the other was not revealed (from God). A man stood up…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And who is more unjust than he who forgeth a lie against God? These shall be presented before their Lord, and shall say the witnesses: "These are those who lied against their Lord; Beware! (Now) verily the curse (Note - that cursing the Tyrants is a godly act - See the other verses also on this.) of God is on the unjust" The 'witnesses' mentioned in this verse refer to:The writer Angels (called Kiraman Katibin) who record the deeds of every individual then and there.The Apostle of God of the age and the place.The Holy Imam of the age.The various organs of the body of every individual.As regards Apostles of God, read verses:"But how (will it be with them) when We bring of every people a witness, and We bring thee (O' Muhammad) a witness against these?" (4:41)."And (bethink you…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who hinder (others) from the path of God and seek to make it crooked; and they in the hereafter, they are the disbelievers. See 11:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That ye should worship not (any one) but God; Verily I am for you from Him, a Warner and a bearer of good tidings. See 11:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These shall in no way weaken (God's design) in the earth nor shall there be for them besides God any protecting friends; The torment shall be doubled for them; They could not bear to hear and they used not to see. See 11:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These are they who have lost their selves and have left (Failed.) them (in lurch) (the false deities) what they (fancifully) used to forge. See 11:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Undoubtedly they are the very ones who in the hereafter will be the greatest losers. See 11:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily those who believe and do good and humble themselves unto their Lord, these are the dwellers of the Garden (Paradise), they will abide therein. See 11:18

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The similitude of the two parties is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing (ones) and the hearing (ones): What! Can they two be (compared as) equals? Will ye not then mind? If the blind and the deaf are compared to the disbelievers, the other group of the seeing and the hearing are naturally the believers. Among the believers those whose faith in God is perfect and flawless and whose practical life is wholly godly, are the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt, whose purity of soul and personal character and conduct is vouched by the divine declaration 33:33.In view of these facts, this verse is to guide us saying, that the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt can never be compared to the others and thus can never be superseded by anyone with any preference in any matter whatsoever.

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed sent We Noah unto his people (and he said unto them) "I am unto you a plain warner." See 11:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That (The purport of the teachings of every apostle of God was the belief in the Unity of God - worship only to Him and to lead a goodly and godly life on earth.) ye shall worship not (any one) but God; verily I fear for you the chastisement of a painful day. See 11:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then (Thus, the true believers were those who had no value for any worldly possessions - who love poverty and do not hate the poor) said the chiefs of those who disbelieved from among his people: "We see not (in) thee but a man like ourselves and we see not any have followed thee but those who are the meanest of us, at first thought (without discretion), nor see we (in) you any excellence over us, nay we deem you liars." See 11:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: "O' my people! think ye, if I be upon a clear proof from my Lord, and He hath bestowed on me mercy from unto Himself and it hath been made obscure unto you; shall we compel you to (accept) it while ye be averse from it?" See 11:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And, O' my people! I ask not of you any wealth in return for it; my reward is (with none) but with God and I will drive not away those who believe; verily they shall meet their Lord, but I see you a people (who act) ignorantly. See 11:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (to preach unto you) that "Seek ye the forgiveness of your Lord, then turn ye unto Him repentant, He will provide you with a goodly provision to an appointed term and bestow (bestows grace on everyone who deserves it.) on every gracious one endowed (Ibne Mardwaih says that 'Zil-Fazl' refers to 'Ali Ibn Abi Talib.) with grace; and if ye turn back, then verily I fear for you the torment of an awful day." See 11:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And, O' my people! Who will help me against God if I drive them away! What! will ye not then mind? See 11:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And I say not unto you that with me are the treasures of God; and I know not the unseen, nor say I that I am an angel; and say I not about those whom your eyes hold in contempt (that) God will never bestow on them (any) good; God knoweth best what is in their hearts, (Lit: -Selves.) for verily then (If I say that.) I should be of the unjust ones. See 11:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "O' Noah! indeed hast thou disputed with us and thou hast prolonged the dispute with us, now bring thou unto us what thou hast threatened (The wrath of God.) us with, if thou art of the truthful ones." See 11:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: (Noah.) "Verily God will bring it unto you only if He willeth, and ye shall by no means prevail against Him." See 11:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And will profit you not my good advice, if I intend to give you good advice if God willeth that He should leave you astray; He is your Lord! and unto Him (only) shall ye be returned. See 11:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or say they: "He (Muhammad) hath forged it (Qur'an)? Say thou! (The Holy Prophet.) If I have forged it, on me be my guilt, and I am free of that which ye are guilty." The people had charged Noah of having forged some matter and presenting it as the revelations from God. This is in reply to the charge. Some say that the reference in this verse is to the charge made by the heathens of Mecca against the Holy Prophet, saying, that the story of Noahwas only a fabrication, and the reply refers to what the people were told.

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And it was revealed unto Noah: that "never will any of thy people believe except those who have already believed, therefore grieve thou not for what they do" See 11:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And make thou an ark under Our (Under the direct protection and the care of God and His angels.) eyes and Our revelation and thou address (plead) not unto Me about those who are unjust; Verily they shall be drowned. See 11:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And he began making the Ark; and whenever the chiefs of his people passed by him, mocked they at him; Said he: "If ye mock at us, verily we too shall mock (The Condition of the mockers shall be as such which would justify any mockery. It does not mean that an apostle of God would retaliate in the mean manner.) at you, even as ye mock (at us)." When Noah began making the Ark, the people laughed at him and ridiculed saying that Noah was making the Ark to sail on the land and he was going to act as a sailor in it. Some said that he was making a wooden house for use in summer and some said he had gone mad:It is said that it took eighty years for the Ark to get ready until then…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Soon shall ye know who it is on whom descendeth a torment which will disgrace him, and on whom (ultimately) falleth a lasting torment. See 11:38

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Unto God is your return; and He over all things hath power. See 11:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Until when came Our command and water gushed forth out of the oven, said We: "Carry (thou O' Noah) in it two of each kind, a pair, and thy family, except him on whom the sentence hath already been passed, and those who believe". And there believed not with him but a few (The maximum number mentioned is 80 and the minimum is 7.) . (The Holy Prophet has compared his Ahl Al-Bayt to the Ark of Noah and those attached to the Ahl Al-Bayt are also few like those with Noah in the Ark.) When the Ark was completed, Noah was ordered by God to get into it his kith and kin and those of the believers, and a pair from each specie of the animals. Noah's three sons with their wives got in, and Kanan, son of Noah…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said he (Noah): "Embark ye in it, In the name of God be its sailing and its anchorage! Verily my Lord is Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful." See 11:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And it (the Ark) moved on with them amid waves (towering) like mountains; and Noah called out unto his son: and he was aloof, "O' My son! embark (See verse 69:11.) (thou) with us and be not with the disbelievers." See 11:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he (Noah's son.) "I will betake me unto a mountain that shall secure me from the water;" Said he (Noah): "There is no protector today from God's decree but (of whom) He hath mercy;" and a wave passed between them, so he was among the drowned (ones). Taking the description of Noah's Ark and the few who believed and joined Noah when the deluge submerged the land and all who remained behind, whether the members of his family or the others, perished and comparing it with the well-known saying of the Holy Prophet that the similitude of my Ahl Al-Bayt is that of the Ark of Noah and whoever got into it was saved and whosoever turns away from it got drowned, holds good, one will realise that only few were those who were saved from the destruction and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And it was said: "O' Earth! swallow down thy water, and O' sky! withhold (thy rain)! And the water abated, and the decree was fulfilled, and it (the Ark) rested on the (Mount) Judi; and it was said "Away with the unjust people!" See 11:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And Noah cried unto his Lord and said: "My Lord! Verily my son is of my family; and verily Thy promise is true, and Thou art the most just of the judges." The supplication of Noah aims to clear the doubt in the mind of his followers of the subsequent ages that mere birth or any other without the spiritual affinity with the prophets would not justify the application of the term, which besides relationship, implies the merit.Therefore, the term 'Ahl Al-Bayt'1 is restricted only to the deserving members of the House of the Prophets and the same restriction is applicable to the term of 'Relatives' which does not mean relationship in blood or in matrimony. Besides this means close affinity in character and spiritual attainment. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said, He (God): "O' Noah! Verily he is not of thy family; Verily he is (of) conduct other (Note that being the son of even a Prophet of God the lack of righteousness gets him disowned from the progeny of the apostolic family.) than righteous; There fore seek thou not of Me that of which thou hast no knowledge; Verily I admonish thee lest thou mayest be of the ignorant ones." Noah's pleading was for his own son, and the reply was that the lad was not worthy of being his son. It is made clear by this verse that though one might be of the same blood and flesh, might have been born to his parents, but if the issue does not possess the good qualities of his parents, he is not of his parents' stock. God rejecting the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: (Noah.) "O' My Lord! Verily I seek refuge in Thee from asking Thee that of which I have no knowledge; And if Thou forgiveth me not and have mercy on me, I should be of the losers." See 11:46

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It was said: "O' Noah! Debark (Get down from the Ark.) thou with peace from Us and blessings on thee and on the people (the springs) of those with thee; and there shall be (other) people (Not included in the blessings from God.) whom We shall afford provisions, then shall afflict them from Us a painful torment." See 11:46

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: These are of the tidings of the unseen which We reveal unto thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad); thou didst not know them thou (thyself) nor thy people (knew it) ere this; Therefore be thou patient; Verily the end is (only) for the pious ones. The opening words of this verse clearly indicate that all that is said of the ancient history in the Qur'an is that which was conveyed to the Holy Prophet through revelation and the knowledge which the Holy Prophet possessed, was that which he received from God and not acquired from any other source.

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Behold! Verily they fold (Hiding the hypocrisy individually or collectively Hearts.) up their breasts that they may conceal (their infidelity) from Him; Behold! when they put their garments as a covering knoweth He what (all) they conceal and what (all) they make known; verily knoweth He (all the inmost secrets) of the breasts (Hearts.) . 'Folding the breast or the bosom' is a term to indicate hiding or concealing of enmity.Ayashi reports on the authority of Jabir Ibn Abdullah that whenever the idolaters saw the Holy Prophet, they used to hang their heads before them and cover their head with some garment so that they might not see him.Ibn Abbas reports that the concluding word of this verse refers to the hypocrites who concealed their envy and enmity against 'Ali which the Holy Prophet said that after his departure from…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And unto (the people) 'Ad (We sent) their brother Hud. (Refer to verses 7:65, 53:50 & 89:6.) Said he: "O' my people! Worship ye (the Only) God, ye have no god other than He; ye are but forgers." (Of false creeds.) See 11:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' my people! I ask you not on it any recompense; my recompense is only with Him Who created me; What! then ye understand not? See 11:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And O' my people! Ask ye the forgiveness of your Lord and then turn ye repentant unto Him, He sendeth clouds (Lit- Skies) on you pouring down abundant rain and addeth He strength to your strength, and turn ye not back as guilty ones. See 11:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "O' Hud! thou hast not brought unto us any clear sign (of your truthfulness) and we will desert not our gods on thy word! and nor are we believers in thee!" See 11:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We say nothing but that have smitten thee some of our gods with evil;" said he (Hud.) : "Verily I call God to witness, and bear ye also witness that I am clear (detach myself from what you associate.) of what ye associate, See 11:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Besides Him, and then conspire ye against me all of you and give ye no respite. See 11:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily I rely on God, my Lord and your Lord; there is no living creature but He holdeth it (in His control) by its forelock; Verily my Lord is on the Right (Never unjust to anyone.) path. See 11:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But if ye turn back, then indeed have I conveyed unto you that which I have been sent with unto you, and my Lord will make to succeed you, people other than you; and ye can not do harm unto Him in any way (In any thing or in the least.) at all; Verily my Lord is over all things the (ever) Protecting. 'Qummi' relates in his commentary that the 'Ad' were a people of strong build and huge stature. They lived in the forests. They worshipped idols. However much the Apostle Hud exhorted them to give up idol-worship and embrace Islam, they paid no heed to his advice. God caused a drought and for years together not a drop of water rained from heaven. At last a group of the people gathered at the door of Hud and a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when Our decree came (to pass), We delivered Hud and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us; and We delivered them from a (very) severe torment. See 11:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And this was (the people) 'Ad, they denied the signs of their Lord, and disobeyed His apostles, and followed the bid dings of every insolent tyrant. See 11:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: There is no moving creature in the earth but on God is its sustenance, And He knoweth its resting-place and its repository; All (things) (Everything.) is in the Manifest Book. See 11:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they were followed in this world by a curse and on the Resurrection Day (also); Behold! verily (the people) 'Ad disbelieved in their Lord; Behold! away with 'Ad the people of Hud. See 11:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And unto the (people) Thamud (sent We) their brother Salih. Said he: "O' my people'! Worship ye (none but the only) God; Ye have no god other than He; (Hear, O' Israel! the Lord, our God is one Lord: Deut 6/4 & Ephesians 4/5-6.) He raised you from the earth and hath given (made you flourish.) you to flourish therein; therefore ask ye forgiveness of Him, then turn ye repentant unto Him: Verily my Lord is (ever) Nigh, (ready) Responser." See 11:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "O' Salih! Indeed thou wert amongst us in whom (our) hopes were centred before this; Dost thou (now) forbid us from worshipping what our fathers did worship? And verily we are in a disquieting doubt about that unto which thou callest us." See 11:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: (Salih.) "O' my people! See ye not? if I am on a clear sign (guidance) from my Lord and He hath granted mercy (His apostleship) from Himself, who will then help me against God if I disobeyed Him? Therefore ye add not to my lot (anything) other than loss." See 11:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And O' my people! This is God's she camel for you, a sign (of my truthfulness), there fore leave her to (freely) pasture on God's earth and ye touch her not with (any) evil, for then will overtake you a ready torment. See 11:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Yet they did hamstring her, Then said he (Salih.) "Enjoy ye in your abode for three days; That is a promise not to be belied." If the people of Thamud deserved punishment for killing the She-camel assigned to God then a believer in Qur'an should think what would deserve those who killed the men and the children of the House of the Holy Prophet and took their women into captivity, whereas the holy ones were those whom the Holy Prophet had left along with Qur'an behind him recommending his followers to adhere to both. It is said the Holy Imam Husain prayed to the Lord when his baby son Ali was brutally killed in the field of Karbala when he was asking the enemy for a few drops of water to quench the killing thirst of the helpless innocent. O'…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When Our decree came (to pass), We delivered Salih and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and (We delivered them) from ignominy of that day; verily thy Lord, He is the Strong, the Mighty. See 11:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And seized those who were unjust the (mighty) blast so they became in their homes motionless corpses, See 11:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: As though they dwelt not in them; Behold! Verily (the people) Thamud disbelieved in their Lord; Behold! verily away with (the people) Thamud. See 11:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed Our messengers (the angels) came unto Abraham with glad tidings; Said they: "Peace! (Abraham in reply), said (And on you also be) "Peace"! and delayed not to bring a roasted calf." See 11:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six (Refer to verses 7:54, 10:14, 18:7, 21:35, 41:9, 67:2.) days - And His Throne was on the water - (He created the Heavens and the earth) that He might try you, which of you is best in conduct; And if thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) sayest, "Verily ye shall be raised up after death," surely would say those who disbelieve: "This is (not) but open sorcery." For a similar reference to the creation of heavens and the earth, see verses 41:9 - 41:12, 7:54.For the object of the creation of the Universe being only to prove the good and the bad among men, see verse 67:2.The concluding words of this Verse relate to what the disbelievers said against the Holy Prophet while explaining the life after death…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But when he saw that their hands extended (Reached. Refer to verses 7:80, 21:71 - 21:74 & 15:59.) not towards it, (The food which Abraham had offered.) (he) mistrusted (deemed strange.) them and conceived fear of them. Said they (the Angels): "Fear (thou) not; Verily we are sent unto Lot's people." See 11:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And his wife was standing (by), and she laughed, (ROT Gen. 18/10-12.) then We gave her the glad tidings of Isaac and after Isaac of (a son's (Grandson.) son) Jacob. See 11:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said she: "O' Woe unto me! shall I bear a son (now) when I am an (extremely) old (woman) and this my husband an (extremely) old (man)? (The wonder on the part of the Lady clearly indicates that her giving birth to Isaac was a miraculous act enacted by the Will of the Lord.) Verily this is a thing wonderful!" See 11:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: (The angels.) "What! wonderest thou at the decree of God? The mercy of God and His blessings be on ye, O' People of the House; (Arabic: Ahl Al-Bayt refer to note on verse 33:33. See note on the use of the address Ahl Al-Bayt on this note & verse 33:33.) Verily He (alone) is Praiseworthy, the All-Glorious!" Since in the mercy and the bounty of God offered in this verse to the people of the house of Abraham and Sarah the wife of Abraham happens to be the probable person included in the address of 'Ahl Al-Bayt' some commentators in their anxiety to find some argument, for their counting the wives of the Holy Prophet in the term, 'Ahl Al-Bayt' have said that since Sarah the wife of Abraham is included in the term 'Ahl Al-Bayt' used in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when had gone away from Abraham the awe and the glad tidings came unto him, he began pleading with Us for Lot's people. Owing to his being extremely merciful, Abraham began to continuously argue with the angels about the punishment they had come to inflict upon the people of Sodom but when he received the commandment from God, he kept fully reconciled with the will of the Lord.

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily Abraham was indeed forbearing, compassionate, oft- returning (to God). See 11:74

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' (Said God unto Abraham.) Abraham! Forsake this! Indeed the decree of thy Lord hath come to pass; and verily unto them cometh a torment (which is) irreversible. See 11:74

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when Our messengers (the angels) came unto Lot, he was grieved for them and felt his arm straitened (Helpless.) to protect them and said: "This is a distressful day." It is evident from the feeling of helplessness expressed by Lot that even being sinless like that of an apostle of God could not be sufficient to defend the people against any heavenly calamity.

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And came his people rushing unto him; for aforetime they did evil deeds; Said he (Lot): "O' my people! these my daughters are - they are purer for you, so guard ye against (the punishment of) God, and disgrace me not about my guests; Is there not among you a single man rightminded?" See 11:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "Indeed knowest thou that we need not thy daughters, and verily well-knoweth thou what we intend." See 11:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if We hold back from them the torment until a reckoned (Arabic 'Ummat'. Note - 'Ummat' has been used here as a distinguished time. This passage shows that there is a reckoned time of respite - It is not the Resurrection.) time, they will surely say: "What holdeth it back?" Beware! on the day it cometh to them it shall not be turned away from them, and will encircle them that which they used to scoff at (Refer to verse 45:33.) . See 11:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: (Lot.) "Would that I had strength to resist you or betake myself to a strong supporter." See 11:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: (The angels.) "O' Lot! Verily we are messengers from thy Lord! Never shall they reach thee! so depart thou with thy people while a part of the night remaineth, and let none of you turn back - but thy wife; Verily shall befall her what befalleth them; Verily their appointed time is the morning; Is not the morning nigh?" See 11:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So when Our decree came to pass, We turned their (township) upside down, and rained on them hard stones of baked clay, (spreading) layer on layer. See 11:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Marked (for punishment) with thy Lord; Nor are they (the ruins of their township) far distant from the unjust ones. See 11:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And unto (the people of) Midian (We sent) their brother Shu'aib. Said he: "O' my people! Worship ye God (alone); Ye have no god other than He; (Refer to note on verses 11:61, 7:73. O.T. Deut. 6/4 N.T. Eph. 4/5-6.) and give not short measure (Scale.) and weight, (Scale.) (Refer to verse 83:1 - 83:3.) Verily I see you in prosperity and verily I fear for you the torment of an all-encompassing day." Besides the great Prophets like Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and the Holy Prophet who were commissioned with the general and more comprehensive reforms of human life, the other prophets whose names have frequently been mentioned in the Qur'an seem to have been commissioned more to reform a particular aspect of human life more than a general one. For example, here 'Hud' was commissioned to divert the attention…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And O' my people! give ye full measure and (correct) weight in justice, and defraud ye not people of their things, (Dues.) and act not corruptly in the earth, making mischief. See 11:84

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:86 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That which is left by God unto you is good for you if ye be believers, and I am not over you a keeper. 'Sabbaghi', one of the renowned scholars of the Sunni School in his famous book 'Fusul al-Muhimmah' has related at length a tradition on the authority of the sixth Holy Imam Jafar Ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq - about the signs of the re-appearance of the Twelfth or the Last Holy Imam at the end of the world. The Holy Imam said: "When the Last one of us (the Holy Imams) will appear, there will be around him only (313). Three hundred and thirteen faithful ones of the believers. He would lean on the wall of the Holy Ka'ba and first of all recite this verse. And the people will address him as 'Baqiatullah', i.e., the Last or the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:87 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "O' Shu'aib! Doth thy religion enjoin thee that we should forsake what our fathers did worship or we (should forsake to) do with our property what we please? Forsooth (May be a mockery and it may be a remark of regard for Shua'ib was regarded by his people as such and they did not expect from him any thing of the warnings he issued against them. This meaning is supported by the next verse, 11:88.) thou art the one forbearing, the rightminded." See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:88 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: "O' my people! See ye not if I am on a clear sign (guidance) from my Lord, and (He) hath provided me from Himself, sustenance (pure and) good; and I desire not that in opposition to you I betake my self unto that which I forbid you from it; I desire naught but reform what (As far as I can.) I am able to (do); and my guidance is not but with God; On Him (alone) do I rely, and unto Him (alone) do I turn." See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:89 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And, O' my people! Let not (your) opposition to me cause you to sin, lest befalleth unto you the like of what befell the people of Noah, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih; and nor the people of Lot are far off from you. See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if We make man taste mercy from Us, (and) then take it off from him; Verily he is despairing, ungrateful. See 11:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:90 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And ask ye forgiveness of your Lord, and turn ye unto Him (repentant); Verily my Lord is All-Merciful, Loving-Kind. See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:91 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "O' Shu'aib We understand not much of what thou sayest, and most surely we see thee weak amongst us; and were it not for thy family we would surely stone thee; and thou art not against us powerful." See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:92 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he (Shu'aib.) : "What! Is my family more esteemed by you than God? and caste ye Him behind your back, with neglect? Verily, my Lord encompasseth what (all) ye do." See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:93 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And O' my people! Act ye according to your ability, I too am acting; soon will ye know on whom cometh the torment that will disgrace him, and who it is a liar; and watch ye, verily I too with you am watching. See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:94 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when came to pass Our decree We delivered Shu'aib and those who believed with him by mercy from Us; and overtook those who did injustice, the (mighty) blast so they became in their homes motionless corpses, See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:95 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (It happened) As though they dwelt not in them; Behold! away with (the people of) Midian even as were cast away (the people of) Thamud! See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:96 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We sent Moses, with Our signs and an authority (which was) manifest, See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:97 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Unto Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they followed the bidding of Pharaoh; and Pharaoh's bidding was no right directive. (Right-minded – correct.) See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:98 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He shall lead his people on the Resurrection Day, and bring them down to the (Hell) fire; but woeful will be the leading and the place led to. See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Hud:99 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They are followed by a curse in this (life) and (also) on the Day of Resurrection; And woeful is the gift which shall be given (unto them). See 11:86

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Alif, Lam, Ra, (A. L. R.) A Book (the Qur'an) (We) sent it down unto thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) that thou mayest lead out men from the darkness into the light, by their Lord's permission, unto the way of the Mighty, the (Most) Praised (One), Alif Lam Ra (A. L. R.)1'Anzalnahu-ilaik', i.e., We have sent it unto thee - indicates that the Holy Qur'an came down from the High in a Complete Book form2 and was not edited or compiled here on earth by anyone.The object of the revelation of the Book is given to be, to take out mankind from the darkness of ignorance and false belief into the correct knowledge about the truth about God, the Creator Lord of the Universe and the relation of the creation to Him. The guidance is meant for mankind as a…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said their apostles! What! about God is there any doubt, the Originator of the heavens and the earth? He inviteth (Subject to the people believing in the Truth and amending their wrong ways. Sins pardonable are not, those against the others for forgiveness of such Sins depends upon their forgiveness from those who have suffered at the hands of the sinner.) you to forgive for you your sins and grant you respite for a term appointed!" Said they: "Nothing are ye but men like unto us; ye intend that ye turn us away from what our fathers did worship, Therefore bring ye unto us some (Miracle.) authority manifesting. See 14:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said unto them their apostles: "(Yes) (nothing) we are but men like you but God bestoweth (Refers to the instructive aspects of the apostles of God.) His favours whomsoever He willeth of His servants; and it is not for us that we bring unto you any authority (Miracle.) except by the permission of God; And on God should the believers (True and genuine reliance is after exhausting all the native resources in the right way & then depending upon the divine mercy.) rely." Reliance or the dependence upon God demands remaining steadfast in the event of trials and sufferings and never resorting to seeking the help of anyone else other than God and the godly sources. The Seventh Holy Imam Musa Ibn Ja'far al-Kazim says that there are grades of 'Tawakkul' or dependence upon God. To depend upon God in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what reason have we that we should rely not on God, and indeed He hath guided us unto our ways; and surely we will endure whatever hurt ye may inflict on us; and on God (alone) should the reliant rely. See 14:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said those who disbelieved unto their apostles: "Certainly will we drive you out of our land or else ye return to our religion." So revealed unto them their Lord; "Certainly will We destroy the unjust ones." See 14:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And certainly We will settle you in the land after them; This is for he who presence (On the day of reckoning.) and who feareth My wrath. See 14:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And sought (Refer to verses 7:89 & 26:118.) they (the apostle's) help (from God against their enemies), and every insolent rebellious one was (As a result.) disappointed, See 14:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Behind (Arabic: 'Wara' - behind - but actually it will be in front of them - The evil doers never look forward - They see only the immediate present & the immediate past - So their future is behind their attention. A.P.) him is Hell and he shall be given to drink a festering (For detailed description refer to verses 18:29 & 47:15.) water, See 14:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He shall drink it little by little and shall not be able to swallow (Easily.) it, and will come unto him death from all sides but he shall die (Refer to verses 35:36 & 87:13.) not; and shall be behind him a vehement torment. See 14:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord; their deeds are like ashes on which bloweth hard the wind on a stormy day; they shall not have any hold (See verse 25:23.) on anything of what they have earned; this is a far-gone wandering. See 14:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Seest thou (People addressed through the Prophet.) not that God created the heavens and the earth with truth? If He willeth He will take you away and bring (in your place) a creation anew, See 14:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Of) God (it is) unto whom belongeth whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth; and woe unto the dis believers for a severe torment, See 14:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And this for God is not difficult. See 14:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they (Came forth.) shall come forth before God all together, then shall (Said.) say the weak unto those who were arrogant: "Verily we had been your followers, can ye therefore avert from us any part of the chastisement of God?" They would say: "If God hath guided us, we too would have surely guided you; it is the same to us (now) whether we implore (impatiently) or we are (Use patience.) patient, (now) there is not for us (any) way of escape." See 14:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And shall say Satan after the affair is decided: "Verily God promised you the promise of truth, and I gave you promises but failed to keep them to you; and I had no (Refer to verses 15:42, 34:21 & 17:65.) authority over you except I called you and ye responded unto me; so blame me not but (rather) blame yourselves; I cannot be your aider (now), nor can ye be my aiders; Verily I disbelieved in your associating me with God from before; Verily the unjust ones, for them shall be a painful chastisement." This clearly indicates the status of Satan and the Satanic forces and the extent of the authority exercised by them in relation to man and the false promises based on the partial view of the things and their authority is only to call and draw attention…

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And will be admitted those who believe and do good deeds to Gardens (of bliss) beneath which flow rivers, to abide in them by the permission of their Lord; their greeting therein will be 'Salam' (Refer to verses 10:10 & 56:26.) (Peace). See verses 10:10 & 56:26. In 56:26 it is said that they shall not hear in Paradise any vain talk save the mention of the blissful peace which they enjoy.

item.title: bil-Quran: Ibrahim:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Seest thou not how setteth forth God a parable? of a goodly word (being) like a goodly tree, whose root is firmly fixed, and its branches (reach) heavens, in the heavens, The Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq says that the Holy Prophet said: "I am the root of the Good Tree, Ali Ibn Abi Talib its trunk and the Divinely chosen ones; of the issues of Ali are its branches and the faithful ones attached to the Holy Ahl al-Bayt, its leaves."
