item.description: Or is it that unto them belongeth the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend with means (Ropes or ladders.) See 38:9

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what a mighty host of the clans shall here be routed. (This is a prophecy about the clans Ahzab, being utterly defeated by the Muslims which was an impossibility.) This is a prophecy saying that even when they would combine all the forces in the land, they could ally themselves with, they would suffer an absolute discomfiture and a total overthrow, miserably routed and crushed.1This is a prophecy about the fate of the group of the Allies which were to be defeated very soon.2 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And did belie before them the people of Noah, and 'Ad, and Pharaoh the lord, of stakes (of established authority), This is a reference to the fate of the previous people who disbelieved and rejected the truth. It is indirectly asked that should not the posterity of those who suffered before take a lesson from their ancestors.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And Thamood and the people of Lot and the dwellers of the wood; these were the clans. See 38:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Not one (of them) but did belie the apostles (from Me) so just was (My) retribution. See 38:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And wait not these (infidels) but a single (Trumpet) blast, there shall be no delaying (No recovery – no escape.) it. See 38:12

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (yet) they (dare to) say: "O' Our Lord! hasten on unto us our lot before the Day of Reckoning" May refer to what the disbelievers used to say in mockery. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Bear (thou) with patience what they say, and remember Our servant David, (who was blessed by Us) with the strength of hand, (and yet) verily he (was the one who) Oft-turned (unto Us in patience). See 38:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, We did subject the mountains to join with him in the hymns (of their Lord) at the night-fall and at sunrise, See 38:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the birds assembled together (to sing the hymns unto their Lord) and were unto him (David.) obedient. See 38:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay! those who disbelieve are (steeped) in self-exaltation and opposition. The disbelievers are involved in false dignity, rebellious pride and self-exaltation, - dissensions among themselves resulting into separation even among their own selves.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And made We strong his kingdom and bestowed We on him wisdom, and the clear (power of) judgment. Two Israelites came to David disputing about a cow. David demanded witnesses from the plaintiff but the plaintiff could not produce them. David asked the disputants to come to him the next day. At night in a dream David was commanded to slay the defendant, but since the crime was not proved by any evidence, he did not execute the decree and yet delayed the decision. When for three consecutive nights David had the same dream, David ordered the defendant to be executed. The defendant pleaded asking the grounds on which the sentence was passed. David replied that he had been commanded by God through dreams consecutively for three nights.When the defendant got sure of his death and helplessly confessed that he…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And hath the story of the litigants come unto thee? when they climbed the wall into the prayer room? Oriya the brother of David had asked for the hand of a woman in marriage to him. The match was fixed but at the last moment the guardians of the woman decided not to give her to Oriya and the match was consequently dissolved. David sent his message for the woman, and her guardians influenced by David's position as the king, gave her away to him in marriage. David had already 99 wives, and this woman added, the number was a complete 100. Oriya was hurt. David ought to have chosen the course preferable for him, i.e., to have used his good services and dominant influence to have somehow brought reconciliation between the girl's party and Oriya and got the woman…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When entered they upon David and he was frightened (Refer to verses 11:70, 20:21, 15:52, 51:53, 51:25 - 51:28.) of them, said they: "Fear (i.e., Surprised. Apostles of God are free from the ordinary fear experienced by the other mortals. Refer to note on verse 10:62.) (thou) not, (we are) two litigants, one of us hath exceeded against the other, so decide thou between us with justice, and act not unjustly, and guide us unto the right way." See 38:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, this my brother; he hath ninety and nine ewes and for me is but a single ewe;" but said he, "Make me the owner of that (also), and hath prevailed over me in arguing The angels in human forms said that one of them already had ninety-nine sheep and the other had only one, but the one who had 99 wanted to have the only one also which the other one had.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (David): "Indeed hath he been unjust unto thee in demanding thine ewe to add her to his own ewes: Verily many of the associates act wrongfully unto one another, save those who believe and do good deeds, and few are they!" And David perceived that We (God.) had tried him: so asked he the forgiveness of his Lord, and he fell down bowing and oft-turning himself (unto Us). David decreed that the demand was unjust. The disputants disappeared. David understood that they were angels sent to him by God to prove his indiscretion. It is said that David lay prostrating for 40 days praying to God for being forgiven and God granted his pardon to him.There are several other versions about David which are impossible to have ever taken place and the Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abi Talib said…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So We forgave him that (lapse), and verily for him with Us is a near approach, and an excellent resort. See 38:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' David! Verily We have appointed thee a vicegerent in the earth, so judge thou between the people with justice and follow not vain desires, lest it should take thee astray from the Way of God; for them shall be a severe chastisement for forgot they the Day of Reckoning. See verse 2:30.It is obvious that David as represented in the Biblical story of the wife of Oriya, does not agree to his divine position as the Vicegerent of God on earth. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We created not the heavens and the earth in vain: that is the imagination of those who disbelieve; then woe unto those who disbelieve - because of the fire. It is made crystal clear that the creation of the Universe has been with a definite plan of its Creator Lord and not an effect of any unintentional act or any purposeless accident.Thinking that the creation is an outcome of a mechanical accident - with no prepared design. (A.P.).Regarding the object of the creation of life and death and the jinns and men, see 67:2 and 51:56; 10:14, 11:7, 18:7, 21:35, 29:3. All these verses clearly say that there is the object of God, in bringing His Universe into existence.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Or) shall We treat those who believe and do good deeds like the mischief-makers in the earth? Or shall We treat the pious ones like the wicked (loose conduct.) ones? See 38:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad! this Qur'an is) the Book (Qur'an i.e., A Book complete.) which We have sent down unto thee, abounding in blessings, that they may ponder over its verses, and bear in mind those (who are) endowed (Mindful.) with understanding. See 38:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: How many We did destroy of the generations before them, and they cried while (there was no longer) the time to escape. Refers to the people who disbelieved the truth, when it was preached to them and who did not reflect and amend their faith and conduct and when respite was granted to them, i.e., they did avail of the respite to their profit and when the chastisement overtook them, they cried for help which was in vain. There was no way of escape left for them.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And to David We gave (a son) Solomon; an excellent servant (of Ours was he); Verily he was oft-turning (unto Us). See 38:27

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Remember when were shown unto him at eventide lightfooted coursers. (chargers horses.) Once while Solomon was busy seeing some horses which had been purchased for purpose of war against some disbelievers, found the time for the afternoon prayer had passed away and Solomon addressed the angels to get back the set sunlight to enable him to offer his prayers to God.By then the sun had set and the stars had appeared in the sky. By the prayer of Solomon the sun returned and it was again an afternoon and when he finished his afternoon prayers it was night again. This is what some commentators say but see A.P.'s note on verse 32.Twice did such a thing happen in the Islamic history, once after the Battle of Khaybar at the prayer of the Holy Prophet and again after the Holy Prophet,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then said he: "Verily I have loved the good things besides the remembrance of my Lord, until (Horse or the sun.) got hidden in the veil (of the darkness of the Night):" 'Khair' in the Arabic language has been used for quality horses.The point to be noted here is that 'Zikr' here cannot be taken to mean compulsory prayer, as otherwise he should have expressed his repentance. The disappearance may refer to the sun. Thus he missed the prayer or the horses - in which case it will mean that the prayer was delayed. Some commentators have taken 'Un' as due to - because the horses and their parade were meant for 'jehad'. Thus there is no question of missing any prayer optional or compulsory resulting in the returning of the sun or the cutting the legs of the animals.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Then said he): "Bring it back unto me!" And he began to rub the legs and necks. The interpretation of this verse, saying that the love of the horses interrupted his devotion to God. Solomon got the horses and slew them is absurd and impossible for an apostle of God to enact the cruelty to the poor animals. Solomon loved horses not for any vanity of possessing them for any worldly pomp and show. He had large armies and abundant wealth, not for himself, but to use it in the way of God. He waged wars not for any lust for blood or for any glory of a mere conquest but to bring men to the right course of faith and righteousness.When he found that in reviewing the horses the time for his devotional service to God had passed away,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We did try Solomon, and cast on his throne a (mere) body, then turned he (unto God). Once Solomon said that he would have a son from each one of his wives. Since he did not rest the fulfilment of his desire upon the will of God, only one of his wives was caused by God to bear a child and even that was a still-born. The woman brought the dead body of the baby and presented it by placing it on Solomon's throne. When Solomon got aware of the cause of the miserable failure of his intention being his neglect of saying 'Insha-Allah', i.e., if God wills, he turned repentant and engaged himself in prayers. Said the Holy Prophet Muhammad that if Solomon had only said 'Insha-Allah' God would certainly have had granted the sons as desired…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: "O' my Lord! Forgive me and grant me a dominion such as shall not befit any one after me, verily Thou alone art the Bounteous Bestower!" Solomon prayed to God for a Kingdom or authority which none else shall snatch it away from him after once he receives it. This prayer could imply Solomon's desire to live as a king unconquered by any one else. It could be his glory in the life after death of which he did not like to be deprived of by any shortcoming on his part in this life under any instigation from any satanic forces.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then We made subservient unto him the wind: it flew gently at his command whithersoever he desired. Solomon's prayer was granted with so many unique gifts.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the satans, (The satans also were employed in building & diving into the Sea.) every builder, and diver, See 38:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the others bound in chains; See 38:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This is Our gift, now give thou freely or withhold it, (for thou hast) not to render (any) account. See 38:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they did wonder that came unto them a warner from among themselves, and said the disbelievers: "This is a sorcerer, a great liar." The people called the Apostle of God as a Threatening Sorcerer.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily, for him unto Us is a near approach and an excellent resort. See 38:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And remember Our servant Job, when he cried unto his Lord; "Verily, Satan hath caused me an affliction and pain." See verses 21:83 & 21:94. There is a mention of Job in Chapter 21, but here some other details about him are given. The Holy Prophet is reminded of Job who was known for his extraordinary patience. He was the son of Ees and the son-in-law of Joseph. His wife was called Rahmat or Rahima. Job who was given abundance of wealth and issues was tested with the loss of everything he possessed. At every kind of loss Job only thanked God and remained patient. Lastly, he was tried with the sickness of his body with ulcers in it. Those who lacked faith in God suspected Job to have committed some sin to have been subjected to the tormenting sufferings…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Said We unto him); "Stamp thou with thy foot" thou this (spring) is (for thee) to wash with, (it is) cool, and a (refreshing) drink Job was commanded by God to strike at the rock and out of it gushed forth two springs, one of hot water for Job to wash his body of all physical ailments, and the other of cold water for him to drink and refresh his soul. Job was cured and his health was restored in full and he was once again a healthy fresh youth.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And gave him his family and the like of them with them, a mercy from Us and a reminder for those with understanding. See 38:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (it was said unto him) "Take in thine hand a bunch of (thin) stick (like fibre) and strike thou (thy wife) with it, and break not thine oath. Verily We found him steadfast; an excellent servant (was he): Verily he was oft-turning (unto Us)." Job had taken an oath that he would punish his wife for listening to Satan, with a hundred stripes. To be true to his solemn commitment in God's holy name, Job was commanded by God to strike her with a bundle of hundred sticks just to fulfil the oath.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And remember thou Our servants, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, men of strength and insight. See 38:44

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily We freed them (from sinning) with a distinction of remembrance of the (eternal) abode. Freed from all other objects of life - keeping up a pure quality, i.e., keeping in mind only the ultimate abode. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, they are with Us, of the chosen ones, the good ones. See 38:46

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And remember Ishmael and Elisha and Dhu'l-Kifl; they all were of the good ones. See 38:46

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This is a reminder; and verily, for the pious ones there is an excellent resort, The whole chapter continues, reminder after reminder about the chosen servants of God. The verse clearly indicates that remembrance and the commemoration of the lives of the chosen servants of God, is commendable in the view of God. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! maketh he (The Warner i.e., the Apostle.) the gods to be but one God? Verily this is a thing indeed strange! The disbelievers wondered at the Unity of God against their polytheistic belief in the many gods of their own imagination and fancy.This is the main reason of Quraysh opposition that they did not want to give up the bureaucratic system of life which was the outcome of the idol worship or the idol worship was the outcome of the system. They did not like to give up idolatry and to surrender or submit to one authority. Here in the beginning of Islam they expressed their surprise and later on, when Islam established its theocratic form of Government in the person of the Holy Prophet as the Vicegerent of God, they said 'Is there for us the authority to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Gardens of eternal bliss, opened for them are the doors (thereof). See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Reclining therein, calling therein for many a fruit and drink. See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And with them shall be of modest gaze, equals in age. See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This is what ye are promised for the Day of Reckoning. See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, this is Our sustenance; for it there is no end, See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This (for the righteous); and verily for the wicked ones there a wretched resort, See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hell, they shall enter it, and so evil is the place, See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Even so, Let them then taste it - boiling water and gore, (The dirty wash from rotten wounds in a body.) See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And other (torment) similar to it, of various sort! See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (To their leaders it shall be said) "This army (of your followers) shall be thrown headlong with you! No welcome for them! Verily they shall enter the fire!" See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the chiefs from them get away (impatiently, exhorting the others saying): "Walk ye away hence and be steadfast unto your gods: verily this is (but) with something designed against us!" 'Shaiyun Yuraad', i.e., thing designed.Behind this doctrine there is some plan against us. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They (The followers.) shall say: "Nay! ye (The leaders.) too! there shall be no welcome for you; Indeed ye did prepare this for us; and wretched is the abode!" See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They (The followers.) shall say: "O' our Lord! Whoever (The leaders.) hath brought this for us, increase Thou a twofold torment in the fire." See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they shall say: "What (This is what the inmates of the hell will say - among themselves.) hath happened unto us that we see not the men whom we counted among the wicked (Vicious.) ones?" See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! was it that we (wrongly) took them to scorn, or have our eyes turned from them? See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, this is truth - the wrangling of one with another of the inmates of the fire. See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "I am only a warner and there is no god but God the One, The Almighty!" See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Lord of the heavens and the earth, and what is between them two, the Almighty, the Most Forgiving. See 38:49

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "It is a message of (great) importance," According to the Ahl Al-Bayt the great message of importance, is the vicegerency of man on earth - the Imamat over the creatures of God. This interpretation is supported by verse 78:3, which was the disputed one, and this was the subject of dispute among the angels1 - and in verse 68 - wherein the turning away of man is referred to, again - there is the reference to the dispute in the angelical sphere about it.2 It is a fact of history that man always revolted and disputed about the vicegerency in the earth.Of the theological doctrines forwarded in the Holy Qur'an, the great and the important one, in its comprehensive or all-embracing nature, is the doctrine of absolute theocracy over the entire universe, represented on the earth by the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (And) ye are turning away from it. See 38:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: I had no knowledge of the exalted (The heavenly beings.) chiefs when they disputed! See 38:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We heard not of this (Such a unity of One Absolute God.) in the former creed. This is nothing but an imposture: 'Ikhtilaq', i.e., a fabricated tale.People were so deeply sunk in idolatry and were so much intoxicated with pride and self-exaltation, that they called the Truth a made-up or a fabricated tale. The reference here is to the immediately preceding faith, i.e., Christianity, saying that unity being absent among the Christians themselves, is a clear proof of their having departed from the purely monotheistic religion preached by Jesus, having adopted the polytheistic Trinity which the pagans say that they did not find any trace of the Unity of God in it.Such a unity - The Jews believed in their national god and the Christians besides Trinity, they allowed the image worship of the saints. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is revealed unto me save that I am an open Warner. See 38:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Remember when thy Lord said unto the angels: "Verily I am about to create man from clay," See 38:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when I have completed and have breathed into him of My spirit, then fall ye prostrating (Note: the prostration to Adam ordained by God Himself - Every prostration is not polytheism.) in obeisance unto him. 'Taswiya' and its derivations have been used in Qur'an for Adam and for the Holy Prophet and the apostles1- it refers to the state of establishment of the cognitive self in such a zenith of realization which enables to have an equal view of all things and that was the state with which Adam was honoured and the angels view was only one-sided. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And did fall prostrating in obeisance the angels all together, See 38:72

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Save Iblis; he was proud and was of the disbelievers. (Note: Refusal to prostrate to the Vicegerent of God is 'Kufr' infidelity.) See 38:72

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (God): "O' Iblis! what prevented thee that thou shouldst not prostrate in obeisance unto him whom I created with My two hands? (Hands refer to the two aspects Spiritual & physical excellence endowed in Adam. See note.) Art thou proud or art thou of the exalted (Indicates that there are some exalted ones who need not prostrate to Adam. Refer to verse 33:33.) ones?" Refers to the two aspects of the spiritual and the physical realms – one as the manifestation of His name 'Az Zaahir', the Manifest, and the other manifestation of His name 'Al-Baatin' - the Hidden. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: "I am better than he: (Adam.) Thou hast created me of fire and Thou didst create him from clay." He was proud of the power of the activity of the nature of the fire he was made of, and despised the infinite power of recipiency of the clay of which Adam was made. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (God): "Begone thou out of it, (God's grace or Heavenly Bliss.) for verily thou art the outcast one!" See 38:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily on thee shall be My curse to the Day of Judgment. See 38:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He said: "O' my Lord! then Respite me to the Day when they (Adam and his posterity) will be raised," See 38:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (What!) Hath the reminder been sent down (only) unto him (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) among us?" Nay! they are in doubt about My reminder, Nay! they have yet tasted not My chastisement! The people said that if any message from God had to be conveyed to them, why should it come to the orphan son of Abdullah, for it ought to have come to one of the rich ones, i.e., the chiefs among them.The reply is also contained in the verse saying that the people had no clear or correct idea as to how God executes His Will. Apostleship or the agency or the medium of the divine guidance like the 'Risalat' apostleship or the 'Imamat' does not need any worldly pomp and show of wealth or possessions. It needs men of ideal purity of soul and body. It needs…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (God): "Verily then thou art of the respited ones," See 38:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Till the day of the time made known! See 38:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: "Then by Thy Might, I will certainly beguile them all," See 38:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Save Thy servants from among them the freed (Refer to note on verse 33:33 freed from sinning.) ones, See 38:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He (God.) said: "Then it is the truth - and the truth do I speak," See 38:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Certainly, will I fill hell with thee and with those who follow thee, all (together) See 38:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:86 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "I ask ye not for any recompense for it; nor am I of the imposters" There is no doubt that the Holy Prophet was commanded to ask for a recompense1 as an exception to other prophets and as pointed out in 24:47 - the reward asked for was in the interest of the people themselves, i.e., the people who wanted to find a way towards their Lord.2 But this roused an objection as in the clause 'Imposter' is implied. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:87 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is naught but a Reminder unto the worlds (i.e., to mankind as a whole.) 'It' refers to the recompense asked for in verse 42:23. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:88 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And certainly ye will come to know about it after a time. History records the guidance the world has and will have to the end of the world, by the Ahl Al-Bayt. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saad:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or is it that with them are the treasures of the mercy of thy Lord, the All-Mighty, the Greater Bestower? If they have all the means, power and authority to set themselves up against the independent and Omnipotent authority of God about His choosing His own men for His mission, let them mount up into the heavens, and see if they could do it at all.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: All praise is God's, Whose is whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, and His is all praise in the hereafter; and He is the All Wise, the All-Aware. This is against the polytheistic view of dividing the universe into different regions and believing in different gods and deities ruling the different regions. Everything in the heavens and the earth and in between belongs to none but the One and only Creator Lord, hence praise of every kind and in any degree is His. The faith in this fact is of so much importance that it has been repeated in the Holy Qur'an (viz. Surahs 1, 6, 18, 34, 35) so that every sensible one of the human race be repeatedly reminded that there is none else other than God, and He alone is the Benefactor…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed gave We unto David from Us, a boon (Indicates what was granted to David, was something extraordinary as a miracle.) saying: "O' Mountains! sing ye the praise of God along with him, and (ye) the birds (Too);" and made We soft for him, the iron, See verses 21:79, 38:17 - 38:19. David had been gifted with an enchanting melodious voice and whenever he sang the glory of God, the mountains around, used to echo the praise and the birds sang along with him in chorus, and iron, which in one of the hardest metals, was made soft in the hands of David for without heating the metal, David could make it pliant enough for making the armour. It is said that David was the first to manufacture coats of mail and the mail armour. Note, as an apostle…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Saying (unto David): "Make thou coats of mail, and measure its links and do good; verily I, of what all ye do, do see." David used to ask everyone he met as to how the man found him (David) as the Ruler. This he did to know if he was just and impartial to all and if anyone had been wronged, so that the necessary redress might be effected. Once God sent an angel in the form of a man and when David was passing a street of his town at midnight, the angel met David and David asked him how he found the Ruler (David). The reply was that the Ruler was all right save that he takes his own sustenance from the public funds. David wept for forty days and prayed to God to teach him some profession.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And for Solomon (We made subservient) the wind which travelled in the morning a month's journey and a month's journey in the evening; And We caused for him to flow a fountain of molten brass and of the jinn there were those who worked before (In his presence.) him by the command of his Lord; and whoever among them turned away from Our Command, We will make him taste, of the chastisement of the flaming fire. See verse 21:81. For other references to Solomon - See verses 2:102, 4:163, 6:85, 27:15 - 27:44, 34:12 - 34:14, 38:30 - 38:40. For Solomon's Navy - See I Kings 9/26 - For the control over time and distance Solomon could command - see 27:38 - 27:39.Regarding the jinn being made to serve under Solomon. See also 27:17. The jinns must naturally be some…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They made for him whatever he willeth of fortresses and statues, and basins (large as) reservoirs, and (huge) cooking cauldrons immovable from their places; "Act ye gratefully, O' family of David! and very few of My servants are grateful!" Of the structure erected by men and the jinns, is the Big Mosque at Jerusalem. It is said that God revealed to David saying: 'I had covenanted with thy father (ancestor) Abraham that I would bless his seed1and multiply it and make it a great nation for he (Abraham) had offered the sacrifice of his son at Our Command and I too have fulfilled my promise to him but his seed has turned ungrateful to My Grace and Bounties. I shall send a chastisement on them.' They were visited by plague and by David's prayer were relieved of it. The Lord…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when We decreed death for him (Solomon), nothing did show them his death, but a worm of the earth which gnawed away his staff; and when it fell down, then came to know the jinn that had they known the unseen, they would have tarried not in the humiliating torment (of their toil) The Eighth Holy Imam Ali ibn Musa ar-Ridha said that once Solomon told his courtiers that "though God has blessed me with the greatest kingdom which none ever had and has favoured me with unique gifts of control over men, jinn, animals and birds - even the knowledge of the language of the birds - I am not even for a moment happy over all these. I want to get on the top of my palace and have a full view of God's Kingdom around me,…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed for (the children of) Saba in their abode, there was a sign; two gardens on the right and the left; (and it was said unto them) "Eat ye of the sustenance of your Lord and give ye thanks unto Him"; A good land (it was, in this world) and (God is the) Lord Oft- Forgiving! The place referred to, is the town of Ma'rib' herein lived the children of Saba son of Yaskhab son of Yaghrab son of Qahran, situated near Yamen. The place was Saba, i.e., the Sheba of the Bible.1 The place flourished with profoundly yielding fruit gardens. The soil was very rich with abundant fresh water. The place was also free from venomous serpents and insects. The climate was very pleasant. There were twelve townships and each had an apostle from God inviting the people to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But they turned away, so sent We upon them a torrent irresistible and in place (God's blessings when not used duly, are snatched away and substituted with curse.) of their two gardens gave We unto them two gardens yielding bitter fruits and tamarisks and a few lote trees. This verse is the continuation of the previous one. The people turned ungrateful and corrupt. The bursting of the dyke of Ma'rib and the destruction of the town by floods are facts of history (See Palmer's note). Thus, the people were punished by the destruction of their habitation, their gardens and their cultivation for the people had become arrogant of their prosperity, their skill and of the achievements of their ancestors (the dams or the dykes). For the report about the traces of the Ma'rib Dam - see Arnald's report on his…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This We recompensed them for what they disbelieved; but do We (thus) recompense any save the ungrateful? The cities were so prosperous that borders of one, practically met that of the other, or was very near the other - i.e., one city was joined with the other, owing to its near proximity or through the straight road connecting each with the other. The cities were connected with highways to the great flourishing kingdoms on the Euphrates and Tigris valleys on the one hand and Egypt on the other, and the great Roman Empire around the Mediterranean and at the other end, the Yemen coastal cities and seaports - To India, Malaya and China. The close proximity of the thickly inhabited stations, the travellers on foot could travel with ease and safety without any opportunity for any highwaymen to attack or…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We caused between them and the towns which We had blest, (other) towns to be seen, and We have made easy the journey therein; travel ye through them nights and days, secure. (With perfect ease and safety.) See 34:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then said they: "O' our Lord! make the spaces to be longer between our journey" and unjust were they unto themselves, We made them stories (Passed them into tales - destroyed them and made their life, example for others) and scattered them with a total scattering; Verily in this are signs for every patient, grateful one. The roads were so safe that the ease and the security was availed of, both by the rich and the poor alike and the rich only envy the poor being equalled to them in their travel. The people of Saba became more and more covetous and selfish and departed from the path of righteousness and became jealous of the other people's prosperity and happiness. Thus, they were denied the grace and the bounties bestowed on them. They lost the blessings which they enjoyed, and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Knoweth He whatever that passeth (Lit. Thirst.) into the earth and whatever that cometh out of it, and whatever that cometh down from the heaven and whatever that goeth up unto it; and He is the Most Merciful, the Oft-Forgiving. Everything hidden and manifest, is known to God and to God alone - Man in his ignorance thinks anything that is dead and buried is lost. Take for instance, the water absorbed by the earth or the seed sown into the soil, replenishes numerous streams and feeds the numerous forms of life and helps the growth of myriad forms of growth which grow and perish, and once again grow, continuously repeating their births and deaths. There are the other things beyond time and space, independent of any physical form. Man thinks that death is the end of the life whereas…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed 'Iblis' (Satan.) found true (Refer to note on verses 6:48 & 15:42.) his conjecture concerning them, so they followed him, except a section of the believers. Satan prayed for a respite and had challenged to lead the children of Adam astray and bring them under his sway save a few.1 The people of Saba, of their own conduct, proved the challenge of Satan true concerning them, save a small group of the sincere believers in God who remained steadfast in their faith and righteousness. This is what has happened in the followers of every apostle of God Excepting the Holy Ahl al-Bayt and those who follow them faithfully, the rest have been led astray by the agents of Satan who appeared in the forms of the false leaders of the faith, while they were devils in human form…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And there is not for him any authority (Refer to note on verses 14:22, 15:42 & 17:65.) over them, (The believers.) save that We would know (distinguish) him who believeth in the here after, from him who is in doubt concerning it; and thy Lord is upon all things a (Ever-watchful – protector.) Guard. See 34:20

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "Call ye upon those whom ye deemed (as gods) besides God; they own not the weight of (even) an atom in the heavens nor in the earth, nor for them is any partnership (share) in either (of them) nor for Him is (there) from among them any one to back up." This refers to the false gods and the imaginary deities the people believed in, who owned no power nor any authority even to help themselves and more so, to help any of their votaries if caught in any distress.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And will avail not aught any intercession with Him save of him whom He hath permitted, Until when terror shall be removed from their hearts, they shall say: "What is it that your Lord said?" They (the angels) shall say: "(that which is) True and He is the Most High, the Greatest!" See 34:22

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Who provideth you with sustenance from the heavens and the earth?" Say thou: "(It is) God, and verily (either) we or ye are guided (Both sides can not be right - any one side must surely be guided aright and the other in error.) aright, or in manifest error?" It asserts that both sides can not be right. It refutes the subjective value which the theosophists attach to every religion saying 'all are subjectively true'. Qur'an asserts that the religions should be valued objectively and both the opposite objects cannot be true. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Ye will not be questioned as to what we are guilty of, nor shall we be questioned as to what ye do." See 34:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Our Lord will gather us together, then will He judge between us with justice; and He is the Greatest Judge, the All Knowing." See 34:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Show me those whom ye associate with Him: Never (can ye ever do (Never can ye show for they do not exist - They are mere imaginations.) it); Nay! He is God the All-Mighty, the All-Wise." See 34:24

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) We sent thee not but unto the whole of mankind, a Bearer of glad tidings and a Warner, but most of the people know (it) not. See verses 4:49, 7:158, 21:107. The mission of the Holy Prophet Muhammad, was not for any one family, tribe, race or nation, but for mankind as a whole and for all times.1 His message is for all men and women. For those who turn to God, there are the glad tidings for them and to those who reject it, therein is the warning they need against their sinful life and the consequent punishment for it.It means that most of the people do not appreciate the universality of the mission of Muham mad who was the Last of the prophets. Even among the Muslims, there are some narrow-minded historians who…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "When will this promise be (fulfilled)? If ye be truthful." See verses 3:144, 7:34, 10:49, 15:5, 16:61, 23:43, and 62:8. When the appointed hour comes the respite automatically ends.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say those who disbelieve: "The Hour (of Judgment) shall not come upon us." Say thou: "Yea: By my Lord, the Knower of the unseen, it shall certainly come upon you, from Him is not hidden, the weight of (even) an atom in the heavens and nor in the earth, nor is there aught less than this and nor aught greater, but it is in the manifesting (Which is perspicuous.) Book," See verses 6:59 and 36:12. It is a matter of certainty which every man and woman has to necessarily believe that the phenomenon of cause and effect, works in the matter of the consequences or the recompense of every act good and bad enacted in this life. No doubt there is the mercy of God which has to be earned. In getting astray from the right path is betraying…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "For you is the appointment of a day from which ye cannot hold it back (even) a while, nor can ye hasten it on." See 34:29

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say those who disbelieve: "Never will we believe in this Qur'an, nor in that which is before (The previous Scriptures.) it;" but couldst thou see when the unjust shall be made to stand before their Lord; returning reproaches from one unto another! Those who were despised (Deemed and looked down as weak.) as weak will say unto those who had prided: (Considered themselves as great.) "Had it not been for you, we would certainly have been believers." The reference is to the people rejecting not only the Holy Qur'an but also the other previous scriptures which contained the prophecies about the advent of the Last Apostle of God who would be the Universal Teacher for mankind as a whole. The people of the Book, in their proud assumption of being on the right path and being superior to all…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who had prided shall say unto those who were despised (Deemed and looked down as weak.) as weak: "What! did we turn you away from the guidance after it had come unto you? Nay! ye were yourselves the guilty ones." There will be mutual reproaches and accusations between the misleaders and the misled but none of them would be uttering the truth.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who were despised as weak shall say unto those who had prided: "Nay! (it was) (your) planning by night and by day, when ye bade us that we should disbelieve in God and set up equals unto Him." And they shall feel regretful when they shall see the chastisement; And We will put shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved; They are recompensed aught save what they did. The intelligent ones always plotted night and day to exploit the weaker in mind, to keep them under their sway.This applies to the present atheistic movements started by the aristocratic circles which is spreading to the lower classes.(a) 'Asrar' has been interpreted by some commentators as to mean that they expressed and by some others as to mean that they hid their regret. Both ways are justified in the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We sent not a warner unto a town but the opulent ones of it said: "Verily we are disbelievers in what ye are sent with" The vested interest of the people always stood against every apostle of God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said they: "We are more (than you) in wealth and in children, and we shall not be the chastised" People got infatuated with worldly power and position.It refers to the general tendency of the people attaching importance to the abundance of wealth and issues and the verses give the common answer on behalf of God that what is reckoned by Him as important and the means of approach to Him - i.e., Faith and good deeds. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad?): "Verily my Lord amplifieth the sustenance for whomsoever He willeth and straiteneth (it) (for whomsoever He pleaseth), but most of the people know not." Man is assured that he need not, worrying for the sustenance, yield to anyone else other than God as it is God and God alone Who provides every creature with the sustenance he needs.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And neither your wealth and nor your children are that which bring you nigh (In Status.) unto Us, but whosoever believeth and doeth good, these are, (the ones) for whom is a double recompense for what they do, and they in the exalted places shall be secure. The criterion for judging one's personal merit, will not be based on any material possessions or any influence other than the spiritual excellence and the actual righteousness in the practical life.All worldly goods are nothing but a passing cloud casting shadow running away with it. The real self-development needs correct faith and righteousness in the day-to-day life. The reward for righteousness will be manifold.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who strive hard in invalidating (Opposing.) Our signs, (Apostles & the Imams.) they shall be brought to the chastisement. See 34:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Verily my Lord amplifieth the sustenance for whomsoever He willeth of His servants and straiteneth (it) for him (whomsoever He pleaseth), and whatever thing ye spend, He returneth (Replaced.) it (with His reward along with it), and He is the Best of Sustainers." See 34:35

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That He may recompense those who believe and do good; these it is for whom is forgiveness and an honourable sustenance. The unfailing law of cause and effect would naturally and surely work in the case of good and evil. They would be recompensed for their good with good and for their evil with evil. No good or evil shall go unrewarded or unpunished.1The sustenance promised to the righteous is not the ordinary one which one gets in this life. It will be sustenance honourable, graceful and generous.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on the day when He will gather them all together, then will He say unto the angels: "Did these worship you?" See 34:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They shall say: "Glory be to Thee! Thou art our Guardian, not they; Nay! they worshipped the jinn; most of them were the believers in them." This is a refutation of the claims of the pagans and the others who consider themselves to follow the angelical course in their enchantments and the angelical practices while actually following the Satanic forces of the lower spheres. This includes the modern ways of attempts on recalling the spirits of the dead. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So on that day shall not own one of you for the other any profit or harm; and We will say unto those who did injustice: "Taste ye the chastisement of the fire which ye did disbelieve." See 34:41

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when are recited unto them Our clear signs say they: "This is none but a man, desireth he to turn ye away from what your fathers (Fathers and the ancestors.) did worship," and say they: "This (Qur'an) is naught but a falsehood forged" and those who disbelieve say of the truth when it cometh unto them: "This is nothing but a clear sorcery." This verse refers to those who, feeling the fascinating force of the Quran, termed it as sorcery. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We have not given them any books (Scriptures.) which they read, nor did We send unto them before thee any (Prophet – Apostle.) warner. Neither any book was ever revealed, nor any apostle was ever sent to preach polytheism to any peoples in the world.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And belied (The truth.) those before them and these have not attained (even) the tithe of what We gave them, and yet they belied My apostles; so how (intense) was My abhorrence (of them). The Qurayshite arrogance and pride over their material wealth and worldly power, is referred to, saying what they are proud of, is not even one tenth of what was given to the earlier people who were also destroyed when they defied God's authority and lived a wicked life.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "I exhort you only to one thing, that rise up ye for God's sake in twos and singly, then (Think without prejudice, without preconceived notions.) ponder ye: your companion (Our Apostle Muhammad) is not possessed, he is none but a warner (sent) unto you, before a severe chastisement." It is an exhortation which only an intelligent one would grasp. The Holy Prophet is commanded by God to invite the people to independent thinking about God and his apostleship. The suggestion is to use individual reflection over the matter, for any crowd-mentality would not serve the object of perceiving or understanding any finer and higher spiritual truth. Each one should earnestly and sincerely commune within oneself. If in need, the promise of the Lord to guide the sincere ones, is there verses 29:69 and 16:43; and…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Whatever recompense (Refer to note on verses 42:23, 6:91 & 10:72.) I have asked of you, it is only for yourselves; my recompense is (to be expected) from God (alone), and He is witness over all things." See 6:91, 10:72, 42:23. The Holy Prophet had nothing to gain in this world by his mission save to guide mankind on the right path. In verse 42:23 God commanded the Holy Prophet "to tell the people that he demands nothing from them as his wages or the return for all that he has done for them as the Apostle of God, save the love of his nearest of kin." This verse makes the meaning of the demand or the object of it, saying that whatever the Holy Prophet would demand as the return for the discharge of the duties of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "Verily my Lord doth hurleth (out) the (light of) Truth, The Greatest Knower of the unseen." What God reveals is, Islam, the right way for the salvation of mankind.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "The truth hath come, (Refer to note on verse 17:81.) and falsehood (Delusions.) neither bringeth forth anything nor doth it reproduce." The Eighth Holy Imam Ali ibn Musa ar-Ridha says that when the Holy Prophet entered Mecca after his victory and visited the Holy Ka'ba, there were 360 idols in it. To every idol he pointed out with his staff repeating this verse, and the idols, one after another, fell headlong to the ground.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And for those who strive hard in invalidating (Oppose.) Our signs, (The Apostle and the Holy Imams.) these it is for whom is a chastisement of a painful torment. God's plan can never be frustrated.1 Those who go against it or attempt to frustrate it, are punished and destroyed.It includes those who attempt to explain all the natural phenomena of the universe, in the atheistic or materialist terms. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "If I stray, I stray only against my own self, and if I am guided aright, it is of (Due to.) what hath revealed unto me my Lord; Verily He is All-Hearing, the (Most) Nigh." 'Heaven and the Nearest', i.e., God knows the truth, for he hears everything uttered low or aloud for He is the Nearest, Nearer to man than his own self. Hence, He knows everything.This is in reply to verse 34:43. This does not mean that the Holy Prophet ever erred because Qur'an expressively says in the following verse,'Your Companion never erred and never did he, nor did he ever utter anything but what was revealed to him' (53:2).I.e., he is of the infallible nature and in several other places Qur'an asserts that the Holy Prophet, in no circumstances follows, did not, does not, but…

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And couldst thou see when they shall get terrified, then there shall be no escape and they shall be seized from a (Refers to Badr.) near place, 'From or near place,' (34:51).I.e., at the time of death, or the occasion of the Battle of Badr.Reference is to the state when the guilty are sentenced and their punishment gets nearest to them in that state of facing their punishment, they will be far away from the state of the life in which, faith would have been of no avail to them. And when they were in the state when they could have believed, they disbelieved and they considered the unseen world as something far beyond imagination. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they shall say: "We (now) believe in it." And whence shall the approach (to faith) be for them from (such) a distant place? 'Distant place', for they would have been removed by death far away from this world. The place or the opportunity to believe in the truth is this world, this life and in the hereafter or on the Day of Judgment any repentant believing, would be of no avail at all to anyone.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed they did disbelieve in it before, and aim their conjectures about the unseen from a distant place. The people disbelieved in the Holy Prophet and rejecting his message imagined to be safe in the hereafter as they were here. What they conjectured was about something unseen and such unseen things or places are termed as distant ones. It is said that what they say, are things very distant for them which they could never know.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And a gulf shall be set between them and that which they desire, as was done unto the likes of them of yore, verily they have been in a disquieting doubt. The disbelievers will meet disappointment for they would never achieve their desires or realise their conjectures.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And will see those whom knowledge hath been given, (Refer to note on verses 4:162, 3:6, 3:17, 29:49 & 58:11.) that which hath been sent down unto thee from thy Lord, that it is the truth, and it guideth unto the path of the All-Mighty, the Most Praised (One) See verses 3:6, 3:17, 4:146, 29:49, 58:22 compare also 13:43. Those whose knowledge is inborn and not acquired of their own efforts. The Holy Prophet and his daughter Fatima and the Twelve Imams are those who never learnt anything from any mortal in this world and yet were the fountainheads of knowledge and wisdom.

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say those who disbelieve, (in ridicule): "Shall we point out to you a man who informeth you that when ye are wholly scattered totally disintegrated, (even then) ye are certainly (returned) into a new creation?" This refers to the taunt of the disbelievers against the Holy Prophet, who disbelieved in the resurrection of man after his death, and said that the Holy Prophet who preached the resurrection of man after his death, to be mad.1According to the theistic view of life, death is not the annihilation of the life but a transfer to a new state. This always appears strange to the atheists. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hath he forged a lie against God or there is madness in him?" Nay! those who believe not in the hereafter are in a torment and are (Those who deny the Truth are far away from the right path.) straying far (away from the truth) See 34:7

item.title: bil-Quran: Saba:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: See they not then what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth? If We please We will make them sink into the earth or We bring down upon them a portion from the heaven; Verily in this is a sign for every servant turning (unto the Lord). The spiritually blind or those whose hearts and minds are covered with falsehood who laugh at the truth about the hereafter for they are unable to observe the power of God in the world of nature surrounding them. See verses 36:77 - 36:83, wherein it is asked of such disbelievers whether the One who created the heavens and the earth will be able to create the like of these again or not? The answer also is given in the same verse saying 'Yes! Certainly!' When He…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ta Ha. (T. H.) 'Ta Ha' - The Sixth Holy Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq says - 'Ta Ha' is one of the names of the Holy Prophet. 'Tayyab' wa 'Tahir', meaning Clean or Pure. This interpretation is in agreement with verse 33:33.It is not a reproaching expression but a consoling one that the Holy Prophet or the faithful should not feel sad for the slow progress of faith among the people. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When he saw fire, then said he unto his family, "Tarry ye here, for verily I perceive a fire: happly I may bring unto you a brand from it, or I find at the fire some guidance." The experiences of Moses have been referred to in many places in the Holy Qur'an and the various references are to the appropriateness of each occasion.1 These verses refer to the occasion when Moses after ten years of marriage with Lady Safura the daughter of Shu'aib, started to his mother's place and during the journey in a wilderness, his wife delivered a son and there was no protection or sufficient provision against the chill of the night in the open desert. Moses saw some fire at a distance and went to the spot to get some fire for his family. There he saw…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:100 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Whosoever turneth aside from it, verily he shall bear on the Day of Resurrection, a burden, See 20:96

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:101 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Abiding in it; while grievous will (The bearing.) it be for them on the Day of Resurrection to bear, See 20:96

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:102 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (On) the day when the Trumpet shall be blown and We will gather the guilty ones, and the blue (Blinded with horror. Refer to verse 20:124.) eyed ones. See 20:96

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:103 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They shall consult among themselves in a low voice (saying): "Ye did tarry but ten (days)" Since the chastisement on the Day of Judgment would be far greater and more grievous than that of the one immediately following death, the sinners will imagine their story in the grave or the interval between their death and the judgment or their stay in the world to be very short, like only a few days.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:104 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We know best what they will say, when the most ideal ones of them in conduct will say: "Ye tarried not but a day!" The opinion of the more sensitive of them would be that the stay before the judgment was only a day, i.e., shorter still.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:105 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they ask thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) about (what will happen to) the mountains (on the Day of Resurrection), say then, "My Lord will root them up and scatter them away as dust," People had asked the Holy Prophet as to what would happen to the huge mountains on the Day of Judgment. This verse is in reply to the enquiry.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:106 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then leave it a plain, smooth level, See 20:105

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:107 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thou shall see not in it any crookedness or unevenness See 20:105

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:108 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On that day they shall follow the summoner no crookedness (shall be shown) unto him, and low shall be the voices before the Beneficent (God), that thou shalt hear not aught but the light footfall. 'Inviter', i.e., the Angel Israfil who would give the call to the world by blowing his Trumpet, to assemble for the Final Judgment.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:109 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On that day shall avail not intercession (of any) save (that of) whom hath permitted God, and whose word He is pleased with. See verses 4:85, 2:255, 4:85, 10:3, 19:86, 21:28, 34:23, 39:44.Indicates that there is intercession but by those permitted, whose words are approved by God. As to who are these - Refer to verse 43:86. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So when he came unto it (the fire) a voice (Sounded.) called: "O' Moses!" God encouraged Moses with a voice of consolation calling Moses by his name. Moses awoke shouting 'Here I am, My Lord.'

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:110 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Knoweth He what is before them and what is behind them, while they comprehend Him not in (their) knowledge. While the knowledge of the finite beings in its widest sense cannot comprehend, it is obvious that no faculties of the senses can ever comprehend Him. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:111 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (all) faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, The Self- Subsistent (by Whom all subsist.) God, and indeed disappointed (Be in loss.) will be he who beareth iniquity. See 20:110

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:112 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whosoever doth good deeds and he be a believer, he shall fear not of (the least) injustice (unto him), nor of (any) curtailment (of his dues). It indicates the gravity of iniquity to which all evils are reduced and as opposed to it the import of equity to which all virtues are reduced. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:113 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus have We sent down (unto thee O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) an Arabic Qur'an and (Displayed.) explained therein some of the threats, that they may adopt piety or that it may serve (Lit. produce.) unto them a reminder. See 20:112

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:114 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: High above all is God, the King, the (Self-Existent) Truth; And (Refer to verses 75:16 - 75:19, 73:4 & 25:32.) hasten not (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) with the Qur'an ere its completed unto thee its revelation, and say thou: "O' my Lord! increase me in (of the hidden significance - folds of the Book.) knowledge!" This verse makes it quite clear that the matter of the whole of the Holy Qur'an was already there in the heart of the Holy Prophet even before it was revealed to him gradually. Here, God desires the Holy Prophet to follow the order of the revelation and to disclose it as it is revealed to him by the Angel Gabriel.Reading verses 25:32, 73:4, 75:16 - 75:19 together shows that these verses and the above verses deal with the method of the recitation of the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:115 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed had We covenanted unto Adam before, but he (Bypassed.) forgot; but We did not find in him any intention (to disobey Us). Adam was advised not to approach the Tree, if he wanted to continue in the blissful life of the lower Paradise, as otherwise he will have to suffer the trouble of being thrown out of Paradise and will have to work hard to gain the bliss of the Heavenly Paradise. But Adam did not show any decision to remain there. Hence, he bypassed the advice. (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:116 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When said We unto the angels "Prostrate ye in obeisance unto Adam!" they did prostrate on obeisance save 'Iblis'; (Who did it not.) he refused. See 20:115

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:117 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then said We: "O' Adam! Verily this is an enemy unto thee and thy wife; therefore, let him not drive ye both out of the Garden (The blissful state.) for (then) thou shouldst be put to toil." See 20:115

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:118 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For thee it is ordained that thou shalt not be hungry in it, nor (shalt thou be) naked, This was all that Adam would have enjoyed in the lower Paradise in the animal life1 and there is no mention in it, of the higher bliss of the Heavenly Paradise promised in verses 8:15 & 9:72, i.e., the blessings of God's being pleased with - which is termed as the greatest enjoyment. But as Satan had no idea of such a Paradise awaiting Adam, he only saw the troubles of the temporal life and the ease and the comfort of the Paradise in which Adam was. Therefore, drifting in the spirit of vengeance, he aimed to see that Adam was out of the Lower Paradise.Otherwise, Satan's action, for Adam and those who followed Adam in the fulfilment of the covenant with…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:119 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And that thou shalt not be thirsty in it, nor shalt thou feel the heat of the sun. See 20:118

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily I; I (alone) am thy Lord! So take off thy shoes! Verily thou art (OT Exodus 3/2-5.) in the sacred valley of 'Tuwa' The voice again said 'Verily I am thy Lord.' Moses asked "Where art Thou my Lord? I do not see Thee!" 'The voice came 'O' Moses! I am above thee - below thee, in front of thee and behind thee!" And Moses was asked to take off his shoes for he was in a sacred valley. The command to take off the shoes is interpreted as to taking away from his mind the love of family and children, i.e., getting selfless and devoted exclusively to the Lord. This is 'Tabarra.' Though the Sunni commentators are unanimous in the interpretation of this clause which is nothing but 'Tabarra' yet when 'Tabarra' is enacted by the believers in…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:120 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But Satan whispered unto him saying: "O' Adam! shall I guide thee unto the tree of eternity and unto a kingdom which decayeth not?" See 20:118

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:121 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then they both ate of it, so their nakedness appeared unto them, and they both began to cover themselves with the leaves of the Garden; And Adam acted not (to the advices of) his Lord (deceived by Satan) and got astray. (From the state of bliss but without any intention to disobey the Lord.) See 20:118

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:122 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then his Lord chose (This indicates that what Adam did was not a revolt or disobedience otherwise there remains no justification for his being chosen. (A.P.).) him and turned unto him (accepting his repentance) and guided him. See 20:118

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:123 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (And God) said: "Get down hence ye two, all together, one of you (being) the enemy unto another. So will surely come unto you guidance from Me, then whoever followed! My guidance, he shall go not astray nor put to grief" See 20:118

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:124 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whoever turneth away from My monition, verily his shall be a life straitened, and We shall raise him up on the Day of Judgment, blind. See 20:118

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:125 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He shall say: "O' my Lord! why hast thou raised me blind? Whereas indeed I was seeing (With sight.) (before)?" See 20:118

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:126 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (God) will say: "Thus (is the recompense) for did come unto thee Our signs but thou didst ignore them; And even so art thou forsaken this day" The address is to the one who would be raised blind on the Day of Judgment. It is giving the reason for his being raised so.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:127 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thus will We recompense him who doth transgress and believeth not in the signs of his Lord; and certainly the torment of the hereafter be more severe and more lasting. See 20:126

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:128 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Doth it guide them not aright (to know) how many of the generations We did destroy before them, amidst whose dwellings they (now) walk about? Verily, in this are signs for those (endowed) with (with intellect - will power – reasoning.) understanding. See 20:126

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:129 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And had not a word (Decree.) (of respite) from thy Lord gone forth their arrest (Catch hold.) had immediately been ensued; And the term (of respite for them) is appointed Reading this verse and verse 25:77 together, it indicates that the respite and the postponement of the punishment is just to give a chance to the people to redress their defects and to repent and resort to prayer to God. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And I have chosen thee (for apostleship) then hearken thou unto what is revealed (unto thee)? Moses was informed of his being chosen by God for the ministry.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:130 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So be thou patient with what they say, and glorify (The address is to the Prophet and through the Prophet to his followers.) thy Lord by praising Him ere the rising of the sun and ere the setting of it; And in some hours of the night also do glorify (Him), and during parts of the day, that thou mayest achieve the pleasure (of they Lord). See verse 11:114. This verse gives out in the best comprehensive way the five obligatory and optional prayers.Before the rising of the sun - 'Salat al-Fajr or the Morning Prayer.Before the setting of the sun - 'Zuhr' - the Noon-Prayer and 'Asr' or the After-Noon Prayer.The hours of the night - 'Maghrib' - the Evening-Prayer and 'Isha' - the Night Prayer.According to Ibn-Abbas the term 'the hours of night' comprehends also the time for…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:131 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And strain not thine (The Prophet addressed for the people.) eyes unto that which We have provided (different) parties of them, (of) the splendour of the life of this world, so that We may try them in it; for the provision of thy Lord is better and more abiding. (More lasting.) The address is meant for the people.
