When the verse was revealed, the Holy Prophet sat erect and addressing the people around him said:He who seeks grace from other than that of God shall depart from this world disappointed and dejected.He who covets the others' wealth shall always be in grief and sorrow.He who being endowed with wealth and does not spend it fearing poverty.Do not cast your eyes upon the wealth of others.Nor do you look down upon the one who owns no wealth.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:132 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And enjoin prayer on thy followers, and adhere thou steadily unto it, We ask thee not for subsistence; (but) We (Ourselves) give thee subsistence; and the (success of the) hereafter is for the guarding (against evil). The first thing a believer would be questioned on the Day of Judgment should be about the Prescribed Compulsory Prayers, because for the offer of prayers, one needs nothing besides his own self. If one cannot stand and pray, he may do it sitting. If that also be not possible, to do it lying, and if one cannot move his hands, he can do it even by signs. Under any circumstances none is exempted from the Prescribed Prayers excepting the ladies when they are under the usual terminal and the delivery confinements1.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:133 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "Why doth he not bring unto us a sign from his Lord," What! Hath not there come unto them the clear evidence which were in the former scriptures? See 20:132

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:134 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And had We destroyed them with a chastisement before him (The Apostle Muhammad) certainly would they have said: "O' Our Lord! Why didst thou not send unto us an apostle, for then would we have followed Thy signs ere that we were (thus) humbled and disgraced." See 20:132

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:135 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Every one (of us) is awaiting, so do ye (also) await: then soon ye will come to know who have been the followers of the even way and who hath been the guided aright." After revealing the truth, i.e., the Right Path to salvation and identifying the proper or the Divinely commissioned guides who should be followed after the departure of the Holy Prophet from this world, the people, particularly those who have joined the ranks of the believers, have been given the respite with the choice of following the right course shown to them and the right guides identified by God and the Holy Prophet or otherwise as they chose. The All-Merciful Lord has not spared anything to guide the hearts to the right course verse 10:35, and verse 67:22 and it is…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily I, I (alone) am God: There is no god but I: worship thou (only) Me, and establish prayer for My remembrance! Moses informed of the strict and the pure monotheistic concept he had to bear and to preach, and was enjoined prayer and remembrance of the Lord.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily the Hour (of Doom) is sure to come but I am about to keep it hidden, so that every soul may be recompensed as he striveth: The coming of the Hour of the Final Judgment being a matter of certainty is made known, saying that the Hour is certain to come but the day or the time of its taking effect, is kept a secret, and by informing that every soul shall get the just return for his own conduct, meaning to impress that every soul shall be responsible for his individual faith and action and none shall bear the burden of the other nor any one be deprived of his due.1

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therefore let him who believeth not in it and followeth his own vain desires turn thee away from the truth, lest thou perish. (A caution to Moses.) The injunction here in this verse though addressed to Moses is meant for the people, for the apostles of God are not such weak-minded beings to be led astray from any forces of falsehood.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what is this in thy hand O' Moses! The Rod is the Miraculous Rod which was made to act as a great sign to prove the bonafide of Moses being the Apostle of God. It is reported1 that the Rod was of different mystic usage to Moses and acted differently in different situations of his needs.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: "This is my staff; I recline on it, and I beat down leaves with it for my sheep, and for me therein are other uses (also)." See 20:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He (God.) said: "Cast it down, O' Moses!" See 20:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) Sent We not down the Qur'an unto thee that thou distressest (Sadden.) thyself! The Sixth and the Seventh Holy Imams say that the Holy Prophet used to stand in prayer the whole night upon the toes of his feet and consequently his legs used to get swollen. The Holy Prophet prayed like this for ten years until this verse was revealed in which is contained God's directive to give up the physical strain which the Holy Prophet inflicted upon his own self. It was asked that when he was the Divinely purified, sinless and an infallible one, where was the necessity of his being so much prayerful. The Holy Prophet replied: 'Should I not be the grateful servant of the Lord?'In fact, all the righteousness and the piety which the Holy Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then he cast it down, and lo! it was a serpent running. See 20:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He said: "Lay hold on it, and fear thou not; for We will restore it to its former state (of a staff)" When Moses saw for the first time his Rod becoming a dreadful huge serpent, he was frightened. Moses was commanded not to fear but to hold it with the assurance of its returning to its original state of a rod.And Moses answered and said, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice: for they will say, The Lord hath not spoken unto thee.And the Lord said unto him, What is that in thine hand?And he said, A rod.And he said, Cast it on the ground, And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from it.The Lord said unto Moses, Put forth thine hand and take it by…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And place thy hand under thy armpit, (Bosom.) it shall come forth white, without any harm (As a miracle without any hurt to Moses.) , (and this is) another sign (miracle), See 20:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That We may show thee of Our greatersigns (miracles) (Refer to verses 27:12 - 15:13;) See 20:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Go (Armed with the two miracles.) thou unto Pharaoh! Verily he hath transgressed the bounds! See 20:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Moses.) he "O' My Lord! Expand for me my breast," Moses was armed with the two Ever-triumphant Weapons of the two wonderful signs, and yet he wanted another one like him to assist him in the task against Pharaoh. It would be seen by the life history of Moses and the Holy Prophet that both these Apostles of God have many things in common. The task before the Holy Prophet was several times greater and more difficult. Moses had to face one Pharaoh, but the Holy Prophet had a multitude of Pharaohs, for every Qurayshite chieftain was in no way less than the Pharaoh of Moses. The Holy Prophet had asked God to give him an assistant to assist him in the great task of facing the leaders of the Devils of the heathen world around him, and the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And make easy for me my task, See 20:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And loosen (Make me fluent in speech.) the knot of my tongue, See 20:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (That) they may understand my speech, See 20:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And appoint for me an aider (Ar. 'Vizier' Henchman Lit. One who carries the burden.) from my family, See 20:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Save it is a Reminder unto him who feareth (The pious ones.) (God) 'An admonition for him whose heart is alive, not dead', i.e., whose heart fears the displeasure of the Lord and longs to please Him. The Holy Qur'an is guidance only for the pious and God-fearing.1 Again in verse 3:137 it is clearly said that the Holy Qur'an is only a statement for ordinary men but an admonition to the pious and God-fearing. Thus, sincere faith and piety is the pre-requisite to be benefited by the Qur'an,2 in other words, a disbeliever or an impious one, instead of being guided aright by Qur'an, might get the reverse effect.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Aaron my brother, See 20:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Strengthen my back by him, See 20:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And associate him (with me) in my affair, See 20:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That we may glorify Thee much, See 20:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And remember Thee much See 20:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily Thou art ever seeing of us. See 20:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (God.) He: "Granted is thy prayer, O' Moses!" Refer to note on verse 20:94 - A justification for the Holy Prophet saying 'O' Ali thou art to me as Aaron was to Moses (in all respects) save that there is no prophet to come after me' (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We conferred Our favour on thee at another time, See 20:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When We revealed unto thy mother what was revealed (unto her), This is a reference to how Moses when he as a just-born, was Divinely saved from being killed by Pharaoh. Pharaoh dreamt that a fire from the habitation of the Israelites was coming around his palace and destroying it. The learned ones of his chiefs interpreted the dream saying, that a boy born of the Israelites would cause his destruction. Pharaoh ordered every male child born to the Israelites to be killed. When Moses was born during that time the mother of Moses did not know how to save the child. 'Wahi', i.e., revelation here means inspiration, as in the case of the Bee.1'Wahi' means also the instinct.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That: "Cast him into a chest, then cast it into the sea, then the sea (River.) shall throw him ashore"; there taketh him (up) one (who is an) enemy unto Me and an enemy unto him; and I cast down upon thee love from Me (that everyone may love thee); so that thou mightest be brought up under My eyes (Attention – Blessings.) (as I will): God inspired Moses' mother to put the baby into a box and float it away into the Nile. A channel from the Nile passed into the Palace Garden of Pharaoh. The box containing Moses went floating into to the channel and Pharaoh and his wife 'Asia' picked up the child and the extraordinary beauty Divinely endowed in the child, enchanted Pharaoh and his wife and they decided to adopt the baby as their own…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is a Missive (Communication from Sovereign.) (sent down) from Him who created the earth and the heavens on high. See 20:3

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When thy sister went (unto Pharaoh's wife) and said: "Shall I show you one who will take care of him?" So We brought thee back unto thy mother, that her eyes be cooled and she might grieve not; And thou didst kill a man (and wert perturbed) and We delivered thee from the grief and We tried thee with a heavy trial and then thou didst tarry years among the people of Midian, then thou didst come hither as ordained (According to our plan.) (by Us), O' Moses! Having floated her baby into the river, Moses' mother told her daughter Mary (Moses' sister) to go along with the box and quietly find out as to who picks it up. Moses was picked up by Pharaoh and his wife, but would never have even a drop of the milk from any…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And I have chosen (Conditioned – Moulded – Cultured - for the apostleship.) thee for Myself; See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Go thou and thy Brother (Aaron.) with My signs (miracles) and (Remiss.) slacken not either of you in remembering Me. See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Go ye both unto Pharaoh, Verily he hath transgressed (Rebelled - Become inordinate.) (the bounds) See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then speak ye both unto him a gentle word, happly he may get admonished (Pay heed.) or fear (Our punishment), See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said both (Moses and Aaron.) "O' Our Lord! Verily fear we that he breaketh forth against us, or lest he getteth uncontrolled." See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (God): "Fear not ye both! Verily I am with ye both; I do hear and see" See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So go ye both unto him, and say": "Verily we are apostles from thy Lord, so send thou with us the children of Israel, and torment them not! indeed have we brought signs (miracles) from thy Lord; and peace will be unto him who followeth the guidance; See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, hath it been revealed unto us that indeed the chastisement shall certainly come upon him who belieth and turneth back. See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Pharaoh): "And who is the Lord of ye two, O' Moses!" See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Beneficent (God) on the 'Arsh' (The throne of administration.) is firm 'Arsh' could be translated into English as the Seat or the Centre of the Authority of the Almighty, All-Knowing and the All-Divine Eternal Being. 'Istawa' - the complete or the perfect universal hold or authority. The whole universe is encircled or enveloped by the 'Arsh'. The hold, the authority or the control of the Omnipotence, Omnipresence and the All-comprehending Knowledge is equally connected and concerned with every composite article of everything in the Universe. The Divine attention is so equitable and so universal that it is the same with everything everywhere and never more in any case nor less in any other. Thus, God's authority penetrates and encompasses everything on the earth, in the heavens and whatever there is in between them.It is to be noted that He…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he (Moses): "Our Lord is He Who gave unto everything its (suitable) form, (Form – mould.) and then (also) guided it (aright)" See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Pharaoh) said: "What then is the state of the generations past?" See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He (Moses.) said: "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a Book (secured by Him), erreth not my Lord, nor doth He forget." See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He Who made the earth for you a bed (Cradle.) and made for you therein paths, and sent down from the heavens water; then thereby have We brought forth pairs of plants, various (Varying from each other.) (in kinds) See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Eat ye and pasture your cattle; Verily in this there are signs for those endowed with (Endowed with intellect & will power & reasoning.) understanding See 20:40

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: From it (the earth) We created you, and into it will We return you, and out of it will We bring you forth for a second time. From this very earth were created men and their ancestors and after death they are sent back into it and from it again they shall be raised for the Final Judgment.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We did show unto him (Pharaoh.) Our signs, all of them, but he belied and refused (to believe) Moses threw down his staff and it became a huge dreadful serpent. He took it back. Then he showed his hand with his palm shining bright, and also the other miracles, and yet Pharaoh did not believe.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: "Hast thou come unto us that thou turneth us out of our land by thy sorcery, O' Moses!" See 20:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then we too will certainly produce before thee a sorcery like unto it, so make between us and thee a tryst, we will not fail it, (neither) we nor thou, in a place alike (Central) for both See 20:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Moses) said: "Your tryst be the day of the (Day of adornment.) Festival, and let the people be gathered together in the bright of the noon." See 20:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: His is what is in the heavens and what is in the earth and what is between them two and what is beneath the lowest of the low below the earth. 'Tahta th-Thara' - Beneath or under, i.e., whatever is in the lower-most chamber below the surface of the earth - or taking in the sense of the relativity of the direction - it will mean, God's alone is every thing, be that in the highest or in the lowest direction or the place of the Universe. This to negate or to refute the false notions of the polytheists who assign the various regions of the earth and the heavens to different imaginary deities to rule the places holding sway over the destinies of the beings therein.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So Pharaoh turned back and collected his crafts (Plans.) thereafter he came. See 20:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said Moses unto them, "Woe unto you! forge ye not a lie against God: lest He destroyeth you by a sorcery. And faileth he who forgeth a lie." See 20:56

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then they (the magicians) disputed about their affair among themselves and they spake apart in secret. The magicians began disputing quietly among themselves acknowledging Moses as not a mere magician but some one with some divine powers.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (At last) Said they: "These two are certainly two (expert) sorcerers who intend to drive you out from your land by the sorcery of them both and wipe out your most exemplary tradition! (Creed - religion – faith – belief.)" On Pharaoh asking what the matter was and the magicians out of fear for him said this.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So muster your plan: then come in (organized) order: And indeed shall succeed he this day who (Succeeds.) overcometh! Then Pharaoh ordered the magicians to join together with a strongly-determined plan to defeat Moses.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They said: "O' Moses! Either cast thou (first) or shall we be the first who cast down?" God and the godly ones never take the initiative of challenging any one but take the challenge and answer it. Moses could have cast the Rod first but, he allowed the magicians to do whatever they could, and then he played his role as needed by the situation. When the Holy Prophet (at Khandaq) faced one of the greatest Pharaohs of the Qurayshite of Mecca viz. Umar ibn Abd Wudd al-Amiri the unconquerable hero of the heathens, challenging the Holy Prophet, asking if there was any one on the side of God (i.e., God's prescribed faith Islam) to meet him in combat, and none of the companions responded to the repeated call from the Holy Prophet.Then the Holy Prophet sent his Vicegerent Ali…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Moses) said: "Nay! cast ye down (first) Then lo! Their cords and their rods, (Imaged.) seemed to him by their sorcery as if they were running." See 20:65

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then Moses felt in himself a fear. Amir al-Mu'minin Ali Ibn Abi Talib says that the fear felt by Moses was not of serpents or for himself but against the people being misled.1 The next verse 20:68 supports this interpretation2. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said We: (God.) "Fear thou not! Verily thou shalt be the uppermost. (Triumphant.)" See 20:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And cast down what is in thy right hand: It shall swallow up what they have wrought; Verily they have wrought by the plan of a sorcerer, and a sorcerer shall not be successful whatso ever manner (of skill) (Whatever point of Skill they may come with.) he may come from. See 20:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if thou utter aloud (or in whisper) Verily (alike) knoweth He (all that is) secret (Mysteries of the Unseen.) and (whatsoever is) yet more hidden. There is nothing hidden from His All-Comprehending and All-Penetrating Knowledge. Every thing in the Universe is wholly manifest to Him, nothing is hidden from Him, be that a loud voice or a low utterance or a whisper of even the heart or the sincerity or the insincerity of the intentions - the love and the hatred, faith and disbelief, all are equally manifest to Him. Hence it is said that with God the actions of man are judged according to the intention behind them.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then fell down the sorcerers prostrating (in obeisance) they said: "We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses!" This indicates the difference between miracle and sorcery. The result of a miracle is real and lasting whereas that of sorcery is unreal and momentary1. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Pharaoh): "Believe ye in him ere I give ye leave (to do it)? Verily he is your Chief (sorcerer) who hath taught you sorcery, so I shall certainly cut off your hands and your feet on the opposite sides, and I will certainly crucify you on the trunks of the palm trees, then will ye certainly know which (Me or the Lord of Moses.) of us is more severe in tormenting and abiding!" See 20:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They said: "Never will we prefer thee (O' Pharaoh!) to what hath come unto us of the clear signs, and to Him Who made us, so decree thou whatever decree thou decreeth; for thou canst decree only about the life of this world" See 20:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily we! we do believe in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and the sorcery thou didst compel us (to do); and God is the Best and the Most (The Eternal.) Abiding! See 20:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily he who cometh unto his Lord as guilty, for him certainly is Hell; he shall die not in it nor shall he live. Those committed to Hell would suffer the life which would be worse than death, and though they would prefer death but it would not be given to them, for death would mean the cessation of the torment to which they would be committed. The life in Hell would be a continued consciousness.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whosoever cometh unto Him as a believer and who hath indeed done good deeds, these, for them are the ranks high, The life in Paradise will be a continued consciousness of enjoyment of the sublime bliss and the grace of the Lord mentioned in these verses.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The Gardens (Paradise.) of Eternity, beneath which flow rivers, to abide therein; and this is the recompense of him who purifieth (Refer to verses 8:14(in contrast) & 91:9 & 91:10.) himself (from evil). See 20:75

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We revealed unto Moses (saying); "Travel thou by night with My servants, and strike for them a dry path in the sea, not fearing to be overtaken (by Pharaoh), nor be thou afraid (of getting drowned)" Moses was Commanded by God to strike at the water of the sea in front of him. Twelve dry paths were effected through the deep water, for the Twelve Tribes of the Israelites to march away to safety. Moses was assured of not being overtaken by Pharaoh in the safe passage through the sea. The water was split and made to stand still like huge walls on both sides.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And followed them Pharaoh with his hosts, so covered them (the billows) of the sea, as they were they covered (drowned). See 20:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And Pharaoh led astray his people and he did not guide them (aright) See 20:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: God, there is no god but He; His are (all) the Best names. It is a natural phenomenon that unless the plate is clean, free from every kind of impression no desired figure can ever have a distinctive impression on it. Unless the mind or heart is thoroughly clean, free from belief of any degree or nature in false deities or falsehood, the correct faith in God and truth can never take its place therein. Hence washing the mind of every kind of false conceptions is the first requisite, the foremost essential step towards faith in God and this act is called 'Tabarra' and embracing the truth thereafter is 'Tawallah'. These two conditions are of the fundamentals of the practice of the Islam-Original identified by the term 'Shiaism.'For the Beautiful Names of God see verse 17:110.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: ("O' Children of Israel!) We rescued you from your foe; and We made a covenant with of Israel!) you on the right side of 'Tur' (the Mount Sinai), and We sent down unto you Manna and quails:" See 20:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Eat ye of the good things We have provided you with and transgress (Exceed not.) not in it, lest descendeth on you My wrath, and on whomsoever My wrath doth descend, indeed he is perished. See 20:77

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And verily I am the Most Forgiving unto him who repenteth and believeth and doth good, then he doth continue to follow the right guidance. Note the most reasonable assurance of forgiveness extended to the sinner which is subject to sincere repentance with the amendment of the conduct on the part of the offender of the Divine Law, against the belief in the unconditional redemption of the sinners based upon the belief of the price of the sins having been paid away to God in the blood of any one. Any such belief is a greatest danger to the moral and the social life of the human race on earth, for any one can merely profess such a dogmatic belief and do whatever the brute in him instigates him to do; for God having received the price of the sins…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Said God): "But what made thee hasten (thyself on apart) from thy people, O' Moses!" After they had been recovered from the clutches of Pharaoh, the Israelites wanted Moses to get for them the laws regulating their lives to be prescribed by God. When Moses prayed for the laws, God summoned Moses to Mount Sinai. Moses left his brother Aaron in his place at the head of the people and went on the Mount. On reaching the Mount, Moses left the chosen men at the foot of the Mountain and hastened himself up on the mountain. Similarly, when the Holy Prophet was commanded by God to migrate to Madina, he left Ali in his bed as did Moses leave Aaron. Again, when the Holy Prophet left for Tabuk, he left Ali in his place in Madina.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Moses): "They are close on my track and I hastened unto Thee O' my Lord! that thou mightest be well pleased (with me)!" Moses' haste was to please God with his readiness and haste in carrying out His Command to report himself with the men at the place.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (God): "Verily We have tried thy people in thine absence, and the Samiri had led them astray." Samiri, a calf-worshipper who only professed belief in God and at heart was a disbeliever, was among those who followed Moses out of Egypt. When Moses had gone on Mount Sinai with the chosen men and there was only Aaron in his place at the head of the people, Samiri managed to get the people agreed to making a calf of the jewels of gold which the Israelites had bought from the Egyptians. By some witchcraft Samiri managed to create some sound from the hollow of the golden calf made by him and in spite of Aaron's efforts to keep the people away from getting deluded by Samiri's device, the Israelites were beguiled by Samiri and they began worshipping the golden calf…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:86 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So returned Moses unto his people angered, sorrowfully said he! "O' my people! Did not your Lord promise you a goodly promise? Did then the promise seem long to you? or did ye wish, or desired ye that the wrath from your Lord should light (Came upon.) upon you? that ye violated the tryst with me?" See 20:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:87 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "We violated not the tryst with thee of our own accord, but we were made to bear the burdens of the ornaments of the people, so we cast them away, and thus didst the Samiri suggest" See 20:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:88 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then he brought forth (from the fire) for them (the image of) a calf, a (mere) body; which (also) gave out the lowing sound; Then they said: "This is your god and the god of Moses, but he (Moses) hath forgotten," See 20:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:89 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! See they not that it could not return unto them a word (In reply.) (for an answer) and that it could neither hurt nor benefit them? See 20:85

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And hath come unto thee the story of Moses? See 20:8

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:90 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed Aaron had said unto them before: "O' my people! Verily, ye are tried by it (the image) and verily your Lord is the Beneficent (God), so follow me and obey ye my order." Though Aaron was warning them against the misleading temptation, the Israelites were being tested by God - the Israelites did not pay any heed to Aaron's admonition.

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:91 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "Never will we cease worshipping it until returneth unto us Moses." See 20:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:92 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Moses) said: "O' Aaron! What hindered thee when thou didst see them going astray," See 20:90

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:93 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That thou didst not follow me? Hast thou then disobeyed my order? The attitude of Moses towards Aaron was not because of any doubt against the stand taken by Aaron towards Samiri but he wanted the matter to be exhibited to the public and that Aaron should explain his stand so that no room be left for accusing Aaron of joining hands with Samiri or neglecting his duty. All that Aaron was anxious to see was that no rift in the ranks of the Children of Israel was created before the return of Moses. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:94 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Aaron): "O' son of my mother! Seize me not by my beard (Get not angry.) nor by my head; I was afraid lest sayest thou: "Thou hast caused a division among the children of Israel and didst not respect my word!" See 20:93

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:95 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Moses) said: "What was thy object O' Samiri?" See 20:93

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:96 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Samiri): "I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful of (the dust) from the track of the Messenger (Angel), and flung it (into the image of the calf) for so did my self prompt me (to do)" Samiri relates that he only used the earth under the hoof of the Messenger Angel and use of it enchanted him.It has already been said above that the life-history of Moses has an identity with that of the Holy Prophet. The Holy Prophet left this world leaving Ali in his place to be at the head of the people. The Samiris among the Muslims set up their own authorities and follow them instead of following the Word of God (the Holy Qur'an) and the word of the Holy Prophet, i.e., his behest about Ali and his Ahl al-Bayt.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:97 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Moses) said: "Begone then, verily for thee it shall be in this life to say: (No contact with any. It is said Samiri was banished into the desert.) 'Touch me not'; and (besides this) thou hast a tryst (of punishment) never will that fail; and (now) look at thy god whose worship thou kept (so long); Certainly will we burn it, then certainly will we scatter (the ashes of) it in the sea (with a wide) scattering!" See 20:96

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:98 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily your God is only 'Allah' (God); There is no god but He; He comprehendeth all things in (His) knowledge! See 20:96

item.title: bil-Quran: Taa-Haa:99 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus do We relate unto thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) of the (historic) accounts of what hath (Gone before.) passed (of old); and indeed have We given unto thee from Ourselves a Reminder (Qur'an). See 20:96

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ya Seen (Y. S.) Some commentators take 'Ya' as the vocative particle, and the letter 'Sin' standing as an abbreviation for 'Insan', i.e., Man - the term 'Ya-Sin' meaning 'O Man!' Taking even this interpretation to be correct it would naturally mean the 'Man-Perfect' or the 'Leader of Men', i.e., the Model-Man sent to guide the human race as a whole, i.e., the Holy Prophet Muhammad, for the context of the events which demanded the revelation of this verse justifies the inference. The pagans had disbelieved in the mission of the Holy Prophet and had said "that the Holy Prophet was not the one sent by God nor was Qur'an the Word of God, it is his own composition.''The First Holy Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib says that 'Yasin' is one of the names of the Holy Prophet. The Fifth…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And alike is it unto them if thou warneth them not, for they will not believe. The history of the early Muslims, bears the best testimony to the truth in this passage. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily thou canst warn only him who abideth by the Reminder (Qur'an and the Holy Prophet.) and feareth the Beneficent (God) unseen; so bear thou unto him the glad tidings of forgiveness and an honourable recompense. (i.e., whoever follows the Book (Qur'an) and the Holy Prophet (Sunnah). Any one deviating even in the least would be classed with the majority - Refer to verses 36:7 & 36:8.) See verse 35:18.(a) Qur'an and the Holy Prophet and 65:10 & 65:11. Book and the tradition meaning whosoever follows the contents of the Qur'an and the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet. Anyone deviating even slightly from the Qur'an and the Sunnah would be classed under majority in verses 36:7 & 36:8. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily We, (and) We (alone) give life unto the dead, and We write down what they have sent before them and (even) their footprints (which they leave behind them): And everything have We confined (recorded) into a (Said the Holy Prophet - He who died while he recognised not the Imam of his age, certainly died of ignorance (Hadith).) Manifesting Imam (Guide). Every individual, man and woman would be brought to account for his or her deeds, on the Day of Judgment and even the effects of the deeds left behind the people will not be spared from the account.It is a clear indication that every individual is accountable not only for what he does in his lifetime but also for what he leaves behind as the marks of his personal goodness and evil. The people of the Banu-Salim tribe…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And set forth unto them the instance of the people of a town when came unto it (Our) Apostles, The reference is said to be to the people of the city of Antioch, one of the most important cities in North Syria. It was a Greek city founded by Seleucus Nicator, one of the successors of Alexander about 300 B.C. in memory of his father, Antiochus.There are stories forwarded as examples. The real application of the passage is to the early conditions. While the Holy Prophet started his mission, from among the people followed only by Ali, the dignitaries of Mecca started ridiculing them. It is said that once Abu Talib accompanied by his elder son Jafar, entered the Holy Mosque of Mecca (Masjid al-Haram) while the Holy Prophet and Ali were praying. Jafar asked his father Abu Talib as…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When sent We unto them two (of Our apostles) they belied them both, then We strengthened (the two) with a third (one from Us) and said they (unto the people): "Verily we are unto you the apostles (from God)" Jesus had sent two of his disciples to preach his message. It is said that they were John and Jonah. When they approached the outskirts of the city, they met a shepherd who asked as to who they were. They said that they were the messengers from Jesus the Apostle of God, and had been sent to invite the people to the Islam, the true faith. The shepherd asked if they had any signs to prove their bonafide. They said that they could cure the sick and restore sight to the born-blind and cure the born lepers. The shepherd took them…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They said: "Ye are not but men like unto us, nor hath sent down the Beneficent (God) any thing, ye only utter a lie." When Simon had gained sufficient influence over the king, he one day asked the king to get the two persons to be questioned about their faith. When the two messengers appeared, they saw Simon but did not give vent to their recognition. Simon asked them as to who they were and the purpose of their visit to the place. They said that they were the messengers of Jesus the Apostle of God, sent to invite the king to give up idolatry and embrace the faith in the Only True God and on being asked, they said that they can cure the sick and even the born lepers and get the sight restored to the blind. When…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They said: "Our Lord knoweth that we are verily unto you the apostles." The best proof of the genuineness of their claim as the apostles of God and their having been sent by none else but God was that whenever the people disbelieved their position as the heavenly teachers and rejected the message they preached, the apostles always invoked the authority and the mercy of God and faithfully and patiently suffered the worst of persecution and tortures and never yielded to any authority other than God's. Their conviction about God's knowledge was so firm and unshakable that in the events of the difficulties they met and the people disbelieving and rejecting them, they were perfectly satisfied for they knew that God was seeing them executing His Command and knew everything of their experiences.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on us is nothing but a clear deliverance (of the message) 'Tayr' means a bird. Like the Romans, the Arabs also derived Omens from birds - For the Egyptians imagining that their ill-luck was due to Moses. See verse 7:131 and Thamud's thinking their ill-luck being due to the preachings of Salih.1 The people warned the messengers from Jesus that if they did not desist, they would be stoned and inflicted with a painful chastisement.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "Verily we augur ill from you, if ye desist not, we will certainly stone you, and there shall afflict you from us a painful torment." See 36:17

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They said: "your augury of ill is with yourselves; What! when ye are admonished (deem ye ill of it) 1 Nay! ye are people transgressing (exceedingly)" The messengers replied that the calamity which would overtake the people, would be the earning of their rebellious conduct.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: By Qur'an (The Word of) the All-Wise, See 36:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And came from the (Also for Mu'min Aal-e-Fir'aun – Refer to note on verse 40:28 - as was Abu Talib, father of Ali who hid his faith and protected the Holy Prophet - and Ali was the first to believe when none believed.) farthest part of the city a man running and said: "O' my people! Follow ye (these) the apostles (of God)," When the people of the city disbelieved and rejected the Message from Jesus, a man from the outskirts of the city, i.e., Habib al-Najjar (Habib the Carpenter) who is a popularly known as the 'Mu'min-e-Aal-e-Ya-Sin' (The believers in the children of Ya-Sin, i.e., Muhammad) came running and exhorted his people to believe in the message of the selfless one, (i.e., the messengers jointly or Jesus from whom the message had come). For Mu'min-Aale-Fir'awn refer to note on…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Follow ye those who ask you not any recompense, and they are guided aright. For no reward was demanded in return for their Services.The one who deserves to be followed, i.e., the person who does not expect any reward or return from you - secondly, he himself should be well guided and not taking guidance from others for himself.1 (A.P.).When Ubaydah ibn Harith fell at the battle of Badr, the Holy Prophet came to him while he was still alive. Ubaydah smiled and said - 'I wished Abu Talib had been alive to see that I am the first one of his house who lays down his life for the sake of the divine cause'. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And why should not I worship only Him Who brought me into being? and unto Whom ye shall all be returned: What is said in this verse is what the individual had been personally convinced, with which he wants to appeal to his people to follow his conviction. He argues for himself saying, as to how it could be possible for him not to serve or adore his real Maker, to whom alone is their ultimate return.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Shall I take besides Him any gods, if (God) The Beneficent willeth to afflict me with harm, their (the false gods & the deities.) intercession shall not avail me aught, neither can they (the false gods & the deities.) deliver (Save – relieve.) me? This is the continuation of the previous verse. Another argument is advanced here, against worship in the false gods. Since God alone is the Omnipotent Whose will to punish anyone shall always be worship in the false gods. Since God alone is the Omnipotent Whose will to punish anyone shall always be done and none of the false deities could ever resist it nor could they even intercede for the victim, why should one acknowledge the godhead of any such being.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, I in which case shall be in manifest error: If what is said in the previous verse is acted upon by anyone, the individual would indeed manifest error.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, I believe in your Lord, so hear me! This refers to the assured personal conviction of the man (the Mu'min-e-Ale-Ya-Sin) about God, which he wants to convey to his people and exhort them to embrace it and get themselves guided aright. While the godly man, preached the truth to the people and exhorted them to embrace it, the people stoned him and killed him and buried him in the marketplace of Antioch (Antakya).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It Was said (unto him): "Enter thou, the (Paradise.) garden!" Said he: "Oh! would (Remembering others in the bliss.) that my people had known," The soul of the godly man was asked by the angels to enter Paradise on which occasion in the bliss granted to him, the liberated soul remembers his people saying: 'Had the people known what a blissful life is granted to the believers in the truth and the righteous ones, they also would have enjoyed the bounties of God and as he has received'.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Of that for which my Lord hath forgiven me and hath made me of the honoured ones This verse is the continuation of the previous one meaning had the people known the worth of the faith in the Only True God and righteousness in life on account of which qualities he has been made honourable in the life after death.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We sent not down upon his people any hosts from heaven, nor were We (in need) to send (any such hosts). The enforcement of the justice of the Almighty God, needs not the pomp, show and the circumstance which the ordinary powers and the authorities of earthly beings, manifest to create awe in the minds of the fellow beings to establish or to increase the regard for their strength and glory, nor does God need any of the forces of human wickedness or any manifest use of the mighty and the unconquerable spiritual forces to punish them or to even wipe them out of existence. Hence no hosts from heaven were sent to punish the people of Antioch for their conduct against the messengers from Jesus and their killing the Believer of Aale-Ya-Sin, i.e., Habib al-Najjar.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It was nothing but one terrible cry, and lo! they were (like ashes) extinct. A single blast either through the rumbling of an earthquake or a violent stormy wind with a thunder was sufficient as it was in the case of the people of Thamud.1 A blast was quite sufficient to effect a complete perdition to the people and they were like ashes, quenched and silent.This verse speaks of hosts not being sent in the case of the event of Antioch, with nothing to speak about what was effected at Badr, Ahzab and elsewhere.Ref. to the sudden disastrous calamity which befell the people who killed Theophilus - (Habib al-Najjar). (A.P.)

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily thou (O' Muhammad!) art of the apostles (sent by Us), See 36:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Alas! the servants (are misled and yet) there cometh not unto them an apostle but they mock at him. See verses 6:10, 21:40. The ignorant masses of the human race have always been mocking at any one and everyone who professed religion seriously and advocated its cause to the others of his race. Particularly the religious leaders and more particularly the apostles of God had suffered heartless persecution and torturous death.1 The people never reflected upon, how countless generations before them, were destroyed for rejecting the Truth. Such people never realised that levity surely and unfailingly reacts on themselves and invites their own degradation, suffering and destruction even in this life, besides what is in store for them in the hereafter.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! See they not how many of the generation We did destroy before them? they will return not unto them. Those punished by God in this life for their wickedness, would not be returned to this world and some commentators say that the people were punished even for their not honouring those apostles of God whom they ridiculed and rejected.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And assuredly all, gathered together, shall be brought before Us. Certainly, every one of them shall be brought together before God as commanded. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And a sign unto them is the dead earth; We give life to it and bring We forth from it grain of which they eat. Let those who disbelieve their resurrection after death for the Final Judgment, take the note of guidance from the earth which for all intents and purposes, seems to be dead in a season every year and get quickened again and becomes once more productive as it was before. it was before1.Indicates here, a higher stage is made to develop from the lower one as a continuity of the movement. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And make We therein gardens of date-palms and grapevines, and cause We to flow therein springs, Date palms and vines are mentioned as symbols of fruit trees of various kinds. It may be noted that the description of the blissful life in the Hereafter given in the Qur'an is figurative for the heavenly bliss is unimaginable here.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: That they may eat of its fruits, and made it not their hands; What! will they not then be grateful? However, much man may prepare the soil and sow the seed or plant a tree but unless the forces of nature help him, which are God's own and are effected only by His independent will, nothing could profit man, in getting any produce from the earth or to do anything else also in the world. Hence whatever grains or fruits man eats, are the products of God's willed functions of the natural forces in the formulation of which energies and their working in perfect harmony with each other, there is no hand of anyone else besides Him. Should not man be grateful to God?The famous quatrain of the world renowned classical Persian poet 'Sa'di' which can be aptly quoted here:Persian:1.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Hallowed is He Who created pairs (of) all things, of what groweth the earth, of their selves and of what they know not. The mystery of sex exists in all species of creation. The constitution of the material world and the various kinds of energies functioning in the universe, are working in pairs of opposite kinds. There is the factor of sex active in the human, animal and vegetable life and in the other forms of activity manifest and hidden, known to us like electricity (positive and negative) and also unknown to us. Scientific enquiry until recently could not reach the fact that even the atom consists of a positive charge called the proton surrounded by a negative charge called electron. The point to note here is that, it was a time when the Holy Qur'an was revealed, the world…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And a sign unto them, is the night, We draw forth from it the day, and Io! they are in the dark, See 36:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the sun travelleth unto a resting-place (Refer to verses 13:2, 21:33 & 55:5.) fixed for it; That (The moment.) is the decree of the All- Mighty, the All-Knowing. Until the very recent past, the sun was supposed to be stationary and all the other planets revolving round it and since very recently it has been found out that the sun also along with the whole of its solar system, is moving towards some destination. This fact had been declared centuries ago by the Holy Qur'an. This verse clearly declares that the sun is travelling towards a fixed destination or an end, and none knows when it would cease to be or stop to function, and this is the decree of the Omnipotent Lord Who is ever Triumphant or Successful, Who is the All-Knowing.1 For the meaning of the word…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (as for) the moon. We have fixed for it stages till it returneth to be bent like an old palm branch. Reference is to the lunar mansions of the Zodiac, 'Urjun' the sickle-like appearance of the new moon.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the straight path See 36:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: It is not (expedient) for the sun that it should overtake the moon, nor can the night outstrip the day; and each (of these luminaries) rotate on in (its peculiar) sphere. Though the sun and moon move in the same Zodiac path, the laws of the movement of each have been so fixed that the one can never clash with the other.Note what a beautiful and realistic technical term has been used to describe the movement of the heavenly bodies in the space as swimming in it.1 This same term is used in our modern days for the planes that fly in the space, using the word navigation.Ali states that over and above this sun are suns and over and above this moon are moons. There is another statement of Ali - as narrated by 'Majma al-Bahrayn' under the word…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And a sign unto them is that We bear their offspring in the laden Ark, Man's own personal experience in his practical life is appealed to. Man is invited to reflect upon his travelling safely along with his cargo through the high seas fighting the violent winds and the mountain-like waves - as it was done in the case of Noah and the Ark1 - which has become a 'sign for all peoples.'

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And that We have created for them (the other conveyances) like it, on which ride they. It is unquestionably God's gifted intelligence with which man has devised the seacraft and the aircraft to manage with the laws of gravity, otherwise it would have been nothing short of an impossibility to pass through the sea or the air.Muhyiddin Ibn Arabi in his mystic interpretation of this verse interprets – 'Like it' as the Ark of Noah and says, that is the Ark belonging to Muhammad, i.e., hinting at the celebrated saying of the Holy Prophet: 'Mathal Ahl-e-Bayti ka-mathal safeenat Nuh; man rakibaha naja, wa man takhallafa anha gharq wa hawa'. i.e., the similitude of my Ahlul-Bait is that of the Ark of Noah; he who got into it was saved and he who turned away from it, got drowned and lost.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if We only will, We can drown them, then there shall not be any one to help them, nor shall they be rescued, See 36:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Save (by) mercy from Us and as an enjoyment for yet awhile. See 36:42

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when it is said unto them: "Guard ye (yourselves) against what is before you and what is behind you, that ye be treated with mercy." Man had always been admonished to reflect upon his faulty past, know its consequences, beware of the future and guard himself against his sins recurring for, when one sincerely does this, God also turns merciful to him, He not only forgives the past but also grants strength to amend his life in the future.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And there cometh not unto them any sign from the signs of their Lord but from it turn they away. See 36:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when it is said unto them: "Spend ye of what God hath provided you with the sustenance," say those who disbelieve unto those who believe: "What! shall we feed him whom, if God willeth, He could feed? Ye are not but in a manifest error." When those who have been granted ample provision of wealth, influence or knowledge, are told to spend out of what God has blessed them with, for the benefit of their fellow beings, they laugh to scorn such appeals and indirectly blame God Himself for not having been merciful to provide the poor as He has done to the rich. Such people think that what God has provided them with, by His grace and mercy, was earned by them by their own personal merits. They forget that everything that is given to anyone in this…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they: "When will this promise (The warning against chastisement.) come to pass, if ye be truthful?" The disbelievers not only reject the belief in the hereafter but also by way of taunting, question as to when the Day of Judgment would come? The answer to them is that it will come but never at your or anybody else's fancy but when the Lord would will it.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They wait not but for a single (terrible) cry which will seize them while they wrangle with one another. See 36:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Sent down of the All-Mighty, the All-Merciful, See 36:1

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then shall they not be able to make a bequest, nor shall they be able to return unto their families. See 36:48

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And is blown the Trumpet, when lo! From the grave unto their Lord they (all) hasten. About the blowing of the Trumpet, see verses 78:18, 39:68, 50:20, 27:87, 23:101'Ajdath', i.e., the place or state where the former shapes and forms of the living beings with which they were buried or lost whether it is in grave or burnt into ashes or eaten away by animals or thrown into the sea. The verse expressively points out that after rising from their burials in new forms, their movements in chain will be towards their Lord.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They shall say: "Oh! woe unto us! who hath raised us up from our place of repose?" (it will be replied): "This (What the believers would say.) is what the Beneficent (God) did promise and the apostles spake the truth." 'Ruqud' means sleeping - 'Marqad' sleeping place, figuratively refers to any state or stage wherein man is not aware of what is awaiting for him in future. It is true of this life in comparison to the life hereafter and it is also true of the life after death in the intermediary stage before the Total Resurrection. The Holy Prophet has said: 'People are asleep, when they will die they will awake.' (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: There will be but a single cry, when lo! they shall all be brought (Summoned.) unto Us. See 36:52

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So this day no soul shall be dealt with unjustly in the least, nor shall ye be recompensed but that which ye were doing. The reward or punishment will be the consequence of one's own actions, or in other words, the actions themselves assuming pleasant or unpleasant forms which will make the doer enjoy or suffer. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, the inmates of the Garden shall on that day be busy enjoying. See 36:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They and their mates, shall be in (Pleasant) shades, on raised couches reclining; See 36:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For them therein shall be fruits, and for them shall be whatever they call for. (desire.) See 36:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (They shall receive the greeting): "Peace" a word (of salutation) from the Lord the Most Merciful. See 36:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (And a voice would say): "And get ye aside this day O' ye the guilty ones!" See 36:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So that thou mayest warn a people whose fathers were (Since Abraham until the Holy Prophet no apostle had visited the place.) not warned, and who therefore are heedless (of the truth) The heathens of Mecca had not received any apostle of God for a long time before, i.e., since Abraham no prophet had visited the place.It does not mean that his mission was exclusively for the particular people. He was sent unto mankind as a whole1 which indicates the universality of his mission. This verse refers only to the people of his immediate audience similar to 'Wa-andhir 'ashirataka al-aqrabin' (26:214) who are supposed to be the descendants of Abraham through Ishmael.(a) Though the lineage between Ishmael and the Holy Prophet's ancestral chain, maintained the religion of Abraham yet none of them stood as a warner to admonish his people.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Enjoined (Did I not announce the command?) I not on you O' children of Adam! that ye should worship (also serve not.) not Satan? for he is your open enemy, See 36:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And ye should worship (only) Me, (and) this is the (only) Right way? See 36:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And yet hath he led astray a great multitude of you; Did ye not then understand? See 36:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: This is the hell which ye were promised, See 36:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Enter ye into it, for what ye were disbelieving. See 36:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On that day will We set a seal upon their mouths, and shall speak unto Us their hands and shall bear witness their feet, of what they were earning. See 36:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if We will, We would certainly put (Make blind.) out their eyes, then they would struggle (groping) to get first to the way, but how could they see? See 36:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if We will, We would certainly transform them in their (own) places, then they would not be able to go on, nor will they return. Indicates for those who lose their human form, there will be no progress or retrogressing. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And whomsoever We lengthen in age, We reverse him to an abject state in life, What! Do they understand not? See 36:67

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We have taught him (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) not poetry, nor would it beseem him; It is naught but a Remin der and manifesting Qur'an, 'Poetry' here means proposition based on imaginary data exciting human emotion. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed the word hath been proved true of most of them, and wherefore they believe not. When the people obstinately refuse to be guided aright and reject all guidance and the respite given only increases their obstinacy and perversity, the decree for their punishment is naturally pronounced.1(a) Ref. to the divine decision declared in the Qur'an against Satan and the children of Adam who followed him Refer to verses 7:13 - 7:18 and in the other places. This indicates that the majority of the people referred to here, would not believe. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: To warn him who is alive, (with awakened heart.) and (that) the word be proved against the disbelievers. See 36:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! See they not that We created the cattle for them, of what Our hands (Powers, authorities, agencies, deputies.) have wrought, and of them they (The people.) are the masters? See 36:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And them (the cattle) We did subject unto them (To the people for their use.) and some of them they ride upon, and some of them they eat. See 36:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And for them (To the people for their use.) in them (The cattle.) are benefits and drinks: What! will they not then be grateful? See 36:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (yet) they have taken gods besides (the only True) God so that they may be helped. See 36:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They shall not be able to help them: and yet they (the disbelievers) are their host (who on the Day of Resurrection) shall be brought forth to account. See 36:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So let not their speech grieve thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!), (for) verily know We what they do hiding, and what they do openly. See 36:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Seest not man that We created him from (a drop of) sperm? (and) yet lo! he is an open disputant! (Adversary.) See 36:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He setteth unto Us an argument, and hath forgotten his (own) creation (origin), Sayeth he: "Who will enliven the bones when they are rotten?" See 36:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "He will enliven them Who created them for the first time, and He is, fully cognizant of (all) the creation," See 36:69

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, We have put chains in their necks, and these reach up to their chins, and their heads are forced up stiffed. Abu Jahl has vowed that if he saw the Holy Prophet praying, he would drop upon him a big stone. Once when the Holy Prophet was engaged in prayer, Abu Jahl fetched a big stone and when he approached the Holy Prophet and raised up the stone to drop it upon his head, his hand got stuck to his neck and the stone remained on his own head. When one of his partymen saw this, he got up saying that he would kill the Holy Prophet, but when he came near and heard the Holy Qur'an recited, he was filled with awe and returned to his party to report that he found a lion guarding the Holy Prophet…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He who made for you the fire from the green tree, and lo! from it ye kindle (fire). Refers to the assumption of being of opposite form, in their evolutionary movements towards the ultimate shape. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Is not He Who created the heavens and the earth able to create (again) the like of them? Yea! and He is the Creator (Omnipotent), the All-Knowing. The stress on 'Alim' shows that no unconscious being can have any creative power.1 (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: His command, when intendeth He anything, is only that He sayeth unto it 'Be' then (and there) it is. The process of creation is given in the term of His Will and attention. Thus, every being is God's Word. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therefore, Hallowed is He in Whose hand is the kingdom of all things, and unto Him ye shall all be returned. See 36:82

item.title: bil-Quran: Yaseen:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And We have to set before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We covered them over, so that they see not. A man from the Banu Makhzum got up with a similar vowful determination to kill the Holy Prophet but when he came near, he was turned blind and could not see the Apostle of God though he was there engaged in prayer. This man also returned to his party with the same report of his finding a lion there intending to attack him. Thus, God had caused some barriers, and they could not see the Holy Prophet.Figurative reference to the pride of the pagans among the Arabs. Similarly, the barriers referred to in the next verse 36:9 refer to heathen arrogance or adamance which prevented them to submit totally. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:1 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: 'Alif, Lam, Ra. (A. L. R.) These are verses of the Book All-Wise. 'Alif Lam Ra - (A. L. R.), 'Hakim' qualifying the Book (The Holy Qur'an), meaning the Book full of wisdom. It has already been said that the letter symbols used in the Holy Qur'an are divine secrets known only to God, the Holy Prophet and the Holy Imams. All interpretations by the people, are only conjectures.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:10 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Their cry therein (will be), "Glory be to Thee O' God!" and their greetings in it (will be) 'Peace' and the last of their cry (will be), that God's is the praise, the Lord of the worlds (The supplication continues to the life here-after even to the final abode but the nature of it will differ as they will be in the state of realisation. They will witness always his glory and absolute Lordship. Thus, they rejoice.) . It is said that the salutation of the people in Paradise will be 'Peace' meaning it will be a life of Bliss-Perfect. This has been mentioned in 56:25& 56:26. These verses explain the meaning of the salutation mentioned in this verse, i.e., there shall not be any vain talk but the mention of the bliss they will be placed in.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:100 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (While.) (although) it is not for any soul to believe except by God's permission (Allowing the deserving individuals to use their choice of faith.) ; while casteth He uncleanliness (of infidelity) on those who use not (their) sense (Not understand.) . See 10:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:101 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou, "Observe (Behold – Consider.) ye What is in the heavens and earth; but avail not signs and warnings people who believe not." See 10:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:102 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! wait they then for (any-thing) but the like of the days of those who passed away before them? Say thou "Wait ye then; Verily I too am with you of the waiting ones." See 10:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:103 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ultimately (when Our wrath fell) We deliver Our apostles and those who believe - even so it is binding on Us (that) We deliver the believers (Indicates the turmoil and the material conflict at last will destroy those who do not appreciate higher values of life save the apostles and the believers who are concerned with nothing but the higher values of life. (A.P.).) . See 10:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:104 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say: "O' people! If ye be in doubt as to my religion, then (know ye that) I worship not those whom ye worship besides God, but worship I (only) God, Who taketh you away (from this world) and commanded I am that I be of the believers." See 10:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:105 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (I have also been commanded) saying "Set thy face towards religion uprightly and be thou not of the polytheists." See 10:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:106 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And call thou not (any one) besides God, that which neither profiteth thee nor harmeth thee; for if thou dost, then (beware!) verily if thou didst it then in that case thou wilt be of the unjust-ones. See 10:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:107 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: If God should afflict thee with any harm, then none can be the remover of it but He, and if willeth He any good to thee none can be the repeller of His grace; He bringeth it unto whomsoever He willeth of His servants; and He is the Oft-Forgiving the Merciful. See 10:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:108 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou: "O' ye people!
