Indeed hath come unto you the truth (Qur'an) from your Lord: therefore whosoever receiveth the guidance, he receiveth the guidance for (the good of) his own self; and whosoever strayeth most surely, he strayeth to the detriment of it; and I am not over you a custodian." See 10:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:109 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) follow thou what is revealed unto thee and forbear till God giveth judgment; and He is the Best of (all) judges. See 10:92

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:11 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if God were to hasten unto men the evil (they have earned) as they would fain hasten on for (their) good, surely should have been decreed unto them their doom (Refer to note to verse 2:15.) ; But We leave those who hope not to meet Us (on the Day of Judgment) in their contumacy (The end of the term of respite.) blindly wandering (bewildered). The use of 'Laqa' in this verse explains the actual meaning of the word being the ultimate return and not seeing without the eyes. In another verse1 it is said that the object of the life and the death of man was nothing but to prove as to who among the men are the best in deeds.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:12 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when toucheth a man (an) affliction he crieth unto Us whether lying, or sitting or standing; but when remove We from him his affliction, he passes on as though he had not called unto Us an account of the affliction which did touch him; thus is made fairseeming unto the transgressors what they do (Refer to verses 39:8, 39:48, 30:36, 42:48. Literally, What they were doing.) . See 10:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:13 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And indeed We did destroy generations before you when they did wrong, and had come unto them apostles for them with clear signs (Miracles to prove their bonafides.) but they would not believe; Thus do We recompense the guilty people. See 10:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:14 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then We made you (their) successors in the land after them, that We might see how ye act. See 10:11

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:15 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when are recited unto them Our clear signs, those who hope not to meet Us (Those who do not believe in spiritual life-life after death & the day of judgment Refer to verses 16:101 - 105.) say, "Bring thou (The Holy Prophet.) a Qur'an other than this or change it;" say thou "it is not for me to change it as prompteth me; mine own self I follow naught but what is revealed unto me; Verily, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the chastisement of a great day." People like Abdullah Ibn 'Ubay, Walid Ibn Mughairah, 'Amr Ibn Abdullah Ibn Al-Qais al-Amiri and As Ibn Amir Ibn Hashim approached the Holy Prophet and wanted him to bring some verses without any condemnation of their idols and without the mention of the chastisement to the idolaters on the Day…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:16 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou, "If God hath so willed, I had not recited it unto you, nor would He have taught it to you; Indeed have I lived among you an age (of forty long years - and you have your selves found me truthful & trustworthy and yourselves titled me - Al-Ameen' the Trustworthy.) before it; What! then (yet) ye understand not?" The Truthfulness, Honesty and Reliability of the character and conduct of the Holy Prophet was first made to be stamped on the hearts of the people to be undisputedly acknowledged by all for forty long years, before the declaration of his apostolic mission so that when he starts to preach the faith and the truth to the people, they should not have the least reason or excuses about his personal qualities thereafter to doubt the bonafide of his mission.…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:17 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Who then doth more wrong than he who forgeth a lie against God or belieth His signs? Verily succeed not the guilty ones. See 10:16

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:18 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And worship they besides God, what can neither hurt them nor profit them, and say they: "These are our intercessors with God." Say thou "What! (imagine) ye (to) inform God of what He knoweth not (of what is) in the heavens and in the earth?" Glory be to Him and Exalted is He (far) above what they associate (with Him). This means to argue saying that which they associate with God is not to be found anywhere in the universe, i.e., it is a mere imagination, how could it hurt or profit anyone? This is in reply to the false belief of the people that their idol gods and the other imaginary deities will help them on the Day of Judgment or against any chastisement from God.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:19 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And mankind was naught but one community (Refer to verses 2:213; 21:92; 21:93; 23:52; 23:53; 11:118.) but (later) differed (Got divided.) ; and had not a word (of decree of respite) already gone forth from thy Lord, it would have been decided between them in respect of what they differ therein. Note the conception of humanity as a whole being one nation on the conviction about which depends on the conception of the Brotherhood of Man and the belief in the Fatherhood of God, i.e., God being the Creator of one and all. The same phenomenon has been referred to with greater details in verse 2:23.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:2 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: What! Is it for the people a wonder that We revealed unto a man from among themselves, saying "Warn thou! mankind and bear good tidings unto those who believe that there is a footing of firmness with their Lord;" (but) say the infidels "Verily this is an obvious sorcerer." 'Rajul', i.e., man - refers to the Holy Prophet Muhammad. It is quite evident that the people believed that guidance from God, if at all had to come to them, could come from some beings like the angels and not from any human being like themselves. Since the Holy Prophet Muhammad was one of them, his claim to be the Apostle of God, the people were not prepared to accept. The first ones to accept the claim, were, Abu Talib, Lady Khadija, and 'Ali. The others either ridiculed or wondered as…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:20 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they say, "Why is not a sign (of destruction) sent unto him from His lord?" Say thou "Verily the unseen is only for God, there-fore wait ye; verily I am (also) with you of the waiting ones." See 10:19

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:21 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when We make people taste of (Our) mercy after an affliction hath touched them; lo! they devise plots against Our signs; Say thou (O' Our Apostle!) "God is quicker in devising; Verily Our messengers (Angels.) write down what (all) ye devise." Whenever any of God's bounty reached the people after any straitness, they attributed it as the gift of some imaginary star-god or some false deity, and they started plotting against the apostles of God. Once a very severe famine and drought visited Mecca for seven continuous years and when at last God turned merciful and sent rain and they became prosperous, the same people were those who teased and inflicted persecutions against the Holy Prophet and the faithful ones. This verse says that God is the Best Deviser. 'Rusulana' refers to the Angels who record the deeds of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:22 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He it is Who enableth you to travel by land and sea; so that ye go on board the ships; and they sail on with them in a favourable (Fair.) breeze, and they rejoice thereat, (and when cometh) unto them a violent gale and the billows surge in on them from all sides and they think (Realise.) that they are encompassed therewith, (then) they cry (Call – pray.) (praying) unto God, professing (Pray devoting their Submission to Him.) sincerity unto Him in (their) faith (in Him), saying: "If Thou (O' Our Lord) dost deliver us from this, we shall indeed be of the grateful ones". See 10:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:23 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But when He (God.) delivereth them, behold! they rebel in the earth unjustly; "O' mankind! your rebellion is against your own selves, a provision for (for enjoying.) the life of (only) this world, then unto Us shall be your return, then will. We inform you of what ye were doing." See 10:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:24 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: The likeness of this world's life is only as water which We send down from the sky; by its mingling grow the produce of the earth of which eat men and cattle; until when the earth puts on its golden raiment and gets garnished, and its people deem that they have power (of disposal) over it, (but suddenly) cometh Our command unto it, by night or by day, then We did render it as reaped (As if did not exist at all.) , as though it had not existed yesterday; Thus do We explain the signs in details for people who reflect (Refer to verses 5:52, 11:40, 16:1.) . See 10:21

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:25 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And God calleth (Mankind in general.) (you) to the abode of peace (The life described in verse 10:24 is the transitory life, but God calls to a permanent abode of bliss.) ; and guideth whomsoever He willeth unto the right way (Refer to verses 36:60 & 36:61.) . 'Salam', i.e., Peace and Bliss, refers to the state in the paradise where prevails bliss-perfect. 'Salam' is one of the holy names with which God is addressed. Applying this interpretation, God invites mankind to Him with Whom nothing, but bliss prevails. It is said that the life on this earth starts with crying (a human child immediately as it lands on earth starts its life with crying), passes through miseries and sorrows of life and ends it with effacement. God invites from this abode of misery and effacement to the abode of…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:26 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For those who do good is excellent reward and more (than this); No darkness shall cover their faces nor shall ignominy (befall them); these are the dwellers of the garden; in it shall they abide (Refer to verses 3:105, 39:60.) . See 10:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:27 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And those who have earned evil, the recompense for evil is the like of it; and ignominy shall come upon them; from (the wrath of) God they shall have no protector; as if their faces have been covered (So dark - darkened) as a piece of the darkening night; these are the inmates of the (Hell) fire; in it shall they abide (Refer to verse 3:105.) . See 10:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:28 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: On the day (of resurrection) when We will gather them all together (This is a definite declaration of the truth about the Common day of the final judgment.) , then will We say unto those who associated others (with Us) "Keep ye where ye are, ye and your associated gods;" then We shall separate them, the one from the other, and shall say (unto them) their associate gods "It was not us that ye worshipped (Served.) ". See 10:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:29 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Therefore, God is a sufficient witness between us and you (that) we certainly, of your worship (of us), were unaware. See 10:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, Your Lord is God Who created the heavens and the earth in six days (terms) and is firmly established on 'Arsh (The Throne of Authority. Refer to note to verse 7:54.) ' He regulateth everything; No intercessor can there be save after His leave (Refer to verses 4:85, 19:86, 20:109, 21:28, 34:23, 39:44, 43:86, 74:48. This clearly indicates that there is intercession but by leave from God. See verse 2:255.) ; This is God, your Lord, Therefore Him (alone) worship ye; What! will ye not then mind?" (Refer to verses 41:9, 2:29, 32:4, 13:2, 11:7, 41:11, 7:54.) The extent of a 'Yawm' or day as used in the Holy Qur'an can be from a moment to fifty thousand years. Refer to verse 70:4.The phrase 'Istawa 'ala al-Arsh' has been used in other places of the Holy Qur'an. Refer to…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: There shall every soul realize what it hath sent (Advanced.) before, and they shall be brought back to God, their true Lord (Master.) , and what they did fabricate (Devised.) (the false deities) will vanish (away) from them. See 10:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (Ask them.) (thou O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Who provideth you sustenance from the sky and from the earth? or who controlled! the hearing and the sight? and who bringeth forth the living (Refer to verses 30:19, 5:16, 69:11, 2:57.) from the dead, and bringeth forth the dead from the living? and who administreth (every) affair?" Then they will say "God". Then say (thou unto them) "Will ye not then guard (yourselves against His displeasure)?" Bringing forth the living from the dead figuratively means bringing forth a faithful one from a disbeliever and the bringing forth of a learned one from an illiterate. And bringing forth dead from the living stands for bringing forth a disbeliever from the believer or bringing forth an illiterate from a learned one. A similar statement is there in 2:257 saying, whomsoever God wills He…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then this is God, your true Lord; and what is apart from truth but error; whereto then are ye turned away? See 10:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus is proved true the word of thy Lord against those who transgress that they believe not (Refer to verse 39:71) . See 10:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Of your associates (False Gods and Deities.) , is there anyone who can originate the creation (and), then return it?" Say thou! "God alone doth originate the creation and returneth it whereunto are ye then inclined away (From the truth.) ?" See 10:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Of your associates is there anyone who can guide unto truth?" Say thou! "It is God alone Who guideth unto truth; Is then He Who guideth unto truth more worthy to be followed or he who himself goeth not aright unless he is guided? What then hath be-fallen you? How (ill) ye judge (Refer to verses 46:4, 5:100, 6:50, 13:16, 39:9, 67:22. This is an open refutation of the Validity of the majority's opinion for they follow their own conjectures instead of following the most learned one 'The A'lam'.) ?" In fact, if the people, particularly the Muslims, recite this one Verse intelligently and act faithfully upon the guidance it gives to every sincere seeker after Truth, it will surely guide them to the right way and keep them on it. This verse is…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And follow not most of them (anything) but (their own) conjecture; verily conjecture cannot avail anything against the truth; verily God knoweth all what they do. This verse clearly exposes the position of those who do not follow the phenomenon or the note of guidance laid down in the last Verse 36 and abide by their own imaginary conceptions which in the words of The Holy Qur'an are nothing but conjectures.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And this Qur'an is not such as to be forged by (any one) besides God, but it is a confirmation of (the scriptures) that went before it and (the clearest) explanation of the Book, there is no doubt in it, (it is) from the Lord of the worlds (It refers to the Book - there is an explanation Book stands for the revealed and the explained form of the Book. Refer to verses 56:77 - 56:80; 85:21, 85:22 and their notes. This verse & the next establish the challenging position of the Qu'ran. See also 2:2 & 2:23.) . See 10:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Or do they say: "He (Apostle Muhammad) hath forged it (This verse asserts that the arrangement of Qur'an in its Suras was regular along with its revelation, otherwise the Challenge here and in verses 2:23, 11:13, 17:88, 52:34 to bring a Sura or ten Suras if there had not been any suras will be meaningless.) ?" Say thou! "Bring ye then a chapter like unto it and call on (to your aid) whomsoever ye can, besides God, if ye be truthful." See 10:36

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Nay, they belied that which they comprehended not with the knowledge of it and the explanation (the ultimate significance) of it came not unto them; even thus did belie those before them, see then what was the end of the unjust ones. The disbelievers were too materialistic to grasp the actual meaning of revelation and the divine wordings and similar were those who were before them and some are those of the present age and will be in future also. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Unto Him shall return ye all; (this is) the promise of God in truth; Verily, (it is only) He (Who) beginneth (Originates.) the creation, then causeth it to return (Unto Him.) that He may with equity recompense those who believe and do good; and those who disbelieve, for them shall be the drink from the boiling fluids (Refer to verse 78:24.) and a chastisement painful for they did disbelieve. See 10:3

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of them is he who believeth in it, and of them is he who believeth not in it; and thy Lord knoweth best the mischief-makers. See 10:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if they belie thee, say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "For me is my work and for you is your work, ye are clear oft' of what I do and I am clear off of what ye do (Refer to verses 104:6; 104:7; 42:43; 7:79.) ." See 10:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of them are those who hearken unto thee; canst thou make the deaf hear? though they understand not (Refer to verse 7:179.) . See 10:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And of them are those who look at thee; canst thou guide (Show the way to the blind.) the blind though they see not (Refer to verse 7:179.) . See 10:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, God doeth not any injustice to people, but men (of their own doing.) to their (own) selves do injustice. See 10:39

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And on the day (of resurrection) when He (God.) will gather them as though they had not tarried (Refer to verses 23:112 - 23:114.) in the world or in the grave but an hour of the day, they will recognise each other; Indeed will perish those who belied the meeting with God and were not guided aright (Refer to verse 79:45.) . Literally 'Labth', stay or halt, may refer to present life or to the intermediary state between this life and the final and the total resurrection. These verses, 23:112 - 23:114, if read together assert that man's memory of the past will be so sharp that the individuals will readily recollect and recognise their own class as if only an hour has passed since their separation, but the memory of the length of time of the intervening of years…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if We let thee behold something of (Our wrath) what We warn them against or (before that) We take thee to Ourselves, (even) then (In any case.) unto Us is their return, then God is a witness to (all) what they do (Refer to verse 40:77.) . See 10:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And for every people (was sent) an apostle (Refer to notes to verses 16:1, 16:36, 5:48, 35:24. The faith in all the previous prophets and Scriptures is one of the unique distinctions of Islam.) ; and when came their apostle, the matter between them was decided with equity (The fate of every nation is determined and decided by God conditioned with their response to their respective apostles.) and they shall not (in the least) be done (any) injustice. See 10:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And say they "When this promise (May refer to the wrath or the resurrection.) (of Our wrath) will come to pass, if ye be truthful." See 10:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Our Apostle!) "I own not for myself any harm nor any benefit save what willeth God; To every people is an appointed term; when cometh their term then shall they neither retard (even) an hour (The least time.) nor go before it (This is a warning as well to mankind, to every nation. Refer to verse 63:11.) ." See 10:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He is (the One) Who made the sun a radiation (Arabic 'Zia'.) and the moon a light and planned (the Zodiac lines of movements.) into stations (Not restricted only to moon, the movement of both the Sun and the moon have been planned into stations. It is quite idiomatic in the Arabic language to use the Singular pronoun in the place of a dual or a plural, if it is evident from the context. (A.P.).) that ye might know the number of years and the reckoning (of time); created not God (all) this but for truth; (Thus) doth God make His signs manifest (clearly) for a people who know (Understand). 'Manazil' or the place one passes through, i.e., passages, - three stages of the Moon are twenty-eight in number.Some commentators have thought that this passage indicates that Qur'an cannot be…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou (O' Muhammad!) "Do ye see (Tell me.) if His chastisement cometh upon you by night or by day, what then is there of it that the guilty hasten for?" See 10:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Is it when it cometh to pass, ye will believe in it? What! now (believe ye)? when ye have been (challenging in it and) hastening it on? See 10:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then shall it be said unto those who had been unjust: "Taste ye abiding punishment! Would ye (then) receive other than what ye have wrought?" See 10:45

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And they ask thee: "Is that true?" Say thou! "Aye! By my Lord! Verily, Verily, it is the truth; and ye will not escape (Will not be in a position to defy.) (His wrath)." Hai Bin Akhtab, a Madinite Jew, prior to the Emigration of the Holy Prophet from Mecca, used to visit Mecca on the business of (trade). When he heard about the Holy Prophet, he once attended the audience and hearing the recitation of the Holy Qur'an, asked the Holy Prophet, "O' Muhammad, is what thou reciteth the Truth or a mere jest?" This verse was revealed in reply to his question (M.S.).The 'EA' in Arabic goes before a swearing to denote stress upon the statement. It is also reported that the people used to ask the Holy Prophet if what he said about the excellence and unique…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And if every soul that hath done injustice had all that is in the earth, it would assuredly ransom itself therewith; and they will proclaim their repentance when they behold the doom, and it shall be decided between them with justice and they shall not be done (any) injustice. Meaning even if all that is in the earth be offered by the iniquitous ones, on the Day of Judgment, as a ransom for their acquittal, i.e., to escape the penalty, it shall not be accepted from them. The word 'Asarro' may mean, either declare or reveal and also conceal or hide. Taking 'declare' or 'reveal' as the meaning, the Verse will mean: 'When the chastisement stares the sinners in their face they would offer anything to escape it and they would even openly declare their repentance or regret which would…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Be it known verily God's is what is in the heavens and the earth; Be it (also) known, Verily, God's promise is true, but most of them know not (See also verses 11:120, 39:51.) . See 10:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He giveth life and causeth to die, and unto Him (Alone) shall ye (all) return. See 10:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' mankind! Indeed hath come unto you an exhortation from your Lord, and a cure for (the diseases) what is in your breasts and a guidance and mercy for the believers. In the place of punishment which the people have earned and which they repeatedly demanded, God has sent the Reminder, thus giving an asked for respite. It is undoubtedly the mercy of the Lord1.The physical heart has been considered as the seat of all feelings and emotions in the sense that what is felt by the cognitive self has an immediate effect on the physical heart, such as the feelings of fear and rage, shyness which effect the movement of the heart and the circulation of the blood and in the case of certain feelings such as extreme grief and envy, jealousy, hatred, greed, avarice, etc., even the nervous…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say! (The above blessings are the outcome of God's grace and His Mercy) (that) in the grace (The 5th Holy Imam Muhammad Ibn 'Ali al-Baqir says - By 'Fazl' is meant the Holy Prophet & by 'Rahmat' 'Ali Ibn Abi Talib - This same is the version of some Sunni Commentators (UB) (Kalbi).) of God and in His mercy, in that they should rejoice; it is better than (the wealth) that they gather. See 10:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou! "See ye what (things) God hath sent down for you of sustenance, then ye made something of it unlawful (Refer to verse 6:146 and the subsequent verses dealing with similar subject) and (something of it) lawful." Say thou! "Hath God permitted you or ye forge a lie against God (This refers to declaring thing made lawful & unlawful against the authority of God and the Holy Prophet- Compare this to the 'Mut'as' being declared as unlawful and the other things. Refer to verses 7:32 & 7:33.) ?" See 10:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily in the variation of the night and the day, and what (all) hath created God in the heavens and in the earth, surely are there signs for a people who guard (The pious. Refer to verses 2:2 & 2:3.) (themselves) against evil. See 10:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And what imagine those who forge lies against God on the Day of Resurrection? Verily, God is the Lord of grace for mankind, but most of them thank not. See 10:57

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thou art not (engaged) in any affair, nor dost thou recite any part of the (Holy) Qur'an and nor any deed ye (mankind) be doing, but We are witness over you when ye are engrossed (Entered into.) therein; And doth not lie concealed from thy Lord (even) the weight of an atom in the earth nor in the heaven, nor anything lesser than that nor greater but it is (recorded) in a clear book (It is a clear and detailed warning against those who forge lies or stand hostile against God.) . This verse makes it clearly understood that the Book of God mentioned here is not the one in any written or printed form but the Sacred Tablet (the Lawh al-Mahfuz) in which is secured the knowledge of everything in the universe and the Will of the Lord.This…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Be it known, verily, the friends of God, no fear shall (does not overtake them.) be on them, nor do they grieve. It is quite natural that those who have befriended themselves to the Lord will naturally get freed from every kind of fear or worry from any quarter whatsoever other than God.The first Holy Imam 'Ali Ibn Abi Talib said that those to whom this verse applies (i.e., those meant by 'Aulia Allah'') are the Holy Imams and those who faithfully follow them.The Holy Prophet of God said the friends of God are those by seeing whom, one should be automatically reminded of the Divine Attributes of God, and whose prayer fulness and godliness should infuse in others the same spirit of submission to the Lord. Again the Holy Prophet declared that the friends of God are those: -They…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Those who believe and guarded (themselves) against evil. Regarding the promise in the next verse i.e., for those who believe and guard themselves against evil, the Holy Prophet said that the good news which the friends of God, i.e., the true believers are promised in this life are the good visions they would see in their sleep and the promise in the hereafter is that, when a believer gets into the agony of death before be breathes his last, the Holy Prophet and the Holy Imams appear to him and give him the glad tidings that whomsoever he loved in his life-time are those ready to receive him and whatever he prayed for, is there already provided for him. (M.S. and U.B. and M.F.A.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: For them are glad tidings in the life in this world and in the hereafter; there is no changing the words of God; that is the great achievement (Refer to verses 6:34, 18:27.) . See 10:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And let not their discourse (Refer to verse 63:8. Discourse of the polytheists.) grieve thee, Verily, glory is wholly God's; He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (God has bestowed His glory on the Holy Prophet and the believers.) . See 10:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Be it known, Verily, God's is whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth; They (really) follow not any associates (of God), who call on others besides God; they follow not anything but (their own) gesture (baseless conjecture.) , and they only lie. See 10:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He it is who did make for you the night that ye might rest in it, and the sight-giving (Illuminating.) day; Verily there are signs in it for people who hearken. See 10:63

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say they: God hath taken a son (unto Himself!) Glory be to Him! He is the Self-Sufficient; His (exclusively) is whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth; ye have no authority for this (What they forged.) ; What! say ye against God what ye know not? This refers to the faith of the heathens who believed the angels to be the daughters of God and the Christians believed Jesus to be the Son of God and some others believed their religious leaders to be the sons of God. Refuting all these imaginary and fantastic beliefs, it is said here that God is independent of the need for any daughter or son or to take any such thing for Him for whatever in there in the Universe, is His.The question of having any authority for any such…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Say thou, Verily those who forge a lie against God succeed not. See 10:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Verily, those who hope not to meet Us (on the Day of Judgment) and are pleased with the life of this world and are satisfied (pleased with.) with it, and those who are neglectful of Our signs (This is in contrast to the preceding verse.) . 'Liqa'ana', i.e., meeting Us, the ultimate and of everyone is the return to God for the final judgment. This does not mean seeing God with the physical eye in any form. It has been clearly laid 'La thoriduh al-Absar', i.e., The eyes will not see Him (God). See verse 10:11.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: A provision (The forging – The means of enjoyment.) (it is only) in this world, then unto Us (only) is their return, then shall We make them taste severe chastisement for what they did disbelieve. See 10:68

item.title: bil-Quran: Yunus:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And recite unto them the story of Noah (This verse, to verse 10:73 refers to the conduct of the people of Noah.) when said he to his people: "O' my people! if my stay and my reminding (you) of the signs of God be hard on you yet on God do I rely, muster therefore your designs (Intellect.) and (gather) your associates (false gods), then let not your designs be dubious (Puzzling.) , then execute on me and give no respite (to me)." item.description: O' Joseph! Leave (To be silent about it - rather to keep it a secret.) thou this affair, and thou (O' my wife!) ask forgiveness for thy sin; Verily thou art of the guilty (ones). See 12:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:3 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: We narrate unto thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) the most excellent of the narratives (Stories - Explanations.) by (means of) what We have revealed unto thee this Qur'an; though thou wert before this of the unaware ones. The story of Joseph is called here as the best or the most beautiful of stories. Commentators have given a great many reasons for terming this story as 'the most beautiful narration'.The beauty of the narration consists in conveying a great amount of meaning in the shortest possible narration through the use of the most minimum of words with most eloquent hints. The story of Joseph deals with the external manly beauty in a man along with the ideal excellence and the purity of his soul, and a woman (Zulaikha), madly falling in love with the manly beauty to own it for herself…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:30 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said the women (The news somehow escaped out of the palace - and became the talk of the town - The title 'Aziz' was the title of the Chief of the Royal Staff i.e. a Vizier.) in the City: "The wife of the (great) 'Aziz' (Aziz the Official Title of the Chief Officer or the Vizier of the King of Egypt.) (the chief) seeketh to seduce her slave from his (pure) self; Verily hath he affected her deeply with love; Verily we see her in manifest error." See 12:25

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:31 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when she ('Zulaikha' the wife of the 'Aziz'.) heard of their scheming (Malicious.) talk, she sent for them, and prepared for them a repast (Lit. Cushioned Couch.) and gave unto each one of them a knife and said (unto Joseph) "Come thou out unto them." So when they saw him, they did extol him; and (in their amazement) cut their hands, and said (exclaimed): "Hasha-lillah!" (Far from God is every imperfection!) This is not a mortal (human being), This is none but a noble angel! The imputation against Zulaikha's conduct had spread almost to every house in the town.Zulaikha at last chose some of the women, the chief characters among the propagandists, and invited them to a feast with a fruit which needed to be cut with a knife. (It is said that it was Citrus or sweet lemons)…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:32 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Zulaikha.) she: "This is he about whom ye blamed me; and indeed I sought to seduce him from his (pure) self, but he did firmly abstain himself guiltless; and (now) if he doth not what I bid him, he shall certainly be imprisoned, and he shall certainly be of those brought low!" See 12:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:33 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he (Joseph.) "O' my Lord! The prison is dearer to me than that unto which they invite me; and if thou turneth (The turning away of the guile by God does not mean overpowering Joseph against his will and choice. It means raising his Cognitive self above the level of the sexual desires, in response to what he asked for.) not away from me their guile I may yearn unto them and become of the ignorant ones." See 12:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:34 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thereupon heard him (granted his prayer.) his Lord and turned (See note to verse 12:33.) He away their guile from him; Verily He is the All Hearing, The All-Knowing. See 12:31

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:35 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then it occurred to them (even) after they had seen the signs (of his innocence) that they should imprison him for a time. When the women got hopeless of winning over Joseph, they suggested Zulaikha to imprison Joseph for a few days and subject him to the miseries therein so that he might then realize the value of the luxuries in the palace. Zulaikha readily accepted the suggestion, for that would make the public know that it was Joseph who was guilty and not she. Joseph was enchained and taken through the streets of the town with an announcer calling in the front 'Look ye'! This is the punishment for the attempt against the chastity of the wife of the 'Aziz', Zulaikha.To know how Joseph felt and whose help he sought Zulaikha was in the guise of an ordinary spectator…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:36 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And with him entered the prison, two youths; Said one of them (Unto Joseph) "Verily I saw (in dream) myself pressing wine." And said the other: "I saw (in dream) myself carrying bread on my head, and birds eating there of. Inform us of its interpretation: Verily we see thee of the doers of good (to all)." The two young men were:The 'Saqi' (the servant who serves the drinks) called 'Yunan' who used to draw wine from the grapes for the King.The Cook of the King. He was called Mahila.These two were imprisoned on the charge of attempting to poison the King. Joseph used to move very sympathetically among the prisoners, treated them very kindly and had been helping them by mending their worn-out clothes and in other possible ways. Joseph had the divine gift of interpreting dreams.The prisoners used…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:37 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he (Joseph): "There shall not come unto you the food which ye are fed with but I inform ye two of its interpretation before it cometh unto ye two; This is of what my Lord hath taught me; Verily I have forsaken the religion of the people who believe not in God, and of the hereafter, they are dis believers." Joseph wanted to be quick in interpreting the dreams for there was death for one of them. He first preached Islam, the correct faith in God, so that the man might die with faith in God and then interpreted the dreams.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:38 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And I follow the religion of my fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; and it is not (lawful) for us to associate aught with God; This is by God's grace upon us and on mankind, but most people give not thanks. See 12:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:39 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' my (two) fellows of the prison! Are (many) lords differing from each other better or God the One, the All-Dominant? See 12:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:4 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When said Joseph unto his father (Jacob): "O' my father! Verily I did see (dreamt) eleven stars and the sun and moon, I saw them (all) prostrating unto me." _Yacoob (_Jacob) had twelve sons and Joseph was the youngest and extremely beautiful. Jacob loved Joseph the most. Joseph's mother Raheel had died and his aunt who was later wedded to Jacob, had brought up Joseph. The eleven brothers of Joseph were envious of him.Joseph when he was yet of twelve years of age dreamt that the gates of heaven had become wide open, a great light had enveloped the whole environment, an ocean with huge waves rising in it and fishes of various kinds singing the glory of God, Joseph standing upon the peak of a mountain surrounded with green trees, with streams of fresh water flowing at the foot…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:40 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Ye worship not besides Him but (mere) names (Mere imaginary beings without any existence - or without any authority or hold as imagined.) which ye have named, ye and your fathers, God hath not sent down for them any authority; there is no judgment but God's; He hath bidden that ye worship not but unto Him; This is the right religion, but most people know (it) not. See 12:37

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:41 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' my (two) fellows of the prison! As to one of you, he will pour out wine for his lord to drink; As for the other, he shall be crucified, so that the birds shall eat from his head. The matter is decreed about which ye two inquired. Note that the word 'Sahibi', i.e., my fellow or companion, has been used by Joseph in addressing polytheists. The mere the two fellow-prisoners who were polytheists. The mere use of the word 'Sahibi' can never mean that two fellows who were disbelievers in God were in any sense of the term the equals of Joseph who was the apostle of God. Thus, if any one is merely called a contemporary or the companion of a great personality can never be an equal or necessarily a good person. Merely because anyone else is…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:42 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And he (Joseph.) said unto him whom he knew would be delivered of the two: "mention me unto thy lord;" (The King.) But the devil caused him (The fellow prisoner.) to forget mentioning (it) to his lord, (The King.) so he (Joseph.) remained in the prison a few years (more). Before the prisoners were released, Joseph had desired them to remind the King of him and since Joseph forgot God, his true Lord, and sought help from the King and not from God, he was made to stay in the prison a few more years. When Joseph was informed of the consequence of his seeking help from the King instead of seeking it from God, he wept and prayed to God in tears. At last, when the prayers of Joseph and also Jacob were heard, the period of the imprisonment…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:43 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said the king "Verily, I did see in (dream) seven fat kine which seven lean ones devoured, and seven green ears and (seven) others dry; O' chiefs (of my court)! Explain (Opine.) ye unto me my dream, if ye can interpret a dream." When the chiefs, the great scholars who were experts in interpreting dreams got helpless against the confused nature of the dreams, the one of the two fellow-prisoners, (i.e., the Saqi), requested permission to go to the prison and get the correct interpretation from the one (i.e., Joseph) who had proved himself to be an expert interpreter of dreams. The King immediately consented.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:44 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "Confused (Fantastic – Jumbled.) dreams (are these)! and we know not the interpretation of such (confused) dreams." See 12:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:45 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said he of the two who had been released, and re membered after a long (Arabic: 'Ummat' used here as time. Considerable lapse of time.) time; "I will expound unto you its interpretation, so let me go (to the prison)." See 12:43

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:46 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Joseph! O' truthful (The term 'Siddeeq' can never be applicable to one who has ever believed in anything besides God.) one! expound thou unto us seven fat kine which seven lean ones devour, and seven ears green and seven (others) dry, that I may return unto the people so that they may know. The Saqi went into the prison and asked the interpretation of the dream from Joseph.Note that the address 'Siddeeq', the truthful one, is given to the one like Joseph the Apostle of God who never, not even once in his life had uttered any falsehood. Thus, the title could not be had by anyone and every one who once worshipped idols and uttered all falsehoods of a false faith and the free practice of infidelity and later embraced the truth.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:47 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Joseph.) he: "Ye shall sow seven years as usual, but that which ye reap leave ye in its ears, except a little of which ye eat." Joseph advises the ruling authority to hoard the surplus of the foodstuff for the unseen emergencies in the interest of the people and how to preserve it so that it may not get rotten and useless. It is a lesson to the authorities to be always on guard against a possible famine which might overtake a country. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:48 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then shall come after that seven years of hardship (famine), which shall eat away all that ye have laid by beforehand for them, except a little of which ye have preserved. (For seeds.) See 12:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:49 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then will come after that a year people will have abundant rain and in having it they will press wine. See 12:47

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:5 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he (Jacob): "O' my (dear) son! (Beware!) Relate thou not thy dream unto thy brothers, lest they plot against thee a plot; Verily Satan unto man is an open enemy!" Joseph was wonderfully beautiful and the envy of his brothers had gradually developed into definite hostility and they only waited for an opportunity even to do away with Joseph's life. When the Omnipotent Lord wills, He can manifest anything in the Universe, let man wonder at it, believe in it or not. Every apostle of God was granted a distinctive excellence, and the divine gift to Joseph was his wonderful personal beauty. It is related that once at night Ayesha (one of the wives of the Holy Prophet) had lost her needle and could not find it. The Holy Prophet placed a finger of his hand before the lamp…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:50 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said the king: "Bring him (Joseph.) unto me!" So when the messenger came unto him, said he (Joseph): "Go thou back unto thy lord and ask him, what is the matter with the women (Joseph when summoned he sent word to the Aziz to first enquire from the women about the guilt. The Aziz called the women and enquired.) who cut their hands; Verily my Lord knoweth their guile." When the Saqi conveyed the interpretation to the King, the King got extremely pleased and wanted to hear the interpretation directly from the prisoner (Joseph) and ordered to present the prisoner to him in person.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:51 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said the king (unto the women) what was the matter with you when ye sought to seduce Joseph from his (pure) self?" Said (replied) the women! "Hasha-lillah (Far from God is every imperfection) we know not any evil against him!" Said the Aziz's (Zulaikha Confessed.) wife: "Now the truth hath become manifest, I (it was who) sought to seduce him from his (pure) self; And verily he is of the truthful ones! See 12:50

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:52 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (Said Joseph) This (Inquiry I caused) that he (the King) might know that I have not been unfaithful unto him in his absence, and that God guideth not the guile of the unfaithful ones. See 12:50

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:53 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: I exculpate not myself, verily (one's) self is wont to bid (him to) evil, except such as my Lord hath had mercy on; Verily my Lord is Oft-Forgiving, All- Merciful. Some say that the wordings of this verse refer to the confession of Zulaikha acknowledging the fault to be her own and declaring Joseph as innocent.'Ammarah' - the urge in man which commands the individual to do evil. If the individual fights out this urge successfully with his faith in God and his determination to do only good, the strength of the will is increased and the individual, he or she, remains safe against the strong attractions from the Satanic forces. To help the individual, the All-Merciful has endowed in every human being the instinct of 'Lawwama'1, the spirit of accusing the self through another native endowment, the Conscience, against…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:54 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And the king said (Ordered) "Bring him (Joseph.) unto me, I will exclude him for (service to) my (own) self!" So when he had spoken unto him: he (the king) said: "Verily thou art (from) this day in our (own) presence, accommodated (honourably) (as) a Trusted one!" Thus, Joseph became the dearest, the most honoured and the nearest in position to the king - and was placed in charge of the treasuries of the land.Joseph ordered that all people should start and carry on cultivation of foodgrains as much as they could. Only the grain fit to be reaped were taken away from the plants and the rest were left in them so that the raw ones could not be wasted or get rotten. A huge grain-store was built outside the town and all that could be procured was gathered…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:55 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he: (Joseph.) "Set me (in authority) over the treasuries of the land; Verily I am a (faithful) keeper, knowing well (its management)." When to be in charge of a terrestrial treasury requires the knowledge and ability as to how to manage it, what about to be in charge of guiding mankind towards the ultimate aim and the object of creation. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:56 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Thus We did establish Joseph in the land; to take possession therein as he pleased; We do bestow Our mercy on whomsoever We will, and We waste not the recompense of the doers of good. See 12:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:57 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And certainly the recompense of the hereafter is (much) better for those who believe and guard (themselves) against evil. See 12:54

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:58 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And came the brothers of Joseph and entered they unto him, (Joseph.) and he knew them but (While.) they knew (Recognise.) him (Joseph.) not. When Canaan also got affected by the famine, people there also became helpless. At last, the sons of Jacob approached Jacob and said, "Father, we hear that the king of Egypt is reported to be a very kind and very charitable man, helping the famine-stricken people and hence we seek thy permission to got to Egypt and try there our luck and get some grain if possible".Jacob permitted but kept Bin-Yamin, the brother of Joseph with him for he felt consoled by the presence of the boy in the absence of Joseph. The party of the ten brothers with all that they could carry with them, to sell or to exchange for the foodgrains, entered Egypt…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:59 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when he (Joseph.) hath furnished them with their provision, said he (unto them): "Bring ye unto me a brother of yours from your father; See ye not that I give full measure? and that I am the best of hosts?" Bin-Yamin (Benjamin) was detained by Jacob to remain with him and the ten brothers had brought a camel to carry his share of the grain. Joseph said that the supply would be according to the number of the men that came demanding it and not according to the number of the camels that people come with and thus they were told to bring their brother (Bin-Yamin) next time along with them. 'Khair al-Munzileen, - i.e., I am such a good host that I am never worried in the least by any number of guests.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:6 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And thus will thy Lord choose thee and teach thee the interpretation of sayings (dreams), and perfect His grace unto thee and unto the children of Jacob, even as He perfected it to thy (fore) fathers aforetime, Abraham, Isaac; Verily thy Lord is All-Knowing, All-Wise. See 12:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:60 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: But if ye bring him not unto me, then there shall be no measure (of corn) for you with me, nor shall ye (even) come near me. See 12:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:61 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They said: "We will seek to get him from his father, and verily We certainly shall do it." See 12:59

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:62 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said he (Joseph.) unto his servants: "Put their goods (Money - or the goods they had brought to barter.) into their saddle-bags that they may perceive it when they return unto their family, so that they may come back." Joseph ordered the slaves who measured the grain to the people to place the things which Joseph's brothers had given as the price of the wheat in their own bags, without their knowledge, so that when after reaching their destination they would see the price of the grain had somehow been returned to them along with the supply and they would surely return.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:63 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So when they returned unto their father, said they: "O' our father! The measure is denied unto us, so send with us our ('Bin-Yamin' (Benjamin).) brother, so that we may get the measure: And verily, certainly we will we guard him (well)." See 12:62

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:64 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He said: "Can I trust him unto you except as I entrusted his (Joseph.) brother unto you aforetime? but God is the Best Guard, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful ones." Jacob wanted his sons to realise that their undertaking to guardianship had no value with him whatsoever. He entrusted them in this case the same as he did in the case of Joseph before, and at that time also he did not attach value to their undertaking; he trusted only God. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:65 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when they opened their belongings, they found their goods (Money - or the goods of barter.) returned unto them. Said they: "O' our father! What (more) can we desire? This our goods hath been returned unto us; and we will bring (more) corn for our family and guard our brother, and we shall have in addition the measure of a camel (load); This (what we have now brought) is (only) an easy (Light measure - small quantity.) measure." See 12:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:66 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said (Jacob) "Never will I send him with you until ye pledge a firm covenant in God's name that ye will most surely bring him back unto me, unless ye are completely (Overpowered.) surrounded; And when pledged they unto him a covenant, said (Jacob.) he: (There is) God over all what we say, a Guardian-Witness." See 12:64

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:67 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And said (Jacob.) he: "O' my sons! Enter (To avoid being envied by the people, they were advised to enter separately by different doors. This indicates that Islam does not discard the effect of the evil eye, and there are authentic traditions from the Holy Prophet indicating that there are some, the evil of whose sight affect the other objects. The remedy for it is firm trust in God. There are particular prayers for this - there are authentic records of the actual instances in support of this. Refer to verses 39:38 & 14:11.) ye not by one gate, but enter ye by different gates; and I cannot avail you aught against God; judgment is only God's; On Him do I rely; and on Him (only) let the reliants rely." The advice to enter by different doors was because the…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:68 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when they had entered as they were bidden by their father; it did not avail them aught against (the decree of) God; but (it was only) a desire in Jacob's soul which he satisfied; and verily, he was possessed of knowledge for we had taught him, but most people know (this) not. In spite of the caution taken, Bin-Yamin entering the city alone, separated by his other brothers, lost his way and Gabriel at last guided him and got him joined to his other brothers.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:69 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when they entered in unto Joseph, he lodged his (own) brother (Benjamin) with himself, said (into his ears) "I am thy brother (Joseph), therefore grieve thou not at what they do." The brothers of Joseph entered the court of Joseph and presented themselves and said they had brought with them their brother Bin-Yameen and they also wanted to return the price of the wheat which by some mistake had been left in the grains supplied to them.Joseph ordered for six trays of food for them and desired that on each tray should sit the children of one and the same parents. On the five trays sat all the others - on the sixth Bin-Yamin was left alone who stood with tears in his eyes. Joseph asked the reason for his shedding tears. Bin-Yamin said that all the others were…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:7 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Indeed there are in (the accounts of) Joseph and their brothers, signs for the inquirers. See 12:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:70 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when he (Joseph.) had furnished them with their provisions, (at the instance of Joseph) was placed the drinking cup in his brother's saddle-bag; Then cried out a crier: "O' ye (of) the caravan! Verily ye are thieves!" The valuable cup with which the supply of the grain was measured was intentionally left in the bag of Bin-Yamin and at last when it was found in it, no amount of argument on the part of the brothers, particularly of Yahood, was of any avail. According to Jacobian Law Bin-Yamin was detained to be a slave to the owner of the stolen property.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:71 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they, while turning unto them: "What is it that ye miss?" See 12:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:72 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they (The King's servants.) : "We miss the king's drinking cup and whosoever bringeth it, shall have a camel load (of corn); and I am responsible for it." See 12:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:73 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: (Brothers of Joseph.) "By God! Ye know that we came not to make mischief in the land, and nor we are thieves." See 12:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:74 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They (The King's servants.) said: "But what shall be the punishment for this, if ye be liars?" See 12:70

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:75 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: (The King's servants.) "The punishment (Refer to note on verse 12:83.) for it shall be that he in whose bag it is found shall himself be (held as bondsman) in penalty for it; Thus do we punish the wrong-doers." According to the Egyptian Law, the penalty for theft was a very severe punishment with whipping - but here the punishment was allowed to be determined by the son of Jacob, who pledged the undertaking according to the Jacobian Law, i.e., the thief to be a slave of the owner of the stolen property for one complete year.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:76 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Then he (Joseph) began (the search) with their sacks before the sack of his brother, then he drew it out from his brother's sack; Thus did We plan (The word 'Kidna' indicates or means that it was the Divine plan & not of Joseph's own.) for Joseph; it was not (lawful) that he should take his brother under the king's law unless God willed it; We raise the degrees (of wisdom and knowledge) whomsoever We will; and above every one endued with knowledge is the All-Knowing (One). (a) Joseph's plan was to remind his family of their misuse of the law. Once before when Joseph was a child living with his aunt who did not like to send him to Jacob in spite of Jacob's earnest demand, she tied a belt of her own round the waist of the child…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:77 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They said: If he stealeth, indeed did steal (Refer to note on verse 12:76 their selling of Joseph to the merchants.) before, a brother (Joseph.) of his, but Joseph kept it a secret to himself, and disclosed it not unto them; he (Joseph.) said: "Ye are in an evil (This remark indicates Joseph's hatred and resentment against falsehood.) condition, and God knoweth best what ye allege." See 12:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:78 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "O' (The title of the Chief Officer - or the King.) Aziz! he hath a father, a very old (who loveth him very much), so take one of us in his place; Verily we see thee of the doers of good (to others)." See 12:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:79 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he "God protect us! (from acting a forbidden deed) that we should seize (any one) other than him (By taking an unwanted person.) with whom found we our property, for verily then we would be of the unjust ones." See 12:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:8 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: When said they: (Brothers of Joseph.) "Surely Joseph and his (own) brother (Bin Yamin' i.e. Benjamin - own brother of Joseph.) are dearer to our father than we, though we are (in) a (bigger) group; Verily our father is in manifest error." See 12:5

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:80 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when they despaired of (moving) him, they retired whispering (to each other); Said the eldest of them: "Know ye not how your father took from you a (firm) covenant in God's name, (and) how failed ye about Joseph aforetime? So never will I leave this land until my father permitteth me or decideth God for me; And He is the Best of judges." See 12:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:81 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Return ye unto your father (Jacob.) and say ye: "O' our father! Verily thy son committed theft; we bear not witness but to what we have known and we could not guard against the unseen." See 12:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:82 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And inquire thou (i.e., Jacob.) in the township in which we were and the caravan which we proceeded with; And verily we are truthful. See 12:76

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:83 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he (Jacob.) "Nay, your self have contrived the story (suitable) for you; so (my course) is comely patience; maybe God bringeth them unto me all together; Verily He is the All-Knowing, The All-Wise." (a) In verse 12:18 Jacob was justified in accusing his sons of scheming for they had actually forged the story but the justification here is because they were responsible for the misinterpretation of the law1 when they declared that from whose bag the missing article comes out, he must be punished. The law was against the one who was proved to be a thief, and the theft was not proved and here they should have defied the accusation against the detention of their brother but they did not argue the case at all, on the contrary they had accepted the accusation on a wrong basis.2(b) This…

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:84 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And he turned away from them, and said: "Alas! my grief for Joseph!" and his eyes were whitened (Lost his sight - could not see.) with the grief, and he was a represser (One who controls himself in sorrow and anger.) (of grief). See 12:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:85 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "By God! Thou wilt not cease to remember Joseph until thou art (seriously) ill or (until) thou art of the perished ones (dead)." See 12:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:86 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He said: "I only complain of my distress and grief unto God, and I know from God what ye know not." See 12:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:87 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: O' my sons! go ye and inquire about Joseph and his (Ben-Yamin (Benjamin).) Brother, and despair not of God's mercy; Verily despaireth (Despair against God's mercy is counted as a major sin.) not of God's mercy but the disbelieving people. See 12:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:88 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So when they (Brothers of Joseph.) came in unto him (Joseph.) said they: "O' Aziz! distress hath touched us and our family; and we have (now) come (but) with scanty capital: so give us full measure and bestow thou charity on us; Verily God rewardeth the charitable ones." See 12:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:89 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said he (Joseph.) : "Know ye what ye did unto Joseph and his brother when ye were ignorant (of the consequences)." See 12:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:9 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: (So) Slay ye Joseph! or cast him out to some (other) land, (so that) unto you (exclusively) be the attention of your father, and ye may be after that a righteous people. It is said that the whole story of Joseph was revealed to the Holy Prophet for more than one purpose, one of which was to inform him of what happened even among the brothers, the children of one and the same father. Thus, there could be no wonder if the people behaved or dealt with him as they did. It could be to hint to the Holy Prophet that as the brothers of Joseph conspired and acted, his people would do the same with him.1Similar was the conspiracy of the Quraysh against the Holy Prophet.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:90 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: They said: "Art thou indeed Joseph?" Said he: "I am Joseph and this is my (Ben-Yamin (Benjamin).) Brother; Indeed God hath been gracious unto us; Verily he who practiceth piety and is patient (is always rewarded) for verily God wasteth not the reward of the doers of good." See 12:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:91 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "By God! indeed hath God chosen thee over us, and we were certainly guilty." See 12:83

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:92 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He said: (This same declaration was that which the Holy Prophet Muhammad had issued on his capture of the Holy City Mecca, for all his enemies.) "(There shall be) no reproof against you (from) this day; God may forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful (ones)." The events of Joseph's story fully agree with those of the Holy Prophet's life and those of the Holy Ahl al-Bayt. When the Holy Prophet captured Mecca, he declared the same kind of amnesty in the same words to all the heathens of the town who had been the bloodthirsty enemies of his own and that of his faithful followers, the early converts to Islam.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:93 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Take ye this my shirt and cast it on the face of my father, he shall become seeing (recover his sight); and come ye unto me with all your family. There is sufficient evidence to the fact that Jacob knew that Joseph was alive and safe and one day they would meet him and yet the extent to which he felt the separation is given in this story. What would have been the feeling and grief of the Fourth Holy Imam Ali Ibn al-Husayn Zayn al 'Abidin who had lost not one but eighteen Josephs of his family who were massacred before his eyes at Karbala whom he would never meet in this world. The Holy Imam wept for all the forty years he lived after the heart-rending tragedy of Karbala.

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:94 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when the caravan (with Yousuf's shirt) had left (Literally, departed.) (Egypt), their father (there in his place) said: "I feel the smell of Joseph, if ye think not that I dote." See 12:93

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:95 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "By God! Verily thou art in thy error." See 12:93

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:96 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: So when came the bearer of glad tidings, he cast it (the shirt) on his (Jacob's) face, and (forthwith) returned (unto him) the eye-sight. He said: "Said I not unto you? Verily I know from God what ye know not." (a) The return of sight means that he turned again seeing. It implies that Jacob had lost his sight and then regained it. The attempt to attach figurative significance means he came to know the whereabouts of Joseph is unwarranted and does not tally with 'Fartadda' which means, return to a state or regaining a thing lost. (A.P.).

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:97 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: Said they: "O' our father! Ask thou forgiveness for us, Verily we are guilty ones." See 12:96

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:98 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: He said: "Soon will I ask forgiveness for you from my Lord: Verily He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful." See 12:96

item.title: bil-Quran: Yusuf:99 with Tafsir The Holy Qur'an - The Final Testament
item.description: And when they entered the presence of Joseph, he accommodated his parents with himself, and said he: "Enter ye Egypt, if God willeth, (all) in security." See 12:96
